Toni Kroos (German; born 4 January 1990) is a German former professional footballer who played as a midfielder.
Written by Michael Jackson and Lionel Richie and produced by Quincy Jones, this 1985 charity supergroup single raised money for Ethiopian famine relief — what is it?

We Are the World: 1985 charity song. It was written by Michael Jackson and Lionel Richie and produced by Quincy Jones for the album We Are the World to raise money for the 1983–1985 famine in Ethiopia.

At a time when Latin ruled scholarly writing, this medieval Italian poet rebelled by composing his masterwork in the everyday vernacular — a poem so revered Boccaccio later christened it 'Divine.' Who was he?
Dante Alighieri: Italian writer and philosopher (1265–1321)
Founded in 1994 in Little Rock, Arkansas by Amy Lee and Ben Moody, this rock band rode 'Bring Me to Life' to a multi-million-selling debut called 'Fallen' — what band is it?
Evanescence is an American rock band founded in 1994 by singer and keyboardist Amy Lee and guitarist Ben Moody in Little Rock, Arkansas.
Featuring the voices of Matthew Broderick, Nathan Lane, and Whoopi Goldberg, this 1994 Disney film traces a prince's journey home after his father is killed by a scheming uncle — what is it?
The Lion King is a 1994 American animated musical drama film directed by Roger Allers and Rob Minkoff, produced by Don Hahn, and written by Irene Mecchi, Jonathan Roberts, and Linda Woolverton.
An American actress and musician known for portraying offbeat characters in dark independent films, she gained prominence in the early 1990s and has been nominated for an Oscar — who is she?
Juliette Lewis (born June 21, 1973) is an American actress, singer and musician.
She played Lucy Carlyle on Raising Hope, but first made her name as a model and singer before films like Bully and Choke — which actress is it?
Bijou Phillips (born April 1, 1980) is an American model, socialite, and actress and singer.
Before acting, this scion of a famous film family assisted Sanjay Leela Bhansali on set, then went on to win seven Filmfare Awards — who is he?
Ranbir Kapoor (born 28 September 1982) is an Indian actor who works in Hindi-language films.
After fame as a youngster in The Goonies, this actor surged back with No Country for Old Men and later played the purple titan Thanos — who is he?
Josh Brolin (born February 12, 1968) is an American actor and producer.
After M. Night Shyamalan spotted her playing Rosalind on stage, this director's daughter went on to roles in The Village and Spider-Man 3 — who is she?
Bryce Dallas Howard (born March 2, 1981) is an American actress and director.
Landlocked in East Africa's Great Lakes region within the Nile basin, this nation shares part of Lake Victoria with Kenya and Tanzania — which country?
Uganda is a landlocked country in East Africa. The southern part includes a substantial portion of Lake Victoria, shared with Kenya and Tanzania.

Their classic lineup paired vocalist Axl Rose with guitarist Slash, and their debut, Appetite for Destruction, eventually sold over 30 million copies on the strength of "Sweet Child o' Mine." Which band is it?
Guns N' Roses is an American hard rock band formed in Los Angeles, California, in 1985 from L.A.
Drafted 30th overall by the Chicago Bulls and later named Most Improved Player, this five-time All-Defensive guard now plays for the Golden State Warriors — who is he?
Jimmy Butler (born September 14, 1989) is an American professional basketball player for the Golden State Warriors of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
This Brooklyn rapper, known for a laid-back delivery and semi-autobiographical tales of hardship, was the first artist signed to Sean Combs's Bad Boy Records — who was he?
This Spanish actor first made his name in films like "Jamón jamón" and "Mar adentro" before his Oscar-nominated turn in "Before Night Falls" — who is he?
Javier Bardem (born 1 March 1969) is a Spanish actor.
The daughter of actress Lisa Bonet and a famous rock musician, this actress broke through playing a mutant named Angel Salvadore in a 2011 X-Men film — who is she?
Zoë Kravitz (born December 1, 1988) is an American actress, singer, and filmmaker.
With Robert Plant on vocals and Jimmy Page on guitar, this 1968 London band fused heavy electric blues into the template for heavy metal — who are they?
Led Zeppelin were an English rock band formed in London in 1968.
Who hustled the courts in White Men Can't Jump, shuffled through Zombieland, and survived 2012 — the same actor known for tending bar on Cheers?
Woody Harrelson (born July 23, 1961) is an American actor.
This actor won a Volpi Cup for Hungry Hearts and turned up in Frances Ha and Inside Llewyn Davis before becoming a galaxy-spanning villain named Kylo Ren. Who is he?
Adam Driver (born November 19, 1983) is an American actor.
Before co-founding the Celtic punk band the Pogues, this poet and singer started his first band, the Nips, in 1977 with his then-girlfriend. Who is he?
Shane MacGowan (25 December 1957 - 30 November 2023) was an English-born Irish singer-songwriter, musician, and poet.
His was the longest reign of any Ottoman sultan, taking Belgrade in 1521 and Rhodes in 1522 and shattering Hungary's army at Mohács in 1526 — who was this sultan?
Suleiman the Magnificent: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire (1520–1566)
His debut novel Carrie launched a horror empire, but this author's range stretched all the way to Stand by Me and The Shawshank Redemption — who is he?
Stephen King (born September 21, 1947) is an American author.

Once grimly nicknamed the "white death" and historically called consumption, this contagious bacterial disease usually starts in the lungs — and most who carry it never show a single symptom. What is it?
Tuberculosis: Infectious disease. Tuberculosis initially infects the lungs, but it can also spread to other parts of the body.
Her breakout was the unsettling 2011 thriller Martha Marcy May Marlene, but the world really met her in 2014 as Scarlet Witch — which actress, sister to two famous twins, is this?
Elizabeth Olsen (born February 16, 1989) is an American actress.
She studied at Oxford, debuted in Kenneth Branagh's Much Ado About Nothing, and later fought werewolves as Selene in the Underworld series — which English actress?
Kate Beckinsale (born 26 July 1973) is an English actress.
He played Alex P. Keaton on Family Ties and a time-traveling teen in a 1985 trilogy before becoming a Parkinson's research advocate — which Canadian-American actor?
Michael J. Fox: Canadian-American actor and activist (born 1961)
A Swedish actress broke through internationally with a starring role in The White Queen and has since earned Golden Globe and Critics' Choice nominations. Who is she?
Rebecca Ferguson (born 19 October 1983) is a Swedish actress.

A French playmaker who won FIFA World Player of the Year three times and the 1998 Ballon d'Or—renowned for elegance, vision, and ball control—later coached Real Madrid to multiple trophies. Who is he?
Zinedine Zidane (born 23 June 1972), popularly known as Zizou, is a French professional football manager and former player who played as an attacking midfielder.
An Italian football manager with a record five UEFA Champions League titles, the only manager in six Champions League finals—who is he?
Carlo Ancelotti (Italian; born 10 June 1959) is an Italian professional football manager and former player who is the head coach of the Brazil national team.
A Russian tennis player ranked world No. 1 who won the 2021 US Open and 2020 ATP Finals—who is he?
Daniil Medvedev (born 11 February 1996) is a Russian professional tennis player.
She rose to fame on two Disney series before shifting to music in 2020—her debut album 'Sour' topped the Billboard 200 and spawned two number-one singles, 'Drivers License' and 'Good 4 U'. Who?
Olivia Rodrigo (born February 20, 2003) is an American singer-songwriter and actress.
Known as a 'scream queen,' this American actress and producer starred in horror and slasher films with box office earnings exceeding $2.5 billion—who is she?
Jamie Lee Curtis (born November 22, 1958) is an American actress, producer, and children's author.
She made an uncredited film debut in 1988's Mac and Me and landed her first major role in the horror comedy Leprechaun, years before her Emmy-winning turn as Rachel Green — who is she?
Jennifer Aniston (born February 11, 1969) is an American actress.

The most populous democracy on Earth since independence in 1947, bounded by the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal with maritime neighbors Sri Lanka and the Maldives nearby—which South Asian nation is seventh-largest by area?
India is a country in South Asia.

On April 15, 1947, this baseball player took his position at first base for the Brooklyn Dodgers, shattering the color line that had separated MLB from Black players since the 1880s. Who became the first African American to play in the modern major leagues?
Jackie Robinson (January 31, 1919 - October 24, 1972) was an American professional baseball player who was the first African American to play in Major League Baseball (MLB) in the modern era.
This civil conflict began after the UN Partition Plan, became an international war with Israel's independence declaration, and resulted in the expulsion of over 700,000 Palestinians. What event?
Australia's most populous city surrounds a famous harbor and stretches 80 kilometers from the Pacific Ocean east to the Blue Mountains west. What is it?
Sydney is the capital city of the state of New South Wales, and the most populous city in Australia.
Northern Italy's economic powerhouse and second-most populous city, accounts for 20% of Italy's GDP—founded as a Celtic settlement around 590 BC—what's this metropolis?
Milan: Second-largest city in Italy. Milan is the regional capital of Lombardy, in northern Italy, and the seat of the Metropolitan City of Milan.
Fought between 1939 and 1945, this global conflict remains history's deadliest, claiming 60 to 75 million lives and ending with the only nuclear weapons ever used in war — which conflict?
World War II: 1939–1945 global conflict. World War II, or the Second World War (1 September 1939 – 2 September 1945), was a global conflict between two coalitions: the Allies and the Axis powers.
Raging from 1914 to 1918 and nicknamed 'the Great War,' this conflict's mass troop movements helped spread the deadly Spanish flu pandemic — which war?
World War I: 1914–1918 global conflict. The war saw important developments in weaponry including tanks, aircraft, artillery, machine guns, and chemical weapons.
Controlled until 2023 by Yevgeny Prigozhin, this Russian state-funded private military company first emerged fighting in the Donbas war — which group?
Wagner Group: Russian private military company. The Wagner Group has used infrastructure of the Russian Armed Forces.
A first-century Jewish preacher in Roman Judaea whose life is chronicled in the four Gospels, he's the central figure of the world's largest religion — who is he?
Jesus: First-century Jewish preacher and religious leader.
Married at St. Paul's Cathedral in July 1981, this royal became mother to two future princes and an international style icon — who was she?
Diana, Princess of Wales: Member of the British royal family (1961–1997)
Dubbed the 'Milwaukee Cannibal,' he killed and dismembered seventeen men and boys between 1978 and 1991 before being arrested — who is he?
Born at the Hofburg in Vienna as the fifteenth child of Empress Maria Theresa, she became Queen Consort of France through a marriage meant to cement a Franco-Austrian alliance — who was she?
Marie Antoinette: Queen of France from 1774 to 1792.
Born in June 1982 and heir apparent to the throne, he met his future wife while studying geography at St Andrews and later flew with an air ambulance service — who is he?
William, Prince of Wales: Heir apparent to the British throne (born 1982). William, Prince of Wales (William Arthur Philip Louis; born 21 June 1982), is the heir apparent to the British throne.
This Abrahamic faith's core texts — the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings — together form the Hebrew Bible, or Tanakh — which religion?
Judaism: Religion of the Jewish people.
Beginning after the Second World War and ending with the Soviet collapse in 1991, this rivalry never saw direct combat but did produce a Space Race — which conflict?
Cold War: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR.
Founded in 1982 by Lebanese clerics reacting to an Israeli invasion, and inspired by Iran's 1979 revolution, this Shia political-paramilitary movement's armed wing is the Jihad Council — which group?
Hezbollah: Islamist movement and militant group based in Lebanon.
Founded by a teacher who lived around the 5th century BCE in the eastern Gangetic plain, this religion teaches a path to nirvana by ending dukkha, or suffering. Which faith is it?

Born Middleton, she met her future husband while studying art history at St Andrews, married him at Westminster Abbey in 2011, and was diagnosed with cancer in early 2024. Who is this member of the British royal family?
Catherine, Princess of Wales: Member of the British royal family (born 1982). Born in Reading, Catherine grew up in Bucklebury, Berkshire.
Often called Sanatana Dharma, or 'eternal dharma,' this umbrella term covers a range of Indian traditions unified around scriptures like the Vedas and Upanishads. Which religion is this?
Hinduism: Range of Indian religious traditions. Vaidika Dharma (lit. 'Vedic dharma') and Arya Dharma are historical endonyms for Hinduism.

Founded by former Confederate soldiers during Reconstruction to oppose civil rights for the newly freed, this secret society is considered one of the earliest terrorist organizations in US history. Which group is this?
Ku Klux Klan: American white supremacist hate group.
Officially known as Ansar Allah, this Zaydi Shia movement emerged in Yemen in the 1990s and is now backed by Iran as part of the 'Axis of Resistance.' Which group is this?
Houthis: Shia Islamist organization in Yemen.
Also called the Decalogue, these covenant directives were given to Moses atop Mount Sinai and later smashed after he found the Israelites worshipping a golden calf. What are they?
Ten Commandments: Biblical principles relating to ethics and worship.
Ruling from Mount Olympus as king of the gods, this son of Cronus and Rhea fathered Athena, Apollo, and Heracles among many others. Who is this Greek deity?
Zeus: Greek god of the sky and king of the gods.
Spanning roughly the 5th to late 15th centuries, this era began with the fall of the Western Roman Empire and gave way to the Renaissance. Which historical period is this?
Middle Ages: European history from the 5th to 15th centuries.
Central to Christianity and Judaism, this anthology of sacred texts was written partly in Hebrew and partly in Koine Greek across its two major sections. Which scripture is this?
A former GRU lieutenant colonel whose military alias gave a Russian mercenary outfit its name, he died alongside Yevgeny Prigozhin in a 2023 plane crash. Who was he?
Hidden by his mother among the bulrushes of the Nile as a baby, this prophet grew up to lead the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt. Who is he?

Known as 'The Destroyer' within the Hindu trinity alongside Brahma and Vishnu, this deity is the Supreme Lord who creates, protects, and transforms the universe in one major tradition. Who is this god?
Shiva: Major deity in Hinduism. Shiva is one of the five equivalent deities in Panchayatana puja of the Smarta tradition of Hinduism.
This ancient Iranian faith centers on the Avesta and reveres Ahura Mazda as the supreme, uncreated deity, teaching a struggle between Asha (truth) and Druj (the lie). What religion is it?
Zoroastrianism: Iranian religion founded by Zoroaster.
Absent from the Hebrew Bible but appearing in the Dead Sea Scrolls and later Jewish folklore, this figure is said to have fled the Garden of Eden rather than submit to Adam. Who is she?
Lilith: Female entity in Near Eastern mythology.

Founded in Peshawar in 1988 by veterans of the Soviet–Afghan War including Osama bin Laden, this militant organization carried out the 1998 U.S. embassy bombings and the September 11 attacks. Which group?
Worshipped as the eighth avatar of Vishnu and central to the Mahabharata and Bhagavad Gita, this major Hindu deity's birthday is celebrated as Janmashtami. Who is he?
Krishna: Major deity in Hinduism. The anecdotes and narratives of Krishna's life are known as Krishna Lila.
Succeeding his father David as king of ancient Israel, this biblical ruler's wealth and foreign wives allegedly introduced idolatry, sowing the seeds for the kingdom's later split. Who is he?
Solomon: Biblical monarch of ancient Israel. The successor of his father David, he is described as the penultimate ruler of all Twelve Tribes of Israel under a united Israel and Judah.
Symbolized by seashells, myrtles, and doves, this Greek goddess of love and beauty was worshipped as a warrior at Sparta and syncretized with the Roman Venus. Who is she?
Aphrodite: Ancient Greek goddess of love. Aphrodite's major symbols include seashells, myrtles, roses, doves, sparrows, and swans.
Son of Zeus and twin brother of Artemis, this Greek god of prophecy, music, and healing was the patron deity of the Delphic Oracle. Who is he?
Apollo: Ancient Greek god. Apollo is one of the Olympian deities in ancient Greek religion and mythology.
Triggered by the 1929 Wall Street crash, this decade-long global economic downturn brought mass unemployment to the US, UK, and Germany — name the era?
Great Depression was a severe global economic downturn from 1929 to 1939.

Raiding, trading, and settling from Scandinavia across Europe, North Africa, and even Newfoundland between the late 8th and 11th centuries, this seafaring people helped establish Kievan Rus'. Who were they?
Vikings: Norse seafarers, merchants and raiders.

A Royal Navy helicopter pilot during the Falklands War and third child of Queen Elizabeth II, this former Duke of York married Sarah Ferguson in 1986 and stepped back from public roles amid scandal. Who is he?
Patron and namesake of Athens, this Greek goddess of wisdom and warfare is honored by the Parthenon and symbolized by owls and olive trees. Who is she?
Athena: Ancient Greek goddess. Athena was regarded as the patron and protectress of various cities across Greece, particularly the city of Athens, from which she most likely received her name.

Founded in 1885 as the first modern nationalist movement anywhere in the British Empire's Asian or African territories, this century-old big-tent party was later led by Mahatma Gandhi toward independence — which party?
Indian National Congress: Political party in India.
Considered the ideal man in Hindu tradition, this seventh avatar of the god Vishnu was born in Ayodhya to King Dasaratha and later married Sita — who is he?

Also known by the acronym Daesh, this jihadist militant group declared a worldwide caliphate in 2014 and at its peak controlled territory in Iraq and Syria home to about 12 million people — which organization?
Islamic State of Iraq and Sham
Islamic State in Iraq and Syria
Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant
Islamic State of Iraq and Syria
Islamic State of Iraq and Levant
Islamic State of Iraq and al-Sham
Islamic State: Salafi jihadist militant organisation.
Inspired by a 4th-century Greek bishop known for secret gift-giving, this white-bearded, red-suited figure is said to deliver presents by sleigh on Christmas Eve — who is he?

Santa Claus: Legendary Christmas figure. Santa Claus is a legendary figure originating in Western Christian culture who is said to bring gifts during the late evening and overnight hours on Christmas Eve.
Raised alongside his companion Patroclus and tutored by the centaur Chiron, this legendary warrior led the Myrmidons and slew Hector outside the gates of Troy — who is he?

Led by oligarch Yevgeny Prigozhin after months of feuding with Russia's defense minister over the war in Ukraine, this June 2023 uprising by a private military company ended a day later with Prigozhin standing down — what was it?
Wagner Group rebellion: 2023 Russian factional conflict.
Falling fifty days after Easter, this moveable Christian feast commemorates the Holy Spirit's descent upon the apostles and is called the 'Birthday of the Church' — what is it?
Pentecost: Christian feast celebrating the Holy Spirit's descent. The Monday after Pentecost is a legal holiday in many European, African and Caribbean countries.
Flourishing along the Tigris and Euphrates in southern Mesopotamia, this is considered the earliest known civilization, home to the world's oldest surviving texts from Uruk — what was it called?
Sumer: Ancient Mesopotamian civilization from 3300 to 1900 BC.
Born on Delos as the twin sister of Apollo, this Greek goddess presided over hunting, wild animals, and childbirth while herself remaining chaste — who is she?
Artemis: Ancient Greek goddess. In one account, Artemis is born first and then proceeds to assist Leto in the birth of the second twin, Apollo.
Son of Zeus and the nymph Maia, this winged-sandaled Greek god served as messenger to the gods and guide of souls to the afterlife — who is he?
Hermes: Ancient Greek deity and herald of the gods.
Honored in Gnostic texts as the 'apostle to the apostles,' this follower of Jesus witnessed both his crucifixion and resurrection — who was she?
Mary Magdalene: Saint and follower of Jesus. Mary Magdalene is regarded by believers as a historical figure, possibly from Magdala.
This gold-covered wooden chest, topped by the 'Seat of Mercy,' was said to house the Ten Commandment tablets, Aaron's rod, and a pot of manna — what relic was it?
Ark of the Covenant: Chest containing the Ten Commandments.
Eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, this Greek god drew the underworld as his domain after overthrowing the Titans alongside Zeus and Poseidon — who is he?
Hades: God of the underworld in Greek mythology. Hades was the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, although this also made him the last son to be regurgitated by his father.
Known as the 'earth shaker' in Bronze Age cult, this Greek god of the sea and horses could strike his trident to create springs — who is he?
Poseidon: Ancient Greek god of the sea, earthquakes, and horses.
Also known as Bacchus, this Greek god of wine, theatre, and ecstatic ritual madness carried a fennel-stem staff wound with ivy called a thyrsus — who is he?
Dionysus: Ancient Greek god of winemaking and wine.
Chaired by Mahmoud Abbas and the largest faction within a confederated Palestinian political organization, this party is also the second-largest in the Palestinian Legislative Council — which party?
Fatah: Palestinian political party. During the Second Intifada (2000–2005), Fatah intensified armed conflict against Israel, claiming responsibility for a number of suicide attacks.

Named for a Swiss castle built in the 1020s, this dynasty rose to power when descendant Rudolph was elected King of the Romans in 1273 and went on to rule both the Holy Roman Empire and Spain — which dynasty?
House of Habsburg: European dynastic family.

Emphasizing harmony with an enigmatic guiding force behind reality, this Chinese philosophical and religious tradition promotes effortless action, simplicity, and the three treasures of compassion, frugality, and humility — which tradition?
Taoism: Religious and philosophical tradition. Taoism or Daoism is a philosophical and religious tradition indigenous to China, emphasizing harmony with the Tao 道.

Identified chiefly by a shared family of Indo-European languages, this collection of ancient peoples included the Gauls, the Britons and Picts of Britain and Ireland, and the Galatians of Anatolia — who were they?
Celts: Collection of indo-European peoples sharing Celtic languages and cultural practices.

Nicknamed the 'Demon King of the Sixth Heaven,' this 16th-century samurai is regarded as the first of Japan's three great unifiers, paving the way for retainers Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu — who is he?
Oda Nobunaga: Japanese samurai and warlord (1534–1582)

Active along the Jordan River in the early first century AD and known in Islam as Yahya ibn Zakariya, this Jewish preacher is described as anticipating a messianic figure greater than himself — who is he?
John the Baptist: Prophet (6 BC – AD 30)

Known by hundreds of names stemming from a Proto-Germanic title meaning 'lord of frenzy,' this Norse deity's stories survive mainly through the 13th-century Prose Edda and the earlier Poetic Edda — which god?
Odin: Widely revered deity in Germanic mythology.
Later renamed Israel, this Hebrew patriarch tricked his aging father into blessing him instead of his twin brother Esau, and eventually followed his son Joseph's path into Egypt — who is he?
Jacob: Biblical patriarch, son of Isaac.
One of the Twelve Apostles, this figure betrayed Jesus to the Sanhedrin for thirty pieces of silver, identifying him with a kiss in the Garden of Gethsemane — who is he?
Judas Iscariot: Disciple and betrayer of Jesus.

After revealing Zeus's abduction of a nymph to a river god and later cheating death itself, this mythical king of Corinth was condemned to forever push a boulder up a hill, only to watch it roll back down — who is he?
Sisyphus: King of Ephyra in Greek mythology.
Also called Narayana and Hari, this Hindu deity known as 'The Preserver' forms one third of the Trimurti alongside Brahma and Shiva — who is he?
Commander of Iran's Quds Force from 1998 until his assassination by the United States in 2020, he was called the single most powerful operative in the Middle East — who was he?
This four-star general commanded the defense of Kyiv and led the 2022 Kharkiv counteroffensive before becoming commander-in-chief of Ukraine's armed forces in 2024 — who is he?
Bearing gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh after following a star, these visitors from the Gospel of Matthew are also known as the Three Wise Men — who were they?
Biblical Magi: Group of distinguished foreigners who visited Jesus after his birth.
Known informally as 'May' after her birth month, this queen consort served as Empress of India during the reign of her husband, George V — who was she?
Mary of Teck: Queen of the United Kingdom from 1910 to 1936.
Commanded by God to build an ark ahead of a great flood, this biblical patriarch later became the first person to cultivate a vineyard — who is he?
Noah: Biblical prophet known for building an ark.
Abducted by her uncle Hades and made queen of the underworld, this daughter of Zeus and Demeter personifies the return of spring each year — who is she?
Persephone: Greek goddess of spring and the queen of the underworld.
Named in the Book of Genesis as the first human being aware of God, he ate from a forbidden tree in the Garden of Eden, bringing sin into the world — who is he?
Adam: First man according to the Abrahamic creation myth.
Sold into slavery in Egypt by his jealous brothers, this favored son of Jacob rose to become Pharaoh's second-in-command after correctly interpreting his dreams — who is he?
Joseph (Genesis): Biblical figure, son of Jacob and Rachel.
The jealous wife and sister of Zeus, this queen of the Olympian gods presided over weddings and protected women in childbirth — who is she?
Hera: Goddess from Greek mythology, wife and sister of Zeus.
Led by their most famous king, Attila, this nomadic people swept out of Central Asia to carve a short-lived empire on Rome's Danubian frontier by 430 CE — who were they?
Huns: Extinct nomadic people in Eurasia (4th–6th centuries)
Son of Zeus and Hera and brother to strategy-minded Athena, which Olympian embodied war's raw brutality and bloodlust rather than tactics?
Ares: God of war in ancient Greek religion.

Reigning imperial dynasty of Russia from 1613 until 1917, this family rose to prominence when one of its women married Ivan the Terrible — which royal line ended with the 1918 execution of Nicholas II and his family?

House of Romanov: Imperial dynasty of Russia (1613–1917). Russian: Романовы, romanized: Romanovy, IPA: [rɐˈmanəvɨ]) is a royal house which was the reigning imperial house of Russia from 1613 until its deposition in 1917.
Revered as the Divine Mother and associated with time, death, and destruction, which Hindu goddess is the first of the ten Mahavidyas, the goddesses of liberating knowledge?
Kali: Major deity in Indian religions symbolizing power, time, and death.
The only mortal among three monstrous sisters, this snake-haired figure could turn onlookers to stone with a glance until the hero Perseus beheaded her and gave her head to Athena — who is she?
Guided by 24 tirthankaras who conquered the cycle of rebirth, this Indian religion built its entire ethical code on strict nonviolence to all living things — which faith?
Jainism: Indian religion. The community supported networks of temples, libraries, and charitable institutions.
This horned Alpine folklore figure accompanies Saint Nicholas each December, swatting badly behaved children with birch rods while good kids get small gifts — who is he?
Krampus: Christmas figure in Alpine folklore. In this tradition, Saint Nicholas rewards well-behaved children with small gifts, while Krampus punishes badly behaved ones with birch rods.
This American divorcée's romance with Britain's king forced his abdication in 1936 rather than let her become queen — who was she?
Wallis Simpson: Wife of Prince Edward, Duke of Windsor (1896–1986)
Composed in an archaic Sanskrit dialect, this collection of four ancient hymn texts forms the oldest layer of Hindu scripture — what are they collectively called?
Renowned for his cunning intelligence, this legendary king of Ithaca spent ten eventful years just trying to get home after the Trojan War — who is he?
Odysseus: Legendary Greek king of Ithaca. Odysseus also plays a key role in Homer's Iliad and other works in that same epic cycle.
Adopted in 1917 to shed a German-sounding surname amid wartime sentiment, this royal lineage has included five monarchs, from George V to Charles III — which royal family?
House of Windsor: British royal family. The House of Windsor is the current royal house of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms.
Possibly descended from Aegean migrants who settled Canaan's southern coast around 1175 BC, this Iron Age people organized their territory into a confederation of city-states — who were they?
Philistines: Ancient people who inhabited Canaan's southern coast.
Founded by Sun Yat-sen in Honolulu and later led to unify China under Chiang Kai-shek, this centre-right party ruled Taiwan under martial law until 1987 — which party?
Kuomintang: Political party in the Republic of China (Taiwan)
After overseeing construction of the Pentagon, this U.S. Army engineer directed the top-secret program that produced the atomic bomb — who is he?
Lieutenant General Leslie Richard Groves, Jr.
Flourishing in central Mexico from 1300 to 1521, this Nahuatl-speaking civilization built an empire through an alliance of three city-states including Tenochtitlan — who were they?
Aztecs: Ethnic group of central Mexico and its civilization.
Affectionately nicknamed 'Nessie,' this long-necked cryptid supposedly lurking in a Scottish Highlands lake shot to worldwide fame in 1933 — what is it?
Loch Ness Monster: Mythical creature in Scottish folklore.
Born into a powerful Florentine family, this queen of France mothered three future kings — Francis II, Charles IX, and Henry III — who is she?
Catherine de' Medici: Queen of France from 1547 to 1559.
Also called the Old Stone Age, this era of human prehistory stretched from the earliest known stone tools roughly 3.3 million years ago until about 11,650 years ago — which period is it?
Paleolithic: Prehistoric period, first part of the Stone Age.
Alongside Andrew Moray, this Scottish knight won the Battle of Stirling Bridge in 1297 before being captured and executed for treason in 1305 — who is he?
William Wallace: Scottish knight (1270–1305). Along with Andrew Moray, Wallace defeated an English army at the Battle of Stirling Bridge in September 1297.
A Thracian gladiator born near the Strymon river, this figure led an escaped-slave uprising against the Roman Republic known as the Third Servile War — who was he?
Spartacus: Thracian gladiator who led a slave revolt. Spartacus is described to be born near the Strymon river, in Thrace (now known as Bulgaria), possibly from the Maedi tribe.
Founded in Egypt in 1928 by schoolteacher Hassan al-Banna, this Sunni Islamist group preaches 'Islam is the solution' and seeks a caliphate under Sharia — what is it?
Muslim Brotherhood: Transnational Sunni Islamist organization.
Nicknamed 'The White Death,' this Finnish marksman is credited with over 500 kills during the 1939-40 Winter War against the Soviets — who was he?
Depicted as a falcon or as a man with a falcon's head, this Ancient Egyptian deity presided over kingship, healing and the sky — who is he?
Horus: Egyptian war and sky deity. Different forms of Horus are recorded in history, and these are treated as distinct gods by Egyptologists.
Stretching from humanity's first stone tools roughly 3.3 million years ago to the invention of writing about 5,200 years ago, this era comes before recorded history — what's it called?
Prehistory: Period of human history before records.
A 1st-century man of Nazareth married to Mary and regarded as the legal father of Jesus, he was later declared protector of the Catholic Church by Pope Pius IX — who was he?

Saint Joseph: Husband of Mary and legal father of Jesus. According to the canonical Gospels, Joseph was a 1st-century Jewish man of Nazareth who was married to Mary, the mother of Jesus, and was the legal father of Jesus.
Grandson of the Mongol Empire's founder, this ruler proclaimed the dynastic name 'Great Yuan' in 1271 and became the first emperor of a new Chinese dynasty — who was he?
Kublai Khan: Emperor of Yuan China from 1271 to 1294.

Said to be the most beautiful woman in the world and a daughter of Zeus, her elopement with a foreign prince triggered a legendary decade-long war after her first husband, the Spartan king, lost her — who was she?
Helen of Troy: Most beautiful woman in Greek mythology.
Used as a self-designation by ancient Indo-Iranian peoples, this term is the etymological root behind the country name Iran — what is it?
Aryan: Self-designation used by ancient Indo-Iranian peoples. Aryan, or Arya (borrowed from Sanskrit ārya), is a term originating from the ethno-cultural self-designation of the Indo-Iranians.
Emphasizing virtues like benevolence, righteousness and propriety, this Chinese school of thought emerged around 500 BCE from the teachings of a sage whose name it bears — what is it called?
Confucianism: Chinese ethical and philosophical system.
These horse-mounted nomads swept out of Central Asia to dominate the Pontic Steppe by the 8th century BC, later raiding West Asia after crossing the Caucasus — who were they?
Scythians: Nomadic Iranic people of the Pontic Steppe.
Emerging from indigenous Canaanite populations in the Iron Age, this Semitic-speaking people worshipped Yahweh and were later divided into Twelve Tribes — who were they?
Israelites: Hebrew ethno-religious group in Canaan during the Iron Age.
Also known as Calvinism, this 16th-century Protestant branch stresses biblical authority, God's sovereignty, and covenant theology as articulated by John Calvin — what movement is this?
Cast off Mount Olympus by his mother for his lameness, this Greek god of blacksmiths and fire is equated with Vulcan in Roman mythology — who is he?
Hephaestus: Greek god of blacksmiths. In Greek mythology, Hephaestus was the son of Hera, either on her own or by her husband Zeus.
Nicknamed after a judge was told to tremble before God's authority by their founder, members of this group call each other Friends and reject creeds and hierarchical structures — which movement?
Accused of torturing and murdering hundreds of young women between 1590 and 1610, this Hungarian noblewoman spent her final years imprisoned in a castle until her death in 1614 — who was she?
Elizabeth Báthory: Hungarian countess and suspected serial killer (1560–1614)
The Olympian goddess of harvest and agriculture, she was swallowed by her father Cronus as an infant and later became the mother of Persephone by Zeus — who is she?
Demeter: Greek goddess of the harvest, grains, and agriculture.

Refusing to carry a weapon because of his faith, this WWII combat medic saved an estimated 75 men during the Battle of Okinawa and became the first conscientious objector awarded the Medal of Honor — who was he, later portrayed by Andrew Garfield?
Desmond Doss: US soldier and Medal of Honor recipient (1919–2006)
The first son of Abraham, born to Sarah's handmaiden Hagar, this biblical figure is regarded in Islam as a prophet and ancestor of the Adnanite Arabs — who is he?
Ishmael: Figure in the Abrahamic religions.
Whose name means 'he will laugh,' this biblical patriarch was the son of Abraham and Sarah and the father of Jacob and Esau, living to age 180 — who was he?

Isaac: Biblical patriarch, son of Abraham and Sarah. Isaac first appears in the Torah, in which he is the son of Abraham and Sarah, the father of Jacob and Esau, and the grandfather of the twelve tribes of Israel.
This Easy Company paratrooper earned the Distinguished Service Cross for his assault on Brécourt Manor during D-Day, and was later played by Damian Lewis in a hit HBO miniseries — who was he?
Richard Winters: United States Army officer and veteran (1918–2011)
Named for a queen who reigned from 1837 until 1901, this period saw the Irish Famine and the Crimean War against Russia — what was it called?
Victorian era: Queen Victoria's reign, 1837 to 1901.

Spanning roughly 1418 to 1620, this period saw European seafarers open sea routes to the East Indies and colonize the Americas, laying the groundwork for today's interconnected global economy — what was it called?

Age of Discovery: Period of European global exploration. The Age of Discovery (c. 1418 – c. 1620), also known as the Age of Exploration, was part of the early modern period and overlapped with the Age of Sail.

Born in a refugee camp in Gaza, this militant commander led the armed wing of Hamas and was considered one of the masterminds of the October 7 attacks before being assassinated by Israel in July 2024 — who was he?

This Hebrew Bible prophet defended the worship of Yahweh against the cult of Baal, performed miracles including calling down fire from the sky, and is said to have ascended to heaven alive without dying — who was he?
Elijah: Biblical prophet. In 1 Kings 18, Elijah defended the worship of the Hebrew deity Yahweh over that of the Canaanite deity Baal.

This Norse goddess of love, beauty, and war rides a chariot pulled by cats, owns a cloak of falcon feathers, and claims half of the warriors who die in battle for her hall — the other half going to Odin — who is she?
Freyja: Norse goddess. Stemming from Old Norse Freyja, modern forms of the name include Freya, Freyia, and Freja.

Modeled on Greco-Roman biography and meaning 'good news' in Greek, this genre of narrative recounts the words, deeds, trial, death, and post-resurrection appearances of Jesus Christ — what is it called?
Gospel: Books on the life and teachings of Jesus Christ.

Appearing in the Hebrew Bible, New Testament, and Quran as either individuals, tribes, or lands, this apocalyptic pairing is prophesied to be defeated near the 'end of days,' ushering in the Messianic Age — who or what are they?
Gog and Magog: Pair of individuals, peoples, or lands in the Bible and the Quran.

The son of the labyrinth's architect, this figure from Greek myth escaped imprisonment on wings of feathers and wax, only to plunge into the sea after ignoring his father's warning not to fly too close to the sun — who was he?
Icarus: Greek mythological figure. Icarus and Daedalus escaped using wings Daedalus constructed from birds' molted feathers, threads from blankets, the leather straps from their sandals, and beeswax.

Often depicted holding twin torches and accompanied by dogs, this Greek goddess of crossroads, night, and magic first appears in Hesiod's 'Theogony' and was worshipped in Athens as a protector of the household — who is she?
Hecate: Greek goddess of magic and transitions. The earliest evidence for Hecate's cult comes from Selinunte, in Sicily.

Though this exact phrase never appears in Abrahamic scripture, it describes beings cast out of Heaven for sins like pride or lust, often blamed for corrupting humanity with forbidden knowledge — what are they called?
Fallen angel are angels who were expelled from Heaven.
Born in Samarra and once held at American-run Camp Bucca in 2004, this Iraqi militant leader proclaimed himself caliph of a self-styled Islamic state in 2014 before dying during a 2019 raid?
Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi: Leader of the Islamic State from 2013 to 2019.

This semi-nomadic Turkic people built a major trading empire from the 6th century CE, dominating the Volga-Don steppes, Crimea, and the Caucasus for roughly three centuries as a crossroads on the Silk Road?
Khazars: Historical semi-nomadic Turkic ethnic group.

Known as Bilqis in Arabic and Makeda in Ge'ez, this Hebrew Bible figure brought a caravan of lavish gifts to King Solomon and is linked by modern historians to an ancient South Arabian kingdom in Yemen?
Queen of Sheba: Historical figure in the Abrahamic religions.
Part man, part bull, this creature of Greek mythology dwelt at the center of a labyrinth designed by Daedalus and was ultimately slain by the Athenian hero Theseus?
This Nazirite judge of ancient Israel slew a lion with his bare hands and later routed a Philistine army using only a donkey's jawbone — who was he?
Samson: Important character from the book of judges of the Hebrew Bible.
In Norse belief, these female figures guide fallen warriors to Odin's hall, sometimes shown accompanied by ravens, swans, or wolves — what are they called?

Named in the Book of Leviticus and traditionally identified as a Canaanite deity linked to child sacrifice, some scholars have since argued the word actually just meant 'sacrifice' in a related ancient language — what is it?
Moloch: Canaanite deity or form of human sacrifice.

Founded by one of Alexander the Great's generals who declared himself pharaoh in 305 BC, this Macedonian Greek royal house ruled Egypt for 275 years until Rome absorbed it in 30 BC — which dynasty is it?

Ptolemaic dynasty: Macedonian Greek royal family which ruled Egypt. Reigning for 275 years, the Ptolemaic was the longest and last dynasty of ancient Egypt from 305 BC until its incorporation into the Roman Republic in 30 BC.

Founded in 1978 and waging an insurgency from strongholds in southeastern Turkey, northern Iraq, and Syria, this militant group shifted its 1990s goal from full independence to autonomy for its people within Turkey — which organization is it?
Kurdistan Workers' Party: Kurdish militant political organization.
This ten-headed demon king of Lanka abducted the hero's wife in an ancient Hindu epic and is now burned in effigy every year during a festival marking his defeat — who is he?
Ravana: Primary antagonist in the Hindu epic Ramayana.
Also known as the Baader-Meinhof Group, this West German far-left militant group waged a campaign of bombings, kidnappings, and shootouts with police from 1970 until 1998 — which organization is it?
Red Army Faction: West German far-left militant organisation (1970–1998). The RAF described itself as a communist and anti-imperialist urban guerrilla group.

Ushered in by a decisive 1600 battlefield victory and a shogun title granted by the emperor, this roughly 260-year era of Japanese history brought prolonged peace, strict social order, and a flourishing of arts under isolationist rule — which era is it?
Edo period: Japanese history from 1600 to 1868.

Believed to cause possession requiring an exorcism, this class of malevolent supernatural being has roots stretching back to the Paleolithic age and entered Jewish tradition via Zoroastrian influence during the Persian era — what is it?
Demon: Evil supernatural being. The original Ancient Greek word daimōn (δαίμων) did not carry negative connotations, as it denotes a spirit or divine power.

Tracing back to 1272 when a younger son of Saint Louis IX married into a French lordship, this royal dynasty later took thrones in Spain, Naples, Sicily, and Parma, and today still reigns in both Spain and Luxembourg — which dynasty is it?
House of Bourbon: Cadet branch of French Capetian dynasty.
According to legend, this mythical city of gold got its name from a Muisca king who covered himself in gold dust before diving into a sacred Andean lake — what is it?
El Dorado: Legendary city in South America.

Named after a 16th-century Frisian cleric, this Anabaptist Christian movement traces to the Radical Reformation and later codified beliefs like adult baptism and foot washing in its 1632 Dordrecht Confession — what is it called?
Mennonites: Anabaptist groups originating in Western Europe.
The second sultan of the Seljuk Empire, this ruler's decisive 1071 victory over the Byzantines at Manzikert opened Anatolia to Turkoman settlement — who is he?
Alp Arslan: Sultan of the Seljuk Empire from 1063 to 1072.
Described in Genesis as 'a mighty hunter before the Lord,' this great-grandson of Noah is linked by tradition to building the Tower of Babel and opposing Abraham — who is he?
Ruling from their capital at Hattusa, this Bronze Age Anatolian civilization reached its peak under Suppiluliuma I and clashed with Egypt's New Kingdom — which people were they?
Hittites: Ancient Anatolian people of Kussara.
Prophesied in the Book of Revelation as the gathering place for armies before the end times, this term is also called the Greatest War in Islamic Hadith — what is it?
This broad concept covers beliefs about consciousness continuing after death — from an eternal soul in a supernatural realm to being reincarnated with no memory of a past self — what is it called?
Afterlife: Postulated continued existence after death.
Introduced to the public in 1954 by a retired British civil servant, this modern pagan, Earth-focused religion blends ancient motifs with 20th-century hermetic ideas — which religion?
Wicca: Modern syncretic pagan religion. Wicca draws upon ancient pagan and 20th-century hermetic motifs for theological and ritual purposes.

This worldview holds that rivers, weather systems, and even inanimate objects can possess a spiritual essence or soul, and anthropologists use the term for many indigenous belief systems — what is it called?
This legendary Thracian musician could charm even stones with his lyre, sailed with Jason in search of the Golden Fleece, and journeyed into the underworld to reclaim his dead wife — who is he?
Orpheus: Legendary musician, poet, and prophet in Greek mythology.
Designated Crown Prince during his father's 1967 coronation, this dissident has lived in exile in the US since the 1979 revolution that abolished the monarchy his family once ruled — who is he?
Reza Pahlavi: Former Crown Prince of Iran (born 1960)
Henry VIII's marriage to his fourth wife lasted barely six months in 1540, doomed partly because a portrait by Hans Holbein flattered her more than reality did — who was she?
Anne of Cleves: Queen of England in 1540.
Lord of the desert and god of storms and chaos in ancient Egyptian religion, he murdered his own brother Osiris before being pursued for revenge by his nephew Horus — who is this god?
Set (deity): Egyptian god of the desert, storms, violence, and foreigners.
Born in Kraków, this lawyer-turned-politician pulled off a surprise upset to become Poland's president in 2015, narrowly winning the runoff with just over 51% of the vote — who is he?
Andrzej Duda: President of Poland from 2015 to 2025.
Elected in February 2023 with 54% of the vote, this politician became the first woman to lead Italy's Democratic Party — who is she?
After Rome ignored her husband's will and annexed their kingdom, this queen of the Iceni tribe led a failed revolt against Roman rule in Britain around AD 60 — who was she?
Boudica: Queen of the British Iceni tribe (d. 60/61)
In 2024, this longtime New Jersey senator became the first sitting member of Congress convicted of conspiracy to act as a foreign agent — who is he?
As third caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, this son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad ordered the standardized compilation of the Quran still used today — who was he?

After his father — a former Andhra Pradesh chief minister — died in a 2009 helicopter crash, this politician toured the state on a consoling 'Odarpu Yatra' before founding his own party and later becoming chief minister himself — who is he?

Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy: Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, India. Jagan Mohan Reddy started his political career in the Indian National Congress and was elected as the Member of Parliament of Kadapa in 2009.
Governing France from the fall of Napoleon III in 1870 until the Nazi invasion of 1940, this parliamentary system weathered the Paris Commune and the loss of Alsace-Lorraine — what was it?

French Third Republic: Government of France from 1870 to 1940. Consequently, the Third Republic, originally envisioned as a provisional government, instead became the permanent form of government of France.
Once an opponent of the Prophet Muhammad before becoming one of his scribes, this governor of Syria went on to found the Umayyad Caliphate as its first ruler in 661 — who was he?
Mu'awiya I: Founder of the Umayyad Caliphate. Mu'awiya I (c. 597, 603 or 605 – April 680) was the founder and first caliph of the Umayyad Caliphate, ruling from 661 until his death.

Known as the Risorgimento, this 19th-century movement folded numerous peninsular states into the Kingdom of Sardinia in 1861 and finished in 1871 when Rome became the new nation's capital — what was it?
Unification of Italy: 1848–1870 consolidation of Italian states.
Born in Kōbe, Japan and educated at Oberlin and Columbia, this politician served as Taiwan's de facto ambassador to the US before becoming the island's vice president in 2024 — who is she?
Hsiao Bi-khim: Vice President of the Republic of China since 2024 (born 1971)
Rebranded in 2013 from a company once called Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, this Paris-based luxury conglomerate owns Gucci, Balenciaga, and Alexander McQueen — which company?
Settled around 814 BC by merchants from the Phoenician city of Tyre, this North African civilization grew into a maritime empire dominating the western Mediterranean — what was it?
Ancient Carthage: Phoenician city-state. Ancient Carthage ( KAR-thij; Punic: 𐤒𐤓𐤕𐤟𐤇𐤃𐤔𐤕, lit. 'New City') was an ancient Semitic civilization based in North Africa.
He made his film debut as the boozy title character in a 1987 comedy, then decades later earned an Oscar nomination for playing Jack Hock in Can You Ever Forgive Me? — who is he?

Descended from a Welsh noble family and Catherine of Valois, this English and Welsh royal dynasty held the throne from 1485 to 1603 across five monarchs including Henry VIII and Elizabeth I — name the dynasty?
House of Tudor was an English and Welsh dynasty that held the throne of England from 1485 to 1603.
This giant Philistine warrior challenged the Israelites to single combat, only to be felled by a young shepherd's sling stone — who is he?
Goliath: Philistine giant in the Bible. According to 1 Samuel, Goliath challenges the Israelites to beat him in single combat.
He became king in 2013 when his father abdicated for health reasons, and his eldest daughter, Princess Elisabeth, is now first in line to succeed him — who is he?
Philippe of Belgium: King of the Belgians since 2013.
Said to have lived 969 years — the longest lifespan recorded in the Bible — this patriarch was the grandfather of Noah — who is he?
The 68th U.S. Secretary of State under Barack Obama, he later became the country's first special presidential envoy for climate and was the Democratic presidential nominee in 2004 — who is he?
John Kerry: American politician and diplomat (born 1943)
This Indian journalist and Lok Sabha MP published The National Herald newspaper; his wife and their elder son both later served as prime minister of India — who was he?
Feroze Gandhi: Indian independence activist, politician and journalist (1912 – 1960)

Serving as the eighth U.S. director of national intelligence starting in 2025, this former Hawaii congresswoman deployed to Iraq with the National Guard and later left the Democrats to become a Republican — who is she?
Tulsi Gabbard: American politician and military officer (born 1981)
This accountant-turned-politician served as governor of Lagos State before becoming Nigeria's 16th president in 2023, having earlier gone into exile under military ruler Sani Abacha — who is he?
Bola Tinubu: President of Nigeria since 2023. Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Adekunle Tinubu (born 29 March 1952) is a Nigerian politician serving as the 16th and current president of Nigeria since 2023.
Founded by Clovis I and later ruled by the Merovingian and Carolingian dynasties, this largest post-Roman kingdom in Western Europe evolved into an empire in the year 800 — what was it called?
This 13th-century marcher-lord, father of the man credited with founding the Ottoman dynasty, was granted the frontier town of Söğüt after serving the Sultanate of Rum — who was he?
Ertuğrul: Father of Osman I, died c. 1280.
Fought over about eleven days in the autumn of 1970, this conflict pitted King Hussein's Jordan against Yasser Arafat's PLO — what was this civil war called?
Black September: 1970–1971 conflict in Jordan. The main phase of the fighting took place between 16 and 27 September 1970, though certain aspects of the conflict continued until 17 July 1971.
Serving as his country's foreign minister since 2004 — longer than anyone since the Soviet era — this diplomat also speaks fluent Sinhala and Dhivehi from his early postings — who is he?
Rooted in a Sanskrit word meaning 'to hold or support,' this concept refers to one's moral duty and responsibility — a farmer's version differing from a soldier's — what's the term?
Dharma: Key concept in Indian philosophy and Eastern religions, with multiple meanings.
Serving as Governor of Jakarta before running for president in 2024, this Indonesian politician founded a program that sends university graduates to teach for a year nationwide — who is he?
According to Genesis, this patriarch lived 365 years before God 'took him' rather than let him die, and tradition credits him as author of an apocryphal book bearing his name — who is he?
Enoch: Biblical figure prior to Noah's flood.
Descended from the founder of the 18th-century Emirate of Diriyah and led today by the descendants of its modern founder, this is the ruling royal family of a Middle Eastern kingdom — which family?
Royal family of the Arabian Kingdom
House of Saud is the ruling royal family of Saudi Arabia.

Born in 1936, this British hereditary peer and investment banker was the eldest son of a peer of the same surname, educated at Eton College and Christ Church, Oxford, and left the family bank he'd joined after a 1980 dispute — who was he?
Jacob Rothschild, 4th Baron Rothschild: English peer, investment banker and philanthropist (1936–2024)
Centered on the island of Crete and famed for palaces at Knossos and Phaistos, this Bronze Age culture is often regarded as Europe's first great society — what was it?

Minoan civilization was a Bronze Age culture which was centered on the island of Crete. Known for its monumental architecture and energetic art, it is often regarded as the first civilization in Europe.
The younger brother of Austria's Emperor Franz Joseph I, this Habsburg archduke ruled as emperor of the Second Mexican Empire before his execution by the Mexican Republic in 1867 — who is he?

Maximilian I of Mexico (6 July 1832 - 19 June 1867) was an Austrian archduke who became emperor of the Second Mexican Empire from 10 April 1864 until his execution by the Mexican Republic on 19 June 1867.
Flying solo for over 33 hours in the Spirit of St. Louis, this aviator completed the first nonstop New York-to-Paris flight in 1927 to claim the Orteig Prize — who was he?
Elected to the Chamber of Deputies in the 2018 Italian general election, this politician represents the Forza Italia party — who is she?
As the 36th padishah, this monarch became the very last sultan of the Ottoman Empire, reigning through the chaotic aftermath of World War One until the sultanate's abolition in 1922 — who was he?
Mehmed VI: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1918 to 1922.
This British Conservative served as Leader of the House of Commons from 2022 to 2024, ran for party leadership against Liz Truss, and later lost her Portsmouth North seat in 2024 — who is she?

Having spent most of his career in his country's security and intelligence services, this Gulf monarch became ruler at age 83 in 2023, after previously holding the record as the world's oldest crown prince — who is he?
Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah: Emir of Kuwait since 2023.
Wounded in the Tunisian campaign, losing an eye and part of his hand, this German officer led the failed 1944 plot to assassinate Hitler at the Wolf's Lair — who was he?
Claus von Stauffenberg: German army officer (1907–1944)
As Adam and Eve's firstborn, this farmer grew jealous when God favored his brother's offering over his own, leading to history's first fratricide — who was he?
The longest-serving prime minister in Dutch history, this politician left The Hague in 2024 to become NATO's secretary general — who is he?

Mark Rutte: Secretary General of NATO since 2024. Mark Rutte (Dutch: [ˈmɑr(ə)k ˈrʏtə]; born 14 February 1967) is a Dutch politician who has served as the 14th secretary general of NATO since October 2024.

Crushed by Soviet tanks after just 15 days, this uprising began when university students rallied at the Parliament Building in Budapest, prompting nearly a quarter-million people to flee the country — which revolt?
Hungarian Revolution of 1956: Citizen rebellion in Hungary.
Serving two non-consecutive terms as Canada's 15th prime minister, this Quebec-born academic co-founded the journal Cité Libre before entering politics via the Liberal Party — who is he?
Pierre Trudeau: Prime Minister of Canada (1968–1979; 1980–1984)
First achieved in Australasia before spreading to Europe and the Americas, this democratic right for female voters began its 'first wave' in 1893 in English-speaking countries — what right?
Women's suffrage: Legal right of women to vote.
Granddaughter of the sun god Helios and niece of the enchantress Circe, this sorceress-priestess helped Jason secure the Golden Fleece before her myth turned dark — who is she?
Medea: Daughter of King Aeëtes of Colchis in Greek mythology.
Assassinated in 1961, this pan-Africanist served as the first prime minister of the newly independent Congo before the Congo Crisis erupted?
Patrice Lumumba: Congolese politician and independence leader (1925–1961)
Revered as the Father of the Nation, this ruler of Abu Dhabi became the first president of a newly unified Gulf federation in 1971?
Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan: President of the United Arab Emirates from 1971 to 2004.
This Roman goddess of love and beauty was claimed as an ancestor by Julius Caesar through her son Aeneas, survivor of the fall of Troy?
Venus (mythology): Ancient Roman goddess of love, sex and fertility.
This reclusive Afghan cleric has almost no digital footprint beyond two photographs and a few audio recordings, yet has led his country's ruling movement since 2016 — who is he?
Hibatullah Akhundzada: Supreme Leader of Afghanistan since 2021.
Author of the memoir 'I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings,' this poet and civil rights activist became the first Reynolds Professor of American Studies at Wake Forest University in 1982 — who is she?
Maya Angelou: American writer and activist (1928–2014)

After the French Army's defeat by Germany in the Franco-Prussian War, radicalized National Guard soldiers seized control of the French capital on 18 March 1871, killed two army generals, and governed for about two months — what was this revolutionary government called?
Serving as Argentina's Minister of Economy from 2022 to 2023, this politician had earlier been Chief of Cabinet under Cristina Fernández de Kirchner and twice mayor of Tigre — who is he?
Sergio Massa: Argentine politician and lawyer (born 1972)
The eldest son of Iraq's longtime dictator, this politician and militia leader was once seen as heir apparent before losing that role to his younger brother. Who is he?
Uday Hussein (18 June 1964 - 22 July 2003) was an Iraqi politician, militia leader, and businessman.
This Ottoman sultan ordered the execution of his brothers upon taking the throne in 1595 and led his army to victory at the Battle of Keresztes during the Long Turkish War — who is he?
Mehmed III: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1595 to 1603.

This Germanic people, first recorded by Greco-Roman writers in the 3rd century near the Lower Danube, played a major role in toppling the Western Roman Empire after being pushed west by the Huns — who were they?
Goths: Early Germanic people. The Goths were a Germanic people who played a major role in the fall of the Western Roman Empire and the emergence of medieval Europe.
This mythical creature combines a human head with a lion's body — in Greek myth she poses a fatal riddle to Oedipus, while in Egyptian tradition it's an unwinged, benevolent guardian — what is it?

Sphinx: Mythological creature with a human head and lion body. In Greek tradition, the sphinx is a treacherous and merciless being with the head of a woman, the haunches of a lion, and the wings of a bird.
The only known biological son of Julius Caesar, this last pharaoh of Ancient Egypt co-ruled with his mother Cleopatra VII before his execution by Octavian — who was he?
Caesarion: Pharaoh of Egypt from 44 to 30 BC.

This week-long 2010 search across Tyne and Wear and Northumberland for the fugitive Raoul Moat ended in his suicide near Rothbury after a six-hour standoff with armed officers — what is this event called?
2010 Northumbria Police manhunt was conducted across Tyne and Wear and Northumberland from 3 to 10 July 2010 with the objective of apprehending fugitive Raoul Moat.

Proclaimed by the Central Council after the October Revolution and formally independent from Russia by January 1918, what short-lived Eastern European state emerged from the collapsing Russian Empire?
Ukrainian People's Republic: 1917–18/1918–21 state in Eastern Europe.
After serving as mayor of Braddock, Pennsylvania and then the state's lieutenant governor, this politician became a U.S. senator from Pennsylvania in 2023 — who is he?
The third son of a former Tamil Nadu chief minister, this DMK leader served as mayor of Chennai before becoming the state's chief minister himself in 2021 — who is he?
Co-leading Germany's Greens alongside Annalena Baerbock, this politician served as Vice Chancellor and climate minister under Chancellor Olaf Scholz — who is he?
A transplant surgeon who pioneered ECMO use in Taiwan, this politician served as mayor of Taipei before founding the Taiwan People's Party in 2019 — who is he?
Ko Wen-je: Taiwanese physician and politician (born 1959)
This Sanskrit term for the ten primary incarnations of a principal Hindu god combines words meaning 'ten' and 'incarnation' — what is it called?
Dashavatara: Ten major avatars of the Hindu god Vishnu.
Trafalgar Square in London is dedicated to this Royal Navy admiral, whose unconventional tactics delivered decisive British victories during the Napoleonic Wars — who is he?
Horatio Nelson, 1st Viscount Nelson: Royal Navy officer (1758–1805)
Founded in 1905 by Arthur Griffith, this Irish party's members established the revolutionary First Dáil and fought in the War of Independence — which party?
Sinn Féin: Political party in Ireland.
Taking office at age 35, this president became his country's youngest elected leader after Ecuador's National Assembly was dissolved via a constitutional mechanism in 2023 — who is he?
Daniel Noboa: President of Ecuador since 2023. Before his political career, Noboa served in several positions at Noboa Corporation, an exporting business founded by his grandfather.
Founded in 312 BC by one of Alexander the Great's generals, this Hellenistic Greek state stretched from Anatolia to Afghanistan before Pompey folded it into Rome — which state was it?
Seleucid Empire: Hellenistic state in West Asia (312–63 BC)
Originating in Judaism, this Hebrew term for an anointed savior figure describes a future human leader descended from King David who will reunite the tribes of Israel — what is the title?
Messiah: Saviour or liberator of a group of people.
Its Sanskrit name evokes weaving or a loom, and this occult Hindu tradition views the body as divine, seeking the union of the god Shiva and his consort — what is it called?
Tantra: Esoteric traditions of Hinduism and Buddhism.
Ruling under martial law for nearly a decade, this Filipino dictator was ousted in the 1986 People Power Revolution and later succeeded by his predecessor's widow — who is he?
Ferdinand Marcos: President of the Philippines from 1965 to 1986.
Leader of Canada's Conservative Party and Official Opposition since 2022, this MP previously worked for Canadian Alliance leader Stockwell Day — who is he?
Auguste Comte pioneered this 19th-century philosophy holding that all genuine knowledge comes from logic and sensory experience, dismissing intuition and faith — what is it?
Dying just 31 days into office in 1841, this ninth U.S. president holds the record for shortest term ever served — who is he?
William Henry Harrison: President of the United States in 1841.
Shared across Jainism, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Sikhism, this state of liberation marks the end of the cycle of rebirth and the extinguishing of worldly passions — what is it?
Nirvana: Liberation from repeated rebirth in saṃsāra.
Built during Solomon's reign in the 10th century BCE and later rebuilt after the Babylonian exile, this sacred structure stood as the central place of Israelite worship in the Old City — what was it?
Temple in Jerusalem: Former places of Israelite and Jewish worship.
Ruled by dictator Mobutu Sese Seko from 1965 to 1997, this Central African nation was, by area, the continent's third-largest country after Sudan and Algeria — which country?
Zaire: Country in Central Africa (1965–1997). With a population of over 23 million, Zaire was the most populous Francophone country in Africa.
Convicted for a killing carried out as part of his uncle's Osage Indian murder ring, this man was pardoned by Oklahoma's governor decades later, in 1966 — who is he?
The first woman and first person of Jewish heritage to become Mexico's president, this energy scientist previously governed Mexico City — who is she?
Claudia Sheinbaum: President of Mexico since 2024.
The only sitting member of the U.S. House ever elected president, this 20th commander-in-chief died in 1881 after being shot just months into office — who is he?
James A. Garfield: President of the United States in 1881.
This Indonesian general became his country's second president in 1967, two years after his troops put down an attempted coup — who is he?
Suharto: President of Indonesia from 1967 to 1998.
Often depicted riding a lion or tiger with many arms, each wielding a weapon, this Hindu goddess embodies the triumph of good over evil — who is she?

Sparked partly by the Witwatersrand Gold Rush and the disenfranchised 'Uitlanders,' this turn-of-the-century conflict saw British garrisons besieged at Ladysmith, Mafeking, and Kimberley — which conflict?
Second Boer War: 1899–1902 war in South Africa.
Born a commoner named Diocles in Dalmatia, this Roman emperor rose through the military ranks to end the Crisis of the Third Century after his troops proclaimed him ruler in 284 — who was he?

Serving as Argentina's 38th vice president since 2023, this conservative politician founded a legal-studies center focused on terrorism victims and belongs to the La Libertad Avanza coalition — who is she?
Victoria Villarruel: Vice President of Argentina since 2023. Villarruel denies such accusations, maintaining that she does not support the "National Reorganization Process".
Nicknamed 'the Liberator' of three South American nations, this general led their independence struggle against the Spanish Empire and served as Protector of Peru — who was he?
José de San Martín: Argentine general and leader (1778–1850)
Forged by Joseph Stalin from Bolshevik roots, this ideology ruled the Soviet Union and still underpins the governments of China, Cuba, Laos, and Vietnam — what is it called?

Crowned king at birth after his father's death, this Spanish monarch reigned until the 1931 proclamation of the Second Republic and was nicknamed 'El Africano' for his colonial ambitions — who was he?
Alfonso XIII: King of Spain from 1886 to 1931.
A former co-owner of Talenti Gelato and Belvedere Vodka, this Minnesota congressman became the first Democrat to win his district in sixty years — who is he?
Dean Phillips: American businessman and politician (born 1969)

War on terror: Military campaign following the September 11 attacks.

Konrad Adenauer: Chancellor of West Germany from 1949 to 1963. Adenauer belied his age by his intense work habits and his uncanny political instinct.

Mentioned on the Merneptah Stele around 1208 BCE, these two neighboring Iron Age kingdoms in the Southern Levant were said to have once been united under kings Saul, David, and Solomon — what are they?
Ancient Israel and Judah: Near Eastern civilization during the Iron Age.
This Republican served as the 55th governor of New Jersey and later ran for his party's presidential nomination in both 2016 and 2024 — who is he?
Chris Christie: Governor of New Jersey from 2010 to 2018.

Hiroo Onoda: Imperial Japanese Army officer (1922–2014)

Robert Kiyosaki: American finance author and investor (born 1947)

Canonized as a saint by both the Catholic and Orthodox churches, this Rurik dynasty ruler seized Kiev with a Varangian army in 978 after his brothers' deadly feud — who is he?
Vladimir the Great: Grand Prince of Kiev from 978 to 1015.

Ayman al-Zawahiri: Egyptian Islamist militant and physician (1951–2022)

Papal States: Italian state ruled by the pope (756–1870)
Gored fatally by a wild boar, this mortal lover of Aphrodite had his blood mingle with her tears to create the anemone flower — who is he?
Adonis: Greek god of beauty and desire.
At 52, he became the youngest person to hold Vietnam's presidency since reunification, then resigned after just over a year amid an anti-corruption campaign — who is he?
Võ Văn Thưởng: President of Vietnam from 2023 to 2024.
Originally depicted as male in Indian Buddhism, this bodhisattva of compassion has been portrayed as female across East Asia since around the 12th century — who is this figure known as?
Guanyin: East Asian manifestation of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Begun when reformer Alexander Dubček became First Secretary in January 1968, this period of liberalization in Czechoslovakia ended with a Warsaw Pact invasion that August — what is it called?

Prague Spring: Liberalisation in Czechoslovakia in 1968. The Prague Spring (Czech: Pražské jaro; Slovak: Pražská jar) was a period of political liberalization and mass protest in 
the Czechoslovak Socialist Republic.
Founded in 2001 by brothers Jarosław and Lech Kaczyński, this Polish right-wing populist party won the 2005 presidential and parliamentary elections — which party?
Law and Justice: Right-wing and nationalist political party in Poland.
This strikingly beautiful hunter from Greek mythology, who spurned every admirer, wasted away staring at his own reflection in a pool and was transformed into a flower bearing his name — who is he?
Narcissus (mythology) (Ancient) is a hunter from Thespiae in Boeotia (alternatively Mimas or modern-day Karaburun, zmir), known for his beauty which was noticed by all.
Known by the honorific Bangabandhu, this founding president of Bangladesh was assassinated in a 1975 coup after leading the country since 1972 — who is he?
Sheikh Mujibur Rahman: Bangladeshi revolutionary and statesman (1920–1975)
Across religions this immortal, immaterial essence goes by many names — atman in Hinduism, jiva in Jainism, ruh in Islam — but what's its common English term?
Soul: In religion and philosophy, immaterial essence of a living being.

Sully Sullenberger: American pilot and diplomat (born 1951)

Theresa May: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 2016 to 2019.

Sino-Vietnamese War: War between China and Vietnam in 1979.
A protégé of the dictator Sulla, this Roman general and statesman celebrated three triumphs and was elected consul on three separate occasions during the late Republic — who was he?
Pompey: Roman general and statesman (106–48 BC)

Reign of Terror: 1793–1794 period of political violence during the French Revolution.

Rising from a royal concubine to regent of the Qing dynasty, this Manchu noblewoman effectively ruled China from 1861 until her death in 1908, at one point installing her own nephew on the throne — who was she?
Empress Dowager Cixi: Regent of China from 1861 to 1908. Cixi was selected as a concubine of the Xianfeng Emperor in her adolescence and gave birth to his son, Zaichun, in 1856.

Code-named Operation Typhoon by the Germans, this WWII campaign aimed to seize the Soviet capital between October 1941 and January 1942 but was ultimately repelled by its defenders — what was this campaign known as?
Battle of Moscow: World War II campaign in Russia.

Founded in 1206 in former Ghurid territory after Muhammad Ghori's rout of the Rajput Confederacy, this medieval Islamic empire ruled large swaths of the Indian subcontinent for three centuries — what was it called?
Delhi Sultanate: Late medieval empire in the Indian subcontinent (1206–1526)

Xiongnu: Eurasian steppe confederation and empire. Modu Chanyu, the supreme leader after 209 BC, founded the Xiongnu Empire.

Through his marriage to Ivanka Trump, this real-estate investor became a senior figure in both Trump administrations after taking over his family's property business and buying a New York newspaper — who is he?
Popularly known by his initials, this politician served as Telangana's first Chief Minister for nearly a decade and founded the regional party Bharat Rashtra Samithi — who is he?
K. Chandrashekar Rao: 1st chief Minister of Telangana from 2014 to 2023.
Fought from 1700 to 1721, this conflict saw a Russia-led coalition break Sweden's dominance over Central and Eastern Europe, turning decisively at the Battle of Poltava — which conflict?
Dictating an account titled 'A Gift to Those Who Contemplate the Wonders of Cities,' this 14th-century Tangier-born traveler covered roughly 117,000 km — more than Marco Polo or Zheng He — who is he?
Ibn Battuta: Maghrebi traveller and scholar (1304–1368/1369)

Storming of the Bastille: Major event of the French Revolution.
Daughter of the sun god Helios, this Greek mythological sorceress turned Odysseus's crew into swine on her island of Aeaea — who is she?
This biblical figure fled the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah with his family, though his wife looked back and turned into a pillar of salt — who is he?
Lot (biblical person): Lot (Hebrew: לוֹט Lōṭ, lit.
Before serving as President of France from 2012 to 2017, this French politician led the Socialist Party and served as mayor of the town of Tulle — who is he?
François Hollande (born 12 August 1954) is a French politician who served as President of France from 2012 to 2017.
The longest-serving chief minister in his Indian state's history, this politician co-founded a socialist party in 1994 alongside George Fernandes — who is he?
Spanning from Homer's earliest epic poetry to the fall of the Western Roman Empire in 476 AD, this era encompasses the interwoven Greco-Roman world — which historical period?
Classical antiquity: Age of the ancient Greeks and Romans.
Originating in the French county of Anjou, this royal dynasty held the English throne from Henry II's accession in 1154 until Richard III's death in battle in 1485 — which dynasty?
House of Plantagenet: Angevin royal dynasty that ruled England in the Middle Ages.
Adopting the pseudonym 'Alexander Supertramp,' this adventurer hitchhiked to Alaska in 1992 and took shelter in an abandoned bus before dying of starvation — who is he?
Chris McCandless: American hiker and explorer (1968–1992)
This Sanskrit term, meaning 'wandering' or 'running around in circles,' describes the ongoing cycle of life, death, and rebirth central to Indian religious philosophy — what is it called?
Saṃsāra: Indian concept of the cyclical process of death and rebirth.
Known for commanding an elite unit called the Red Guards, this samurai general served Tokugawa Ieyasu as one of the Four Guardians of the Tokugawa — who is he?
Ii Naomasa: Japanese samurai general and daimyō (1561–1602)
Nicknamed 'the Magnificent,' this unofficial ruler of the Florentine Republic patronized Botticelli and Michelangelo and survived a plot known as the Pazzi conspiracy in 1478 — who is he?
Lorenzo de' Medici: Lord of Florence from 1469 to 1492.
Indonesia's first and only female president, she took office in 2001 after her predecessor's impeachment and is the eldest daughter of the nation's founding president — who is she?
Megawati Sukarnoputri: President of Indonesia from 2001 to 2004.
