Jacques Cousteau: French oceanographer and author (1910–1997)
Firstborn child of Cronus and Rhea, this virgin goddess of the hearth chose never to marry despite her status among the Twelve Olympians — who is she?
Hestia: Greek goddess of the hearth. In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Hestia (Ancient Greek: Ἑστία, lit. 'hearth, fireplace, altar') is the virgin goddess of the hearth and the home.
This Cuban revolutionary succeeded his brother as president in 2008 and served as the country's defense minister for nearly five decades — who is he?
Raúl Castro: President of Cuba from 2008 to 2018.
This politician became the first female governor of South Dakota before later serving as U.S. secretary of homeland security — who is she?
At just 33, this Marxist revolutionary became president after a coup staged on his behalf, then launched sweeping reforms he called the people's democratic revolution — who is he?
Thomas Sankara: President of Burkina Faso from 1983 to 1987.
This Macedonian Greek general, one of Alexander the Great's most trusted companions, retrieved his leader's body after his death and founded a new ruling dynasty in Egypt — who is he?
Ptolemy I Soter: Pharaoh of Egypt from 305 to 282 BC.
Nicknamed 'the Mad' by his opponents, though historians debate whether he was simply incompetent rather than insane, this son of Ahmed I ruled the Ottoman Empire from 1640 to 1648 — who is he?
Ibrahim (Ottoman sultan) (13 October 1617 - 18 August 1648) was the sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1640 until 1648.
Which Japanese statesman brought his family clan's control over the country's politics to its historic peak?

Fujiwara no Michinaga: Japanese statesman. Fujiwara no Michinaga (藤原 道長; Japanese pronunciation: [ɸɯ.(d)ʑi.wa.ɾa no (|) mʲi.tɕiꜜ.na.ɡa, -mʲi.tɕi.na.ɡa, -na.ŋa], 966 – 3 January 1028) was a Japanese statesman.
Which Pakistani leader became the first woman to head a democratic government in a Muslim-majority nation, serving two terms as prime minister before her assassination in 2007?
Benazir Bhutto: Prime Minister of Pakistan (1988–1990; 1993–1996)
Considered the third person of the Trinity in Nicene Christianity, which concept represents God's animating presence across the Abrahamic faiths?
Holy Spirit: Religious concept with varied meanings.

A labour lawyer and longtime Communist Party member, which Spanish politician founded the left-wing alliance Sumar and serves as Second Deputy Prime Minister?
Yolanda Díaz: Spanish politician and lawyer (born 1971)
Fulfilling a prophecy despite his father's attempt to thwart it, which mythical king of Thebes unwittingly killed his father and married his mother?
Oedipus: Mythical Greek king of Thebes. Oedipus (UK:, also US:; Ancient Greek: Οἰδίπους Oidípous, lit. 'swollen foot') was a mythical Greek king of Thebes.
The son of a former Greek prime minister himself, who has led Greece's centre-right governing party since 2016 and served as PM since 2019?
Kyriakos Mitsotakis: Prime Minister of Greece (2019–2023; since 2023). Mitsotakis has been president of the New Democracy party since 2016.
Growing out of Lübeck in the late 12th century, which medieval trading network eventually spanned nearly 200 towns from Estonia to the Netherlands?
Hanseatic League: 1200s–1669 trade confederation in Northern Europe.
This Polish politician co-founded a conservative party with his twin brother in 2001 and served as Prime Minister of Poland from 2006 to 2007 — who is he?
Jarosław Kaczyński: Prime Minister of Poland from 2006 to 2007. Jarosław Aleksander Kaczyński (born 18 June 1949) is a Polish politician.
This Germanic people had a semi-legendary hero named Widukind who fought against Charlemagne's Frankish forces — who were they?
Saxons: Medieval cultural group from what is now Northern Germany.

Purgatory: Religious belief of Christianity, primarily Catholicism.

Condoleezza Rice: American diplomat and political scientist (born 1954)
This Ukrainian-born Russian military blogger and convicted bank robber, who became a pro-war propagandist, was assassinated in a Saint Petersburg bombing in April 2023 — who was he?

The longest-serving member of any democratic German parliament, this CDU politician served as president of the Bundestag from 2017 to 2021 — who was he?

Combining Sanskrit words for 'five' and 'principles,' this state ideology of Indonesia rests on tenets including belief in one god and social justice for all — what is it called?

L. K. Advani (born 8 November 1927) is an Indian lawyer, journalist, politician and statesman who served as the 7th Deputy Prime Minister of India from 2002 to 2004.
Serving as ealdorman of Northumbria from 1006 until his assassination in 1016, this ruler's death sparked a blood feud with Thurbrand the Hold — who was he?
Established as a federal holiday in 1894 and celebrated on the first Monday of September, this U.S. observance honors the contributions of American workers — which holiday?
Labor Day: Federal holiday in the United States.
This protagonist of German legend strikes a deal with the Devil at a crossroads, trading his soul for limitless knowledge and pleasure — who is he?
Faust: Protagonist of a classic German legend. Faust ( FOWST; German: [faʊst]) is the protagonist of a classic German legend based on the historical Johann Georg Faust (c. 1480–1540).
Founded in 1973 by Menachem Begin and Ariel Sharon, this party's 1977 landslide marked the first time Israel's political left lost power. Which party?
The first of the Twelve Apostles to be martyred, this saint is the patron of Spain, with relics enshrined at Santiago de Compostela. Who was he?
James the Great: Apostle of Jesus (died 44)
Deported to Auschwitz as a teenager, she later championed France's 1975 law legalizing abortion and became the first woman to lead the European Parliament. Who was she?

Konstantin Chernenko: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1984 to 1985. After Brezhnev took over as First Secretary of the CPSU in 1964, Chernenko was appointed to head the General Department of the Central Committee.
This philosophy and practice rejects treating animals as commodities, leading its followers to abstain from all animal-derived food, clothing, and entertainment. What is it?

Nicknamed the 'Russian Bear,' this Greco-Roman wrestler won gold at three straight Olympics under three different flags before a controversial single-point loss ended his win streak at 887-2. Who is he?
Aleksandr Karelin: Russian wrestler and politician. Karelin competed in Greco-Roman wrestling, representing the Soviet Union and Russia between 1986 and 2000.
Once an actor who ran the film company Red Giant Movies, he served as Tamil Nadu's Deputy Chief Minister from 2024 to 2026 before becoming the state's Opposition Leader. Who is he?
Udhayanidhi Stalin: Indian politician and former actor.
Cursed by Apollo to speak true prophecies that no one would ever believe, this Trojan priestess survived the fall of Troy only to be murdered alongside Agamemnon. Who was she?
Cassandra: Mythological prophetess and princess of Troy.
First named in the third century AD near the lower Rhine, this confederation of Germanic tribes eventually gave much of western Europe its medieval identity — who were they?
Franks: Germanic people from the Lower Rhine.
A former EU-affairs researcher who became Finland's prime minister in 2014, this politician has served as the country's president since 2024 — who is he?
Alexander Stubb: President of Finland since 2024. Cai-Göran Alexander Stubb (born 1 April 1968) is a Finnish politician serving as the president of Finland since 2024.
Known in Hebrew as 'praises,' this anthology of 150 religious hymns is divided into five sections each closing with a doxology — which book of the Bible is it?
Psalms: Book of sacred songs in the Hebrew Bible.
Crowned King of Prussia in 1861, this Hohenzollern monarch became the first emperor of a unified Germany a decade later — who was he?
Wilhelm I: German Emperor from 1871 to 1888.
The first Englishman to complete a circumnavigation of the globe, this privateer later served as vice admiral against the Spanish Armada in 1588 — who was he?
Francis Drake: English sailor and privateer (c. 1540–1596)
Elected as a moderate Republican in 2014, this New York congresswoman later chaired the House Republican Conference and grilled university presidents in a viral 2023 hearing — who is she?
In Greek myth, this first human woman was fashioned by Hephaestus at Zeus's command and later opened a jar that unleashed evil upon the world — who was she?
Fought mainly for influence over Korea and ending with the Treaty of Shimonoseki in 1895, this conflict pitted the Qing dynasty against the Empire of Japan — what was this conflict called?
First Sino-Japanese War: 1894–1895 war between China and Japan.
The longest-serving president in his country's republican history, this Italian statesman has held office since 2015 and helped found the Democratic Party in 2007 — who is he?
Sergio Mattarella: President of Italy since 2015. Sergio Mattarella (born 23 July 1941) is an Italian politician who has been serving as the president of Italy since 2015.
Known by the kunya Abu Idris, this Chechen guerrilla commander helped recapture Grozny in 1996 and later masterminded some of Russia's worst hostage-taking attacks — who is he?
Derived from the Greek word for 'last,' this branch of theology studies beliefs about the end of the world, judgment, and final redemption across religious traditions — what's the term?
Eschatology: Conceptions of the end of the present age.
By 1440 this Baltic-founded state was the largest in Europe, stretching from the Baltic Sea to the Black Sea before it was dissolved in the 1795 partitions — what state was it?
Grand Duchy of Lithuania: European state (c. 1236–1795)
In Greek myth, this goddess personified divine retribution for the sin of hubris, and was also known as the goddess of Rhamnous — who is she?
Nemesis: Goddess of retribution in Greek mythology.
Born after his brother Abel was murdered by their brother Cain, this third son of Adam and Eve was believed by his mother to be sent by God as a replacement — who is he?
Seth: Third son of Adam and Eve. The Hebrew Bible names two of his siblings as Cain and Abel.
Her name means 'living one' or 'source of life,' and some scholars link it to an Aramaic word for snake — who was the first woman in the Book of Genesis?
Eve: First woman according to the Abrahamic creation myth.
This Indian politician served four terms as Chief Minister of Maharashtra and founded a new party in 1999 after splitting from the Indian National Congress — who is he?
Sharad Pawar: Indian politician. Sharadchandra Govindrao Pawar (born 12 December 1940) is an Indian politician who has served as a Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha since 2014.
This German field marshal surrendered his 6th Army after Soviet forces encircled it at the Battle of Stalingrad, a defeat that led to the death or capture of roughly 265,000 troops — who was he?
Known until 2003 as the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, this Balkan union dissolved in 2006 when its junior partner voted for independence — which two-republic state?
Serbia and Montenegro: Country in Southeast Europe (1992–2006)
Cao Wei, Shu Han and Eastern Wu carved up China between 220 and 280 AD after the collapse of the Han dynasty — what is this era called?
Three Kingdoms: Period of Chinese history from 220 to 280 CE.
Leading Russia's Liberal Democratic Party from 1992 until his death in 2022, this firebrand ran in nearly every presidential election and openly called for military action against NATO — who is he?
An electrician by trade at the Gdańsk shipyard, this Nobel Peace Prize laureate led the Solidarity movement that helped end Communist rule in Poland and later became president — who is he?
Lech Wałęsa: President of Poland from 1990 to 1995.
Leading a far-right party called 'Jewish Power,' this Israeli lawyer has served as minister of national security since 2022 despite a long history of convictions for incitement to racism — who is he?
Itamar Ben-Gvir: Israeli far-right politician and lawyer (born 1976)
Deposed in a 2017 coup after ruling Zimbabwe for 37 years as both prime minister and president, who was this revolutionary-turned-leader?
Robert Mugabe: Leader of Zimbabwe from 1980 to 2017.
Second in line to the throne at birth and later a three-time Olympic sailor, who has reigned as monarch of Norway since 1991?
Harald V: King of Norway since 1991. A member of the House of Glücksburg, Harald was the third child and only son of King Olav V of Norway and Princess Märtha of Sweden.
Widely considered the greatest mountaineer ever, who made the first solo ascent of Everest and was the first to climb all fourteen eight-thousanders without supplemental oxygen?
Reinhold Messner: Italian mountaineer, adventurer and explorer (born 1944)
Colombia's first left-wing president, he joined a guerrilla movement at just 17 before later founding a party called the Historic Pact — who is he?
Gustavo Petro: President of Colombia since 2022.

Akkadian Empire: State in Mesopotamia (c. 2334–2154 BC)

Benito Juárez: President of Mexico from 1858 to 1872.
In Greek mythology, this king of Mycenae commanded the Achaean forces at Troy and was killed by his own wife upon returning home — who is he?

Madame de Pompadour: Chief mistress of Louis XV (1721–1764)
Traditionally chanted by a muezzin from a mosque's minaret before each of the five daily prayers, what is this Islamic call known as?
Adhan: Islamic call to prayer. The five prayer times are known in Arabic as fajr (فجر), dhuhr (ظهر), asr (عصر), maghrib (مغرب), and isha (عشاء).
Fought in two stages, a winter and summer campaign from 1614 to 1615, this conflict ended the Toyotomi clan and cemented Tokugawa rule over Japan — which historic clash?
Siege of Osaka: 1614-15 series of battles in Japan at the end of the Sengoku Period.
Hailed by the historian Thucydides as 'the first citizen of Athens,' this statesman transformed the Delian League into an Athenian empire during the city's Golden Age — who is he?
As Abu Dhabi's ruler from 2004, this leader helped bring the Louvre, a New York University campus, and Etihad Airways to the emirate — who was he?
Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan: President of the United Arab Emirates from 2004 to 2022.
This half-goat, half-human deity of the wild, shepherds, and rustic music was often identified with Rome's Faunus and later became a favorite symbol of the Romantic movement — who is he?
Pan (god): Ancient Greek god of the wilds, shepherds, and flocks.
Consisting of right view, right speech, and six other 'right' practices, this early Buddhist teaching charts the way toward liberation from the cycle of rebirth — what is it called?
Noble Eightfold Path: Buddhist practices leading to liberation from saṃsāra.
Son of Mehmed III and Halime Sultan, this Ottoman ruler held the throne twice, briefly in 1617–1618 and again in 1622–1623 — who was he?
Mustafa I: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire (r. 1617–1618, 1622–1623)

A former financial analyst for Merrill Lynch subsidiaries, this Taiwanese politician became a Legislative Yuan member in 2022 and ran as Ko Wen-je's vice-presidential running mate in the 2024 Taiwanese presidential election — who is she?
Cynthia Wu: Taiwanese business executive and politician.
Known by many names including Skanda and Muruga, this Hindu god of war is the son of Shiva and Parvati and the brother of Ganesha — who is he?
Kartikeya: Hindu god of victory and war. Kartikeya (IAST: Kārttikeya), also known as Skanda, Subrahmanya, Shanmukha or Muruga(n), is the Hindu god of war.
Crushed by the Albigensian Crusade and the Medieval Inquisition by 1350, this dualist Christian movement believed in two opposing gods — what was it called?
Catharism: Medieval southern European Christian dualist movement.
Ascending the Danish throne when his mother abdicated in January 2024, this king first met his future queen, an Australian marketing consultant, at the 2000 Sydney Olympics — who is he?
Frederik X: King of Denmark since 2024.
Sanskrit for 'circle,' this geometric configuration of symbols is used across Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, and Shinto traditions to aid meditation and represent sacred space — what is it?
Mandala: Spiritual and ritual symbol in Hinduism, Jainism and Buddhism.
As France's Minister of Justice, this lawyer and politician abolished capital punishment there in 1981 under President Mitterrand — who is he?
Robert Badinter: French politician, lawyer and author (1928–2024)
As the first Premier of the People's Republic of China, he helped orchestrate Richard Nixon's landmark 1972 visit while also serving as foreign minister during the 1950s — who is he?
Zhou Enlai: Premier of China from 1949 to 1976.
Born in the Mexican state of Morelos, this guerrilla leader championed land reform for peasants during the 1910-1920 revolution against dictator Porfirio Díaz — who is he?
Irish premier from a multiracial family — his father was a doctor born in Mumbai — he championed referendums legalizing same-sex marriage and liberalizing abortion law — who is he?
Formed in 1428 as an alliance of three Nahua city-states ruling the Valley of Mexico, this civilization fell to Hernán Cortés and his allies in 1521 — what was it?
Aztec Empire: Alliance of three Nahua city states in Mexico (1428–1521). Its people and civil society are historiographically referred to as the Aztecs or the Culhua-Mexica.
Alongside Tenzing Norgay, this New Zealand mountaineer became one of the first two people confirmed to reach the top of Mount Everest, on 29 May 1953 — who is he?

In 1999, she became the first woman to graduate from a South Carolina military college's Corps of Cadets program, then went on to become the state's first Republican woman elected to Congress — who is she?
An economist educated at Cambridge, he served as Singapore's Deputy Prime Minister and central bank chairman before becoming the country's ninth president in 2023 — who is he?

Tharman Shanmugaratnam: President of Singapore since 2023. Tharman Shanmugaratnam (born 25 February 1957) is a Singaporean politician and economist who has served as the ninth president of Singapore since 2023.

Spanning from the end of the Franco-Prussian War in 1871 to the outbreak of World War I, this era of French optimism, prosperity, and flourishing Parisian arts was named in retrospect as a golden age. What's it called?
Belle Époque: Period in European history, 1871–1914.

Elected vice president on the 1840 Whig ticket, this man became the tenth U.S. president just 31 days into his running mate's term after his sudden death — leaving him estranged from both major parties. Who was he?
John Tyler: President of the United States from 1841 to 1845.
Known as 'Mr. Titanic' for his deep-sea expertise, this French explorer was among the five people killed when a submersible imploded near the famous wreck in June 2023 — who was he?
Paul-Henri Nargeolet: French naval officer and explorer (1946–2023)

Depicted in reliefs at Ramesses III's mortuary temple, this mysterious maritime confederation was long blamed for Late Bronze Age raids on Egypt around 1200 BC, though scholars now see them more as a symptom of the era's collapse than its cause. Who were they?
Sea Peoples: Purported ancient tribal confederation of the Late Bronze Age.

Briefly the Soviet Union's top leader after Stalin's death in March 1953, this politician lost a power struggle with Nikita Khrushchev and was stripped of his Central Committee seat by 1957. Who was he?
Georgy Malenkov: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1953 to 1955.
Crowned Holy Roman Emperor in 1155, this ruler earned a nickname meaning 'Red Beard' from Florentines more than a century after his death — who was he?
Frederick Barbarossa: Holy Roman Emperor from 1155 to 1190. Frederick, therefore, descended from the two leading families in Germany, making him an acceptable choice for the Empire's prince-electors.

Set to become just the fourth queen to rule her Scandinavian kingdom in her own right — and the first since 1720 — she is heir apparent thanks to a 1980 law that was Western Europe's first with absolute primogeniture. Who is she?
Victoria, Crown Princess of Sweden: Heir apparent to the Swedish throne (born 1977)
This prince of Troy, also called Alexander, ran off with Helen and sparked a decade-long war, then later fired the arrow that killed the mighty warrior Achilles — who is he?
Paris (mythology): Trojan prince, second husband of Helen of Troy.
This South Korean general seized power after the 1979 assassination of the country's previous dictator, then declared martial law and became the nation's fifth president — who is he?
Chun Doo-hwan: Leader of South Korea from 1979 to 1988.

Sparked when Qing officials seized British merchants' stockpiles of a profitable but banned drug at Canton, this 1839-1842 conflict — also called the Anglo-Chinese clash — ended with a technologically superior Royal Navy defeating Chinese forces. What conflict is it?
First Opium War: 1839–1842 war between the United Kingdom and China.
This 8th-century BC Israelite prophet lends his name to a 66-chapter biblical book traditionally believed to have been written across two periods some 15 years apart — who is he?
Isaiah: Israelite prophet. The text of the Book of Isaiah refers to Isaiah as "the prophet", but the exact relationship between the Book of Isaiah and the actual prophet Isaiah is complicated.
The most frequently mentioned deity in the Rigveda, this Vedic god of storms and the sky slew a great asura named Vritra to bring rain to humankind — who is he?
Indra: Hindu god of rain, lightning, storm and weather.
Twice queen consort of England as the wife of Edward IV, this key Wars of the Roses figure was first married to a Lancastrian supporter who died at the Second Battle of St Albans — who is she?

As the 35th White House press secretary, this spokesperson became the first Black person and the first openly LGBTQ person to hold the role, having previously served as chief of staff for Kamala Harris's 2020 vice-presidential campaign — who is she?

This Chinese warlord, statesman, and poet seized effective control of a crumbling dynasty's government, laying the groundwork for a state his son would found once the old dynasty finally fell — who is he?
Cao Cao: Chinese warlord and statesman (155–220)
Married to the youngest sibling of King Charles III since 1999, this member of the British royal family previously worked in public relations before her wedding at Windsor Castle — who is she?
Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh: Member of the British royal family (born 1965)
Serving as the 41st U.S. vice president under Gerald Ford, this wealthy New York governor previously held posts under three earlier presidents dating back to the 1940s — who is he?
Nelson Rockefeller: Vice President of the United States from 1974 to 1977.
The eldest son of Singapore's founding prime minister, this former military officer served as Singapore's third prime minister for two decades before becoming Senior Minister in 2024 — who is he?
Lee Hsien Loong: Prime Minister of Singapore from 2004 to 2024, Senior Minister of Singapore since 2024.
This German cobbler founded Adidas after a bitter post-war feud with his brother, who started the rival Puma — who is he?

This Pennsylvania state treasurer, convicted of accepting a bribe in a state tax-processing scandal, shocked the nation by taking his own life live on camera during a 1987 press conference — who was he?
R. Budd Dwyer (November 21, 1939 - January 22, 1987) was an American politician who served as the 70th treasurer of Pennsylvania from 1981 until his suicide in 1987.

This 19th-century South American conflict was the deadliest interstate struggle in Latin American history, pitting one nation against an allied trio of neighboring countries from 1864 to 1870 — which conflict?
Paraguayan War: Major international war in South America (1864–1870)
This legendary king of Phrygia was said to turn everything he touched into gold — who was he?
Midas: Phrygian royals, including mythical king with golden touch.
Sent to the Ottoman court as a hostage before deserting to lead a league of Albanian noblemen against his former masters, he's remembered as Albania's national hero — who is he?
Skanderbeg: Albanian warlord and military commander (1405–1468)
Led first by Alaric I, this Gothic people sacked Rome in 410 before founding a kingdom centered on Toulouse and later Spain — who were they?
Visigoths: Germanic people of late antiquity and the early Middle Ages.

Serving as the 15th U.S. president from 1857 to 1861 after previously working as secretary of state and minister to Russia, he was a vocal advocate for states' rights before the Civil War — who is he?

James Buchanan: President of the United States from 1857 to 1861. James Buchanan Jr. (bew-KAN-ən; April 23, 1791 – June 1, 1868) was the 15th president of the United States, serving from 1857 to 1861.
This Indian politician has served as finance minister since 2019, having previously been the country's defence minister from 2017 to 2019 — who is she?
Nirmala Sitharaman: Indian economist and politician (born 1959)
Launched by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1592, this pair of Japanese invasions of Korea ended in 1598 after Ming reinforcements and Joseon Navy attacks forced a withdrawal — what is this conflict called?
Imjin War: 1592–1598 Japanese invasions of Korea. The conflict ended in 1598 with the withdrawal of Japanese forces from the Korean Peninsula after a military stalemate in Korea's southern provinces.
Anointed by the prophet Samuel as the first king of a newly unified Israelite kingdom, he died falling on his own sword after defeat by the Philistines at Mount Gilboa — who was he?
Saul: Biblical figure and Israelite monarch.
After Nebuchadnezzar II destroyed Jerusalem's temple in 587 BCE, thousands of Judeans were forcibly resettled in Mesopotamia — what is this exile called?
Babylonian captivity: Period in Jewish history during the 6th century BCE.
Named after its most prominent site and stimulated by contact with Minoan Crete, this Bronze Age mainland civilization built palatial states from roughly 1750 to 1050 BC — what's it called?
Mycenaean Greece: Late Bronze Age Greek civilization.
On 30 January of that year, British paratroopers shot 26 unarmed civilians during a civil-rights march in Derry's Bogside — which infamous shooting became a defining atrocity of the Troubles?
Bloody Sunday (1972): Mass shooting in Derry, Northern Ireland.
Proclaimed in 1931 after King Alfonso XIII's ouster and toppled in 1939 by Franco's Nationalists, which democratic government ruled Spain through the Civil War era?
Second Spanish Republic: Government of Spain, 1931–1939. It was dissolved on 1 April 1939 after surrendering in the Spanish Civil War to the Nationalists rebels led by General Francisco Franco.
A longtime aide to Gerhard Schröder before serving as Germany's top diplomat twice, he has been President of Germany since 2017 — who is he?

Frank-Walter Steinmeier: President of Germany since 2017. Frank-Walter Steinmeier (German: [ˈfʁaŋkˌvaltɐ ˈʃtaɪnˌmaɪ.ɐ]; born 5 January 1956) is a German politician who has served as President of Germany since 2017.
First adopted by the Old Swiss Confederacy, this system of government divides power between a central authority and regional states like provinces or cantons — what is it called?
Hailed as a 'hero of the revolution' for his role in the 1908 Young Turk uprising, this Ottoman military officer later became part of a ruling three-man dictatorship in the empire — who was he?
Enver Pasha: Turkish general and politician (1881–1922)
Serving as Italy's president from 2006 to 2015, this former Communist Party member became the country's longest-serving head of state and the first ever re-elected to the office — who was he?
Giorgio Napolitano: President of Italy from 2006 to 2015. In 2005, Napolitano was appointed a senator for life in Italy by then president Carlo Azeglio Ciampi.

With backing from the U.S. and Belgium, this military chief of staff deposed Congo's first democratically elected government in 1960 and later ruled the renamed nation of Zaire for over two decades — who was he?
Mobutu Sese Seko: President of DR Congo and Zaire from 1965 to 1997.

This wave of mass production, standardization, and rapid scientific discovery, sometimes dubbed the Technological era, is generally dated between 1870 and the outbreak of World War I in 1914. What period was this?
Second Industrial Revolution: 1870–1914 electrical and chemical era.
This Polish economist served as Prime Minister from 2017 to 2023 under the Law and Justice party, after earlier stints as both Finance Minister and Deputy Prime Minister. Who is he?

Mateusz Morawiecki: Prime Minister of Poland from 2017 to 2023. Mateusz Jakub Morawiecki (born 20 June 1968) is a Polish economist and politician who served as Prime Minister of Poland from 2017 to 2023.

Fought from 1919 to 1921, this conflict pitted the newly independent Second Republic under Józef Piłsudski against Lenin's forces seeking to spread revolution westward, redrawing Eastern Europe's borders after the collapse of the Central Powers. What conflict was this?
Polish–Soviet War: 20th-century conflict between Poland and Russia.

Once the Chief Mufti of a breakaway Chechen republic, this politician switched allegiances during the Second Chechen War to become the region's president, before being assassinated by a bomb in Grozny in 2004. Who was he?
Akhmad Kadyrov: Chechen militant and revolutionary (1951–2004)
Leading East Germany from 1971 until just before the Berlin Wall fell, this General Secretary previously spent years imprisoned by the Nazis for his Communist Party activism. Who was he?
Erich Honecker: Leader of East Germany, 1971–1989.

Spanning roughly 800 to 1050 CE, this era of Norse raiding, trading, and settlement saw Scandinavians reach as far as Newfoundland, becoming the first Europeans known to set foot in North America. What period was this?
Viking Age: Period of European history (about 800–1050)

Erupting in October 1962 partly over India's decision to grant asylum to the Dalai Lama, this month-long conflict pitted China against India along disputed Himalayan borders, coinciding with the Cuban Missile Crisis. What conflict was this?
Sino-Indian War: 1962 war between China and India. It was a military escalation of the Sino-Indian border dispute.

In Hesiod's 'Theogony,' this Greek personification of night was said to be so powerful that even Zeus feared displeasing her, and she rode across the sky in a chariot pulled by horses. Who is this goddess?
Nyx: Ancient Greek goddess of the night. In ancient Greek art, Nyx often appears alongside other celestial deities such as Selene, Helios and Eos, as a winged figure driving a horse-pulled chariot.
This Russian physicist-turned-politician served as the first governor of Nizhny Novgorod Oblast before becoming an outspoken critic of Vladimir Putin — who was he?
Boris Nemtsov: Russian scientist, statesman, and politician (1959–2015)
Originating near a Swabian castle town in the 11th century, this German dynasty supplied Prussian kings, German emperors, and the Romanian monarchy — which family?
House of Hohenzollern: German royal and imperial dynasty.
The eighth U.S. president is the only one to have spoken English as a second language, having grown up in a Dutch-speaking New York community — who is he?
Martin Van Buren: President of the United States from 1837 to 1841.
The first person to navigate the Northwest Passage by sea, this Norwegian explorer later led the first party to reach the South Pole aboard the ship Fram — who is he?
Serving as Argentina's Minister of National Security under both Javier Milei and Mauricio Macri, this senator represents Buenos Aires for La Libertad Avanza — who is she?
This Austrian-born SS commando led the Gran Sasso raid that freed Mussolini from captivity and later advised Egypt's Gamal Abdel Nasser after fleeing to Franco's Spain — who was he?

The third son of Japan's founding Edo-period shōgun, this samurai ruled as the second shōgun of that dynasty from 1605 until his 1623 abdication, and became grandfather to Empress Meishō — who was he?
Tokugawa Hidetada: Japanese Samurai, Daimyo and Military ruler of Japan from 1605 to 1623.

This King of Italy also claimed the titles Emperor of Ethiopia and King of the Albanians after Italy's invasions of those countries, and reigned through the entire rise and fall of the Fascist regime — who was he?
Victor Emmanuel III: King of Italy from 1900 to 1946.

Founded in British India in the late 19th century by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad, who claimed to be the promised Messiah and Mahdi awaited by Muslims, this messianic movement is centered on his teachings — name the movement?

Ahmadiyya: Islamic messianic movement founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad. Adherents of the Ahmadiyya—a term adopted expressly in reference to Muhammad's alternative name Ahmad—are known as Ahmadi Muslims or simply Ahmadis.
A former national police chief turned mayor of New Taipei, this Taiwanese politician ran as the Kuomintang's candidate in the 2024 presidential election — who is he?
Rooted in shamanism and animism on the Eurasian steppes and centered on a sky god, this belief system was the state religion of the Mongol Empire — which one?
Tengrism: Religion of the Eurasian steppe nations.
Renowned in the Book of Genesis for her hospitality and beauty, this matriarch was the wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac — who is she?
Sarah: Biblical matriarch. Sarah (originally Sarai) is a biblical matriarch, prophet, and major figure in Abrahamic religions.
After seizing power in a 1961 coup, this South Korean army officer ruled as president until his assassination in 1979, presiding over rapid economic growth — who was he?
Park Chung Hee: President of South Korea from 1963 to 1979.
Chairman of a militant group's political bureau from 1996 to 2017, this Palestinian leader has twice served as its acting head since 2024 — who is he?
Ruling the Franks from the 5th century until Pepin the Short in 751, this royal house defeated the Visigoths and Burgundians to dominate Gaul — which royal house was this?
Merovingian dynasty: Ruling family of the Franks (c. 481–751)
A former IDF Chief of General Staff who studied physics and mathematics before earning a master's at Stanford, this politician served as Israeli prime minister from 1999 to 2001 — who is he?
Ehud Barak: Prime Minister of Israel from 1999 to 2001. Born in kibbutz Mishmar Hasharon, Barak is the eldest of four sons; his maternal grandparents were murdered in the Holocaust.
According to the Book of Kings, this wife of King Ahab of Israel promoted Baal worship and met her end thrown from a window and devoured by dogs — who is she?
Jezebel: Biblical figure; Phoenician princess and wife of Ahab.

Fighting for both Christian and Muslim armies in 11th-century Spain, this Castilian knight earned the Arabic honorific 'the Lord' and ruled the Principality of Valencia until his death in 1099. Who was he?
El Cid: Castilian warlord and Prince of Valencia from 1094 to 1099.
This Polish statesman served as Chief of State after World War I and is regarded as the father of the Second Republic, re-established in 1918 after 123 years of partition. Who was he?
Spanning 1868 to 1912, this period saw Japan transform from an isolated feudal society into a modern industrial power under Western influence. What era, named for the reigning emperor, was it?
Meiji era: Period of Japanese history (1868–1912)

One October night, a gunman killed 18 people at a bowling alley and a bar in a Maine city, triggering the largest manhunt in the state's history before he was found dead two days later. What event was this?
2023 Lewiston shootings: Spree shooting in Maine, U.S.
This ferryman of Greek mythology transported souls across the river bordering the underworld, demanding a coin as payment, and even once carried living heroes like Heracles across. Who is he?

Charon: Ferryman of Hades in Greek mythology. In Greek mythology, Charon or Kharon (KAIR-on, -⁠ən; Ancient Greek: Χάρων Ancient Greek pronunciation: [kʰá.rɔːn]) is the ferryman of the Greek underworld.

This early 20th-century youth movement emphasizes outdoor skills like camping and woodcraft, uses a uniform designed to hide social class differences, and awards merit badges bearing a fleur-de-lis. What movement is it?
Scouting: Youth movement. Scouting or the Scout Movement is a youth movement which became popularly established in the first decade of the 20th century.
A key figure of the Heroic Age of Antarctic Exploration, this Anglo-Irish explorer led three British expeditions south and set a new Farthest South record in 1909 — who was he?

Founded in 2013 and led by Santiago Abascal, this national-conservative Spanish political party became the third-largest force in parliament after winning 52 seats in the November 2019 election — what party is it?
Vox (political party) (Spanish; Latin for 'voice'; often stylized in all caps) is a national conservative political party in Spain.
Swallowed by a great sea creature after fleeing his divine mission to warn Nineveh of God's judgment, this reluctant prophet later became known as a symbol of repentance — who was he?

Existing from 1918 to 1941 and initially named for its Serb, Croat, and Slovene peoples, this Southeast European kingdom formed by uniting Serbia, Montenegro, and former Austro-Hungarian territory — which kingdom?
Kingdom of Yugoslavia was a country in Southeast and Central Europe that existed from 1918 until 1941.
Son of a Trojan prince and the goddess Aphrodite, this mythological hero became, in Virgil's epic, the ancestor of Romulus and Remus — who is he?
Aeneas: Trojan hero in Greco-Roman mythology.
Considered the most influential artist of the Flemish Baroque, this painter and diplomat was known for dramatic, sensual compositions and designs for tapestry workshops — who is he?
Peter Paul Rubens: Flemish artist and diplomat (1577–1640)
Based on the doctrine of a 20th-century Argentine leader, this political movement is defined by three 'flags' — social justice, economic independence, and political sovereignty — what is it called?
Peronism: Argentine political movement. Peronism, also known as justicialism, is an Argentine ideology and political movement, based on the ideas, doctrine, and legacy of Juan Perón (1895–1974).
Traditionally dominated by Jerusalem, this mountainous region of the Levant was renamed Syria Palaestina by the Romans after the Bar Kokhba revolt — what was it called?
Judea: Region in the Levant. The name is derived from the Hebrew name Yehudah, and was used during the Babylonian, Persian, Hellenistic, and Roman periods.
Founded in 918 and ruling until the rise of Joseon in 1392, this Korean dynasty unified the Later Three Kingdoms and gave its name to the modern word 'Korea' — what was it called?
Goryeo: Korean dynasty (918–1392). Throughout its existence, Goryeo, alongside Unified Silla, was known to be the Golden Age of Buddhism in Korea.
Honored with the title 'Lokmanya' and famed for declaring 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it,' this Indian independence leader formed one third of a famous nationalist trio — who is he?
Bal Gangadhar Tilak: Indian self-rule activist (1856–1920)
Serving as Malaysia's 10th prime minister since 2022, this politician also held the post of deputy prime minister back in 1993 — who is he?
Anwar Ibrahim: Prime Minister of Malaysia since 2022. Anwar bin Ibrahim (born 10 August 1947) is a Malaysian politician who has served as the 10th prime minister of Malaysia since 2022.
After two failed attempts in 1944, this Hindu nationalist activist shot Mahatma Gandhi three times at a Delhi prayer meeting in January 1948 — who was he?
Nathuram Godse: Assassin of Mahatma Gandhi (1910–1949)
The elder daughter of a former U.S. vice president, this Wyoming representative chaired the House Republican Conference before becoming a vocal opponent of Donald Trump — who is she?
Liz Cheney: American lawyer and politician (born 1966)

President of Spain's People's Party who led the Galician regional government from 2009 to 2022, this politician's investiture as government formateur ultimately failed after the 2023 election — who is he?
His nickname means 'The Hammer' in Old French — this Frankish ruler served as Mayor of the Palace and defeated an Umayyad invasion of Aquitaine — who is he?
Charles Martel: Frankish military and political leader (c. 688–741)
Commissioned as an armor officer after Princeton ROTC, this retired general served as Army chief of staff before President Trump named him the 20th chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff — who is he?
Mark Milley: United States Army general (born 1958)
Governor of Central Java for a decade before running for Indonesian president in 2024 alongside former Chief Justice Mahfud MD, this left-wing populist finished third — who is he?

After training at Britain's Sandhurst military academy, this ruler seized power from his own father in a bloodless 1995 palace coup and turned his country's natural gas wealth into the world's highest average income per person — who was he?
Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani: Emir of Qatar from 1995 to 2013.
At just 16, this Australian sailor spent seven months attempting a solo circumnavigation of the globe, an achievement later dramatized in the 2023 Netflix film True Spirit — who is she?
After opening a camera store in San Francisco's Castro neighborhood, this politician became the first openly gay man elected to public office in California — who was he?
Harvey Milk: American gay rights activist (1930–1978)
In Abrahamic religions, this is the region God covenanted to give to the family and descendants of Abraham — what is this area traditionally called?
Promised Land is an area in the Levant that God chose to bestow, via a series of covenants, upon the family and descendants of Abraham.
Mentioned only in John's Gospel among the New Testament writers, this Pharisee and Sanhedrin member secretly admired Jesus and earned the nickname 'defender of Jesus' — who is he?
Nicodemus: Pharisee, biblical figure appearing in the Gospel of John.
Ruling twice as Ottoman sultan — first from 1421 to 1444, then again from 1446 until his death in 1451 — who was this 15th-century monarch?
Murad II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire (r. 1421–1444, 1446–1451)
Founder of Turkey's Good Party, this politician served as interior minister under Necmettin Erbakan in the 1990s before later becoming a vice-speaker of the Grand National Assembly — who is she?
This Eighteenth-Dynasty Egyptian ruler was only the second woman confirmed to reign in her own right, and had herself depicted as a man to reinforce her authority — who was she?
Hatshepsut: Pharaoh of Egypt from 1479 to 1458 BC.
Rumored to have plotted the deaths of several of her husband's relatives, including his own grandson, this woman became empress of Rome as wife of its first emperor — who was she?
Livia: Roman empress from 27 BC to AD 14.
Born in Georgia, this Red Army officer and engineer was the eldest son of a Bolshevik revolutionary who became head of the Soviet Union — who is he?
Yakov Dzhugashvili: Red Army officer and Joseph Stalin's son (1907–1943)
The first woman to serve as chief minister of West Bengal, this politician also became the first sitting Indian chief minister to argue a case before the Supreme Court — who is she?
Mamata Banerjee: Chief Minister of West Bengal from 2011 to 2026.
Centered first at San Lorenzo and later at La Venta, this early Mesoamerican civilization is thought to have pioneered ritual bloodletting and an ancient ballgame — which culture?
Olmecs: Earliest known major Mesoamerican civilization.
A Princeton and Harvard Law graduate who became the first Hispanic American to represent the Lone Star State in the Senate, he led the charge in the 2013 government shutdown — who is he?
Ted Cruz: American politician and attorney (born 1970)
Once believed to be Russia's richest man with a $15 billion fortune built on Siberian oil fields under Yukos, this exiled oligarch became an opposition activist — who is he?
Worshipped since Egypt's Second Dynasty and known to the Greeks as Ailuros, or 'cat', this goddess embodied a gentler counterpart to the fierce lioness deity Sekhmet — who is she?

She served as France's Minister of Justice under Sarkozy before later becoming Minister of Culture across four different governments, and has been mayor of one of Paris's arrondissements since 2008. Who is this French politician?

In January 2021, Reddit's r/wallstreetbets drove the stock of an American video game retailer up nearly 30-fold in a single month, inflicting massive losses on the hedge funds betting against it. What is this market event known as?
GameStop short squeeze: 2021 financial markets event.
This uprising ended the Qing dynasty's 267-year reign and more than two thousand years of imperial rule in China, ushering in the country's republican era. What is it called?
1911 Revolution: End of Qing dynasty in China. The revolution was the culmination of a decade of agitation, revolts, and uprisings.

A South African businessman who served on Pretoria's city council and dabbled in emerald trading, he's perhaps best known today as the father of a tech billionaire and two other children from his first marriage. Who is he?
Errol Musk: South African businessman and politician (born 1946)
In Christian eschatology, this future event will see Jesus Christ return to sit on a "great white throne" and render a final verdict on every person who has ever lived — what is this event called?
Last Judgment is a central Christian eschatological event marking the return of Jesus Christ to evaluate all of humanity, both the living and the resurrected dead (Jn 5:28-29).

Ruling Mexico for more than three decades until his 1911 overthrow, this general-turned-dictator once studied for the priesthood before switching to law under the mentorship of future president Benito Juárez. Who is he?
Porfirio Díaz: President and Dictator of Mexico from 1876 to 1911.

Fought between 1877 and 1878, this war pitted the Ottoman Empire against a Russian-led coalition that included Romania, Serbia, and Montenegro, ending with Russian forces at the gates of Constantinople — what war was it?
Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878) (1877-1878) was a conflict between the Ottoman Empire and a coalition led by the Russian Empire which included Romania, Serbia, and Montenegro.

The father of Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, this career army officer serving in the Balkan Wars was exiled with most of his royal family after his brother Constantine's wartime neutrality forced an abdication. Who was he?
Prince Andrew of Greece and Denmark
Prince Andrew of Greece and Denmark

Prince Andrew of Greece and Denmark was a Greek prince and army officer, father of Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh. A career soldier, Andrew began military training at an early age, and was commissioned as an officer in the Greek army.
Prince Andrew of Greece and Denmark
Central to Judaism and recounted every Passover, this founding narrative describes the Israelites' escape from Egyptian bondage through a parting of the Red Sea under Moses — what is it?
The Exodus: Founding myth of the Jewish people.
Restored to life four days after death by Jesus in the Gospel of John, this New Testament figure's name is now used to describe any apparent return from the brink of death — who is he?
Lazarus of Bethany: Person resurrected by Jesus in the Gospel of John.
Founded in 1792 when the Convention abolished the constitutional monarchy, this government lasted until Napoleon Bonaparte declared an empire in 1804 — what political entity was it?
French First Republic: Three regimes of revolutionary and early Napoleonic France (1792–1804)
Nicknamed 'the Thunderbolt,' this Ottoman sultan crushed a crusader army at Nicopolis in 1396 but was later defeated and captured by Timur — who is he?
Bayezid I: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1389 to 1402.
Meaning 'the one who yawns' in Mescalero-Chiricahua, this name belonged to the Bedonkohe Apache medicine man who led raids against Mexican and U.S. forces from 1850 to 1886. Who was he?
Geronimo: Leader of the Bedonkohe Apache (1829–1909)

This Israeli politician served as defense minister from 2022 until his dismissal by the prime minister in November 2024, having earlier held posts including construction, immigration, and education minister after starting out in the navy. Who is he?
Yoav Gallant: Israeli politician & military officer (born 1958)

This Egyptian-born Israeli spy infiltrated Syria's political and military elite between 1961 and 1965 before being uncovered, convicted under martial law, and publicly hanged in Damascus — an event that helped escalate tensions ahead of the 1967 war. Who is he?
Eli Cohen: Israeli spy (1924–1965). Though he was initially successful, Cohen's activity became increasingly risky and he expressed a sense of impending danger to Mossad in 1964.

This Ottoman sultan ruled from 1481 to 1512, welcomed Sephardi Jews expelled from Spain following the 1492 Alhambra Decree, and eventually abdicated his throne to his son, Selim I. Which sultan is this?
Bayezid II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1481 to 1512. Bayezid; 3 December 1447/1448 – 26 May 1512) was the sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1481 to 1512.

A protégé of murdered dissident Boris Nemtsov, this Russian-British activist and filmmaker has served as vice-chairman of an NGO founded by an exiled former oligarch, and received the Civil Courage Prize in 2018 after being repeatedly targeted for his opposition to the Kremlin. Who is he?

Philip the Handsome: Habsburg ruler, King of Castile in 1506. Philip was the son of Maximilian I of Austria and Mary of Burgundy.
Ruling Jordan since 1921 and tracing its lineage to the great-grandfather of the Islamic prophet Muhammad, which royal family once also held the thrones of Hejaz, Syria and Iraq?
Hashemites: Royal family of Jordan since 1921. The family belongs to the Dhawu Awn, one of the branches of the Ḥasanid Sharifs of Mecca, also referred to as Hashemites.
In Śaiva Tantra, what is the name for the divine feminine energy said to coil at the base of the spine, whose awakening through meditation is believed to lead to liberation?
Kundalini: Form of divine energy in Hindu mysticism.
This French lawyer-turned-politician served as prime minister under Emmanuel Macron from 2017 to 2020, then returned to serve as mayor of Le Havre — who is he?
Édouard Philippe: Prime Minister of France from 2017 to 2020. A lawyer by occupation, Philippe is a former member of the Union for a Popular Movement (UMP), which later became The Republicans (LR).
Known in his home region as the 'Bahubali of Uttar Pradesh,' this six-term Indian MP formerly presided over the Wrestling Federation of India — who is he?
Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: Indian politician (born 1957)
A Brooklyn native and Harvard graduate, this U.S. senator has led the Senate Democratic Caucus since 2017 and surpassed two predecessors as New York's longest-serving senator — who is he?
This Finnish lawyer chaired the National Coalition Party from 1994 to 2001 and later served as president from 2012 to 2024, defeating Pekka Haavisto in a 2012 runoff — who is he?
Sauli Niinistö: President of Finland from 2012 to 2024. Sauli Väinämö Niinistö (born 24 August 1948) is a Finnish politician who served as the president of Finland from 2012 to 2024.

Born to a Tutsi family that fled to Uganda when he was two, this politician commanded a rebel force that ended the 1994 genocide in his home country and has served as its president since 2000 — who is he?
Paul Kagame: President of Rwanda since 2000. The RPF was one of the main belligerents of the Rwandan Civil War and was the armed force which ended the 1994 Rwandan genocide.
As chairman and CEO of Chase Manhattan, this banker was the youngest child of a wealthy family famous for its oil fortune, and died in 2017 with a $3.3 billion net worth — who was he?
David Rockefeller: American banker and philanthropist (1915–2017)
As one of the youngest MPs ever elected to India's Lok Sabha in 1977, he went on to serve as Bihar's chief minister and later as the national railways minister — who is he?
Lalu Prasad Yadav: 20th chief minister of Bihar. Lalu was convicted in the Fodder Scam and was serving a term until 17 April 2021, when he was granted bail by the High Court.

Founded in 1912 to oppose oppression of Black South Africans, this liberation movement has governed the country since 1994's first post-apartheid election, when Nelson Mandela became president — which party?
African National Congress: Political party in South Africa.

He mortgaged inherited farmland to invest in a software company he later sold to Microsoft for $1.1 billion, then became governor of North Dakota before serving as Secretary of the Interior — who is he?
Doug Burgum: American politician and businessman (born 1956)
This Ukrainian politician fled to Russia in 2022 and publicly backed its invasion of Ukraine, leading parliament to strip his mandate and Ukrainian courts to convict him of treason — who was he?
Dubbed the 'Peter the Great of Turkey,' this Ottoman sultan disbanded the conservative Janissary Corps and ceded Bessarabia to Russia after ascending via an 1808 coup — who was he?
Mahmud II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1808 to 1839.
Often equated with the Israelites, this term for an ancient nomadic Semitic-speaking people appears 34 times across 32 verses of the Old Testament — what's the term?

Enslaved as a young Orthodox Christian, this close friend of Suleiman the Magnificent became the Ottoman Empire's first grand vizier in 1523 before being executed on the sultan's orders in 1536 — who was he?

Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha: Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire from 1523 to 1536. Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha (c. 1495 – 15 March 1536), was the first grand vizier of the Ottoman Empire appointed by Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent.
Closely tied to moral responsibility, praise, and blame, this philosophical capacity to choose one's own actions is debated over whether it can coexist with physical determinism — what is it called?
Free will: Ability to make choices voluntarily.
This act of deliberate communication with a deity — through hymns, incantations, or spontaneous words — has been documented in written sources for some five thousand years — what is it called?
Prayer: Invocation or act that seeks to activate a rapport with a deity.
This lawyer and revolutionary led Russia's short-lived Provisional Government in 1917, insisting on staying in World War I despite mass public opposition — who is he?
Known from early medieval carved stones, this people lived north of the Firth of Forth before merging with Dál Riata to form the Kingdom of Alba — who were they?
Picts: Medieval tribal confederation in northern Britain.

Fought in 937, this clash saw King Æthelstan defeat an alliance of the kings of Dublin, Scotland, and Strathclyde — historians credit it as a birthplace of English national identity. What is this clash known as?
Battle of Brunanburh: Part of the Viking invasions of England.

A follower of a controversial Bohemian religious reformer, this Czech military leader led Hussite forces to victory against three separate crusades and was never defeated in his military career — who is he?
This wide-scale shift from nomadic hunting and gathering to farming and settled life began in Mesopotamia around 11,700 years ago — what is it called?
Neolithic Revolution: Human transition from foraging to settlement.
Led for years by Donald Tusk, this Polish centre-right party overtook its rivals in the 2007 parliamentary election to put him in the prime minister's seat — which party?
Civic Platform: Political party in Poland (2001–2025)
The penultimate Ottoman sultan, this constitutional monarch reigned from 1909 to 1918 after succeeding his half-brother in the wake of a failed coup — who is he?
Mehmed V: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1909 to 1918. Mehmed V Reşâd (Ottoman Turkish: محمد خامس, romanized: Meḥmed-i ḫâmis; Turkish: V.
On April 9, 1948, Zionist paramilitary forces attacked a village near Jerusalem despite an agreed non-aggression pact, an event now seen as a central part of the Nakba — which attack?
Deir Yassin massacre: 1948 mass killing by Zionist militants.
Born under a different name and later adopting a new surname, this religious leader grew a small Detroit-based movement into a nationwide organization during the civil rights era — who is he?
Elijah Muhammad: African American religious leader (1897–1975)
This ancient Egyptian sky goddess, linked to Horus and Ra, represented beauty, music, dance, and joy, while also serving as a vengeful protector known as the Eye of Ra — who is she?
Hathor: Major goddess in ancient Egyptian religion.
The youngest person and first woman ever elected governor of Alaska, she was the Republican Party's vice presidential nominee alongside John McCain in 2008 — who is she?
In Ovid's 'Metamorphoses,' this son of Somnus, the Roman god of sleep, visits mortals in their dreams disguised in human form — who is he?
Morpheus: Deity associated with sleep and dreams.

Grandson of the last Austro-Hungarian emperor, this pro-European former member of the European Parliament has devoted his career to protecting cultural heritage from war and disaster — who heads this once-ruling dynasty?
Educated at Sandhurst and Oxford, this monarch reigned as King of Malaysia from 2019 to 2024 while also serving as a Malaysian state's sixth sultan — who is he?
Abdullah of Pahang: King of Malaysia from 2019 to 2024. Abdullah became Sultan of Pahang upon his father's abdication in January 2019 who later died in May 2019.
Founded in 1972 and rebranded from its earlier name in 2018, this French far-right, anti-immigration party is now the largest opposition bloc in parliament — what party is this?
National Rally: Political party in France.
The first UN Secretary-General to rise from within the organization's own staff, this Ghanaian diplomat shared the 2001 Nobel Peace Prize with the UN itself — who is he?
Kofi Annan: UN Secretary-General from 1997 to 2006.
This Chinese diplomat served as ambassador to Japan before becoming Minister of Foreign Affairs and later director of the Communist Party's Central Foreign Affairs Commission Office — who is he?

Born to a poor family of pig farmers in Spain, this conquistador accompanied the first European crossing to sight the Pacific from the Americas before leading the conquest of the Inca Empire — who is he?
This political analyst served as the 34th White House press secretary under one president after holding communications posts under another, and later hosted her own political talk show — who is she?
The niece of Japan's current emperor, this art historian gave up her imperial title in 2021 upon marrying a commoner, as required by law — who is she?
In the Gospels, Jesus warns that no one can serve God alongside this Aramaic personification of wealth, later depicted in medieval tradition as one of Hell's princes of greed — what is it?
Mammon: Wealth or an entity that promises wealth.
Described in both the Bible and the Quran, this edible substance was said to have been provided by God to sustain the Israelites during their 40 years wandering the desert — what was it?
Manna: Edible substance described in the Bible.
Founded in Japan in 1930 and rooted in the teachings of the 13th-century monk Nichiren, this Buddhist organization centers its practice on chanting a specific mantra — what is it?
Soka Gakkai: Japanese Buddhist religious movement.

This successful insurrection by enslaved Africans against French colonial rule in Saint-Domingue climaxed with independence on New Year's Day, 1804, led by the general Toussaint Louverture — what was it called?
Haitian Revolution: 1791–1804 slave revolt in Hispanola.
Leading Bavaria's Free Voters party since 2018, this politician also serves as the state's deputy minister president and economics minister — who is he?
The 39th vice president of the United States, he resigned in 1973 under Nixon, becoming only the second VP in history to do so — who was he?
Spiro Agnew: Vice President of the United States from 1969 to 1973.

Head of the Catholic Church for nearly 32 years — the longest verified reign in history — this pontiff convened a council that defined papal infallibility before declaring himself a 'prisoner' after Rome's capture in 1870 — who was he?
Pope Pius IX: Head of the Catholic Church from 1846 to 1878.
Serving as Japan's foreign minister from 2023 to 2024, she previously held the justice portfolio and worked on gender-equality policy under two different prime ministers — who is she?

Defined by a one-man police state, forced agricultural collectivization, and a sweeping cult of personality, this set of Soviet policies held sway from 1927 until the dictator's death in 1953 — what is it called?
Stalinism: Political and economic policies implemented by Joseph Stalin.
One of Noah's sons in Genesis, this biblical figure is considered an ancestor of Abraham and lent his name to the term for a group of West Asian peoples — who is he?
Shem: Biblical figure, son of Noah. Shem (Hebrew: שֵׁם Šēm; Arabic: سَام, romanized: Sām) is one of the sons of Noah in the Bible (Genesis 5–11 and 1 Chronicles 1:4).
Nicknamed 'Pepe,' this former guerrilla fighter spent 14 years imprisoned under a military dictatorship before becoming Uruguay's president and legalizing marijuana consumption — who is he?
José Mujica: President of Uruguay from 2010 to 2015.
Toppling King Charles X and installing his cousin Louis Philippe as France's final monarch, this 1830 uprising also became known as 'Trois Glorieuses,' or Three Glorious Days — what's it called?
July Revolution: 1830 overthrow of the Bourbon monarchy in France.
Rising from vice president to head of state after her husband's death in 1974, this Argentine leader became the first woman ever to serve as a country's president — who was she?
Isabel Perón: President of Argentina from 1974 to 1976.
This 19th-century Indian reformer and his wife opened one of the country's first schools for girls in Pune in 1848 and later founded the 'Society of Truth Seekers' — who was he?
Jyotirao Phule: Indian social activist and reformer (1827–1890)
This Turkish socialist academic-turned-politician leads the Workers' Party of Turkey and represents Istanbul in parliament — who is he?
A former NYPD captain, this Democrat became the first Black Brooklyn Borough President before winning election as New York City's 111th mayor in 2021 — who is he?
Eric Adams: Mayor of New York City from 2022 to 2025.
Ruling from the mountain fortress of Alamut from 1090, this founder of the Order of Assassins was dubbed the 'Old Man of the Mountain' by Marco Polo — who was he?
Hasan-i Sabbah: Ismaili religious and military leader (c. 1050–1124)
Educated at Al-Azhar and later a preacher in his native Jableh, this early-20th-century leader fought against French rule in Syria and British rule in Palestine — who was he?
Izz ad-Din al-Qassam: Syrian Muslim preacher (1882–1935)
Napoleon's older brother wore two crowns, Naples then Spain, before fleeing to a New Jersey estate under an assumed comital title — who was he?
Joseph Bonaparte: King of Naples (1806–08) and Spain (1808–13)
Raised partly in Brazil, this Japanese wrestling legend founded and owned New Japan Pro-Wrestling for over three decades — who is he?
Antonio Inoki: Japanese wrestler and politician (1943–2022)

This 1866 conflict pitted the Austrian Empire against the Kingdom of Prussia, whose Italian allies used it to help complete their unification struggle, and ended with the abolition of the German Confederation — what's this conflict called?
Austro-Prussian War: 1866 war in Europe. Prussia had also allied with the Kingdom of Italy, linking this conflict to the Third Independence War of Italian unification.
The first Somali American ever elected to Congress, this Minnesota representative also became one of the first two Muslim women to serve there, alongside Rashida Tlaib — who is she?
The son of Jupiter and Juno, this Roman deity oversaw both war and farming, and gave his name to the month that begins the campaigning season — who is he?
Mars (mythology): Roman god of war, guardian of agriculture.

Once a member of the State Duma, this Russian financial fraudster's donation-based scheme defrauded thousands of investors — and he later claimed the same scheme was behind a bitcoin price rally — who is he?
Co-leading a pro-Kurdish party to double-digit vote shares in Turkey's 2015 elections, this politician ran for president from behind bars in 2018 after his 2016 imprisonment — who is he?
Selahattin Demirtaş: Turkish politician. Selahattin Demirtaş (born 10 April 1973) is a Kurdish politician, lawyer and author.

Sometimes called, controversially, the 'Dark' era due to a scarcity of surviving written sources, this stretch of European history ran from the late 5th to the 10th century, following Rome's decline in the west — what period is this?
Early Middle Ages: Period of European history. The term is rarely used by academics today.
Serving as his brother's spokesman before Pharaoh, this Israelite figure became the first High Priest after receiving that role at Sinai — who is he, the elder brother of Moses?
Aaron: Prophet in the Abrahamic faiths.
Because its large profile and low operating altitude make it an easy target, this heavily armed gunship variant of the C-130 Hercules usually flies missions at night. What aircraft is it?
History of Australia was proclaimed on 1 January 1901 as a federation of six self-governing former British colonies.
French for 'let do,' this economic philosophy holds that markets self-regulate best when free from subsidies and government regulation — what's it called?
Laissez-faire: Economic system free from interventionism.
First launched in June 2007 with the original iPhone, this mobile operating system had rolled out nineteen major updates by the time its numbering reached 26 in September 2025 — which one is this?
IOS version history: iOS (formerly iPhone OS) is a mobile operating system developed by Apple Inc.
Known as Rama V, this Siamese king modernized his country and skillfully preserved its independence despite being surrounded by British and French colonies — who is he?
Chulalongkorn: King of Siam from 1868 to 1910.

In 1989, the assault of a young woman running through a Manhattan green space led to the conviction — and eventual exoneration — of five teenagers now known as the Exonerated Five. What is this notorious incident known as?
Central Park jogger case: 1989 crime in New York City.
This 17th-century Cossack Hetman led an uprising against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth that forged an independent Cossack state in Dnieper Ukraine — who was he?
Bohdan Khmelnytsky: Hetman of the Zaporozhian Host from 1648 to 1657.
This Iranian prime minister's land reforms and social security programs ended abruptly in a 1953 coup engineered by the CIA and MI6 — who was he?
Mohammad Mosaddegh: Prime Minister of Iran from 1951 to 1953.
After defeating his half-brother Sviatopolk in a war for the throne, this son of Vladimir the Great ruled Kiev from 1019 to 1054 — who was he?
Yaroslav the Wise: Grand Prince of Kiev from 1019 to 1054.
Leader of La France Insoumise, this French politician has run for president three times and announced a fourth bid for 2027 — who is he?
Meaning 'praise Yah' in Hebrew, this interjection appears 24 times in the Book of Psalms and echoes through Christian liturgy in its Latin form 'alleluia' — what's the word?
Hallelujah: Religious interjection. The term is used 24 times in the Tanakh (in the book of Psalms), twice in deuterocanonical books, and four times in the Christian Book of Revelation.
Established in 1832 after the War of Independence, this monarchy survived on and off — including a 1935 restoration — until its final abolition in 1973. What was this Hellenic state called?
Kingdom of Greece: Period of Greek statehood from 1832 to 1923 and 1935 to 1973.
In Greek mythology, this minor deity personified death itself, and was known to the Romans as Mors or Letum — who is he?
Thanatos: Ancient Greek personification of death.
Succeeding his brother Baudouin on the throne in 1993, this monarch abdicated in 2013 for health reasons, becoming only the second in his country's history to step down — who is he?
Albert II of Belgium: King of the Belgians from 1993 to 2013.
A former Air Force JAG officer who served as the military's chief prosecutor in Europe, this Republican represented South Carolina in the US Senate from 2003 until his death in 2026 — who is he?

Entering a power-sharing arrangement with his father in 2022, this politician became president after winning 73% of the vote in what's widely considered a sham election, making his nation the first in modern Central Asia ruled by a father-son dynasty — who is he?
Serdar Berdimuhamedow: President of Turkmenistan since 2022.
This Norse god sacrificed his right hand to bind the monstrous wolf Fenrir, and English weekdays still preserve his name in the middle of the work week — who is he?

Serving as Ukraine's Defence Minister from 2023 to 2025 before becoming Secretary of the National Security and Defence Council, this Crimean Tatar politician has co-chaired a Crimea diplomatic initiative since 2020 — who is he?
Serving as Israel's prime minister from 2021 to 2022, this politician and former special-forces soldier co-founded the tech company Cyota after growing up in Haifa — who is he?
Naftali Bennett: Prime Minister of Israel from 2021 to 2022. Bennett has served as the head of Bennett 2026 since 2025; the party is allied with Yesh Atid as part of an alliance called Together.

Once the sixth-richest person on Earth and head of a conglomerate spun off from his family's industrial empire in 2006, this Indian businessman later declared bankruptcy before a UK court in 2020 — who is he?
Rising from a cavalry regiment to become one of Napoleon's marshals, this French officer was crowned King of Naples in 1808 after also serving as Grand Duke of Berg — who is he?
Joachim Murat: French military officer and statesman (1767–1815)
This Israelite priest-prophet foretold Jerusalem's fall to the Neo-Babylonians in 587 BC and has an entire book of the Hebrew Bible named for him — who is he?
Ezekiel: Prophet in the Abrahamic religions.
This Argentine general seized power in a 1976 coup that deposed Isabel Perón, ruled during the dark years of Operation Condor, and was later convicted in the Trial of the Juntas — who was he?
Jorge Rafael Videla: President of Argentina from 1976 to 1981.

This Prussian-born general masterminded German victories at Liège and Tannenberg in 1914, then oversaw the country's WWI strategy as First Quartermaster General before later joining Hitler's failed 1923 Beer Hall Putsch — who is he?
Erich Ludendorff: German general and politician (1865–1937)
One of the 'Princes in the Tower,' this boy king reigned for less than three months in 1483 before his uncle deposed him to become Richard III — who was he?
Edward V: King of England in 1483. Edward V (2 November 1470 – presumably July 1483) was King of England from 9 April to 25 June 1483.

Suppressed by Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist government and sparked by resentment toward corrupt post-1945 rule, this 1947 Taiwanese uprising became a key catalyst for the island's independence movement — what's it called?
February 28 incident: 1947 uprising in Taiwan. Directed by provincial governor Chen Yi and president Chiang Kai-shek, thousands of civilians were killed beginning on February 28.
Nicknamed an 'uncrowned monarch,' this Mexican general served as president eight separate times between 1833 and 1855 and is blamed for losing territory to the United States — who was he?
Antonio López de Santa Anna: President of Mexico many times, 1833 to 1855.
Founded in 1804 by a Corsican-born general who'd just transformed the French Republic into an empire, this royal dynasty placed family members on thrones across conquered Europe — which family?
House of Bonaparte: French imperial dynasty. The House of Bonaparte (originally Buonaparte) is a former imperial and royal European dynasty of Corsican origin.
Crowned king of a Rajasthan realm as a child in 1177, this ruler beat a Ghurid army near Taraori in 1191 - only to be defeated and executed there the following year. Who was he?
Prithviraj Chauhan: King of Ajmer from 1177 to 1192.

Born into a priestly family in the Kingdom of Judah, this reluctant prophet endured imprisonment during a fifty-year ministry and is traditionally credited with writing the Book of Lamentations. Who was he?
Jeremiah: Biblical prophet. Jeremiah (c. 650 – c. 570 BC), also called Jeremias, and occasionally in older English texts Jeremy, was one of the major prophets of the Hebrew Bible.

This Indian activist-turned-politician won a 2006 Ramon Magsaysay Award for an anti-corruption campaign before becoming Delhi's chief minister and founding a party as its national convener. Who is he?
Arvind Kejriwal: Chief Minister of Delhi (2013–14; 2015–2024)

Named for Charles Martel and his grandson Charlemagne, this Frankish royal family toppled the Merovingians in 751 and reached its height in 800 when Charlemagne was crowned the first Western Roman emperor in three centuries. Which family was this?
Carolingian dynasty: Frankish noble family founded by Charles Martel.

A physician turned journalist, this French prime minister demanded total victory after 1.4 million of his countrymen died in the First World War and pushed through the Treaty of Versailles's harsh terms. Who was he?
Georges Clemenceau: Prime Minister of France (1906–1909, 1917–1920)

Inheriting leadership of a Sufi military order from his brother as a child, this ruler founded a Persian dynasty in 1501 and unified Iran under native rule for the first time in over eight centuries. Who was he?
Ismail I: Shah of Safavid Iran from 1501 to 1524.

The first woman to run a successful US presidential campaign, this pollster managed a 2016 White House bid after her preferred candidate dropped out of the primary, and went on to serve as a senior White House counselor. Who is she?
Kellyanne Conway: American political consultant and pollster (born 1967)

This Republican politician served as Arkansas's governor from 2015 to 2023 after earlier stints as a US attorney and member of Congress, and later ran for the 2024 GOP presidential nomination. Who is he?

Asa Hutchinson: Governor of Arkansas from 2015 to 2023. In 1982, President Ronald Reagan appointed Hutchinson to serve as the U.S. attorney for the Western District of Arkansas, which covers most of Fort Smith.
This former army chief seized power in a 2014 coup, installed a military junta, and went on to serve as Thailand's prime minister for nearly a decade. Who is he?
Prayut Chan-o-cha: Prime Minister of Thailand from 2014 to 2023.
The son of the Ottoman Empire's founder and half-brother of its second ruler, this prince stayed home managing state affairs rather than fight to expand the realm — who was he?
Alaeddin Pasha: Ottoman prince, brother of Orhan I Gazi.

Nicknamed the 'Sheikh of slaughtering,' this Jordanian militant formed a group in 1999 before pledging allegiance to al-Qaeda's leader in 2004 and masterminding bombings during the Iraq War — who was he?
A key figure in Japan's Meiji Restoration, this samurai later led a doomed 1877 uprising against the very government he helped create, dying in the fighting — who was he?
Saigō Takamori: Japanese samurai and politician (1828–1877)
This French politician served as Secretary of State for Gender Equality before being sacked from government in 2023 amid a scandal over an anti-extremism fund she had set up — who is she?
Marlène Schiappa: French politician. The fund has faced criticism for its lack of transparency and the conditions under which grants were awarded.
In Vedic and Hindu philosophy, this term denotes the ultimate reality from which all existence proceeds and to which everything returns — what is it?
Brahman: Metaphysical concept, unchanging Ultimate Reality in Hinduism.

Between 1764 and 1767, one or more man-eating creatures with a tufted tail and dark-striped tawny coat terrorized a swath of south-central France near the Margeride Mountains — what were locals convinced stalked them?
Beast of Gévaudan: Man-eating animal in the 1760s.

Historians generally date this current period of human history from around 1500, though many now reserve its label for events from the 19th century onward, like the Industrial Revolution — what span of time is this?
Modern era: Current period of history. Since the 1990s, it has been more common among historians to refer to the period after the Middle Ages and up to the 19th century as the early modern period.
The only Israeli soldier killed during a daring 1976 hostage-rescue raid on a hijacked airliner in Uganda, he was the elder brother of a future Israeli prime minister — who was he?

Emerging around the 5th century BC as bearers of La Tène culture, this Celtic-speaking people controlled trade routes along the Rhône, Seine, Rhine, and Danube before clashing with Rome and the Greeks — who were they?
Gauls: Ancient Celtic peoples of Europe.
Founded by a Varangian prince who settled at Novgorod in 862, this noble lineage ruled Kievan Rus' and, through its Moscow branch, the tsars of Russia until 1598 — what dynasty was it?
Rurikids: Noble lineage and rulers of Kievan Rus'. The Rurikids were the ruling dynasty of Kievan Rus' and its principalities following its disintegration.

Fought on 8 September 1380 near the Don River, this clash saw Grand Prince Dmitry of Moscow defeat a Golden Horde commander, earning the epithet 'Donskoy' and marking a turning point against Mongol influence — which battle?
Battle of Kulikovo was fought between the forces of Mamai, a powerful Mongol military commander of the Golden Horde, and Russian forces led by Grand Prince Dmitry of Moscow.

Formed in 2007 from the merger of the PDS and a labor splinter group, this German democratic socialist party traces its lineage back to East Germany's ruling Socialist Unity Party — which party is it?
Die Linke: Political party in Germany. The party was founded in 2007 as the result of the merger of the Party of Democratic Socialism (PDS) and Labour and Social Justice – The Electoral Alternative.

After helping secure the Qing dynasty's abdication, this Chinese general became the Republic's first formal president, only to declare himself emperor in 1915 and abdicate again months later — who was he?
Yuan Shikai: First president of the Republic of China (1859–1916)
This period of drier-than-normal weather can stretch from days to years, drying out wetlands, fueling larger wildfires, and battering both farms and local economies — what climate phenomenon is it?
Drought: Period with less precipitation than normal.
Half-woman, half-snake, this solitary cave-dwelling monster of Greek myth mated with the fearsome Typhon and mothered many of mythology's most famous creatures. Who was she?

Compiled over roughly a thousand years by Egyptian priests, this papyrus collection of magic spells was tucked into coffins to help guide the deceased through the underworld into the afterlife. What is it commonly called?
Book of the Dead: Ancient Egyptian funerary text.
