Junichiro Koizumi: Prime Minister of Japan from 2001 to 2006. Coming from the prominent Koizumi family, Koizumi was first elected to the House of Representatives in 1972.

The first Asian-American woman in a U.S. presidential cabinet, this Taiwan-born official served as secretary of labor under George W. Bush and secretary of transportation under Donald Trump, resigning after the January 6 Capitol attack. Who is she?
Elaine Chao: American businesswoman and government official (born 1953)
Derived from the Latin word for 'to assess,' this systematic count of a population's members is recommended by the UN to be conducted at least once every ten years. What is it?
Census: Compilation of information about a given population.

Serving as Brazil's president both from 1930 to 1945 and from 1951 until his 1954 suicide, this São Borja-born leader is regarded by historians as the most influential Brazilian politician of the 20th century. Who is he?

Getúlio Vargas: President of Brazil (1930–1945; 1951–1954). Born on 19 April 1882 in São Borja, Rio Grande do Sul, to a powerful local family, Vargas had a short stint in the Brazilian Army before entering law school.

The day after her coronation in 1610, this Queen of France became regent for her young son Louis XIII following her husband King Henry IV's assassination, and only relinquished power via a 1617 coup. Who is she?
Marie de' Medici: Queen of France from 1600 to 1610.
The youngest mayor in the history of Taipei, this politician is the great-grandson of a former Nationalist Chinese president — who is he?
Chiang Wan-an: Taiwanese politician and lawyer (born 1978)
Nicknamed the 'people's leader,' this two-time Chief Minister of Bihar was posthumously awarded India's highest civilian honor in 2024 — who was he?
Originating from an Old English word meaning 'being truly guilty,' this concept covers immoral or wrongful thoughts, words, or acts across many religions — what is it?
Working alongside Norman Borlaug, this Indian geneticist helped save South Asia from famine by developing high-yielding wheat and rice varieties — who is he?
After resigning as Germany's finance minister within six months of taking office, this politician later co-founded a left-wing party opposing his former party's reforms — who is he?
Described by Homer as the most handsome of mortals, this Trojan youth was abducted by the gods to become Zeus's cup-bearer on Olympus — who is he?
Ganymede (mythology) (Ancient) is a divine hero whose homeland was Troy.
This retired Royal Navy vice admiral served as an equerry to Queen Elizabeth II before marrying her only daughter in 1992 — who is he?
Timothy Laurence: Retired Royal Navy officer (born 1955)
Nicknamed 'Father of Ignorance' by his rival for his fierce opposition to a new monotheistic faith, this Meccan Qurayshite leader had earlier been known as 'Father of Wisdom' — who was he?
Amr ibn Hisham: Arab polytheist leader (c. 570–624)
This barbarian general deposed the child emperor Romulus Augustulus in 476 AD, an event traditionally marking the end of the Western Roman Empire — who was he?
Born in Arkansas to a banker and a teacher, this Yale Law graduate clerked for the Chief Justice before unseating a two-term Democratic senator from Missouri in 2018 — who is he?
Josh Hawley: American lawyer and politician (born 1979)
Described in its founding text as formless, eternal, and the 'Mother of the universe,' this East Asian philosophical concept's Chinese character means 'the way' or 'path' — what is it?
Tao: Philosophical concept native to China.
According to Arthurian legend, this queen of Great Britain was famously seduced by Mordred during his rebellion against her husband, King Arthur — who is she?
Guinevere: Arthurian legend character. Guinevere has continued to be a popular character featured in numerous adaptations of the legend since the 19th-century Arthurian revival.
The son of Spain's dictator from 1923 to 1930, this lawyer founded the national syndicalist Falange Española in October 1933 — who was he?
José Antonio Primo de Rivera: Spanish politician and founder of Falange Española (1903–1936)
Emerging in the 1970s among disillusioned liberal hawks, this political movement peaked in influence under George W. Bush and helped drive the push to invade Iraq in 2003 — what is it called?
Neoconservatism: Political movement of former liberals that combines political and social conservatism.

This organizational process shifts planning and decision-making authority away from a central group to smaller units, and applies across politics, business, and even monetary systems — what's it called?
The first person to walk to both the North and South Poles, this explorer later led his son on a 600-mile renewable-energy-only trek to the South Pole in 2017 — who is he?
Serving as Adolf Hitler's personal lawyer before becoming governor-general of occupied Polish territory during World War II, which convicted war criminal ran a brutal wartime administration there?
Hans Frank: German politician and war criminal (1900–1946)
Serving as Saudi Arabia's crown prince and interior minister before being abruptly replaced in 2017, this royal has been held in detention since March 2020 — who is he?
A Polish politician known by his initials, he served in the European Parliament and led several parties before founding a new one in 2024 — who is he?
Janusz Korwin-Mikke: Polish far-right politician and publicist (born 1942)
Regarded as Troy's greatest warrior in Homer's Iliad, this prince was ultimately slain by Achilles, who dragged his body around the city behind a chariot — who was he?
Hector: Trojan hero in Greek mythology.

This Greek king of the Hellenistic era was among ancient Rome's fiercest early opponents, and his costly victories over the Romans inspired a phrase still used today for a win that costs too much — who was he?
Pyrrhus of Epirus (Ancient; 319/318-272 BC) was a Greek king and statesman of the Hellenistic period.
Serving as Ukraine's Minister of Defence from late 2021 until his dismissal in 2023, this politician previously held several other senior government roles in Kyiv — who is he?
Oleksii Reznikov: Ukrainian lawyer and politician (born 1966)
At age 47, he became the oldest person to walk on the Moon in 1971 — a full decade after piloting Freedom 7 to become the first American in space. Who is he?
Based on the island of Sumatra, this maritime empire became a key center for spreading Buddhism across Southeast Asia between the 7th and 11th centuries — which empire?
Srivijaya: Empire based on Sumatra (c. 671–1025 AD)
Serving as Lord Chancellor before becoming Archbishop of Canterbury, this cleric clashed with King Henry II and was murdered by the king's men in 1170 — who was he?
Thomas Becket: Archbishop of Canterbury from 1162 to 1170.
This North Carolina senator ran as the Democratic vice-presidential nominee alongside Kerry in 2004, after twice seeking his party's presidential nomination — who was he?
John Edwards: American lawyer and politician (born 1953)
Proclaimed emperor the day after his brother Nicholas II abdicated in 1917, this youngest son of Alexander III declined the throne just a day later — who was he?
Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia
Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia
Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia: Son of Tsar Alexander III (1878–1918)
Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia
An Islamic scholar and Sufi who unexpectedly found himself commanding tribal fighters, he held off French colonial forces in Algiers for seventeen years before surrendering in 1847 — who was he?
Emir Abdelkader: Algerian religious and military leader (1808–1883)
This World War II Army officer served with the 101st Airborne's parachute infantry regiment and was portrayed by Ron Livingston in Band of Brothers — who was he?
Lewis Nixon III: United States Army officer (1918–1995)

Named by the prophet Mani as one of the four great powers of the 3rd century — alongside Persia, Rome, and China — this African realm was centered on a city in what's now Eritrea and northern Ethiopia. What was it?
Kingdom of Aksum: Polity in Africa and Arabia before 960.
Leading the final leg of the 1925 dash to deliver diphtheria antitoxin to Nome, Alaska, this sled dog earned a statue in Central Park — who is he?
Balto: Siberian husky and sled dog (1919–1933)
Elected to India's parliament at just 26 — the youngest in the country's history at the time — this Congress politician later served as Rajasthan's deputy chief minister — who is he?
In Greek myth, this Phoenician princess was abducted by a god disguised as a bull and became mother to Crete's King Minos — who was she?
Europa (consort of Zeus): Greek mythology character, daughter of Agenor.

Serving as the Soviet Union's largely ceremonial head of state from 1919 to 1946 while real power sat with Stalin, this former metalworker had been mayor of Petrograd after the October Revolution — who was he?
Leader of Finland's National Coalition Party since 2016, this politician became prime minister after his party topped the 2023 parliamentary election with a plurality of the vote — who is he?
Petteri Orpo: Prime Minister of Finland since 2023. Antti Petteri Orpo (born 3 November 1969) is a Finnish politician currently serving as the prime minister of Finland since 2023.
Elected to Israel's Knesset at just 28, this politician later served two terms as Mayor of Jerusalem before becoming prime minister from 2006 to 2009 — who is he?
Ehud Olmert: Prime Minister of Israel from 2006 to 2009. The son of a former Herut politician, Olmert was first elected to the Knesset for Likud in 1973, at the age of 28.
Nicknamed the 'Expressway Man of India' for spearheading projects like the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, this politician has served as Minister of Road Transport since 2014 — who is he?

Since 2019, this politician has led the Community of Madrid — the first time the region's government relied on a coalition, and the first time a far-right party propped it up from outside. Who is she?
This Haitian general rose from a slave rebellion to become Governor-General-for-life of Saint-Domingue before ultimately clashing with Napoleon's troops. Who was he?
Toussaint Louverture: Haitian general and revolutionary (1744–1803)
Fill in the blank: “____ (born 16 February 1983) is a Galician publicist and political activist.”
Alejandra Silva (born 16 February 1983) is a Galician publicist and political activist.
A World War II Army veteran, this civil rights activist became the NAACP's first field secretary in Mississippi and applied to the state's all-white law school before his assassination. Who was he?
Medgar Evers: American civil rights activist (1925–1963)
The first Ottoman sultan to travel diplomatically to Western Europe — visiting Paris, London, and Vienna in 1867 — he was overthrown in a coup in 1876. Who was he?
Abdulaziz: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1861 to 1876.
This ancient Levantine kingdom appears in the campaign records of pharaohs Seti I and Ramesses III, and was ultimately destroyed by the Babylonians in the 6th century BC. What was it?
Edom: Ancient kingdom in the southern Levant.
A nephew of Constantine the Great, this Roman emperor rejected Christianity in favor of Neoplatonic paganism, earning him the enduring nickname 'the Apostate' — who was he?
Julian (emperor) (Ancient; 331 - 26 June 363) was the Caesar of the West from 355 to 360 and Roman emperor from 361 to 363, as well as a notable philosopher and author in Greek.
Elected in 2019 after a brief stint as prime minister that same year, this head of state became, following a 2026 death, the only living former president of his North African nation. Who is he?
Abdelmadjid Tebboune: President of Algeria since 2019.

The younger brother of Louis XIV and founder of a cadet branch of the House of Bourbon, this 17th-century French royal, known simply as 'Monsieur,' won a notable military victory over William of Orange at the Battle of Cassel. Who was he?
Philippe I, Duke of Orléans: French prince (1640–1701)

The mother of Diana, Princess of Wales, and maternal grandmother of two future heirs to the British throne, this aristocrat devoted her later years to Catholic charity work after converting to that faith. Who was she?
Frances Shand Kydd: Mother of Diana, Princess of Wales (1936–2004)

Serving as governor of California in two widely separated stretches, 1975-83 and 2011-19, this politician also worked as the state's secretary of state, mayor of Oakland, and attorney general, and is the son of a man who held the same governorship two decades earlier. Who is he?
An Olympic gold medal-winning horseman for Great Britain, this equestrian was the first husband of Anne, Princess Royal, and now works as a course designer and magazine columnist. Who is he?
Mark Phillips: English equestrian. Mark Anthony Peter Phillips (born 22 September 1948) is an English Olympic gold medal-winning horseman who competed for Great Britain.

Developed by Giovanni Gentile and Benito Mussolini as an originally left-wing, anti-clerical movement, this ideology governed the Kingdom of Italy from 1922 to 1943, then its Social Republic until 1945 — which specific strain of the ideology is this?
Italian fascism: Fascist ideology as developed in Italy. Italian fascism is also associated with the post-war Italian Social Movement (MSI) and later Italian neo-fascist political organizations.
On 5 May 1862, outnumbered Mexican forces repelled a French army trying to storm two hilltop forts outside a Mexican city, inspiring today's Cinco de Mayo celebrations — which clash was it?
Battle of Puebla: Part of the French intervention in Mexico.
Ruling Galilee and Perea as tetrarch, this New Testament figure is blamed for the executions of John the Baptist and Jesus of Nazareth — who was he?
Herod Antipas: 1st-century AD tetrarch of Galilee and Perea (r. 1–39)
Ascending the Siamese throne in 1782 following the deposition of King Taksin, this monarch became the first ruler of the Chakri dynasty and founded the city that is now Bangkok — who was he?
Rama I: King of Siam from 1782 to 1809.

Sparked partly by Emperor Hadrian's plan to rebuild Jerusalem as a Roman colony dedicated to Jupiter, this 132–136 CE uprising was the last and most devastating of the major Jewish rebellions against Rome, leading to Judea's near-total depopulation — which uprising was it?
Bar Kokhba Revolt: Jewish rebellion against Roman rule (132–136 CE)

This ancient Greek term, found throughout the New Testament, denotes God's covenant love for humanity and a sacrificial love that transcends personal circumstance, distinct from brotherly philia or romantic eros — what's the word?
Agape: Greek word for love. Agape (from Ancient Greek ἀγάπη (agápē)) is "the highest form of love, charity" and "the love of God for [human beings] and of [human beings] for God".

The principal wife of Ramesses the Great, this Egyptian queen was rare among her peers for being literate in hieroglyphs — a skill she used in royal diplomatic correspondence — and had her own temple built beside his at Abu Simbel. Who was she?
Nefertari: Wife of the Egyptian pharaoh Ramesses II.

The first Mexican-American woman elected to Congress from Florida, this Air Force veteran represents the state's 13th district after winning her seat in 2022 with a Trump primary endorsement — who is she?
Widely credited as the founder of modern conservative political philosophy, this Anglo-Irish Whig MP's writings shaped British and French opinion after the 1789 Revolution — who is he?
Edmund Burke: Anglo-Irish politician and philosopher (1729–1797)

The only daughter of a famous Egyptian queen and her Roman general lover, this princess was raised in Rome after her parents' deaths and went on to rule Mauretania as queen alongside her husband, the Berber prince Juba — who was she?
Cleopatra Selene II: Queen of Mauretania, 25 to 5 BC.
Ruling as the fifth Umayyad caliph from 685 until 705, this leader spent his reign wrestling back control of the fractured Caliphate from a Mecca-based rival — who was he?
Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan: Umayyad caliph from 685 to 705. Abd al-Malik's final years were marked by a domestically peaceful and prosperous consolidation of power.

Rising from minor gentry to become the assassinated favourite — and rumored lover — of King James VI and I, this courtier kept his hold on royal favour into the reign of James's son Charles I — who was he?
George Villiers, 1st Duke of Buckingham: English politician (1592–1628)

Stretching from the Gulf of Finland to the Ural Mountains, this medieval city-state thrived as the easternmost outpost of the Hanseatic League and let its citizens' assembly elect and depose princes — what was it?

Named for the Latin word for 'body,' this political ideology has trade and professional associations bargain collectively with government, advocating cooperation between classes rather than struggle between them — what is it?
Corporatism: Political ideology which advocates the organization of society by corporate groups.

This Renaissance-era Florentine banker used his fortune to become the city's de facto first ruler, commissioning a bronze statue considered the first freestanding nude male sculpture since antiquity — who was he?
Cosimo de' Medici: Lord of Florence from 1434 to 1464.
Founded by Serge Kampf in 1974 and headquartered in Paris, this French IT consulting giant made headlines in 2000 by buying Ernst & Young's consulting arm for roughly $11 billion — which company?

Before becoming president of the European Council in 2024, this Lisbon-born politician served nearly nine years as prime minister of Portugal after earlier stints as mayor of his home city — who is he?

António Costa: President of the European Council since 2024. António Luís Santos da Costa (born 17 July 1961) is a Portuguese lawyer and politician who has served as president of the European Council since 2024.
Existing from the mid-12th century to the early 20th, this western Iberian monarchy briefly anchored a transatlantic union with Brazil and the Algarves from 1815 to 1822 — which kingdom?
Kingdom of Portugal was a monarchy in the western Iberian Peninsula and the predecessor of the modern Portuguese Republic.
After seizing power in a 1966 coup, this Central African leader later crowned himself emperor of a short-lived empire before being overthrown in 1979 — who was he?
Jean-Bédel Bokassa: Leader of Central Africa from 1966 to 1979.
On January 15, 1919, a burst storage tank sent a wave of sticky liquid rushing through Boston's North End at 35 mph, killing 21 — what disaster was this?
Great Molasses Flood: 1919 accident in Massachusetts, United States.
A member of Japan's Liberal Democratic Party, this politician served as Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary and State Minister for Foreign Affairs under the Third Abe Cabinet — who is he?
This Iron Age kingdom in western Anatolia, capital at Sardis, minted some of the world's oldest coins from electrum before falling to the Achaemenid Empire in 546 BC — which kingdom?

This historiographical term describes unrestrained monarchical power during Europe's transition from feudalism to capitalism, marked by the consolidation of state power and a decline in the church's influence — what is it called?
Absolutism (European history): Form of unrestrained monarchical power. There is a considerable variety of opinion by historians on the extent of absolutism among European monarchs.
Sometimes anachronistically called Elizabeth, this woman was empress consort to China's last emperor before later becoming empress consort of the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo — who was she?
Wanrong: Empress of Manchukuo from 1934 to 1945 (1906–1946)

Born in Centreville, Mississippi and educated at Vanderbilt, UVA Law, and Oxford, this Republican has served as Louisiana's junior U.S. Senator since 2017 after 17 years as the state's Treasurer — name this politician?
John Kennedy (Louisiana politician) (born November 21, 1951) is an American politician and attorney who has served as the junior United States senator from Louisiana since 2017.
This King of Sweden turned his country into a major European power during the Thirty Years' War, clinching a decisive win at the Battle of Breitenfeld in 1631 — who was he?
Gustavus Adolphus: King of Sweden from 1611 to 1632.
A media consultant for three Republican presidents, this longtime Fox News chairman had hemophilia, a condition that complicated the injury that eventually caused his 2017 death — who was he?
Roger Ailes: American TV executive and consultant (1940–2017)
Likely fictional according to most scholars, this legendary heroine from China's Northern and Southern dynasties era was later depicted in the 'Table of Peerless Heroes' — who is she?
Hua Mulan: Legendary Chinese heroine. Scholars generally consider Mulan to be a fictional character.
Born Amir, this military commander was one of ten companions promised Paradise by the Prophet Muhammad and led a large section of the Rashidun Army before dying in the Plague of Amwas — who was he?
Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah: Companion of Muhammad and military leader (583–639)
Starting out as a cartoonist for The Free Press Journal in Bombay, this Indian politician went on to found the original Shiv Sena party — who was he?
Bal Thackeray: Indian cartoonist and politician (1926-2012)
A former Conservative Cabinet minister under both Thatcher and Major, this broadcaster now hosts Great British Railway Journeys — who is he?
Michael Portillo: British broadcaster, journalist and former politician (born 1953)
Serving as Chief Minister of Odisha for 24 years until 2024, this politician also founded the Biju Janata Dal in 1997 — who is he?
Switching from the Congress party to the BJP in 2020, this Indian politician now serves as Minister of Communications after decades representing the Guna constituency — who is he?
Nicknamed the 'Red Napoleon' for his Civil War victories, this Soviet general was later executed during Stalin's purges after commanding forces in the Polish-Soviet War — who is he?
Mikhail Tukhachevsky: Russian and Soviet military leader (1893–1937)
After leading Taiwan's Environmental Protection Administration, this media personality co-founded the pro-unification New Party and ran for vice president on the KMT ticket in 2024 — who is he?
Jaw Shaw-kong: Taiwanese media personality and politician.
This giant huntsman of Greek myth was placed among the stars by Zeus or Artemis, and one legend even credits him with carving out the shape of the Strait of Sicily — who is he?
Orion (mythology) (: Ancient) was a giant huntsman whom Zeus or Artemis placed among the stars as a constellation.
Trained as a barrister in London before leading a Hyderabad-based Indian political party founded by his family, who is this five-term MP repeatedly named among the world's most influential Muslims?
The daughter of a former Arkansas governor, this politician became the third woman ever to serve as White House press secretary before winning the Arkansas governorship herself in 2022 — who is she?
Sarah Huckabee Sanders: Governor of Arkansas since 2023.
Famed for slicing his military cloak in two with his sword to clothe a freezing beggar, this Roman-cavalry-veteran-turned-bishop became one of Europe's most venerated patron saints — who was he?
Martin of Tours: Christian cleric and saint (316/336–397)
Undertaken by Muhammad and his companions in December 629 or January 630, this military campaign against the Quraysh confederation formally ended their long conflict — what was it called?
Conquest of Mecca: Military campaign in early Muslim history, 629–630 CE.
A Russian lawyer-turned-politician who chaired the Duma's Family, Women and Children Affairs committee, she drew attention in 2012 for drafting controversial LGBT-related legislation — who is she?

Beginning immediately after independence from Portugal in November 1975 and lasting, with interludes, until 2002, this conflict pitted the communist MPLA against the anti-communist UNITA — which nation's power struggle was this?
Angolan Civil War: 1975–2002 military conflict. The Angolan Civil War (Portuguese: Guerra Civil Angolana) was a civil war in Angola, beginning in 1975 and continuing, with interludes, until 2002.
Serving under four different chief ministers across more than eight years and six terms, this politician was Maharashtra's longest-serving deputy chief minister until his death in 2026 — who was he?

Centered on the Armenian highlands between three great lakes and locked in frequent wars with Assyria, this Iron Age kingdom left behind cuneiform inscriptions and massive fortresses before falling to the Medes or Cyrus the Great — what kingdom was it?
Urartu: Iron-Age kingdom of the ancient Near East.
Called the "Chief of all Muses" by both Hesiod and Ovid, this Greek goddess whose name means "beautiful-voiced" presided over eloquence and epic poetry — who was she?
According to the New Testament, this imprisoned bandit was freed instead of Jesus when a Passover crowd chose him for pardon by the Roman governor Pontius Pilate — who was he?
Barabbas: Figure mentioned in the New Testament.

Serving four non-consecutive terms as British Prime Minister between 1868 and 1894 — more than anyone else — this Liverpool-born statesman began as a Conservative MP before becoming the face of the Liberal Party — who was he?
The eldest son of a former U.S. president and first lady, this businessman and environmentalist ran as the Democratic nominee in Nevada's 2006 Senate election — who is he?
Jack Carter (politician) (born July 3, 1947) is an American businessman, politician and environmentalist.

Founded in 1892 by Filipino nationalists including Andrés Bonifacio, this revolutionary secret society was abbreviated KKK and sought independence from Spain, its 1896 discovery sparking a revolution — what was it called?
Katipunan: Filipino secret society during the Spanish colonization.

Born to a family of strawberry farmers in Akita Prefecture, this politician rose to become Japan's Prime Minister from 2020 to 2021 after years as Chief Cabinet Secretary under Shinzo Abe — who is he?

Yoshihide Suga: Prime Minister of Japan from 2020 to 2021. Yoshihide Suga (菅 義偉, Suga Yoshihide; born 6 December 1948) is a Japanese former politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan from 2020 to 2021.
Said to be a daughter of Loki, this Norse underworld ruler was appointed by Odin to preside over a shadowy realm in Niflheim, where she receives a portion of the dead — who is she?
Hel (mythological being): Underworld entity in Norse mythology.
The only communist state ever to exist in the Arab world, this nation in southern Arabia had its capital at Aden before unifying with its northern neighbor in 1990 — what was it?
South Yemen: 1967–1990 state in Western Asia.
Awarded the Pour le Mérite after being wounded in a 1918 offensive, this German author turned his World War I experiences into the memoir Storm of Steel — who is he?
Ernst Jünger: German soldier and author (1895–1998)
Born and raised in Oklahoma, this Massachusetts senator finished third in the 2020 Democratic presidential primary behind Joe Biden and Bernie Sanders — who is she?
A four-star general who staged a 1999 coup against Nawaz Sharif's government, this military officer went on to serve as Pakistan's president from 2001 to 2008 — who was he?

Pervez Musharraf: President of Pakistan from 2001 to 2008. Pervez Musharraf (11 August 1943 – 5 February 2023) was a Pakistani politician and military officer who served as the tenth president of Pakistan from 2001 to 2008.
Existing from 57 BCE to 935 CE and forming the Three Kingdoms of Korea alongside Paekche and Goguryeo, which kingdom had the smallest population of the three?
Silla: Korean kingdom (57 BCE–935 CE). Silla was one of the longest-lasting countries in Korean history.
An Iranic nomadic people connected to the Yancai and Aorsi of ancient sources, this group dominated the Pontic-Caspian steppe before the Goths broke their hold in the 3rd century CE — who were they?
Alans: Ancient Iranic people of the North Caucasus.
This New Zealand politician served as the country's 41st prime minister for just ten months in 2023 before becoming leader of the Opposition — who is he?

Chris Hipkins: Prime Minister of New Zealand in 2023. Hipkins was born and raised in the Hutt Valley in Wellington, and while at Victoria University of Wellington became heavily involved in student politics.
The only U.S. Army general ever awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, in 1953, he devised the postwar European recovery program that bears his name after serving as Army Chief of Staff — who is he?
George C. Marshall: American politician and United States Army general (1880–1959)
Known as the 'Bandit Queen,' this Indian outlaw-turned-politician was charged in absentia over a 1981 massacre before later serving as a member of parliament — who is she?
Phoolan Devi: Indian bandit and politician (1963–2001)

Louis Philippe I styled himself 'King of the French' rather than 'King of France' during this liberal regime that began with an 1830 revolution and ended with another uprising in 1848 — what was it called?
Nicknamed 'Black Jack,' this general commanded the American Expeditionary Forces in World War I and mentored future leaders like Eisenhower, Patton, and MacArthur — who is he?
John J. Pershing: United States Army general (1860–1948)
Serving as the 44th vice president under George H. W. Bush, this Republican represented Indiana in both the House and Senate before his time in the White House — who is he?
Dan Quayle: Vice President of the United States from 1989 to 1993.
A leading orator of the Cordeliers Club, this French Revolutionary politician became Minister of Justice in 1792 and the first president of the Committee of Public Safety — who is he?
This Iraqi militant became the second caliph of the Islamic State in 2019, appointed by a shura council within a week of his predecessor's suicide, and died by his own suicide in 2022. Who was he?

Abu Ibrahim al-Hashimi al-Qurashi (born Amir Mohammed Abdul Rahman al-Mawli al-Salbi; 1 or 5 October 1976 - 3 February 2022) was an Iraqi militant and the second caliph of the Islamic State from 2019 until his suicide in 2022.
Son of King Telamon, this towering Greek warrior was considered second only to Achilles in Homer's Iliad — who is he?
Ajax the Great: Character in Greek Mythology.
Faithful wife of Odysseus, this legendary Queen of Ithaca famously used weaving schemes to stall over a hundred suitors — who is she?
Penelope: Wife of Odysseus in Greek mythology.
Also called 'the Canaanite,' this apostle of Jesus was omitted from Jerome's fourth-century collection of biographies despite some writings falsely attributed to him — who is he?
Simon the Zealot: Apostle of Jesus.

According to this piece of folklore, chanting a name repeatedly in front of a mirror will summon a spirit — sometimes benevolent, sometimes malevolent — said to reveal glimpses of the future. Name the legend?
Bloody Mary (folklore) is a legend of a ghost, phantom, witch, or spirit conjured to reveal the future.
This military officer became North Yemen's president after his predecessor's assassination in 1978, then led the unified Republic of Yemen from 1990 until resigning in 2012 — who is he?

Ali Abdullah Saleh: President of Yemen from 1978 to 2012. A veteran and officer of the North Yemen civil war, Saleh consolidated power and restored civilian rule after al-Ghashmi's assassination in 1978.

Dubbed Kyiv's 'Green Cardinal' by Politico, this former film producer served as Volodymyr Zelenskyy's right-hand man atop the presidential office until resigning after a 2025 corruption raid — who is he?
Andriy Yermak: Ukrainian film producer and politician (born 1971)
Founded in Limoges, France in 1969 and now owned by LVMH, this beauty retailer stocks nearly 340 brands alongside its own private label — which company?
After a U.S. Navy frigate nearly sank hitting an Iranian mine in the Persian Gulf, American forces launched this 1988 one-day retaliatory strike on Iranian naval targets — what was it called?
Operation Praying Mantis: 1988 US attack on Iran in the Iran-Iraq War.
Denmark's youngest-ever prime minister, she became the second woman to hold the post when she succeeded Helle Thorning-Schmidt as party leader — who is she?
Mette Frederiksen: Prime Minister of Denmark since 2019.
Formed in 2015 as a reformation of a party once led by Jacques Chirac, this conservative party, inspired by Gaullism, saw its 2017 presidential candidate place third — which party?
In Arthurian legend, this enchantress figure gifts Excalibur to the king, raises the knight Lancelot, and later helps carry the dying king to Avalon — who or what is she?
Lady of the Lake: Sorceress in Arthurian legend. As either single character or multiple ones, the figure of the Lady of the Lake often appears in various roles in the works of modern culture.
A former New Left activist at Meiji University, this Japanese writer founded a now-disbanded militant group that relocated to the Middle East in 1971 to pursue world revolution — who is she?
Fusako Shigenobu: Japanese communist activist. Born in Japan, Shigenobu became involved in New Left activism while attending night school at Meiji University in Tokyo.
Serving three non-consecutive terms as Chief Minister of Rajasthan, this Congress politician represents the Sardarpura constituency in Jodhpur — who is he?
Governor of five different Indian states over his career, this politician was serving as the final governor of Jammu and Kashmir when its special status was revoked in 2019 — who is he?
Originally founded as Thomson-CSF in 1968 and headquartered in Paris's La Défense district, this French aerospace and defence electronics giant was rebranded in 2000 — which company?

Thales Group: French multinational company. Thales S.A., trading as Thales Group (French pronunciation: [talɛs]), is a French multinational aerospace and defence corporation specialising in electronics.
As Vice Chair of Russia's State Duma from a liberal-leaning party, he ran in the 2024 presidential election calling for peace negotiations 'without a rollback' — who is he?

This Yemeni religious and political leader has headed a Zaydi Shia rebel movement since 2004, succeeding his brother, the group's founder, after his death in battle, and became a central figure in Yemen's civil war. Who is he?

Abdul-Malik al-Houthi (born 22 May 1979) is a Yemeni politician and religious leader who is the second leader of the Houthis (Ansar Allah), an organization principally made up of Zaydi Shia Muslims, since 2004.
This Austrian mountaineer joined the four-man team that first climbed the Eiger's North Face in 1938, then later spent years in Tibet, chronicled in a bestselling memoir — who is he?
Heinrich Harrer: Austrian mountaineer and author (1912–2006)
This 7th-century Chinese Buddhist monk journeyed to the Indian subcontinent from 629 to 645 CE and brought back more than 650 Sanskrit texts to translate — who is he?
Xuanzang: Chinese Buddhist monk and scholar (602–664)

After a failed plot to kidnap Eleanor of Aquitaine got him banished from Poitou, this Frankish knight became king of Jerusalem through marriage to Queen Sibylla, only to lose the kingdom to Saladin — who was he?
Guy de Lusignan, King of Jersusalem and Cyprus
Guy of Lusignan: King of Jerusalem from 1186 to 1192.
Worshipped as the consort of the god El and associated with fertility, motherhood, and sacred trees like the date palm, this ancient Semitic goddess was also known by the title Elat — who is she?
Asherah: Ancient Semitic goddess. Asherah was a major goddess in ancient Northwest Semitic cultures, often associated with fertility, motherhood, and sacred trees.

Beginning in 1964 and rooted in a period of violence sparked by the 1948 assassination of a liberal leader, this decades-long struggle pitted the government against far-right paramilitaries and far-left guerrillas like the FARC — what's it called?
Colombian conflict: Low-intensity asymmetric war in Colombia.
Bookended by the Black Death and the Hundred Years' War, this 1300–1500 stretch of European history preceded the Renaissance — what period is it?
Late Middle Ages: Period of European history between AD 1300 and 1500.
Dwelling in the wetland halls of Fensalir, this Norse goddess of marriage and prophecy was the wife of Odin — who is she?
Frigg: Germanic goddess. The names ultimately stem from the Proto-Germanic theonym *Frijjō.
One of the original Mercury Seven, this astronaut became the second American in space in 1961 and later commanded Gemini and Apollo missions — who is he?

Developed in early 20th-century Europe, this modern pagan movement reconstructs the pre-Christian beliefs of the Germanic peoples using historical, archaeological, and folkloric evidence — what is it called?
Heathenry (new religious movement): Modern pagan religion. Heathenry, also termed Heathenism, contemporary Germanic Paganism, or Germanic Neopaganism, is a modern pagan religion.
This Cold War-era proxy conflict broke out after a Central African nation's abrupt 1960 independence from Belgium, ending with Joseph-Désiré Mobutu in full control — which crisis?
Congo Crisis: 1960–1965 political unrest in Central Africa.
Founded in 1949 and central to Bangladesh's independence struggle, this party dominated the country's politics from 2009 until being ousted in 2024's July Uprising — which party?
Awami League: Banned political party in Bangladesh.
Born in New Jersey and partly raised in Iran, this highly decorated Vietnam veteran commanded all coalition forces in the Gulf War as head of U.S. Central Command — who is he?
Norman Schwarzkopf Jr.: United States Army general (1934–2012)
Often appearing as a crow and said to wash the bloodstained clothes of those fated to die in battle, which Irish goddess of war and fate is known as the 'phantom queen'?
The Morrígan: Figure from Irish mythology.
Equated by the Romans with the Greek goddess Athena, this member of the Capitoline Triad favors an owl as her sacred creature — who is she?
Sympathizing with the Girondins, this young Frenchwoman fatally stabbed revolutionary leader Jean-Paul Marat in his bath in 1793 — who was she?
Marie Anne Charlotte de Corday d'Armont
Also known as Brahmanism, this ancient belief system of Indo-Aryan peoples in Punjab and the western Ganges plain (c. 1500-500 BCE) gave rise to today's Hinduism — what was it called?
Historical Vedic religion: 1500–500 BC Indo-Aryan religious practices of northwest India.
Worshipped by the peoples of the Andes as a mother goddess of space and time, this Inca deity is the wife of Pachacámac and mother of the sun and moon gods — who is she?

This sweeping historical period saw two new superpowers emerge, the United Nations get founded, Western Europe rebuilt under the Marshall Plan, and colonies across Asia and Africa gain independence — what period is this?
Aftermath of World War II: Events after the end of the war in 1945.
Recording six visions seen by a prophet exiled in Babylon between 593 and 571 BC, this prophetic text follows Isaiah and Jeremiah in the Christian Bible — which text?
Book of Ezekiel is the third of the Latter Prophets in the Tanakh (Hebrew Bible) and one of the major prophetic books in the Christian Bible, where it follows Isaiah and Jeremiah.
Rising to power under Theodoric the Great, who founded a kingdom in Italy in 493 after defeating Odoacer and ruled from Ravenna, which Germanic people were these?
The youngest son of Genghis Khan, this Mongol general served as regent of the empire before his brother Ögedei took the throne, and fathered future khans Möngke and Kublai — who was he?
Tolui: Regent of the Mongol Empire from 1227 to 1229.
On May 4, 1886, a dynamite bomb thrown at police during a Chicago labor rally for the eight-hour workday triggered gunfire that killed eleven people — what is this incident called?
Haymarket affair: 1886 bombing aftermath in Chicago, US.
Named for the two censuses of the Israelites it records, this fourth part of the Torah opens at Mount Sinai just after the Law is given — which text?
Book of Numbers (from Greek, Arithmoi, lit. 'numbers') is the fourth book of the Hebrew Bible and the fourth of five books of the Jewish Torah.
Deified after her life as a Fujian shamaness in the late 10th century, this sea goddess is revered by Chinese sailors and fishermen and honored as a Queen of Heaven -- who is she?
Mazu: Chinese sea goddess. Mazu or Matsu is a sea goddess in Chinese folk religion, Chinese Buddhism, Confucianism, and Taoism.
Loyal to the Polish government-in-exile in London, this WWII underground resistance force swelled to as many as 600,000 fighters against German occupation — which organization?
Home Army: World War II Polish resistance movement.
Often shown as a nude woman covered in stars and arching protectively over the Earth, this Egyptian deity embodies the sky itself — who is she?
Nut (goddess) (Ancient), also known by various other transcriptions, is the goddess of the sky, stars, cosmos, mothers, astronomy, and the universe in the ancient Egyptian religion.
Lasting from about 800 BC until a Persian invasion in 480 BC, this era saw a massive population boom and the rise of the city-state, or polis — which historical period?
Archaic Greece was the period in Greek history lasting from c.

Regarded as the fourth person to accept Islam, this former slave became the adopted son of the Prophet Muhammad and later commanded early Muslim military expeditions, including a final raid on Byzantine-held Bosra in 629 CE — who was he?
Zayd ibn Haritha al-Kalbi: Companion and adopted son of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.
Bribed by Philistine lords to learn the secret of a mighty Nazirite's strength, this biblical woman finally coaxed out the truth about his hair — who is she?
Delilah: Woman in the Book of Judges of the Hebrew Bible.

Beginning with the 1916 death of Yuan Shikai, this chaotic decade-plus in Chinese history saw the country splinter under rival military cliques until Sun Yat-sen's Nationalists challenged the Beijing government for legitimacy — which period?
Warlord Era: Period in the history of the Republic of China (1916–1928)
Led by Stepan Petrichenko in March 1921, this 16-day uprising by Soviet sailors was the last major revolt against Bolshevik rule during the Russian Civil War — what was it called?
Kronstadt rebellion: 1921 anti-Bolshevik revolt in Russia.
Coined by Suharto to distinguish his rule from that of his predecessor Sukarno, this label described the government that lasted from 1966 to his 1998 resignation — what was it called?
New Order (Indonesia) was the regime of the second Indonesian President Suharto from his rise to power in 1966 until his resignation in 1998.
Sparked by King Antiochus IV's ban on Jewish religious practices in 168 BCE, this uprising against Seleucid rule eventually won the rebels independence in Judea — which historic rebellion?

Maccabean Revolt: Jewish rebellion against the Seleucids. The rebels as a whole would come to be known as the Maccabees, and their actions would be chronicled later in the books of 1 Maccabees and 2 Maccabees.
This elastic, muscular part of the female reproductive tract extends from the vulva to the cervix and is where mammals give birth. What is it?

Vagina: Part of the female reproductive tract. The vagina (pl.: vaginas or vaginae) is the elastic, muscular reproductive organ of the female genital tract through which mammals copulate and give birth.
Co-founding a company in his Harvard dorm room in February 2004, he became the world's youngest self-made billionaire at age 23. Who is he?
Mark Zuckerberg: American businessman and programmer (born 1984)
Feigning injury or authority to lure victims to his car, this American serial killer murdered young women across five states in the mid-1970s before revisiting their graves. Who was he?
After a cross-country road trip from New York to Seattle, this Princeton engineering graduate founded an online bookstore in 1994 that grew into a global e-commerce giant. Who is he?
Its visible portion, the glans, is roughly the size of a pea yet packs over 10,000 nerve endings, making it the primary source of female sexual pleasure. What is this organ?
Clitoris: Erectile female sexual organ. In amniotes, the clitoris (KLIT-ər-iss or klih-TOR-iss; pl.: clitorises or clitorides) is a female sex organ.
Comprising the mons pubis, labia, clitoris, and vaginal opening, these external structures of the female genitalia are supplied by the pudendal arteries. What is this collectively called?
Vulva: External genitalia of the female mammal. The folds of the outer and inner labia provide a double layer of protection for the vagina (which leads to the uterus).
Dropped out of Stanford to co-found Loopt, later led Y Combinator, then became CEO of the company behind ChatGPT — briefly ousted by its board in 2023 for not being 'consistently candid.' Who is he?
Sam Altman: American entrepreneur and investor (born 1985)
Predicted by Einstein's general relativity, this astronomical body is so compact that not even light can escape past its event horizon. What is it?
Black hole: Compact astronomical body. A black hole is an astronomical body so compact that its gravity prevents anything, including light, from escaping.
A Communist Party member and Stanford-trained psychiatrist, this woman is best remembered for her romantic relationship with J. Robert Oppenheimer, which put her under FBI surveillance. Who is she?
Ejaculated through the urethra and containing fructose plus enzymes that help sperm survive their journey to fertilize an egg, this bodily fluid is also collected for animal breeding. What is it?
Semen: Reproductive biofluid of male or hermaphroditic animals.
This NMDA-receptor-blocking anesthetic induces a trance-like dissociative state while preserving breathing and raising blood pressure, and at lower doses treats resistant depression — which drug?
Once used in Italy for hunting large game and herding cattle, this mastiff breed today mostly serves as a guard dog or companion — which breed?
Cane Corso: Italian breed of mastiff. It is usually kept as a companion dog or guard dog; it may also be used to protect livestock.
About the size of a closed fist and enclosed in a protective sac called the pericardium, this four-chambered organ sits in the chest between the lungs and pumps blood through the body — which organ?
Heart: Organ found in humans and other animals.
After stints at the CIA, Dell, and Booz Allen Hamilton, this NSA contractor flew to Hong Kong in 2013 and leaked thousands of classified documents exposing global surveillance — who is he?
Edward Snowden: Whistleblower and NSA contractor (born 1983)
Named from a Greek word meaning 'wanderers,' these large rounded bodies orbit a star or similar object — our solar system has eight, from Mercury to Neptune. What are they called?
Planet: Large, round non-stellar astronomical object.
Immature at birth but developed by puberty, this network of organs includes the vagina, uterus, and fallopian tubes, protected by a fold called the labia majora — what's it called?
Female reproductive system is made up of the internal and external sex organs that function in the reproduction of new offspring.
First synthesized in 1912 by a Merck chemist, this stimulant known on the street as ecstasy or molly became linked to raves and electronic dance music in the 1980s — which drug?
MDMA: Psychoactive drug, often called ecstasy.
Tucked mostly beneath the right rib cage, this organ detoxifies the body, stores glucose as glycogen, and produces the bile that helps digest fat — which organ?
Liver: Vertebrate organ involved in metabolism.

Unique among mammals, human females are the only ones to permanently develop this secondary sex organ at puberty rather than just during pregnancy, and it later produces milk via the mammary gland — which body part?
Breast: Part of the female primate torso that has mammary glands.
A luminous ball of plasma held together by its own gravity, the closest example to Earth is the Sun — what celestial object is this?
Star: Large self-illuminated object in space.
Named after the Italian word for lemon, this citrus-scented compound comes in two mirror-image forms — one smelling of oranges, the other like pine — what is it?
This standard markup language structures web documents using elements delineated by tags, often paired with CSS and JavaScript — what is it?
HTML: Markup language for documents. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.

This British aviation entrepreneur held three Guinness World Records after visiting the South Pole, the Challenger Deep, and space, then died in 2023 aboard the submersible that imploded near the Titanic wreck — who was he?
Once used by German butchers to herd cattle and pull meat carts to market, this mastiff-type breed now works as a search-and-rescue and police dog — which breed?
Rottweiler: Large German dog breed. The Rottweiler (UK also, German: [ˈʁɔtvaɪ̯lɐ]) is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.
Located behind the stomach, this gland is 99 percent exocrine yet still secretes insulin and glucagon to regulate blood sugar — which organ?
Pancreas: Organ of the digestive system and endocrine system of vertebrates.
This physics principle states that current through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage across it, expressed as V equals I times R — what's it called?
Ohm's law: Law of electrical current and voltage. Ohm's law states that the electric current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.

Triggered when the body's own dysregulated response to infection starts damaging its tissues and organs, this life-threatening condition brings fever, rapid heartbeat, and confusion — which condition?

Sepsis: Life-threatening response to infection. Sepsis is a potentially life-threatening condition that arises when the body's dysregulated response to infection causes injury to its own tissues and organs.

Designed under the philosophy 'write once, run anywhere,' this high-level, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language compiles to bytecode executed by a dedicated virtual machine — name the language?
Java (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language.
With over three hundred species and tens of thousands of cultivars, this thorny, often-fragrant flowering shrub blooms in shades from white to pink, red, orange, and yellow — which plant?

Comprising two Einstein-authored physics frameworks published in 1905 and 1915 — one covering phenomena without gravity, the other explaining gravitation itself — this pair introduced four-dimensional spacetime and superseded Newtonian mechanics. Which pair of physics frameworks is this?
Theory of relativity: Two interrelated physics theories by Albert Einstein.

Marked by small white Koplik spots inside the mouth and a red rash that starts on the face before spreading, this highly contagious, vaccine-preventable disease can bring fevers over 40°C — which disease?
Typically starting to work within an hour, this NSAID relieves pain, fever, and inflammation but can worsen asthma and, in later pregnancy, is considered harmful — which drug?

First arising in wormlike organisms 550 to 600 million years ago, this body-wide network splits into a central hub of brain and spinal cord and a peripheral web of nerve fibers relaying signals to and from every body part — which network?
Nervous system: Part of an animal that coordinates actions and senses.
Bound together by gravity, this vast system of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter can range from a dwarf with under a thousand stars to a supergiant with a hundred trillion — what is it?
Galaxy: System of stars and interstellar matter. The word is derived from the Greek galaxias (γαλαξίας), meaning 'milky', a reference to the Milky Way galaxy that contains the Solar System.
Bred around 1890 by a Thuringian tax collector looking for a loyal guard dog, this sleek, high-alert German breed traditionally had its ears cropped and tail docked — which breed?
Dobermann: Black and tan dog breed from Germany.
Bred at a Scottish estate by crossing a flat-coated gun dog with Tweed Water Spaniels, this gentle, honey-coated working dog was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1913 — which breed?
Golden Retriever: Scottish breed of dog. It is characterised by a gentle and affectionate nature and a striking golden coat.
Typically housed in the head near the organs for vision, hearing, and smell, this organ processes thought and cognition while coordinating muscle activity — which organ?
Brain: Organ central to the nervous system.
Composed of plasma plus red cells, white cells, and platelets, this circulatory fluid delivers oxygen and nutrients to the body while carrying away waste — what is it?
Blood: Body fluid in the circulatory system. Plasma, which constitutes 55% of blood fluid, is mostly water (92% by volume), and contains proteins, glucose, mineral ions, and hormones.
Tucked beneath the liver, this pear-shaped organ stores and concentrates bile before releasing it to aid fat digestion in the small intestine — which organ?
Gallbladder: Organ in humans and other vertebrates.
First identified as a chemical in 1887 and later marketed as the drug Benzedrine, this CNS stimulant is prescribed today for ADHD and narcolepsy — which drug?

This late Cretaceous carnivore, whose scientific name pairs a word for 'tyrant' with the Latin for 'king,' roamed western North America right up until the mass extinction 66 million years ago — which iconic predator is it?
Tyrannosaurus: Genus of Late Cretaceous theropod.
Acting as a blood filter and red-blood-cell recycling center, which vertebrate organ also stores a reserve of blood for use during hemorrhagic shock?
Spleen: Immune organ that filters blood.

Caused by blocked or bleeding blood flow to the brain, this medical emergency can cause facial drooping and one-sided weakness — and if symptoms fade within a day, it's called a 'mini' version instead. What is this condition?
Stroke: Death of a region of brain cells due to poor blood flow.
Bearing distinctive fatty humps and used for milk, meat, and transport across deserts for millennia, which ungulate comes in a common one-humped form and a rarer two-humped form?
Bred in Germany with short legs and a long body to chase badgers into their burrows, which hound breed comes in smooth-, wire-, and long-haired varieties?
Starting his career as a materials engineer and later overseeing the launch of Chrome and Google Drive, who has served as CEO of both Google and its parent company since 2015 and 2019 respectively?
Sundar Pichai: CEO of Alphabet Inc. and Google (born 1972)
Sold under brand names like Ritalin and Concerta, which stimulant medication is preferred as the first-line treatment for ADHD in children, while amphetamine is favored for adults?
Hailing from the Anglo-Scottish frontier and frequently cited as the most intelligent dog breed on Earth, which sheepdog dominates sheepdog trials?
Border Collie: Working dog breed. The Border Collie is a breed of British herding dog of the collie type of medium size.
Also known as hemp when grown for fiber rather than its psychoactive use, this Asian-native plant genus includes up to three disputed species — which plant?
Found just below the bladder with the urethra passing through it, this male-only gland acts like a muscle-driven switch between urination and ejaculation — which organ?
Prostate: Gland of the male reproductive system.
The brightest star in Earth's night sky, this binary system in Canis Major pairs a bright main-sequence star with a faint white dwarf companion — which star?
Sirius: Brightest star in Earth's night sky. Its name is derived from the Greek word Σείριος (Latin script: Seirios; lit. 'glowing' or 'scorching').
Equal to the work done when a one-newton force moves an object one metre, this SI unit of energy is named for a 19th-century English physicist — which unit?
Joule: SI unit of energy. The joule ( JOOL, or JOWL; symbol: J) is the unit of energy in the International System of Units (SI).
This Greek-derived name means 'thin skin' and refers to a piece of mucosal tissue that partially covers the vaginal opening in many mammals — which structure?
Hymen: Membrane that surrounds or partially covers the vaginal opening.
Nicknamed the 'powerhouse of the cell' after a phrase popularized in a 1957 magazine article, this double-membraned organelle generates ATP through respiration — which organelle?
Mitochondrion: Organelle in eukaryotic cells responsible for respiration.
First domesticated some 5,000 years ago on the Iranian plateau, this fruit-bearing shrub reached California in 1769 via Spanish settlers — which fruit?
Pomegranate: Fruit-bearing deciduous shrub. Pomegranate was first domesticated by ancient Iranians in the Iranian plateau and nearby regions about 5,000 years ago.

Designed at a major tech company in 2007 by Robert Griesemer, Rob Pike, and Ken Thompson, this statically typed, compiled programming language borrows C-like syntax while adding garbage collection and built-in concurrency support — name the language?
Go (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose programming language that is statically typed and compiled.

The smallest recognized dog breed in the world, this Mexican toy breed has large erect ears and a rounded skull, and its genes carry a trace of pre-Columbian indigenous American dog ancestry — which breed?

Chihuahua (dog breed) is a Mexican breed of toy dog and the smallest recognized dog breed in the world. It is primarily kept as a companion animal and is characterized by its compact size, large erect ears, and rounded skull.
Represented by symbols like '11' in the Hindu-Arabic system used worldwide, these mathematical objects serve to count, measure, and label — what are they called?
Number: Used to count, measure, and label. The most basic examples are the natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so forth.
Unearthed in Montana by Jack Horner's team in 1987, this 20-foot horned dinosaur sported a bony neck-frill and lived roughly 75 million years ago — which species?
Achelousaurus: Genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from North America.
First cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9600 BC, this cereal grass is grown on more land worldwide than any other food crop — which grain?
Wheat: Genus of grass cultivated for grain. Wheat is a group of wild and domesticated grasses of the genus Triticum.
Shaped like a butterfly and sitting in the neck just below the Adam's apple, this endocrine gland secretes hormones that regulate metabolic rate — which gland is it?
Thyroid: Endocrine gland in the neck. The lower two thirds of the lobes are connected by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus (pl.: isthmi).

This paraphilia describes a sexual fixation on non-human animals, distinct from acting on such attraction, and was estimated in one 2021 study to affect about 2 percent of the population — name the term?
Zoophilia is a paraphilia in which a person experiences a sexual fixation on non-human animals.
Also nicknamed 'rose mallow,' this genus of large, showy tropical flowers includes both herbaceous plants and woody shrubs — which genus is it?
Hibiscus: Genus of plants. Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.

Caused by a bacterium spread through contaminated water and undercooked shellfish, this intestinal infection produces severe watery diarrhea that can trigger dehydration within hours — which disease is it?
Cholera: Bacterial infection of the small intestine.
Situated between two larger folds of skin, these paired flaps extend from the inner vaginal and urethral openings and form the clitoral hood above — which structures are these?
Labia minora: Flaps of skin on either side of the vaginal opening in the vulva.
Nicknamed the 'brushwood dog' for its game-flushing hunting style, this is the smallest of Japan's six native dog breeds — which breed?
Shiba Inu: Japanese dog breed. The Shiba Inu (Japanese: 柴犬; Japanese pronunciation: [ɕi.ba.i.nɯ]) is a breed of hunting dog from Japan.

Equal to about 9.46 trillion kilometres, this astronomical distance unit is defined by how far illumination travels through a vacuum in 365.25 days — despite its name, it isn't a measure of time. What is it?
Light-year (ly or lyr), is a unit of length used to express astronomical distances and is equal to exactly 9460730472580.8 km, which is approximately 9.46 trillion kilometres or 5.88 trillion miles.
Homologous to the ovary in females, this male gonad produces sperm and secretes testosterone under the control of the pituitary gland's luteinizing hormone — which organ?
Testicle: Internal organ in the male reproductive system.
Named after a 17th-century French mathematician and physicist, this SI unit of pressure is defined as one newton of force per square metre — name the unit?
Pascal (unit) (symbol: Pa) is the unit of pressure in the International System of Units (SI).
Produced by mammary glands and rich in calcium, protein and lactose, this liquid is often prized for its antibody-packed early form, colostrum — what is it?
Milk: Nutrient-rich liquid produced by mammals.

Marked by delusions, hallucinations and disorganized thinking, this state — not a diagnosis itself — often stems from schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or alcohol-related brain damage — what is it called?
Psychosis: Abnormal condition of the mind.

Named for the physicist who reportedly asked 'but where is everybody?' at Los Alamos in 1950, this puzzle questions why we've found no evidence of alien civilizations despite the odds favoring them — what's it called?
Fermi paradox: Discrepancy of the lack of evidence for alien life despite its apparent likelihood.

Located partly outside the body and partly within the pelvis, this set of sex organs includes the testicles, which produce sperm to fertilize an egg during conception — which body system is being described?
Male reproductive system consists of a number of sex organs that play a role in the process of human reproduction.
Sold under the brand name Prozac, this SSRI treats depression, OCD and panic disorder, and is also prescribed off-label for premature ejaculation — what is it?
Fluoxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It is also approved for treatment of major depressive disorder in adolescents and children 8 years of age and over.
Named for a pioneering physicist's work on classical mechanics, this SI unit of force equals the push needed to accelerate one kilogram at one metre per second squared — name the unit?
Newton (unit) (symbol: N) is the unit of force in the International System of Units (SI).
The first woman of Indian origin to fly to space, she served as a mission specialist on two Space Shuttle Columbia flights, the second ending in the 2003 disaster that killed her — who was she?

Named after the mathematician who introduced it in 1715, this infinite sum built from a function's derivatives at a single point becomes a special case named for Colin Maclaurin when centered at zero — what is it?
Taylor series: Mathematical approximation of a function.
This hormone-responsive organ nourishes a developing embryo and fetus until birth, connecting at its narrow lower end to the cervix and at its upper corners to the fallopian tubes — what is it?
Uterus: Female sex organ in mammals.
These paired skin folds run from the mons pubis to the perineum and are considered the anatomical counterpart to the male scrotum — what are they called?
Labia majora: Folds of skin that contain and protect the vulva's other parts.
Named for its rough alignment with the Moon's cycle — the two words are even linguistic cognates — this calendar unit varies from 28 to 31 days in the Gregorian system — what is it?
Month: Unit of time, usually 28 to 31 days.
Proposed in 1724 by a physicist who set water's freezing point at 32 degrees and boiling at 212, this temperature scale was originally anchored to a freezing brine solution — which scale?
Fahrenheit: Temperature scale. The Fahrenheit scale is a temperature scale based on one proposed in 1724 by the physicist Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit (1686–1736).
Originally called 'centigrade' from Latin words for a hundred and steps, this SI temperature scale was renamed in 1948 to honor the Swedish astronomer who proposed it in 1742 — which scale?
Celsius: Unit of measurement for temperature.
Located near the backbone on either side of the heart, this organ extracts oxygen from the air and releases carbon dioxide, driven mainly by the diaphragm — which organ is it?
Lung: Primary organ of the respiratory system.

Developed by the Chukchi people in the Russian Far East for pulling sleds and companionship, this medium-sized Spitz-family dog breed is smaller than the similar-looking Alaskan Malamute — name the breed?
Siberian Husky is a breed of medium-sized working sled dog.
Known as aubergine or brinjal elsewhere, this purple, spongy fruit in the nightshade family is technically a berry despite usually being cooked as a vegetable — what is it?
This genus of great apes emerged from Australopithecus and includes modern humans alongside extinct relatives, with chimpanzees and bonobos as its closest living kin — what genus is it?
Homo: Genus of hominins. Homo erectus and Homo neanderthalensis) classified as either ancestral or closely related to modern humans, collectively called archaic humans.

This fluid-dynamics rule holds that a fluid's pressure drops as its speed increases; the Swiss physicist credited with it published the idea in 1738, though Leonhard Euler derived the actual equation — what's it called?
Bernoulli's principle is a key concept in fluid dynamics that relates pressure, speed and height.
This rounded mound of fatty tissue overlies the junction where the two pubic bones meet — what is it?
Mons pubis: Rounded mass of fatty tissue found over the pubic symphysis.
Sitting between the esophagus and the small intestine, this muscular organ uses acid and enzymes to chemically break down food, giving us the word 'gastric' — which organ?
Stomach: Digestive organ. The stomach is a muscular, hollow organ in the upper gastrointestinal tract of humans and many other animals, including several invertebrates.
Surrounded by a typically darker-colored areola, this raised region of breast tissue is where milk exits through the lactiferous ducts during lactation — what is it?
Nipple: Part of the breast. The milk can flow through the nipple passively, or it can be ejected by smooth muscle contractions that occur along with the ductal system.
Bred in Britain to hunt rabbits and hares, this scent hound's keen nose also makes it a popular detection dog for smuggled food at airports — which breed?
Beagle: Breed of small scent hound. The Beagle is a British breed of scent hound, similar in appearance to the much larger foxhound.
A red supergiant in Orion so vast that, placed at the Sun's position, it would engulf the orbits of Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars, this variable star is designated Alpha Orionis — which star?
Betelgeuse: Red supergiant star in the constellation Orion. It is usually the tenth-brightest star in the night sky and, after Rigel, the second brightest in its constellation.
Based on how long Earth takes to orbit the Sun, this unit of time comes in tropical and sidereal forms differing by about 20 minutes, with leap years keeping our calendar in sync — what unit?

Year: Unit of time based on Earth's orbit. In scientific use, the tropical year (approximately 365 solar days, 5 hours, 48 minutes, 45 seconds) and the sidereal year (about 20 minutes longer) are more exact.
Named after the Turkish word for turban, which it was thought to resemble, this spring-blooming bulb belongs to the lily family and includes about 75 species — which flower?

Sitting between tissue and a full body system in life's hierarchy, this general term describes a structural unit built from functional tissue (parenchyma) plus supportive tissue (stroma), as seen in the intestinal wall — what is such a unit called?
Organ (biology): Collection of tissues with similar functions.
Believed to be bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso, this toy dog breed originated in Tibet — name the breed?
Shih Tzu is a toy dog or pet dog breed originating from Tibet and believed to be bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso.
Strongly associated with human habitation and now the most widely distributed wild bird on Earth thanks to introductions across multiple continents, this small brown-and-black bird is which species?
House sparrow: Species of bird. The house sparrow (Passer domesticus) is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in most parts of the world.
Named from a Greek root meaning 'light' or 'brightness' in reference to its luminous, reflective eyes, this genus includes the bobcat among its four wild cat species — which genus?
Lynx: Genus of medium-sized wild cats.
Originating in the Swiss Alps' canton of Bern, this large farm breed historically pulled carts for alpine herders and traces its ancestry to Roman mastiffs — which breed, recognized in 1912?
Bernese Mountain Dog: Swiss breed of dog. The Bernese Mountain Dog, German: Berner Sennenhund or Dürrbächler, is a large dog breed originating from the canton of Bern, Switzerland and the Swiss Alps.
Created by Rasmus Lerdorf in 1993, this scripting language's name began as 'Personal Home Page' before becoming a recursive backronym meaning 'Hypertext Preprocessor' — what is it?
PHP: Scripting language created in 1994. PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
Named from Greek words for 'twisted' and 'grain,' this genus of spherical bacteria divides along a single axis to form chains, unlike its grape-cluster-forming cousins — coined in 1877, what is it?
Streptococcus: Genus of bacteria. In 1984, many bacteria formerly grouped in the genus Streptococcus were separated out into the genera Enterococcus and Lactococcus.
Developed by the MIT Media Lab for children ages 5 to 16, this block-based visual programming language and website has been translated into more than 70 languages — name it?
Scratch (programming language) is a high-level, block-based visual programming language and website aimed primarily at children as an educational tool, with a target audience of ages 5 to 16.

In math, this concept assigns exactly one element of a codomain to each element of a domain, and was formalized via set theory by the end of the 19th century after originating as a way to describe how one varying quantity depends on another — what is it called?
Function (mathematics): Association of one output to each input.

Despite its name being something of a misnomer, this herding dog breed was developed in California and takes its name from imported collies that arrived alongside sheep from Down Under — what breed is it?
Australian Shepherd: American breed of dog. The Australian Shepherd, also known as the Aussie, is a breed of herding dog from the United States.
In placental mammals, this is the region of the body between the anus and the genitals, running from the pubic bone to the tailbone, and is often considered an erogenous zone — what is it called?
Perineum: Region of the body between the genitals and anus. The perineum (pl.: perineums or perinea) in placental mammals is the space between the anus and the genitals.

Made of contractile proteins called actin and myosin, this soft tissue exists in three vertebrate forms — skeletal, cardiac, and smooth — and forms during a developmental process called myogenesis — what is it?
Muscle: Important Biological tissue that allows movement.
Distinguished from living elephants by spirally twisted tusks and a thick coat of fur for cold climates, this extinct genus survived from the late Miocene until roughly 4,000 years ago — what was it?
Mammoth: Extinct genus of mammals. The oldest mammoth representative, Mammuthus subplanifrons, appeared around 6 million years ago during the late Miocene in southern and Eastern Africa.

Convicted in 2013 for leaking nearly 750,000 classified documents to WikiLeaks while serving as an Army intelligence analyst in Iraq, this whistleblower had her sentence commuted by President Obama in 2017 — who is she?
Chelsea Manning: American activist and whistleblower (born 1987)

Born in London, raised in Milan, and self-taught in web design, this Catholic teenager built a website cataloguing Eucharistic miracles before dying of leukemia at fifteen — he was beatified in 2020. Who was he?
Equal to one-twelfth of a foot and derived from the Roman word for 'twelfth,' this unit of length has been pegged to exactly 25.4 millimeters since the mid-20th century — what is it?
Inch: Unit of length. The inch (symbol: in or ″) is a unit of length in the British Imperial and the United States customary systems of measurement.

Producing a distinctive capped nut and supporting more than 950 species of caterpillar, this keystone hardwood genus ranges across the Northern Hemisphere in some 500 species, some evergreen, some deciduous — what tree is it?
Oak: Tree or shrub in the genus Quercus.
This external body opening at the end of the digestive tract, positioned opposite the mouth, lets gas and solid waste pass out after digestion?
Anus: Digestive tract waste expulsion opening. Passage of feces through the anus is typically controlled by muscular sphincters, and failure to stop unwanted passages results in fecal incontinence.
Native to the rainforests of New Guinea and northeastern Australia, this flightless ratite is the fourth-tallest and third-heaviest living bird, trailing only the ostriches and the emu?

Published by Einstein in 1916 as a refinement of Newton's law of gravitation, this geometric framework describes gravity as curved spacetime, summed up by Wheeler as 'space-time tells matter how to move; matter tells space-time how to curve'?
General relativity: Theory of gravitation as curved spacetime. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
This messenger network of hormone feedback loops releases chemicals from internal glands like the thyroid, pituitary, and adrenal glands straight into the bloodstream to regulate distant organs?
Endocrine system: Hormone-producing glands of a body.
This sensory organ detects light and converts it into electro-chemical signals in neurons, using an adjustable lens system to focus incoming light and form images — name the organ?
Eye is a sensory organ that allows an organism to perceive visual information.
This tech entrepreneur co-founded Twitter, later built a fintech company behind Square, Cash App, and Tidal, and also helped launch the decentralized network Bluesky?

Made up largely of the gluteus maximus — the largest muscle in the human body — these two rounded parts of the posterior pelvic region sit between the lower back and the perineum, and have long served as a target for corporal punishment?
Buttocks: Anatomical feature on the posterior of some primates.
Making up a quarter to a third of all protein in mammals, this triple-helix fibrous protein needs vitamin C for its synthesis and gives structure to cartilage, tendons, and skin — what is it?
Collagen: Most abundant structural protein in animals.
Evergreen conifers of the genus Pinus, these trees grow their needle leaves in bunches of two to five and yield both the nuts used in pesto and the resin that flavors retsina wine?
Pine: Genus of coniferous trees. A pine is any conifer in the genus Pinus of the family Pinaceae.
Occurring in our galaxy roughly once every 61 years, though the last confirmed sighting was back in 1604, this luminous stellar explosion can briefly outshine an entire galaxy?

Brought from China to Europe in the sixteenth century and popularized by the House of Orange in the Netherlands, this dog breed is known for its wrinkly, short-muzzled face and curled tail — name the breed?
Pug is a breed of dog with the physically distinctive features of a wrinkly, short-muzzled face, and curled tail.
This concept in calculus, a continuous analog of a sum, computes the signed area under a curve and pairs with differentiation as one of the field's two fundamental operations?
Bred in Córdoba in the early 1900s to hunt wild boar and puma, this large mastiff-type breed's ancestry includes an extinct local fighting dog and a Bull Terrier — which breed is it?
Dogo Argentino: Argentine breed of dog. It was bred in the early twentieth century in Córdoba in central Argentina, primarily for hunting large game such as peccaries, wild boar, and pumas.

Encased by the vertebral column and running from the brainstem down to about the first lumbar vertebra, this hollow, fluid-filled structure forms the other half of the central nervous system alongside the brain — what is it?
Spinal cord: Part of the vertebral column in animals.

First published in 1785 by a French physicist, this principle holds that the electrostatic force between two charged particles is proportional to their charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them — which principle is it?
Coulomb's law: Fundamental physical law of electromagnetism.
Coined in 1852 but now considered stigmatizing in clinical settings, this WHO-estimated 283-million-person global condition involves continued drinking despite the harm it causes — what is it called?

Made of a segmented series of bones cushioned by intervertebral discs, this defining feature of some 50,000 animal species surrounds and protects the nerve tissue running through it — what is it, also known as the backbone?
Spinal column: Bony structure found in vertebrates.
Descended from medieval hunting dogs once used to take down bears, boar, and deer for German nobility, this breed ties with the Irish Wolfhound as one of the world's two largest — which breed is it?
Great Dane: German breed of dog. The Great Dane is a German breed of large mastiff-sighthound, which descends from hunting dogs of the Middle Ages used to hunt bears, wild boar, and deer.
This icy wanderer of the solar system grows a gassy halo and sometimes a tail stretching more than an astronomical unit as it nears the sun — what is it?
Comet: Natural object in space that releases gas.

Encompassing conditions marked by a clinically significant disturbance in thinking, emotional regulation, or behavior that causes real distress or impaired functioning, this broad psychiatric category has causes that remain often unclear — what is the umbrella term for it?

Captured by Einstein's famous equation E=mc², this principle shows that a tiny amount of one physical quantity converts into an enormous amount of another thanks to the speed of light being squared — what is this relationship called?
Mass–energy equivalence: Physics concept expressed as E = mc².
Originating in Northern China, this spitz-type dog breed is known for a dense double coat that forms a distinctive ruff around the neck — name the breed?
Chow Chow is a spitz-type of dog breed originally from Northern China.
Born in the Soviet Union, this entrepreneur co-founded a social network in 2006 before developing a messaging app now headquartered in Dubai — who is he?
Equal to one joule per second, this SI unit of power honors an 18th-century Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine in 1776 — which unit is it?
