Dubbed 'the father of nuclear physics,' this New Zealander won a Nobel Prize in Chemistry despite proposing that atoms have a tiny, densely charged nucleus — who is he?
Ernest Rutherford: New Zealand physicist and chemist (1871–1937)

Originally hoping to become an engineer, this Italian physician became one of the first women to graduate from medical school in Italy and later devised an influential educational philosophy — who is she?
Maria Montessori: Italian physician and educator (1870–1952)
This painful collection of pus built up within body tissue often causes redness, warmth, and swelling, and includes boils and carbuncles as common types — what is it called?
Abscess: Localized collection of pus in body tissue. An abscess is a collection of pus that has built up within the tissue of the body, usually caused by bacterial infection.
This class of chemical compound forms when an acid's hydroxyl hydrogen is swapped for an organic group, and includes the glycerides that make up most animal fats — what is it?
Ester: Compound derived from an acid.
Also called sallows or osiers, this genus of roughly 350 mostly deciduous tree and shrub species thrives on moist soil in cold, temperate regions — which plant?
Ranked the world's richest person by Forbes from 2010 to 2013, this Mexican tycoon built his fortune largely through telecommunications and remains Latin America's wealthiest individual — who is he?
This British chemical engineer founded a major chemicals group in 1998 and later became a minority shareholder with control over football operations at Manchester United — who is he?
Jim Ratcliffe: British engineer and businessman (born 1952)
A likely hybrid of lemon and a bitter citrus relative, this fragrant fruit flavors tea, snus, and perfume, though it can heighten skin's sensitivity to sunlight — which fruit?
These large, heavyset American game birds have a distinctive fleshy growth called a snood hanging from the base of their beak, with wild and ocellated species. What birds are they?
Turkey (bird) are large, heavyset galliforms in the genus Meleagris, indigenous to the Americas.
Located at the base of the penis in most male mammals, this sac of skin holding the testicles tends to tighten when exposed to cold — what is it called?
Scrotum: Sac of skin that protects the testicles.
Boiled down from its sap to make a beloved breakfast syrup, this genus of roughly 132 tree and shrub species counts the sycamore as its type species — which genus of trees?
What's the name for hardened, foul-smelling deposits of trapped debris that form in the crevices of the tonsils, sometimes visible as white flecks at the back of the throat?
Tonsil stones are mineralizations of debris within the crevices of the tonsils.

First flown in August 1970 and introduced by American Airlines the following year, this trijet wide-body aircraft has two underwing engines and a third mounted at the base of its tail fin — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas DC-10: Wide-body three-engine airliner.
Usually appearing on the hands and feet due to a human papillomavirus infection, this benign skin growth typically clears on its own within months to years — what is this common growth called?
Wart: Small, rough growth resembling a cauliflower or a solid blister.
Also known as jimsonweed or devil's trumpet, this poisonous nightshade plant likely native to Central America has been used both in folk medicine and, unpleasantly, as a hallucinogen — which plant?
Datura stramonium: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family.

Describing how closely two variables move together, this statistical measure is famously not proof of causation, and two variables can even be linked this way without truly depending on each other — what is it called?
Correlation: Statistical relationship. In statistics, correlation is a type of statistical relationship between two random variables or bivariate data.
Nicknamed for its shaggy white spines that dangle over a centimeter long, this edible mushroom is commonly called lion's mane and is used in traditional Chinese medicine — which fungus?
Hericium erinaceus: Edible mushroom. Hericium erinaceus, commonly known as lion's mane, yamabushitake, bearded tooth fungus, or bearded hedgehog, is a species of tooth fungus.

Defined by a –COOH functional group attached to an R-group, and only partially dissociating in water, this general class of organic compounds includes fatty compounds and the building blocks of proteins — what is this functional class called?
Carboxylic acid: Organic compound containing a –C(=O)OH group.

Described as 'the translation of politics into the reality that citizens experience every day,' this field implements government policies and programs to solve social and economic problems — what is it called?
Public administration: Academic discipline; implementation or management of policy.
Native to the Mediterranean, this legume tree's seed pods are ground into a chocolate substitute, while its seeds yield a common food thickener known as locust bean gum — which tree?
Carob: Small tree grown for its edible pods and landscaping.
This legume, also called the broad bean, can trigger a dangerous reaction called favism in people with a certain metabolic blood disorder — what species is it?
Vicia faba: Species of plant in the pea and bean family.

Providing the USAF with intercontinental strategic airlift for oversized cargo, this jumbo transport is among the largest military aircraft ever built and shares lineage with the smaller Starlifter — what is it?
Lockheed C-5 Galaxy: American heavy military transport aircraft.
This 14th-century Arab scholar wrote his most famous work, the Muqaddimah, in just six months and once met the conqueror Tamerlane — who is he?
Ibn Khaldun: Arab Islamic scholar, historian and philosopher (1332–1406)
Succeeding the Castro brothers, this engineer became Cuba's first head of state in nearly six decades who wasn't a member of that family — who is he?
Miguel Díaz-Canel: Leader of Cuba since 2021.
Distinguished by its darker camouflage, conformal fuel tanks, and a two-seat cockpit, this all-weather multirole fighter first flew in 1986 for long-range interdiction missions — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle: American all-weather multirole fighter aircraft.
Designed by R. J. Mitchell with a distinctive elliptical wing and sunken rivets for minimal drag, this was the only British fighter kept in continuous production throughout World War II — what is it?
Supermarine Spitfire: British single-seat WWII fighter aircraft.

Found along the Andes and Pacific coasts of South America, this enormous New World vulture is one of the largest flying birds by wingspan, with males sporting a fleshy comb atop a bald red head — which species is it?
Andean condor: Species of bird. The Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur.
Native to North African deserts from Western Sahara to the Sinai, this diminutive canid uses its oversized ears to shed heat and detect prey burrowing underground — which species is it?
Fennec fox: Species of fox. The fennec fox (Vulpes zerda) is a small fox native to the deserts of North Africa, ranging from Western Sahara and Mauritania to the Sinai Peninsula.
This field statistically studies human populations — their size and makeup — through the interplay of births, deaths, and migration — what is it?
Demography: Study of human populations and their structures.

Originally from the Mediterranean, this yellowish-gray arthropod has up to 15 pairs of long legs and preys on insects with venom too mild to harm humans — what species commonly invades homes worldwide?
Scutigera coleoptrata: Species of arthropod. Scutigera coleoptrata, also known as the house centipede, is a species of centipede that is typically yellowish-gray and has up to 15 pairs of long legs.
This basic unit of time — averaging 24 hours, or 86,400 seconds — marks one full rotation of the Earth relative to the Sun, and got split into weeks, months, and years. What is it?
Day: Time of one rotation around a planet axis.

This dimensionless ratio of inertial to viscous forces predicts whether fluid flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent, and is used everywhere from pipe flow to aircraft wings — what is it?
Reynolds number: Ratio of inertial to viscous forces acting on a liquid.

Designed to replace the Lockheed C-130 Hercules and sized between it and the Boeing C-17, this four-engine European turboprop military transporter first flew from Seville in December 2009 despite nearly being cancelled over cost overruns. What's the aircraft?
Airbus A400M Atlas: Multi-national four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft.

The tallest and heaviest living species of deer, this Northern Hemisphere giant is topped in North American body mass only by the bison, and its males sport broad, hand-shaped antlers unlike any other deer's pointed racks. What is it?
Moose: Largest species of deer. It is also the tallest, and the second-largest, land animal in North America, falling short only to the American bison in body mass.

Originally launched in 2008 as Bombardier's CSeries, this five-abreast narrow-body airliner family was rebranded in 2018 after a European aerospace giant acquired a majority stake. What's it called today?
Airbus A220: Canadian narrow-body airliner family. The Airbus A220 is a family of five-abreast narrow-body airliners by Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (ACLP).
First named by Karl Friedrich Burdach in 1822, this paired brain structure tucked in the temporal lobes drives fear, anxiety, and aggression as part of the limbic system. What is it?
Amygdala: Paired structure within the brain temporal lobe.

With a red face, a black-and-white head, and a bold yellow wing bar, this small finch native to the Palearctic often appears in Italian Renaissance paintings of the Madonna and Child. What bird is it?
European goldfinch: Species of bird. It has been introduced to other areas, including Australia, New Zealand, Uruguay and the United States.
This bird family contains both doves and pigeons — including the feral rock dove common in cities — spanning 52 genera and 353 species worldwide. What's the family called?
Columbidae: Family of birds. The bird most commonly referred to as "pigeon" is the domestic pigeon, descendant of the wild rock dove, which is a common inhabitant of cities as the feral pigeon.

Once meaning a Christian life oriented toward the Holy Spirit, this concept broadened over centuries to describe a subjective sense of the sacred and 'the deepest values and meanings by which people live,' often apart from organized religion. What's the term?

This inner-ear condition brings on episodes of vertigo, ringing in the ears, and hearing loss lasting anywhere from 20 minutes to several hours — believed to stem from fluid buildup in the labyrinth. What is it?
Ménière's disease: Disorder of the inner ear. The hearing loss and ringing in the ears can become constant over time.
Introduced in 1984, this turboprop regional airliner series was developed from an earlier company model and later gained 'Quiet' variants with active noise-cancellation — which aircraft family?

De Havilland Canada Dash 8: Canadian turboprop airliner. The De Havilland Canada DHC-8, commonly known as the Dash 8, is a series of turboprop-powered regional airliners, introduced by de Havilland Canada (DHC) in 1984.

First described in 1915 by a German paleontologist from Egyptian fossils that were destroyed during World War II, this dinosaur genus wasn't represented by new material until the early 2000s — which genus?
Spinosaurus: Genus of spinosaurid dinosaur. The genus was known first from Egyptian remains discovered in 1912 and described by German palaeontologist Ernst Stromer in 1915.
Produced continuously by the liver and stored in the gallbladder, this yellow-green fluid is released into the small intestine to help digest fats — what is it?
Bile: Dark greenish-brown fluid aiding in the digestion of fats.
This citrus fruit of Chinese origin is believed to be a natural hybrid of a wild mandarin subspecies and the ichang papeda — what fruit?
Yuzu: Citrus fruit and plant. Yuzu (Citrus × junos, from Japanese 柚子 or ユズ;) is a citrus fruit and plant in the family Rutaceae of Chinese origin.
First made in Belgium in 1956 and sold under the brand names Atarax and Vistaril, this first-generation antihistamine also treats anxiety and insomnia — what drug?
Hydroxyzine: Antihistamine drug. It is used in the treatment of itchiness, anxiety, insomnia, and nausea (including that due to motion sickness).
As the only surviving son of a legendary Italian carmaker, this billionaire owns just over 10% of the company that bears his father's name and serves as its vice chairman — who is he?
Piero Ferrari: Italian billionaire businessman. Piero Ferrari (born Piero Lardi, 22 May 1945; later Piero Lardi Ferrari) is an Italian billionaire businessman and sport personality.
Oblate rather than round, with a thin, loose peel that makes it easy to separate into segments, this citrus fruit is sweeter and stronger-tasting than its spherical, hybrid cousin — which fruit?
Mandarin orange: Small citrus fruit. A mandarin orange (Citrus reticulata), often simply called mandarin, is a small, rounded citrus tree fruit.
This genus of early African hominins, which lived during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene, is considered ancestral to the genus that includes modern humans — which genus?
Australopithecus: Genus of hominin ancestral to modern humans. The genera Homo (which includes modern humans), Paranthropus, and Kenyanthropus evolved from some Australopithecus species.

With nearly 24,000 ommatidia in each compound eye and wings usually held flat rather than folded, this iridescent flying insect is often confused with its lighter-bodied damselfly cousins — what is it?
Which large Southern African dog breed, whose standard was drafted in 1922 in what's now Zimbabwe, descends from ridged hunting dogs of the Khoikhoi crossed with European breeds used to bay lions?
Rhodesian Ridgeback is a large dog breed originally bred in Southern Africa.
Latin for 'raven,' this widely distributed bird genus includes crows and rooks and gave a group of its members the eerie collective noun 'a murder' — what genus is it?
Corvus: Genus of birds including crows, ravens and rooks.
Native to the Mediterranean and used to season food as a bay leaf, this aromatic evergreen prominent in classical Greco-Roman culture can grow up to 20 metres tall — what is its scientific name?
Laurus nobilis: Species of flowering plant in the laurel family Lauraceae.

This physical law holds that within an isolated system, nothing is created or destroyed — only transformed, as when a stick of dynamite converts stored chemical potential into heat, sound, and motion — what law is it?
Conservation of energy: Law of physics and chemistry.
First described by Linnaeus in 1753, this Old World vegetable — better known on dinner plates as celery — is also cultivated for a bulbous root form called celeriac. What is its scientific name?

Named from the Greek word for 'honey bee' because its flowers attract them, this citrus-scented herb in the mint family has been cultivated since at least the 16th century for tea and aromatic oils — what is it?
Made up mostly of undigested food broken down by gut bacteria, this bodily waste is expelled through the anus and can even be dried for fuel or used as fertilizer — what is it?
Feces: Solid or semisolid remains of undigested food.

Taught in universities and seminaries, this academic discipline studies religious belief from within a religious perspective, focusing on divinity, revelation, and how God might interact with the world — what field is it?
Theology: Study of the nature of deities and religious beliefs.
This white crystalline sodium borate dissolves in water to form a basic solution and finds uses as a pesticide, a soldering flux, and an ingredient in glass and pottery glazes — what mineral is it?
Borax: Boron compound, a salt of boric acid.
The third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere at nearly 1%, this noble gas takes its name from an Ancient Greek word meaning 'lazy' or 'inactive' — what element is it?
Argon: Chemical element with atomic number 18 (Ar)

This Scottish physicist's equations unified electricity, magnetism, and light into a single theory — the second great unification in physics after Newton's — while also helping found statistical mechanics — who is he?
James Clerk Maxwell: Scottish physicist and mathematician (1831–1879)

This academic framework examines how systemic bias against certain ethnic groups is embedded in laws and institutions, using the concept of intersectionality to explain overlapping forms of inequality — what is it called?
Critical race theory: Conceptual framework. The word critical in the name is an academic reference to critical theory, not criticizing or blaming individuals.
Reproducing via spores rather than seeds or flowers, this group of vascular plants unfurls from coiled 'fiddleheads' into fronds and numbers over 10,000 species — what are they?
Fern: Class of vascular plants. The group includes about 10,560 known extant species.

Discovered in 1817 by Jöns Jacob Berzelius and named after the moon because of its resemblance to an element named for the Earth, this semiconductor finds use in glassmaking, pigments, and photocells — what element is it?
Selenium: Chemical element with atomic number 34 (Se)
Native to northeastern Australia and first commercially grown at scale in Hawaii during the 1880s, this is the only widely cultivated food plant indigenous to Australia — what nut is it?
Macadamia: Genus of plants indigenous to Australia.
Often striking one side of the head and sometimes preceded by a sensory 'aura,' this neurological disorder brings nausea and sensitivity to light and sound — what is it?
Migraine: Disorder resulting in recurrent moderate–severe headaches.
Known commonly as palms, this family of over 2,600 flowering plant species includes climbers, shrubs, and tree-like forms mostly found in the tropics — what's the family called?
Arecaceae: Palm family of flowering plants.
The largest genus in the mint family, this group of nearly 1,000 shrubs and herbs includes common cooking sage and rosemary — what's the genus called?
Salvia: Largest genus of plants in the mint family. Salvia is the largest genus of plants in the sage family Lamiaceae, with just under 1,000 species of shrubs, herbaceous perennials, and annuals.
This Canadian physician and author has written five books linking childhood trauma to conditions like ADHD and addiction, though critics question the evidence behind some claims — who is he?

Attributed to 19th-century pathologist Rudolf Virchow, this term for the premature death of cells caused by trauma or infection contrasts with the body's own programmed cell death — what's the condition called?
Necrosis: Unprogrammed cell death caused by external cell injury.
This protein filament that grows from follicles in the skin is one of the defining traits of mammals, and its removal or styling carries different meanings across cultures — what is it?
Hair: Protein filament that grows from follicles found in the dermis, or skin.
Living on ocean floors worldwide, this leathery-skinned echinoderm recycles nutrients as a detritivore and is named for its resemblance to a common garden vegetable — what is it?
This reddish-brown, bitter tincture dissolved opium poppy extract in alcohol and was once sold without a prescription as a cough and pain remedy — what is it?
Laudanum: Tincture of opium. Laudanum is a tincture of opium containing approximately 10% powdered opium by weight (the equivalent of 1% morphine).
Known on the street as 'angel dust,' this dissociative anesthetic acts as an NMDA receptor antagonist and can cause hallucinations and psychosis — what is this drug?
Phencyclidine: Dissociative hallucinogenic drug, mostly used recreationally.
Discovered in 1915, this red dwarf is the closest star to Earth besides the Sun, orbiting its two larger neighbors once every 550,000 years — which star?
Proxima Centauri: Nearest star to the Solar System.
Commonly known as elder, with its blossoms called elderflower and its fruit elderberry, this genus contains between 20 and 30 flowering plant species — which genus?
Built from a nitrogen-containing base, a five-carbon sugar, and a phosphate group, these molecules are the monomer building blocks of DNA and RNA — what are they called?
Nucleotide: Biological molecules constituting nucleic acids.
Which genus of about 28 grass species includes one member grown worldwide both as a cereal grain for human consumption and as fodder for livestock?
Sorghum (genus) is a genus of about 28 species of flowering plants in the grass family (Poaceae).
Caused by viruses like herpes simplex or rabies, this inflammation of the brain can bring fever, confusion, and a stiff neck — what is this condition?

Encephalitis: Inflammation of the brain. The severity can be variable with symptoms including reduction or alteration in consciousness, aphasia, headache, fever, confusion, a stiff neck, and vomiting.
Sold under the brand name Zyprexa, this atypical antipsychotic treats schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and is sometimes used off-label to fight chemotherapy-induced nausea — what is this drug?
Olanzapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Olanzapine, sold under the brand name Zyprexa among others, is an atypical antipsychotic primarily used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
This daisy-family weed's yellow flowers give way to fluffy silver-tufted seed heads nicknamed 'clocks' or 'blowballs,' whose seeds scatter on the wind — which plant, better known by its common name?
Taraxacum officinale: Flowering plant species known as dandelion.
Made by giving a paper loop a half-twist before joining the ends, this non-orientable surface first appeared in Roman mosaics — what is it called?
Möbius strip: Non-orientable surface with one edge.
This psychological state describes a lack of feeling, motivation, or concern, sitting on a spectrum between normal drive and akinetic mutism — what is it called?
Apathy: State of indifference, or the suppression of emotions.
Sometimes called 'pigweed,' this genus of plants is grown worldwide as a leaf vegetable and for its edible grain — which genus?
Amaranth: Genus of plants. The plant can grow from 1 to 2.5 metres (3 to 8 feet) tall with a succulent, hollow stem.
Also known as wattles, this genus of over 1,000 shrub and tree species is now largely reserved for Australian natives — which genus?
Acacia: Genus of plants. Acacia, commonly known as wattles or acacias, is a genus of about 1,084 species of shrubs and trees in the subfamily Mimosoideae of the pea family Fabaceae.
Blue above and orange below, this sparrow-sized bird dives for fish and nests in burrows dug into riverbanks — which species?
Common kingfisher: Species of bird. It is resident in much of its range, but migrates from areas where rivers freeze in winter.
Its edible 'curd' is actually a dense head of undeveloped flower buds, and one variety grows its curds in spiral fractal patterns — which vegetable?
Cauliflower: Vegetable in the species Brassica oleracea.
Marketed under brand names like Quaalude and Sopor, this sedative was pulled from commercial production in the mid-1980s due to widespread misuse — which drug?
With a melting point of just under 30 degrees Celsius, this metal will turn to liquid in the palm of your hand — which element?
Gallium: Chemical element with atomic number 31 (Ga)
A former mayor of Tehran and engineer by training, he served as Iran's sixth president from 2005 to 2013 and championed the country's nuclear program — who is he?

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad: President of Iran from 2005 to 2013. Mahmoud Ahmadinejad (né Sabbaghian; born 28 October 1956) is an Iranian politician who served as the sixth president of Iran from 2005 to 2013.

Massive enough to be rounded by its own gravity but too small to clear its orbital neighborhood like the solar system's eight major planets, Pluto became the prototype of this category after a 2006 reclassification. Name the category?

Dwarf planet is a small planetary-mass object that is in direct orbit around the Sun, massive enough to be gravitationally rounded, but insufficient to achieve orbital dominance like the eight classical planets of the Solar System.
Its name comes from Latin words meaning 'to strangle' and 'chest,' and it describes pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle — what is this condition called?
Angina: Chest discomfort due to disorder of the heart muscles.
Native to the tropical Americas, this small evergreen tree's fermented seeds become cocoa powder, cocoa butter, and chocolate — which tree?
Theobroma cacao: Species of tree grown for its seeds.
This biological process lets a cell make an exact copy of its genetic material by using each strand of the double helix as a template for a new one — what is it called?
DNA replication: Biological process. DNA replication ensures that each of the newly divided daughter cells receives its own copy of each DNA molecule.
First described in 1845 by a German physicist, these two equalities govern current and voltage in electrical networks and generalized Georg Ohm's work — what are they called?
Kirchhoff's circuit laws: Two equalities that deal with the current and potential difference.
Often bonded to glucose to form sucrose, this simple sugar is found in honey, fruit, and most root vegetables — which sugar?
Fructose: Simple ketonic monosaccharide found in many plants.
Sometimes called gadflies, the females of this fly family bite land animals, including humans, to get the blood protein they need to produce eggs — which family?
Tabanidae: Family of insects. Horse flies and deer flies are true flies in the family Tabanidae in the insect order Diptera.
Ukraine's first female prime minister, she co-led the Orange Revolution and later led the Batkivshchyna party while championing EU integration — who is she?
Yulia Tymoshenko: Prime Minister of Ukraine (2005, 2007–2010)
Descended from a wild bovine ancestor, this large domesticated animal from the Indian subcontinent now also grazes fields in Italy, the Balkans, and Australia — what is it?
Water buffalo: Species of large bovine. The wild water buffalo (Bubalus arnee) is most probably the ancestor of the domestic water buffalo.
Released from prison in June 2025, this Turkish politician resumed leading the nationalist Victory Party after previously serving as deputy leader of the MHP — who is he?
Belonging to a fish family whose fossils date back to the Late Cretaceous, these long-lived, late-maturing fish share their order with paddlefish and once swam as far as North Africa — what are they?

A summer migrant to Europe and Asia that winters in Africa, this bird tricks other species into raising its young by laying eggs that mimic the host's, and even disguises itself as a hawk — what bird is it?
Common cuckoo: Species of bird. It is a brood parasite, which means it lays eggs in the nests of other bird species, particularly of dunnocks, meadow pipits, and reed warblers.
Sold under the brand name Abilify, this atypical antipsychotic treats schizophrenia, bipolar mania, and irritability linked to autism spectrum disorder — what is it?
Aripiprazole: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Aripiprazole is taken by mouth or via injection into a muscle.
Nicknamed the 'Sleeping Dragon' during his years in seclusion, this strategist was sought out three times by Liu Bei and helped engineer victory at the Battle of Red Cliffs — who is he?
Zhuge Liang: Chinese statesman and strategist (181–234)

A German former computer repair technician, this man received international attention after murdering and cannibalizing a voluntary victim he had found over the Internet in March 2001, and was ultimately convicted of murder in a 2006 retrial — who is he?

Armin Meiwes (born 1 December 1961) is a German former computer repair technician who received international attention for murdering and cannibalising Bernd Brandes, whom he had found via the Internet as a voluntary victim, in March 2001.
Awarded the 1976 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, this University of Chicago economist championed monetarism over Keynesianism and mentored future laureates like Gary Becker — who is he?
Milton Friedman: American economist and statistician (1912–2006)
Native to the Americas from Patagonia to western Canada, members of this succulent plant family thrive in the bone-dry Atacama Desert — what are they?
Cactus: Family of mostly succulent plants, adapted to dry environments.
This Dutch-born entrepreneur produced Japan's first major turn-based role-playing game and later secured the console distribution rights to a Russian puzzle game called Tetris — who is he?
Henk Rogers: Dutch-born American computer programmer (born 1953)
Continuous with the outer nuclear membrane and absent from red blood cells, this organelle comes in rough and smooth forms and handles protein folding — what is it?
Endoplasmic reticulum: Cell organelle that processes proteins.
Despite its name, this blister-agent chemical weapon isn't always gaseous, and to this day there is no antidote for exposure to it — what is it?
Mustard gas: Chemical warfare agent. There is no preventive agent against mustard gas, with protection depending entirely on skin and airways protection, and no antidote exists for mustard poisoning.
Also called ramsons or bear leek, this bulbous woodland plant native to Eurasia is a wild cousin of onion and garlic — what is it?
Allium ursinum: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
Encompassing several superfamilies and families, this taxonomic order groups together cephalopods that each have ten arms — which order is it?
Latin for 'little brain,' this hindbrain structure fine-tunes motor coordination and timing without actually initiating movement — what is it?
Cerebellum: Structure at the rear of the vertebrate brain, beneath the cerebrum.
Connected to the fetus by the umbilical cord, this temporary organ handles nutrient and waste exchange between mother and baby during pregnancy — what is it?
Placenta: Organ that connects the fetus to the uterine wall.
Awarded the 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering energy quanta, this German physicist originated quantum theory and lent his name to a fundamental physical constant — who is he?
Writing in 499 CE that he was 23 years old, this pioneering Indian scholar's explicit discussion of the relativity of motion marks him as an early physicist too — who was he?
Numbering roughly 160,000 species and mostly active at night, these insects share an order with butterflies but are known for their duller, darker wings — what are they?
Moth: Group of mostly-nocturnal insects in the order Lepidoptera.
Son of a U.S. vice president, this young art collector vanished in 1961 during an expedition into New Guinea's Asmat region, with some accounts claiming he was killed by local tribesmen — who was he?
Michael Rockefeller: American anthropologist and art collector (1938–1961)

The only woman among Einstein's classmates at Zurich Polytechnic, this Serbian mathematician was his first wife and is still debated as a possible collaborator on his 1905 miracle-year papers. Who was she?
Mileva Marić: Wife of Albert Einstein (1875–1948)

This biological process splits a parent into two daughters, either producing genetically identical copies via mitosis or reducing chromosome number by half via meiosis to form gametes. What process is it?
Cell division: Biological process. Cell division usually occurs as part of a larger cell cycle in which the cell grows and replicates its chromosome(s) before dividing.
Sold under the brand name Mobic, this NSAID in the oxicam family blocks COX-2 more strongly than COX-1 and ranked 27th among the most prescribed US medications in 2023. What drug is it?
This broad category of creative disciplines spans painting, sculpture, photography, and architecture, and includes applied fields like industrial and fashion design — what do we call it?
Visual arts are art forms such as painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, photography, video, image, filmmaking, design, crafts, and architecture.
Grown for both food and fiber, this plant's seeds are pressed into linseed oil while its stem fibers are woven into linen for sheets and clothing. What plant is it?

Derived from an East Asian evergreen tree's wood, this waxy, strong-smelling terpenoid can also be synthesized from oil of turpentine and occurs in small amounts in rosemary leaves. What compound is it?

Named after a long-nosed, insect-eating African animal, this 1960s supersonic fighter-bomber pioneered variable-sweep wings and automated terrain-following radar under Robert McNamara's TFX program. What aircraft is it?
General Dynamics F-111 Aardvark: Family of strike aircraft developed in 1960s.
The only living relative of the extinct Steller's sea cow, this seagrass-grazing marine mammal is most abundant in the waters of northern Australia — what is it?
Dugong: Species of marine mammal. It is one of four living species of the order Sirenia, which also includes three species of manatees.
Element 88 reacts with nitrogen rather than oxygen in air, turning black, and once glowed in self-luminous paints despite being highly carcinogenic — which element is it?
Radium: Chemical element with atomic number 88 (Ra)
Dating back to the Neolithic Revolution around 13,000 BC, this branch of agriculture covers the breeding, feeding, and day-to-day care of livestock raised for meat, milk, or fiber — what's it called?
Animal husbandry is the branch of agriculture concerned with animals that are raised for meat, fibre, milk, or other products.

With black-tipped wings and long red legs and bill, this long-distance migrant famously avoids the open Mediterranean, detouring instead via Gibraltar or the Levant on its way to African wintering grounds — which bird is it?
White stork: Species of bird. The white stork (Ciconia ciconia) is a large bird in the stork family, Ciconiidae.

Associated with the early 20th century, this philosophical movement tries to objectively describe subjective conscious experience exactly as it appears, without assuming anything about the outside world — which movement?
Phenomenology (philosophy) is a philosophical study and movement largely associated with the early 20th century that seeks to objectively investigate the nature of subjective, conscious experience.
A cole crop related to broccoli, cauliflower and Brussels sprouts, the heaviest recorded head of this leafy vegetable weighed nearly 138 pounds — what is it?
Cabbage: Leafy vegetable in the flowering plant family Brassicaceae.
This Russian polymath discovered the atmosphere of Venus and formulated the law of conservation of mass, while also helping shape the modern Russian literary language as a poet — who is he?

Named in 1842 from Brazilian fossils and often called a saber-toothed tiger despite no close kinship to true tigers, this genus of prehistoric predator roamed the Americas until the early Holocene — which animal?
Smilodon: Extinct genus of saber-toothed cat.
This English musician played bass on the Rolling Stones' first nineteen studio albums across three decades before later fronting his own blues outfit, the Rhythm Kings — who is he?
Originating from the heart's left ventricle, this is the largest artery in the human body, eventually splitting into the two common iliac arteries in the abdomen — what is it?
Aorta: Largest artery in the human body. The aorta distributes oxygenated blood to all parts of the body through the systemic circulation.
Named for its 'skin wings,' this insect order sports pincer-like cerci on its abdomen and displays unusually attentive maternal care for its young — which insect?
Earwig: Order of insects. Damage to foliage, flowers, and various crops is commonly blamed on earwigs, especially the common earwig Forficula auricularia.

Driven by a gradient in chemical potential, this stochastic process describes the net movement of particles from areas of higher to lower concentration and can even reverse direction in spinodal decomposition — what physical process is this?
Diffusion: Transport of dissolved species from the highest to the lowest concentration region.

Originally cultivated by the ancient Egyptians and now grown worldwide with China producing over half the crop, this leafy Asteraceae vegetable also has a stem-focused variety called celtuce — name the vegetable?
Lettuce: Species of annual plant of the daisy family, most often grown as a leaf vegetable.

This atypical antipsychotic treats schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and autism-related aggression, but carries a risk of the potentially permanent movement disorder tardive dyskinesia — name the drug?
Risperidone: Antipsychotic medication. It is taken either by mouth or by injection (i.e., subcutaneous or intramuscular).
As the largest member of the grass family, one species of this plant can grow stalks over 46 meters tall and 36 centimeters thick — name the plant?
Bamboo: Subfamily of plants in the grass family.
Convicted in 1995 of fraud and illegally intercepting communications, this hacker served five years in prison before founding his own computer-security consulting firm — who is he?
Native to Asia, Europe, and western North America, this flowering shrub's fragrant blooms last just 7 to 10 days each spring — which plant?
Peony: Genus of flowering plants in the family Paeoniaceae.
Nicknamed the fish hawk, this diurnal bird of prey has a wingspan up to 180 centimeters and hunts almost exclusively fish — which bird?
Osprey: Species of bird. The osprey (Pandion haliaetus), historically known as sea hawk, river hawk, and fish hawk, is a diurnal, fish-eating bird of prey with a cosmopolitan range.
Sold under the brand name Cialis, this erectile dysfunction medication can remain effective for up to 36 hours after a single dose — which drug?
Tadalafil: Medication used to treat erectile dysfunction.
Responsible for nearly 40 percent of blindness cases worldwide in 2020, this condition clouds the eye's lens and causes halos around lights — which condition?
Cataract: Clouding of the lens inside the eye, causing poor vision.

David Attenborough called this English particle physicist the natural successor for the BBC's scientific programming, thanks to shows like The Infinite Monkey Cage and his Wonders of... series — who is he?
Brian Cox (physicist) (born 3 March 1968) is an English physicist and musician.
Prized both as a delicacy and, in some species, for the pearls grown within its shell, which salt-water bivalve is this?
Oyster: Variety of families of Mollusca.
Named after the American diplomat who introduced it from Mexico, this red-and-green Christmas plant is not actually toxic to pets — which plant?
A wartime myth claimed eating this vegetable helped British pilots see in the dark — really a cover story for radar — which root vegetable?
Carrot: Root vegetable. The carrot (Daucus carota subsp. sativus) is a root vegetable in the umbellifer family Apiaceae.
Colloquially known as a moon, this type of astronomical body orbits a planet or dwarf planet, with 455 confirmed examples across the Solar System's six major systems — what is it called?
Natural satellite: Astronomical body that orbits a planet. Natural satellites are colloquially referred to as moons, by analogy with the Moon, Earth's natural satellite.
Colloquially called a buffalo in the US and Canada, this large bovine is actually more closely related to yaks and cattle than to true buffalo — which animal?
Caused by viral infections, autoimmune disorders, or pulmonary embolism, this condition inflames the membranes lining the lungs and chest cavity, causing sharp pain when breathing — which condition?
Pleurisy: Disease of the lungs. Pleurisy, also known as pleuritis, is inflammation of the membranes that surround the lungs and line the chest cavity (pleurae).
Native to the Baltic, Black, and Caspian Sea basins, this large freshwater fish's range now stretches from the UK to western China — which species?
Wels catfish: Species of fish. It has been introduced to several countries in Western Europe, Mediterranean and Asia as a prized sport fish.
Spread mainly through blood-to-blood contact, this viral infection becomes chronic in about 70 percent of those first infected and can lead to liver failure over decades — which disease?
Hepatitis C: Human viral infection. Hepatitis C is an infectious disease caused by the hepatitis C virus (HCV) that primarily affects the liver; it is a type of viral hepatitis.
Historically fermented and used in gunpowder production, leather tanning, and textile dyeing, this bodily fluid also helps plants grow when used as fertilizer — what is it?
Urine: Liquid by-product of animal metabolism.
This rhythmic process of inhaling and exhaling delivers oxygen to the alveoli and removes carbon dioxide, with its per-minute rate counted as a vital sign — what is it?
Breathing: Process of moving air in and out of the lungs.

A member of the mint family native to the Mediterranean, this grayish-leaved perennial subshrub is used both in cooking and as an ornamental garden plant — which herb, better known by its common name sage?
Salvia officinalis: Species of plant. Salvia officinalis, common sage or sage, is a perennial, evergreen subshrub, with woody stems, grayish leaves, and blue to purplish flowers.
This group of inherited blood disorders reduces hemoglobin production and is classified as alpha or beta depending on which globin gene is deficient. What condition is it?
Thalassemia: Family of inherited blood disorders. Symptoms depend on the type of thalassemia and can vary from none to severe, including death.

The smallest member of this genus, found in Great Britain, is also considered the tiniest carnivorous mammal species on Earth, with some populations turning white in winter. What group of small predators is this?
Weasel: Mammal of the mustelid family.

Native to New Guinea and domesticated by Papuan and Austronesian peoples, this tall grass with sucrose-rich stalks was carried across the Pacific and eventually to India and China in ancient times. What crop is it?
Sugarcane: Several species of grass used for sugar production.

Originating in South America and rapidly diversifying after the extinction of the dinosaurs, this plant family — commonly known as the nightshades — includes toxic alkaloid-rich species alongside tomatoes, potatoes, and peppers. What family is it?

First proposed as early as the 3rd century BC by Aristarchus of Samos, this astronomical model places the sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe. What is this superseded model called?
Heliocentrism: Sun-centered astronomical model. Historically, heliocentrism was opposed to geocentrism, which placed Earth at the center.

Found in many cough and cold medicines, this morphinan-class compound was approved by the FDA in 2022 as part of a rapid-acting antidepressant combo, but can act as a dissociative hallucinogen at high doses. What substance is it?
Dextromethorphan: Cough suppressant and dissociative drug.

This informal name applies to any shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc — a body plan that evolved independently many times through convergent evolution across unrelated lineages. What creature is it?
Slug: Shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc. Slug or land slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.
This Soviet chemist led efforts to contain the 1986 Chernobyl disaster and later briefed the international community in Vienna, though he omitted key design flaws in the reactor. Who was he?
Valery Legasov: Former Soviet inorganic chemist and member of the USSR Academy of Sciences (1936–1988)
Known as linden, lime, or basswood depending on the region, this genus of about 30 tree species is the only one in its plant family to form ectomycorrhizal fungal partnerships. What genus is it?
Tilia: Plant genus. Tilia is a genus of about 30 species of trees or bushes, native throughout most of the temperate Northern Hemisphere.
A Russian pediatric endocrinologist also known by the surname Faassen, this woman is the elder child of Russia's president. Who is she?
Maria Vorontsova: Daughter of Vladimir Putin (born 1985)

Often stereotyped as ferocious predators, these South American freshwater fish actually have varied diets that include plant matter, making them more omnivorous than their reputation suggests. What fish are they?
Piranha: Common name for certain fishes of the family Serrasalmidae.

Nicknamed the 'dark lady of DNA,' this X-ray crystallographer's crucial contributions to the discovery of DNA's structure went largely unrecognized in her lifetime — James Watson believed she'd have won a Nobel Prize had she lived. Who was she?

Known for quoting multiple religious scriptures in English lectures delivered in a suit and tie rather than traditional robes, this Indian preacher had his foundation banned in 2016 amid hate-speech and money-laundering accusations. Who is he?
Used to treat nausea, vomiting, and gastroparesis, this dopamine receptor antagonist is also prescribed for migraines and appears on the WHO's List of Essential Medicines — what is it?
Metoclopramide: Medication. It is thus rarely recommended that people take the medication for longer than twelve weeks.
This semiaquatic rodent swims using webbed hind feet while its scaly, flattened tail works mainly as a rudder for steering — what is it?
Muskrat: Species of rodent. The muskrat or common muskrat (Ondatra zibethicus) is a medium-sized semiaquatic rodent.
Comprising 18 to 24 species that hybridize freely where their ranges overlap, this genus of the mint family thrives in wet, moist soils worldwide — what is it?
Mentha: Genus of flowering plants in the family Lamiaceae.
Native to Central and Western Asia, this leafy green vegetable's high oxalate content can be reduced by blanching before eating — what is it?

Though its wild populations are considered vulnerable to extinction, this domesticated freshwater fish has been introduced so widely that it's listed among the world's 100 worst invasive species — what is it?
Common carp: Species of fish. It gives its name to the carp family, Cyprinidae.
Native to the subcontinent, the male of this bird species is called a peacock and sports a fan-shaped crest with a dazzling train of eyespot feathers used in courtship — which species?
Indian peafowl: Species of bird. The Indian peafowl (Pavo cristatus), also known as the common peafowl, or blue peafowl, is a species of peafowl native to the Indian subcontinent.
This condition involves a buildup of cerebrospinal fluid around the brain, causing headaches, vision problems, and in babies a rapidly enlarging head — what is it?
Hydrocephalus: Abnormal increase in cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles of the brain.
Most commonly referring to a type called PET, this category of polymers built from ester linkages is often blended with cotton to reduce wrinkling — what is it called?
Polyester: Category of polymers, in which the monomers are joined together by ester links.
This biennial vegetable in the onion family has an edible bundle of leaf sheaths sometimes colloquially called a 'stem' — what is it?
Leek: Vegetable in the onion family. A leek is a biennial vegetable, a cultivar of Allium ampeloprasum, the broadleaf wild leek (syn.
Running a boutique called Sex with partner Malcolm McLaren, this English designer helped bring punk fashion into the mainstream and shaped the look of the Sex Pistols — who is she?
This medical emergency occurs when the heart suddenly stops beating effectively, cutting off blood flow to the brain and other organs within minutes — what is it called?
Cardiac arrest: Sudden or unexpected loss of heartbeat.
This junctional area between the torso and thigh, where the lower abdominal wall meets the leg, is commonly strained in a familiar sports injury — what is it called?
Groin: Area between the torso and the thigh. In human anatomy, the groin, also known as the inguinal region or iliac region, is the junctional area between the torso and the thigh.
Despite being just 12 to 20 cm long, this small marine creature's vivid markings flash brighter when it feels threatened, and its bite delivers a neurotoxin called tetrodotoxin — what is it?
Blue-ringed octopus: Four species of mollusk.
Patented in 1922 and later marketed as Novalgin or Analgin, this painkiller's sale is restricted in some countries due to a rare blood-cell risk called agranulocytosis — what is it?
Metamizole: Medication. Metamizole or dipyrone is a painkiller, spasm reliever, and fever reliever drug.
Credited as the inventor of radio, this Italian engineer shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics and later set up Vatican Radio for Pope Pius XI — who is he?
Guglielmo Marconi: Italian radio-frequency engineer and inventor (1874–1937)

Named after the patron saint of sailors, this luminous blue or violet glow appears around masts, spires, or aircraft during a strong electric field and can warn of an imminent lightning strike — what is this phenomenon called?
St. Elmo's fire: Luminous plasma created in an electric field.
Deriving its name from Greek words for 'earth' and 'study of', this branch of natural science examines rocks and the processes that have shaped the planet over time — what is it called?
Geology: Scientific study of Earth's physical composition.
This genus of coniferous trees and shrubs in the cypress family includes a species that forms the world's highest-known forest, at 4,900 metres in the Himalayas — what is it called?
This system of rules governing clauses, phrases, and word use is often absorbed unconsciously in childhood, long before anyone studies its syntax formally — what field?
Grammar: Structural rules of a language.
With red compound eyes set wider apart in females, this insect lays batches of about 100 eggs on decaying matter that hatch into maggots — which species?
Housefly: Species of insect. The housefly (Musca domestica) is a fly of the suborder Cyclorrhapha.

Typically begun with an induction of preliminary instructions, this state of focused attention and heightened suggestibility is debated as either an altered trance or a form of imaginative role-play — what is it?
Hypnosis: State of increased suggestibility. There are competing theories explaining hypnosis and related phenomena.
Rooted in prehistoric herbalism for identifying edible and medicinal species, this branch of biology studies roughly 410,000 species of land plants — what field of study?

Caused by a bacterium and often symptomless for weeks after exposure, this sexually transmitted infection can lead to pelvic inflammatory disease and infertility in women if untreated — which infection?
Chlamydia: Sexually transmitted bacterial infection. Chlamydia, or more specifically a chlamydia infection, is a sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis.
Originally conceived as the average Earth-Sun distance before its 2012 redefinition, this measure equals about 499 light-seconds and underpins the definition of the parsec — what is it called?
Astronomical unit: Mean distance between Earth and the Sun.
Best known for its powerful, beautiful song, this small Old World flycatcher sometimes hybridizes with a closely related thrush species where their ranges overlap — which bird?
Common nightingale: Species of bird. Its range partly overlaps with that of the more northerly thrush nightingale (Luscinia luscinia), a closely related species with which hybrids have occurred.

This steel-gray, brittle alkaline earth metal is found naturally only in combination with other elements, making up gemstones like aquamarine and emerald, and bonds so strongly to oxygen that extracting it is notoriously difficult — which element, atomic number 4?
Beryllium: Chemical element with atomic number 4 (Be)
This biochemical process lets an organism turn food and water into energy and building blocks, and can go wrong with too much or too little of certain essential substances — what process?
Nutrition: Provision to cells and organisms to support life.
First described in 1821, this family of large herbivorous mammals features a snout modified into a trunk and includes extinct relatives such as mammoths — which taxonomic family?
Elephantidae: Family of mammals. The family was first described by John Edward Gray in 1821, and later assigned to taxonomic ranks within the order Proboscidea.
Developed by a South Korean aerospace firm with Lockheed Martin and first flown in 2002, this supersonic jet trainer became the country's first indigenous supersonic aircraft — which aircraft family?
KAI T-50 Golden Eagle: Family of South Korean jet aircraft. It is South Korea's first indigenous supersonic aircraft and one of the world's few supersonic trainers.
Famous for drumming tree trunks with its beak to forage for insects and send signals, one desert species of this bird family pecks into cacti instead — what is it?
Woodpecker: Family of birds. The family Picidae includes about 240 species arranged in 35 genera.

Native to Europe and North Africa, this member of the carrot family can grow to 8 feet tall, with hollow stems blotched dark maroon and a distinctly foul smell carried on the wind — which highly poisonous plant is this?
Conium maculatum: Poisonous plant. The plant is herbaceous, with no woody parts, and has a biennial lifecycle.

Often called the mirror image of depression, this psychiatric state brings racing thoughts, pressured speech, boundless energy, and a shrinking need for sleep — what is this elevated mood syndrome called?
Mania: State of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, arousal, and/or energy levels.
The body's primary muscle of respiration, this dome-shaped sheet separates the chest cavity from the abdomen and contracts to pull air into the lungs — what is it?
Thoracic diaphragm: Sheet of internal skeletal muscle.

Marked by tea-colored urine and triggered by crush injuries or extreme exertion, this condition involves skeletal muscle breaking down so fast that released myoglobin can damage the kidneys — what is it called?
Rhabdomyolysis: Condition in which damaged skeletal muscle breaks down rapidly.
Also known as the penny bun or porcino, this prized edible fungus can grow a brown cap up to a foot wide and forms symbiotic partnerships with forest tree roots — which mushroom?
Boletus edulis: Species of mushroom, widely distributed in the Northern Hemisphere.
Also known as hawthorn, quickthorn, or May-tree, this genus of several hundred shrub and tree species in the rose family is native across the temperate Northern Hemisphere — which genus?
Crataegus: Genus of flowering plants in the rose family Rosaceae.

Sold under the brand name Zofran, this serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist prevents chemotherapy- and surgery-related nausea without the dopamine-blocking side effects that cause muscle restlessness — what is this drug?
Ondansetron: Medication to prevent nausea and vomiting.
Co-founder of the file-sharing service Napster, this entrepreneur became Facebook's first president before later founding a philanthropic foundation focused on life sciences — who is he?
Sean Parker: American entrepreneur and philanthropist (born 1979)
Native to sub-Saharan grasslands and woodlands, this animal is the largest living land species, with the largest recorded specimen standing nearly 13 feet tall at the shoulder — which species is it?
African bush elephant: Species of mammal. Its skin is grey with scanty hairs, and bending cracks which support thermoregulation by retaining water.
Nicknamed 'handy man' for its toolmaking, this archaic human species lived in East and South Africa as far back as 2.4 million years ago — which species?
Homo habilis: Archaic human species from 2.4 to 1.65 mya.
This healthcare profession uses patient education and hands-on interventions to prevent, treat, and restore mobility, with specialties from sports medicine to pediatrics — which field?
Physical therapy: Profession that helps a disabled person function in everyday life.
Nearly odorless with a faintly sweet taste, this diol is approved as a food additive under E-number E1520 and serves as a solvent vehicle in many medications — which compound?
Propylene glycol: Chemical compound. Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
This field studies how geography shapes international relations and foreign policy, though critics have dismissed its early theories as pseudoscience — which discipline?
Geopolitics: Study of geography's effects on politics.
This throat infection causes fever, red tonsils, and swollen neck glands, and can trigger a sandpaper-textured rash known as scarlet fever — which condition?
Septic throat due to streptococcal infection
Septic sore throat due to streptococcal infection
Streptococcal pharyngitis: Medical condition. It may be spread directly through touching infected sores.
Discovered via its telltale green spectral line in 1861, this silvery post-transition metal takes its name from the Greek word for a green shoot — which element?
Thallium: Chemical element with atomic number 81 (Tl)
Discovered in 1910 and stored in mast cells and basophils, this compound triggers immune responses and doubles as a neurotransmitter in the brain, spinal cord, and uterus — what is it?
Histamine: Organic compound involved in immune responses.
Formed when quicklime reacts with water, this compound goes by names like slaked lime and builders' lime, and is used in food prep under the additive code E526 — what is it?
Calcium hydroxide: Inorganic compound of formula Ca(OH)2.
Often triggered by H. pylori infection or NSAID use, this inflammation of the stomach lining can, in its autoimmune form, lead to pernicious anemia — what condition is it?
Gastritis: Inflammation of the stomach lining. It may occur as a short episode or have a long duration.
Sold under the brand name Protonix, this proton-pump inhibitor treats ulcers and acid reflux but can, with long-term use, cause vitamin B12 deficiency and low magnesium — what is this drug?

Known in France as the Patou and in the US by another name, this French livestock guardian breed hails from a range straddling France and Spain, protecting flocks from wolves and bears. What breed is it?
Pyrenean Mountain Dog: French breed of dog. The Pyrenean Mountain Dog (Chien de Montagne des Pyrénées) is a French breed of livestock guardian dog.
This insect order unites cockroaches with termites, after genetic evidence showed termites are actually evolved, eusocial cockroaches. What's the order called?
Blattodea: Order of insects that includes cockroaches and termites.

Once diagnosed almost exclusively in women during the 19th century and studied intensely by Sigmund Freud and Jean-Martin Charcot, this term for 'ungovernable emotional excess' is no longer accepted as a medical diagnosis. What is it called?
Hysteria: Excess, ungovernable emotion. Hysteria is a term used to mean ungovernable emotional excess and can refer to a temporary state of mind or emotion.
Covered in sharp keratin quills for defense, this rodent's largest species ranks as the third-biggest living rodent in the world, behind only the capybara and the beaver. What animal is it?
Porcupine: Rodent with a coat of sharp spines.

Identified in 1898 by an Italian pathologist and later named in his honor, this cell organelle packages proteins into vesicles and adds sugar chains before shipping them to their destination. What is it called?
Golgi apparatus: Cell organelle that packages proteins for export.

Also called 'German measles,' this vaccine-preventable viral infection is usually mild but can cause severe birth defects — including cataracts and deafness — if a mother catches it early in pregnancy. What disease is it?
Rubella: Human viral disease. Rubella, also known as German measles or three-day measles, is a vaccine-preventable infection caused by the rubella virus.

Usually triggered by a viral infection and common in people with asthma or cystic fibrosis, this inflammation of the facial mucous membranes causes congestion, facial pain, and loss of smell. What condition is it?
Sinusitis: Inflammation of the sinus' membranes. Sinusitis is a condition that affects both children and adults.
Its name translates to 'three-horned face,' and this frilled dinosaur roamed present-day western North America right up until the asteroid strike 66 million years ago — what dinosaur is it?
Triceratops: Genus of Late Cretaceous dinosaur.
This warbler's head marking gives it its name — dark in the male, chestnut in the female — and its closest relative is the garden warbler. What bird is it?
Eurasian blackcap: Bird in the Old World warbler family from Eurasia and Africa.
Named after the German city where it originated, this all-purpose gun dog breed was officially recognized in 1891 — what breed is it?
Weimaraner: German breed of dog. The Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.
Domesticated in Asia, this crunchy root vegetable in the mustard family owes its peppery bite to compounds like glucosinolate — what vegetable is it?
Radish: Root vegetable of the Brassicaceae family. The radish (Raphanus sativus or Raphanus raphanistrum subsp. sativus) is a flowering plant in the mustard family, Brassicaceae.
This field of study focuses on the methodological principles of interpreting texts — especially biblical and philosophical writings — and is closely related to exegesis. What is it called?
Hermeneutics: The study of the methodological principles of interpretation. As necessary, hermeneutics may include the art of understanding and communication.
Native to the northern tundra, this small mammal grows thick white fur for winter camouflage and forms monogamous breeding pairs while preying on lemmings and seabirds — what animal is it?
Arctic fox: Species of fox. It is well adapted to living in cold environments, and is known for its thick, warm fur that can be used as camouflage against snow in the winter.
This Canadian-born entrepreneur co-founded and serves as CEO of Roblox Corporation, after his earlier company was acquired by MSC Software in 1998 — who is he?

Nicknamed the deaf adder or long-cripple in parts of Europe, this legless, burrowing lizard has smooth scales that don't overlap — and despite its name, it's neither a snake nor what it sounds like. What is it?
Common slow worm: Species of legless lizard. The common slow worm (Anguis fragilis) is a non-venomous species of legless lizard native to Europe.
This cat-family genus contains the five biggest living cats — jaguar, leopard, lion, snow leopard, and tiger — plus extinct relatives like the cave lion and American lion. Which genus is it?

Defined by a single oxygen atom bridging two organyl groups (R−O−R′), this class of organic compounds includes a once-standard surgical anesthetic that lends its common one-word name to the whole family. What class of compound is this?
Ether: Organic compounds made of alkyl/aryl groups bound to oxygen (R–O–R')

Marketed under brand names like Sudafed, this nasal decongestant can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant at higher doses, making it both a medicine-cabinet staple and, at times, a drug of abuse. What is it?
Pseudoephedrine: Synthetic decongestant. Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic medication which is used as a nasal decongestant to treat nasal congestion.

Latin for 'worm-shaped,' this finger-like, blind-ended tube branches off the cecum and, though long considered vestigial, may actually serve as a reservoir for beneficial gut bacteria. What structure is this?
Appendix (anatomy): Tube attached to the intestine.

This umbrella term for joint disease covers conditions like osteoarthritis, most common in weight-bearing joints as people age, and the autoimmune form that typically targets the hands and feet. What condition is this?

Cultivated in China for more than 2,000 years despite not being formally described until 1780, this tree produces the most widely grown fruit in its genus, known by names like Japanese or Chinese persimmon. Which species?
Diospyros kaki: Oriental fruit. Although its first botanical description was not published until 1780, D. kaki cultivation in China dates back more than 2000 years.

This psychological term describes reduced motivation or ability to experience pleasure, recognized in the DSM-5 as a component of depressive, substance-related, psychotic, and personality disorders. What is it called?

Nicknamed 'Huey,' this American utility helicopter became the first turbine-powered rotorcraft in U.S. military service, developed in the 1950s to meet an Army need for medical evacuation and utility missions. Which aircraft?
Bell UH-1 Iroquois: Huey family of American military utility helicopters.

Grown for its fleshy, edible stalks since before the 18th century in Europe and Scandinavia, this plant's broad triangular leaves are actually poisonous due to their high oxalic acid content. What is it?
Rhubarb: Species of herbaceous perennial plant with fleshy, sour edible stalks.
Documented anatomically since the time of Hippocrates over 2,000 years ago, this roughly 4-centimeter-long fibromuscular organ connects the vagina to the uterine cavity. What structure is this?
Cervix: Lower part of the uterus in the female reproductive system.

Also known as the wisent, this species is the heaviest wild land mammal on its continent — hunted to extinction in the wild by the early 20th century before being restored through captive breeding programs. Which animal?
European bison: Eurasian species of mammal. It is one of two extant species of bison, alongside the American bison.
Also called the red date or Chinese date, this buckthorn-family fruit is eaten fresh, dried, or candied — what is it?
Jujube: Species of plant with edible fruit.
Grown as the source of the tropical mango fruit, this evergreen tree in the cashew family can reach 30 meters tall and comes in two genetic types — what species is it?
Mangifera indica: Species of flowering plant in the cashew family Anacardiaceae.
This colorless, odorless nerve agent can kill within minutes of inhalation and was banned by the 1993 Chemical Weapons Convention — what is it?
Sarin: Chemical compound and chemical warfare nerve agent.
Home to cereal crops like wheat, rice, and maize as well as bamboo, this is the fifth-largest plant family on Earth — what is it called?
Poaceae: Family of flowering plants commonly known as grasses.
This genus native to South and Southeast Asia gave rise to oranges, lemons, and limes through extensive hybridization — what is it?
Creator of both a widely used open-source operating system kernel and the version-control system Git, this engineer won the 2012 Millennium Technology Prize — who is he?
Linus Torvalds: Finnish and American software engineer (born 1969)

Known mainly through DNA evidence rather than plentiful fossils, this extinct archaic human group ranged across Asia until about 32,000 years ago, and DNA analysis confirmed the Harbin skull belonged to it — what group is it?
Denisovan: Archaic human species from Asia.
Despite its common name, this Eurasian wolf-like canid is more closely related to wolves and coyotes than to its African namesakes — what animal is it?
Derived from an ancient Roman unit called the uncia, this measure comes in an avoirdupois version equal to 1/16 of a pound and a heavier troy version used for precious metals — what unit is it?
Ounce: Unit of mass. The ounce is any of several different units of mass, weight, or volume and is derived almost unchanged from the uncia, an Ancient Roman unit of measurement.

Known also as the Zambezi or Lake Nicaragua species, this aggressive fish can thrive in both salt and fresh water, having been tracked more than 1,100 kilometers up the Mississippi River — what animal is it?
Bull shark: Species of fish. Bull sharks are listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.
Unlike its counterpart which returns blood to the heart, this blood vessel usually carries oxygen-rich blood away from it — what is it?
Artery: Blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart.
This crustacean typically swims forward using its swimmerets but can flick its tail to dart backward in a defensive move called 'lobstering' — what is it?
Named for the mathematician who used it to solve the heat equation, this expansion writes a periodic function as an infinite sum of sines and cosines — what is it?
Fourier series: Decomposition of periodic functions.
This medical term describes a resting heart rate that exceeds 100 beats per minute — what is it?
Tachycardia: Heart rate exceeding normal resting rate.
Covered in taste buds and divided into oral and pharyngeal parts, this muscular mouth organ also helps clean the teeth and enable speech — what is it?
Tongue: Muscular organ in the mouth of most vertebrates.
This glucocorticoid medication used to suppress the immune system is actually a prodrug that the liver must convert into its active form before it works — what is it?
Prednisone: Steroid medication. It is also used to treat high blood calcium due to cancer and adrenal insufficiency along with other corticosteroids.

This interdisciplinary field combines a power source, mechanical construction, control circuits, and software to design machines that assist humans in fields from medicine to space exploration — what is it?
Robotics: Design, construction, use, and application of robots.
Native to North Africa and West Asia, this annual herb in the celery family lends its leaves and seeds as both an herb and a spice — what is it?
Dill: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae.
This normal, occasionally embarrassing bodily process brings intestinal gas to the rectum, pressurizes it with muscle contractions, and releases it through the anus — what is it?
Flatulence: Bodily function of expelling intestinal gas from the anus.

First imagined by Olaf Stapledon in his 1937 novel Star Maker and later named for a physicist who explored the idea in 1960, this hypothetical megastructure would encircle a star to harvest its energy — what is it?
Dyson sphere: Hypothetical megastructure around a star. A Dyson sphere is a hypothetical megastructure that encompasses a star and captures a large percentage of its power output.

The most widespread bird in its family, found on every continent except Antarctica (where only stray vagrants appear), this species has blue upperparts, a deeply forked tail, and usually nests in man-made structures — what is it?
Barn swallow: Species of bird. The barn swallow (Hirundo rustica) is the most widespread species of swallow in the world, occurring on all continents, with vagrants reported even in Antarctica.
Developed for the Soviet Union, this swept-wing jet fighter dominated early dogfights in the Korean War and prompted the US to rush its F-86 Sabre into combat — which aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15: Soviet fighter aircraft. The MiG-15 was one of the first successful jet fighters to incorporate swept wings to perform near Mach 1.
With the chemical formula CaO, this white, caustic, alkaline solid is produced by heating limestone and has been used since antiquity in construction and agriculture — what's the compound's name?
Calcium oxide (formula: CaO), commonly known as quicklime or burnt lime, is a widely used chemical compound.
Described in the New Testament as a physician, this traditional author of two New Testament books is said to have been martyred by hanging from an olive tree — who is he?
Luke the Evangelist: One of the four traditionally ascribed authors of the canonical gospels.
Sometimes called the paleomammalian cortex, this set of brain structures — including the amygdala — governs emotion, motivation, and long-term memory — what is it called?
Limbic system: Set of brain structures involved in emotion and motivation. Its various components support a variety of functions including emotion, behavior, long-term memory, and olfaction.

This anabolic steroid, derived from the nandrolone group, is used legally in livestock to boost muscle growth but also circulates illegally on the black market under a shortened nickname — what is it?
Trenbolone: Anabolic steroid. Trenbolone is an androgen and anabolic steroid (AAS) of the nandrolone group which itself was never marketed for human use.
This organ stores urine received from the kidneys via the ureters before it exits through the urethra, and gives us the medical term 'cystitis' when inflamed — what is it?
Bladder: Organ in vertebrates that collects and stores urine from the kidneys before disposal.
This group of RNA viruses, named for the club-shaped spikes that crown their surface, causes illnesses ranging from the common cold to SARS, MERS, and COVID-19 — what are they called?
Coronavirus: Subfamily of viruses in the family Coronaviridae.
Denoted by the Greek letter lambda, this measure of a repeating wave's spatial period shrinks as frequency rises for a wave moving at constant speed — what is it called?
Wavelength: Distance over which a wave's shape repeats.
With the formula B(OH)3 and found in nature as the mineral sassolite, this weak, water-soluble compound of boron serves as an antiseptic, insecticide, and flame retardant — which acid?
Boric acid is a compound of boron, oxygen, and hydrogen with formula B(OH)3.
Sometimes called a 'collapsed lung,' this condition involves air trapped in the space between the lung and chest wall, causing sudden sharp one-sided chest pain — what is it?
Pneumothorax: Abnormal collection of air in the pleural space.
Named from Greek words meaning 'porous bones,' this disorder causes bone density loss serious enough that fractures can occur with minor stress, especially in the elderly — what is it?
Osteoporosis: Skeletal disorder. Osteoporosis is the most common reason for a broken bone among the elderly.
Also known as warble flies or gadflies, the larvae of which insect family live as internal parasites in mammal flesh or gut, with one species routinely infesting humans?
Botfly: Parasitic insect. Dermatobia hominis is the only species of botfly known to parasitize humans routinely, though other species of flies cause myiasis in humans.
Sold under the brand name Provigil, this first-line narcolepsy treatment boosts dopamine without the euphoria or addiction risk of classic stimulants like amphetamine — what is it?
Made of the same tough protein as claws, hooves, and horns, this protective plate covers the tip of your fingers and toes — what is it?
Nail (anatomy): Hard keratin protection of digit.
Sold under the brand name Phenergan, this first-generation antihistamine treats allergies and nausea but has also seen recreational misuse alongside codeine — which drug?
Promethazine: Sedating antihistamine. Promethazine is taken by mouth (oral), as a rectal suppository, or by injection into a muscle (IM).
Broader than linguistics, this field studies how signs — from words to maps to clothing — form systems that carry meaning, split into syntactics, semantics, and pragmatics — what is it called?
Semiotics: Study of signs. It is an interdisciplinary field that examines what signs are, how they form sign systems, and how individuals use them to communicate meaning.
Extracted from the seeds of the castor oil plant, this lectin toxin carries an estimated lethal oral dose in humans of about one milligram per kilogram — what is it?
Dubbed the 'Prophet of the Space Age,' this English science fiction author co-wrote the screenplay for 2001: A Space Odyssey and formed sci-fi's 'Big Three' with Heinlein and Asimov — who is he?
Arthur C. Clarke: British science fiction writer (1917–2008)
Named for both the tree and its edible nut, this genus of temperate deciduous trees belongs to the beech family — what is it?
Chestnut: Genus of plants. The name also refers to the edible nuts they produce.
Nicknamed the painted hunter for its mottled coat, this sub-Saharan canine hunts cooperatively at dawn and dusk and is the only living member of its genus, Lycaon — which species?
African wild dog: Species of canine. The African wild dog (Lycaon pictus), also called painted dog and Cape hunting dog, is a wild canine native to sub-Saharan Africa.
This medical specialty diagnoses and treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves, from epilepsy and stroke to Parkinson's disease — which field?
Neurology: Medical specialty dealing with disorders of the nervous system.

Known to NATO by the reporting name Hokum A and nicknamed 'Black Shark' for its distinctive coaxial rotors, this Russian single-seat attack helicopter has a rare rescue ejection system — which aircraft?
Kamov Ka-50: Attack helicopter. It was designed in the 1980s and adopted for service in the Russian army in 1995.
This Taiwanese-American engineer co-founded YouTube and served as its CTO before later building the video app MixBit — who is he?
A pseudoscientific but ancient component of traditional Chinese medicine, this practice involves inserting thin needles into the body, most often for pain relief — what is it called?
This essential amino acid, which the body can't make on its own, is a precursor to serotonin, melatonin, and vitamin B3 — which amino acid?
Marked by high blood pressure and protein in the urine after 20 weeks of pregnancy, this disorder can progress to seizures if left untreated — what is it called?
Nicknamed 'The Professor' on The Chase, this record-breaking contestant won 74 consecutive games on a legendary quiz show in 2004 before eventually becoming its host — who is he?
Ken Jennings: American game show host (born 1974)
Split into structural biology, enzymology, and metabolism, this scientific field studies the chemical processes that occur within living organisms — which field?

Biochemistry: Study of chemical processes of living organisms. Biochemistry, or biological chemistry (distinct from chemical biology), is the study of chemical processes within and relating to living organisms.

Proposed in 1904 and finally proven a century later using Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow techniques, this problem asks whether any loop-shrinkable finite 3D space must be a hypersphere — which famous problem?
Poincaré conjecture: Theorem in geometric topology.

This male sexual dysfunction occurs when orgasm happens very soon after minimal sexual stimulation, with medical experts generally setting the threshold at around one minute — what's this condition called?

Premature ejaculation (PE) is a male sexual dysfunction that occurs when a male expels semen (and most likely experiences orgasm) soon after beginning sexual activity, and with minimal penile stimulation.
Sometimes grown just for looks, this cabbage relative's leaves can be bumpy, curly, or flat, in colors from purple to green — what leafy vegetable is it?
Kale: Form of cabbage with green or purple leaves.
Native to the arid Americas, most rosettes of this succulent genus flower gloriously just once before dying, earning one species the nickname 'century plant' — what genus is it?
First named in 1703 to honor a French botanist, this genus of 200-plus flowering trees and shrubs produces large fragrant blooms and cone-like autumn fruits — which genus?
