Magnolia: Genus of angiosperms. Magnolia is a large genus of about 210 to 340 flowering plant species in the subfamily Magnolioideae of the family Magnoliaceae.
Formed when hydrogen atoms in ammonia are swapped out for carbon-based groups, which class of nitrogen-containing organic compounds includes aniline as its simplest aromatic member?
Amine: Chemical compounds and groups containing nitrogen with a lone pair (:N)
Made by chlorinating ordinary table sugar and roughly 600 times sweeter than it, what is this sugar substitute also known by the E number E955?
Also known as face blindness, this cognitive disorder leaves a person unable to recognize familiar faces — even their own — while other visual skills stay intact. What is it?
Prosopagnosia: Cognitive disorder of face perception. Prosopagnosia should not be confused with prosopometamorphopsia, a disorder characterized by altered perceptions of faces.
Nicknamed the 'brain-eating amoeba,' this free-living microorganism lurks in warm freshwater lakes, hot springs, and poorly chlorinated pools — what is it?
This paired female gonad releases egg cells and secretes hormones that regulate the menstrual cycle and fertility — which organ?
Ovary: Female reproductive organ that produces egg cells.
Known by the common name yarrow, this pungent, fernleaved plant in the daisy family is used in traditional medicine and as livestock feed — what is its scientific name?
Achillea millefolium: Species of plant. Achillea millefolium, commonly known as yarrow or common yarrow, is a flowering plant in the family Asteraceae.
Recognized as the world's longest ray-finned fish, this ribbon-shaped, silvery-blue deep-sea creature is often blamed for sea-serpent legends — which fish?
Giant oarfish: Species of oceanic ray-finned fish.

This semi-solid tissue inside the spongy portions of bones serves as the primary site of new blood cell production in birds and mammals, making up roughly 5% of an adult human's body mass — what tissue is it?
Bone marrow is a semi-solid tissue found within the spongy (also known as cancellous) portions of bones.
Named in 1880 from Greek words meaning 'bunch of grapes,' this genus of spherical, grape-clustered bacteria can grow with or without oxygen — which genus?
Lacking a tail due to a mutation in the TBXT gene, this superfamily of primates includes gibbons as the 'lesser' branch and humans among the 'great' branch — which animal group?
Ape: Superfamily of primates. The family Hylobatidae, the lesser apes, include four genera and a total of 20 species of gibbon, including the lar gibbon and the siamang, all native to Asia.
This practice of secure communication sits at the intersection of math, computer science, and electrical engineering, and underpins e-commerce and chip-based payment cards — what is it called?
Cryptography: Practice and study of secure communication techniques.
This umbrella term covers mental processes like perception, attention, memory, and reasoning that let us acquire and apply knowledge — what is it called?
Cognition: Mental process dealing with knowledge.
This Russian physiologist won the 1904 Nobel Prize for his work on digestion, but is far better remembered for training dogs to salivate at a signal — who was he?
Known as 'swede' in British English, this root vegetable is a hybrid of cabbage and turnip — what is it?
Rutabaga: Root vegetable in the Brassica family.
This carnivorous freshwater fish, found widely across cold waters worldwide, has a current all-tackle world record of 25 kg, caught in Germany in 1986 — what species is it?
Northern pike: Species of fish. The northern pike (Esox lucius), also known as jack, northern or simply pike, is a species of carnivorous fish of the genus Esox (pikes).
Native to the Americas, this plant genus in the nightshade family produces the fruits we call peppers, including sweet bell types and fiery chilies — what genus is it?
This branch of linguistics studies how speech sounds are articulated, transmitted as sound waves, and perceived, split into three sub-disciplines — what field is it?
Phonetics: Study of how humans produce and perceive sounds.
Also called the dorado or common dolphinfish, this surface-dwelling ray-finned fish is found around the Gulf of Mexico, Costa Rica, and Hawaii — what is it?
Mahi-mahi: Species of fish. It is also widely called dorado (not to be confused with Salminus brasiliensis, a freshwater fish) and dolphin (not to be confused with the aquatic mammal dolphin).
This scientific field studies the atmosphere and short-term weather phenomena, with applications spanning aviation, agriculture, and disaster management — what field is it?
Meteorology: Scientific study of the atmosphere focusing on weather forecasting.
Native to South America and first cultivated by the Guaraní people, the steeped leaves of this holly-genus plant produce a caffeinated beverage — what is it?
Yerba mate: South American holly plant. Yerba mate or yerba maté ( YUR-bə MAH-tay), Ilex paraguariensis, is a plant species of the holly genus native to South America.
Named from the Greek for 'red skin,' this bacterial infection produces a raised, sharply defined, bright-red rash typically on the face or legs — what's the condition?
Erysipelas: Human disease from a bacterial infection of the skin.

This small nocturnal marsupial has membranes stretching from its forelegs to hindlegs that let it soar between trees, and its scientific name translates to 'short-headed rope-dancer' — what animal is it?
Sugar glider: Species of Australian marsupial.
This first section of the small intestine, often the principal site of iron absorption, connects the stomach to the middle portion of the intestine — what is it?
Duodenum: First section of the small intestine. The duodenum is the first section of the small intestine in most vertebrates, including mammals, reptiles, and birds.
Also known as green gram, this legume is a staple ingredient across East, Southeast, and South Asian cuisine in both savory and sweet dishes — what is it?
Discovered in 1940 and making up as much as 40% of cannabis extract, this compound is an anticonvulsant used to treat two rare forms of childhood epilepsy — what is it?

Cannabidiol: Phytocannabinoid discovered in 1940. In the United States, the cannabidiol drug Epidiolex was approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2018, for the treatment of two seizure disorders.
This group of diseases occurs when misfolded proteins accumulate in body tissue, causing fatigue, swelling, and shortness of breath among roughly 36 distinct protein-driven types — what is it?
Amyloidosis: Metabolic disease involving abnormal deposited amyloid proteins.
Curving around the chest, these bones protect the lungs and heart and, in snakes, support and protect the whole body — what are they called?
Rib: Long bone in vertebrates that protects vital respiratory and cardiovascular organs.

Famous for oversized, colorful bills nearly useless for excavation, these Neotropical birds nest in hollows dug by other animals and share an ecological niche with Africa and Asia's hornbills — what are they?
Toucan: Family of birds. The family includes five genera and over 40 different species.
Sold under the brand name Celexa, this SSRI antidepressant treats major depressive disorder, OCD, panic disorder, and social anxiety — what is it?
Citalopram: SSRI antidepressant. Citalopram, sold under the brand name Celexa among others, is an antidepressant of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class.
The wild ancestor of the domestic pigeon, this pale grey bird has two black bars on each wing and gave rise to feral pigeons worldwide — what is it?
Rock dove: Ancestor of domestic pigeon. The domestic pigeon, often called "Columba livia domestica", which includes about 1,000 different breeds, is descended from this species.
Found on the forelimbs of most tetrapods, these prehensile, often opposable digits give primates like humans their dexterity for grasping and fine movement — what are they called?
Equal to exactly 1,000 kilograms — about 2,204.6 pounds — this unit of mass has an SI equivalent called the megagram. What is it called?

Tonne: Metric unit of mass equivalent to 1,000 kilograms or 1 megagram. It is also referred to as a metric ton in the United States to distinguish it from the non-metric units of the short ton and the long ton.
This fibromuscular tube carries food from throat to stomach using peristaltic contractions, and its name traces to Ancient Greek roots meaning roughly 'I carry what I ate.' What is it?
Esophagus: Vertebrate organ through which food passes to the stomach.
Grown in South Africa's Fynbos biome, this caffeine-free herbal infusion has an earthy flavor similar to yerba mate and carries protected designation of origin status in the EU. What is it?
Rooibos: Species of plant in the family Fabaceae.
Packed with chlorophyll, this plant-cell organelle captures sunlight, splits water to release oxygen, and feeds sugar-making in the Calvin cycle — what is it called?
Chloroplast: Plant organelle that conducts photosynthesis.
Marketed as Cymbalta, this serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor treats depression, anxiety, and fibromyalgia pain — what is it?
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
This Asian insect species, first found in Pennsylvania in 1998, cost Mid-Atlantic apple growers $37 million in a single year and now threatens hazelnut harvests worldwide — what is it?

Brown marmorated stink bug: Species of Pentatomid insect. The brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.
This American psychologist devised a pyramid-shaped theory of human needs culminating in self-actualization, and was later ranked the 10th most-cited psychologist of the 20th century — who is he?
Making up about 80 percent water and mostly colorless, this catch-all term covers everything inside a cell's outer membrane except its nucleus — what is it?
Cytoplasm: All of the contents of a cell including organelles but excluding the nucleus.
This secretive Soviet chief designer built the rocket that launched the first satellite, the first animal in orbit, and the first human into space — who was he?
This Pakistani-American billionaire owns an NFL franchise and a Premier League club, made his fortune supplying auto parts, and backs a wrestling promotion run by his son — who is he?
Shahid Khan: Pakistani and American businessman (born 1950)
Colorless and odorless, this radioactive noble gas with atomic number 86 is a decay product of radium and eventually settles into stable isotopes of lead?
Radon: Chemical element with atomic number 86 (Rn)
Typically occurring between ages 45 and 55, this natural decline in estrogen and progesterone permanently ends a woman's menstrual periods?
Menopause: Time when menstrual periods stop permanently.
Marketed as Imodium, this opioid-class medication treats diarrhea without crossing the blood-brain barrier at normal doses?
Loperamide: Medicine used to reduce diarrhea.
A young one of this fast-running lagomorph is called a leveret, and a group of them may be known as a 'husk' or a 'down'?
Hare: Genus of mammals in the family Leporidae.
Named from Latin words meaning 'around' and 'day,' this roughly 24-hour internal biological cycle appears independently across animals, plants, fungi, and cyanobacteria?
Circadian rhythm: Natural internal process that regulates the sleep-wake cycle.
Regarded as one of Formula One's greatest engineers, his car designs have won 14 Drivers' and 12 Constructors' Championships across three decades?
Adrian Newey: British engineer, aerodynamicist and motorsport executive (born 1958)
The only trijet ever produced by its manufacturer, this airliner entered service with Eastern Air Lines in 1964 powered by three rear-mounted turbofans?
After dropping out of Stuyvesant High School and serving in the Korean War, this economist went on to earn a PhD from Chicago and a National Humanities Medal in 2002?
This medical specialty uses manual and instrumental techniques to treat disease, reshape the body, or remove diseased tissue, performed by a lead practitioner and an assistant?
Surgery: Medical procedures that involve incisive or invasive instruments into body cavities.

Bred by Polynesians in the pre-Columbian era from two Pacific island species, this tropical flowering plant is the national flower of Malaysia and the unofficial national flower of Haiti — what is it?
Hibiscus × rosa-sinensis: Hybrid species of flowering plant. It is widely cultivated as an ornamental plant in the tropics and subtropics.
Closely related to salmon, these carnivorous freshwater fish spawn in shallow gravel beds of headwater creeks after migrating upstream — what are they called?
Trout: Freshwater fish from subfamily Salmoninae.
This corticosteroid treats conditions from rheumatoid arthritis to asthma but can cause bone loss and psychiatric side effects with long-term use — what is it called?
Prednisolone: Corticosteroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a vein, used topically as a skin cream, or as eye drops.
This small rodent, pointed-snouted with large rounded ears, has become the standard laboratory model organism after thriving alongside human settlements — what is it?
This principle describes how a changing magnetic field generates an electric current, underpinning the operation of transformers, generators, and motors — what is it called?
Faraday's law of induction: Basic law of electromagnetism.
This term describes the practice of exposing normally covered body parts to others in public or semi-public settings, whether in person or via a nude photo shared digitally — what is it?
Exhibitionism is the practice of exposing one's intimate parts - such as the breasts, genitals, or buttocks - in a public or semi-public environment.

This childhood illness of unknown cause mainly affects kids under five, causing a prolonged fever lasting more than five days that doesn't respond to typical fever-reducing medicine, plus inflamed blood vessels throughout the body — name the syndrome?
Kawasaki disease (also known as mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome) is a syndrome of unknown cause that results in a fever and mainly affects children under 5 years of age.
A pungent root vegetable in the same family as mustard, wasabi, and cabbage, this spice is likely native to Southeastern Europe and Western Asia — what is it?
Horseradish: Species of flowering plants in the cabbage family Brassicaceae.
Nicknamed for the stripes on its legs and body, this day-biting mosquito native to Southeast Asia spreads dengue, yellow fever, and Chikungunya — what is it called?
Aedes albopictus: Species of mosquito. The insect is called a tiger mosquito as it has stripes, as does a tiger.
This branch of biology and medicine studies the glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream, governing everything from growth to mood and metabolism — what is it called?
Endocrinology: Branch of medicine pertaining to the endocrine system.
Making its first flight in 2001 and entering Indian Air Force service in 2015, this delta-wing multirole fighter is the smallest and lightest supersonic jet of its generation — which aircraft?
HAL Tejas: Indian combat aircraft. The aircraft made its first flight in 2001 and entered into service with the IAF in 2015.
With six species native to Africa (and one also found in Arabia), these large Old World monkeys have dog-like muzzles and have existed for at least two million years — what are they called?
This highly soluble, hygroscopic crystalline salt is prized as a high-nitrogen fertilizer but is also the major ingredient in the industrial explosive ANFO — what is it?
Ammonium nitrate: Chemical compound with formula NH4NO3.
Nicknamed the blue dragon, this pelagic sea slug floats upside down using surface tension and a stomach gas bubble, and feeds on the Portuguese man o' war — what is it?
This rare genetic disorder linked to chromosome 15 leaves affected children constantly hungry, often leading to obesity, alongside a narrow forehead and small hands and feet — what is it?
Prader–Willi syndrome: Genetic disorder involving an imprinted genomic region.
Also called the lammergeier, this bird of prey is the only known vertebrate whose diet is 70 to 90 percent bone — which bird?
Bearded vulture: Species of bird. The bearded vulture (Gypaetus barbatus), also known as the lammergeier and ossifrage, is a very large bird of prey in the monotypic genus Gypaetus.
In 1990, this theoretical physicist became the first physicist ever awarded the Fields Medal, later becoming known as the practical founder of M-theory — who is he?
Edward Witten: American theoretical physicist. Witten is a researcher in string theory, quantum gravity, supersymmetric quantum field theories, and other areas of mathematical physics.
This scientific term covers walruses, sea lions, and true seals — fin-footed marine mammals whose closest living relatives are weasels and raccoons — what is the term?
Pinniped: Taxonomic group of semi-aquatic mammals.

Characterized by cycles of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors like self-induced vomiting, this eating disorder has an estimated genetic risk factor between 30 and 80 percent — what is it called?
Bulimia nervosa: Eating disorder. Bulimia is more common among those who have a close relative with the condition.
Covering patents, copyrights, trademarks, and trade secrets, this legal category of intangible creations first developed as a concept in 17th- and 18th-century England — what is it called?
Intellectual property: Ownership of creative expressions and processes.
Flying aboard Soyuz T-11 in April 1984 as part of the Soviet Interkosmos programme, who became the first citizen of his country to reach outer space?
Rakesh Sharma: First Indian to travel to space (born 1949)
Its species name honors Colchis, an ancient region on the Black Sea, and it's often released into the wild as a game bird — which Asian-native, ring-necked bird is this?
Common pheasant: Species of bird. The common pheasant (Phasianus colchicus), ring-necked pheasant, or blue-headed pheasant, is a bird in the pheasant family (Phasianidae).
Shaped roughly like a necktie and made up of the manubrium, body, and xiphoid process, which flat bone protects the heart and lungs at the front of the rib cage?
Sternum: Flat bone in the middle front part of the rib cage.
Also called a steer or bullock, and usually yoked in pairs, which castrated male bovine has long served as a draft animal for ploughing and hauling?
Ox: Common bovine draft and riding animal.
First selectively bred for color in imperial China over 1,000 years ago, which popular aquarium pet has become an invasive pest after being released into rivers in North America and Australia?
Goldfish: Freshwater fish common in aquariums.
Derived from a Greek word meaning 'that which is thought worthy,' which term denotes a statement accepted as true without proof, serving as a starting point for further reasoning?
Axiom: Statement that is taken to be true.
Combined with obstetrics as a joint medical specialty and touching on everything from family planning to pelvic reconstructive surgery, which field focuses on the female reproductive system?
Gynaecology: Medical area for women's reproductive health.
Homologous with the male foreskin and developing as part of the labia minora, which fold of skin surrounds and protects the tip of the clitoris?
Clitoral hood: Part of the vulva that covers and protects the glans of the clitoris.
Serving as chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria, which ancient Greek polymath was the first known person to calculate Earth's circumference?
Eratosthenes: Greek librarian, mathematician, geographer, and poet.
This unit of speed equals exactly one nautical mile per hour, roughly 1.15 mph, and is the standard measure used in maritime and aviation contexts — what is it called?
Knot (unit) is a unit of speed equal to one nautical mile per hour, exactly 1.852 km/h (approximately 1.151 mph or 0.514 m/s).
Most often triggered by a viral infection and capable of progressing to heart failure or cardiac arrest, which condition involves inflammation of the heart muscle itself?

Myocarditis: Inflammation of the heart muscle. Myocarditis can progress to inflammatory cardiomyopathy when there is associated ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction due to chronic inflammation.
Genetic in roughly 80% of cases, this long-term skin condition clogs hair follicles with dead skin and sebum, producing blackheads and pimples on the face, chest, and back — what is it?
Acne: Skin condition characterized by pimples.
Caused by about 40 types of fungus and often picked up in public showers or contact sports like wrestling, this infection produces a red, itchy, scaly circular rash — what is it?
Dermatophytosis: Fungus infection of the skin. Dermatophytosis, also known as tinea and ringworm, is a fungal infection of the skin (a dermatomycosis), that may affect skin, hair, and nails.

Named from Greek words meaning 'naked seed,' this group of woody plants — including conifers, cycads, and ginkgos — lacks the protective covering that encloses a flowering plant's seeds. What is it called?
Gymnosperm: Clade of non-flowering, naked-seeded vascular plants.
This spiny thistle species has distinctive red-to-purple flowers and shiny, pale green mottled leaves, and is a fairly typical member of the daisy family — what plant is it?
Silybum marianum is a species of thistle.
Belonging to the order Urodela and reaching their greatest diversity in the Appalachian Mountains, these tailed, lizard-shaped amphibians never have more than four front toes — what are they?
Salamander: Order of amphibians. All ten extant salamander families are grouped together under the order Urodela, the sole surviving order from the group Caudata.
Native to the Mediterranean and containing roughly 350 aromatic species, this herb genus lends its name to a common seasoning found in kitchens worldwide — which genus?
The son of a famous physicist and his first wife, this Swiss-American engineer taught hydraulic engineering at Berkeley and became renowned for research on sediment transport — who is he?

Hans Albert Einstein: Swiss-American engineer and educator. Hans Albert Einstein (May 14, 1904 – July 26, 1973) was a Swiss-American engineer, the second child and first son of physicists Albert Einstein and Mileva Marić.
The simplest alkene and the most-produced organic compound on Earth, this colorless gas is also a natural plant hormone used to ripen fruit — what is it?

In the Renaissance this field of study covered classical literature and language rather than religion or divinity, and today it groups subjects using critical and interpretive methods rather than empirical ones — what broad academic category is this?
Humanities: Academic disciplines that study society and culture.
This Austrian-German automotive engineer built the first gasoline-electric hybrid car and designed the Volkswagen Beetle, but also contributed tanks to Nazi Germany's war effort — who was he?
Ferdinand Porsche: Austrian-born German automotive engineer, inventor (1875–1951)
This French physicist shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with his wife, making them the first married couple to win a Nobel — who is he?
Pierre Curie: French physicist and chemist (1859–1906)
Also called German turnip despite not being related to true turnips, this stout cabbage cultivar can be eaten raw or cooked, stem and leaves alike — what vegetable?
Kohlrabi: Biennial cultivar of wild cabbage.
This colorless, highly flammable liquid with a sweet smell was once widely used as a general anesthetic before modern alternatives — what compound?
Also known as silver beet or perpetual spinach, this leafy green shares its species with beetroot — which vegetable?
Chard: Green leafy vegetable. Chard (Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris, Cicla Group and Flavescens Group) is a green leafy vegetable.
Unlike arteries, most of these thin-walled blood vessels carry deoxygenated blood back toward the heart — what are they?
Vein: Blood vessels that carry blood towards the heart.
A former director of Russia's FSB who later served as Security Council secretary, this close Putin ally played a key role in the decisions to annex Crimea and invade Ukraine — who is he?
Nikolai Patrushev: Russian politician and security officer (born 1951)
Credited as the 'father of toxicology,' this Swiss Renaissance physician and alchemist also wrote prophetic 'Prognostications' later studied by Rosicrucians — who is he?
Paracelsus: Swiss physician, philosopher, theologian, and alchemist (c. 1493 – 1541)
Sold under the veterinary brand name Rompun and often combined with ketamine for animal sedation, which structural analog of clonidine is this alpha2-adrenergic drug?
Xylazine: Veterinary anesthetic, sedative and analgesic.

Introduced in 2001 and originally developed under the name Tier II+, which remotely piloted, high-altitude surveillance aircraft supports the US Air Force with long-endurance radar and infrared sensors?
Northrop Grumman RQ-4 Global Hawk: Unmanned surveillance aircraft. It was initially designed by Ryan Aeronautical (now part of Northrop Grumman), and known as Tier II+ during development.
The tallest of the three camel species, standing up to 2.4 meters at the shoulder, which animal carries a single hump of fat on its back?
Known by the pseudonym 'Notch,' this Swedish programmer created the best-selling video game of all time and became a billionaire when Microsoft bought his studio for $2.5 billion in 2014 — who is he?
Markus Persson: Swedish video game programmer (born 1979)
Rich in vitamin C and polyphenols, this deciduous shrub's glossy dark berries are cooked into jams and syrups or fermented into cassis — what is it?
Blackcurrant: Species of flowering plant in the gooseberry family Grossulariaceae.
Home to jellyfish, corals, and sea anemones, this phylum of aquatic invertebrates is defined by specialized stinging cells used to capture prey — what is it?
Cnidaria: Aquatic animal phylum having cnidocytes.
Extremely cold-hardy and thriving in poor soil, this cereal grass is a staple grain behind Scandinavian crispbread and a certain whiskey style — what is it?
Rye: Species of grain. Rye (Secale cereale) is a grass grown extensively as a grain, a cover crop and a forage crop.
This lincosamide antibiotic treats infections from strep throat to acne, but raises the risk of a specific gut infection roughly fourfold — what is it?
Clindamycin: Antibiotic. It can also be used to treat acne, and some cases of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
This industry extracts everything from coal and gemstones to rock salt and gravel from the Earth, but is also linked to land degradation and habitat loss — what is it?
Mining: Extraction of valuable minerals or other geological materials from the Earth.

Combining textual criticism, literary criticism, history, and linguistics, this scholarly field traces its classical roots to the libraries of Pergamum and Alexandria in the 4th century BC — what is it?
Philology: Study of language in historical sources.

Native to the North Pacific coastline, this marine mammal is the heaviest member of the weasel family yet one of the smallest marine mammals, and one of few animals known to use rocks as tools to crack open shells — what is it?
Sea otter: Species of marine mammal. The sea otter (Enhydra lutris) is a marine mammal native to the coasts of the northern and eastern North Pacific Ocean.

After dropping out of Harvard to help build early versions of Windows at Microsoft, this developer co-founded a studio that made Half-Life and later launched a digital storefront called Steam — who is he?

Developed in Germany from the Old English Bulldog and the now-extinct Bullenbeisser, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog breed is known for its square muzzle, underbite, and powerful bite — name the breed?
Boxer (dog breed) is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.

A former Chicago options trader with finance degrees but no PhD, this entrepreneur co-founded a dot-com company whose peer-reviewed project evolved into the world's largest free encyclopedia — who is he?
Also called the broadbill, this large migratory predator sports a long, flat, pointed bill and can reach nearly 15 feet in length — what fish is it?
Swordfish: Fish which has a long, pointed bill. Swordfish are elongated, round-bodied, and lose all teeth and scales by adulthood.
The second-largest member of the deer family, this animal is also called "wapiti," a Shawnee and Cree word meaning "white rump" for the pale fur it flashes to signal alarm — what animal is it?
Elk: Species of deer. The word "elk" originally referred to the European variety of the moose, Alces alces, but was transferred to Cervus canadensis by North American colonists.
This genus of flowering plants, whose stinging hairs give it the common name 'stinging nettle,' takes its scientific name from the Latin word for 'sting' — what is it?
Urtica: Genus of flowering plants. Due to the stinging hairs, Urtica are rarely eaten by herbivores, but provide shelter for insects.
Nicknamed the 'palm thief,' this giant terrestrial arthropod can weigh over 9 pounds, making it the largest land-dwelling arthropod alive today — what is it?
Since the 1960s, growing movements have pushed governments to restrain activities that damage the natural world and its resources — what is this broad field of effort called?
Environmental protection: Practice of protecting the natural environment.
Nicknamed 'water warts,' this viral skin infection causes small pink bumps with a telltale dimple in the center and usually clears up on its own within a year — what is it?

Molluscum contagiosum: Viral infection of the skin. Molluscum contagiosum (MC), sometimes called water warts, is a viral infection of the skin that results in small raised pink lesions with a dimple in the center.
Usually caused by a virus but sometimes by strep bacteria, this inflammation of the back of the throat brings on a sore throat, fever, and sometimes a hoarse voice — what is it called?
Pharyngitis: Inflammation of the back of the throat. Pharyngitis is a type of upper respiratory tract infection.
Making up 2 to 8 percent of milk by mass, this disaccharide combines galactose and glucose and takes its name from the Latin word for milk — what is it?
Lactose: Carbohydrate. Lactose is a disaccharide composed of galactose and glucose and has the molecular formula C12H22O11.
First prescribed in 1934, this steroid sex hormone plays a key role in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryonic development — what is it?
Progesterone: Sex hormone. Progesterone (P4) is an endogenous steroid and progestogen sex hormone involved in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryogenesis of humans and other species.
Originally defined as the heat needed to raise one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius, this unit of energy in nutrition actually refers to a kilocalorie — what is it?

Calorie: Unit of energy used in nutrition. The small calorie or gram calorie is defined as the amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius (or one kelvin).
Discovered in 1778 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele and boasting the sixth-highest melting point of any element, this metal is mostly used in steel alloys — what is it?
Molybdenum: Chemical element with atomic number 42 (Mo)
First confirmedly detected in 1992 orbiting a pulsar, this term describes any planet found outside our solar system — what is it?
Exoplanet: Planet outside of the Solar System. The first confirmed detection of an exoplanet was in 1992 around a pulsar, and the first detection around a main-sequence star was in 1995.
Co-founder and former CEO of a ride-hailing giant, this businessman resigned in 2017 amid allegations he ignored harassment reports, later selling most of his shares for $2.5 billion — who is he?
Travis Kalanick: American entrepreneur and former CEO of Uber.
In this prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, a person cannot be awakened, shows no normal sleep-wake cycle, and may even be induced deliberately during general anesthesia — what is it?
Coma: State of unconsciousness. The person may experience respiratory and circulatory problems due to the body's inability to maintain normal bodily functions.
Standing up to a meter tall with a white head marked by a black stripe to its crest, this wading bird of Europe, Asia, and Africa hunts motionless beside water — what is it?
Grey heron: Long-legged predatory wading bird.
Broken down from creatine phosphate in muscle metabolism, this compound is released into the blood at a rate tied to a person's muscle mass — what is it?
Creatinine: Breakdown product of creatine phosphate.
Despite helping develop the Soviet Union's thermonuclear weapons, this physicist won the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize for his human-rights activism and was later persecuted as a dissident — who was he?
Andrei Sakharov: Soviet nuclear physicist and human rights activist (1921–1989)
Formed by stripping three protons from phosphoric acid, this triply-charged ion carries the formula PO4³⁻ and lends its name to esters like trimethyl ester in organic chemistry — what anion is it?
Phosphate: Anion, salt, functional group or ester derived from a phosphoric acid.
Best known in its heptahydrate form as Epsom salt, this white crystalline compound (MgSO4) is also used in agriculture to fix soils deficient in an essential plant nutrient — what compound is it?
Magnesium sulfate: Chemical compound with formula MgSO4.
Named after the Greek word for tumor, first used this way by the physician Galen nearly two millennia ago, this medical field focuses on diagnosing and treating cancer — what is it called?
Oncology: Branch of medicine dealing with, or specializing in, cancer.
This cream-skinned root vegetable, a cousin of the carrot and parsley, actually grows sweeter in flavor after a winter frost — what is it?
Parsnip: Root vegetable in the flowering plant family Apiaceae.

Recognized by their pod-like fruit and compound leaves, this plant family — the third-largest among flowering plants — includes beans, peas, and lentils along with genera like Acacia and Mimosa. What family is it?
Fabaceae: Family of legume flowering plants. Fabaceae or Leguminosae, commonly known as the legume, pea, or bean family, is a large and agriculturally important family of flowering plants.
Known as mugwort or wormwood, this daisy-family plant has long been used for both medicinal and culinary purposes — what species is it?

Artemisia vulgaris: Medicinal plant known as common mugwort. It is one of several species in the genus Artemisia commonly known as mugwort, although Artemisia vulgaris is the species most often called mugwort.
Named for barbels that resemble a cat's whiskers, these scaleless, ray-finned fish include giants like the Mekong species and go by nicknames such as 'mud cat' in the Southern US — what are they?
Catfish: Order of fish. Catfish are a diverse group of ray-finned fish of the order Siluriformes (historically Nematognathi).

Symbolized by the Greek letter omega, this SI unit of electrical resistance was named after a 19th-century German physicist and, since 2019, is defined as an exact value based on fundamental constants — what unit is it?
Ohm: SI derived unit of electrical resistance. The ohm (symbol: Ω, the uppercase Greek letter omega) is the unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units (SI).
Developed as a 14-bed sleeper upgrade of an earlier airliner, which low-wing propeller monoplane cruised at 207 mph and reshaped air travel from the 1930s through World War II?
Douglas DC-3: Airliner and military transport aircraft family.
Known as holy basil and sacred within the Vaishnava tradition of Hinduism, which aromatic herb is widely used in Ayurvedic tea?
Ocimum tenuiflorum: Species of flowering plant.
Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, which benign condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men?
Gynecomastia: Enlargement of the human male breast.
Marked in its severe stage by hallucinations and paradoxical undressing, which condition is defined as a body core temperature below 35 degrees Celsius?
Hypothermia: Human body core temperature below 35 °C (95 °F)
Which medical specialty focuses on diagnosing, treating, and preventing conditions related to cognition, mood, emotion, and behavior, using tools like the DSM-5?
Psychiatry: Branch of medicine devoted to mental disorders.

Affecting about 1 in 15,000 people, this rare genetic disorder causes severe intellectual disability, little to no speech, and balance problems — yet those affected are often noted for a notably happy personality. Which condition is it?
Angelman syndrome: Genetic disorder caused by a mutation of chromosome 15.

Closely related to the beech-oak family and including species widespread across the Northern Hemisphere's temperate and boreal zones, which thin-leaved deciduous hardwood genus is prized for its versatile wood?
Birch: Genus of flowering plants in the family Betulaceae.
Normally solitary and harmless, these short-horned grasshoppers can undergo a serotonin-triggered shift into gregarious swarming behavior under drought-then-growth conditions — what are they called?
Locust: Grasshopper that has a swarming phase.
Caused by prolonged exposure to excess cortisol, this condition produces abdominal weight gain with thin limbs, a rounded red face, and reddish stretch marks — which condition is it?
Cushing's syndrome: Symptoms from excessive exposure to glucocorticoids such as cortisol.

Named from an Ancient Greek word for 'soap,' this cheesy secretion of shed skin cells, oils, and moisture collects under the foreskin in males and around the folds of female genitalia — what is it called?
Smegma (from Ancient Greek, smgma, 'soap') is a cheesy substance composed of shed skin cells, skin oils, and moisture that occurs in male and female mammalian genitalia.
Commonly called the voice box, which organ in the upper neck houses the vocal cords and protects the windpipe from food entering it?
Larynx: Voice box, an organ in the neck of amphibians, reptiles, and mammals.
This genus of bacteria mainly infects amoebae but can cause a pneumonia-like illness in humans when it spreads via poorly maintained cooling towers — what genus is it?
Legionella: Pathogenic genus of Gram-negative bacteria.
A healthy kidney contains up to 1.5 million of these microscopic filtering units, each pairing a capillary tuft with a cup-shaped capsule — what is it called?
Nephron: Microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney.
Known to NATO as 'Halo,' this Soviet-designed aircraft holds the record as the largest helicopter ever built in serial production — which one?
Mil Mi-26: Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter.
Lacking any nervous, digestive, or circulatory system, these ancient sea-bound filter feeders pump water through pore-riddled bodies using flagella to survive — what are they?
Sponge: Animals of the phylum Porifera.

Manufactured under license by both Goodyear and Brewster during World War II, this American carrier-based fighter aircraft became one of the most capable fighter-bombers of the war and later saw service in Korea — which aircraft?
Vought F4U Corsair is an American fighter aircraft that saw service primarily in World War II and the Korean War.
This plant genus — whose members go by names like poplar, aspen, and cottonwood — includes the first tree species ever to have its complete genome sequenced, in 2006 — what genus is it?
Populus: Genus of plants. Populus is a genus of 25–30 species of deciduous flowering plants in the family Salicaceae, native to most of the Northern Hemisphere.
Striking 48 to 72 hours after a heavy drinker's last drink, this potentially fatal condition brings hallucinations, seizures nicknamed 'rum fits,' and dangerously high body temperature — what is it?
Delirium tremens: Rapid onset of confusion caused by alcohol withdrawal.
This Swedish tech entrepreneur founded and chairs a streaming giant, with a net worth estimated at $8.7 billion in December 2025 — who is he?
Thought extinct since the age of dinosaurs 66 million years ago, this lobe-finned fish was found alive off the west Indian Ocean, more closely related to lungfish than typical fish — what is it?
This mucolytic drug is the go-to antidote for acetaminophen overdose, working by boosting glutathione to neutralize the drug's toxic byproducts — what is it?
Acetylcysteine: Medication used to treat overdose of paracetamol.
With almost 500 species in the daisy family, this large plant genus includes mugwort, wormwood, and sagebrush, and is sometimes confused with a related genus of sages — which genus?
Artemisia (plant) (art--) is a large, diverse genus of plants belonging to the daisy family, Asteraceae, with almost 500 species.
This flowering legume genus boasts over 199 species and has become such a successful invasive spreader in Iceland that it's now considered an ecological problem — which genus?
This genus of demersal fish, named by Linnaeus in 1758, includes an Atlantic and a Pacific species prized for their mild flavor and flaky white flesh — what fish is it?
Cod: Common name for several fish, but mainly the demersal genus Gadus.
Comprising around 90 species split between river martins and all other members, this family of aerial-feeding songbirds is thought to have evolved as hole-nesters in Africa — what are they called?
Swallow: Family of songbirds. The term "swallow" is used as the common name for Hirundo rustica in the United Kingdom and Ireland.
Named for its four heads, this large muscle group covers the front of the thigh and is the sole muscle that extends the knee — what is it?
Quadriceps: Group of human leg muscle.
This unit of energy equals the kinetic energy a single electron gains while crossing an electric potential difference of one volt — what is it called?
Recognizable by its bold red-and-black pattern, this true bug is often confused with the unrelated cinnamon bug and forms large aggregations across Europe and Asia — which species is it?
Pyrrhocoris apterus: Species of true bug. The firebug, Pyrrhocoris apterus, is a common insect of the family Pyrrhocoridae.
This shelled reptile retracts its head and neck straight back into its shell for protection, with the largest species growing over a metre long and weighing more than 100 kilograms — what is it?
A famous singer known for her CCTV New Year's Gala appearances, she has served as China's First Lady since 2012 as the wife of its paramount leader — who is she?
Peng Liyuan: First Lady of China since 2012. Peng also sang the theme songs of several popular TV series, such as The Water Margin (1998).

Triggered by certain serotonergic medications, this group of symptoms can range from mild high blood pressure to severe, potentially fatal spikes in body temperature and dangerous muscle breakdown — what's it called?
Serotonin syndrome (SS) consists of a group of symptoms that may occur with the use of certain serotonergic medications or drugs.
This long-term skin condition causes flaky, greasy patches on the scalp, face, and chest, and is called cradle cap when it appears on a baby's scalp — what is it?
Seborrhoeic dermatitis: Skin disease. Seborrhoeic dermatitis (also spelled seborrheic dermatitis in American English) is a long-term skin disorder.
Native to Mexico and Central America, this tuberous flowering plant blooms in nearly every hue except blue, and its tubers store energy as inulin rather than starch — what is it?
Dahlia: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae.

Discovered in January 2005 by a Palomar Observatory team and named after a Greco-Roman goddess of strife, this trans-Neptunian object is the most massive known dwarf planet in the solar system — which one?
Eris (dwarf planet) (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
Sold under the brand name Lamictal, this medication treats epilepsy and helps stabilize mood in bipolar disorder — what is it?

Lamotrigine: Anticonvulsant medication. Lamotrigine ( luh-MOH-trih-jeen), sold under the brand name Lamictal among others, is a medication used to treat epilepsy and stabilize mood in bipolar disorder.
One of the original citrus fruits, this large fragrant relative of the lemon has a thick, coarse rind and is a genetic ancestor of most modern citrus hybrids — what is it?
Native to the Iberian Peninsula and introduced to hundreds of locations worldwide, this grassland herbivore digs extensive burrow networks called warrens — what is it?

Named after a French mathematician but reportedly learned from his Swiss tutor, this calculus theorem evaluates tricky limits by taking derivatives of the numerator and denominator — what is it called?
L'Hôpital's rule (loh-pee-TAHL) is a mathematical theorem used for evaluating the limit of a quotient of two functions, each of which tends to zero or infinity, by taking each function's derivative.

This German chemist won a Nobel Prize for inventing a process that synthesizes ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen gas — a breakthrough that today supports nearly half the world's food production. Who is he?
Also nicknamed the prairie wolf, this adaptable North American canine fills a similar ecological niche to Eurasia's golden jackal and was first spotted in Panama in 2013 — what is it?
Coyote: Species of canine native to North America.

This crystalline mineral form of frozen water occurs naturally on Earth, other planets, and even in Oort cloud objects, and has at least nineteen known phases depending on temperature and pressure — what is it?
Ice: Frozen water; the solid state of water.
This surgical medical subspecialty treats the ear, nose, and throat — organs connected via the Eustachian tube — earning its specialists the nickname 'ENT surgeons.' What field is it?
Otorhinolaryngology: Medical specialty of the head and neck.
Developed for chemical warfare after research into pesticide toxicity, this oily amber liquid is lethal in just tens of milligrams and is more potent than sarin — what is this compound?
VX (nerve agent): VX is an extremely toxic synthetic chemical compound in the organophosphorus class, specifically, a thiophosphonate.
With atomic number 76 and symbol Os, this bluish-white transition metal has the highest density of any stable element and was once prized for fountain-pen nib tips — what is it?
Osmium: Chemical element with atomic number 76 (Os). Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.

Nicknamed wolfsbane, monkshood, and devil's helmet, this highly toxic genus of over 250 mountain-dwelling flowering plants thrives in moist, well-draining soils across the Northern Hemisphere — what is it?
Aconitum: Genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae.
This portmanteau of 'binary digit' is the most basic unit of information in computing, representing one of two possible states like 0 or 1 — eight of them make up a byte. What is it?
Bit: Unit of information. The bit represents a logical state with one of two possible values.
Excess fluid pooling in the lungs' air sacs impairs oxygen exchange and can be triggered by either heart failure or a range of unrelated causes — what condition is this?
Pulmonary edema: Fluid accumulation in the tissue and air spaces of the lungs.
Native to Europe and southwestern Asia, this herbaceous perennial is the type species that lends its name to an entire genus of flowering plants — what is it?
Valerian (herb): Species of flowering plant. Valerian (Valeriana officinalis) is an herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Caprifoliaceae, native to Europe and southwestern Asia.

With a wingspan reaching 188 centimeters and distinctive ear tufts atop mottled blackish-and-tawny plumage, this raptor is one of the largest of its nocturnal kind, ranging widely across Europe and Asia — what bird is it?
Eurasian eagle-owl: Species of owl. The Eurasian eagle-owl (Bubo bubo) is a species of eagle-owl, a type of bird that resides much over Eurasia.

Famous for the giant throat pouch beneath its long beak, this large water bird's eight living species range from the tropics to temperate zones, with some even flying inland to Australia's Red Centre after heavy rains — what bird is this?
Pelican: Genus of large water birds with a throat pouch.

This medium-sized bird of prey ranges across Europe into northwestern China, hunting rodents like voles from a perch, with northern populations migrating as far as South Africa for winter — what bird is this?
Common buzzard: Species of bird of prey. It is a member of the genus Buteo in the family Accipitridae.
Located at either side of the back of your throat, these paired lymphoid organs form part of a defensive ring guarding the entrance to your digestive and respiratory tracts — what are they?

Tonsil: Lymphoid organs in the mouth and throat. The palatine tonsils and the adenoid tonsil are organs consisting of lymphoepithelial tissue located near the oropharynx and nasopharynx (parts of the throat).
This American WWII twin-engine, twin-boom fighter carried its pilot alone in a central nacelle and served as fighter-bomber, night fighter, and long-range escort — which aircraft was it?
Lockheed P-38 Lightning: American twin-engined fighter of WWII. The Lockheed P-38 Lightning is an American single-seat, twin-engined fighter aircraft that was used during World War II.

This tropical tree's moderately ripe flesh, once cooked, is said to taste like a fresh-baked loaf with a potato-like flavor, and 18th-century navigators carried it in seedless form to the Caribbean — what is it?
Breadfruit: Edible fruit-bearing tree in family. Moraceae.
Founder of the world's largest electronics contract manufacturer, this Taiwanese billionaire said the sea goddess Mazu came to him in a dream urging a 2019 run for president — who is he?
Terry Gou: Founder and former Chief Executive Officer of Foxconn.
Named by naturalist Constantine Rafinesque in 1815, this predatory saltwater fish prowls near coral reefs and is a favorite target of sport anglers worldwide — what is it?

Marked by heartburn, regurgitation, and even dental corrosion from stomach acid creeping back up the digestive tract, this chronic condition can, if untreated, lead to esophageal stricture or Barrett's esophagus — what is it?
Gastroesophageal reflux disease: Flow of stomach contents into the esophagus.

This organic functional group, structured R−CH=O and alternatively called a formyl group when isolated from its side chain, appears throughout biologically and technologically important chemicals — what is it?
Aldehyde: Organic compound containing the functional group R–CH=O.
Squat-bodied and built for digging, this group includes the European, ferret, honey, and American species despite not truly sharing one family tree — what are they?
This herpesvirus genus's human species can cause mononucleosis in adults but birth defects affecting the eyes, ears, liver, and spleen when passed to a fetus — which virus?
Cytomegalovirus: Genus of viruses. The 11 species in this genus include Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV, HHV-5), which is the species that infects humans.
Found in every ocean but never in fresh water, most of these bivalves can swim in rapid bursts across the seafloor rather than staying put — which shellfish?
Scallop: Family of shellfish, many edible.
Containing the potent compound salvinorin A, this plant used by Mazatec shamans for spiritual healing sparked a US media panic around 2007 after being shared in online videos — which plant?
Salvia divinorum: Species of plant. The leaves contain the potent compound salvinorin A and can induce a dissociative state and hallucinations.
The most widely distributed member of its subfamily, this semiaquatic, fish-eating mustelid ranges across Europe, much of Asia, and North Africa's Maghreb — which animal?
Both heads of this upper-arm muscle originate on the scapula and let you flex your elbow while turning your palm upward — what muscle is it?

Biceps: Muscle on the front of the upper arm. While the long head of the biceps crosses both the shoulder and elbow joints, its main function is at the elbow where it flexes and supinates the forearm.
Named after the Greek word for rainbow because its compounds show so many colors, this brittle silvery-white metal is the second-densest element found in nature — what is it?
Iridium: Chemical element with atomic number 77 (Ir)
These feather-gilled freshwater crustaceans share their taxonomic order with lobsters and turn up in everything from brooks to rice paddies — what are they?
Crayfish: Freshwater crustaceans. Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.
Nicknamed the 'upside-down tree' for its unusual silhouette, this genus of long-lived African and Malagasy giants was named after a French naturalist — what genus is it?
Adansonia: Genus of trees known as baobab.
One of the six Celtic nations, this peninsula in northwest France was known as Armorica under Roman rule before becoming an independent kingdom and later a duchy. What region is it?
Hydra (genus) is a genus of small freshwater hydrozoans in the phylum Cnidaria.
This silvery-gold alkali metal has a melting point just above room temperature, making it one of only five elemental metals that go liquid in warm conditions — what is it?
Caesium: Chemical element with atomic number 55 (Cs)
With a half-life of just 138 days, this rare radioactive element occurs only in trace amounts within uranium ore and is chemically similar to selenium — what is it?
Polonium: Chemical element with atomic number 84 (Po)
Brought to market by Monsanto in 1974 under the brand name Roundup, this herbicide works by blocking a key enzyme that plants need to grow — what is it?
Glyphosate: Systemic herbicide and crop desiccant.
About 60 to 70 percent as sweet as table sugar yet virtually calorie-free, this sugar alcohol is fermented from corn and was commercially pioneered by Japanese companies in the 1990s — what is it?
Erythritol: Sugar alcohol that is used as a sweetener.
Ranging from a racing tachycardia to a sluggish bradycardia, this catch-all term covers any heartbeat that strays from normal sinus rhythm — what is it called?
Arrhythmia: Group of medical conditions characterized by irregular heartbeat.
Patented in 1980 and marketed as Claritin, this second-generation antihistamine treats hay fever and hives but can still cause sleepiness and dry mouth — what is it?
Loratadine: Antihistamine medication. Loratadine, sold under the brand name Claritin among others, is a medication used to treat allergies.
Beloved in gardens for gobbling up pests, this spiny mammal native to Iberia and Scandinavia was introduced to New Zealand in the late 1800s but is now Red Listed in Britain — what is it?
European hedgehog: Species of small spiny mammal.
Belonging to a bird family that's the only survivor of its order, this wading bird comes in four American species plus two more across Africa and Eurasia — what is it?
Flamingo: Family of birds. There are four flamingo species distributed throughout the Americas (including the Caribbean), and two species native to Afro-Eurasia.
This species includes honeydew, cantaloupe, and Casaba varieties, and traveled along ancient caravan routes long before its exact origin in the Levant or Egypt was ever confirmed — what fruit is it?
Cucumis melo: Species of plant. Cucumis melo, also known as melon or true melon, is a species of Cucumis that has been developed into many cultivated varieties.
Nicknamed 'Viper Zero' and built with a 60/40 Japan-US manufacturing split, this fighter derived from the F-16 was the first combat aircraft to carry an AESA radar — what jet is it?
Mitsubishi F-2: Japanese supersonic jet fighter.
Defined by a carbon-oxygen double bond flanked by two carbon groups, this class of organic compound includes acetone and gives some sugars and steroids like testosterone their structure — what is it?
Ketone: Organic compounds of the form >C=O.
Named by Linnaeus in 1753 but called cempōhualxōchitl by the Nahua long before, this genus of Mexican-native flowers is commonly known as marigolds — what's the genus?
Caused by white blood cells migrating into and damaging vessel walls, this group of disorders inflames both arteries and veins, and sometimes even the lymphatic vessels — what condition is it?
Vasculitis: Medical disorders that destroy blood vessels by inflammation.
Known on the street as a date-rape drug but used medically to treat narcolepsy and cataplexy, this natural neurotransmitter is also a precursor to GABA in the brain — what compound is it?

Γ-Hydroxybutyric acid: Chemical compound. γ-Hydroxybutyric acid, also known as gamma-hydroxybutyric acid, GHB, or 4-hydroxybutanoic acid, is a naturally occurring neurotransmitter and a depressant drug.
A group of these black birds is famously called a 'murder,' and their larger cousins are known as ravens — what bird is this?
Crow: Index of animals with the same common name.
This pigmented ring of skin around the nipple contains sebaceous glands as well as the openings of the milk ducts — what's it called?
Areola: Pigmented area on the breast around the nipple.
This small European finch's male sports a blue-grey cap and rust-red underparts, while both sexes flash white wing bars — what species is it?
Eurasian chaffinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian chaffinch, common chaffinch, or simply the chaffinch (Fringilla coelebs) is a common and widespread small passerine bird – in the finch family.
This tangy reddish spice, made from a shrub in the cashew family, is a staple of Arab cuisine and holds symbolic significance on the Haft-sin table at Persian New Year — what is it?
Sumac: Related species of plants in the family Anacardiaceae.
This waterfowl family member is smaller than a swan but larger than a duck; its young are called goslings, and a flock on the ground is known as a gaggle — what bird is it?
Goose: Common name for a group of waterfowl.

Boldly patterned in black and yellow to warn predators of its toxicity, this European amphibian can live for more than 50 years and is now vulnerable due to an introduced fungal disease — what species is it?
Fire salamander: Species of amphibian. The fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) is a common species of salamander found in Europe.
Born Leonardo Bonacci in Pisa, this medieval Italian mathematician's 1202 book 'Liber Abaci' introduced Europe to Indo-Arabic numerals and a famous number sequence bearing his nickname — who is he?
Named from the Latin word for 'sparrow,' this bird order — making up over half of all species — is defined by perching feet with three toes forward and one back. What's it called?
Passerine: Perching birds of the order Passeriformes.
Some called egrets and others bitterns, these 75 species of long-legged, long-beaked wading birds make up the family Ardeidae — what are they?
Heron: Family of birds. The OED also observes that shiterow or shederow are terms used for herons, and also applied as derogatory terms meaning a thin, weakly person.
This Danish midfielder won three Eredivisie titles at Ajax before being twice named his London club's Player of the Year during a six-year spell there. Who is he?
Priapism is a condition in which a penis remains erect for hours in the absence of stimulation or after stimulation has ended.

While working as an instrument maker at the University of Glasgow, this Scottish engineer's separate-condenser design transformed Newcomen's steam engine into the machine that powered the Industrial Revolution — who was he?
James Watt: Scottish inventor, engineer and chemist (1736–1819)
Named for the Aztec god of fire and lightning, this ancient Mexican dog breed comes in hairless and fully-coated varieties within the same litter — which breed?
Xoloitzcuintle: Hairless dog breed from Mexico.
Encompassing everything from the electrical telegraph to modern radio, this field is defined as the transmission of information over distance using electrical or electronic means — what field is it?
Telecommunications: Transmission of information electromagnetically. The physical limitations of metallic media prompted the development of optical fibre.
Prized by fur trappers for its yellowish-to-dark-brown coat, this bushy-tailed, weasel-like mammal is adapted to life in the taiga's coniferous forests — what is it?

Marketed under a well-known brand name, this typical antipsychotic treats everything from schizophrenia to Tourette tics, but carries risks of tardive dyskinesia and dangerous QT-interval prolongation — what drug is it?
Haloperidol: Typical antipsychotic medication. Haloperidol, sold under the brand name Haldol among others, is a typical antipsychotic medication.

Distinguished by its wide, square-lipped mouth built for grazing, this is the largest and most social species in its family; its northern subspecies lost its last known male, Sudan, in 2018 — which animal?
White rhinoceros: Species of large land mammal.

Ranked alongside Aristotle and Frege among history's most significant logicians, this thinker proved his completeness theorem in his 1929 Vienna dissertation before publishing his famous incompleteness theorems two years later — who is he?
Kurt Gödel: Mathematical logician and philosopher.
Also known as estragon, this perennial herb in the daisy family comes in a French variety prized for cooking and a milder Russian variety — which herb?
Tarragon: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family Asteraceae.
Native to China, Japan, Korea and Nepal and blooming in late summer after heavy rainfall, this plant's alternate names include the hurricane lily and the corpse flower — what is it?
Lycoris radiata: Species of plant. It is originally from China, Japan, Korea and Nepal and spread from there to the United States and elsewhere.
Belonging to the suborder Vermilingua and closely related to sloths, these mammals include giant, silky, and tamandua species that feed almost exclusively on ants and termites — what are they called?
Anteater: Mammals known for eating ants and termites.
This biological process is the fusion of two gametes to create a zygote, distinct from earlier steps like insemination or pollination that merely bring the gametes together — what is it called?
Fertilisation: Union of opposite-sex gametes in sexual reproduction to form a zygote.

As the United States' first swept-wing fighter jet, this Korean War-era aircraft dueled Soviet MiG-15s in some of history's earliest jet-to-jet battles — which plane, produced in more than 7,800 units?
North American F-86 Sabre: Family of US fighter aircraft.

Composed of repeating siloxane units with a backbone of oxygen and silicon rather than carbon, this synthetic material fills sealants, cookware, and medical devices, and is often confused with the chip-making element it's named after — what is it?
Sold under the brand name Aldactone, this diuretic medication treats heart failure and acne, and is also used to block testosterone's effects during feminizing hormone therapy — what is it?
Nicknamed 'Vigorous Dragon' and known to NATO as the Firebird, this Chinese delta-wing, canard-design fighter jet has been exported to Pakistan's air force — which aircraft, capable of Mach 1.8?
Chengdu J-10: Chinese multi-role fighter aircraft family.

Positioned behind the mouth and nasal cavity, this throat structure channels food toward the esophagus and air toward the larynx, with a flap of cartilage guarding against the two crossing paths — what is it?
Pharynx: Part of the throat that is behind the mouth and nasal cavity.
Also called the belly button, this flat or hollowed spot on the abdomen marks where the umbilical cord once attached — what is it?
Navel: Scarred area on the abdomen after detachment of the umbilical cord.
Roughly 12 centimeters long in adults, this final section of the large intestine temporarily stores waste before it passes into the anal canal — what is it?
Rectum: Final portion of the large intestine. The rectum (pl.: rectums or recta) is the final straight portion of the large intestine in humans and some other mammals, and the gut in others.
Sold under the brand name Paxil, this SSRI antidepressant treats conditions from panic disorder to PTSD, and is also prescribed for premature ejaculation and menopausal hot flashes — what is it?
Paroxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It has also been used in the treatment of premature ejaculation, and hot flashes due to menopause.
Named after the Latin word for a small shovel, this flat triangular bone connects the upper arm bone to the collarbone and forms the back of the shoulder girdle — what is it?
Scapula: Bone that connects the humerus and clavicle.

This rare chromosomal condition gives affected females four copies of a single chromosome instead of the usual two, and is linked to distinctive facial features and skeletal quirks like incurved pinky fingers — what is it called?
Tetrasomy X: Chromosomal disorder with 4 X chromosomes.
This genus of muroid rodents gives its scientific name to the common rat, though not every animal called a rat actually belongs to it — which genus?
This Austrian striker had a brief, injury-hit loan spell at Inter Milan before becoming a regular at Werder Bremen and later playing for a Serbian club. Who is he?
Pan (genus) consists of two extant species: the bonobo and the chimpanzee.
Also called caustic potash and written KOH, this dangerously corrosive white solid is a prototypical strong base and the key precursor to most liquid and soft soaps — which compound?
Potassium hydroxide: Inorganic compound (KOH). It has many industrial and niche applications, most of which utilize its caustic nature and its reactivity toward acids.
Native to Africa, India, the Middle East and Central Asia, these fleet-footed members of the family Bovidae aren't actually one single evolutionary group — what are they?
Sporting a dark facial mask and famous for a seriously foul-smelling territorial secretion, this stocky mustelid ranges across the continent and Morocco's Rif mountains — which species is it?
Designed in the late 1950s as a six-engine, delta-winged prototype bomber capable of Mach 3+ at 70,000 feet, this aircraft was meant to outrun any interceptor of its era — which plane?
North American XB-70 Valkyrie: Prototype supersonic strategic bomber.
In this concept, a random variable's average uncertainty is measured by how much data is needed, on average, to describe which outcome occurred. What is this quantity called?

Entropy (information theory): Average uncertainty in variable's states. The choice of base for 
 
 
 
 log
 
 
 {\displaystyle \log }, the logarithm, varies for different applications.
This common bowel condition produces hard, infrequent stools and can lead to hemorrhoids or fecal impaction, with hypothyroidism and diabetes among its underlying causes. What is it?
Constipation: Infrequent or difficult bowel movements.

Best known for his role as Ben Hunter in a soapy prime-time revenge drama, this American actor also starred as Will Davis on The CW's 'Privileged' and Kyle Parks on Lifetime's 'The Client List.' Who is he?

Marketed under the brand name Captagon, this amphetamine-theophylline combination drug became Syria's largest export under the Assad regime, with tablet stockpiles seized when anti-government forces took Damascus in December 2024. What drug is this?
Fenethylline: Codrug of amphetamine and theophylline. Fenethylline (BAN, USAN) or fenetylline (INN) is a codrug of amphetamine and theophylline and so a mutual prodrug of both.

Commonly known as mad cow disease, this fatal neurodegenerative illness in cattle is caused by a misfolded prion and can spread to humans as a variant of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. What is this cattle disease called?
Bovine spongiform encephalopathy: Fatal neurodegenerative disease of cattle. The United Kingdom was afflicted with an outbreak of BSE and vCJD in the 1980s and 1990s.

Codenamed 'Havoc' by NATO, this Soviet tandem-seat attack helicopter carries a single gun in an under-nose barbette and, unlike its predecessor, has no secondary troop-transport role. What aircraft is this?
Mil Mi-28: Russian attack helicopter. The Mil Mi-28 (NATO reporting name "Havoc") is a Soviet heavy-weight, all-weather, day-night, tandem-seat anti-armour military attack helicopter.

This exaggerated immune response occurs when the body mistakes a harmless substance for a threat, triggering histamine release from mast cells and conditions like hay fever or anaphylaxis. What is this reaction called?
Allergy: Immune system response to a substance that most people tolerate well.
Originally a dry-season staple for ǃKung hunter-gatherers, this tropical vine in the Cucurbitaceae family produces an intensely bitter edible fruit widely used across Asian cuisine — what is it?
Momordica charantia: Species of plant in the gourd family.
Marked by itchy 1-2mm blisters on the palms and soles that clear in three to four weeks but often return, this form of dermatitis has no known cause — what is it?
Dyshidrosis: Inflammatory disease of the skin in humans.
First described in 1740 under the name Compositae, this enormous flowering-plant family includes daisies, asters and sunflowers — what is it?
Asteraceae: Large family of flowering plants.
This medical specialty trains physicians for four years after medical school to diagnose, medically treat, and surgically correct eye disease — what is it?
Ophthalmology: Field of medicine treating eye disorders.

This family within the superfamily Delphinoidea includes species with 'whale' in their common names, like the pilot and false killer types, and ranges up in size to the massive orca — what is this family called?
Oceanic dolphin: Family of marine mammals.
Native to China and Vietnam but now invasive across the US after spreading through South Korea and Japan, this planthopper prefers the also-invasive tree of heaven as its host — what insect is it?
Spotted lanternfly: Species of planthopper indigenous to Southeast Asia.
Known as 'crawling' pinnipeds to distinguish them from their eared, sea-lion-like cousins, this group's only completely freshwater population lives in Lake Baikal — what are they called?
First flown in 1955 as a tricycle-gear evolution of an earlier taildragger model, this four-seat high-wing aircraft is the most-produced plane in history — which model is it?
Cessna 172: Propeller driven single engine aircraft.
Co-founder and CEO of Snap Inc., this businessman was the youngest billionaire in the world back in 2015 — who is he?

Members of this insect order have just one pair of true wings — the hindwings evolved into balance organs called halteres — and the group includes mosquitoes among its 150,000+ species. What are they commonly called?
Fly: Order of insects. A fly (pl. flies) is an insect of the order Diptera (from Ancient Greek δι- di- 'two' and πτερόν pteron 'wing'), named for the single pair of wings.
Discovered in 1857 by French chemist Marcellin Berthelot, this three-carbon alkane turns liquid under pressure and now fuels countless backyard barbecues — what gas is it?

This healthcare profession blends the art and science of caring, focusing on protecting and promoting health, preventing illness, and easing suffering through compassionate, hands-on care — what field is it?
Nursing: Health care profession. Nurses may help coordinate care performed by other providers or act independently as nursing professionals.

Nicknamed for its resemblance to a stinging insect, this orb-weaver spider sports bold yellow, white, and black bands across Central and Northern Europe, parts of Asia and Africa, and even the Azores — what species is it?
Argiope bruennichi: Species of orb-weaver spider. Like many other members of the same genus Argiope, this species has distinctive yellow, white and black markings on its abdomen.

Despite lacking the tight head of typical cabbage, this leafy Chinese vegetable has a flavor often compared to spinach and water chestnuts, with a milder white bulb and stronger-tasting green leaves — what vegetable is it?
Bok choy: Subspecies of flowering plant.
Named for its three-lobed shape, this extinct marine arthropod left over 22,000 fossilized species behind after roughly 270 million years in ancient oceans. What creature is it?
Trilobite: Class of extinct, Paleozoic arthropods.

The first production helicopter with fully fly-by-wire flight controls, this European twin-engine military chopper comes in troop-transport and naval anti-submarine variants flown by over a dozen NATO nations. What is it?
NHIndustries NH90: Family of military helicopters.
Every part of this evergreen tree is poisonous except its fleshy red aril, yet its wood was long prized for making longbows and lutes. What species, often planted in churchyards, is it?
Taxus baccata: Species of conifer in the family Taxaceae.

Derived from arachidonic acid and containing a distinctive 5-carbon ring among its 20 carbons, this lipid compound can trigger opposite effects in different body tissues. What hormone-like substance is it?
Prostaglandin: Group of physiologically active lipid compounds.
After a record 43 years as crown prince, this Swedish monarch approved constitutional reforms stripping the crown of its remaining political powers shortly before his 1973 death. Who was he?
Gustaf VI Adolf: King of Sweden from 1950 to 1973.
Also nicknamed the 'baum' or 'sweet' variety, this mustelid species ranges across much of the continent into Asia Minor, the Caucasus, and parts of Iran, Iraq, and Syria. What animal is it?
European pine marten: Species of mammal in the mustelid family.
This flowering plant genus boasts 310 species with showy blooms, some known by the common name 'flags' and a horticultural subgroup called 'junos' — what genus is it?
Iris (plant) is a flowering plant genus of 310 accepted species with showy flowers.
Grown on one of the Amazon's largest and longest-lived trees, this selenium-rich edible seed comes in a shell weighing up to 2 kilograms combined with its fruit. What is it?
Brazil nut: Species of tree and its edible seeds.

A trained engineer by profession, this royal consort married King Mohammed VI in 2002, becoming the first publicly acknowledged wife of a reigning monarch there to hold an official title, before their discreet 2018 divorce. Who is she?
Princess Lalla Salma of Morocco: Moroccan royal (born 1978)

Working at Tuskegee Institute, this agricultural scientist urged cotton farmers to plant peanuts and sweet potatoes instead, publishing dozens of practical bulletins to fight soil depletion. Who is he?
George Washington Carver: American botanist and inventor (1864–1943)
Nicknamed the 'gympie-gympie' by Queensland's Gubbi Gubbi people, this Australian and Malaysian rainforest plant delivers an infamously painful, long-lasting sting. What species is it?
Dendrocnide moroides: Species of plant in the nettle family.
This anatomical term for the hollow between a woman's breasts was coined in its modern sense by a Hollywood censor reviewing the 1943 film starring Jane Russell — what is the term?
Cleavage (breasts) is the narrow depression or hollow between the breasts of a woman.
Sold under the brand name Lasix, this loop diuretic treats edema from heart failure and kidney disease and can also cause tinnitus and light sensitivity?

Furosemide: Loop diuretic medication. Furosemide, sold under the brand name Lasix among others, is a loop diuretic medication used to treat edema due to heart failure, liver scarring, or kidney disease.
The platypus and the four species of echidna are the only living mammals in this order that lay eggs rather than bear live young — what is it called?
Named for a discredited belief that it 'rows' itself with its pelvic fins, this family of long pelagic fish includes the longest bony fish alive at up to 8 meters?
Oarfish: Pelagic lampriform fish belonging to Regalecidae.
Famous for a repetitive, melodic call often referenced in poetry, this brown, spotted-breasted bird uses a favorite stone as an 'anvil' to crack open snail shells — which species?
Song thrush: Species of bird. The song thrush (Turdus philomelos) is a thrush that breeds across the West Palearctic.
Its Greek-derived genus name Xylocopa literally means 'wood-cutter,' fitting for an insect that burrows nesting tunnels into dead wood or bamboo — which insect is it?
Carpenter bee: Common name for a genus of bees.
Once sold under the brand name Flexeril and chemically similar to tricyclic antidepressants, this oral medication treats sudden muscle spasms — what's the drug?
Cyclobenzaprine: Muscle relaxant medication. It should not be used together with MAOIs.
Powered by four Aviadvigatel turbofans and built in Voronezh, this Soviet-designed wide-body jet now serves mainly as the Russian president's aircraft — which airliner?
Ilyushin Il-96: Russian four-engined long-range wide-body jet airliner.
Known also as the gnu, this African antelope comes in black and blue varieties whose lineages split roughly a million years ago — which animal?
Wildebeest: Genus of antelope. Wildebeest (WIL-di-beest;, VIL-,), also called gnu (NOO or, NEW), are antelopes of the genus Connochaetes and native to Eastern and Southern Africa.
Caused by certain strains of HPV, this sexually transmitted skin growth can appear flat or raised, sometimes clustering into a cauliflower-like shape — what condition is it?
Genital wart are a sexually transmitted infection caused by certain types of human papillomavirus (HPV).

Manufactured by a Turkish company and credited largely to a former MIT graduate, this medium-altitude combat drone has become one of the most exported unmanned aircraft of its era — what aircraft (family) is it?
Baykar Bayraktar TB2 is a family of medium-altitude long-endurance (MALE) unmanned combat aerial vehicles (UCAV) capable of remotely controlled or autonomous flight operations.
This independent examination of financial records culminates in a report expressing an opinion on whether the books are free of material misstatement — what is it called?
Audit: Independent examination of an organization. The term is most frequently applied to audits of the financial information relating to a legal person.
This genus of about 850 tropical tree, shrub, and vine species is best known for two cultivated fruit-bearing members and serves as a vital food source for wildlife across the tropics — which genus?
Ficus: Genus of flowering plants in the mulberry family Moraceae.

Ranging from microscopic to a record-breaking 58 meters long for one bootlace-shaped marine species, these limbless, usually eyeless invertebrates gave their name from the Old English 'wyrm' — what are they?
With the formula H2CO3, this fleeting compound has a lifespan of only about 20 milliseconds at body temperature before converting to water and carbon dioxide — which compound?
Carbonic acid: Chemical compound. The molecule rapidly converts to water and carbon dioxide in the presence of water.
