Also known as talk therapy, this practice uses regular personal interaction to help people change behavior and improve well-being, with effects research suggests often outlast those of medication — what is it called?
Psychotherapy: Clinically applied psychology for desired behavior change.
This cone-shaped part of the brainstem controls involuntary functions from sneezing to heart rate, and was once known simply as 'the bulb' — which structure?
Medulla oblongata: Structure of the brain stem.

Prescribed under the tongue, as a cheek film, an injection, a skin patch, or an implant, this opioid treats pain and opioid use disorder — often combined with naloxone in Suboxone to deter injection misuse. What is it?
Buprenorphine: Opioid used to treat pain and opioid use disorder.
This localized pooling of blood outside the vessels — often triggered by injury, surgery, or blood-thinning medication — starts out liquid before clotting solid within the tissue. What is it called?
Hematoma: Localized bleeding outside of blood vessels. An ecchymosis is a hematoma of the skin larger than 10 mm.
Farmed largely around a South African town, this flightless bird is the heaviest bird alive and can sprint 70 km/h — the fastest of any bird on land. What is it?
Ostrich: Genus of largest living birds.

This family of fifteen tall, long-necked bird species mostly wears muted gray-and-white plumage with a patch of bare red skin on the face — except for one crowned genus that stands out — what bird is it?
Crane (bird) are a type of large bird with long legs and necks in the biological family Gruidae of the order Gruiformes.
This highly soluble white crystalline salt is spread on icy roads for de-icing and, in its anhydrous form, works as a moisture-absorbing desiccant. What compound is it?
Calcium chloride: Chemical compound. The compound is a white crystalline solid at room temperature, and it is highly soluble in water.
Named from ancient Greek for 'footless' after being mistaken for a legless swallow, this bird's closest relatives are actually hummingbirds — and it almost never touches the ground. Which bird?
Common swift: Species of bird. The resemblances between the groups are due to convergent evolution, reflecting similar contextual development.
This structural framework supporting an animal's body can take the form of a rigid outer shell, an internal bony frame, or simply fluid pressure inside the body. What is it?
Skeleton: Part of the body that forms the supporting structure.
This birth defect involves incomplete closure of the spinal column and its surrounding membranes during early pregnancy, occurring in three recognized forms — what condition is it?
Spina bifida (SB; Latin for 'split spine') is a birth defect in which there is incomplete closing of the spine and the membranes around the spinal cord during early development in pregnancy.

Its mating has never once been observed in the wild, and its five life stages were once mistaken for five separate species — this critically endangered fish is threatened by dams and overfishing. What is it?
European eel: Species of fish. The five stages of their development were originally thought to be different species.

Nicknamed the 'stone' or 'house' version of its family, this adaptable mustelid outcompetes its forest-specialist, pine-dwelling cousin in open habitats — and has even gone feral in North America. Which species is it?
Beech marten: Species of carnivore. It is listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List on account of its wide distribution, its large population, and its presence in a number of protected areas.
This contagious, vaccine-preventable viral disease is best known for causing painful swelling of the glands beside the jaw — its hallmark symptom. What is it?
Mumps: Human disease caused by paramyxovirus.
Published in 1931 by an Austrian logician, these two results proved that any consistent axiom system for arithmetic will always contain true statements it cannot prove — what are they called?
Gödel's incompleteness theorems: Limitative results in mathematical logic.

Making up the brain's outer layer of neural tissue, this six-layered structure handles attention, memory, language, and consciousness, and is folded to fit more surface area inside the skull — what is it called?
Cerebral cortex: Outer layer of the cerebrum of the mammalian brain.
Native to East Asia but now a popular ornamental across Europe, this woody twining vine in the legume family is also known in French as 'glycine' — which plant?
Wisteria: Genus of vines with lavender or white flowers.
Resembling a long-nosed mouse but actually a closer relative of hedgehogs and moles, this small mammal has sharp spike-like teeth rather than gnawing incisors — what is it?
This order of predatory flying insects includes dragonflies and damselflies, whose aquatic larvae are voracious carnivores capable of overpowering small fish and tadpoles — what is it called?
Odonata: Order of insects that includes the dragonflies and damselflies. The adults are superb aerial hunters and their legs are specialised for catching prey in flight.
Unlike benzodiazepines, this anti-anxiety medication doesn't cause sedation or dependence, and works through serotonin 5-HT1A receptors with a delayed onset of two to four weeks — which drug?
Buspirone: Medication used to treat anxiety disorders.
Named for its carbon-carbon double bond, this class of hydrocarbon includes terminal versions known as alpha-olefins — what's the general term for it?
Alkene: Hydrocarbon compound containing one or more C=C bonds.

First described by a 17th-century French mathematician in 1653, this fluid mechanics principle states that a pressure change at any point in a confined, incompressible fluid is felt equally throughout it — what's it called?
Pascal's law: Principle in fluid mechanics. The law was established by French mathematician Blaise Pascal in 1653 and published in 1663.
This motorsport engineer led the Haas Formula One team from 2016 to 2023 before becoming CEO of a MotoGP outfit — who is he?
Guenther Steiner: Italian and American motor racing engineer (born 1965)
Sometimes called the common, lawn, or English variety, this European plant is considered the archetypal member of the daisy family — what's its scientific name?

Bellis perennis: Species of plant in the daisy family. Bellis perennis ( BEL-iss pə-REN-iss), the daisy, is a European species of the family Asteraceae, often considered the archetypal species of the name daisy.
Native to the steppes of Central Asia, this two-humped pack animal's cold and drought tolerance made it indispensable to Silk Road caravans — what is it?
Bactrian camel: Species of mammal of Asia.
First synthesized by chemist Alexander Shulgin in 1974, this psychedelic compound produces hallucinogenic effects considered milder than LSD or psilocybin — what is it commonly known as?
2C-B: Psychedelic drug. 2C-B, also known as 4-bromo-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine or by names such as Nexus or Erox, is a psychedelic drug of the phenethylamine and 2C families.
Domesticated in Mexico roughly 6,000 years ago, this nightshade produces berries used in cooking, medicine, and even self-defense sprays — which plant species is it?
Capsicum annuum: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family.
Also known as black cumin or kalonji, this flowering plant native to the Levant and Iran is used across the world as a culinary spice — which species is it?
Nigella sativa: Species of flowering plant in the buttercup family.
Cultivated since the days of the Inca Empire and known in English as the Cape gooseberry or goldenberry, this South American nightshade now grows wild worldwide — which species is it?
Physalis peruviana: Species of cultivated South American fruit. Physalis peruviana is a species of plant in the nightshade family (Solanaceae) native to Chile and Peru.
Nicknamed 'The Lawyer' and once controlling over 4% of Italy's GDP as Fiat's principal shareholder, this stylish industrialist was the richest man in modern Italian history — who is he?

First identified from skulls found in a Dutch chalk quarry near Maastricht and initially mistaken for crocodile or whale bones, this giant marine lizard genus lived until 66 million years ago — which genus is it?
Mosasaurus: Extinct genus of marine lizard from the Late Cretaceous.
Used in randomized clinical trials as a genuine-looking but pharmacologically inert stand-in — like a sugar pill or saline shot — what's this sham treatment called?
Placebo: Substance or treatment of no therapeutic value.
Committed to accuracy and verification, this occupation and set of methods involves gathering and distributing the day's news — what field is it?
Journalism: Production of reports on current events.
Named in 1883 by a German anthropologist who wrongly believed it was most common among his patients, this bluish congenital birthmark usually fades by puberty — what is it?
Mongolian spot: Type of birthmark. It normally disappears three to five years after birth and almost always by puberty.
This scientific field studies microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi, and protists, encompassing sub-disciplines like virology and mycology — which discipline?
Known as the passion flower, this genus of about 550 species also has ornamental hybrids that have won Royal Horticultural Society awards and varieties used in ayahuasca analogs — name the genus?
Passiflora: Genus of flowering plants in the passion flower family.
Nicknamed the ZZ plant or eternity plant, this glossy-leaved houseplant genus native to eastern Africa is prized for being nearly impossible to kill — name the genus?
Zamioculcas: Species of plant. Zamioculcas is a genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae, containing the single species Zamioculcas zamiifolia.
Sold as button, cremini, or portobello depending on its stage of maturity, this cultivated mushroom is grown in more than 70 countries — what species is it?
Agaricus bisporus: Species of fungus. Agaricus bisporus, commonly known as the cultivated mushroom, is a basidiomycete mushroom native to grasslands in Eurasia and North America.
Often contracted from undercooked shellfish or contaminated water, this foodborne viral liver disease causes symptoms like jaundice and fever that typically last around eight weeks — what is it?
Hepatitis A: Acute infectious disease of the liver.
Also known as the windpipe, this cartilaginous tube linking the throat to the lungs is reinforced by horseshoe-shaped rings of cartilage — what is it?
Trachea: Cartilaginous tube. The trachea extends from the larynx and branches into the two primary bronchi.
Part of the rose family and prized for fruit that ranges from very sweet to notably tart, this genus's garden hybrid is an important commercial crop worldwide — which genus is it?
Made from shredded pastry dough layered with cheese and soaked in sugar syrup, this Arab dessert is especially popular during Ramadan, with a famous variant hailing from Nablus — what is it?
This seasonal state of drastically reduced metabolism, breathing, and heart rate lets animals conserve energy through winter months, with 'aestivation' as its summer counterpart — what is it called?
Hibernation: Physiological state of dormant inactivity in order to pass the winter season.
Known by the Reddit username 'spez,' this web developer co-founded the platform and also launched the now-defunct airfare search engine Hipmunk — who is he?
Steve Huffman: American web developer and entrepreneur (born 1983)
Native to West Africa and later naturalized across Asia and the West Indies, this plant's stems yield fibre while its calyces are steeped for a popular infusion — what is it?
Roselle (plant) (Sabdariffa gossypiifolia) is a species of flowering plant in the genus Sabdariffa that is native to Africa, most likely West Africa.
This condition describes a shortage of oxygen at the tissue level rather than in the blood itself, and can occur normally during intense exercise — what is it?
Hypoxia (medicine): Medical condition of lack of oxygen in the tissues.

Governed by rules laid out in a document called a blazon, this medieval discipline of coats of arms, crests, and mottoes may have arisen so knights could recognize commanders behind their helmets — what is it?
Heraldry: Discipline of the design and study of coats of arms.
Widespread across Europe, Asia, and Africa, this small predatory falcon has occasionally strayed as far as Guam and the U.S. east coast — what bird is it?
Common kestrel: Species of bird. In the United Kingdom, where no other kestrel species commonly occurs, it is generally just called the "kestrel".
This Indian economist and philosopher won the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for his work on welfare economics, and later received India's highest civilian honor — who is he?
Amartya Sen: Indian economist and Nobel laureate (born 1933)
This thorny European shrub's tart fruit gives sloe gin its name in Britain, while its wood becomes the classic Irish walking stick — what is it?
Prunus spinosa: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
This flowering shrub in the family Erythroxylaceae is one of only two species whose leaves are cultivated to produce a notorious stimulant — which plant is it?
Erythroxylum coca: Species of flowering plant.
Distinguished by a cube-shaped body, this class of stinging cnidarians includes species such as Chironex fleckeri, whose venom is often fatal to humans — what is it?
Box jellyfish: Class of cnidarians distinguished by their cube-shaped medusae.
Known by common names like greenfly and blackfly, these small sap-sucking insects reproduce via live-born nymphs without males, a trick called telescoping generations — what are they?
Aphid: Superfamily of insects. The group includes the fluffy white woolly aphids.
First flown in October 1972, this was the world's first twin-engine wide-body airliner, born from a 1967 France-West Germany-UK collaboration that later lost its British partner — what is it?
Airbus A300: World's first twin-engine widebody jet airliner.
Also known as dihydrocodeinone, this semi-synthetic opioid is often combined with acetaminophen or ibuprofen for pain and is sold alone as an extended-release drug called Zohydro ER — what is it?
Hydrocodone: Opioid drug used in pain relief.
This term describes a short chain of amino acids joined by a particular kind of bond; string together enough of them (10,000 daltons or more) and you get a protein instead — what is it?
Peptide: Short chains of 2–50 amino acids.

Native to the western Palearctic and closely related to the rock dove, this large bird feeds mainly on cereals and other plant matter, making it an agricultural pest despite being heavily hunted across its range — what is it?
Common wood pigeon: Species of large, white/green-naped, arboreal bird of Eurasia.
Packing a mass comparable to the Sun into a volume the size of Earth, this dense stellar remnant glows from leftover heat rather than nuclear fusion — what is it?
White dwarf: Stellar core remnant. A white dwarf is a very dense type of star: in an Earth-sized volume, it packs a mass that is comparable to the Sun.
Genetic studies trace this most widely cultivated apricot species to Central Asia, though its scientific name nods to a country in the Caucasus — what is it?
Prunus armeniaca: Species of apricot. The native range is somewhat uncertain due to its extensive prehistoric cultivation.
Coined by Horace Walpole in 1754, this term for a lucky accidental discovery describes how penicillin, Post-it Notes, and the microwave oven all came about — what is it?
Named for the ancient Greek word for a ship's helmsman, this transdisciplinary field studies feedback loops and circular causal processes across engineering, biology, and social systems — what is it?

Cybernetics: Study of circular causal processes. Cybernetics' transdisciplinary character means that it intersects with a number of other fields, resulting in a wide influence and diverse interpretations.
This order of even-toed hoofed mammals turns out to include whales and dolphins, molecular biology having revealed their close kinship to hippos — what order is it?
Artiodactyla: Order of mammals. Artiodactyla ( AR-tee-oh-DAK-tih-lə; from Ancient Greek ἄρτιος ártios 'even' and δάκτυλος dáktylos 'finger, toe') is an order of placental mammals.
This English scientist's 1808 book, 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy,' laid the foundations of modern atomic theory, and he also kept daily weather records for over fifty years — who was he?
John Dalton: British chemist and physicist (1766–1844)
This branch of discrete mathematics studies structures made of vertices connected by edges, modeling pairwise relationships between objects — what field is it?

Graph theory: Area of discrete mathematics. In mathematics and computer science, graph theory is the study of graphs, which are mathematical structures used to model pairwise relations between objects.
Also known as the English or Persian walnut, this tree species native to Eurasia is cultivated worldwide, with China as its leading producer today — what is it?
Juglans regia: Species of tree (walnut). Juglans regia, known by various common names including the common walnut, English walnut, or Persian walnut amongst other names, is a species of walnut.
This Austrian economist shared the 1974 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences with Gunnar Myrdal for his work on how prices communicate information — who is he?
Friedrich Hayek: Austrian economist and philosopher (1899–1992)

Present in about 80% of adults as harmless white or yellow bumps on the lips, cheeks, or gums, these visible sebaceous glands were first described in 1896 by an American dermatologist — what are they called?
Fordyce spots: Sebaceous glands that are present in most individuals.

Native to North America and classified in the genus Vaccinium, this fruit comes in wild 'lowbush' and cultivated 'highbush' varieties, with Canada leading global production of the wild type — what fruit is it?
Blueberry: Perennial plant with blue berries.
Native to South and Southeast Asia, this non-venomous constrictor is the world's longest snake and has been spotted swimming far out at sea — what species is it?
Reticulated python: Species of snake. It is the world's longest snake, and the third heaviest after the green anaconda and Burmese python.
This broadly distributed genus of spiders is informally known as the widow spiders, including the black widow and brown widow — what is it called?
Latrodectus: Genus of spiders. Latrodectus is a broadly distributed genus of spiders informally called the widow spiders, with several species that are commonly known as the true widows.
Commonly known as rays, this division of cartilaginous fish is instantly recognizable by its flattened body and enlarged pectoral fins fused to the head — what's it called?
Batomorphi: Division of cartilaginous fishes. Batomorphi, along with the shark division Selachii, both compose the subclass Elasmobranchii.
Known as simple sugars, these colorless, water-soluble crystalline compounds include glucose and fructose and serve as the building blocks of starch and cellulose — what are they called?
Monosaccharide: Simple sugars such as glucose and fructose.
A group of these mid-sized Galliformes birds is called a covey or bevy, and 40 million of them were farm-raised in the US back in 2007 alone — what bird is it?
Quail: Index of animals with the same common name.

This Indian aerospace engineer led the nation's space agency as chairman and served as secretary of the Department of Space, after directing both the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre and the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre — who is he?
This German physicist became the first-ever winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for discovering X-rays — who is he?
This branch of economics studies how individual firms and consumers allocate scarce resources, as opposed to the economy-wide view of its counterpart — which field?
Microeconomics: Behavior of individuals and firms.
Recognizable by its striking yellow-and-azure plumage, this small European songbird nests in tree holes and can acrobatically hang upside-down from branch tips — which bird?
Eurasian blue tit: Species of bird. The Eurasian blue tit (Cyanistes caeruleus) is a small passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae.
Famous for kite-shaped plates along its back and spikes on its tail, this Late Jurassic herbivore may have been preyed on by Allosaurus — which dinosaur?
Stegosaurus: Genus of Late Jurassic armored dinosaur.
Discovered in 1973 by Ruth Bishop via electron micrograph images, this fecal-oral pathogen is the leading cause of diarrheal illness in infants worldwide — which pathogen?
Rotavirus: Specific genus of RNA viruses.
Widely brewed as a calming herbal tea despite limited clinical evidence for its effects, this annual plant in the daisy family goes by the nickname 'scented mayweed' — which plant?
Matricaria chamomilla: Species of flowering plant.
Sold under the brand name Luminal, this WHO-recommended barbiturate treats epilepsy in children and can be given intravenously for status epilepticus — which drug?
Phenobarbital: Medication of the barbiturate type.
Unlike its more predictably spreading cousin, this group of blood cancers can appear in multiple parts of the body at once and cause enlarged lymph nodes, fevers, and night sweats — which condition?
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma: Type of cancer of lymph nodes.
Operating under the alias 'Dread Pirate Roberts,' this American created and ran the dark-web marketplace Silk Road until his 2013 FBI arrest — who is he?
Ross Ulbricht: American cybercriminal founder of Silk Road (born 1984)
Sporting pied black-and-white plumage with a red patch on its lower belly, this Palearctic bird drums on trees to mark territory and excavate nest holes — which species?
Great spotted woodpecker: Species of bird. The great spotted woodpecker (Dendrocopos major) is a medium-sized woodpecker with pied black and white plumage and a red patch on the lower belly.
Most commonly caused by liver cirrhosis and its resulting high blood pressure in the portal system, this condition is the abnormal buildup of fluid in the abdominal cavity — which one?
Ascites: Abnormal build-up of fluid in the abdomen.
Also known as hexogen, this nitroamine explosive is the key energetic agent in C-4 and a core ingredient of Semtex — which compound?
RDX: Explosive chemical compound. RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
Defined as the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends an angle of one arcsecond, this unit equals about 3.26 light-years — which unit?
Parsec: Unit of length in astronomy.
Publishing a landmark 1912 paper on 'vital amines,' this Polish biochemist helped pioneer the concept now known as vitamins while researching pellagra and rickets — who is he?
Sold under the brand name Vyvanse, this prodrug of dextroamphetamine treats ADHD and moderate-to-severe binge eating disorder, taking effect within about 90 minutes — which medication?
Lisdexamfetamine: Central nervous system stimulant prodrug.
Known commonly as tapeworms, this class of ribbon-like parasitic flatworms sheds egg-packed segments called proglottids — what is this class called?
Cestoda: Class of flatworms. Cestoda is a class of parasitic worms in the flatworm phylum (Platyhelminthes).
This stage of development begins right after fertilization, progressing from a single-celled zygote through a ball of cells called a morula — what is it called?
Embryo: Multicellular diploid eukaryote in its earliest stage of development.
Commonly known as snails and slugs, this class is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after insects — what is it called?
Gastropod: Class of molluscs. The fossil record of gastropods extends back to the Late Cambrian.
Also called the corn poppy or Flanders poppy, this red flowering weed has symbolized remembrance in the Commonwealth since World War I — what plant is it?
Papaver rhoeas: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family.
Known as the brain's chief inhibitory neurotransmitter, this compound is also sold as a dietary supplement despite debate over whether it crosses the blood-brain barrier — what is it?
GABA: Main inhibitory neurotransmitter in the mammalian brain.
Nicknamed the 'sensitive plant,' this legume's leaves fold inward within seconds of being touched and reopen a few minutes later — what plant is it?
Mimosa pudica: Species of creeping annual plant.
Extracted from the cochineal insect, this bright-red pigment is also known by the food-additive code E120 — what is it called?
Carmine: Pigment, aluminium salt of carminic acid.
This legume's raw seeds contain a toxic compound that must be boiled away before eating, though its unripe green pods are eaten as-is — which species is it?
This serous membrane lines the abdominal cavity and serves as a conduit for the blood vessels and nerves of the organs it covers — what is it called?
Peritoneum: Membrane that forms lining of abdominal cavity or coelom.
Known as 'the father of modern optics,' this Islamic Golden Age scholar wrote the influential 'Book of Optics' and proved that vision begins in the eye, not by rays leaving it — who is he?
Ibn al-Haytham: Arab physicist, mathematician and astronomer (c. 965 – c. 1040)
In 1886 this German engineer patented what's considered the first practical automobile, and his Mannheim company later merged with Daimler — who is he?
Carl Benz: German designer and engineer (1844–1929)
Also known as meridian fennel, this biennial plant in the Apiaceae family is native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa — what is it?
Caraway: Species of plant in the carrot family.

Thought to have originated in northern China, this widespread rodent is now dominant across Europe and much of North America, and gave rise to both a pampered pet variant and the standard laboratory strain — which species?
Brown rat: Species of common rat. One of the largest muroids, it is a brown or grey rodent with a body length of up to 28 cm (11 in) long, and a tail slightly shorter than that.
This protrusion in the neck, formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage around the larynx, becomes more prominent in most men during puberty — what is it?
Adam's apple: Feature of the neck. The Adam's apple is the protrusion in the neck formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx, typically visible in men and less so in women.

Covering more than 200 conditions from arthritis to soft-tissue pain syndromes, this umbrella term for chronic joint and connective-tissue pain gives its name to a whole medical specialty — what is it called?
Rheumatism: Medical conditions affecting the joints or connective tissue.
Built from many linked simple sugars and including starch, glycogen, and cellulose among its examples, this class of carbohydrate is the most abundant in our food — what is it called?
Polysaccharide: Long carbohydrate polymers such as starch, glycogen, cellulose, and chitin.
Born in ancient Pergamon to a wealthy architect, this Roman-era Greek physician's writings shaped anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology for centuries — who was he?
Galen: Greek physician, surgeon, and philosopher (c. 129–216 AD)
Making up most of Earth's crust, this class of chemical compound pairs oxygen with another element — the same chemistry behind the thin protective layer on aluminium foil — what is it called?
Oxide: Compounds containing an oxygen atom.
Made from strained yogurt mixed with cucumber, garlic, and herbs like dill or mint, this cold Greek dip is a classic topping for souvlaki and gyros — what is it called?
Tzatziki: Cold cucumber–yogurt dip, soup, or sauce.
Also called a slater or sow bug depending on region, this terrestrial crustacean is one of the few crustacean lineages to fully colonize dry land — what is it?
This crested songbird in the crow family sports a black, U-shaped collar and is known for hiding acorns to eat later — which eastern North American bird?
Blue jay: Species of bird. The blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America.

Developed in the early 1950s to replace the propeller-driven Skyraider, this US Navy carrier jet had a maximum takeoff weight of just 24,500 pounds — about half the Navy's specification — which aircraft?
Douglas A-4 Skyhawk: Carrier-based attack aircraft.
White, green, oolong, and black tea all come from the same evergreen shrub, simply processed to different levels of oxidation — name the plant species?
Camellia sinensis: Species of evergreen shrub. Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae.
With a heart-shaped white facial disc and an eerie screech instead of a hoot, this nocturnal hunter locates small mammals purely by sound — which bird?
Western barn owl: Species of owl. The western barn owl (Tyto alba) is a species of barn owl native to Europe, southwestern Asia, and Africa.
Nicknamed 'gold cap' and 'golden halo,' this is the world's best-known psilocybin-containing mushroom thanks to its wide distribution and how easily it's cultivated — which species?
Psilocybe cubensis: Species of fungus. It belongs to the fungus family Hymenogastraceae and was previously known as Stropharia cubensis.

Caused by the deletion of about 27 genes on chromosome 7, this genetic disorder is known for an unusually outgoing, empathetic personality alongside visual-spatial learning challenges — which condition?
Williams syndrome: Genetic disorder. Williams syndrome (WS), also Williams–Beuren syndrome (WBS), is a genetic disorder that affects many parts of the body.
Known for a bitter metallic aftertaste that gets worse if you rinse with water, this antiseptic is used before surgery and to prevent dental plaque — what is it?
Chlorhexidine: Disinfectant and antiseptic. Chlorhexidine is a disinfectant and antiseptic which is used for skin disinfection before surgery and to disinfect surgical instruments.

Also called black locust or false acacia, this deciduous legume-family tree is native to just a few small pockets of the United States but has been planted so widely it's now considered invasive elsewhere — which tree?
Robinia pseudoacacia: Species of tree native to North America.
Found in the hundreds inside most animal cells but almost never in plant cells, this acidic, enzyme-packed organelle serves as the cell's degradation center — which organelle?
Lysosome: Cell membrane organelle. A lysosome (/ˈlaɪsəˌsoʊm/) is a membrane-bound organelle that is found in all animal cells (except red blood cells), and rarely in plant cells.

Capable of constantly changing its shape by extending and retracting temporary 'false feet,' this single-celled organism turns up across nearly every branch of the eukaryotic tree of life — what is it?
This Polish tax advisor turned politician placed third in the 2025 presidential election while chairing the libertarian New Hope party — who is he?
Sławomir Mentzen: Polish economist and politician (born 1986)
Nicknamed the ALX, this Brazilian turboprop light-attack aircraft is assembled in Jacksonville, Florida with an American defense partner for low-threat counter-insurgency missions — which aircraft?
Embraer EMB 314 Super Tucano: Light ground attack and training aircraft.
Widely planted along London's streets as a hybrid variety, this tree genus includes the sycamores of North America and can tower up to 50 meters — which genus?
Platanus: Genus of flowering plants constituting the family Platanaceae.
Its Inuktitut name means 'the bearded one,' and males emit a strong odor during rut to attract mates — which thick-coated Arctic mammal is this?
Muskox: Species of arctic land mammal.

These ductless glands throughout the body secrete their products directly into the bloodstream rather than through a duct — together with the pineal, pituitary, thyroid, and others, what are they called?
Endocrine gland is a network of glands and organs located throughout the body.
Awarded the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physics, this British scientist discovered in 1897 that cathode rays were made of what we now call electrons — who is he?
Formed naturally around volcanic vents and on burning coal dumps, this white crystalline salt is mildly acidic in solution and is used as both a fertilizer and food additive — which compound?
Ammonium chloride: Chemical compound. Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as [NH4]Cl.
This highly contagious virus, spread through feces, can kill up to 91% of untreated dogs and wolves and also strikes foxes, cats, and skunks — what is it?
Canine parvovirus: Contagious virus mainly affecting dogs.
Created by Yukihiro 'Matz' Matsumoto in 1990s Japan, this dynamically typed programming language treats absolutely everything — even primitive data types — as an object — what's the language?
Ruby (programming language) is a general-purpose programming language designed with an emphasis on programming productivity and simplicity.
Despite no clinical evidence it treats any disease, this daisy-like herb is brewed into calming teas and can trigger uterine contractions in its Roman variety — what is it?
Chamomile: Common name for several daisy-like plants.
Noted for producing one of the most variable litter sizes of any dog breed, this active gun dog comes in 'field' and 'house' varieties and gave rise to its American cousin breed — what is it?
English Cocker Spaniel is a breed of gun dog. It is noteworthy for producing one of the most varied numbers of pups in a litter among all dog breeds.
Native to the western slopes of California's Sierra Nevada, this endangered conifer is the largest tree species on Earth, with a record height of 94.8 meters — what is it?
Sequoiadendron giganteum: Species of tree native to North America.
These astringent polyphenolic compounds bind proteins and are found abundantly in oak bark, historically used to turn animal hides into leather — what are they?
Tannin: Class of astringent, bitter plant polyphenolic chemical compounds.

Ancient Greek, Chinese, and Indian cultures lacked a concept for this, seeing art as discovery rather than invention, while the Judeo-Christian-Islamic tradition later reserved it for God alone — what mental faculty is this?
Creativity: Forming something new and somehow valuable.
Nicknamed the 'liberty cap' for its distinctive conical shape, this psychoactive mushroom grows in grassland and produces psilocybin — what is it?
Psilocybe semilanceata: Species of fungus in the family Hymenogastraceae, native to Europe.

Though isolated observations date back to the 6th century BC, this science's modern foundation is credited to Georges Cuvier's 1796 work demonstrating that species could go extinct — what field is this?
Paleontology: Study of past life through fossils.
Named for the Latin for 'thousand feet,' no species of this many-legged arthropod class was confirmed to have 1,000-plus legs until a 2020 discovery with over 1,300 — what are they?
Millipede: Class of arthropods. Its primary defence mechanism is to curl into a tight coil, thereby protecting its legs and other vital delicate areas on the body behind a hard exoskeleton.
Patented in 1962 and sold under a brand name synonymous with 'roofies,' this benzodiazepine is notoriously linked to date-rape drug use — what is it?
Flunitrazepam: Benzodiazepine sedative. Flunitrazepam, sold under the brand name Rohypnol among others, is a benzodiazepine used to treat severe insomnia and assist with anesthesia.

Discovered in 1801 by a Spanish-Mexican scientist but only confirmed as a new element in 1830, this hard silvery-grey transition metal takes its name from a Scandinavian goddess of beauty — what element is it?
Vanadium: Chemical element with atomic number 23 (V)
With long, whip-like antennae and a global range except Antarctica, this insect family — known as true crickets — includes burrowing giants that dig meter-deep tunnels. What is the family called?
Gryllidae: Family of crickets. The family Gryllidae contains the subfamilies and genera which entomologists now term true crickets.
Its type species, a common freshwater organism constantly studied in classrooms and labs, lends its name to an entire genus of shape-changing single-celled organisms — what's the genus?
Amoeba (genus) is a genus of single-celled amoeboids in the family Amoebidae.
Sharing its engine, transmission, and rotor system with the Huey utility helicopter, this rapidly-developed attack chopper became America's dedicated gunship escort in the Vietnam War — what is it?
Bell AH-1 Cobra: Family of attack helicopters.
Native to North America and infamous for occasionally eating their mates after reproduction, the females of this venomous spider species sport striking black-and-red coloring — what species is it?
Latrodectus mactans: Species of spider. Latrodectus mactans, known as southern black widow or simply black widow, and the shoe-button spider, is a venomous species of spider in the genus Latrodectus.
Emitting beams of radiation from its magnetic poles like a cosmic lighthouse, this highly magnetized, rapidly rotating neutron star produces remarkably precise, repeating pulses — what is it?
Pulsar: Type of neutron star with beams of radiation.
Historically called the cucullaris, this large paired back muscle runs from the base of the skull to the lower spine and swings the shoulder blade — what is it?
Trapezius: Muscle between the lower spine and the shoulder blade. It moves the scapula and supports the arm.
Comprising over 22,000 species including ragworms, earthworms, and leeches, this phylum of segmented worms use parapodia to move — what is it?
Annelid: Phylum of segmented worms. The basic annelid form consists of multiple segments called metameres.
Also known as the Congo variety, this African bird in the family Psittacidae lost its old 'African' nickname once a related Timneh species was split off as its own species — what is it?
A breakdown product of purine nucleotides found naturally in urine, elevated blood levels of this heterocyclic compound can trigger gout and kidney stones — what is it?
Uric acid: Organic compound. Uric acid is a heterocyclic compound of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and hydrogen with the formula C5H4N4O3.
Named for a Swedish medical physicist, this SI unit measures the stochastic health risk of ionizing radiation, such as equivalent and effective dose — what unit is it?
Sievert: Derived SI unit of equivalent dose of ionizing radiation. One sievert equals 100 rem, which is an older, CGS radiation unit.
Dating back roughly 250 million years to the early Triassic, this ground-dwelling insect hears through an organ on its abdomen and leaps away from danger using powerful hind legs — what is it?
Grasshopper: Common name for a group of insects.
Also known by the common names bilberry, blaeberry, and whortleberry, this holarctic shrub produces edible blue fruit — what is it?
Its Nahuatl name means 'caterpillar cocoon,' but this spineless desert cactus is better known for containing the psychoactive alkaloid mescaline — what is it?
Peyote: Species of psychoactive cactus. Peyote, also known as Lophophora williamsii, is a small, spineless cactus which contains psychoactive alkaloids, particularly mescaline.
Caused by bacteria producing acid that breaks down enamel, dentin, and cementum, this common condition can turn dental cavities anywhere from yellow to black — what is it?
Tooth decay: Deformation of teeth due to acids produced by bacteria.

Often triggered by a preceding throat infection, this childhood autoimmune disease causes raised skin bruising, joint pain, and sometimes kidney trouble from IgA immune-complex deposits — what is it called?
Henoch–Schönlein purpura: Autoimmune vascular inflammatory disease.
Named for its resemblance to a tiny mouse's ear, this flowering plant genus is known in the Northern Hemisphere by a romantic common name and is Alaska's official flower — what is it?
Myosotis: Genus of flowering plants in the family Boraginaceae.
Originating in Central Africa, this hunting dog breed doesn't bark but makes an unusual yodel-like sound instead, earning it a nickname — what breed is it?
Basenji: Central African breed of dog. The Fédération Cynologique Internationale places it in the Spitz and "primitive types" categories, while the American Kennel Club classifies it as a hound.
Domesticated in Southwest China roughly 2,000 years ago, this corm-producing plant is nicknamed 'devil's tongue' and gets boiled down into a jelly-like noodle called shirataki — what is it?
Amorphophallus konjac: Edible plant from Yunnan, China.
From the Greek for 'lack of order,' this neurological sign involves loss of voluntary muscle coordination, often linked to cerebellum dysfunction — what is it called?
Ataxia: Neurological impairment of voluntary muscle movement.
Also known by his Latinized name Rhazes, this Persian polymath authored over 200 manuscripts on medicine, philosophy, and astronomy during the Islamic Golden Age — who was he?
Abu Bakr al-Razi: 10th-century Iranian physician and polymath.
Home to crows, ravens, magpies, and jays, this bird family boasts a brain-to-body ratio rivaling great apes, and one of its members even passed the mirror self-recognition test — what family is this?

This Soviet cosmonaut commanded the first spaceflight to carry more than one crew member in 1964, then became the first human to die during a space mission when his parachute failed in 1967 — who was he?
This evergreen shrub or small tree native to South America is pollinated chiefly by the honey bee and gives us a popular tropical fruit — what species is it?
Psidium guajava: Species of flowering plant.
In tetrapods this body region between the neck and abdomen houses the heart, lungs, and thymus gland, while in insects and crustaceans it forms one of three main body segments — what is it called?
Thorax: Frontal part of an animal's body, between its head and abdomen.
Discovered in 1803 by William Hyde Wollaston and named for the rose color of one of its compounds, this rare silvery-white metal of the platinum group is used to enhance jewelry — which element?
Rhodium: Chemical element with atomic number 45 (Rh)

Given the NATO reporting name 'Hip,' this Soviet-designed helicopter family has been in continuous production since 1975 as a medium twin-turbine transport, with an armed gunship variant — which aircraft?
Mil Mi-17: Family of Russian military transport helicopters.
Derived from Greek words for 'movement' and 'study,' this scientific field examines biomechanics, motor control, and rehabilitation to understand how the human body moves — what field is this?
Kinesiology: Study of human body movement. Kinesiology addresses physiological, anatomical, biomechanical, pathological, neuropsychological principles and mechanisms of movement.
This linguistic term describes a combination of two vowel sounds gliding together within a single syllable, as heard five times in the phrase 'no highway cowboys' — what is it called?

Diphthong: Combination of two adjacent vowel sounds. A diphthong ( DIF-thong, DIP-), also known as a gliding vowel or a vowel glide, is a combination of two adjacent vowel sounds within the same syllable.
Caused by a single mutation in the LMNA gene, this rare disorder causes children to age dramatically faster than normal, with most not living past their twenties — which condition?
Progeria: Genetic disorder that causes early aging.

Distinguished from its smaller cousin mainly by size rather than any strict taxonomy, this long-tailed rodent genus numbers 56 known species, with 'kangaroo' and 'bandicoot' variants named for their appearance — which rodent?
Marketed as a COX-2 inhibitor, this NSAID treats arthritis pain and menstrual cramps but carries heart attack and stroke risk warnings — which drug?
Prized as the standard soundboard material for stringed instruments, this coniferous genus has four-sided needles and dominates boreal forests across the Northern Hemisphere — which tree genus?
Spruce: Genus of coniferous evergreen trees.
This antiandrogen medication lowers DHT production by about 70 percent and is used to treat pattern hair loss and an enlarged prostate — which drug?

Finasteride: Antiandrogen medication. Finasteride, sold under the brand names Proscar and Propecia among others, is a medication used to treat pattern hair loss and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).

This analytical framework describes how overlapping identities like race, gender, and class combine to create unique experiences of discrimination or privilege, and emerged partly as a critique of mainstream feminism — which concept?
Intersectionality: Theory of discrimination. The term intersectionality was coined by Kimberlé Crenshaw in 1989.
Lacking a body cavity and equipped with just one opening for both eating and excreting, these simple unsegmented invertebrates are named for their shape — what are they?

With a fruiting body resembling an open umbrella, this fungus often grows in fairy rings across Eurasian pastures and is prized as a good edible despite resembling toxic look-alikes — what's its scientific name?
Macrolepiota procera: Species of fungus. Macrolepiota procera, the parasol mushroom, is a basidiomycete fungus with a large, prominent fruiting body resembling a parasol.
This closed sac in the body, distinct from an abscess of pus, forms a shell of abnormal cells and may contain air, fluid, or semi-solid material — what is it, medically?
Cyst: Closed sac growth on the body. A cyst is a closed sac in the body, having a distinct envelope and division compared with the nearby tissue.
Descended from Southern Italy's traditional guard dogs and closely related to the Cane Corso, this large wrinkly Italian breed was recognized in 1949 — which dog breed?
Neapolitan Mastiff: Italian breed of dog. The Neapolitan Mastiff or Mastino Napoletano is an Italian breed of large dog of mastiff type.

Also known as Willis–Ekbom disease, this neurological disorder creates an overwhelming urge to move one's limbs, especially when at rest, often described as a crawling or tingling sensation — what's the condition called?
Restless legs syndrome: Medical condition. There is often an unpleasant feeling in the legs that improves temporarily by moving them.
Native to French Polynesia but nicknamed 'devil's ivy' for staying green even in the dark, this hardy houseplant has become an invasive nuisance worldwide — what's its scientific name?
This fig tree spreads outward indefinitely by growing extra trunks from its own prop roots, and its most famous species is the national tree of India — what is it?
This beetle family produces light mainly at twilight to attract mates — though some females mimic another species' flash pattern just to lure and eat the males — what are they commonly called?
Firefly: Family of beetles. The Lampyridae are a family of elateroid beetles with more than 2,400 described species, many of which are light-emitting.
Despite its common name, this burrowing rodent native to North American grasslands is actually a type of ground squirrel, not a canine — what is it?
Prairie dog: Genus of ground squirrels.
The only living member of its entire mammalian order, this nocturnal African burrower uses its long snout and powerful claws to dig ants and termites out of their mounds — what animal is it?
Aardvark: Burrowing mammal native to Africa.
As president of the European Commission from 1985 to 1995, this French politician spearheaded the creation of the single market and laid the groundwork for the euro — who is he?

Also nicknamed 'the bends,' this diving-related condition happens when dissolved gases form bubbles in body tissue during a too-rapid ascent, often settling painfully in the knees and elbows — what is it called?
Decompression sickness: Disorder caused by dissolved gases forming bubbles in tissues.

Dubbed the 'saviour of mothers,' this Hungarian doctor proved in 1847 that hand-washing with chlorinated lime solutions could drastically cut deadly childbed fever at a Vienna maternity clinic — who is he?
Ignaz Semmelweis: Early pioneer of antiseptic procedures.
With a pointed snout, round ears, and a scaly tail as long as its body, this small rodent species is usually distinguished from its larger cousin the rat mainly by size — which animal?
Mouse: Small long-tailed rodent. A mouse (pl. mice) is a small rodent, characteristically known to have a pointed snout, small rounded ears, a body-length scaly tail, and a high breeding rate.
Also called the pikeperch, this ray-finned game fish native to western Eurasian waters is the type species that gave its whole genus a name — which fish?
Zander: Species of fish. The zander (Sander lucioperca), sander or pikeperch, is a species of ray-finned fish from the family Percidae (which also includes perch, ruffe and darter).
Found in the Eastern Atlantic and the Mediterranean, this prized food fish from the porgy family is a cornerstone of European aquaculture — which fish?
Gilt-head bream: Mediterranean fish. It is a highly esteemed food fish and an important species in aquaculture.
In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature into healthy ones, and some cases progress into acute myeloid leukemia — what is it called?
Myelodysplastic syndrome: Diverse collection of blood-related cancers.
In quantum mechanics, this idea captures how photons and electrons can act like discrete billiard-ball-like objects in some experiments and like spreading ripples in others — what is it?
Wave–particle duality: Concept in quantum mechanics. It expresses the inability of the classical concepts such as particle or wave to fully describe the behavior of quantum objects.
Many species of this venomous snake can rear up and flare a hood when threatened — what is it?
Cobra: Index of animals with the same common name.
Originally known as amethopterin, this chemotherapy drug also treats autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and can end ectopic pregnancies — what is it?

Usually made from unleavened dough that's rolled, cut, or extruded into long strips, this staple food is called pasta in Italian cuisine and split into wheat-based and starch-based varieties in Chinese cooking — what is it?
Noodle: Staple food made from unleavened dough, commonly long and thin.
Recognizable by a prominent crest and curved bill, this Australasian parrot family includes 21 species, the smallest of which is the cockatiel — which family of birds?
Cockatoo: Any bird in the family Cacatuidae.
Patented in 1948, this first-generation antihistamine blocks the H1 receptor to relieve allergy symptoms like hay fever within about two hours — what is it?
Chlorphenamine: Antihistamine used to treat allergies.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
Enclosed in a papery husk derived from its calyx, this nightshade genus includes the tomatillo and Cape gooseberry among its edible-fruited species — which genus?
A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime, this social psychologist and democratic socialist helped found a psychoanalytic institute in New York and was linked to the Frankfurt School — who is he?
This twin-engine fighter jet program made its home nation the fourth in the world to develop stealth avionics, joining the ranks of the US, China, and Russia — which aircraft?
KAI KF-21 Boramae: South Korean fighter aircraft.
These colonial marine invertebrates secrete calcium carbonate to build the hard skeletons that form tropical reefs — what are they?
Coral: Marine invertebrates of the subphylum Anthozoa.

Nicknamed the 'Jug,' this WWII American fighter-bomber carried eight .50-caliber machine guns and weighed up to eight tons fully loaded, making it one of the heaviest fighters of the war — which aircraft?

Republic P-47 Thunderbolt: Family of fighter aircraft. The Republic P-47 Thunderbolt (nicknamed the "Jug") is a World War II-era fighter aircraft produced by the American company Republic Aviation from 1941 through 1945.
This imperial and US customary unit of volume is exactly one-eighth of a gallon, though the British version is about 20% larger than its American counterpart — which unit?

Pint: Unit of volume in the imperial and US systems. The pint (symbol pt, sometimes abbreviated as p) is a unit of volume or capacity in both the imperial and United States customary measurement systems.
NATO code-named 'Careless,' this three-engined Soviet airliner once carried half of Aeroflot's passengers and could operate from unpaved gravel airstrips in Arctic conditions — which aircraft?
Tupolev Tu-154: Soviet and Russian medium-range trijet airliner.
Sold under the brand name Pepcid, this H2-receptor-blocking medication treats stomach-acid conditions like peptic ulcers and begins working within an hour — which drug?
Famotidine: Medication that reduces stomach acid.
This Indian social activist founded the Azadi Bachao Andolan and later teamed with yoga guru Ramdev to promote swadeshi economics — who was he?
Rajiv Dixit: Indian activist. Rajiv Dixit (30 November 1967 – 30 November 2010) was an Indian social activist who founded the Azadi Bachao Andolan.
Patented in 1976 and sold under the brand name Zebeta, this beta-1-selective medication treats high blood pressure and heart failure — what is it?
Bisoprolol: Beta-1 selective adrenenergic blocker medication used to treat cardiovascular diseases.
Usually hidden underground, this plant organ anchors it in place while drawing in water and nutrients — what is it?
Root: Basal organ of a vascular plant.
Native to the western Himalayas and the Mediterranean's high altitudes, this coniferous genus bears erect cones and wood that naturally repels moths — which genus?
The first variable-sweep-wing aircraft to enter Soviet service, this fighter-bomber was produced from 1967 to 1990 and exported in variants flown across the Arab world — which jet?
Sukhoi Su-17: Soviet variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber. The Sukhoi Su-17 (Russian: Су-17; NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
Also known as the Cornelian cherry, this dogwood-family shrub or small tree is native to western and southern Europe as well as southwestern Asia — what's its scientific name?
Cornus mas: Species of flowering plant in the family Cornaceae.
Caused by heat, electricity, chemicals, friction, or radiation — and most often the result of scalding at home — what type of skin injury is classified from first- to higher-degree severity?
Burn: Injury to flesh or skin, often caused by excessive heat.
Nicknamed the 'ern' or 'erne,' this large bird of prey breeds from Greenland all the way to Hokkaido, Japan — what is it?
White-tailed eagle: Species of bird. The white-tailed eagle (Haliaeetus albicilla), sometimes known as the "sea eagle", is a large bird of prey, widely distributed across temperate Eurasia.
Sold under the brand name Robaxin and developed in 1956, this centrally acting muscle relaxant treats short-term musculoskeletal pain but its exact mechanism remains unclear — what is it?
Methocarbamol: Medication for musculoskeletal pain. It may be used together with rest, physical therapy, and pain medication.
Nicknamed the 'white rats' of its phylum for how often it's cultivated in classrooms and labs, this single-celled ciliate thrives in stagnant ponds — what is it?
With evidence of practice dating back to 7000 BC, this field is considered the very first specialization to branch off from general medicine — what is it?
Dentistry: Branch of medicine. Dentistry, also known as dental medicine and oral medicine, is the branch of medicine focused on the teeth, gums, and mouth.
Spread mainly by the Aedes aegypti mosquito, this viral illness can cause a brief recovery before a relapse brings liver damage and jaundice — what disease is it?
Yellow fever: Viral disease. In most cases, symptoms include fever, chills, loss of appetite, nausea, muscle pains—particularly in the back—and headaches.

Known by names like lingonberry and cowberry, this evergreen shrub's tart berries are a Nordic cuisine staple and are commercially grown in the Pacific Northwest and the Netherlands — what is its scientific name?
Vaccinium vitis-idaea: Species of shrub with edible fruit.
With velvety fur, tiny eyes, and powerful digging forelimbs, this subterranean mammal aerates garden soil and feasts on earthworms and slugs despite being seen as a pest — what is it?
Mole (animal): Common name for several small mammals.
Jointly developed by Pakistan and China as a lightweight fourth-generation fighter meant to eventually succeed the F-16 in Pakistan's air force, this jet's Chinese designation is FC-1 — what is it?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: Sino-Pakistani multirole fighter aircraft.
Once widespread during the Pleistocene and later reintroduced by humans to its ancient range, which hoofed mammal species is native to Turkey and possibly Italy, the Balkans, and Rhodes?
European fallow deer: Species of hooved mammal. The European fallow deer (Dama dama), also known as the common fallow deer or simply fallow deer, is a species of deer native to Eurasia.
This small Arctic rodent is the unwitting star of a persistent myth that it hurls itself off cliffs in mass suicide — what is it?
Lemming: Tribe of rodents of the family Cricetidae.
This Italian physicist built the first true electric battery in 1799 and discovered methane, disproving the idea that electricity could only come from living bodies — who is he?
Alessandro Volta: Italian chemist and physicist (1745–1827)
Found from the Labrador Sea to the Barents Sea and able to live up to 25 years, this widely eaten fish can occasionally top 180 centimeters and 50 kilograms — what species is it?
Atlantic cod: Species of fish. The Atlantic cod (pl.: cod; Gadus morhua) is a fish of the family Gadidae, widely consumed by humans.
Usually caused by Staphylococcus bacteria and treated at home with warm compresses, this tender red bump at the edge of the eyelid is also known as a hordeolum — what is it?
Stye: Swelling of the eyelid due to infection of an oil gland.
Blending science, aesthetics, and technique, this discipline wrestles with projecting a round world onto flat media while deciding what details to keep or cut — what is it called?
Cartography: Study and practice of making maps.
Sitting at the bottom of the forebrain and including the striatum and substantia nigra, this cluster of brain nuclei governs voluntary movement and habit formation — what is it called?
Basal ganglia: Group of subcortical nuclei involved in the motor and reward systems.
This self-taught Dutch draper turned lensmaker began exploring microbial life with his own single-lensed microscopes in the 1670s, earning him the title 'Father of Microbiology' — who was he?
Sold under the brand name Strattera, this selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor treats ADHD and is only recommended for patients age six and up — what is this medication?
Atomoxetine: Medication used to treat ADHD.

Nicknamed 'banana spiders' and 'armed spiders' for their aggressive posture, this genus found mainly in northern South America is better known by a name describing its roaming habits — what genus is this?
Also called dinkel wheat, this high-protein relict crop has been a staple in parts of Europe since the Bronze Age and is considered a hexaploid hybrid of common wheat and emmer — what is it?
Spelt: Species of wheat. It is a relict crop, eaten in Central Europe and northern Spain.
Known informally for resembling a certain dairy product due to its shape, this popular edible fungus grows wild across temperate and subtropical forests worldwide — what is its scientific name?
This skin sensation includes the classic 'pins and needles' feeling when a limb falls asleep, and can also be triggered by hitting your funny bone — what is it called?
Paresthesia: Dermal sensation with no physical cause.

Nicknamed the Swiss cheese plant for its perforated leaves, this houseplant native to southern Mexico and Central America produces a fruit that's edible once ripe, despite needle-like calcium oxalate crystals elsewhere in the plant — what is its scientific name?
Monstera deliciosa: Species of plant. Monstera deliciosa, the Swiss cheese plant or split-leaf philodendron, is a species of flowering plant.

Often triggered by medications like lamotrigine or allopurinol, this severe skin reaction starts with flu-like symptoms before the skin begins to blister, peel, and affect mucous membranes — what is this condition called?
Stevens–Johnson syndrome: Skin disease. The most common cause is certain medications such as lamotrigine, carbamazepine, allopurinol, sulfonamide antibiotics and nevirapine.

Named from Greek words meaning 'a chain of berries' and 'pus-forming,' this Gram-positive bacterial species is the predominant carrier of the Lancefield group A antigen, often abbreviated GAS — what is this bacterium's full scientific name?
Streptococcus pyogenes: Species of bacterium. The name group A (beta-hemolytic) Streptococcus is thus also used.

Equal to one weber per square metre, this SI unit of magnetic flux density was adopted in 1960 and named for a Serbian-American electrical engineer, on the proposal of a Slovenian engineer — name this unit?
Tesla (unit) (symbol: T) is the unit of magnetic flux density (B) (also called magnetic B-field) in the International System of Units (SI).

This acute medical syndrome develops over hours or days and causes disturbed attention, awareness, and sometimes hallucinations — often triggered by illness, substances, or their withdrawal — what is it called?
Delirium: Severe confusion that develops quickly, and often fluctuates in intensity.
Until 2010, this onion relative was classified as its own species before being folded back into the common onion — what is it?

Predicted by Mendeleev in 1869 under the placeholder name 'ekasilicon' and discovered in 1886 by Clemens Winkler, this metalloid element was named for its discoverer's home country — what element is it?
Germanium: Chemical element with atomic number 32 (Ge)
Also called elder or elderberry, this tree or shrub's flowers and berries are traditionally used to make cordial and wine — what's its scientific name?
Sambucus nigra: Species of flowering plant in the moschatel family.
The most common type of skin cancer, this slow-growing tumor is sometimes called a 'rodent ulcer' and rarely spreads beyond its original site — what is it?
Basal-cell carcinoma: Most common type of skin cancer. Basal-cell carcinoma (BCC), also known as basal-cell cancer, basalioma, or rodent ulcer, is the most common type of skin cancer.
In this heart condition, the heart chambers become enlarged and lose their ability to pump blood effectively, with causes ranging from genetics to alcohol and cocaine use — what is it called?
Dilated cardiomyopathy: Condition involving an enlarged, ineffective heart.
Also known scientifically as emesis, this forceful bodily reflex expels stomach contents through the mouth—and sometimes the nose—often preceded by a queasy feeling called nausea. What is it?
Vomiting: Expulsion of stomach contents via the mouth or nose.
After co-founding a social media giant, this entrepreneur left in 2008 to launch the workplace software company Asana — who is he?
Soft, movable, and painless, this benign fatty-tissue growth most often shows up under the skin on the upper back, shoulders, or abdomen — what is it?
Lipoma: Benign tumor made of fat tissue.
He earned a PhD in physics from Cambridge for the first-ever thesis on quantum mechanics, then shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Erwin Schrödinger — who is he?
Native to tropical Africa, this gourd-producing vine yields fruit that can be eaten young as a vegetable or dried and hollowed out into bowls, ladles, or even musical instruments — what is it?
Calabash: Species of bottle gourd plant.
Best known for pioneering radical behaviorism at Harvard, this psychologist invented a chamber for studying operant conditioning that came to bear his name — who is he?
B. F. Skinner: American psychologist and social philosopher (1904–1990)
Named from Greek for 'four teeth,' this family includes the pufferfish, blowfish, and toadfish — many of them among the most poisonous vertebrates alive. What is this family called?
Tetraodontidae: Family of pufferfish. Tetraodontidae is a family of marine and freshwater fish in the order Tetraodontiformes.
Known only from teeth and four jawbones, this extinct genus of giant ape roamed China for nearly two million years and is now thought to be a close relative of the orangutan — what is it?
Gigantopithecus: Extinct genus of primate. The species may have been sexually dimorphic, with males much bigger than females.

Allowing one neuron to send signals to a neighboring cell, this junction can be chemical or electrical, with coupled electrical types creating synchronized brain activity via gap junctions — what is it?
Synapse: Structure connecting neurons in the nervous system.
Feeding exclusively on vertebrate blood across tropical Africa, this biting fly folds its wings completely over its abdomen at rest and spreads trypanosomiasis — which insect?
Tsetse fly: Genus of disease-spreading insects.
Nicknamed 'forever chemicals' for their long environmental lifetimes, this class of synthetic compounds has been used in everything from Teflon to firefighting foam since 1938 — what's it called?
PFAS: Class of perfluorinated chemical compounds.

First isolated from lymphoid tissue behind the nose in 1953, this family of nonenveloped DNA viruses ranges from causing the common cold to life-threatening illness in the immunocompromised — which family?
Occurring in any of the senses, this perception feels completely real despite the absence of any actual external stimulus — what is it?
Hallucination: Perception that only seems real.
Born in Germany, this businessman founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans, beginning operations in San Francisco in 1853 — who is he?
Comprising seven species from the flatback to the leatherback, five of these ocean-dwelling reptiles are threatened with extinction — what are they?
Sea turtle: Reptiles of the superfamily Chelonioidea.

Flown by William J. Knight to a record 4,520 mph in 1967 — a mark that still stands — this rocket-powered aircraft was part of an experimental series operated by the Air Force and NASA — which aircraft?
North American X-15: Rocket-powered aircraft and spaceplane operated by the US Air Force and NASA.
What term describes herbivorous mammals like cattle and giraffes that digest plant matter by regurgitating and re-chewing it as cud?
Ruminant: Hoofed herbivorous grazing or browsing mammals.

Related to the tufted and horned members of its family found in the Pacific, this seabird breeds from Iceland to Newfoundland and dives underwater to catch zooplankton, small fish and crabs — which auk is this?
Atlantic puffin: Species of seabird. The Atlantic puffin (Fratercula arctica), also known as the common puffin, is a species of seabird in the auk family.
In this small bird of prey, females can be up to 25% larger than males — one of the biggest size gaps between sexes of any bird — and it hunts garden songbirds across Europe and Asia — which raptor?

Eurasian sparrowhawk: Species of bird. The Eurasian sparrowhawk (Accipiter nisus), also known as the northern sparrowhawk or simply the sparrowhawk, is a small bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.
Also known as shadbush, serviceberry, or juneberry, this rose-family shrub's berries inspired the name of a Canadian city — which genus?
Native to the mountains of Honduras and Guatemala and nicknamed the 'custard apple' for its creamy texture, this fruit was called 'the most delicious fruit known to men' by Mark Twain — which fruit?
Cherimoya: Edible fruit-bearing species of plant.
This medical specialty treats the kidneys, bladder and urinary tract, along with the male reproductive organs, covering conditions from infections to kidney stones — which field of medicine?
Urology: Medical specialty on the urinary and reproductive systems. The urinary and reproductive tracts are closely linked, and disorders of one often affect the other.
Named from a Greek word meaning 'heavy,' this soft silvery alkaline earth metal with atomic number 56 wasn't isolated until 1808 via electrolysis, decades after being identified — which element?
Barium: Chemical element with atomic number 56 (Ba)
Native to the Andes and Mesoamerica, this plant genus includes five edible species known variously as squash, pumpkin or gourd — which genus?
Tracing its formal origins to Aristotle and later shaped by Carl Linnaeus, this branch of biology studies the structure, classification and behavior of animals — which field?
First domesticated in China's Yangtze River basin more than 8,000 years ago, this grass species is the world's most widely cultivated rice — which species?
Oryza sativa: Species of plant. Oryza sativa belongs to the genus Oryza and the BOP clade in the grass family Poaceae.
Lacking a cell wall entirely, this genus of bacteria is naturally resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics that target cell-wall synthesis — which genus?
Mycoplasma: Genus of bacteria. Mycoplasma is a genus of bacteria that, like the other members of the class Mollicutes, lack a cell wall (peptidoglycan) around their cell membrane.
Also known as brewer's or baker's yeast, this single-celled fungus believed to have originated on grape skins is one of biology's most-studied model organisms — which species?
Saccharomyces cerevisiae: Species of yeast. The species has been instrumental in winemaking, baking, and brewing since ancient times.

Distinguished by its massive head, huge size, and trademark black facial mask, this gentle British dog breed is now classed as vulnerable in its homeland, with just 104 UK births recorded in 2020 — which breed?
English Mastiff: British breed of dog. The English Mastiff, or simply the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large dog of mastiff type.

This chronic skin condition causes facial redness, small dilated blood vessels, and in severe cases an enlarged red nose, and can be triggered by spicy food, alcohol, or sun exposure — which condition?
Rosacea: Skin condition, usually on the face.
North of the Arctic Circle in summer, this phenomenon keeps the sky lit long after the clock strikes twelve — what is it called?
Midnight sun: Natural phenomenon when daylight lasts for a whole day.
Nicknamed the barking deer for its unusual call, this small Asian deer genus has fossils dating back as far as 35 million years — what is it?
Used to treat everything from pneumonia to Legionnaires' disease, this broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic is the left-handed mirror-image isomer of a drug called ofloxacin — what is it?
Levofloxacin: Antibiotic. Levofloxacin, sold under the brand name Levaquin among others, is a broad-spectrum antibiotic of the fluoroquinolone drug class.
Native to the Indonesian island that gave part of its scientific name, this legume flower also goes by butterfly pea or blue pea — what is it?
Starting life bilaterally symmetrical as larvae but growing into five-pointed radial adults, this animal phylum includes starfish, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers — what is it called?
Echinoderm: Marine phylum of animals often with radial symmetries.
This small leafy vegetable, a cultivar of cabbage grown for its edible buds, shares its name with a European capital — what is it?
Brussels sprout is a member of the Gemmifera cultivar group of cabbages (Brassica oleracea), grown for its edible buds.
This white compound found in sunscreen, paint, and food coloring under the number E171 makes up two-thirds of all pigments used worldwide and is valued at over $13 billion — what is it?
Titanium dioxide: Chemical compound. Titanium dioxide, also known as titanium(IV) oxide or titania, is the inorganic compound derived from titanium with the chemical formula TiO2.
This business magnate founded the world's largest retailer by revenue in 1962, was the richest person in America throughout the 1980s, and left behind the country's wealthiest family — who is he?
The brightest star in the constellation Lyra, this star sits just 25 light-years away and served as Earth's northern pole star around 12,000 BCE — which star?
Vega: Brightest star in the constellation Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr.
First appearing in English in 1656 and later formalized in Latin by philosopher Christian Wolff, this field of study addresses the nature and origin of the universe — what field is it?
Cosmology: Study of the universe. Cosmology (from Ancient Greek κόσμος (cosmos) 'the universe, the world' and -λογία (logia) 'study of') is the study of the nature of the universe, the cosmos.
Built after a 1962 tech-transfer deal with the Soviets fell short on documentation, this Chinese fighter jet is a reverse-engineered derivative of the MiG-21 — which aircraft?
Chengdu J-7: Chinese version of the Soviet MiG-21.
A genus of roughly 125 succulent species native mostly to Madagascar, one of its members became one of the first plants ever sent into space, aboard a Soviet resupply mission in 1979 — which genus?
Kalanchoe: Genus of flowering plants in the stonecrop family.

This small, ground-nesting game bird has a call of three quick chirps repeated in succession, breeds across Europe, and winters in Africa and southern India — which species, often confused with a similar-sounding Japanese cousin?
Common quail: Species of bird. The common quail (Coturnix coturnix) or European quail is a small ground-nesting game bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae.
Based on the L-188 Electra airliner and distinguished by a tail 'stinger' used to magnetically detect submarines, this four-engine turboprop has served the US Navy since the 1960s — which aircraft?
Lockheed P-3 Orion: Maritime patrol and anti-submarine aircraft family.
Also known as a trefoil for its three-part leaves, this legume has been farmed for over 1,000 years to fix nitrogen in soil, and a rare four-leaf version is considered a good-luck charm — what plant?
This genus contains every living species of a large, snout-nosed herbivorous mammal, including the Malayan form sometimes split into its own genus — what is it?
Tapirus: Genus of tapir. The Malayan tapir is usually included in Tapirus as well, although some authorities have moved it into its own genus, Acrocodia.
Born in 1946, this German facilitator and non-fiction writer built a career exploring esoteric subjects until her death in 2011 — who was she?
Vera F. Birkenbihl: German facilitator, writer. Vera Felicitas Birkenbihl (26 April 1946 - 3 December 2011) was a German facilitator, non-fiction writer, and esoteric.
The earliest vertebrates known to achieve powered flight, these warm-blooded Mesozoic reptiles had wings stretched from ankle to a dramatically lengthened fourth finger — what were they called?
Pterosaur: Extinct order of flying reptiles.
This natural anticoagulant boosts the activity of antithrombin and is used to prevent clotting during dialysis and in blood test tubes — what medication is it?
Heparin: Anticoagulant. Heparin, also known as unfractionated heparin (UFH), is a medication and naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan.
This condition restricts blood flow to tissue, starving cells of oxygen and nutrients due to causes like thrombosis or embolism — what's it called?
Ischemia: Restriction in blood supply to tissues.
As Jimmy Carter's National Security Advisor from 1977 to 1981, this Polish-American scholar organized the Trilateral Commission and oversaw normalized ties with Communist China — who was he?
Zbigniew Brzezinski: Polish-American diplomat and political scientist (1928–2017)
Developed in 1964 at Britain's Royal Radar Establishment and influenced by JOVIAL, this programming language was chosen by the UK Ministry of Defence in 1971 for military applications — what is it?
CORAL: Early programming language. The R was originally for "radar", not "real-time".
Found in birds, crocodilians, and earthworms alike, this thick-muscled digestive organ grinds food with the help of swallowed grit — what's it called?
Gizzard: Digestive organ of some animals.

Native across the arctic and temperate Northern Hemisphere, this fern relative grows both a spore-bearing stem and a separate sterile green one, and is often mistaken for mare's tail — what plant is it?
Named after the Greek word for butter via butyric acid, this colorless, highly flammable gas exists as two isomers and vaporizes quickly at room temperature — what alkane is it?

This relationship, expressed as A = εcl, links how much light a solution absorbs directly to its concentration — what is this principle called, named after two scientists whose work dates back to the mid-18th century?
Beer–Lambert law: Scientific law describing absorption of light.
Developed by IBM with a reference manual released in 1956, this programming language became the go-to choice for numerical weather prediction and supercomputer benchmarks — what language is it?
This golden fungus — also known as 'girolle' — is often confused with a poisonous lookalike, though it remains a prized edible mushroom and the type species of its genus — which one is it?
Cantharellus cibarius: Species of fungus. Despite its characteristic features, C. cibarius can be confused with species such as the poisonous Omphalotus illudens.
A type of necrotizing tissue infection affecting the genitals or perineum, this condition most often strikes older men, diabetics or the immunocompromised — what is it called?
Fournier gangrene: Medical condition. It most commonly occurs in older men, but it can also occur both in women and children, diabetics, alcoholics, or the immunocompromised.
Best known for creating Gmail, this engineer also built the first prototype of Google's ad platform and once suggested the company's old motto, 'Don't be evil' — who is he?
Named for a modified fin ray it dangles like bait to lure in prey, this order of mostly bottom-dwelling creatures is known for extreme sexual dimorphism between the sexes — what are they called?
Anglerfish: Bony fish with a natural lure.
Caused by a mutation in the FGFR3 gene, this genetic disorder is the most common cause of short stature, marked by shortened limbs, a normal-length torso and a prominent forehead — what is it called?
Achondroplasia: Genetic condition, the most common form of dwarfism.
Native to the Americas from Mexico to South America, this diurnal member of the Procyonidae family goes by the name 'quash' in Belize — what is it?
Serving as prime minister of Turkey seven separate times before becoming president from 1993 to 2000, he was also the first PM to have been born in the Turkish Republic — who was he?

Süleyman Demirel: President of Turkey from 1993 to 2000. Demirel was the leader of the opposition from 1971 to 1975 before forming a right-wing government known as the First Nationalist Front, which collapsed in 1977.
