Brontosaurus: Genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaur. In subsequent years, two more species of Brontosaurus were named: B. parvus in 1902 and B. yahnahpin in 1994.
Arching shrubs or twining vines in the genus Lonicera, some 158 species of this fragrant plant attract hummingbirds in North America — what is it?
Brought to Asia by Spanish traders aboard the Manila galleons, this tropical American tree produces a knobby, sweet fruit known as sugar apple or custard apple — what is this plant?
Annona squamosa: Species of tree. Annona squamosa is a small, well-branched tree or shrub from the family Annonaceae that bears edible fruits called sugar apples or sweetsops or custard apples.
Spread mainly by the oriental rat flea, this gram-negative bacterium caused the Black Death and the Plague of Justinian — what is it?
Yersinia pestis: Species of bacteria, cause of plague.
Named partly for Jack Northrop, designer of a tailless aircraft, which genus of enormous azhdarchid pterosaur is a top candidate for the largest flying animal ever?
Quetzalcoatlus: Genus of azhdarchid pterosaurs from the Late Cretaceous.
This is the most abundant genus of trees on Earth, dominating the boreal forests of Siberia and Canada despite dropping its needles every fall. What genus is it?
Larch: Genus of deciduous conifers in the family Pinaceae.
This symbiotic partnership between fungus and plant roots plays a crucial role in plant nutrition and soil chemistry — usually mutualistic, but sometimes parasitic. What's the association called?
Mycorrhiza: Fungus-plant symbiotic association. The term mycorrhiza refers to the role of the fungus in the plant's rhizosphere, the plant root system and its surroundings.
Encompassing domestic pigs and their ancestor the Eurasian wild boar, this genus within the even-toed ungulate family Suidae is native across Eurasia and Africa — which genus?

Sus (genus) is the genus of domestic and wild pigs, within the even-toed ungulate family Suidae. Sus includes domestic pigs (Sus domesticus) and their ancestor, the common Eurasian wild boar (Sus scrofa), along with various other species.
With a coat of dusky-grey blotches that inspired its common name, this wild cat is one of the few able to climb down tree trunks head-first, using a long tail for balance — what species is it?

Clouded leopard: Species of wild cat. Its head-and-body length ranges from 68.6 to 108 cm (27.0 to 42.5 in) with a 61 to 91 cm (24 to 36 in) long tail, which it uses for balancing when moving in trees.
Boasting the longest cones of any spruce and widely planted as a Christmas tree, this European conifer was also the first gymnosperm to have its genome sequenced — which species?
Picea abies: Species of plant. Picea abies, the Norway spruce, Norway fir or European spruce, is a species of spruce native to Northern, Central and Eastern Europe.
This transparent structure at the front of the eye provides about two-thirds of its focusing power and can be reshaped with LASIK surgery — what is it?
Cornea: Transparent front layer of the eye. The cornea is the transparent front part of the eye which covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.

Defined by the American Thoracic Society as a subjective, uncomfortable experience of breathing discomfort that can include chest tightness or a sense of effort to breathe — what is this sensation called?
Shortness of breath (SOB), known as dyspnea (in AmE) or dyspnoea (in BrE), is an uncomfortable feeling of not being able to breathe well enough.

This speech disorder involves involuntary repetitions and prolongations of sounds or words, affects roughly 1% of the world's population, and is unrelated to a person's ability to structure their thoughts — what's it called?
Stuttering: Speech disorder. Persistent stuttering into adulthood often leads to outcomes detrimental to overall mental health, such as social isolation and suicidal thoughts.
Nicknamed for a Native American tribe, this mulberry-family tree produces a bumpy, orange-like fruit that oozes sticky white latex and is rarely eaten by animals — what's its scientific name?
Maclura pomifera: Plant species in the fig family.
Reaching about 200 kg at its largest, this reddish-brown-shelled reptile ranges through the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans as well as the Mediterranean — which species?
Loggerhead sea turtle: Species of marine reptile distributed throughout the world.
This involuntary, striated tissue forms the thick middle layer of the heart wall, with individual cells joined by structures called intercalated discs — what is it?
Cardiac muscle: Muscular tissue of heart in vertebrates.
Known medically as tinea pedis, this common fungal infection often begins between the toes and spreads in places like swimming pools and locker rooms — what is it?
Athlete's foot: Skin infection caused by fungus.
Also nicknamed the 'Maybug' or 'doodlebug,' this European scarab beetle's males swarm during mating season while females stay put munching leaves that release telltale scent chemicals — which beetle?
Cockchafer: Species of scarab beetle. The cockchafer develops via metamorphosis, in which the beetle undergoes stages of eggs, larvae, pupae and adults.

This grayish-brown, wart-skinned amphibian (scientific name Bufo bufo) is found across most of Europe, hides by day, and hunts invertebrates at dusk, moving with a slow, ungainly walk or short jumps — which species?
Common toad: Species of amphibian. It belongs to a group of closely related species descended from a common ancestral line of toads and forming a species complex.
Nicknamed for the Greek goddess of wisdom, this roughly 22-centimeter nocturnal bird was introduced to Britain in the late 1800s and to New Zealand's South Island soon after — which species?
Little owl: Species of owl. It was introduced into Britain at the end of the 19th century and into the South Island of New Zealand in the early 20th century.

Recognizable by V-shaped nostrils and a layer of blubber that keeps it warm in Arctic and temperate coastal waters, this pinniped is the most widely distributed of its kind and can weigh up to 370 pounds — which species?
Harbor seal: Species of pinniped. Blubber under the seal's skin helps to maintain body temperature.
This slender projection of a nerve cell typically carries electrical impulses away from the cell body toward other neurons, muscles, or glands — what is it called?
Axon: Long projection on a neuron that conducts signals to other neurons.
Called lucerne in the UK, Australia and New Zealand, this perennial legume has been grown as livestock fodder since ancient times — which plant?
Alfalfa: Plant species in pea family.
This seabird's large, colorful beak fades after breeding season, and its short wings beat up to 400 times a minute to keep it airborne — what bird is it?
With a siphon that can stretch over three feet and a shell just 6 to 8 inches across, this giant Pacific burrowing clam can live up to 179 years — which creature?

Endemic to North America and known for long, upward-curving upper tusks with little to no lower tusks, this proboscidean's genus split from other elephant relatives at least 28 million years ago — which ancient beast?
Normally containing two arteries and one vein cushioned in Wharton's jelly, this conduit links a developing fetus to the placenta — what is it?
Umbilical cord: Conduit between embryo/fetus and the placenta.
This outermost skin layer ranges from about 31 micrometers thick on delicate areas to nearly 600 micrometers on the sole of the foot — what is it?
Epidermis: Outermost of the three layers that make up the skin.

Despite its name, this marine reptile's shell ranges from olive to black — its nickname actually comes from the color of the fat beneath its carapace, built up from an all-plant diet — which species is this?
Green sea turtle: Species of large sea reptile. The dorsoventrally flattened body of C. mydas is covered by a large, teardrop-shaped carapace; it has a pair of large, paddle-like flippers.
Produced by glands throughout the body's linings — including the respiratory, digestive, and urogenital tracts — which slippery substance traps and destroys harmful bacteria and viruses?
Mucus: Secretion produced by mucous membranes.
Recognizable by its long, black-and-white ringed tail, this highly social Madagascar primate lives in troops of up to 30 and is dominated by females — which species?
Ring-tailed lemur: Species of mammal from Madagascar.

Discovered in Arizona in the 1940s and first classified as a species of Megalosaurus, this theropod was reassigned to a new genus in 1970 once paleontologists noticed the twin crests on its skull — which dinosaur?
Dilophosaurus: Genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic.
Known as the barn funnel weaver in North America and simply the house spider in Europe, this species belongs to the funnel-web family Agelenidae — which arachnid?
The world's largest nocturnal primate, this Madagascar lemur has ever-growing rodent-like teeth and taps tree trunks with a bony middle finger to fish out grubs by echo — which animal?
Aye-aye: Species of primate. This foraging method is called percussive foraging, and takes up 5–41% of the aye-aye's foraging time.
This complex of DNA and histone proteins packages long strands of genetic material into compact structures while controlling access for transcription, replication and repair — what is it?
Chromatin: Complex of DNA and protein in eukaryotic cells.
Named by paleontologist Barnum Brown in 1908, this armored dinosaur is considered the archetypal member of its group despite no complete skeleton ever being found — which genus?
Ankylosaurus: Ankylosaurid dinosaur genus from the Late Cretaceous Period.
Injected by a mosquito's bite and multiplying first in the liver before invading red blood cells, this parasite genus is the cause of malaria — what is it?
Plasmodium: Genus of parasitic protists that can cause malaria.
Fossils of this genus, found in Germany's Solnhofen limestone, mark the first pterosaur ever identified as a flying reptile — which genus?
Pterodactylus: Genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Late Jurassic.
Long-tailed and originally from the Indian subcontinent, this whiskered rodent is a major agricultural pest yet is honored as sacred at the Karni Mata Temple in India — which species is it?
Black rat: Species of rodent. It is a generalist omnivore that can live on a wide variety of foods.
This classical physics model imagines matter as countless invisible particles in constant, random collisions, explaining pressure, temperature and viscosity alike — what is it?
Kinetic theory of gases: Understanding of gas properties in terms of molecular motion.
First isolated in 1921 and encoded by the codon AUG, this essential amino acid also serves as the precursor to cysteine — which amino acid is this?
This lipid-rich substance wraps around nerve axons in segments, leaving gaps called nodes of Ranvier that let electrical signals leap along in a process called saltatory conduction — what is it?
Myelin: Fatty substance insulating nerve cell axons.

Known only from fragmentary remains including vertebrae and a giant femur first found by a farmer in 1987, this titanosaur may be the largest land animal ever discovered, stretching up to 35 meters — which genus?
Argentinosaurus: Late Cretaceous giant sauropod dinosaur genus.

Inspired by Ørsted's 1820 discovery that current creates a magnetic field, this principle relating a magnetic field's circulation to the current passing through a loop was later generalized by Maxwell with a displacement current term — which physics principle?
Ampère's circuital law: Concept in classical electromagnetism.

This elephant-sized extinct genus of South American ground sloths, whose type species weighed up to four tonnes, was first identified from a fossil found on an Argentine riverbank in 1787 — which genus?
Megatherium: Genus of extinct ground sloth. The first (holotype) specimen of Megatherium americanum was discovered in 1787 on the bank of the Luján River in what is now northern Argentina.
The longest member of the weasel family at up to 1.8 meters, this noisy, highly social river-dweller lives in family groups along the Amazon and in the Pantanal — which animal?

Created by Martin Odersky to address criticisms of Java, this statically typed tool blends object-oriented and functional styles, compiles to JVM bytecode, and can even transpile to JavaScript — which one?
Scala (programming language) is a strongly statically typed high-level general-purpose programming language that supports both object-oriented programming and functional programming.

The northernmost marsupial on Earth, this cat-sized nocturnal opportunist is a familiar visitor to trash cans and compost piles across North America, and often ends up as roadkill due to its slow pace — what is it?
Virginia opossum: Species of North American marsupial.
Carried harmlessly in the noses of about 10% of adults, this bacterium is the only cause of bacterial meningitis known to occur in epidemics, especially across Africa and Asia — which microbe?
Neisseria meningitidis: Species of bacterium that can cause meningitis.

Introduced to the British Isles by 1500 and known there simply as 'sycamore,' this wind-tolerant maple from Central Europe can grow to 35 metres and has turned invasive in North America and Australia — which species?
Acer pseudoplatanus: Species of maple tree. It is a large deciduous, broad-leaved tree, tolerant of wind and coastal exposure.
Found only in placental mammals, this roughly four-inch bundle of 200 to 300 million nerve fibers is the brain's largest white-matter structure, linking its left and right hemispheres — what is it?
Corpus callosum: White matter tract connecting the two cerebral hemispheres.
Made up of the collarbone, the scapula, and the upper-arm bone meeting in a ball-and-socket joint, which body part lets the arm swing in a full circle?
Shoulder: Part of the body. The articulations between the bones of the shoulder make up the shoulder joints.
Indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains and grown across Asia and Africa largely for hashish production, this plant species carries far more THC than industrial hemp — which species is it?
Cannabis indica: Species of plant. Cannabis indica is an annual plant species in the family Cannabaceae indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains of Southern Asia.

Thought to enjoy 'hybrid vigor' and a reduced risk of inbreeding-linked health problems, this catch-all term covers roughly 150 million dogs worldwide that don't belong to any officially recognized breed — what's it called?
In the standard anatomical position, this is the outermost digit of the hand, right next to the index finger — which digit, known in Latin as the pollex?
Thumb: First digit of the hand. When a person is standing in the medical anatomical position (where the palm is facing to the front), the thumb is the outermost digit.

Responsible for nearly half a million deaths each year, this condition occurs when the body produces or absorbs more heat than it can dissipate, most often from heat stroke or a drug reaction — what condition?
Hyperthermia: Elevated body temperature due to failed thermoregulation.

Named for its resemblance to a related crested dinosaur, this duck-billed herbivore could grow over 9 meters long, moved on two or four legs, and was first described in 1922 by William Parks — which dinosaur genus?
Parasaurolophus: Hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur genus from Late Cretaceous Period.
First unearthed in Mongolia's Gobi Desert in 1948, this Late Cretaceous giant is known mainly from claw bones over half a meter long, giving it a name meaning 'scythe lizard' — which dinosaur genus?
Therizinosaurus: Therizinosaurid genus from the Late Cretaceous period.

Discovered as a single well-preserved skeleton in Argentina's Chubut Province in 1984, this short-snouted, lightly built predator belongs to a South American branch of large theropods — which dinosaur genus?
Carnotaurus: Genus of dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period.
First described by a German entomologist in 1818 and known as the 'marsh mosquito,' this genus is the only one that transmits malaria to humans — which genus is it?
Anopheles: Genus of mosquito. The genus Anopheles diverged from other mosquitoes approximately 100 million years ago (mya), and, like other mosquitoes, the eggs, larvae, and pupae are aquatic.
First described in 1689 by a local naturalist, this aquatic cave-dwelling salamander is the only exclusively cave-dwelling chordate native to Europe — what is it?
Named after both a biblical sea monster and the author of 'Moby-Dick,' this extinct predatory sperm whale roamed ancient oceans roughly 9 million years ago — which genus?
Livyatan: Extinct genus of sperm whale from the Miocene epoch.
Known as silver birch for its peeling white bark, this deciduous tree native to Europe and Asia has become invasive in parts of North America — which species?
Betula pendula: Species of birch. Its range extends into Siberia, China, and southwest Asia in the mountains of northern Turkey, the Caucasus, and northern Iran.
Usually numbering four and tucked behind the thyroid, these small endocrine structures release a hormone that kicks in when blood calcium runs low — which structures?
Parathyroid gland are small endocrine glands in the neck of humans and other tetrapods.
First described by Linnaeus in 1758 and introduced to North America to control aphids, this red beetle with seven black spots gets its genus name from the Latin word for 'scarlet' — which species?
Coccinella septempunctata: Species of beetle. It inhabits many regions with a temperate climate.
Known as the 'snow monkey' for surviving areas buried in snow half the year, no other primate lives farther north than this species — which one?
Japanese macaque: Species of Old World monkey.
Sold under the brand name Anafranil, this tricyclic antidepressant treats obsessive-compulsive disorder but also premature ejaculation and the cataplexy that comes with narcolepsy — which drug?
Clomipramine: Antidepressant. It has also been notably used to treat premature ejaculation and the cataplexy associated with narcolepsy.
Domesticated in Africa and thriving in sandy, low-rainfall soil, this ancient legume is now grown mostly in Nigeria and Niger, which together supply two-thirds of the world's crop — which plant?
Cowpea: Species of plant. The cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) is an annual herbaceous legume from the genus Vigna.
As commander of Apollo 8, he led the first crew to circle the Moon and earned the Congressional Space Medal of Honor — who is he?
Frank Borman: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1928–2023)
Native to India, Nepal and Sri Lanka, this tiny feline is one of the smallest members of its family, and has been listed as Near Threatened since 2016 due to deforestation — which species?
Rusty-spotted cat: Small wild cat species native to South Asia.
Also called sweet flag, this wetland plant contains psychoactive compounds and has been banned from American food products despite centuries of use in traditional medicine — which species?
Acorus calamus: Species of plant. Acorus calamus (also called sweet flag, sway or muskrat root, among many other common names) is a species of flowering plant with psychoactive chemicals.
Roughly 20 to 30 centimeters long in adults, this smooth-muscle tube carries urine from each kidney down to the bladder — what is it called?
Ureter: Tubes used in the urinary system in most animals.

Derived independently in the 1830s by two European researchers and later given theoretical backing by George Stokes, this law describes the pressure drop of laminar flow through a drinking straw or a hypodermic needle — what's it called?
Hagen–Poiseuille equation: Law describing the pressure drop in an incompressible and Newtonian fluid.

Kicked off by a 2008 film about a billionaire in an iron suit and building toward 2012's team-up blockbuster, this shared superhero franchise organizes its films into numbered 'Phases' — which franchise?
Marvel Cinematic Universe: American superhero media franchise.
Created by George Lucas and launched in 1977, this space opera's first film was later retitled 'Episode IV: A New Hope' — which franchise?
Starting out in 2012 under an early YouTube handle, this Kansas-born creator became the first ever to cross 500 million subscribers in 2026 — who is he?
Created by Ruth Handler and introduced by Mattel in 1959, this fashion doll was inspired by a German toy called Bild Lilli and has sold over a billion units. Which franchise is this?
Created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko, this Marvel superhero first appeared in Amazing Fantasy #15 in 1962 and moonlights as a teen raised in Queens by his aunt and uncle. Who is this hero?
Spider-Man: Marvel Comics superhero. Spider-Man is a superhero in American comic books published by Marvel Comics.

Created by George Lucas and starring Harrison Ford as an archaeology professor since a 1981 debut, this adventure franchise's fifth film was directed by James Mangold in 2023. Which franchise is this?
Indiana Jones: American film franchise. Indiana Jones is an American media franchise consisting of five films and a prequel television series, along with games, comics, and tie-in novels.

Published by Activision since 2003 and originally set in World War II, this first-person shooter franchise's breakthrough came with a 2007 entry that introduced a modern military setting. Which series is this?
Call of Duty: Video game franchise.

Published by Ubisoft and considered a spiritual successor to Prince of Persia, this franchise depicts a centuries-long secret war between an order fighting for free will and the Knights Templar. Which series is this?
Created by Matt Groening for Fox and set in the fictional town of Springfield, this satirical animated sitcom was named by Time the greatest television series of the 20th century. Which show?
The Simpsons: American animated sitcom. It is a satirical depiction of American life, epitomized by the Simpson family, which consists of Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and Maggie.
Set in an Asian-inspired world where select people can bend water, earth, fire, or air, this Nickelodeon series follows twelve-year-old Aang across three seasons (2005–2008) — which show?
Avatar: The Last Airbender: American animated television series.
Created by Akira Toriyama and inspired by Journey to the West, this manga follows Son Goku from childhood as he searches for seven wish-granting orbs — which franchise?
Dragon Ball: Japanese media franchise created by Akira Toriyama.

Created by marine science educator Stephen Hillenburg and drawing on his unpublished educational comic The Intertidal Zone, this Nickelodeon series follows an eager yellow undersea dweller and his friends in Bikini Bottom — which show?
Created by Derek Kolstad and directed by Chad Stahelski, this neo-noir franchise stars Keanu Reeves as a legendary hitman drawn back into the underworld after retirement — which franchise?

Originating from Satoshi Tajiri's concept and debuting as Game Boy role-playing games in 1996, this Japanese franchise about creatures with special powers is the world's highest-grossing media property — what is it?
Pokémon: Japanese media franchise. Pokémon is a Japanese media franchise consisting of video games, animated series and films, a trading card game, and other related media.
Created by Thomas Astruc, this French animated series follows two Parisian teenagers who transform into superheroes to battle villains conjured by the antagonist Hawk Moth — which show?
Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir
Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir
Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir: 2015 French animated superhero television series.
Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir

Born from two shorts both titled The Spirit of Christmas, the second of which became an early viral internet video, this profane animated sitcom follows four boys in a fictional Colorado town — which show?
South Park: American animated sitcom. South Park is an American animated sitcom created by Trey Parker and Matt Stone for Comedy Central.
Created by Gene Roddenberry, this sci-fi franchise follows a 23rd-century vessel's voyages 'to boldly go where no man has gone before' — which franchise?
Star Trek: American science fiction media franchise.
Known in Japan as Biohazard, this Capcom survival-horror game franchise has sold over 201 million copies worldwide and spawned a live-action film series about battling zombies — which franchise?
Resident Evil: Japanese horror game series and media franchise.

Michelle Buteau: American actress and writer.

This 2015 black comedy horror film reunites the lead actors from its two predecessors in new roles as a psychopathic prison warden and his accountant, and was named one of the year's worst films — which movie?
The Human Centipede 3 (Final Sequence): 2015 film by Tom Six.
This British-American actress made her film debut in River's Edge (1986) before gaining mainstream fame in Cameron Crowe's 1989 film Say Anything... — who is she?
In this 1944 psychological thriller — a remake of a 1940 British film — a husband slowly manipulates his wife into believing she is losing her mind, in Angela Lansbury's film debut. Name the movie?
Gaslight (1944 film) is a 1944 American psychological thriller film directed by George Cukor, and starring Charles Boyer, Ingrid Bergman, Joseph Cotten and Angela Lansbury in her film debut.
Created in 1955 and originally performed by Jim Henson, this anthropomorphic green Muppet hosted a sketch-comedy TV show and sang 'Rainbow Connection' — who is he?

This sandbox life-simulation franchise, spun off from the 'SimCity' series, tasks players with directing virtual people's moods and desires — and has sold nearly 200 million copies worldwide. What's it called?
The Sims: Series of video games.

Based on Carl Barks's comics, this 1987 animated series follows a wealthy waterfowl tycoon, his three grandnephews Huey, Dewey, and Louie, and their treasure-hunting adventures across 100 episodes — name the show?
DuckTales (1987 TV series) is an American animated television series produced by Walt Disney Television Animation.
Set in the fictional Elwood City, this PBS animated series follows an anthropomorphic aardvark and his friends and family across 25 seasons ending in 2022 — which show?
Arthur (TV series) is an animated children's television series developed by Marc Brown and Kathy Waugh and produced by WGBH Boston for PBS.
Bounty hunter Samus Aran defends the galaxy from Space Pirates in this Nintendo franchise that fuses Mario-style platforming with Zelda-style exploration — which series?
First published by Maxis in 1989, this city-building franchise later spawned the blockbuster spin-off The Sims, before a disastrous 2013 reboot led to the studio's downfall — which series?
An unincorporated US territory in the Caribbean whose capital is San Juan, this self-governing archipelago sits between the Dominican Republic and the US Virgin Islands. Which territory is this?

Puerto Rico: U.S. territory in the Caribbean. Puerto Rico was settled by a succession of Indigenous peoples of the Americas beginning 2,000 to 4,000 years ago; these included the Ortoiroid, Saladoid, and Taíno.
Sitting within the Tigris-Euphrates river system and roughly corresponding to modern Iraq, this region is credited with inspiring the wheel and the world's first cursive script. Which region is this?
Mesopotamia: Historical region of West Asia.
Located about 100 kilometres off the northwest coast of Africa, this Spanish archipelago is the EU's most populous overseas special territory, with Tenerife as its largest isle — which archipelago?
Canary Islands: Spanish archipelago in the Atlantic Ocean.
Spanning from the 12th-century BC Dark Ages to roughly 600 AD, this Mediterranean civilization of loosely linked city-states was unified only once, under the Kingdom of Macedon — which civilization?
Ancient Greece: Greek civilization from 1200 BC to 600 AD.

Comprising all of Egypt and West Asia apart from the Caucasus, this geopolitical region has grown into an increasingly prominent, if often vaguely defined, term since the early 20th century. Which region is it?
Middle East: Transcontinental geopolitical region. The Middle East is a geo-political region that is generally defined as encompassing all of Egypt and all of West Asia except for the Caucasus.

Linked to the Russian mainland by a bridge built in 2018 across the Kerch Strait, this Black Sea peninsula has been under Russian occupation since 2014 despite international recognition as Ukrainian territory — which peninsula?
Crimea: Peninsula in Europe. The Isthmus of Perekop connects the peninsula to Kherson Oblast in mainland Ukraine.
Defined by culture rather than geography, this region spans two continents where Spanish and Portuguese predominate, and can therefore include countries as far north as Mexico — name this region?
Latin America is the cultural region of the Americas where Romance languages are predominantly spoken, primarily Spanish and Portuguese.
Home to Mount Etna, Europe's tallest active volcano, this Mediterranean island off the toe of Italy's boot is separated from Calabria by a narrow strait — which island?
Sicily: Island in the Mediterranean, region of Italy. Sicily's namesake is the Sicels, who inhabited the eastern part of the island during the Iron Age.
Known from Bronze Age sites like Hazor and Megiddo, this Semitic-speaking region of the Southern Levant is named in the Bible as the 'Promised Land' — what was it called?
Canaan: Region in the ancient Near East.
Home to over 241 million people, making it India's most populous state, its capital is Lucknow while a nearby city serves as its judicial seat — which state?
Uttar Pradesh: State in northern India. UP; Hindi: Uttar Pradēś, pronounced [ˈʊt̪ːəɾ pɾə.ˈdeːɕ], lit. 'Northern Province') is a state in northern India.
The fourth-largest island in the Mediterranean, this French region lies just north of Sardinia and has Ajaccio as its capital — which island?
Corsica: Island and administrative region of France.

Black, white, and green horizontal stripes overlaid by a red hoist triangle, first combined during the 1916 Arab Revolt — this pan-Arab tricolour has flown since the 1920s over which Middle Eastern territory?
Flag of Palestine is a tricolour of three equal horizontal stripes - black, white, and green from top to bottom - overlaid by a red triangle issuing from the hoist.
Formed in 1956 by uniting the Malayalam-speaking regions of southern India, this state has exported spices since 3000 BCE and calls Thiruvananthapuram its capital — which state?
Kerala: State in southwestern India. It was formed on 1 November 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act, which unified the country's Malayalam-speaking regions into a single state.

Covering much of the Deccan Plateau and bordered by the Arabian Sea, this Indian state is the country's second-most populous, having been ruled historically by dynasties from the Satavahanas to the Tughlaqs — which state?
Home to the Telugu language and bordered by the Bay of Bengal, Odisha, and Tamil Nadu among others, which southern Indian state has Amaravati as its capital and Visakhapatnam as its largest city?
Andhra Pradesh: State in southeastern India.

India's southernmost state, home to a classical language that was the first in India to earn that official recognition, has Chennai as its capital and is bisected by the Kaveri River — which state is this?
Tamil Nadu: State in southern India. Politically, Tamil Nadu is bound by the Indian states of Kerala, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh, and encloses a part of the union territory of Puducherry.
Known as Mysore State until a 1973 renaming, this southwestern Indian state's capital and largest city is Bengaluru — which state?
Karnataka: State in southwestern India. It was formed as Mysore State on 1 November 1956, with the passage of the States Reorganisation Act, and renamed Karnataka in 1973.
Home to most of the Thar Desert and bordering Pakistan's Punjab and Sindh provinces, this is India's largest state by area — which state?
Rajasthan: State in northwestern India. Rajasthan (Hindi: Rājasthāna, pronounced [ɾaːd͡ʒəsˈtʰaːn]; lit. 'Land of Kings') is a state in northwestern India.
Introduced by Peter the Great in 1693 and later banned by the Bolsheviks after 1917, this white-blue-red tricolor is the national banner of which country?
Flag of Russia is a tricolour of three equal horizontal bands: white on the top, blue in the middle, and red on the bottom.

Spanning nineteen to twenty-two countries across West Asia and North Africa, this region shares a common Semitic tongue and includes minority peoples like the Berbers, Kurds, and Somalis — what's it called?
Arab world: Geocultural region in Asia and Africa. Arabic is used as the lingua franca throughout the Arab world.

Once known narrowly for its valley between the Great Himalayas and the Pir Panjal Range, this northernmost South Asian region was ceded to a local ruler under an 1846 treaty — which disputed territory?
Kashmir: Region in South Asia. Kashmir ( KASH-meer or kash-MEER) is the northernmost geographical region of the Indian subcontinent.
Overlaying the crosses of Saint George, Saint Andrew, and Saint Patrick — though leaving out Wales entirely — this is the national flag of which country?
Union Jack: Flag of the United Kingdom.
Once the capital of the Portuguese empire in the East until 1961, this is India's smallest state by area, with Panaji as its capital — which state?
Goa: State in Southwest India. Goa ( GOH-ə; Konkani: [ɡɔ̃j]; Portuguese: [ˈɡoɐ]) is a state on the southwestern coast of India within the Konkan region.
Adopted during the Revolution and arranged in blue, white, and red vertical bands, this banner replaced the golden fleurs-de-lis of the old royal arms — which country's national tricolour is it?
Flag of France is a tricolour featuring three vertical bands coloured blue (hoist side), white, and red.
Home to 23 sites of the ancient Indus Valley Civilisation and India's longest coastline, this western state has Gandhinagar as its capital and Ahmedabad as its largest city — which state?
Gujarat: State in western India. Gujarat (Gujarati: Gujarāt, pronounced [ˈɡudʒəɾaːt]) is a state along the western coast of India.
Bordering Myanmar and historically home to the Meitei kingdom in its central valley, this northeastern Indian state has Imphal as its capital — which state?
Manipur: State in northeastern India. Manipur (IPA: [məɳiˈpʊɾ]) is a state in northeastern India, with Imphal as its capital city.
Split by the Ganges and home to the temple where the Buddha reached enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, this Indian state is the country's second-most populous — which one?
First flown in 1848 by a loose confederation of states and reintroduced by a postwar republic in 1949, this black-red-gold tricolor belongs to which European nation?
Flag of Germany is a tricolour consisting of three equal horizontal bands displaying the national colours of).
Home to Kolkata and the Sundarbans mangrove delta, this eastern Indian state borders Bangladesh, Nepal, and Bhutan and includes the Darjeeling Himalayan hill region — which state?
West Bengal: State in eastern India. West Bengal is the fourth-most populous and thirteenth-largest state by area in India, as well as the eighth-most populous country subdivision of the world.
Carved out of Andhra Pradesh after decades of protest, this southern Indian state on the Deccan Plateau was once ruled by the Qutb Shahis and the Satavahana dynasty — which state?
Telangana: State in southern India. Telangana is a state in southern India on the Deccan Plateau bordering Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh to the north and Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka to the south.

Used in Western European maps and literature from the 13th to 19th centuries, this blanket term described a vast, poorly understood swath of Asia stretching from the Caspian Sea and the Urals to the Pacific and the borders of China, India, and Persia?
Tartary: Historical term for northern and central Asia.
Bordered by Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat, and home to the ancient city of Ujjain, capital of the old Avanti Mahajanapada, this central Indian state's own capital today is Bhopal?
Madhya Pradesh: State in central India. Madhya Pradesh (Hindi: [ˈmədʱjə pɾəˈdeːʃ]; lit. 'Central Province') is a state in central India.
Encompassing today's Northeast China and part of Russia's Far East, portions of this historical region were ceded to the Russian Empire between 1858 and 1860 by a dynasty based in Beijing?
Manchuria: Geographical region in Northeast Asia.

Encompassing Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and autonomous territories like Greenland and the Faroe Islands, this Northern European region has never quite merged into one state despite a 19th-century movement pushing for just that — which region is it?
Nordic countries: Geographical and cultural region.
Located in the Mozambique Channel between Madagascar and the African mainland, this overseas department of France also belongs to the eurozone — which territory is it?
Mayotte: Overseas department of France. It is one of the overseas departments of France as well as one of the 18 regions of France, with the same status as the departments of Metropolitan France.
Blending German and French influences on the west bank of the upper Rhine, this territorial collectivity merged into the Grand Est region in 2016 — which historic French region is it?
Alsace: Region of France. Until 1871, Alsace included the area now known as the Territoire de Belfort, which formed its southernmost part.

Coined by 19th-century Western geographers for the part of the Orient closest to Europe, this transcontinental region includes the historical Fertile Crescent, Anatolia, and Egypt — which region is it?
Near East: Geographical term that roughly encompasses West Asia.
Adopted in October 1948, this white banner features a six-pointed star centered between two horizontal blue stripes echoing a prayer shawl — which national banner is it?
Flag of Israel was officially adopted on 28 October 1948.
Home to Pythagoras and birthplace of Italy's very name, this southern Italian peninsula separated from Sicily by the Strait of Messina later became a Byzantine dominion — which region is it?
Calabria: Region of Italy. It has 1,832,147 residents as of 2025 across a total area of 15,222 km2 (5,877 sq mi).
Serving as the national capital from 1947 until 1959, this Arabian Sea port is Pakistan's largest city and financial hub, with a population topping 20 million — which city?
Karachi: Capital of Sindh, Pakistan. It is situated at the southern tip of the country along the Arabian Sea coast, and formerly served as the country's capital from 1947 to 1959.

The coldest national capital in the world by average temperature, this Mongolian city began life in 1639 as a nomadic Buddhist monastic center before permanently settling at its current site in 1778 — which city?
Ulaanbaatar: Capital and largest city of Mongolia.
Built across a volcanic field of 53 cones on a narrow isthmus between two harbours, this North Island metropolis is New Zealand's most populous city — which one?
Auckland: Largest city in New Zealand. It has an urban population of about 1,547,200 (June 2025).

Encouraged by Thomas Jefferson after the Louisiana Purchase and later mythologized as the 'Wild West,' this era of westward expansion closed in 1912 with the last territories becoming states — what is it?
American frontier: Historical region of Western United States, c. 1607–1912.
Nicknamed 'the Steel City' for its central role in U.S. steel production, this Pennsylvania city sits where two rivers merge to form the Ohio — which city?
Pittsburgh: Second-most populous city in Pennsylvania, U.S.
Home to about 56% of Indonesia's population despite covering just 7% of its land, this island held the capital Jakarta and was the heart of the fight for independence — which island?
Java: Island and region in Indonesia. Java is one of the Greater Sunda Islands in the South East Asian country of Indonesia.
The only U.S. state with a one-house legislature, its capital is Lincoln and its largest city sits on the Missouri River — which state?
Nebraska: U.S. state. Nebraska (nə-BRASS-kə) is a triple-landlocked state in the Midwestern region of the United States.
Home to Kangchenjunga, India's highest peak, this least-populous Indian state borders Bhutan, Nepal, and Tibet, and touches only one other Indian state — which one?
Sikkim: State in northeastern India. Sikkim ( SIK-im; Nepali: [ˈsikːim]) is a state in northeast India.
Launched in 1958 as the largest vessel then sailing the Great Lakes, this freighter sank in a Lake Superior storm on November 10, 1975, taking all 29 crew with it — what ship was it?

SS Edmund Fitzgerald: Great Lakes freighter sunk in Lake Superior. Sometime after 5:30 p.m., Edmund Fitzgerald reported being in difficulty; at 7:10 p.m., Captain McSorley sent his last message, "We are holding our own".
Home to about 2.8 million people, this is the capital of Queensland and Australia's third-most populous city, sitting on a river of the same name near Moreton Bay — which city is it?
Brisbane: Capital city of Queensland, Australia. Brisbane lies at the centre of South East Queensland, a bio-geographical and urban region with an estimated population of 4.1 million as of 2024.
Once known as the North-East Frontier Agency until 1972 and now capitaled at Itanagar, this Indian state is claimed in large part by China as 'Southern Tibet' — which state is it?
Arunachal Pradesh: State in northeast India.
This German city, capital of Lower Saxony, was once the seat of its own kingdom from 1814 to 1866 and ranks as the fourth-largest city in northern Germany — which city is it?
Hanover: Capital of Lower Saxony, Germany. Hanover (German: Hannover [haˈnoːfɐ]) is the capital and largest city of the German state of Lower Saxony.
A dormant twin-summited stratovolcano in the Caucasus, this peak is both the highest point in Europe and the highest volcano in Eurasia — which mountain?

Mount Elbrus is the highest mountain in Russia and Europe. It is situated in the southern Russian republic of Kabardino-Balkaria in the western extension of Ciscaucasia, and is the highest peak of the Caucasus Mountains.
Connected to open water through the Strait of Hormuz, this body of water separates the Arabian Peninsula from Iran and receives the Shatt al-Arab river delta — what sea?
Persian Gulf: Mediterranean sea in West Asia.
This Mediterranean port city is the second-largest in Spain's Valencian Community after its regional namesake, and forms an almost million-strong conurbation with nearby Elche — which city is it?
Alicante: Municipality in Valencian Community, Spain. Together with Elche (Elx) and other municipalities, Alicante forms a conurbation of nearly 1 million inhabitants.
Once known as Léopoldville until 1966, this DRC capital is projected to reach 18.5 million residents in 2026, making it the world's seventh most populous city proper — which city is it?
Kinshasa: Capital and most populous city of DR Congo.
Meaning 'new flower' in Amharic, this Ethiopian capital sits 2,355 meters above sea level, making it the highest capital city on its continent — which city is it?
Addis Ababa: Capital and largest city of Ethiopia.
Home to the largest city in Northeast India, Guwahati, this state sits along the Brahmaputra Valley and connects to the rest of the country via the narrow Siliguri Corridor — which state is it?
The Land of Red Rivers and Blue Hills
Assam: State in Northeast India. Assam is a state in Northeast India, located south of the Eastern Himalayas along the Brahmaputra Valley and Barak River valleys.
Built around a sacred pool and topped by the Akal Takht, one of Sikhism's five seats of authority, this Amritsar gurdwara draws more than 150,000 worshippers a day — which shrine is it?
Golden Temple: Sikh religious site in Punjab, India.

Founded around 515 BC as the Achaemenid Empire's ceremonial capital, this Iranian palace-city was burned after Alexander the Great's army captured it in 330 BC, possibly at a courtesan's urging during a feast. Which UNESCO site?
Persepolis: Ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire. It is situated in the plains of Marvdasht, encircled by the southern Zagros Mountains, Fars province of Iran.
Renamed from its colonial-era spelling in 2011, this Indian state was once home to the ancient kingdom of Kalinga, invaded by Emperor Ashoka in 261 BCE — which state?
Ruled for generations by the della Scala family and still hosting an opera season inside its ancient Roman amphitheater, which city is the largest in Italy's Veneto region?
Verona: City in Veneto, Italy. Verona ( və-ROH-nə, Italian: [veˈroːna]; Venetian: Verona or Veròna) is the largest city in the region of Veneto in Italy, with 255,131 inhabitants.
Designated by Caliph Uthman in 647 CE as the main port for pilgrims heading to Mecca, this Red Sea city is Saudi Arabia's second-largest and serves as the OIC's administrative center — which city?
Jeddah: Second-largest city in Saudi Arabia. Jeddah is the largest city in Mecca Province, the second-largest city in Saudi Arabia after Riyadh, and the country’s main commercial center.
Historically called Kantipur, this Himalayan capital sits at over 1,300 metres elevation and is among the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities?
Kathmandu: Capital and largest city in Nepal.
Home to Milan and more comuni than any other region, this northern Italian territory sits between the Alps and tributaries of the Po?
Lombardy: Region of Italy. It is the second-most populous region of the European Union (EU), and the second region of the European Union by nominal GDP.
Founded in 1621 by King Gustavus Adolphus as a fortified Dutch trading colony, this is Sweden's second-largest city?
Gothenburg: City in Västergötland, Sweden. King Gustavus Adolphus founded Gothenburg by royal charter in 1621 as a heavily fortified, primarily Dutch, trading colony.
Built for a Carian satrap and his sister-wife around 350 BC in present-day Bodrum, this roughly 45-metre tomb gave us the modern word for a monumental grave?
Mausoleum at Halicarnassus: One of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
Once known as Little Britain and united with the French crown in 1532, this peninsula is the traditional homeland of the Breton people?
Brittany: Cultural area in northwestern France.
Russia's largest island, its southern tip lies just 40 kilometres from Hokkaido and its name derives from a Manchu word for a Qing dynasty city?
Carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000 with Raipur as its capital, this landlocked central Indian state is home to the ancient Sitabenga Caves?
Chhattisgarh: State in central India. Chhattisgarh (Hindi: [ˈtʃʰət̪ːiːsgəɽʱ]) is a landlocked state in central India.

Described by the Romans as encompassing present-day France, Belgium, and parts of Germany and Italy, this ancient region's warriors sacked Rome in 387 BC under a chieftain named Brennos — what was the region called?
Gaul: Historical region of Western Europe inhabited by Celtic tribes.

Nicknamed 'The Emerald Isle of the Caribbean' for its Irish heritage, this British Overseas Territory saw its capital destroyed by the eruption of the Soufrière Hills volcano in 1995 — which territory?
Montserrat: British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean. It is part of the Leeward Islands, the northern portion of the Lesser Antilles chain of the West Indies.
Home to the financial hub of Frankfurt am Main and the historic cities of Darmstadt and Kassel, this landlocked German state has a population of over six million — which state?
Hesse: State in Germany. Hesse or Hessen (German pronunciation: [ˈhɛsn̩]), officially the State of Hesse (German: Land Hessen), is a landlocked state in Germany.
This Mediterranean archipelago off Spain's eastern coast includes Ibiza, Formentera, Mallorca, and Menorca, with Palma as its capital — which archipelago?
Balearic Islands: Spanish archipelago in the Mediterranean. The Balearic Islands are an archipelago in the western Mediterranean Sea, near the eastern coast of the Iberian Peninsula.
Founded in 1829 by Captain James Stirling and often called the world's most isolated major city, which Australian state capital sits on the Swan Coastal Plain?
Perth: Capital city of Western Australia.
Named after the medieval city of Halych and first recorded in a 1206 Hungarian chronicle, this historical region spans present-day southeastern Poland and western Ukraine — which region?
Galicia (Eastern Europe): Historical region. It covers much of the other historic regions of Red Ruthenia (centered on Lviv) and Lesser Poland (centered on Kraków).
Ringed by a lagoon and barrier reef around the remains of an extinct volcano, this French Polynesian island lies about 230 km northwest of Papeete — which island?
Bora Bora: Island in French Polynesia. Bora Bora has a total land area of 30.55 km2 (12 sq mi).
Self-governing in free association with New Zealand, this Polynesian nation of 15 isles has no armed forces, and its capital, Avarua, sits on Rarotonga — what country is it?
Cook Islands: Country in the South Pacific Ocean.
Made up of roughly 607 islands across four regions—Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae—this Pacific nation covers most of the Caroline Islands north of the equator — which country?
Federated States of Micronesia: Island country in Oceania.
Filippo Brunelleschi engineered the dome for this Italian basilica, completed in 1436 with a marble exterior of green, pink, and white panels — which landmark?
Florence Cathedral: Church in Tuscany, Italy.
Capital of Spain's Balearic Islands and home to over 438,000 people, this city sits on a bay along the southern coast of its namesake island — which city?
Palma de Mallorca: City in the Balearic Islands, Spain. The Cabrera Archipelago, though widely separated from Palma proper, is part of the municipality.
Founded by Phoenicians on a North African peninsula and annexed by Portugal in 1415, this autonomous Spanish city sits on the boundary between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic — what is it?
Ceuta: Spanish autonomous city in northwestern Africa.
Serving as West Germany's capital from 1949 until reunification, this Rhine-side city remained the seat of government until 1999 — which city is it?
Bonn: City in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.
Formerly called the Sandwich chain, this Pacific archipelago of eight major volcanoes rises from a hotspot at the end of a long undersea mountain range — which archipelago?
Hawaiian Islands: Archipelago in the Pacific Ocean. Formerly called the Sandwich Islands, the present name for the archipelago is derived from the name of its largest island, Hawaiʻi.
Rebuilt with Soviet assistance after being devastated in the Korean War, this East Asian capital sits on the Taedong River and claims a legendary founding date of 1122 BC — which city?
Pyongyang: Capital and largest city of North Korea.
Rising near Smolensk and flowing through Belarus and Ukraine to the Black Sea, this waterway is the longest river in both those countries — which river?
Dnieper: Major river in Eastern Europe.
This historiographical term covers a medieval and early modern state whose colonial holdings once made it the second-largest empire in the world after Spain's — what is it called?
Kingdom of France: Country in Western Europe (843–1792; 1815–1848)
Separating southern England from northern France and narrowing to just 34 km at its strait, this stretch of water is the world's busiest shipping area — what is it called?
English Channel: Body of water between Great Britain and France.
Nicknamed the 'Green City under the Sun,' this East African capital is the only capital city on Earth that contains a national park within its own boundaries — which city is it?
Nairobi: Capital and largest city of Kenya.

Formally founded in 972 AD by Buluggin ibn Ziri and later shaped by Ottoman and French rule, this Mediterranean capital is the largest city in its country and the third-largest on that sea — which city is it?

Algiers: Capital and largest city of Algeria. Algiers, officially Capital City of Algiers, is the capital city of Algeria, located on the Mediterranean Sea in the north-central portion of the country.

Nicknamed the 'City of Lakes' for its thirteen lakes and wetlands, this Minnesota metropolis sits on the Upper Mississippi River and adjoins its state capital to form the Twin Cities — which city is it?
Minneapolis: City in Minnesota, United States.
Meaning 'Northern Land,' this Indian state borders Tibet and Nepal, with Dehradun as its winter capital and the Himalayas covering most of its terrain — which state?
Uttarakhand: State in northern India. Uttarakhand has a total area of 53,483 km2 (20,650 sq mi), equal to 1.6 per cent of the total area of India.
Stretching 3,000 miles from western Canada down to New Mexico, this range is the largest system of peaks in North America — which range?
Rocky Mountains: Major mountain range in western North America.
This South African city serves as the country's executive capital and hosts every foreign embassy, straddling a river near the Magaliesberg mountains — which city?
Pretoria: Administrative capital of South Africa.

Sometimes mislabeled a 'supervolcano' in the media despite not meeting the technical threshold, this large caldera west of Naples has erupted with a volcanic explosivity index as high as 7 — which caldera?
Phlegraean Fields: Caldera volcano west of Naples, Italy.
Home to the world's oldest known statues of the human form dating to the 8th millennium BC, this Jordanian capital was once known as Philadelphia under Greco-Roman rule — which city?
Amman: Capital City of Jordan. Amman is the capital and the largest city of Jordan, and the country's economic, political, and cultural center.
Named the northernmost arm of the Mediterranean, which body of water separates Italy from the Balkan Peninsula and contains over 1,300 islands?
Adriatic Sea: Body of water between the Italian and Balkan Peninsulas.
Nicknamed the 'Manchester of India' for its cotton industry, which Gujarat city sits on the Sabarmati River near the state capital?
Ahmedabad: Most populous city in Gujarat, India.
This archipelagic nation in the eastern Caribbean's Windward Islands has Kingstown as its capital and includes the islands of Bequia, Mustique, and Canouan — which country?
Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: Archipelagic country in the Caribbean. To the north lies Saint Lucia, to the east is Barbados and Grenada lies to the south.
The capital of Pakistan's Punjab province, this city of over 14 million reached its splendor under the Mughal Empire in the late 16th century — which city?
Lahore: Capital of Punjab, Pakistan. It is the second-largest city in Pakistan, after Karachi, and 27th largest in the world, with a population of over 14 million.
Home to the Caroline, Gilbert, Mariana, and Marshall island groups, this Pacific subregion of Oceania is governed by six different sovereign nations — what is it?
Micronesia: Subregion of Oceania. Micronesia (UK:, US:) is a subregion of Oceania, consisting of approximately 2,000 small islands in the Northwestern Pacific Ocean.
This Ukrainian city, the country's fourth-largest with about a million people, sits on the river that gave it its name and was once called Yekaterinoslav after a Russian empress. What city is it?
Dnipro is Ukraine's fourth-largest city, with about one million inhabitants.
Split into Lower and Upper halves along the Oder River, this heavily industrialized historical region lies mostly in Poland with slivers in Czechia and Germany — what is it?
Silesia: Historical region of Central Europe.
Built on an island in Lake Texcoco, this Aztec capital was the largest city in the pre-Columbian Americas before falling to the Spanish in 1521 — what was it called?
Tenochtitlan: Former city-state in the Valley of Mexico.

Projecting into the ocean between the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea below the Himalayas, this physiographic region is today divided among Bangladesh, Pakistan, and the large nation between them — what's it called?
Indian subcontinent: Physiographical region in South Asia.
Running from near the Caspian Sea north to the Arctic Ocean, this range forms the conventional boundary between Europe and Asia, separating European Russia from Siberia — what's it called?
Ural Mountains: Mountain range in Eurasia.
Adopted after independence from Spain, this vertical green-white-red tricolor features an eagle devouring a serpent atop a cactus at its center — whose national banner is it?
Flag of Mexico is a vertical tricolour of green, white, and red with the national coat of arms charged in the center of the white stripe.

Sitting on the Neckar River in Baden-Württemberg, this German city of about 163,000 has roughly a quarter of its population enrolled as students and anchors part of the Rhine-Neckar region — which city is it?

Heidelberg: City in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. Located about 78 km (48 mi) south of Frankfurt, Heidelberg is part of the densely populated Rhine-Neckar Metropolitan Region which has its centre in Mannheim.
Nicknamed 'the Tube,' this transit system opened in 1863 as the world's first sub-surface passenger railway and now runs 11 lines across 250 miles of track — which network?
London Underground: Rapid transit system in England.

Home to the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, this pre-Aztec metropolis near modern Mexico City may have housed 100,000 people at its height around the year 500 — what's this ancient site?
Teotihuacan: Ancient Mesoamerican city. Although close to Mexico City, Teotihuacan was not a Mexica (i.e.

Founded as Scupi under Roman emperor Domitian, destroyed by a 518 earthquake, and later a brief capital of the Serbian Empire, this Vardar River city is now North Macedonia's capital — what city is it?

Skopje: Capital and largest city of North Macedonia. It lies in the northern part of the country, in the Skopje Valley along the Vardar River, and is the political, economic, and cultural centre of the country.

Officially called the Nisshōki — literally 'sun disc' — but nicknamed the Hinomaru, this white banner with a red circle embodies its country's nickname as the Land of the Rising Sun — which national symbol is it?
Flag of Japan is a rectangular white banner with a red circle at its center.

This remote Yemeni island in the Indian Ocean makes up about 95% of its archipelago's landmass and is geologically considered part of Africa despite belonging administratively to Yemen. What island is it?
Socotra is a Yemeni island in the Indian Ocean. It is situated between the Gulf of Aden, the Guardafui Channel and the Arabian Sea, and lies near major shipping routes.
Connected to the Black Sea via the Dardanelles and Bosphorus, this arm of the Mediterranean between Greece and Turkey is dotted with islands including Crete and Rhodes — what sea is it?
Aegean Sea: Mediterranean between Greece and Turkey. The Aegean Sea is an elongated embayment of the Mediterranean Sea between Europe and Asia.
Founded around 882 and once the 'chief city' of the Hanseatic League's Rhine-Westphalia circle, this German city is the largest in the Ruhr region — which city?
Dortmund: City in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.

Nicknamed 'the land of forests,' this landlocked eastern Indian state is home to the pilgrimage site Baidyanath Dham and produces more than 40% of India's minerals despite widespread poverty — which state?
Jharkhand: State in eastern India. Jharkhand (Hindi: Jhārkhaṇḍ, pronounced [d͡ʒʱaːɾkʰəɳɖ]; lit. 'the land of forests') is a landlocked state in eastern India.
Home to West Lake and the southern end of the Grand Canal, this Chinese city once served as capital of the Southern Song dynasty and now hosts Alibaba's headquarters — which city?
Hangzhou: Prefecture-level and sub-provincial city in Zhejiang, China.

France's sixth-largest city sits on the Loire near the Atlantic coast, and its historic ties to Brittany — despite being left out of the modern Breton region — remain a sore point locally. Which city?
Nantes: Prefecture and commune in Pays de la Loire, France.
The third-largest island in a Spanish archipelago off northwest Africa, home to roughly 40% of the whole chain's population and Spain's ninth-largest city — which island?
Gran Canaria: Spanish island in the North Atlantic.
Sitting on Lake Erie's southern shore about 60 miles from the Pennsylvania line, this Ohio city trails only Columbus in statewide population — which city?
Cleveland: City in Ohio, United States.
Founded at the meeting point of the Scheldt and Leie rivers, this Belgian city was one of northern Europe's largest and richest around 1300, with a well-preserved historic core today — which city?
Ghent: Capital of East Flanders province, Belgium.
Known as the city of Saint Nicholas, this Adriatic port in southern Italy is the ninth-largest city in the country and capital of the Apulia region — which city?
Bari: City in Apulia, Italy. It is one of the most important economic centres of mainland southern Italy.
Home to Timanfaya National Park and declared a UNESCO biosphere reserve in 1993, which is the easternmost of Spain's Canary Islands?
Lanzarote: Canary Island. Covering 845.94 square kilometres (326.62 square miles), Lanzarote is the fourth-largest of the islands in the archipelago.
Once the only Japanese port open to Portuguese and Dutch traders for centuries, this Kyushu city later became the second in the world to suffer a nuclear attack, in 1945 — which city?
Nagasaki: Core city in Kyushu, Japan.
Nicknamed 'The Rock' for being one of the world's largest coral islands, this South Pacific nation is self-governing in free association with New Zealand — which country?
Niue: Island country. It is situated in the South Pacific Ocean, is part of Polynesia, and is predominantly inhabited by Polynesians.
Just 10 km off Piombino in Tuscany, this island was the site of Napoleon's first exile from 1814 to 1815 — which island?
Elba: Mediterranean island in Tuscany, Italy.
Roughly matching a medieval duchy and including the Channel Islands as its 'insular' portion, this northwestern French region is home to Rouen, Caen, and Le Havre — which region?
Normandy: Geographical and cultural region of northwest Europe.
Nicknamed 'Land of the Gods,' this northernmost mountain state of India in the Western Himalayas shares its eastern border with Tibet — which state?

Himachal Pradesh: State in northwestern India. Himachal Pradesh (Hindi: Himācal Pradeś, pronounced [ɦɪˈmäːtʃəl pɾəˈd̪eːʃ]; lit. 'Snow-laden Mountain Province') is a state in the northern part of India.
Formed in 1966 when a neighboring state was split by parliament, this northwestern Indian state shares its capital with that neighbor and includes the tech hub of Gurgaon — which state is it?
Haryana: State in northwestern India. The modern state of Haryana was formed on 1 November 1966 after the Punjab Reorganisation Act was passed by the Indian Parliament.
The world's southernmost capital of a sovereign nation, this New Zealand city at the tip of the North Island also claims the title of the world's windiest city by average wind speed. What's the city?
Wellington: Capital city of New Zealand. It is located at the southwestern tip of the North Island, between Cook Strait and the Remutaka Range.
Which line of latitude, sitting at about 66°34' N, marks the boundary where the sun doesn't rise at all during the winter solstice, or set at all during the summer solstice?
Arctic Circle is one of the two polar circles, and the northernmost of the five major circles of latitude.
Home to South Korea's busiest port and the world's sixth-largest container port, this metropolis trails only Seoul in national population — which city?
Busan: City in South Korea. Busan is divided into 15 major administrative districts and a single county, together housing a population of approximately 3.6 million.
Seat of Bolivia's government, this city sits in a canyon-like bowl in the Andes, overlooked by the snow-capped, triple-peaked Illimani — which city?
La Paz: Seat of government of Bolivia. La Paz (Spanish: [la ˈpas]; lit. 'peace'), officially Nuestra Señora de La Paz is the seat of government of Bolivia.
Founded in 1496, this Caribbean capital is the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the Americas and home to the hemisphere's first university, cathedral, and fortress — which city?
Santo Domingo: Capital and largest city of the Dominican Republic.
Flourishing after a visit from Mansa Musa around 1325, this Saharan trading hub grew rich on salt, gold, and ivory and became a magnet for Islamic scholars — which city?
Timbuktu: City in Tombouctou Region, Mali.

Encompassing adherents of the Quran across roughly 1,400 years — including a golden age of science, medicine, and philosophy — this civilizational community is also called the Ummah. What is it commonly known as?
Islamic world: Muslim-majority countries, states, districts, or towns.
The second-largest island in the Hawaiian archipelago, this island's historic town was largely destroyed by wildfire in 2023, while Kahului serves as its commercial hub — which island is it?
Maui: Second largest island in Hawaii. Maui is the second-largest island in the Hawaiian archipelago, at 727.2 square miles (1,883 km2).

Defined biblically in the Book of Ezekiel and also called the Holy region or Canaan, this traditional Jewish term for the Southern Levant is distinct from the modern nation that shares part of its name — what is it?
Land of Israel: Area of the Southern Levant. Related biblical, religious, and historical English terms include the Land of Canaan, the Promised Land, the Holy Land, and Palestine.

Comprising the central, eastern, southern, and western regions of a continent, this area lying south of a great desert is grouped by the UN as counterpart to a northern region often classified with the Middle East — what is it?

Sub-Saharan Africa: Regions south of the Sahara. The African Union (AU) uses a different regional breakdown, recognising all 55 member states on the continent—grouping them into five distinct and standard regions.
First flown during the 1848 Spring of Nations in Lviv and later banned under Soviet rule in favor of a red-and-hammer-and-sickle design, this blue-and-yellow bicolor represents which nation?
Flag of Ukraine consists of equally sized horizontal bands of blue and yellow.
Standing 6,967 metres tall in Argentina's Mendoza Province, this Andean peak is the highest mountain in the Americas and the tallest anywhere outside Asia — what is it?
Aconcagua: Highest mountain in the Americas. Aconcagua (Spanish pronunciation: [akoŋˈkaɣwa]) is a mountain in the Principal Cordillera of the Andes range, located in Mendoza Province, Argentina.
Sitting in a valley along the Guaire River and shadowed by the 2,200-meter Cerro El Ávila, this metropolis of over 5 million is Venezuela's capital — what city is it?
Caracas: Capital and largest city of Venezuela. Caracas is located along the Guaire River in the northern part of Venezuela, within the Caracas Valley of the Venezuelan coastal mountain range.
The sixth-largest island in the world and the largest lying entirely within Indonesia, this landmass is separated from the Malay Peninsula by the Strait of Malacca — which island is it?
Sumatra: Region and island in western Indonesia.

Towering 20,310 feet in Alaska, this peak has the greatest base-to-summit rise of any mountain on Earth and was named by the Koyukon people long before a gold prospector tried renaming it — what's it called?
Denali: Highest mountain in North America.
Known as a major port since the 1st century CE, this Arabian capital sits near the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz and is known for its low-lying white buildings — which city is this?
Muscat: Capital and largest city of Oman.
Sitting on the River Warta in western Poland, this city is famous for its Saint Martin's Day croissant tradition and was once one of medieval Poland's historical capitals — which city is this?
Poznań: City in Greater Poland Voivodeship, Poland.
Bounded by Cuba and Puerto Rico to the north and Central America to the west, this Atlantic tropical body of water reaches its deepest point at the Cayman Trough near Jamaica — which body of water?
Caribbean Sea: Sea of the Atlantic Ocean bounded by North, Central, and South America.
The fourth-largest city in Baden-Württemberg, this university city sits at the southwestern edge of the Black Forest and is Germany's southernmost city with over 100,000 residents — which city?

Freiburg im Breisgau: City in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. Freiburg im Breisgau or simply Freiburg, is the fourth-largest city in the German state of Baden-Württemberg after Stuttgart, Mannheim and Karlsruhe.
The fifth-most populous city in Australia, this state capital sits between the Gulf St Vincent and the Mount Lofty Ranges on land traditionally owned by the Kaurna people — which city?

Adelaide: Capital city of South Australia, Australia. Adelaide is situated on the Adelaide Plains north of the Fleurieu Peninsula, between the Gulf St Vincent in the west and the Mount Lofty Ranges in the east.
Sitting on the Deule river near the Belgian border, this city is the capital of France's Hauts-de-France region — which city?
Lille: Prefecture and commune in Hauts-de-France, France.
Bounded by the Dniester and Prut rivers, this historical region is now mostly part of Moldova — what is it called?
Bessarabia: Historical region in Moldova and Ukraine. Bessarabia is a historical region in Eastern Europe, bounded by the Dniester river on the east and the Prut river on the west.
As Italy's southernmost point, this Mediterranean island lies just 113 kilometers from Tunisia — which island?
Lampedusa: Italian island in the Mediterranean Sea.
This landlocked Great Plains state borders Canada's Saskatchewan and Manitoba, with Bismarck as its capital and Fargo as its largest city — which state?
North Dakota: U.S. state. North Dakota (də-KOH-tə) is a landlocked U.S. state in the Upper Midwest, named after the indigenous Dakota and Sioux peoples.
Planned in the 1960s by Greek architect Constantinos Doxiadis along the Margalla Hills, this city replaced Karachi as its country's capital in 1967 — which city?
Islamabad: Capital of Pakistan. It is located north of the city of Rawalpindi, the largest in northern Punjab, with which it forms a metropolitan area of over 5.7 million inhabitants.
Founded by the Spanish Empire in 1519 and made Cuba's capital in 1552, this port city once served as a stopping point for treasure galleons returning to Iberia — which city?
Havana: Capital and largest city of Cuba. Havana (US also; Spanish: La Habana [la‿aˈβana]) is the capital and largest city of Cuba.
Founded in 1821 at the meeting point of the White Nile and Blue Nile, which city serves as Sudan's capital?
Khartoum: Capital of Sudan. Khartoum, also spelled Khartum, is the capital city of Sudan as well as Khartoum State.
At 1,791 meters above sea level, this Hindu Kush valley city is one of the highest capital cities on Earth — which Afghan capital is it?
Kabul: Capital and the largest city of Afghanistan.
Home to the tiny nation of Andorra along its crest, which mountain range forms the natural border between France and Spain?
Pyrenees: Range of mountains in southwest Europe.
Nicknamed the Pink City for its terracotta-hued old town, which Rajasthani capital was founded in 1727 by Sawai Jai Singh II?

Existing from 1819 to 1831, this short-lived South American state stretched across present-day Venezuela, Ecuador, Panama, and parts of Peru and Brazil, and claimed the disputed Essequibo region. What state was this?
Gran Colombia: Republic in South and Central America from 1819 to 1831.
Stretching 145 kilometers along Russia's Black Sea coast, this resort city — Europe's longest by territory — hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics — which city?
Sochi: City in Krasnodar Krai, Russia.

Formed after seven rebellious provinces signed the Union of Utrecht and later declared independence from Spain in the Act of Abjuration, this confederation lasted from 1588 until the Batavian Revolution — which state?
Dutch Republic: Predecessor state of the Netherlands (1581–1795)

Built in the 9th century in Central Java, this Buddhist monument features nine stacked platforms topped by a dome ringed with 72 perforated stone stupas, each sheltering a Buddha statue — which site is it?
Borobudur: 9th-century Buddhist temple in Java, Indonesia.
Once known as Pishpek and later renamed Frunze under Soviet rule, this city serves as the capital of Kyrgyzstan and sits near the Kazakh border — name the city?
Bishkek: Capital and largest city of Kyrgyzstan. Bishkek, formerly known as Pishpek (until 1926), and then Frunze (1926–1991), is the capital and largest urban city of Kyrgyzstan.

Named after a British diplomat and known to the local Cowlitz people as Lawetlat'la, this Cascade Range volcano's 1980 eruption remains the most economically destructive volcanic event in U.S. history — name the peak?
Mount St. Helens: Volcano in Washington, U.S. It lies 52 miles (83 km) northeast of Portland, Oregon, and 98 miles (158 km) south of Seattle.
Serving as the shared capital of both Punjab and Haryana, this planned Indian city's master plan was designed by the architect Le Corbusier — name the city?
Chandigarh: Union territory and capital of Punjab and Haryana, India.
Carved into a mountainside in the 13th century BC under Ramesses II, these twin rock-cut temples in Upper Egypt were relocated in 1968 to save them from a rising reservoir. What is this site?
Abu Simbel: UNESCO World Heritage Site in southern Egypt.

Nicknamed the 'city of seven mountains,' this west-coast Norwegian settlement is the country's second-largest city after the capital, with trading there dating back to perhaps the 1020s. What city is it?
Bergen: City and municipality in Vestland, Norway.

Home to a partially restored ziggurat dedicated to a moon god, this Sumerian city-state near the mouth of the Euphrates dates back to around 3800 BC and once had a king named Mesannepada. What ancient city is it?
Ur: Ancient Mesopotamian city-state. The city's patron deity was the moon god Nanna (Sin in Akkadian), and the name of the city is derived from UNUGKI, literally "the abode (of Nanna)".
Its name literally means 'bridge over the Inn,' and this Tyrolean capital was later enriched with the Golden Roof under Emperor Maximilian I — which city?
Innsbruck: Capital city of Tyrol, Austria.

Located on the Tigris near modern-day Mosul, this city served as capital of the Neo-Assyrian Empire until it was sacked by a coalition of Babylonians, Medes, and Scythians in 612 BC — what was it called?
Nineveh: Ancient Assyrian city. Nineveh was an ancient Near Eastern city of Upper Mesopotamia, located in the modern-day city of Mosul in northern Iraq.
The second-largest city in Austria after Vienna, this Styrian capital boasts a historic Altstadt considered one of Central Europe's best-preserved — which city?
Graz: Capital of Styria, Austria. Graz (German: [ɡraːts]) is the capital of the Austrian state of Styria and the second-largest city in Austria, after Vienna.
Historically known in English by its German name of Stettin, this Baltic seaport is the capital of West Pomeranian Voivodeship and Poland's seventh-largest city — which city?
Szczecin: Capital city of West Pomerania, Poland. Szczecin is located on the Oder River, south of the Szczecin Lagoon and the Bay of Pomerania.
Founded by the Almohads in the 12th century and later a haven for Barbary corsairs, this Atlantic coast city became Morocco's capital when the country gained independence in 1956 — which city?
Rabat: Capital city of Morocco. Rabat is the capital city of Morocco, located on the northwestern coasts of the Atlantic Ocean.

Named by a Spanish expedition in 1691 in honor of a Catholic saint, this Texas city became the state's first chartered civil settlement in 1731 and is today the seventh-most populous city in the US — which city?
San Antonio: City in Texas, United States.

The capital of Jalisco state and Mexico's eighth most populous city, this metropolis boasts the country's second-highest population density after Mexico City and anchors the Bajío region's economy — which city?
Guadalajara: City and municipality in Jalisco, Mexico. Guadalajara has the second-highest population density in Mexico with over 10,361 people per km2, surpassed only by Mexico City.
Sitting at 2,850 meters on the slopes of an active volcano, this Andean capital is either the highest or second-highest national capital city in the world — which city?
Quito: Capital city of Ecuador. Quito is in a valley on the eastern slopes of Pichincha, an active stratovolcano in the Andes.
Built around the River Aire in West Yorkshire, this city grew rich on the wool trade before Queen Victoria granted it a city charter in 1893 — which city?
Leeds: City in West Yorkshire, England. The city was a small manorial borough in the 13th century and a market town in the 16th century.

Originally built as Emperor Hadrian's mausoleum in Rome, this cylindrical structure was later converted into a papal fortress dedicated to the Archangel Michael, and was once the city's tallest building. What is it?
Castel Sant'Angelo: Historic building in Rome, Italy.

Sitting in the Yangtze River Delta, this Chinese city served as the capital of various dynasties and republican governments from the 3rd century until 1949, and is now the capital of Jiangsu province. Which city is it?
Nanjing: Capital of Jiangsu, China. It has also been awarded the title of 2008 Habitat Scroll of Honor of China, Special UN Habitat Scroll of Honor Award and National Civilized City.

This historical and cultural region stretching from central Mexico through Guatemala and Belize is where indigenous societies flourished for more than 3,000 years before Spanish colonization — what region is it?
Mesoamerica: Pre-Columbian cultural area in the Americas.
Named for a 'beautiful spring' artesian well and located in Vienna's Hietzing district, this 1,441-room Baroque residence served as the Habsburg rulers' summer retreat — which palace?
Schönbrunn Palace was the main summer residence of the Habsburg rulers, located in Hietzing, the 13th district of Vienna.
Continuously inhabited for over 5,500 years, this city has been Cyprus's capital since the 10th century and remains the last divided capital in Europe — what city is it?
Nicosia: Capital of the Republic of Cyprus. Nicosia, also known as Lefkosia or Lefkoşa, is the capital of Cyprus.
Squeezed between the Andes and the Chilean Coast Range in a double rain shadow, this arid plateau in northern Chile is the driest non-polar place on Earth — what is it?
Atacama Desert: Plateau on Pacific coast of South America.
This coastal Indian city, capital of its Union Territory, sits on the Bay of Bengal and shares much of its culture and language with neighboring Tamil Nadu — name the city?
Pondicherry is the capital and most populous city of the Union Territory of Puducherry in India.

Occupied by Nazi Germany for five years during the Second World War and liberated on May 9, 1945, this island — the second-largest in the Channel Islands — sits about 27 miles off Normandy's coast. Which island is it?
Guernsey: English Channel island near Normandy.
