At 678.9 meters, this Kuala Lumpur skyscraper is the second-tallest building on Earth, trailing only a tower in Dubai — what is it called?
Merdeka 118: Megatall skyscraper in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.
The fifth-most populous city in Japan and the largest one north of Tokyo, this Hokkaido capital was laid out on a grid plan inspired by ancient Kyoto — what city is it?
Sapporo: City in Hokkaido, Japan. It is the fifth-most populous city in Japan and is Hokkaido's cultural, economic, and political center.
This Mexican resort city on the Yucatán Peninsula's Caribbean coast is home to a Hotel Zone and sits just north of the Riviera Maya — what is it?
Cancún: City in Quintana Roo, Mexico.
This volcanic archipelago stretches roughly 1,300 km from Japan's Hokkaido to Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula, separating the Sea of Okhotsk from the Pacific — what is it?
Kuril Islands: Island chain in Northeast Asia.
One of the two historical principalities that founded modern Romania, this region sits north of the Lower Danube and split traditionally into Greater and Lesser sections — what is it?
Wallachia: Principality of Romania from 1330 to 1862.
Purchased by Prince Albert in 1852 and rebuilt to his amended designs, this Aberdeenshire estate was where Queen Elizabeth II died in 2022 — what is it?
Balmoral Castle: Royal residence in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.
Stretching between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea, this range is home to Mount Elbrus, Europe's highest peak — which range?
Caucasus Mountains: Mountain system at the intersection of Europe and Asia.
Founded by the Romans in the late 1st century BC and still Germany's oldest city today, this Moselle-side settlement once served as one of four capitals during the Tetrarchy — which city?
Granted town rights in 1423 and transformed by a textile-manufacturing boom after 1850, which Polish city 120 km southwest of Warsaw is the country's fourth-largest?
Rising in the Tanggula Mountains of the Tibetan Plateau and flowing to the East China Sea, which river is the longest in China and third-longest in the world?
Yangtze: Longest river in Asia. It is the fifth-largest primary river by discharge volume in the world.
Sitting at the Danube's northernmost point and home to the historic Perpetual Diet of the Holy Roman Empire, which Bavarian city's medieval centre became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2006?
Founded in the 8th century BC and sitting at the foot of Mount Etna on Sicily's east coast, which city is the island's second-largest after Palermo?
Catania: City in Sicily, Italy. Despite being the second largest city of the island, Catania is the centre of the most densely populated Sicilian conurbation, which is among the largest in Italy.
Once part of the ancient Dardanian Kingdom and later ruled successively by Byzantine, Bulgarian, Serbian, and Ottoman powers, which city is the capital and largest city of Kosovo?
Pristina: Capital and largest city of Kosovo. Pristina (or Prishtina; UK: PREE-shtin-ə, prish-TEE-nə, US: PRISHT-in-ə) is the capital and largest city of Kosovo.
Connected to mainland Greece by the Isthmus of Corinth and once known as the Morea, which peninsula forms the southernmost region of the Balkans?
Peloponnese: Traditional peninsular region in Greece.
Home to the Avignon papacy in the Middle Ages, and originally the first Roman province beyond the Alps, which southeastern French region has Marseille as its capital?
Provence: Historical province in southeastern France.
Once a fishing town and military base on the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, which Egyptian Red Sea resort city now hosts major international conferences and clubbing?
Sharm El Sheikh: City in Egypt. Its population is approximately 77,000 as of 2017.
Once known as Poona until 1978 and nicknamed the 'Oxford of the East' for its universities, which Maharashtra city is India's seventh most populous metro area?
Pune: City in Maharashtra, India. It is the administrative headquarters of the Pune district, and of Pune division.
Founded in 1728 by a Danish-Norwegian missionary, this is the capital of Greenland and one of the world's smallest national capitals by population — which city?
Nuuk: Capital and largest city of Greenland. Nuuk (Greenlandic pronunciation: [nuːk]; Danish: Godthåb) is the capital and most populous city of Greenland, an autonomous territory of Denmark.
Home to a university founded in 1220 with the oldest medical school still in operation, this southern French city is the country's seventh-largest overall — which city?
Montpellier: Prefecture and commune in Occitania, France.
Spanning parts of northern Israel and southern Lebanon between the Litani River and the Jordan Valley, this region is divided into Upper and Lower halves — which region?
Galilee: Region in northern Israel. Galilee encompasses the area north of the Mount Carmel-Mount Gilboa ridge and south of the east-west section of the Litani River.
The capital of Heilongjiang province, this Chinese metropolis is the eighth most populous city in the country and a key industrial hub of the northeast — which city?
Harbin: Capital of Heilongjiang, China. Harbin has direct jurisdiction over nine metropolitan districts, two county-level cities, and seven counties.
This Italian city served as the last capital of the Western Roman Empire before its fall in 476, later becoming the ruling seat of the Ostrogoths and Byzantines — which city?
Once a small town that boomed as a coal-exporting port, this city was officially declared the capital of Wales in 1955 — which city?
Cardiff: Capital and largest city of Wales. Cardiff had a population of 383,919 in 2024 and forms a principal area officially known as the City and County of Cardiff (Welsh: Dinas a Sir Caerdydd).
Home to a giant panda research base and designated a UNESCO City of Gastronomy in 2011, this city is the capital of Sichuan province — which city?
Chengdu: Capital of Sichuan, China. The surrounding Chengdu Plain is known as the "Country of Heaven" and the "Land of Abundance".
This tiny Spanish city on Morocco's coast belonged to the province of Malaga until becoming autonomous in 1995 — which enclave?
Melilla: Spanish autonomous city in northwestern Africa.
Made up of 33 local districts and bordered by Essex, Kent, Surrey, and Hertfordshire, this administrative area covers the UK capital's entire urban sprawl — which region?
Greater London: Metropolitan area in England.

Explored by Leif Erikson around AD 1000 — nearly five centuries before Columbus — this coastal North American region beyond Greenland was later confirmed by a Norse site found at L'Anse aux Meadows in 1960 — what was it called?
Vinland: Area of coastal Canada explored by Norse Vikings.
Bounded by the Balkan Mountains, the Aegean, and the Black Sea, this Southeast European region today spans parts of Bulgaria, Greece, and Turkey — what is it called?
Thrace: Geographical and historical region in Southeast Europe.
Sitting atop some of Earth's largest nickel deposits and 300 km north of the Arctic Circle, this Russian city is the world's northernmost with over 175,000 residents — which city?
Norilsk: City in Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russia.
Bounded not by land but by four ocean currents forming a gyre, this Atlantic region is known for its calm blue waters and drifting brown seaweed, with Bermuda near its edge — what is it called?
Sargasso Sea: Region of the North Atlantic Ocean. It is the only named sea without land boundaries.
Straddling the Arno River in Tuscany, this Italian city is famous for its tilting bell tower and is home to a university dating back to the 12th century — which city?
This Uttar Pradesh capital, home to 2.8 million people per the 2011 census, forms a heritage arc with Agra and Varanasi and traces its roots to the ancient region of Kosala — which city?
Lucknow: Capital of Uttar Pradesh, India. It is an important centre of education, commerce, aerospace, finance, pharmaceuticals, information technology, design, culture, tourism, music, and poetry.
Once called Petrovskoye and then Port-Petrovsk, this Caspian Sea port is the capital of Dagestan and the largest city in the North Caucasus. What is it?
Makhachkala: City in Dagestan, Russia. The city is extremely ethnically diverse, with a minor ethnic Russian population.
This city in Italy's Veneto region sits on the Bacchiglione River and inspired poetry from Petrarch and Shelley thanks to its nearby Euganean Hills. What city is it?
Padua: City in Veneto, Italy. Padua ( PAD-ew-ə; Italian: Padova) is a city and comune (municipality) in Veneto, northern Italy, and the capital of the province of Padua.
Named after an ancient seaport destroyed in 1270 and originally founded in 1949 as Migdal, this Israeli coastal city sits just north of the Gaza Strip border — what is it?
Ashkelon: City in Israel. The modern city is named after the ancient seaport of Ascalon, which was destroyed in 1270 and whose remains are on the southwestern edge of the modern metropolis.

Originally built as a retirement home and hospital for wounded soldiers, this Paris military complex includes a domed chapel that ranks as the tallest church in the city and now serves as a shrine to French military heroes — what is it?
Les Invalides: Building complex in Paris, France.
Founded in 300 BC by a successor of Alexander the Great on the Orontes River, this city became capital of the Seleucid Empire and later a Crusader principality?
Antioch: Hellenistic city, modern Antakya, Turkey.
Lying about 30 kilometers southeast of another French Caribbean island, this overseas collectivity voted to secede from Guadeloupe in 2003?
Saint Barthélemy: Overseas collectivity of France. Saint Barthélemy, officially the Territorial Collectivity of Saint Barthélemy, also known as St.
Named for a mythological Titan, this North African range separates the Sahara from the Mediterranean and stretches through Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia — which range?
Atlas Mountains: North African mountain range. The range's highest peak is Toubkal, in central Morocco, with an elevation of 4,167 metres (13,671 ft).
Sitting at the confluence of the Tonlé Sap and Mekong rivers, this city has been Cambodia's capital since 1865 and was once nicknamed the 'Pearl of Asia' — which city?
Phnom Penh: Capital of Cambodia. It has been the national capital since 1865 and has grown to become the nation's primate city and its political, economic, industrial, and cultural centre.
Stretching across four Nordic countries mostly north of the Arctic Circle, this cultural homeland of the Sámi people has never been a sovereign state — what is it called?
Sápmi: Sámi cultural region of Fennoscandia.
Home to 17 major tribes each with distinct customs and languages, this northeastern Indian state has its capital at Kohima and borders Myanmar to the east — which state?
Nagaland: State in northeastern India. Its capital city is Kohima and its largest city is the twin Chümoukedima–Dimapur.
Located about 40 km northeast of Milan at the foot of its namesake Alps, which Lombard city's historic walled core is known as the 'Upper Town'?
This South Yorkshire city fueled a tenfold population boom in the 19th century after pioneering processes for crucible and stainless steel used in its cutlery trade — which city?
Sheffield: City in South Yorkshire, England. Sheffield is a city in South Yorkshire, England, situated 29 miles (47 km) south of Leeds and 32 miles (51 km) east of Manchester.
Founded in 1884 on the shores of the Beagle Channel, this Argentine city claims the title of the world's southernmost city — which city?
Ushuaia: City and port in Tierra del Fuego, Argentina.
Home to the first European fort built in the Americas, this Caribbean island split between Spanish- and French/Creole-speaking nations lies between Cuba and Puerto Rico — which island?
Hispaniola: Caribbean island shared by the Dominican Republic and Haiti.
Built along Hakata Bay as the nearest of Japan's main islands to the Asian mainland, which Kyushu city has served as a gateway for international trade since ancient times?
Fukuoka: Prefecture capital and Designated city in Kyushu, Japan.
Sitting on the westernmost point of mainland Africa, this city replaced Saint-Louis as the capital of French West Africa in 1902 — what is it?
Dakar: Capital and the largest city of Senegal.
Known today by the ruins of Warka in Iraq, this Sumerian city was home to as many as 50,000 people around 3100 BC, making it the largest urban area on Earth at the time — what was its name?
Uruk: Ancient city of Sumer and Babylonia.
Rising in the Giant Mountains of the Czech Republic, this river flows through Bohemia and Germany before reaching the North Sea near Hamburg — which river is it?
Elbe: Major river in Central Europe.
Founded as a 16th-century village, this southern Polish city boomed after rich coal reserves were discovered nearby, industrializing it into a steel-making hub — what city is it?
Katowice: City county in Silesian Voivodeship, Poland.
Sitting on the River Havel just southwest of Berlin, this city was home to Prussian kings and the German Emperor until 1918 — what is it?
Once the capital of the Inca Empire, this Peruvian city near the Sacred Valley is home to the ancient hilltop fortress of Sacsayhuamán and was named a World Heritage Site in 1983 — what city is it?
Cusco: City in Peru. It is the capital and largest city of the eponymous Cusco Province and Cusco Department.
Located in the Someșul Mic river valley and considered the unofficial capital of Transylvania, this is Romania's second-most populous city — name it?
Cluj-Napoca is a city in northwestern Romania. The Cluj-Napoca metropolitan area had a population of 411,379 people, while the population of the peri-urban area is approximately 420,000.
Once known as Chang'an and home to the 3rd-century BC Terracotta Army, this city served as capital under dynasties from the Zhou to the Tang and sat at the end of the Silk Road — what is it?
Sitting on the Gulf of Thailand about 150 kilometers southeast of Bangkok, this city is the second-largest in Chonburi province and part of Thailand's industrial Eastern Seaboard zone — what is it?
Pattaya: City in Chonburi, Thailand. It is on the east coast of the Gulf of Thailand, about 150 kilometres (93 mi) southeast of Bangkok, and has a population of 351,391 as of 2025.
The largest city and former capital of Ivory Coast, this metropolis is the most populous French-speaking city in all of West Africa — what is it?
Abidjan: Largest city and district of Ivory Coast. Abidjan ( AB-ih-JAHN, French: [abidʒɑ̃]; N'ko: ߊߓߌߖߊ߲߬) is the largest city and the former capital of Ivory Coast.
Rising in the Tibetan Plateau and known as the Lancang in China, this transboundary river flows through Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam — what is it?
Mekong: Major river in Southeast Asia.

With a surface area of nearly 60,000 square kilometers, this African Great Lake is the continent's largest lake, the world's largest tropical lake, and trails only a North American lake for freshwater surface area — which lake?
Lake Victoria is one of the African Great Lakes.
This German federal highway network is famous for having no speed limit on many stretches, though an advisory limit of 130 km/h (81 mph) applies — what is it called?
Home to Germany's Federal Constitutional Court and Federal Court of Justice, which city on the Rhine near the French border is the nation's legal center?
The third-largest and southernmost of Japan's four main islands, this land mass covers over 36,000 square kilometers and was historically administered from Dazaifu — which island is it?
Kyushu: Island and region of Japan. Kyushu (九州, Kyūshū; pronounced [kʲɯꜜː.ɕɯː], lit. 'nine provinces') is the third-largest and most southerly of Japan's four main islands.

Home to cities like Lahore, Faisalabad, and Amritsar and settled along five rivers since the ancient Indus Valley civilization, which South Asian region straddles modern Pakistan and northwestern India?
Punjab: Geographical region in South Asia.
Known as Titograd from 1946 to 1992 in honor of Yugoslavia's leader, this city sits at the confluence of the Ribnica and Morača rivers and serves as Montenegro's capital — what's it called?
Podgorica: Capital and largest city of Montenegro. The city is just north of Lake Skadar and close to coastal destinations on the Adriatic Sea.
Founded by the Romans in 15 BC and named for Emperor Augustus, this Bavarian city was later home to the powerful Fugger and Welser banking families — which city?
Sitting at the confluence of the Rhine and Neckar rivers, this is the second-largest city in Baden-Württemberg after Stuttgart — which city?
Mannheim: City in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. It is located at the border with Rhineland-Palatinate.
Connected to the Black Sea by the narrow Strait of Kerch, this shallow inland sea is bordered by Russia and Ukraine and serves as a route to Central Asia via the Volga-Don Canal — which sea?
Sea of Azov: Inland sea in eastern Europe.
Known as the 'Olympic capital,' this Swiss city on the shores of Lake Geneva is also where the country's Federal Supreme Court convenes — which city?
Lausanne: City in Switzerland. Lausanne ( loh-ZAN, US also loh-ZAHN; French: [lozan]) is the capital and largest city of the Swiss French-speaking canton of Vaud, in Switzerland.
Croatia's third-largest city and chief seaport, this Adriatic port on Kvarner Bay was fought over for centuries by Venice, the Habsburgs, Italy, and Yugoslavia — which city?
Rijeka: City in Primorje-Gorski Kotar County, Croatia.
Founded as a fortress on Ivan the Terrible's orders in 1574, this Russian city of over a million is now Bashkortostan's capital and an oil-refining hub — which city?
Ufa: Capital of Bashkortostan, Russia. Ufa is the tenth-most populous city in Russia, and the fourth-most populous city in the Volga Federal District.
This 777-kilometre river rises near Dijon and flows through Paris before emptying into the English Channel at Le Havre — which river?
Seine: Major river in northern France.
Often cited as the richest city in Latin America, this Mexican metropolis sits at the foothills of the Sierra Madre Oriental as the capital of Nuevo León — which city?
Monterrey: City in Nuevo León, Mexico. Monterrey (MON-tə-RAY; Spanish: [monteˈrej]) is the capital and largest city of the northeastern Mexican state of Nuevo León.
Known historically as Zara and traced to a 9th-century-BC Liburnian settlement, this Adriatic city is the oldest continuously inhabited one in Croatia — which city?
Zadar: City in Croatia. It is situated on the Adriatic Sea, at the northwestern part of Ravni Kotari region.
Sitting where the River Danube meets a small stream called the Blau, this German city on the Bavarian border is the sixth-largest in Baden-Württemberg — what is it?
Ulm: City in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. The mouth of the Iller also falls within Ulm's city limits.

Commissioned by a Catalan industrialist and designed by architect Antoni Gaudí on Barcelona's Turó del Carmel hill, this complex of parks and gardens overlooks the city from the Gràcia district — which park?
Park Güell is a complex of parks and gardens in Barcelona with architectural elements, located in the La Salut neighborhood of the Grcia district in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.
In this region surrounding the equator, the sun can appear directly overhead, giving it the planet's smallest seasonal temperature swings and rainfall-defined seasons instead — which zone?
Tropics: Region of Earth surrounding the Equator. Because of Earth's axial tilt, the width of the tropics (in latitude) is twice the tilt.
This Hanseatic city on Germany's Baltic coast sits where the Trave River reaches the sea, giving Hamburg its closest access point to the Baltic — which city?
This English actor broke out in the second season of a satirical HBO anthology set at a luxury resort, then starred in a Netflix miniseries and a Bridget Jones sequel. Who is he?
Macedonia (region) is a geographical and historical region of the Balkan Peninsula in Southeast Europe.
Home to the world's oldest bank, still operating since 1472, this Tuscan city gave rise to Renaissance and Medieval painters like Duccio and Simone Martini — what city is it?
Nicknamed the Ruhr region's 'secret capital,' this German city sits where the Ruhr River is dammed to form two lakes, Baldeney and Kettwig — what city is it?
Essen: City in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.

Believed to be the birthplace of settled farming, this Middle Eastern region stretching from Iraq to Lebanon saw the earliest rise of writing, the wheel, and irrigation in Mesopotamia — what's it called?
Fertile Crescent: Region of the Middle East.

Seized by the newly formed German Empire after the Franco-Prussian War in 1871 and returned to France only after World War I, this Rhine Valley border territory's loss fueled French resentment before the Great War — what's the region?
Alsace–Lorraine: 1871–1918 territory of the German Empire. It was established in 1871 by the German Empire after it had occupied the region during the Franco-Prussian War.
Home to the ancient Kerma culture and later the Kingdom of Kush, whose king Piye conquered Egypt to become its 25th Dynasty, this Nile region stretched between Khartoum and Aswan — what's it called?
Nubia: Region in northern Sudan and southern Egypt.

Nicknamed 'The Rock,' this maximum-security island prison in San Francisco Bay began as a U.S. Army military lockup before the Justice Department took it over in 1933, its cold currents supposedly making escape impossible — what's the prison?
Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary: Former island prison in San Francisco Bay. The site of a fort since the 1850s, the main prison building was built from 1910 to 1912 as a U.S.
Formed from the merger of three historic towns at the confluence of the Yangtze and Han rivers, this Hubei capital was the site of a 1911 uprising that toppled China's last dynasty — which city?
Wuhan: Capital of Hubei, China. It is also one of China's nine national central cities.
Known as Tourane during French colonial rule, this Vietnamese port city hosted the 2017 APEC summit and is the country's fourth largest by population — which city?
Da Nang: Municipality in central Vietnam.
Nicknamed the 'Scotland of the East' by British colonial authorities, this northeastern Indian state with capital Shillong follows a matrilineal system — which state?
Meghalaya: State in northeastern India. Meghalaya (lit. "the abode of clouds") is a state in northeast India, with Shillong as its capital city.
Home to ethnic German speakers in the borderlands of Bohemia and Moravia, this region was annexed by Nazi Germany following the 1938 Munich Agreement — what was it called?
Sudetenland: Historical name for areas of Czechoslovakia.
Named after its central city of York, this Northern English county takes in Leeds, Sheffield, Bradford, and the wild moorland of the Dales — which historic county?
Yorkshire: Historic county of England. Yorkshire ( YORK-shər, -⁠sheer) is an area of Northern England which was historically a county.
Named for the ring they form around the sacred island of Delos, this Aegean island group's largest island is Naxos though Syros is the most populated — which archipelago?
Cyclades: Greek island group in the Aegean Sea.
The westernmost city in Mexico, this Baja California metropolis sits just across the border from San Diego and had grown to roughly 2.3 million people by 2024 — which city?
Tijuana: Largest city in Baja California, Mexico. Tijuana is the most populous city of the Mexican state of Baja California, located on the northwestern Pacific Coast of Mexico.
A treaty port since 1860 and the seat of a provisional government during the Boxer Rebellion, this walled Chinese city on the Bohai Sea was first built in 1404 — which city?
Known locally as Xamar, this Indian Ocean port city controlled the medieval gold trade as capital of a sultanate from the 9th to 13th centuries — which capital is it?
Mogadishu: Capital and the largest city of Somalia.
Nicknamed the 'Capital of the Alps,' this French city sits where the Drac River meets the Isère, and its metro area is the largest in the entire mountain range — which city?
Grenoble: Prefecture and commune in Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, France.
This Seine-side city in Normandy was once a medieval capital of the Anglo-Norman dynasty and the site where Joan of Arc was put on trial — which French city?
Rouen: Prefecture and commune in Normandy, France.
Stretching along the Adriatic from the island of Rab down to the Bay of Kotor, this historical region's largest city is Split, followed by Zadar and Dubrovnik — which region?
Dalmatia: Historical region in Croatia and Montenegro.

For nearly 500 years, pharaohs and nobles of Egypt's New Kingdom were buried in rock-cut tombs carved into this wadi opposite Luxor, including one chamber complex with over 120 rooms for the sons of Ramesses II. What is this burial site?
Valley of the Kings: Necropolis in ancient Egypt.

Flowing from the Armenian Highlands past Mosul, Tikrit, Samarra, and Baghdad before merging with the Euphrates, this river nurtured the ancient Assyrian Empire and is used for baptism by the Mandaean faith today. What river is this?
Tigris: River in Turkey, Iraq, and Syria.
Claimed to be the longest city in Europe, this Ukrainian city sits at the confluence of two rivers and grew rich on 1880s iron-ore investment from Belgium, France and Britain — which city is it?
Kryvyi Rih: City in Ukraine. It hosts the administration of Kryvyi Rih Raion and its subordinate Kryvyi Rih urban hromada in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast.
Home to an ancient citadel and inhabited since the 5th millennium BC, this is the capital of Iraq's Kurdistan Region — which city is it?
Erbil: Capital of Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Erbil is described as the region's cultural, economic, industrial, educational and medical hub.

This Welsh village on Anglesey, next to the Britannia Bridge, is often shortened for convenience but officially carries a 58-character, 18-syllable name — one of the longest place names on Earth. Where is it?
Llanfairpwllgwyngyll: Village on the Isle of Anglesey, Wales.

Serving as Sri Lanka's judicial and financial capital along its west coast, this city retained its status as the country's seat of government even after independence in 1948, only ceding administrative functions decades later — which city is it?
Colombo: Most populous city of Sri Lanka.

Built between the ancient Greek cities of Amathus and Kourion, this coastal city is Cyprus's most populous municipality and was named a top up-and-coming destination by TripAdvisor in 2014 — which city is it?
Limassol: City in Cyprus. Limassol, also known as Lemesos, is a city on the southern coast of Cyprus.

This North Atlantic archipelago off Europe's northwest coast contains Great Britain, Ireland, the Hebrides, Orkney, and Shetland, and is home to two sovereign nations and nearly 75 million people — what is this group of islands called?

British Isles: Archipelago in north-western Europe. Under the UK Interpretation Act 1978, the Channel Islands are clarified as forming part of the British Islands, not to be confused with the British Isles.
This German city hosted the 1648 signing of the treaties ending the Thirty Years' War, and today calls itself the country's bicycle capital thanks to its huge student population. Which city?
Münster: City in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.
This Indian city on the Yamuna River became the Mughal Empire's capital under emperors from Babur to Shah Jahan and is home to a namesake fort?
Agra: Metropolis in Uttar Pradesh, India.
Known as Fiumicino until 1933, this shallow Italian river was famously crossed by Julius Caesar in 49 BC, defying Roman law?
Nicknamed 'Lion Rock,' this ancient Sri Lankan fortress was built atop a 180-meter granite column by a king in the 5th century?
Sigiriya: Ancient rock fortress near Dambulla, Sri Lanka.
Grown from a small fishing village into a sprawling 40-kilometer resort strip on Egypt's Red Sea coast, this city serves as capital of the Red Sea Governorate — which city?
Hurghada: Capital of the Red Sea Egyptian Governorate. Hurghada has grown from a small fishing village to one of the largest resort destinations along the Red Sea coast, stretching close to 40 km.
Home to seven successive popes between 1309 and 1377, this southern French city on the Rhône was purchased by Pope Clement VI from Joanna I of Naples in 1348 — which city?
Avignon: Prefecture of Vaucluse, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France.
Rebuilt in white marble under a 'White City' renewal project after a devastating 1948 earthquake, this Central Asian capital sits between a desert and a mountain range. Which city?
Ashgabat: Capital and largest city of Turkmenistan.
This city on the Sunzha River, capital of Chechnya, grew from a 2002 population of about 210,000 to over 328,000 by 2021 — which city is it?
Grozny: Capital of Chechnya, Russia. Grozny (Russian: Грозный, IPA: [ˈgroznɨj]; Chechen: Соьлжа-ГӀала, romanised: Sölƶa-Ġala) is the capital city of Chechnya, Russia.

Surrounding the South Pole and directly opposite the Arctic, this polar region encompasses a continent, the Kerguelen Plateau, and various island territories governed by an international treaty — what is it?
Antarctic: Polar region around Earth's South Pole.
Situated where the Meuse meets the Ourthe in eastern Belgium's Wallonia region, this city gives its name to a whole province — what is it?
Liège (lee-EZH, lee-AYZH) is a city and municipality in the Belgian region of Wallonia, and the capital of the eponymous province.
Two horizontal stripes, white above red, colors officially adopted in 1831 though tied to a royal white eagle since the Middle Ages — this is the banner of which country?
Flag of Poland (flaga Polski) consists of two horizontal stripes of equal width, the upper one white and the lower one red.
Traditionally the site where French kings were crowned, this city's cathedral once housed a holy vial of anointing oil said to have been delivered by a dove — which city?
Reims: Subprefecture and commune in Grand Est, France.
A seaport on Mexico's Pacific coast, this city became Mexico's largest beach resort and a favorite 1940s–1960s getaway for Hollywood stars — which city?
Acapulco: City in the Mexican state of Guerrero.
Stormed by a Paris crowd on 14 July 1789, this eight-towered fortress-turned-state-prison became the defining symbol of the French Revolution — what was it?
Perched on a lake of the same name near the Alps, this Lombardy city is home to Villa Olmo and a Duomo overlooking the water — which city?
Mexico's northwesternmost state, this became a state in 1952 and covers the northern half of a peninsula bordering the U.S., with Guadalupe Island also part of its territory — which state?
Baja California: State of Mexico. Before becoming a state in 1952, the area was known as the North Territory of Baja California (Territorio Norte de Baja California).
Standing 309.6 metres tall and designed by Renzo Piano, this pyramid-shaped skyscraper in Southwark is the tallest building in the UK and Western Europe — what is it?
The Shard: Skyscraper in London, England.
This Adriatic seaside resort in Emilia-Romagna opened Europe's first bathing establishment in 1843 and is the birthplace of film director Federico Fellini — what city is it?
Rimini: City in Emilia-Romagna, Italy. Rimini ( RIM-in-ee, Italian: [ˈriːmini]; Romagnol: Rémin or Rémne; Latin: Ariminum) is a city in the Emilia-Romagna region of Northern Italy.
This ceremonial county in the East of England is separated from Kent by the Thames Estuary, and its largest town is Southend-on-Sea — which county is it?
Essex: County of England. The county has an area of 3,670 km2 (1,420 sq mi) and had an estimated population of 1,929,610 in 2024.
Separated from Asia Minor by a narrow strait, this Greek island is the third largest in the country and home to the capital city of Mytilene — which island is it?
Lesbos: Greek island in the North Aegean.
Named for the Spanish word for 'reddish' due to its heavy silt load, this 1,450-mile river carves through the Grand Canyon on its way from the Rocky Mountains to Lake Mead — which river?
Colorado River is one of the principal rivers (along with the Rio Grande) in the Southwestern United States and in northern Mexico.
Featuring a green field with the Islamic creed in white Arabic script above a sword, this national banner has been used since March 1973 — which country's is it?
Flag of Saudi Arabia is a green background with Arabic inscription and a sword in white.
This resort town in the easternmost Dominican Republic draws more visitors than any other city in the Caribbean, and its airport handles 64% of the country's arriving flights — where is it?
Punta Cana: Resort town in La Altagracia Province, Dominican Republic.
Bounded by Taiwan, the Philippines, Borneo, and the Indochinese Peninsula, this marginal body of water saw $3.4 trillion of shipping pass through it in 2016 — which one is it?
South China Sea: Marginal sea of the Western Pacific Ocean.
Named after a series of forts from the Second Seminole War, this Broward County seat sits 30 miles north of Miami along the Atlantic — what city is it?
Fort Lauderdale, Florida is a coastal city located in the U.S.
Home to the reclusive Sentinelese people who are legally off-limits to visitors, this 200-isle archipelago in the Indian Ocean sits southwest of Myanmar — which one?
Andaman Islands: Indian archipelago in the Bay of Bengal.

Founded in 756 BC as a Greek colony called Trapezous, this Black Sea port in northeastern Turkey served for over two centuries as capital of the Empire of Trebizond before falling to Ottoman rule in 1461 — which city?
Trabzon: City in Turkey. Trabzon (Turkish pronunciation: [tɾɑbzon]) is a city on the Black Sea coast of northeastern Turkey and the capital of Trabzon Province.
A horizontal tricolour of red, white, and blue descended from the 16th-century orange-white-blue Prinsenvlag, this banner is the oldest tricolour in continuous use — which one?
Flag of the Netherlands is a horizontal tricolour of red, white, and blue. The national flag of the Netherlands (Dutch: de Nederlandse vlag) is a horizontal tricolour of red, white, and blue.
The capital of South Tyrol in northern Italy, this city tied with Bologna for first place in a 2020 Italian quality-of-life ranking and was named a UNESCO City of Music in 2023 — which one?

Bolzano: Capital city of the province of South Tyrol, Northern Italy. Bolzano, also known as Bozen (see § Names), is the capital city of South Tyrol, officially the province of Bolzano/Bozen, in northern Italy.
Founded by German emigrants in post-WWII Chile, this secretive settlement led by fugitive preacher Paul Schäfer became a byword for abuse under Pinochet's dictatorship — what was it called?
Colonia Dignidad: Secretive colony founded by Germans in Chile, formerly torture center.
This city replaced Lagos as Nigeria's capital in December 1991 and sits beside a 400-metre monolith known as Aso Rock — which city?
Abuja: Capital of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.
Nicknamed 'Killer Mountain' for its high climber fatality rate, this ninth-highest peak on Earth marks the western anchor of the Himalayas — which mountain?
Nanga Parbat: 9th-highest mountain on Earth. Nanga Parbat, known in Shina as Diamer, is the ninth-highest mountain on Earth with its summit at 8,126 m (26,660 ft) above sea level.
Comprising Donetsk and Luhansk Oblasts, roughly 90 percent of this contested Ukrainian border region was under Russian military control as of late 2025 — which region?
Once part of Guangdong province until 1988, this island whose name means 'South of the Sea' was designated a special economic zone by Deng Xiaoping — which Chinese province?
Hainan: Province of China. The Hlai are recognized by the Chinese government as one of the country's 56 ethnic groups.
Named for the bridge keepers who once guarded its Ottoman-era Old Bridge over the Neretva River, this Bosnian city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — which city?
Mostar: City in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Germany's largest city on the Baltic Sea, this Schleswig-Holstein capital hosts the terminus of the world's busiest artificial waterway — what city is it?
Kiel: German city, capital of Schleswig-Holstein. Kiel ( KEEL; German: [kiːl]) is the capital and most populous city in the northern German state of Schleswig-Holstein.
With 84.53% forest cover — the fourth-highest of any Indian state — this northeastern state bordering both Bangladesh and Myanmar is also its region's most urbanised — which state?
Mizoram: State in Northeast India, India.
Located in Thailand's northern highlands about 700 km from Bangkok, this walled, moat-ringed city's name literally translates to 'new city' — which city is it?
Chiang Mai: City in Thailand. Chiang Mai is the largest city in northern Thailand, the capital of Chiang Mai province and the second-largest city in Thailand by urban population.
This ancient Mediterranean port, settled since the Early Bronze Age, features in the biblical story of Jonah and the Greek legend of Andromeda — what city, now part of Tel Aviv, is it?
Jaffa: Ancient port and city in Tel Aviv, Israel. The city sits atop a naturally elevated outcrop on the Mediterranean coastline.
Japan's seventh-largest city and third-busiest port after Tokyo and Yokohama, this Kansai metropolis traces its Ikuta Shrine back to a legendary empress in AD 201 — which city is it?
Kobe: City in Kansai region, Japan. With a population of around 1.5 million, Kobe is Japan's seventh-largest city and the third-largest port city after Tokyo and Yokohama.
Bordered by Greater London, Kent, and Hampshire, this South East England ceremonial county's largest settlement is Woking, with Guildford anchoring its center — what is it?
Surrey: County of England. It is bordered by Greater London to the northeast, Kent to the east, East and West Sussex to the south, and Hampshire and Berkshire to the west.
Operating for nearly a thousand years near ancient Rajagriha in what is now Bihar, this Buddhist monastic complex is often called the world's first residential university — what is it?
Nalanda mahavihara: Buddhist monastery and centre of learning in India.
Created in 1815 as a successor to Napoleon's Duchy of Warsaw, this semi-autonomous kingdom fell under Russian control until a German-run regency replaced it in 1915 — what was it?
Congress Poland: Semi-autonomous polity (1815–1915). It was established when the French ceded a part of Polish territory to the Russian Empire following France's defeat in the Napoleonic Wars.
One of the three historical Czech lands alongside Bohemia and Czech Silesia, this eastern region was a crown land of the Holy Roman Empire for centuries — what region is it?
Moravia: Historical region in the Czech Republic. Moravia was one of the five lands of Czechoslovakia founded in 1918.
Formerly known as Thebes and nicknamed the 'City of a Hundred Gates,' this Egyptian city sits across the Nile from the Valley of the Kings — which city is it?

This UNESCO World Heritage rock-cut complex in India includes over 100 excavations combining Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain shrines, with its largest chamber housing the world's biggest single monolithic rock temple — what site is this?
Ellora Caves: Ancient cave temples in Maharashtra, India.

Mentioned in the Ramayana as a sacred site, this fortified city served as capital of the Vijayanagara Empire from 1336 until its abandonment in 1565, and is now a UNESCO World Heritage ruin in Karnataka — what site is this?
Hampi: Ancient and medieval monuments, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Karnataka, India.
This Swiss city on the shores of a lake of the same name is known for the wooden Chapel Bridge and its views of Mounts Pilatus and Rigi — which city?
Lucerne: City in Switzerland. Lucerne is the capital of the canton of Lucerne and part of the district of the same name.
Home to Islam's two holiest cities and bordered by the Red Sea, this historical region of western Saudi Arabia is also the kingdom's most populous area — what region is this?
Hejaz: Geographic region of the Arabian Peninsula.
Located on the Hudson River's west bank about ten miles south of its confluence with the Mohawk, this state capital had a population just over 99,000 at the 2020 census — which city?
Albany, New York is the capital city of the U.S. It is also the county seat of, and the most populous city in Albany County.

Lithuania's second-largest city served as the country's temporary capital from 1920 to 1939 while its usual capital was under Polish control, and is celebrated for its Art Deco architecture — which city?
Kaunas: Second-largest city in Lithuania. Kaunas was the largest city and the centre of Kaunas County in the Duchy of Trakai of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and Trakai Palatinate since 1413.
Known until 1888 as El Paso del Norte, this Mexican border city sits across the Rio Grande from its Texas twin, forming the second-largest binational metro area after San Diego–Tijuana — which city?
Ciudad Juárez: City in Chihuahua, Mexico.
Coined by explorer Amerigo Vespucci in a 16th-century pamphlet, this term described the Americas as previously unknown continents, distinct from Africa, Asia and Europe — what was the term?
New World: Majority of lands of the Western Hemisphere.
Known as Iconium in antiquity and today home to the Whirling Dervishes' Mevlevi Order, this Turkish city was once capital of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum — which city?
Konya: Metropolitan municipality in Central Anatolia, Turkey.
Nicknamed the 'Island of the Winds' for its fierce gusts, this Cycladic island is famed today for its vibrant nightlife — which Greek island?
Mykonos: Greek island. Mykonos (UK also; Greek: Μύκονος [ˈmikonos]) is a Greek island, part of the Cyclades, lying between Tinos, Syros, Paros and Naxos.
One of the most densely populated cities on Earth, this island-nation capital was once a walled royal seat known as Mahal before its palace was torn down under a modern president — which capital?
Malé: Capital of the Maldives. The city is geographically located in the southern edge of North Malé Atoll (Kaafu Atoll).
Nicknamed the 'Pearl of the French Alps,' this French city sits on the northern tip of its namesake lake just 35 kilometers south of Geneva — which city?
Annecy: Prefecture of Haute-Savoie, Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, France.
This southern Israeli desert is home to the resort city of Eilat at its southern tip, and to the kibbutz where Israel's first prime minister retired — which desert?
Negev: Desert in southern Israel. Today, it forms the bulk of the Southern District of Israel, whose largest city and administrative capital is Beersheba (pop. 223,587), in the north of the Negev.
Split into a 'Greater' and 'Lesser' portion, this Caribbean archipelago includes Cuba, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico — what is it called?
Antilles: Archipelago bordering the north and east of the Caribbean Sea.

Developed by Larry Silverstein and designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, this 52-story Lower Manhattan office tower replaced a building destroyed in the September 11 attacks and was completed in 2006 — what is it?
7 World Trade Center: Office building in Manhattan, New York.

Sitting at the confluence of the Ille and Vilaine rivers, this prefecture of Brittany was once known by the Gallic name Condate and served as the region's parliamentary seat for centuries — what city is it?
Rennes: Prefecture and commune in Brittany, France.

First recorded in 805 in a capitulary of Charlemagne, this Elbe river city became the capital of Saxony-Anhalt and lent its name to a set of town-law codes that spread across Central and Eastern Europe — what city is it?

Magdeburg: Capital city of Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Magdeburg (MAG-də-burg, German: [ˈmakdəbʊʁk], locally [ˈmaχdəbʊɐ̯ç]; Low Saxon: Meideborg [ˈmaˑɪ̯debɔɐ̯x]) is the capital of the German state of Saxony-Anhalt.
Nicknamed 'Snake Island,' this isolated spot off Brazil's coast is the only wild home of the critically endangered golden lancehead pit viper — where is it?
Ilha da Queimada Grande: Island off the coast of Brazil. Ilha da Queimada Grande, more commonly referred to as Snake Island, is an island off the coast of Brazil in the Atlantic Ocean.
Sitting on the Tigris beside the ruins of ancient Nineveh, this is Iraq's second-largest city after Baghdad — what is it?
Mosul: City in Nineveh Governorate, Iraq. Mosul is a major city in northern Iraq, serving as the capital of Nineveh Governorate.
Split today between Germany and Poland along the southern Baltic coast, this historical region includes Kashubia and stretches east to the Vistula River — what is it?
Pomerania: Historical region on the southern shore of the Baltic Sea in Central Europe.

Surrounded entirely by Soviet-controlled territory during the Cold War, this politically isolated enclave was claimed by — but not legally part of — the Federal Republic of Germany until reunification in 1990 — what was this territory called?
This historical region of the Iranian Plateau once stretched from the Caspian coast to the Pamir Mountains, taking in parts of modern Afghanistan, Iran, and Central Asia — what was it called?
Khorasan: Historical region of Greater Iran. The extent of the region referred to as Khorasan varied over time.
Bordered by Cumbria, the Yorkshires, Greater Manchester and the Irish Sea, this North West England county's largest settlement is the city of Preston — which county?
Lancashire: County of England. Lancashire ( LANG-kə-shər, -⁠sheer; abbreviated Lancs) is a ceremonial county in North West England.
Nicknamed the 'New York of the Mediterranean' for its forest of beachfront skyscrapers, this Spanish resort city has drawn sunseekers since the 1950s — which city?
Benidorm: City and municipality in Spain.
Sitting on the Rhine opposite Mainz and nestled in a famous wine-growing region, this city serves as the capital of the German state of Hesse — which city?
Wiesbaden: Capital of Hesse, Germany. Wiesbaden forms a conurbation with a population of around 500,000 with the neighbouring city of Mainz.
Home to the birthplaces of both a global electronics giant and a well-known truck manufacturer, this Dutch city is the largest outside the Randstad conurbation — which city?
Eindhoven: City and municipality in North Brabant, Netherlands.
As Kerala's capital, this city is one of the few in the world to house both an international airport and an international seaport within its limits — which city?
Thiruvananthapuram: Metropolis and capital of Kerala, India.
Known as the shipbuilding capital of India and home to the country's central naval command on the east coast, which Andhra Pradesh city is this?
Visakhapatnam: Metropolis in Andhra Pradesh, India. It is between the Eastern Ghats and the coast of the Bay of Bengal.
Home to the shimmering Blue Grotto and the dramatic Faraglioni sea stacks, this Italian island off the Sorrento Peninsula has drawn tourists since Roman times — which island?
Capri: Island in the Tyrrhenian Sea, Italy.
Named for being the smaller counterpart to Mallorca, this Balearic island's capital is Mahón and its highest point is a hill called El Toro — which island?
Menorca: Island in Spain. Its name derives from its size, contrasting it with nearby Mallorca (Majorca).
Sitting on the Meuse River near the Belgian border, this Dutch city grew from a Roman settlement into the capital of Limburg province — which city?
Maastricht: City and municipality in Limburg, Netherlands.
Sitting on the Seyhan River in southern Turkey, this city anchors the historic region of Cilicia near a key pass through the Taurus Mountains — which city?
Adana: City in Turkey. The city is situated on the Seyhan River, 35 km (22 mi) inland from the northeastern shores of the Mediterranean Sea.
Covering most of Kansas, Nebraska, and the Dakotas east of the Rocky Mountains, this vast North American grassland region also includes parts of Texas and Wyoming — what's it called?
Great Plains: Flat expanse in western North America.
Home to the ancient Knossos Palace and continuously inhabited since at least 7000 BCE, this city is the capital of Crete — which city?
Heraklion: City in Crete, Greece. The greater area of Heraklion has been continuously inhabited since at least 7000 BCE, making it one of the oldest inhabited regions in Europe.

This southern Mexican state is bordered by Guerrero, Puebla, and Chiapas, has a Pacific coastline, and is home to the Zapotec and Mixtec peoples among its 16 recognized Indigenous groups — which state?
Estado Libre y Soberano de Oaxaca
Oaxaca: State of Mexico. Oaxaca, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Oaxaca, is one of the 32 states that compose the Federative Entities of the United Mexican States.

Founded in 997 as a trading post along a Norwegian fjord, this city served as Norway's capital through the Viking Age until 1217 and is now home to the country's top technical university, NTNU — which city?
Trondheim: City in Norway. Trondheim is the third most populous municipality in Norway, and is the fourth largest urban area.
Sitting on the Vrbas river, this is the second-largest city in Bosnia and Herzegovina and serves as the main hub of the Republika Srpska entity — which city?
Banja Luka: City in Republika Srpska, Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is Republika Srpska's main economic, political, and administrative center.
Birthplace of Napoleon Bonaparte in 1769, this west-coast city is the capital of Corsica and gained a Genoese citadel in 1492 — which city is it?
Ajaccio: Prefecture and commune in Corsica, France.
Rising from a glacier in the Swiss canton of Valais and flowing through Lake Geneva before reaching the Mediterranean, this river's delta forms the wetlands of the Camargue — which river is it?
Rhône: Major river in Switzerland and France.

Bounded by Pakistan to the north, India to the east, and Somalia to the southwest, this arm of the Indian Ocean reaches a maximum depth of 5,395 meters and connects to the Persian Gulf via the Gulf of Oman. What is it?
Arabian Sea: Marginal sea of the northern Indian Ocean.

Founded in the 14th century by Holy Roman Emperor Charles IV at the confluence of two rivers, this Czech spa city became a favorite haunt of European aristocracy and now hosts a major international film festival. Which city?
Karlovy Vary: Statutory city in the Czech Republic.

Home to a temple dedicated to Krishna that forms one of the four Chardham pilgrimage sites founded by Adi Shankaracharya, this coastal Gujarat town sits where the Gomti River meets the Gulf of Kutch. Which town?
Dwarka: Town in Gujarat, India. Dwarka is a coastal town and municipality of Devbhumi Dwarka district in the Indian state of Gujarat.
Lying just south of Cape Cod, this affluent Massachusetts summer colony is the ninth-largest island in the contiguous US and includes the peninsula of Chappaquiddick — what is it?
Martha's Vineyard: Island in Massachusetts, US. Martha's Vineyard (Wampanoag: Noepe;), often simply called the Vineyard, is an island in Massachusetts, lying just south of Cape Cod.
Known to the ancients as Waset and now lying within modern Luxor, this Nile city served as capital during the Middle and New Kingdom eras and was home to the temples of Karnak — what was it called?
Thebes, Egypt (Egyptian), known to the ancient Egyptians as Waset, was an ancient Egyptian city located along the Nile about 800 kilometers (500 mi) south of the Mediterranean.
Split by the Great Glen into two mountain ranges, this rugged region was originally home to the Picts before becoming a stronghold of Gaelic culture — which region?
Scottish Highlands: Cultural and historical region of Scotland.
Spelled 'Cassel' until 1926, this German city on the Fulda River hosts the documenta contemporary art exhibitions and a UNESCO-listed park called Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe — which city?
Home to the Dalai Lama and the Tibetan government-in-exile since 1960, this Himachal Pradesh town includes the colonial-era suburb of McLeod Ganj — which town?
Dharamshala: Winter capital of Himachal Pradesh, India.
Sitting on the Main river in northern Bavaria, this Franconian city's baroque palace, the Residenz, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — what's the city?
Würzburg: City in Bavaria, Germany. Würzburg is the administrative seat of the Regierungsbezirk Lower Franconia.
Founded in 1536 by Spanish explorer Sebastián de Belalcázar, this southwestern Colombian city hosted the 1971 Pan American Games and the 2013 World Games — which city?
Cali: District and city in Valle del Cauca, Colombia.
Home to the golden Shwedagon Pagoda, this Myanmar city was the country's capital until 2005, when the government relocated administrative functions to a purpose-built new capital — which city?
Yangon: Largest city of Myanmar. Yangon, sometimes romanised in English as Rangoon, is the capital city of the Yangon Region and the most populous city of Myanmar.
Now open as a museum, hotel, and restaurant, this WWII military headquarters in the Masurian woods was Adolf Hitler's first base on the Eastern Front — what was it called?
Wolf's Lair: Adolf Hitler's Eastern Front military headquarters during World War II.
The de facto capital of Yemen since 2014, this ancient port city sits near the eastern approach to the Red Sea, roughly 110 miles from the Bab-el-Mandeb strait — which city?
Aden: Temporary capital of Yemen. It is approximately 170 km (110 mi) east of the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.
Nicknamed 'Flower of the East' by its former Venetian rulers, this Greek island in the Ionian Sea takes its myth-based name from a son of Dardanus. Which island?
Zakynthos: Greek island in the Ionian Sea. It is the third largest of the Ionian Islands, with an area of 405.55 km2 (156.6 sq mi), and a coastline 123 km (76 mi) in length.
Located about 19 miles southwest of Gaza City, this city became home to roughly 1.4 million displaced people by 2024 before being largely destroyed by 2025 — which city?
Rafah: Palestinian city in southern Gaza Strip.
Sitting on a plateau over 3,000 feet above sea level, this Brazilian city is the capital of Paraná state and the largest in the country's South Region. Which city?
Curitiba: Capital city of Paraná, Brazil. Curitiba ( KOOR-ih-CHEE-bə, Brazilian Portuguese: [kuɾiˈtʃibɐ]) is the capital and largest city in the state of Paraná in Southern Brazil.

This Norwegian archipelago north of the Arctic Circle draws a million tourists a year for its dramatic peaks and northern lights, despite one of the world's largest positive temperature anomalies for its latitude — what is it?
Lofoten: Archipelago and traditional district in Nordland, Norway.

Named after a 19th-century British whaling captain who sighted it in 1843, this disputed South China Sea archipelago holds less than 200 hectares of natural land scattered across hundreds of reefs and cays — what is it?

Spratly Islands: Disputed archipelago in the South China Sea. Additionally, Brunei has claimed an exclusive economic zone in the southeastern part of the Spratly Islands, which includes the uninhabited Louisa Reef.

Sitting near where the Negro and Amazon rivers meet, this Brazilian state capital started life in 1669 as a riverside fort before taking its current name from an indigenous people in 1832. Which city is this?
Manaus: Capital and largest city of Amazonas, Brazil.
Built in the 9th century and home to the Bohemian Crown Jewels in a hidden chamber, this complex holds the Guinness World Record for the largest ancient fortress on Earth. What is it?
Prague Castle: Historic building in the Czech Republic.
Known as Karl-Marx-Stadt from 1953 to 1990, this city is the third-largest in the German state of Saxony, behind only Leipzig and Dresden. Which city is this?
Chemnitz: City in Saxony, Germany. The city stands on the Chemnitz River, which is formed through the confluence of the rivers Zwönitz and Würschnitz in the borough of Altchemnitz.

Centered on the confluence of the Ruak and Mekong rivers where Myanmar, Thailand, and Laos meet, this mountainous region's nickname was coined by a US State Department official in 1971 discussing the opium trade. What region is this?

Golden Triangle (Southeast Asia) is a large, mountainous region of approximately 200,000 km2 (77,000 sq mi) in northeastern Myanmar, Northern Thailand and northern Laos, centered on the confluence of the Ruak and Mekong rivers.
Home to four of the world's fourteen peaks above 8,000 metres, including K2, this Asian mountain range straddles Pakistan, China, and India. Which range is this?
Karakoram: Mountain range spanning the borders between Pakistan, India and China.
This circle of latitude marks the southernmost point where the sun appears directly overhead, currently at about 23.4 degrees south — which line?
Tropic of Capricorn: Line of southernmost latitude at which the Sun can be directly overhead.
Forming an arc from the Virgin Islands through the Leeward and Windward Islands toward South America, this island chain marks the eastern edge of the Caribbean Sea — which island group?
Lesser Antilles: Archipelago in the Southeast Caribbean.
Once known as Halicarnassus and home to one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, this Turkish port town sits at the mouth of the Gulf of Gökova — which town?
Bodrum: District and municipality in Muğla, Turkey.
Historically known as Aintab, this Turkish city sits about 60 miles north of Aleppo and once fell within the Crusader County of Edessa — which city?
Once known as Tsingtao and linked to its Huangdao district by the Jiaozhou Bay Bridge, this Chinese seaport looks out on the Yellow Sea from the Shandong Peninsula — which city?
Qingdao: City in Shandong, China. The Jiaozhou Bay Bridge links the main urban area of Qingdao with Huangdao district, straddling the Jiaozhou Bay sea areas.
Known by its Zulu name eThekwini, this South African port city on the Indian Ocean is the busiest harbor in sub-Saharan Africa — which city is it?
Durban: City in South Africa. Within the city limits, Durban's population was 595,061 in 2011.
Connected to the Île de Ré by a bridge completed in 1988, this French Atlantic seaport serves as the capital of the Charente-Maritime department — which city is it?
La Rochelle: City in Nouvelle-Aquitaine, France.
Located along the Indigirka River in Russia's Sakha Republic, this remote village holds the record as the coldest permanently inhabited place on Earth — what's it called?
Oymyakon: Selo in Sakha Republic, Russia.

Buried in the same 79 AD eruption that destroyed Pompeii but discovered nearly 40 years earlier, in 1709, this Roman town's volcanic burial helped preserve wooden furniture, food, and papyrus scrolls — which site?
Herculaneum: Roman town destroyed by eruption of Mount Vesuvius.
Colombia's fourth-most populous city sits just a few kilometers from where the Magdalena River empties into the Caribbean Sea — which city?
Barranquilla: Capital district of Atlántico Department, Colombia.

Originally called Zaca Laderas, this Santa Barbara County property became the private amusement park and home of a pop superstar from 1988 to 2005, renamed for Peter Pan's ageless island — what was it known as?
Neverland Ranch: Home of Michael Jackson from 1988 to 2005.
Sitting in the shadow of the Southern Carpathians about 166 km north of Bucharest, this Transylvanian city was once a stronghold of Saxon merchants — what is it called?
Brașov: City in Romania. According to the 2021 census, with 237,589 inhabitants, Brașov is the 6th most populous city in Romania.
This southern French city, once the historic capital of its surrounding region, sits about 30 km north of Marseille and is home to roughly 148,000 residents — what's it called?
Aix-en-Provence: City and commune in Southern France.
The smallest of Japan's four main islands, this landmass south of Honshu takes its name from the four ancient provinces that once made it up — what is it called?
Shikoku: Island and region of Japan.

Seat of its state's most populous parish and center of its second-largest metro area, this state capital had a 2020 population of 227,470, making it the state's second-most populous city — which city?
Baton Rouge, Louisiana (ROOZH) is the capital city of the U.S.
Built in the 1890s to replace Ouro Preto as capital of Minas Gerais, this metropolis is considered Brazil's first planned modern city. What is it?
Belo Horizonte: Capital city of Minas Gerais, Brazil. It is the 13th-largest city in South America and the 18th-largest in the Americas.
First raised during the 1945 declaration of independence in Jakarta, this red-over-white national banner shares its exact dimensions with the ensign of Singapore. What is it?
Flag of Indonesia is bicolor, with two horizontal bands, red (top) and white (bottom) with an overall ratio of 2: The design of the flag has remained unchanged since.
This northern Italian city in the Po Valley lends its name to a Ferrari model and hosts the headquarters of luxury sports car makers including De Tomaso, Pagani, and Maserati. Which city is it?

This Polish city, the largest one lying east of the Vistula River, serves as capital of its namesake voivodeship, and its development was boosted by the Polish-Lithuanian Union of Krewo in 1385 — what city is it?
Lublin is the eighth-largest city in Poland and the second-largest city of historical Lesser Poland.
Nicknamed the 'Queen of hill stations,' this Tamil Nadu town sits at 2,240 metres in the Nilgiri Mountains and once served as the summer capital of the Madras Presidency — which town is it?
Ooty: Hill station in Tamil Nadu, India.
Founded in 1576 by Portuguese explorer Paulo Dias de Novais, this Atlantic port later became a hub of the slave trade to Brazil and is now home to over 8.8 million people — which capital is it?
Luanda: Capital and largest city of Angola.
This German city on the Baltic coast, once East Germany's most important port, straddles the River Warnow for about 16 kilometers as it flows toward the sea — which city?
Rostock: Largest city in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany.
Sitting atop the Khomas Highland plateau at 5,600 feet, this Namibian capital grew up around a hot spring after a 19th-century Orlam captain built a stone church there in 1840 — which city?
Windhoek: Capital and largest city of Namibia.
This French Riviera resort city hosts a world-famous annual film festival plus advertising's top creativity awards, drawing the rich and famous to its luxury hotels — which city?
Cannes: City in Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France.
Named after a medieval king and once part of the Holy Roman Empire, this eastern French region was annexed by the Kingdom of France in 1766 before merging into Grand Est in 2016 — which region?
Lorraine: Cultural and historical region in France.
Sitting at the foot of the Alps near Lake Garda, this city is Lombardy's second-largest, trailing only Milan, with roots stretching back over 3,200 years — which city?
Brescia: City and comune in the region of Lombardy, Italy.
India's third-smallest state, this northeastern territory was ruled for centuries by the Manikya Dynasty before merging with India in 1949, with Agartala as its capital — which state?
Tripura: State in northeastern India. The third-smallest state in the country, it covers 10,491 km2 (4,051 sq mi); and the seventh-least populous state with a population of 3.67 million.
Founded in 1923 by the Dawasir tribe fleeing British persecution, this Saudi Arabian city on the Persian Gulf boomed as the export port for Aramco's early oil operations — which city?
Khobar: City in Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia.
Lying between the tropics and the temperate zones, roughly 23 to 40 degrees latitude, this climate zone typically features hot summers, mild winters, and rare frost — what's it called?
Subtropics: Geographic and climate zone. The subtropical zones or subtropics are geographical and climate zones immediately to the north and south of the tropics.
Founded by King Francis I in 1517 on the Normandy coast near the Prime Meridian, this city's name simply means 'the harbour' in French — which port?
Le Havre: City in Normandy, France. Le Havre is a major port city in the Seine-Maritime department in the Normandy region of northern France.
Home to the city of Honolulu on its southeast coast, this island is the most populous of its Hawaiian chain despite ranking only third in size — which island?
Oʻahu: Third largest island in Hawaii.
Once capital of a princely kingdom for nearly six centuries and nicknamed the 'City of Palaces,' which Karnataka city sits at the foot of Chamundi Hills?
Mysore: City in Karnataka, India. Mysore (my-SOR), officially Mysuru (Kannada: [ˈmaɪˈsuːɾu]), is a city in the southern Indian state of Karnataka.
Home to Maruti Suzuki's manufacturing plant and later General Electric's outsourcing arm Genpact, which satellite city near Delhi is officially known by a newer name?
Called by a different name south of the border, this waterway forms much of the US-Mexico boundary as it flows from Colorado to the Gulf of Mexico — which river?
Rio Grande: Major river forming part of the United States and Mexico border.
Under Israeli occupation since 1967 and later placed under Palestinian Authority control in 1995, this West Bank city's refugee camp has become a flashpoint in the ongoing conflict — which city?

Jenin: Palestinian city, northern West Bank. Jenin ( zhin-EEN; Arabic: جنين, romanized: Jinīn, locally pronounced [ʒɪˈniːn]) is a city in the West Bank, Palestine, and is the capital of the Jenin Governorate.

Sitting on the shore of Great Slave Lake about 400 km south of the Arctic Circle, this Canadian territorial capital takes its name from a local Dene tribe once known as the 'Copper Indians' — which city?
Yellowknife: Capital city of the Northwest Territories, Canada.
Once home to the Dukes of Burgundy for four centuries, this eastern French city was the most populous commune in its region as of 2023 — which city?
Home to Scandinavia's largest cathedral and the seat of Sweden's Archbishop since 1164, this city north of Stockholm briefly served as the country's secondary capital — which city?
Uppsala: City in Uppland, Sweden. Located 71 km (44 mi) north of the capital Stockholm, it is also the seat of Uppsala Municipality.
Home to the football club Schalke 04 and its Veltins-Arena stadium, this German city sits at the centre of the Ruhr, the country's largest urban area — which city?
Gelsenkirchen: City in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.
Sitting at the farthest navigable point of the river Oker in Lower Saxony, this city's urban area is Germany's most ethnically diverse, with over 40% having a migration background — which city?
Braunschweig: City and urban agglomeration in Lower Saxony, Germany. It is one of the largest regiopolitan cities in Northern Germany and the largest regiopolis in Lower Saxony.

Stretching from the Grenen spit in the north to where the Elbe and Sude rivers meet in the southeast, this peninsula forms the continental portion of Denmark plus part of northern Germany — which peninsula?
Jutland: Peninsula in Europe. The historic southern border river of Jutland as a cultural-geographical region, which historically also included Southern Schleswig, is the Eider.
This central Iraqi city, the second-largest in the region after Baghdad, sits just east of Lake Milh and serves as a major spiritual hub — name the city?
Karbala is a major city in central Iraq. With a population of around 800,000 people in 2024, Karbala is the second-largest city in central Iraq, after Baghdad.
Home to Davao City and divided into six administrative regions including Bangsamoro, this is the second-largest island in the Philippines — which island is it?
Mindanao: Island in the Philippines. Mindanao (MIN-də-NOW) is the second-largest island in the Philippines, after Luzon, and seventh-most populous island in the world.
Since 1981, this Bosnian village nestled "between mountains" has drawn Catholic pilgrims after six local children reported apparitions of the Virgin Mary — which village is it?
Medjugorje: Village in Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bosnia and Herzegovina.
The largest city in Switzerland's Italian-speaking canton of Ticino, this lakeside city of about 62,000 people ranks as the country's ninth largest — which city is it?
Lugano: City in Switzerland. Lugano has a population (as of December 2020) of 62,315, and an urban agglomeration of over 150,000.
Ecuador's largest city and economic capital, this Pacific port sits on the west bank of a river that empties into a gulf sharing its name — which city is it?
Guayaquil: Most populous city in Ecuador.
This Uttar Pradesh city, formerly known by another name, hosts India's highest state court and was once ranked the world's 40th fastest-growing city — what is it called today?

Prayagraj: Metropolis in Uttar Pradesh, India. Prayagraj (Hindi: [pɾəjaːɡ.ɾaːd͡ʑ]; ISO: Prayāgarāja), formerly and colloquially known as Allahabad, is a metropolis in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.
Encircled by nearly intact Renaissance-era walls, this Tuscan city on the Serchio River is famed as the birthplace of opera composer Giacomo Puccini — what city is it?
Lucca: City and comune in Tuscany, Italy.
Crossed by the River Tiber and home to a university founded in 1308, this Umbrian capital sits atop a hilltop about 164 km north of Rome — which city?
Covering nearly 350 square miles as the seat of Tarrant County, this city is the second-largest in the Dallas metroplex and reached an estimated population over one million in 2025 — which city?
Fort Worth, Texas is a city in the U.S. It is the county seat of Tarrant County, covering nearly 350 square miles (910 km2) and extending into Denton, Johnson, Parker, and Wise counties.
Located on the Gulf of Guinea, this city is Ghana's capital, with a metropolitan district of just over 20 square km but a wider region home to more than 5 million people — which city?
Accra: Capital and the largest city of Ghana. Accra is the capital and largest city of Ghana, located on the southern coast at the Gulf of Guinea, which is part of the Atlantic Ocean.
Stretching 800 km from Afghanistan into Pakistan and Tajikistan, this mountain range buttresses the Pamirs to the north and divides the Amu Darya valley from the Indus River valley — which range?
Hindu Kush: Mountain range near the border of Afghanistan and Pakistan.
Purchased by Abraham as a burial plot according to Abrahamic tradition, this holy site in Hebron's Old City sits under a Herodian-era enclosure — what is it?
Cave of the Patriarchs: Holy site in Hebron, Palestine. The site is considered a holy place in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

Introduced in its current form in 2006, this yellow-blue-red tricolor traces its stripes back to 1811 and carries a set of stars plus an optional coat of arms in the corner — which country's banner is it?

Flag of Venezuela was introduced in 2006. The basic design includes a horizontal tricolour of yellow, blue, and red, dating to the original flag introduced in 1811, in the Venezuelan War of Independence.

Designed in a high-tech style by Richard Rogers and Renzo Piano and opened in Paris in 1977, this building complex is named for the French president who commissioned it and houses a modern art museum — what is it?

Centre Pompidou: Art museum in Paris, France. It was designed in the style of high-tech architecture by the architectural team of Richard Rogers, Su Rogers and Renzo Piano, along with Gianfranco Franchini.
This university city in Lower Saxony, Germany, sits along the River Leine and had a population of about 124,500 as of the 2022 census — which city?
Göttingen: City in Lower Saxony, Germany. Göttingen (US also; German: [ˈɡœtɪŋən]; Low German: Chöttingen) is a university city in Lower Saxony, central Germany, the capital of the eponymous district.
Built where the ancient city of Antioch once stood on the Orontes River, this Turkish city is said to be where the term 'Christian' was first used — which city, capital of Hatay Province?
Sitting on the Saar River right on the French border, this German city is the capital of Saarland and home to an 18th-century castle overlooking its old town — which city?
Saarbrücken: Capital of Saarland, Germany. The city has 181,959 inhabitants and is Saarland's administrative, commercial and cultural centre.
Known locally as Kovai, this Tamil Nadu metropolis on the Noyyal River is the state's second-largest city after Chennai — which city?
Coimbatore: City in Tamil Nadu, India. Coimbatore (Tamil: kōyamputtūr, IPA: [koːjɐmbut̪ːuːɾ]), also known as Kovai (IPA: [koːʋaj]), is a metropolitan city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
Home to pharmaceutical giant Bayer and its top-flight football club, this Rhine city of about 163,000 sits between Cologne and Düsseldorf — which city?
Leverkusen: City in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.
Nicknamed 'City of Science,' this Hessian city hosts the European Space Agency's satellite control centre and a heavy-ion research lab that helped discover new chemical elements — which city?

Halfway between a New England state's capital and its largest city, this is that state's second-most populous city, forming a twin-city metro area recognized for low cost of living and low crime. Name it?

Lewiston, Maine is the second-most populous city in the U.S. Lewiston ( LOO-is-tən) is the second-most populous city in the U.S. state of Maine, with a population of 37,121, according to the 2020 United States census.
This Central Asian mountain system's lowest point, the Turpan Depression, sits below sea level, while its highest peak tops 7,400 metres in Kyrgyzstan — which range?
Tian Shan: System of mountain ranges in Central Asia.

Second only to Lake Superior in volume and depth among the Great Lakes, this lake shares its water level with Lake Huron via the Straits of Mackinac, forming together the world's largest freshwater lake — which lake?
Lake Michigan is one of the five Great Lakes of North America.

Known as the 'Mother of Cities' for launching colonial expeditions that founded Buenos Aires and Córdoba, this capital sits where the Pilcomayo meets a major river in landlocked South America — which city?
Asunción: Capital and most populous city of Paraguay.
Home to Guadalajara, this Mexican state gave the world mariachi music, tequila, and birria, inspiring a motto declaring that it simply IS the country — which state?
Free and sovereign state of Jalisco
Jalisco: State of Mexico. Jalisco, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Jalisco, is one of the 31 states which, along with Mexico City, comprise the 32 Federal Entities of Mexico.
This ceremonial county in the East of England borders Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire, Essex, Greater London and Buckinghamshire, with Watford as its largest settlement. What county is it?
Hertfordshire: County of England. Hertfordshire (HART-fərd-sheer, -⁠shər; often abbreviated Herts) is a ceremonial county in the East of England.
Home to Southampton, Portsmouth, and the cathedral city of Winchester, this South East England county sits across the Solent from the Isle of Wight — which county?
Hampshire: County of England. The county has an area of 3,769 km2 (1,455 sq mi) and had an estimated population of 1,920,959 in 2024.
Home to the city of Norwich and the wetland network known as the Broads, this ceremonial English county borders Lincolnshire, the Wash, and Suffolk — which county?
Norfolk: County of England. Norfolk ( NOR-fək, -⁠fuuk) is a ceremonial county in England, located in the East of England and East Anglia.
England's northernmost ceremonial county, it borders Scotland and is the country's least densely populated county, with Morpeth as its administrative centre — which county?
Northumberland: County of England. It is bordered by the North Sea to the east, Tyne and Wear and County Durham to the south, Cumbria to the west, and the Scottish Borders council area to the north.
Mexico's southernmost state, its capital is Tuxtla Gutiérrez and it shares a border with Guatemala — which state?
Chiapas: State of Mexico. Chiapas, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Chiapas, is one of the states that make up the 32 federal entities of Mexico.
This North West England county has a short coastline on the Dee Estuary, is bordered by Shropshire to the south, and calls Warrington its largest settlement — which county is it?
Cheshire: County of England. Cheshire ( CHESH-ər, -⁠eer) is a ceremonial county in North West England.
Bordering Arizona to the north and fronting the Gulf of California, this Mexican state's capital and largest city is Hermosillo — which state?
Sonora: State of Mexico. The state is divided into 72 municipalities; the capital (and largest) city of which is Hermosillo, located in the center of the state.
Founded by the Spanish in 1531 to guard the trade route from Mexico City to the port of Veracruz, this east-central Mexican state is divided into 217 municipalities — which state?
Free and Sovereign State of Puebla
Puebla: State of Mexico. Puebla, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Puebla, is one of the 31 states that, along with Mexico City, comprise the Federal Entities of Mexico.
Bordered by Somerset, Wiltshire, and Hampshire, this South West England county's largest settlement is Bournemouth, though its historic county town is Dorchester — which county?
Dorset: County of England. Dorset ( DOR-sit; archaically: Dorsetshire DOR-sit-sheer, -⁠shər) is a ceremonial county in South West England.
Home to the town where Mexico's War of Independence began, this central Mexican state's 'Bicentennial Route' winds through San Miguel de Allende to its own colonial capital — which state?
Guanajuato: State of Mexico. Guanajuato, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Guanajuato, is one of the 32 states that make up the Federal Entities of Mexico.
Launched in 1955 as the European Champion Clubs' Cup, this is the most-watched club competition on the planet — which one?
UEFA Champions League: European association football tournament.
Organised by the ICC and first played in England back in 1975, this quadrennial One Day International tournament is considered the flagship event of its sport's calendar — which competition?
Cricket World Cup: Men's One Day International (ODI) event.
Founded in 1880 as St. Mark's (West Gorton) and adopting sky-blue shirts in 1894, this English club moved from Maine Road to a new stadium in 2003 — which one?
Manchester City F.C.: Association football club in England.
Founded in 1902 and granted its royal title by King Alfonso XIII in 1920, this all-white-kitted Spanish giant plays at the Santiago Bernabéu — which club?
Real Madrid CF: Association football club in Spain.
In this 2023 T20 league season, Chennai Super Kings edged Gujarat Titans by five wickets via the DLS method to claim their fifth title — which tournament?
2023 Indian Premier League: Cricket tournament. It is organised by the Board of Control for Cricket in India.
Founded in 1955 and based in Riyadh, this club is one of only three sides never relegated from the Saudi top flight — which one?
Al-Nassr FC: Association football club in Saudi Arabia.
Playing home matches at Anfield since 1892 and built into a European force under manager Bill Shankly in the 1960s, which English club has won six European Cups?
Liverpool F.C.: Association football club in England.
Jointly hosted by Australia and New Zealand in mid-2023, this was the first edition of the tournament ever held in the Southern Hemisphere — which competition?
2023 FIFA Women's World Cup: Football championship.
