Founded in 1905 and playing home games at Stamford Bridge, this West London club are the reigning club world champions — which one?
Chelsea F.C.: Association football club in England.

A former kickboxer turned controversial social-media figure, dubbed the 'king of toxic masculinity,' he faces multiple criminal and civil investigations across Romania, the UK, and the US — who is he?
Andrew Tate: American and British internet personality (born 1986)
First held in 1957 with just three teams — Sudan, Egypt, and Ethiopia — after a fourth invitee was disqualified over its apartheid policies, which biennial men's football tournament is this?
Africa Cup of Nations: Football tournament. It is sanctioned by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and was first held in 1957.
Played across Pakistan and Sri Lanka in a first-ever 'hybrid' format during August and September 2023, this cricket tournament crowned a new continental champion — which one?
2023 Asia Cup: Cricket tournament in Pakistan and Sri Lanka. The 2023 Men's Asia Cup, also known as Super 11 Asia Cup for sponsorship, was the 16th edition of the men's Asia Cup cricket tournament.
Founded in 1900 by eleven players led by Franz John, this German giant strung together eleven straight national titles from 2013 to 2023 — which club?
FC Bayern Munich: Association football club in Germany.
The first club from southern England to join the Football League back in 1893, this Islington side boasts the longest unbroken run in England's top flight — which club?
Arsenal F.C.: Association football club in England. The Arsenal Football Club is an English professional football club based in Islington, North London, England.
Jointly hosted by three North American countries and the first ever to feature 48 teams, this tournament kicked off with eleven US host cities alone — which edition?
2026 FIFA World Cup: International men's soccer tournament in North America.
Starting in karting at age six and joining McLaren's Young Driver Programme in 1998, he became Formula One's first Black driver and later tied the record for world titles — who is he?
The only club with an unbroken run in Italian football's top flight since 1909, this side has shared its home stadium — Italy's largest — with a fierce crosstown rival since 1947. Which club?
Inter Milan: Association football club in Italy. The club was founded on 9 March 1908 after a split within the Milan Foot-Ball and Cricket Club (now AC Milan), and won its first championship in 1910.
Staged in Qatar during the northern-hemisphere winter to dodge summer heat, this tournament was the first World Cup ever hosted in the Middle East — which one?
2022 FIFA World Cup: Association football tournament in Qatar.
Introduced in 1971 as a replacement for the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, this competition ranks just below Europe's top club prize — which one?
UEFA Europa League: European annual club football competition.
Contested by 20 clubs over 38 matchdays, this Spanish top flight has been dominated by two giants who've combined for 65 titles — which league?
La Liga: Spanish association football league.
Born from a 1970 merger of two French clubs and playing at the Parc des Princes, this side has racked up 60 trophies, more than any other in its country — which club?
Paris Saint-Germain FC: French football club. The club was founded in 1970 by the merger of Paris FC and Stade Saint-Germain, and competes in Ligue 1, the top tier of French football.
The only non-League club ever to win the FA Cup, back in 1901, this North London side's emblem is a cockerel perched on a football — which club?
Tottenham Hotspur F.C.: Association football club in England.
Formed in 1926 through a merger of two local clubs in southern Italy, this Serie A side's fortunes transformed after Diego Maradona arrived in 1984 — which club?
SSC Napoli: Association football club in Italy.
Established in 1983 alongside its governing council, this biennial cricket tournament saw India boycott the 1986 edition over tensions with Sri Lanka — which competition?
Asia Cup: Men's cricket tournament. It features senior men's national teams from Asian member countries and determines the continental cricket champion of Asia.

Hosted by Ivory Coast and organized by CAF, this biennial football tournament's 34th edition was postponed to avoid summer heat despite keeping its original sponsorship name. Which competition is this?
2023 Africa Cup of Nations: International football competition. It was hosted by Ivory Coast, taking place in the country for the second time following the 1984 edition.
This Italian club's second chairman had its home stadium built in 1926, a ground the team has shared with its city rival since 1947. Which side is this?
AC Milan: Association football club in Italy.
Established in the 1929-30 season as the top tier of Italian football, this league restructured a championship that had been played since 1898. Which competition is it?
Serie A: Association football league in Italy.
After beating 90,000 entrants in a video-game talent search with zero real-world racing experience, this British driver earned a professional Nissan contract and later podiumed at Le Mans. Who is he?
Nicknamed for the crescent moon and based in Riyadh, this club has won a record 21 Saudi league titles and four AFC Champions League crowns. Which team is this?
Al Hilal SFC: Association football club in Saudi Arabia.
Becoming the youngest champion in UFC history by beating Mauricio Rua at age 23, this American fighter later held both the light heavyweight and heavyweight titles. Who is he?
Jon Jones: American mixed martial artist (born 1987)
Retiring with a perfect 29-0 record as the longest-reigning UFC lightweight champion, this Russian fighter had a background in wrestling, judo, and sambo. Who is he?
Khabib Nurmagomedov: Russian mixed martial artist (born 1988)
Playing home matches at St James' Park since 1892 after absorbing a defunct crosstown rival, this English club has won four league titles and six FA Cups. Which team is this?
Newcastle United F.C.: Association football club in England.
Organized by CONMEBOL since 1960 and named for the leaders of South America's independence wars, this is the continent's top club football competition. Which tournament is this?
Copa Libertadores: South American association football tournament.

Played since 1966 and awarding the Vince Lombardi Trophy to its winner, this NFL championship game is often called 'the big game' by non-sponsoring advertisers due to trademark restrictions. Which game is this?
Super Bowl: National Football League championship game.

Held as a two-night event at SoFi Stadium in April 2023 with The Miz and Snoop Dogg as hosts, this WWE spectacle had originally been slated for a different year before COVID forced a relocation. Which event is this?
WrestleMania 39: 2023 WWE pay-per-view and livestreaming event.
Nicknamed 'The Black and Yellows' and founded by eighteen players in 1909, this German club contests 'Der Klassiker' against Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga. Which club is this?
Borussia Dortmund: Association football club in Germany.

Inspired by an ancient event held in Olympia, Greece, and revived through Baron Pierre de Coubertin's 1894 committee, this modern sporting event alternates between summer and winter editions. Which event is this?
Founded in 1930 in Catalonia and part of the City Football Group, this Spanish club plays its home matches at Estadi Montilivi and was recently relegated from La Liga. Which club is this?
Girona FC: Association football club in Spain.

Winner of consecutive Formula One titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006, this Spanish driver is also a two-time Le Mans winner and the only person to claim both F1 and World Endurance titles. Who is he?

Restructured in 2025 into a quadrennial tournament resembling its international namesake, this competition for the sport's top teams crowned Chelsea champions after they beat Paris Saint-Germain 3-0 in the final — which tournament?
FIFA Club World Cup: Men's football tournament.
Founded in 1903 as a branch of a Bilbao club, this Spanish football side plays its home games at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano stadium in the Spanish capital. Which club?
Atlético Madrid: Association football club in Spain.

Founded in Birmingham in 1874, this English club has played home matches at the same ground since 1897 and was once managed by Scotsman George Ramsay, the world's first professional football manager. Which club?
Aston Villa F.C.: Association football club in Birmingham, England.

Hosted by Argentina after original host Indonesia lost its rights for refusing to face Israel, this biennial youth football championship saw defending champions Ukraine fail to even qualify. Which tournament?
2023 FIFA U-20 World Cup: International youth football championship tournament. The official match ball used in the tournament was Adidas Oceaunz.

Held at Tropicana Field in Florida for the first time with a live crowd, this 37th annual WWE pay-per-view was the first major show since Vince McMahon's resignation not to involve any McMahon at all. Which event?
Royal Rumble (2024): World Wrestling Entertainment event.

Held every four years since 1960 and originally called the European Nations' Cup until a 1968 rebrand, this continental men's national-team tournament trails only the World Cup in global viewership. Which competition?
UEFA European Championship: Association football tournament.
A Cameroonian-French heavyweight fighter who competed in both the UFC and PFL, this athlete ended seven of his fourteen UFC bouts by first-round knockout. Who is he?
Francis Ngannou: Cameroonian mixed martial artist and boxer (born 1986)
Played at Dublin's Aviva Stadium, this European secondary club tournament saw Atalanta beat Bayer Leverkusen 3-0, becoming the first Italian side to win it since Parma in 1999 — which competition?

2023–24 UEFA Europa League: European football tournament. Sevilla were the defending champions, but could not defend their title after being eliminated in the group stage of the 2023–24 UEFA Champions League.
Contested at the Agia Sophia Stadium in Athens, Europe's tertiary club tournament crowned Olympiacos champions after they edged Fiorentina 1-0 in extra time — which competition?
2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League: European football tournament.

Based in Italy's capital and formed by a 1927 merger, this club has won Serie A three times and lifted the UEFA Conference League in 2021-22, having also claimed the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup in 1960-61. Which club?
AS Roma: Association football club in Italy.
Home at Falmer Stadium since 2011 after decades at the Goldstone Ground, this English club lost the 1983 FA Cup final to Manchester United after a replay — which team?
Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.: Association football club in England.
Founded in 1895 as Thames Ironworks, this East London club plays at the London Stadium after leaving its century-old former home in 2016 — name it?
West Ham United F.C.: Association football club in England.
Founded in 1904 by employees of a German pharmaceutical company's paint factory, this Bundesliga side plays home matches at the BayArena in red and black — which club?
Bayer 04 Leverkusen: German association football club.
Born in Monte Carlo, this Ferrari driver was runner-up in the 2022 Formula One World Drivers' Championship after winning karting's junior World Cup as a kid — who is he?

Contested by national teams for players under 18, this youth football tournament was hosted by Indonesia for the first time — the sixth time an Asian country had staged it, after China, Japan, South Korea, the UAE, and India. Which tournament?
2023 FIFA U-17 World Cup: International football competition.
His first go-kart was built by his father using a lawnmower engine; this Brazilian driver went on to win three Formula One titles with McLaren before his death in 1994 — who was he?
Founded in 1890 by a Scottish-born president, this Andalusian club has won a record seven UEFA Cup and Europa League titles — which team, based in Seville, is it?
Sevilla FC: Association football club in Spain.

Sitting just below England's top flight, this 24-club second tier traces its lineage to the old Second Division and hands its winner the trophy once awarded to England's pre-Premier-League champions — which division?
EFL Championship: English association football league.

Organized by Asia's continental football body and rebranded in 2024, this 32-club competition splits into East and West regions and sends its winner to the FIFA Intercontinental Cup — which tournament?
AFC Champions League Elite: Asian association football tournament for clubs.
Inaugurated in 1932 under the name 'National' before later renaming, this 18-club competition is the top flight of French football, with matches running from August to May — which league?

Ligue 1: French association football league. Administered by the Ligue de Football Professionnel, Ligue 1 is contested by 18 clubs and operates on a system of promotion and relegation from and to Ligue 2.
A three-time Swedish national wrestling champion, this Russian-Emirati fighter became the UFC's former middleweight champion and sits at number one in the division's rankings — who is he?
Khamzat Chimaev: Russian-Emirati mixed martial artist (born 1994)
Based in a Buenos Aires neighborhood it's named after, this club has never played outside Argentina's top flight and holds more official trophies than any other Argentine side — which team?
Boca Juniors: Association football club in Argentina.
Holding both Georgian and Spanish nationality, he became the first undefeated fighter in UFC history to win championships in two different weight divisions — who is he?
Ilia Topuria: Georgian and Spanish mixed martial artist (born 1997)
Renamed in 1919 to match its town's new official status, this East Midlands club stunned English football with a Premier League title before dropping down to the third tier — which team?
Leicester City F.C.: Association football club in England.
A professional since 2008 and a former King of the Cage titleholder, this American fighter became a two-time UFC middleweight champion — who is he?
Sean Strickland: American mixed martial artist (born 1991)
After buying the family wrestling business from his father in 1982, he built it into WWE, also dabbling in bodybuilding promotion and founding the XFL football league — who is he?
Vince McMahon: American professional wrestling promoter (born 1945)
A combat sambo world champion who once held a 14-fight UFC winning streak, he became the eleventh double champion in promotion history after moving up to welterweight — who is he?
Islam Makhachev: Russian mixed martial artist (born 1991)
Created by Joe Weider so amateur bodybuilding winners could keep competing and earn money, this annual title has been won a record eight times each by Lee Haney and Ronnie Coleman — which contest?
Mr. Olympia: Annual bodybuilding competition. Olympia was held on September 18, 1965, at the Brooklyn Academy of Music, New York City, with Larry Scott winning his first of two straight titles.

Marking the 100th anniversary of the inaugural edition, this tournament jointly hosted by Portugal, Spain, and Morocco will also stage a special centenary match in Uruguay, host of that first final — which competition?
2030 FIFA World Cup: Upcoming association football tournament.
First staged in Tunisia back in 1977, this biennial football championship for national teams' under-20 men has seen Maradona, Messi, and Pogba win its top-player honor — what tournament is it?
FIFA U-20 World Cup: Football tournament. The reigning champions are Morocco, which won their first title at the 2025 tournament in Chile.

First run in 1923 near a French city, this endurance race is won by whichever car covers the greatest distance in a day, and forms part of a 'Triple Crown' with the Indianapolis 500 and Monaco Grand Prix — what is this race?
24 Hours of Le Mans: Annual sports car race held in France.
Founded in 1903, this annual knockout tournament is Spanish football's oldest competition, and its winners earn a spot in next season's Europa League — what's the cup, most won by Barcelona?
Copa del Rey: Spanish association football tournament. The competition was founded in 1903, making it the oldest Spanish football competition played at a national level.
Working alongside Carroll Shelby, this English engineer-driver helped develop the Ford GT40 and was later portrayed in the Oscar-winning film Ford v Ferrari — who was he?
Hosted by Russia, this football championship became the first edition staged in Eastern Europe and, at $14.2 billion, the most expensive ever until the following tournament — which one was it?
2018 FIFA World Cup: Association football tournament in Russia. The 2018 FIFA World Cup was the 21st FIFA World Cup, the quadrennial world championship for national football teams organised by FIFA.
Inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2022, this retired wrestler built his ring persona around funeral and undead imagery after joining the WWF in 1990 — who is he?
The only driver to win Formula One titles with both Ferrari and McLaren, this Austrian racer held the record for career podium finishes upon retiring — who is he?
Named after a legendary Greek hero, this Amsterdam club holds Dutch football's records for both league titles and domestic cups — which club?
AFC Ajax: Association football club in Netherlands.
Organized by the ICC, this biennial tournament in cricket's shortest format was rebranded under its current name in 2018 — name the competition?
Men's T20 World Cup: Twenty20 International (T20I) cricket competition.
One of only six English clubs to win the European Cup, this side has actually won that trophy more often than its home league title — which club, once managed to glory by Brian Clough?
Nottingham Forest F.C.: Association football club in England.
This Australian wrestler's first Women's World Championship reign tied Bayley's record at 380 days, and she later became WWE's inaugural NXT UK Women's Champion — who is she?
Nicknamed 'The Eagles' for its crest and 'The Reds' for its shirts, this Lisbon club has played at the Estádio da Luz since 2003 — which club?
S.L. Benfica: Association football club in Portugal.

Held August 5, 2023, at Ford Field in Detroit — the first WWE event there since WrestleMania 23 in 2007 — this pay-per-view saw Roman Reigns beat Jey Uso in Tribal Combat to retain the Universal Championship. Which event?

SummerSlam (2023): WWE pay-per-view and livestreaming event. The 2023 SummerSlam, also promoted as SummerSlam: Detroit, was a professional wrestling pay-per-view (PPV) and livestreaming event produced by WWE.

Nicknamed 'il Drake' after English privateer Francis Drake, this Italian founded a Grand Prix racing team and later an iconic sports car marque, winning nine World Drivers' Championships as team boss — who is he?
Enzo Ferrari: Italian racing driver, engineer and entrepreneur (1898–1988)

Held in Brazil for the second time — 64 years after its first hosting — this quadrennial men's football tournament introduced goal-line technology and vanishing spray for the very first time. Which tournament?

2014 FIFA World Cup: Association football tournament in Brazil. The 2014 FIFA World Cup was the 20th FIFA World Cup, the quadrennial world championship for men's national football teams organised by FIFA.

Devised to replace meaningless friendlies with competitive matches between similarly ranked teams, this European men's football competition debuted in 2018 with a promotion-and-relegation structure — hosts Portugal won the first finals in 2019. Which competition?
UEFA Nations League: European football competition. The competition was devised to minimise friendlies and give nations competitive encounters with equally ranked teams.

Playing home matches at the Stade Vélodrome and founded in 1899 with a name inspired by the ancient Olympic Games, this French club boasts the country's highest average attendance and a fierce rivalry with a Parisian giant — which club?
Olympique de Marseille: Association football club in France.
Contested by 20 clubs with promotion and relegation to a second tier, this top-flight Brazilian football league was ranked the world's strongest national league by the IFFHS in 2021 — which league?

Campeonato Brasileiro Série A: Brazilian association football league. The various formats already adopted include a knockout tournament system (1959–1968) and a mixed system with a group stage followed by playoffs (1967–2002).
Kicking off on 11 June in Johannesburg, this month-long tournament made South Africa the first African nation to host the men's global football championship — which edition was it?
2010 FIFA World Cup: Association football tournament in South Africa. The bidding process for hosting the tournament finals was open only to African nations.
Nicknamed 'the Honey Badger,' this Perth-born Formula One driver competed from 2011 to 2024 and racked up eight Grand Prix wins — who is he?
Wrestling under a masked luchador persona, this WWE Hall of Famer also serves as the on-screen general manager of a major Mexican lucha libre promotion — who is he?
The first fighter to hold UFC titles in both the middleweight and light heavyweight divisions, this Brazilian also became a two-weight Glory kickboxing champion — who is he?
Alex Pereira: Brazilian kickboxer and mixed martial artist (born 1987)
The son of wrestling legend Dusty and half-brother of Dustin, he co-founded All Elite Wrestling before returning to WWE to become Undisputed Champion — who is he?
Founded in 2009 by an energy-drink company that bought a fifth-tier club's playing rights, this German football side plays at Red Bull Arena and is nicknamed 'The Red Bulls' — which club?
RB Leipzig: Association football club in Germany.
Based in Liverpool and founded in 1878, this club is one of just three sides to have been a founding member of both the old Football League and the Premier League — which club?
Everton F.C.: Association football club in England.
Based in Rome and sharing the Stadio Olimpico with their city rival, this Serie A club won Italian titles in 1974 and 2000 plus a European Cup Winners' trophy in 1999 — which club?
SS Lazio: Association football club in Italy.
Founded in 1907 and based in Istanbul, this football club holds the record for the most Turkish national championships, with 28 titles across various eras of the league system — which club?
Fenerbahçe S.K. (football) (Turkish), commonly known simply as Fenerbahe, or colloquially as Fener is the football branch of Fenerbahe Sports Club association, based in Istanbul, Turkey.
The first true freshman to win the Heisman Trophy, this dual-threat Texas A&M quarterback was later drafted by the Cleveland Browns — who is he?
Based in Florence and refounded in 2002 after bankruptcy, this Italian club won a European Cup Winners' trophy in 1960–61 and has played among the most Serie A seasons of any side — which club?
ACF Fiorentina: Association football club based in Florence, Tuscany, Italy.
Measuring 42.195 kilometres and inspired by a story from ancient Greece, this long-distance road race has been part of the Olympics since 1896 in Athens — which event?
Marathon: Long-distance running event of 42.195 kilometres. The marathon can be completed by running or with a run/walk strategy.
Held on July 1, 2023 at London's O2 Arena — WWE's first major show in the city since 2002 — which annual ladder-match spectacular saw Jey Uso pin Roman Reigns in a 'Civil War' tag bout?
Money in the Bank (2023): WWE pay-per-view and livestreaming event.
The son of a two-time World Rally Champion who shares his exact name, which Spanish Formula One driver — now racing for Williams — has claimed four Grand Prix wins across a dozen seasons?
Carlos Sainz Jr.: Spanish racing driver (born 1994)
With 28 total Olympic medals — more than any athlete in history — including a record-breaking eight golds at the 2008 Beijing Games alone, who is this American swimming legend?
The 21st and final edition under its old name before a rebrand to 'Elite,' this Asian club football tournament's champion earned a spot in the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup — which competition is it?
2023–24 AFC Champions League: 42nd edition of premier club football tournament organized by the AFC.
Known until 1975 as the South American Football Championship and first held in 1916, which quadrennial tournament has been won 16 times by Argentina — more than any other nation?
Copa América: Association football tournament. It is the oldest still-running continental football competition.
Founded in 1902 as Rio de Janeiro's oldest football club, which Brazilian side finally won the Copa Libertadores in 2023 after also claiming the 1952 Copa Rio, regarded by fans as a world title?
Fluminense FC: Brazilian football club. It competes in the Campeonato Brasileiro Série A, the first tier of Brazilian football, and the Campeonato Carioca, the state league of Rio de Janeiro.
Nicknamed 'Checo' and born in Guadalajara, this Mexican driver finished runner-up in the 2023 Formula One championship with Red Bull and now races for Cadillac — who is he?
Staged in Germany for a second time, after 1974, this quadrennial men's football championship saw Italy beat France on penalties in the final to claim a fourth title — which global tournament is it?
2006 FIFA World Cup: Association football tournament in Germany. It was held from 9 June to 9 July 2006 in Germany, which had won the right to host the event in July 2000.

Held in Saudi Arabia in the final edition of its old seven-team format, this tournament for the world's top teams saw Manchester City rout Fluminense 4-0 in the final for their first title — which competition is it?
2023 FIFA Club World Cup: Football competition in Saudi Arabia. The English team won the edition by beating the Brazilian team Fluminense 4–0 in the final, claiming their first title.

The shortest standard outdoor sprint distance in track and field, this blue-riband dash has been run at the Olympics since 1896 for men and 1928 for women, always starting with 'on your marks, set' — which event is it?
100 metres: Sprint race. The shortest common outdoor running distance, the 100-metre (109.36 yd) dash is one of the most popular and prestigious events in the sport of athletics.

Founded in 1895 as a rowing club before playing its first football match in 1912, which Rio de Janeiro team — famous for its red-and-black striped shirts — boasts more fans than any other club in Brazil?
CR Flamengo: Brazilian football club. It was founded and named after the Flamengo neighborhood in 1895 and is best known for its professional football team.

The first edition of this quadrennial men's football championship to be jointly hosted by two nations — Japan and South Korea — saw defending champion France crash out in the group stage without scoring a goal. Which tournament is it?

2002 FIFA World Cup: Association football tournament in Japan and South Korea. It was held from 31 May to 30 June 2002 at sites in Japan and South Korea, with its final match hosted by Japan at International Stadium in Yokohama.

Originally launched as an under-16 championship before both the age cutoff and the name changed, this annual global football tournament for teenage boys saw Portugal claim its first-ever title in 2025 — which competition is this?
FIFA U-17 World Cup: Football tournament.

Ashley Biden: American social worker and fashion designer (born 1981)
Loosely based on the tale of Pinocchio, this 2023 Soulslike game casts you as an automaton navigating a Belle Époque-inspired city called Krat — what is this game called?
Lies of P: 2023 video game. Lies of P is a 2023 action role-playing game developed by Neowiz and Round8 Studio and published by Neowiz.
Set in Venice and Cyprus, this Shakespeare tragedy follows a Moorish military commander manipulated by his ensign into believing his wife has been unfaithful — what is the play called?
Othello: Play by William Shakespeare written circa 1603.
A former competitive fencer turned Hong Kong idol, this Got7 member founded his own record label and fashion brand, and later topped Chinese celebrities' Instagram follower counts — who is he?

Released in 2013 by Swedish developer Robert Topala, this rhythm-based platformer sends players guiding an icon past obstacles across 26 built-in levels, with an editor for user-made ones — what is this game called?
Geometry Dash: 2013 video game. Geometry Dash is a 2013 side-scrolling rhythm platform video game developed by Swedish game developer Robert Topala and published by his company RobTop Games.
Known by a pen name meaning 'the one who helps,' this Emirati royal has served as Crown Prince of Dubai since 2008 and is also a multiple world champion equestrian — who is he?
Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum: Crown Prince of Dubai (born 1982)
Studying architecture in Paris when she met her future husband, this philanthropist became the last empress of Iran and founded the country's first American-style university — who is she?
Farah Pahlavi: Queen-Empress of Iran from 1959 to 1979.
This actress appeared in Blade Runner in 1982 and returned for its 2017 sequel, having also starred in Stripes, Dune, and Wall Street throughout the 1980s — who is she?
Launching his eponymous fashion house in 1968, this American designer went on to lend his name to a range of perfumes, watches, and jewelry — who is he?
This literary device tells a story where characters, places, or events symbolize deeper moral or political meanings, often personifying abstract ideas — what is it?
Allegory: Literary device. The title of "first allegorist", however, is usually awarded to whoever was the earliest to put forth allegorical interpretations of Homer.
In 1982, this Georgia-born writer became the first African-American woman to win the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, for a novel called The Color Purple — who is she?
Alice Walker: American author and activist (born 1944)
Born in 810 in what is now Uzbekistan, this 9th-century scholar compiled a landmark collection of hadith in 846 and is revered as Sunni Islam's most important such scholar — who is he?
This 8th-century Indian scholar-monk founded the school of Advaita Vedanta and wrote influential commentaries on the Brahma Sutras — who is he?
Adi Shankara: 8th-century Indian Vedic scholar. Reliable information on Shankara's actual life is scant, and the historical influence of his works on Hindu intellectual thought has been questioned.
This Russian lyric poet's verses nostalgically evoke his rural childhood village while implicitly cursing the rise of cities and industry — who is he?
This Dutch humanist and Catholic theologian prepared pioneering Latin and Greek scholarly editions of the New Testament that proved vitally influential during the Protestant Reformation — who is he?
After escaping slavery in Maryland in 1838, this orator and writer became a leading voice of the American abolitionist movement — who is he?
Written by Shakespeare around 1605, this tragedy set in pre-Roman Britain follows an aging monarch who divides his realm based on his three daughters' professions of love — which play?
King Lear: Play by William Shakespeare. The Tragedy of King Lear, often shortened to King Lear, is a tragedy written by William Shakespeare in late 1605 or early 1606.
Born Józef Teodor Konrad Korzeniowski in Poland, this novelist didn't speak English fluently until his twenties yet became a master prose stylist known for nautical settings — who is he?
Written by Yōichi Takahashi and serialized in Weekly Shōnen Jump from 1981 to 1988, this football-themed manga follows a boy named Oozora as he grows through rivalries and matches — which series?
Captain Tsubasa: Japanese manga series. Across the multiple Captain Tsubasa series, the plot shows Tsubasa's and his friends' growth as they face new rivals.

Developed by Insomniac Games, this 2018 action-adventure video game sends its web-slinging hero after a crime lord named Mister Negative who threatens to unleash a deadly virus on New York City — what is it?
Marvel's Spider-Man (video game) is a 2018 action-adventure game developed by Insomniac Games and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment.

Originally self-published as an ebook in 2011 by E. L. James, this erotic romance novel follows a college graduate's deepening relationship with a young business magnate and set a UK record as the fastest-selling paperback ever — which novel?

Fifty Shades of Grey: 2011 erotic novel by E.L. James. It contains explicitly erotic scenes featuring elements of sexual practices involving bondage/discipline, dominance/submission, and sadism/masochism (BDSM).
This 2016 role-playing game from P-Studio, the sixth entry in a spin-off series from Megami Tensei, later got an enhanced 'Royal' edition — which game?
Persona 5: 2016 video game. Royal was released on the PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch, and Windows on October 21, 2022.
Born Anthony J. Mahavorić, this American motivational speaker wrote the bestsellers Unlimited Power and Awaken the Giant Within — who is he?
A CIA officer turned Watergate burglar, this member of Nixon's so-called White House Plumbers helped orchestrate the break-in alongside G. Gordon Liddy — who is he?
E. Howard Hunt: American intelligence officer and author (1918–2007)
Players control monster slayer Geralt of Rivia as he searches for his adopted daughter Ciri in this 2015 open-world RPG from CD Projekt — which game?
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt: 2015 video game. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt‍ is a 2015 action role-playing game developed and published by CD Projekt.
Originally a divination manual from the Western Zhou period, this ancient Chinese classic later gained philosophical commentaries known as the Ten Wings — which text?
I Ching: Ancient Chinese divination text. Each of the 64 possible sets corresponds to a hexagram, which can be looked up in the I Ching.
Largely unrecognized in his lifetime, this English poet and printmaker described imagination as 'the body of God' and was considered mad by contemporaries — who is he?
William Blake: English poet and artist (1757–1827)
This medieval style, born from Romanesque forms in 12th-century Northern France, is recognized through sculpture, stained glass, fresco and illuminated manuscripts — which style?
Gothic art: Style of medieval art. It spread to all of Western Europe, and much of Northern, Southern and Central Europe, never quite effacing more classical styles in Italy.
Robert Louis Stevenson's tale of buccaneers and buried gold, serialized under the pseudonym Captain George North, helped define our modern image of pirates — which novel?
Treasure Island: 1883 novel by Robert Louis Stevenson.
Which 16th-century French theologian, based in Geneva, developed the reformed doctrine of predestination that came to bear his own name?
Married in 1863 to the future Edward VII, which queen consort held the title Princess of Wales longer than anyone else in history?
Alexandra of Denmark: Queen of the United Kingdom from 1901 to 1910.
Known for a raw, frenetic technique he calls 'dirty style,' which Los Angeles artist and podcast host has illustrated for Vice and Hustler magazines?
Released for PlayStation 4 in 2018, this Quantic Dream adventure game follows three androids whose story branches based on player choices — which game?
Detroit: Become Human: 2018 video game. Detroit: Become Human is a 2018 adventure game developed by Quantic Dream and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment.
This genre of dramatic works aims to induce laughter across theatre, film, stand-up, television, and radio — what genre?
Comedy: Genre of dramatic works intended to be humorous.
This British political commentator and Spectator associate editor wrote a controversial 2017 book warning about immigration, identity, and Islam in Europe. Who is he?
Douglas Murray (author) (born 16 July 1979) is a British conservative political commentator, cultural critic, author, and journalist.
Fleeing North Korea for China at age 13 in 2007, this defector later wrote a bestselling memoir, In Order to Live, before becoming an American conservative commentator — who is she?
Yeonmi Park: North Korean defector and activist (born 1993)
Devoted to the deity Rama, this Hindu poet-saint authored the Hanuman Chalisa and retold the Ramayana in the vernacular Awadhi language as an epic still performed today — who was he?
This psychopathic, narcissistic leader of a corporate-funded superhero team in The Boys is a dark parody of Superman and archenemy of Billy Butcher — who is he?
Nearly all written in rhymed verse and considered the greatest work of German literature, this two-part tragic play was first published as a fragment in 1790 — which play?
Goethe's Faust: Play by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe.
A protégé of Gustave Flaubert, this 19th-century French author wrote 300 short stories, including his renowned 1880 debut about a dumpling-selling traveler. Who was he?
Dubbed the 'Father of Comparative Religion' and the founder of Indology, this 10th-century Khwarazmian polymath is also considered history's first anthropologist. Who was he?
Convicted of masterminding the 1995 sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway, this doomsday cult leader was executed in 2018. Who was he?
Shoko Asahara: Founder of Aum Shinrikyo (1955–2018)
As the youngest child and only daughter of Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin, her dramatic 1967 defection to the United States made her an overnight sensation. Who was she?
Svetlana Alliluyeva: Youngest child of Joseph Stalin (1926–2011)
This Chinese actor is considered one of the 'Big Four Traffic Stars' for his immense influence, debuting in a 2010 drama and later starring in adaptations like The King's Avatar. Who is he?
Yang Yang (actor) (simplified; traditional) is a Chinese actor.
Often called the father of tragedy, this ancient Greek playwright wrote as many as ninety plays, though only seven survive complete — who was he?
Collected by the Brothers Grimm in 1812, this German fairy tale features an imp who spins straw into gold in exchange for a woman's firstborn child — what is it called?
Serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump from 2016 to 2020, this manga follows orphaned children plotting an escape after discovering a dark secret about their orphanage — which series?
The Promised Neverland: Japanese manga series and franchise.
Born in Persia's Gilan province around 1077 and buried in Baghdad, this Hanbali preacher and Sufi mystic lent his name to one of the oldest Sufi orders — who was he?
Abdul Qadir Gilani: Muslim preacher, mystic and theologian (1078–1166)
After co-founding a chain of jeans stores called People's Place, this American designer built a preppy menswear label he later sold for $1.6 billion in 2006 — who is he?
Called the most performed Norwegian playwright since Henrik Ibsen, this author won the 2023 Nobel Prize in Literature for plays that give 'voice to the unsayable' — who is he?
Jon Fosse: Norwegian author and dramatist (born 1959)
Announced at the PlayStation 5 reveal event, this 2021 survival horror sequel has Ethan Winters searching a monster-filled European hamlet for his kidnapped daughter — what's the game?
Resident Evil Village: 2021 video game. Players control Ethan Winters, who searches for his kidnapped daughter in a mysterious European village filled with mutant creatures.
This CNN anchor has hosted The Source since 2023 and has twice served as the network's chief White House correspondent, including during the second Trump presidency — who is she?

Painted by Eugène Delacroix to commemorate the 1830 revolution that toppled King Charles X, this canvas personifies a virtue as a bare-breasted woman in a Phrygian cap guiding citizens over a barricade — what's its title?
Liberty Leading the People: 1830 painting by Eugène Delacroix. The figure of Liberty is also viewed as a symbol of France and the French Republic known as Marianne.
Serialized in Square Enix's Young Gangan since 2017, this manga by Ryohgo Narita and Shinta Fujimoto received a two-cour anime adaptation from Geek Toys in 2023 — what's its title?
Dead Mount Death Play: Japanese manga series and its adaptations.
Regarded as the father of the Japanese short story, this Taishō-era writer has Japan's premier literary award named in his honor and died by suicide at 35 — who is he?

Released in 2017, this action RPG follows a huntress named Aloy through a post-apocalyptic America dominated by robotic machines — Guerrilla Games' first new IP since a 2004 shooter series. What's the game?
Horizon Zero Dawn: 2017 video game. Horizon Zero Dawn is a 2017 action role-playing game developed by Guerrilla Games and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment.
Known for his 'drip technique' of pouring and splashing paint onto a canvas laid on the floor, this abstract expressionist painter was married to fellow artist Lee Krasner — who was he?
This Japanese manga, serialized in Kodansha's Morning since 1998, fictionalizes the life of a legendary swordsman and has sold over 82 million copies despite being on hiatus since 2015. What is it?
Vagabond (manga) is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Takehiko Inoue.
Serialized in Kodansha's Monthly Afternoon since 2018 and adapted into a 2023 anime by P.A. Works, this manga won the Kodansha Manga Award's general category that same year — which series?
Skip and Loafer: Japanese manga series. Skip and Loafer (Japanese: スキップとローファー, Hepburn: Sukippu to Rōfā) is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Misaki Takamatsu.

Born under a slightly different surname, this Scottish philosopher argued that belief in cause and effect can never be proven by pure reason alone, laying out his ideas in an 1739 treatise on human nature — who is he?
David Hume: Scottish philosopher, historian, economist and essayist (1711–1776)
Written by Alice Walker in 1982, this epistolary novel won both the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction and the National Book Award before becoming a hit stage musical — which novel?
The Color Purple: 1982 novel by Alice Walker.
This literary genre stars anthropomorphized animals or objects to deliver an explicit moral at the end — unlike a parable, which sticks to human characters. What is it called?
Fable: Short fictional story that anthropomorphises non-humans to illustrate a moral lesson.

Born in Venice and trained in canon law, this legendary 18th-century adventurer traded a churchly career for life as a gambler, violinist and card sharp, memorialized in his own sprawling memoir — who is he?
Giacomo Casanova: Venetian adventurer and writer (1725–1798)
Teaching at a school called 'The Garden' in Athens, this ancient Greek philosopher held that a pleasant life comes from managing desires and banishing needless fears — who was he?
After a painful breakup, a Tokyo college student in this manga hires a paid companion to pose as his partner — and falls for her for real. What's the series?
Rent-A-Girlfriend: Japanese manga series. It has been serialized in Kodansha's Weekly Shōnen Magazine since July 2017, and has been compiled into forty-six tankōbon volumes as of June 2026.
This viral internet horror tale claims five Soviet test subjects were kept awake indefinitely with a stimulant — fact-checkers traced it to a 2010 Creepypasta Wiki post. What's the story called?
Born in Gaza and raised in Mecca, this 8th-century scholar wrote the first book on the principles of Islamic jurisprudence and gave his name to a major school of Sunni Islamic law — who is he?
Al-Shafi'i: Muslim scholar, jurist, and traditionist (767–820)

This Marvel Comics character is a sentient alien organism that bonds with a host for enhanced powers, first appearing as a living costume before Spider-Man himself became its original human host. What is it?
Venom (character) is a character appearing in American comic books published by Marvel Comics.
Reclusive after the runaway success of his 1951 novel about adolescent alienation, who wrote 'A Perfect Day for Bananafish' and The Catcher in the Rye?
Traditionally created by carving away stone or modelling with clay, which three-dimensional visual art form has left far more stone examples than wooden ones from ancient cultures?
Sculpture: Artworks that are three-dimensional objects.
Often metaphorical and rooted equally in the Bible and medieval Latin tradition, what term describes a short traditional saying that expresses a perceived truth?
Proverb: Traditional saying that reveals a thought truth.
Northrop Frye called its irony 'militant' — which genre uses ridicule, parody, and exaggeration to expose the vices and follies of society?
Satire: Literary and art genre with a style of humor based on parody.
Written by Machiavelli as an instruction guide for rulers, this 16th-century treatise argues that immoral acts are sometimes necessary to achieve political glory — what is it called?

The Prince: Political treatise by Niccolò Machiavelli. Although The Prince was written as if it were a traditional work in the mirrors for princes style, it was generally agreed as being especially innovative.
This Puccini opera premiered at Milan's La Scala in 1904 to a poor initial reception, based on a story dramatized by David Belasco after a French novel by Pierre Loti — which opera?
Madama Butterfly: 1904 opera by Giacomo Puccini. The original version of the opera, in two acts, had its premiere on 17 February 1904 at La Scala in Milan.
Born in 1963, this Russian fashion designer died in 2023 — who is he?
Traditionally credited as the author of The Art of War, this ancient Chinese strategist's very existence remains historically uncertain — who is he?
Sun Tzu: Chinese general (26 August 544 – 10 September 496 BC)
This American diplomat and former Fox News host, once first lady of San Francisco during her marriage to Gavin Newsom, has served as U.S. ambassador to Greece since 2025 — who is she?
Answering a 1967 New Musical Express ad seeking songwriters, this English lyricist teamed up with Elton John and later shared an Oscar for a song from the film Rocketman — who is he?
Born Juan Pablo Escobar Henao, this Colombian architect and author took a new name after his father, a notorious Colombian drug lord, was killed — who is he?

Sebastián Marroquín: Colombian architect, author, and the son of Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar. Juan Sebastián Marroquín Santos (born Juan Pablo Escobar Henao; 24 February 1977) is a Colombian architect, author, and the son of Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar.
Legend holds that seventy-two Hebrew scholars translated the Jewish scriptures into Koine Greek for Ptolemy II — what is this earliest known Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible called?
Septuagint: Greek translation of Hebrew scriptures. The remaining books were presumably translated in the 2nd century BC.
A member of the Brazilian Academy of Letters since 2002, this novelist's 1988 book The Alchemist became an international best-seller — who is he?
Paulo Coelho: Brazilian lyricist and novelist (born 1947)
Serialized in 1897 and published as a novel the following year, this H. G. Wells story follows an alien invasion of Earth by beings from a dying, exhausted planet — which novel?
The War of the Worlds: 1898 science fiction novel by H. G. Wells.
Serialized in Weekly Shōnen Jump from 1983 to 1988, this manga follows a martial artist named Kenshiro as he battles gangs and warlords on a post-apocalyptic Earth after nuclear war — which series?
Fist of the North Star: Japanese manga series and franchise.
Serialized digitally in Shueisha's Shonen Jump+ from 2017 to 2021, this mystery manga by Yasuki Tanaka got an anime adaptation by OLM in 2022 — what's the series?
Summer Time Rendering: Japanese manga series by Yasuki Tanaka and its franchise.
Created by Robert Kirkman for Image Comics, this alien superhero is secretly the father of the teen hero Invincible, and is voiced by J.K. Simmons in the animated series — who is he?
Omni-Man: Fictional character from Image Comics.
Inspired by Romeo and Juliet, this Leonard Bernstein musical follows warring 1950s New York gangs the Jets and the Sharks — and the doomed romance between two of their own. Which show is it?
West Side Story: Musical by Leonard Bernstein and Stephen Sondheim.
Rediscovered by the Pre-Raphaelites after a long slump in reputation, this Early Renaissance Italian painter created The Birth of Venus and Primavera — who is he?
Considered the most authentic Islamic text after the Quran, this ninth-century hadith collection was organized in Mecca and Medina before being completed by a renowned scholar — what is it?
Sahih al-Bukhari: First hadith collection of the Six Books of Sunni Islam.
Having once studied medicine, this designer left Cerruti 1881 to found his own Italian fashion house in 1975, becoming famous for minimalist suits and dominating red-carpet style — who is he?

Serialized in Weekly Shōnen Magazine from 2015 to 2022, this manga by Atsushi Ohkubo follows a boy with pyrokinetic powers battling flame-based monsters in a devastated Tokyo, and serves as a prequel to the author's earlier hit, Soul Eater. What's the series?
Fire Force: Japanese manga series and its franchise.

Published posthumously in 1977 by his son Christopher, this collection of Tolkien myths was originally meant to be The Hobbit's sequel, but publisher Stanley Unwin rejected the draft as 'too Celtic' — prompting Tolkien to write The Lord of the Rings instead. What's the book?
The Silmarillion: Collection of J. R. R. Tolkien's mythopoeic works.
Born in Nuremberg, this German Renaissance master built his early reputation on masterful woodcut prints before Emperor Maximilian I became his patron in 1512 — who is he?
Albrecht Dürer: German artist and theorist (1471–1528)

The granddaughter of L'Oréal's founder and the only child of its principal shareholder, this French heiress saw her fortune triple after her mother's 2017 death, making her the world's second-richest woman — who is she?
Françoise Bettencourt Meyers: French billionaire heiress (born 1953)

Though it won only second place at its debut around 429 BC, Aristotle later hailed this Sophocles tragedy as one of the greatest Greek plays ever written — and it's arguably the most famous of them all. What's the play?
Oedipus Rex: Classical Athenian tragedy by Sophocles.
This actress played Laurie Keller on Cougar Town, later hosted her own E! talk show, and starred in the streaming comedy Girls5eva — who is she?
Busy Philipps: American actress, singer and comedian.
Since 1995, this Canadian journalist has served as a correspondent for the true-crime newsmagazine Dateline NBC — who is he?
Written in 1937 by Genzaburō Yoshino, this Japanese novel is known in the original as Kimi-tachi wa Dō Ikiru ka. What's its English title?
How Do You Live?: 1937 novel by Yoshino Genzaburō.
Born a princess in Scandinavia, this woman became Empress of Russia as the wife of Alexander III, and her eldest son would become the country's last emperor — who was she?
Maria Feodorovna (Dagmar of Denmark): Empress of Russia from 1881 to 1894.
Commissioned by a political league and published in London in 1848, this pamphlet opens with a warning about a 'spectre' haunting Europe and closes urging workers worldwide to unite — what is it?
The Communist Manifesto: 1848 political pamphlet by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels.

With a €70 million budget, this 2023 survival horror sequel became one of the priciest video games ever made in Finland, following a best-selling novelist trapped in an alternate dimension for over a decade — what game?
Alan Wake 2: 2023 video game. Alan Wake 2 is a 2023 survival horror video game developed by Remedy Entertainment and published by Epic Games Publishing.
Written over 25 years and awarded the 2006 Pulitzer Prize, this biography chronicles the physicist who led the Manhattan Project — and his downfall in a McCarthy-era security hearing. What book?
American Prometheus: 2005 biography of J. Robert Oppenheimer.
Recruited by Soviet intelligence while at Cambridge in 1934, this British double agent became the most successful member of a notorious spy ring exposed in 1963 — who is he?
Kim Philby: British intelligence officer and Soviet double agent (1912–1988)

Announced in 2012 after a Kickstarter that raised over $2 million, this long-in-development space trading and combat sim from Cloud Imperium Games still has no firm release date — its single-player spinoff is Squadron 42. What game is it?
Star Citizen: In-development multiplayer space game. Star Citizen is a multiplayer, space trading and combat simulation video game currently under development by Cloud Imperium Games for Windows.

Writing under a pen name, this Russian author and politician led the National Bolshevik Party for over two decades before founding a national-conservative party that later merged into A Just Russia — who is he?
Zakhar Prilepin: Russian writer and politician (born 1975)
Played by Marlon Brando in 1972 and by Robert De Niro as a young man two years later, this orphaned Sicilian immigrant builds a Mafia empire and is succeeded as Don by his son Michael — who is he?
Vito Corleone: Fictional character from The Godfather.

Released in 2019 by Respawn Entertainment, this Metroidvania-style action-adventure follows Padawan Cal Kestis as he evades Imperial Inquisitors while trying to rebuild what the Empire destroyed — what game is it?
Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order: 2019 video game. Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is a 2019 action-adventure game developed by Respawn Entertainment and published by Electronic Arts.

An outspoken democratic socialist and public intellectual, this American philosopher ran as an independent candidate in the 2024 U.S. presidential election after professorships at Harvard, Yale, and Princeton — who is he?
Cornel West: American philosopher, activist, and theologian (born 1953)

A leading figure of the Russian Futurist movement, this poet co-signed the manifesto 'A Slap in the Face of Public Taste' and later produced agitprop posters supporting the Bolsheviks during the Russian Civil War — who is he?

Imprisoned in 1926 for his outspoken opposition to Mussolini, this founding member of the Italian Communist Party filled more than 30 notebooks with political theory before his death in 1937 — who is he?
Antonio Gramsci: Italian Marxist philosopher, writer, and politician (1891–1937)
A furniture maker and honorary chairman of Christie's, this member of the British royal family is Princess Margaret's only son and was once fifth in line to the throne — who is he?
David Armstrong-Jones, 2nd Earl of Snowdon: British businessman and peer (born 1961)
This English sports broadcaster has anchored CBS Sports' UEFA Champions League coverage since 2020, having worked across the UK, Spain, France, Germany, and the US — who is she?
Kate Scott (British presenter): English sports broadcaster (born 1981)
Raised by great apes in the Congolian rainforest after being orphaned as an infant, this Edgar Rice Burroughs hero briefly embraces civilization before choosing to return to the wild — who is he?
Tarzan: Fictional character by Edgar Rice Burroughs.

Published in 1996, this epic fantasy novel by George R. R. Martin opens a saga where noble houses vie for power across the Seven Kingdoms, while a wall of ice guards against enemies to the north — which book is this?
A Game of Thrones: 1996 novel by George R. R. Martin. It was published in August 1996 as the first entry in his series A Song of Ice and Fire.
Born in St. Louis but later a British subject, this poet won the 1948 Nobel Prize in Literature and startled readers with 'The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock' — who is he?
T. S. Eliot: Poet, essayist and playwright (1888–1965)

In this 2023 side-scrolling platformer, players stop the series' longtime villain from fusing a magical flower with a kingdom's castle, becoming the fastest-selling entry in its franchise — which game?
Super Mario Bros. Wonder: 2023 video game. Wonder is a 2023 platform game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo Switch.
She earned Emmy and Golden Globe nominations for playing Joan Girardi, then won Best Actress at the Locarno Film Festival for a role opposite Tilda Swinton — who is this actress-turned-director?
Amber Tamblyn: American actress and author (born 1983)
Blending the Greek myths of Orpheus and Eurydice with Hades and Persephone, this musical began as a Vermont concept album before reaching Broadway in 2019 — which show?
She married a martial arts film legend who died in 1973, and later wrote a biography of him that inspired a 1993 movie — who is she?
Linda Lee Cadwell: American teacher, writer, the widow of Bruce Lee.
In this 1845 Edgar Allan Poe poem, a grieving man is visited by a bird perched on a bust of Pallas that repeats a single word: 'nevermore' — which poem?
The Raven: 1845 narrative poem by Edgar Allan Poe. It tells of a distraught lover who is paid a visit by a mysterious raven that repeatedly speaks a single word: "nevermore".
This Dr. Seuss character has been voiced by actors ranging from Boris Karloff to Jim Carrey to Benedict Cumberbatch since debuting in a 1957 book — who is he?
Grinch: Fictional character created by Dr. Seuss.
Emerging in response to secularization and the rise of science, this early 20th-century movement rejected tradition in favor of experimentation and abstraction across the arts — what is it called?
In this Agatha Christie novel, a girl who boasts of once witnessing a murder is later found drowned in an apple-bobbing bucket, sending Hercule Poirot to investigate — which book?
Hallowe'en Party: 1969 mystery novel by Agatha Christie.
After her Italian roommate's 2007 murder in Perugia, this American author was convicted, acquitted, reconvicted, and finally acquitted for good by Italy's highest court in 2015 — who is she?
Amanda Knox: American writer and activist (born 1987)
Attributed, disputedly, to a 13th-century Sufi scholar, this grimoire on Arabic magic has a notorious reputation for being banned throughout much of Islamic history — what's this work called?
Shams al-Ma'arif: 13th-century book by Ahmad al-Buni.
Planned as ten novels by Brandon Sanderson within his broader Cosmere universe, this fantasy series saw its fifth entry, 'Wind and Truth,' released in December 2024 — what's the series called?

The Stormlight Archive: Series of epic fantasy novels by Brandon Sanderson. The Stormlight Archive is a high fantasy novel series written by American author Brandon Sanderson, planned to consist of ten novels.
Famous for 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa' from his series on Mount Fuji, this Edo-period printmaker later influenced Van Gogh and Monet during Europe's Japonisme craze — who is he?
Writing in both English and French, this Irish playwright won the 1969 Nobel Prize in Literature for tragicomic works including 'Waiting for Godot' — who is he?
The only daughter of Princess Margaret, she was seventh in line to the British throne at birth and is now 29th as of 2026 — who is she?
Lady Sarah Chatto: British royal family member (born 1964)
Written by Virgil between 29 and 19 BC in dactylic hexameter, this Latin epic follows a Trojan survivor's journey to Italy to become an ancestor of the Romans — what's this poem called?
Aeneid: Latin epic poem by Virgil. Written by the Roman poet Virgil between 29 and 19 BC, the Aeneid comprises 9,896 lines in dactylic hexameter.
A radical in both his poetry and politics, this English Romantic poet found little fame in his own lifetime but went on to influence Browning, Swinburne, Hardy, and Yeats — who is he?
Dubbed 'the poet of the Caucasus,' he became Russia's most important poet after Pushkin's 1837 death and founded the tradition of the Russian psychological novel — who is he?
Mikhail Lermontov: Russian writer, poet and painter (1814–1841)
Raised in a French-speaking household in Lowell, Massachusetts, this Beat Generation pioneer achieved fame with his 1957 novel 'On the Road' — who is he?
This Japanese fashion model wrote 'I Love Being Me,' a book about self-acceptance — who is she?
This American fashion entrepreneur co-founded a wildly popular handbag and accessories brand carrying her own name, active from 1962 until her death in 2018 — who was she?

Kate Spade: American fashion designer (1962–2018). Katherine Noel Valentine Brosnahan Spade (born Katherine Noel Brosnahan; December 24, 1962 – June 5, 2018) was an American fashion designer and entrepreneur.
Called the bridge between 19th-century Impressionism and early Cubism, this French Post-Impressionist painter reshaped how artists approached perspective and structure — who was he?
Developed by FromSoftware for PS4, this 2015 action RPG sends a Hunter into the Gothic city of Yharnam to battle beasts and eldritch horrors — which game?
Bloodborne: 2015 video game. Bloodborne is a 2015 action role-playing game developed by FromSoftware and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 4.

In this web manga serialized on Shonen Jump+ since 2019, a young man who stumbles into a dimensional portal is rescued by an elite officer of an all-female defense force — which series, whose 2024 anime was animated by Seven Arcs?
Chained Soldier: Japanese manga series and its adaptation(s)

The leading theorist of Russian neo-Eurasianism, he co-founded the National Bolshevik Party in 1993 and later wrote 'Foundations of Geopolitics,' urging Russia to rebuild its influence through alliances and conquest — who is he?

Co-founder of the largest fund for food-allergy research in the U.S. and once briefly employed at Andy Warhol's Factory, this designer-turned-fundraiser's 2012 death drew major national attention after a highly publicized separation — who was she?
Mary Richardson Kennedy: American designer and philanthropist (1959–2012)

Franz Kafka's protagonist Josef K. is arrested and prosecuted by an authority that never reveals his crime in this unfinished novel, published posthumously in 1925 by his friend Max Brod — what's the book?
The Trial: 1925 novel by Franz Kafka. The Trial (German: Der Prozess) is a novel written by Franz Kafka in 1914 and 1915 and published posthumously on 26 April 1925.
Created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby in 1962, this armored monarch of the fictional nation of Latveria is the archenemy of the Fantastic Four — who is he?
Doctor Doom: Supervillain appearing in Marvel Comics.
Premiering in Turin in 1896 under a 28-year-old Arturo Toscanini, this Puccini opera follows a poor seamstress and her artist friends in 1830s Paris — which opera is it?
La bohème: 1896 opera by Giacomo Puccini.
Only the first of this three-volume critique of political economy was published in Marx's lifetime, in 1867 — the rest were completed by Friedrich Engels. What's the work?
Das Kapital: Three-volume work by Karl Marx, 1867–1894.
Released in 2015, this action RPG casts you as the 'Sole Survivor' emerging from cryo-sleep in Vault 111 to explore a post-apocalyptic Boston known as the Commonwealth — which game?
Fallout 4: 2015 video game. Fallout 4 is a 2015 action role-playing game developed by Bethesda Game Studios and published by Bethesda Softworks.
Despite the name, this digestive organ is about 6.5 metres long; it's just narrower in diameter than its large counterpart. What organ is it?
Control (video game) is a 2019 action-adventure game developed by Remedy Entertainment.
This American author is best known for writing the young-adult dystopian series 'The Hunger Games' as well as the children's fantasy series 'The Underland Chronicles' — who is she?
Suzanne Collins: American author and television writer (born 1962)
As Japan's 15th and final shogun, this samurai resigned his post in late 1867 but lost his remaining influence after defeat at the Battle of Toba–Fushimi — who was he?
Tokugawa Yoshinobu: Japanese samurai and Military ruler from 1866 to 1868 (1837–1913)
Born into slavery in Phrygia, this Stoic philosopher was later banished from Rome and founded his own school in Nicopolis, teaching calm acceptance of what's beyond our control — who was he?
In this 2016 Naughty Dog game, retired treasure hunter Nathan Drake is coaxed back into action by his presumed-dead brother in search of a legendary pirate's lost fortune — which game?
Uncharted 4: A Thief's End: 2016 video game. Uncharted 4: A Thief's End is a 2016 action-adventure game developed by Naughty Dog and published by Sony Computer Entertainment.
This fictional Fleet Street barber murders his customers with a straight razor, then hands the corpses to his partner to bake into meat pies — who is he?
Sweeney Todd: Fictional serial killer barber.
Championed by critic John Ruskin, this English Romantic painter left behind more than 550 oil paintings and pioneered a turbulent, colour-drenched style that foreshadowed Impressionism — who was he?
J. M. W. Turner: English painter (1775–1851)
Fired from a Montana copper mine after causing a city-wide power outage, this daredevil went on to attempt more than 75 ramp-to-ramp motorcycle jumps — who was he?
Written by Riichiro Inagaki and illustrated by Ryoichi Ikegami, this seinen manga won the 69th Shogakukan Manga Award in 2024 before getting a Madhouse anime adaptation — what is it called?
In this 2017 novel by Taylor Jenkins Reid, an aging fictional Old Hollywood star grants a young journalist one final tell-all interview — what is the book called?
The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo

The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
This German film depicts the final days of Adolf Hitler, played by Bruno Ganz, during the Battle of Berlin in World War II. What film is it?
Cyrano de Bergerac (play) (d, - BAIR-) is a French play written in 1897 by Edmond Rostand.
Named after a French term evoking wandering artists, this 19th-century movement idealized art and friendship over money among Latin Quarter creatives in Paris — what is it called?
Bohemianism: Practice of an unconventional lifestyle.
Created in 1941 and later reimagined as the weighty king of an undersea kingdom, this founding Justice League member is the son of a lighthouse keeper and an oceanic queen — who is he?
Named after a T. Rex song, this Naoki Urasawa manga follows Kenji Endo's fight against a shadowy cult leader called 'Friend' whose symbol matches one from his childhood — what's the series?
20th Century Boys: Japanese manga series. 20th Century Boys (Japanese: 20世紀少年, Hepburn: Nijusseiki Shōnen) is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Naoki Urasawa.
Voted the world's best football referee six years running from 1998 to 2003, this Italian later chaired FIFA's referees committee — who is he?
Pierluigi Collina: Italian football referee and financial advisor.
Self-styled 'Mr. Wonderful,' this Canadian businessman built his reputation on Dragons' Den before becoming a fixture on the American version, Shark Tank — who is he?
Kevin O'Leary: Canadian businessman and author (born 1954)
Claiming to have been trained by mystical 'Masters of Ancient Wisdom' in Tibet, this Russian-born writer co-founded the Theosophical Society in 1875 — who is she?
Helena Blavatsky: Russian-American mystic and writer (1831–1891)
The only book in its wizarding-school series to win a Hugo Award, this fourth installment follows a young wizard mysteriously entered into a deadly three-way magical tournament — what's the book?
Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire: 2000 fantasy novel by J. K. Rowling.
Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire

Ten young Florentines shelter in a country villa from the Black Death, passing the time by telling 100 tales of love, wit, and tragedy — what's this 14th-century collection by Boccaccio?
The Decameron: 14th-century collection of stories by Giovanni Boccaccio.
A socially anxious high schooler teams up with her classmate on a mission to make 100 friends in this manga by Tomohito Oda — what's the series?

Komi Can't Communicate: Japanese manga series by Tomohito Oda. It was serialized in Shogakukan's shōnen manga magazine Weekly Shōnen Sunday from May 2016 to January 2025, with its chapters collected in 37 tankōbon volumes.
Written by Italian author Carlo Collodi and serialized before its 1883 book publication, this novel follows a mischievous wooden marionette who dreams of becoming a real boy — what's the story?
The Adventures of Pinocchio: 1883 children's novel by Carlo Collodi. Since then, Pinocchio has been one of the most popular children's books and has been critically acclaimed.
A psychic boy named Shigeo Kageyama struggles to control his emotions in this manga by creator One, later adapted into an anime by studio Bones — name the series?
Mob Psycho 100: Japanese manga series and franchise.
A Baptist pastor's 1992 relationship guide proposes a numbered set of ways partners express affection to each other, though studies haven't strongly backed the theory — name the book?
The Five Love Languages: 1992 book by Gary Chapman.
The third son of a legendary Tamil Nadu chief minister, this Indian politician became president of the DMK party in 2018 and later chief minister himself. Who is he?
The Summer I Turned Pretty (trilogy) is a trilogy of young adult romance novels written by Asian-American author Jenny Han and published by Simon & Schuster.
Four consecutive writing Emmys for Late Night with David Letterman preceded this comedian's cult film Cabin Boy and his later role as Roland Schitt on Schitt's Creek — who is he?
Chris Elliott: American actor, writer, and comedian (born 1960)

First appearing in a trilogy of novels by Timothy Zahn, this blue-skinned Imperial military leader from the Chiss race commands remnants of a fallen empire against Luke Skywalker and friends. Who is he?
The Quarry (video game) is a 2022 interactive drama horror game developed by Supermassive Games and published by 2K.
Set in a Boston bar where regulars gather to escape their troubles, this sitcom's owner and head bartender is a womanizing former Red Sox relief pitcher. What show is it?
Counter-Strike (video game) (also known as Half-) is a 2000 tactical first-person shooter game developed by Valve Corporation and published by Sierra Studios.

Written by Rei Hiroe since 2002, this seinen manga follows a four-member team of pirate mercenaries smuggling goods around Southeast Asia aboard their PT boat, later adapted into an anime by Madhouse — which series?
Black Lagoon: Japanese manga series. Black Lagoon (stylized in all caps) is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Rei Hiroe.
Nicknamed 'The Master of Speech' by Persian scholars, this 13th-century Sufi poet wrote 'Bustan,' later ranked among the 100 greatest books ever by The Guardian — who is he?
Published in 1940, this Hemingway novel follows Robert Jordan, an American demolitions expert assigned to blow up a bridge during the Spanish Civil War's Segovia Offensive — which novel?
For Whom the Bell Tolls: 1940 novel by Ernest Hemingway.
Written by Natsuki Takaya, this manga follows orphan Tohru Honda as she discovers a family cursed to transform into the animals of the Chinese zodiac — which series?
Fruits Basket: Japanese manga series and its adaptations.

In this potentially lethal game of chance, a single round is loaded into a revolver's cylinder before a player spins it, aims at a head or body, and pulls the trigger — what is this dangerous pastime called?
Russian roulette: Potentially lethal game of chance.
This English singer's gritty, bluesy voice turned a cover of a Beatles song into a signature hit on his debut album. Who is he?
Robert Greene (American author) (born May 14, 1959) is an American author of books on strategy, power, and seduction.

Written by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe in just five and a half weeks in 1774, this epistolary novel drew on the author's own tangled love triangles and became a landmark of the Sturm und Drang movement — which book?
The Sorrows of Young Werther: 1774 novel by J.W. Goethe.
This American-Israeli designer coined the term 'material ecology' and led an MIT research group that built structures in collaboration with silkworms, bees, and ants — who is she?
Neri Oxman: American-Israeli designer and academic. Oxman was a professor of Media Arts and Sciences at the MIT Media Lab, where she founded and led the Mediated Matter research group.

Abstract art: Art with a degree of independence from visual references.
This lawyer prosecuted the Rosenbergs in the early 1950s, served as Senator Joseph McCarthy's chief counsel, and later mentored a young Donald Trump in New York business circles — who was he?
Roy Cohn: American lawyer and prosecutor (1927–1986)

Raised in a Quaker family and already collecting anti-slavery petitions at 17, this activist teamed up with Elizabeth Cady Stanton in 1851 to become a driving force of the women's suffrage movement — who was she?
Susan B. Anthony: American women's rights activist (1820–1906)
Created by Steve Ditko and Stan Lee in 1963, this Marvel superhero began as an arrogant neurosurgeon whose car accident led him to become Earth's Sorcerer Supreme — who is he?
Doctor Strange: Marvel Comics fictional character.

According to legend, this Brahmin adviser helped install Chandragupta as the first Mauryan emperor and is traditionally credited as the author of the ancient political treatise Arthashastra — who is he?
Chanakya: Semi-legendary adviser of Chandragupta Maurya.
Named for the French phrase for 'wild beasts,' this early-20th-century art movement led by André Derain and Henri Matisse prized bold color over realistic representation — which movement?

Spot (Marvel Comics) is a supervillain appearing in American comic books published by Marvel Comics, most often as an adversary of Spider-Man and Daredevil.
In this Shakespeare comedy, twins separated by a shipwreck set off a tangled love triangle after Viola disguises herself as a page named Cesario — which play?
Twelfth Night, or What You Will
Twelfth Night: Play by William Shakespeare. The play was not published until its inclusion in the 1623 First Folio.
In this 2024 cooperative shooter from Arrowhead Game Studios, players join the shock troops of Super Earth to spread 'managed democracy' across the galaxy — which game?
Helldivers 2: 2024 video game. Helldivers 2 is a 2024 cooperative multiplayer third-person shooter video game developed by Arrowhead Game Studios and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment.

Often called the father of English literature for The Canterbury Tales, this medieval poet also wrote a scientific treatise on the astrolabe for his young son and became the first writer buried in Poets' Corner — who is he?
Set on the fictional Caribbean island of Yara, this 2021 Ubisoft shooter casts you as guerrilla fighter Dani Rojas battling a dictator voiced by Giancarlo Esposito — which game?
Far Cry 6: 2021 video game. Far Cry 6 is a 2021 first-person shooter game developed by Ubisoft Toronto and published by Ubisoft.
Written and illustrated by Kouta Hirano, this manga follows a secretive organization defending England from vampires and ghouls — what's the series?
Hellsing: Japanese manga series. It was serialized in Shōnen Gahōsha's seinen manga magazine Young King OURs from April 1997 to September 2008, with its chapters collected in ten tankōbon volumes.
First serialized in Shōnen Sunday S in 2010 before moving to Weekly Shōnen Sunday, this Haro Aso manga was collected into 18 volumes and adapted into a three-episode OVA — what's the series?
Alice in Borderland: Japanese suspense manga series by Haro Aso.
The first African American to earn a doctorate from Harvard, this sociologist and civil rights leader founded the Niagara Movement and spent his final years in Ghana — who is he?
W. E. B. Du Bois: American sociologist and activist (1868–1963)

Often called 'the father of modern drama,' this Norwegian playwright pioneered theatrical realism with works like 'A Doll's House' and 'Hedda Gabler,' and by 2014 was the most performed dramatist after Shakespeare. Who was he?

An Armenian genocide survivor and poet, this communist activist led a Paris resistance network of immigrants that carried out attacks on Nazi targets before his 1944 execution - he was later entombed in the Panthéon. Who was he?
This literary and theatrical form depicts an exchange between two or more speakers, most famously developed in the West by Plato through the Socratic method. What form is this?
Dialogue: Conversation between two or more people.

Poor Things: 1992 novel by Alasdair Gray. It won the Whitbread Award and the Guardian Fiction Prize the same year.

Michel de Montaigne: French author and philosopher (1533–1592)
This dance instructor's Pittsburgh studio became the subject of a hit Lifetime reality series about competitive young dancers and their mothers, spawning two spin-off shows in the 2010s. Who is she?
Abby Lee Miller: American dance instructor (born 1965)

W. B. Yeats: Irish poet and playwright (1865–1939)
Published in 2004, this bestselling science-fiction book by a German author became an international hit — what is its title?
The Swarm (Schätzing novel) is a science fiction novel by German author Frank Schtzing.
Canonized in 1900 and often depicted with a bleeding forehead wound believed to be a partial stigmata, this Italian widow-turned-nun is known as the patroness of impossible causes — who is she?
Rita of Cascia: 15th-century Italian Augustinian nun and saint.
Host of a political podcast featuring a recurring 'Change My Mind' segment, this conservative commentator had his YouTube channel demonetized twice, first in 2019 — who is he?

This Czech Art Nouveau artist's swirling theatrical posters for Sarah Bernhardt made him famous in Paris, before he returned home late in life to paint twenty vast canvases chronicling Slavic history — who was he?
Alphonse Mucha: Czech painter, illustrator and graphic artist (1860–1939)

After cutting his teeth on Michael Moore's 'TV Nation,' this British-American broadcaster became known for BBC documentaries probing offbeat American subcultures, beginning with 'Weird Weekends' — who is he?
Louis Theroux: British and American journalist and author (born 1970)
Called the closest thing to a Renaissance man among 20th-century French avant-garde artists, he wrote 'Les Enfants Terribles' and directed 'The Blood of a Poet' — who was he?
Jean Cocteau: French writer and film director (1889–1963)
According to tradition, this semi-legendary monk from Central Asia or India carried Chan Buddhism into China and is popularly, if dubiously, credited with founding Shaolin kung fu — who was he?
Bodhidharma: Semi-legendary founder of Zen Buddhism.

Granddaughter of Grace Kelly and Rainier III, and daughter of Princess Caroline of Hanover, this Monégasque writer ranks twelfth in line to Monaco's throne and has pursued philosophy alongside equestrianism — who is she?

Charlotte Casiraghi: Eldest daughter of Princess Caroline of Monaco. Charlotte Marie Pomeline Casiraghi (born 3 August 1986) is a Monégasque writer and philosopher with experiences working in journalism and publishing.
This American sculptor moved from small tabletop pieces to large free-standing bronze works in the 1980s, and was married to Meryl Streep until their 2017 separation. Who is he?
