Before serving as Chicago's mayor and later as U.S. ambassador to Japan, this Illinois Democrat was Barack Obama's first White House chief of staff — who is he?
Rahm Emanuel: American politician and diplomat (born 1959)

Convicted in 2018 of acting as an unregistered Russian agent, this activist infiltrated the NRA and allegedly tried to set up a secret back channel between the Kremlin and a US presidential campaign — who is she?
Maria Butina: Russian activist and spy (born 1988)

Rivals of the Tories from the 1680s onward, this faction championed constitutional monarchy and played a central role in the 1688 Glorious Revolution before merging into the Liberals by the 1850s — which faction?
Whigs (British political party) were a political party in the Parliaments of England, Scotland, Ireland, Great Britain and the United Kingdom.
Born Farid Khan, this 16th-century ruler founded an empire after defeating the Mughals and made Delhi his capital, earning the title 'the Just King' — who is he?
Sher Shah Suri: Sultan of Hindustan from 1540 to 1545.
A retired Army colonel who led an early tank battle in the Gulf War, this author's 1997 book 'Breaking the Phalanx' argued for radical military reform — who is he?
Douglas Macgregor: U.S. Army colonel and government official (born 1947)
This Dutch politician served as the EU's climate action commissioner from 2019 to 2023 after being First Vice-President of the European Commission under Juncker — who is he?

Raised alongside Alexander the Great and compared by ancient writers to Achilles' companion Patroclus, this Macedonian general commanded the Companion cavalry and corresponded with Aristotle — who was he?
Hephaestion: Macedonian nobleman and general (c. 356–324 BC)

Ruling for just eight months during the chaotic Year of the Four Emperors, this Roman ruler took the honorific Germanicus instead of Caesar and tried to boost his popularity by imitating the still-beloved Nero — who was he?

Despite its name literally meaning 'sour dictionary,' this Turkish collaborative website doesn't require factual accuracy and instead functions as one of the country's oldest social hubs for opinions and debate — which site?
Ekşi Sözlük: Dictionary-based social networking service.
Holding the title 2nd Marquis of Estella, this Spanish military officer ruled as dictator-prime minister from 1923 to 1930 during the twilight of the Bourbon Restoration — who is he?
Miguel Primo de Rivera: Prime Minister of Spain from 1923 to 1930. The coup enjoyed the acquiescence of the monarch, and Primo de Rivera was ensuingly tasked to form a government.
This Turkish engineer-turned-politician founded and leads an Islamist party that's the successor to one his father once led as Turkey's prime minister — who is he?
This biblical figure, son of Nahor, is best known as the father of the patriarch Abraham in the Book of Genesis — who is he?
Terah: Figure in the Hebrew Bible; son of Nahor.

This Colombian economist served as his country's president from 1990 to 1994, then led the Organization of American States for a decade, and summoned the assembly that wrote Colombia's 1991 constitution. Who is he?
César Gaviria: Colombian economist and politician (born 1947)

Rising through the Communist Youth League in Tibet, this Chinese politician later governed Hebei, led the Communist Party in Inner Mongolia and Guangdong, and served as Vice Premier from 2018 to 2023 — who is he?
Hu Chunhua: Vice Chairperson of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference since 2023.
After leaving the Christian Democratic Appeal in 2019, this Dutch journalist-turned-politician founded the Farmer–Citizen Movement and has sat in the House of Representatives since 2021 — who is she?
Caroline van der Plas: Dutch politician and journalist (born 1967)
A former physician, she became First Lady of Azerbaijan and, in 2017, was appointed by her husband the president to a newly created role as First Vice President — who is she?
Mehriban Aliyeva: First Vice President of Azerbaijan since 2017.
Nicknamed the 'Black Baron,' this scion of a Baltic German noble family became the last commander-in-chief of the White forces in southern Russia during the Civil War — who was he?

The only person ever elected governor of two different US states, he also served as president of the Republic of Texas after spending years living with the Cherokee, who nicknamed him 'Raven' — who was he?
Sam Houston: American general and statesman (1793–1863)
Also known by two other names, this Israelite judge and prophet defeated the Midianites in the Hebrew Bible by leading just 300 men into battle — who is he?
Gideon: Character in the biblical Book of Judges.
Nicknamed 'The Acquitator' for his string of courtroom wins as a criminal defense lawyer, he served as France's Minister of Justice from 2020 to 2024 — who is he?
Éric Dupond-Moretti: French-Italian politician and lawyer (born 1961)
Named in the Synoptic Gospels as blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, this concept describes the one transgression Christian theologians agree can never be forgiven — what is it called?
Eternal sin: Sin which will never be forgiven by God.
Born in Newcastle upon Tyne to Russian émigré parents, this KGB spy ring leader in New York was arrested by the FBI on espionage charges in 1957 — who was he?

Married to Frederick, heir apparent to King George II, this woman never became queen consort since her husband died before his father — but she was mother to the future George III and served as presumptive regent until 1756 — who was she?
Princess Augusta of Saxe-Gotha was Princess of Wales, mother of King George III. Augusta's eldest son succeeded her father-in-law as George III in 1760.

Estranged wife of King George IV, this queen consort had never even met her first cousin and husband-to-be before their 1795 wedding, and was cleared by royal investigators of rumors about her private life — who was she?
Caroline of Brunswick: Queen of the United Kingdom and Hanover from 1820 to 1821.

Once a close ally of Sun Yat-sen and celebrated for his part in the 1911 Revolution, this Chinese politician later led a Japanese-backed puppet government in WWII and is remembered by many as a traitor — who is he?
Appointed by President Joko Widodo in November 2023, this general became the 23rd commander of Indonesia's national armed forces, succeeding an admiral — who is he?
Agus Subiyanto: Commander of the Indonesian National Armed Forces (born 1967)
Twice Austria's chancellor, this politician served as the country's top diplomat from 2013 to 2017 before becoming his party's leader and campaigning to modernize the political system — who is he?
This Swedish king seized power in a 1772 coup that ended the 'Age of Liberty,' then was assassinated two decades later — who is he?
Gustav III: King of Sweden from 1771 to 1792.
Elected in January 2022 after the sudden death of her predecessor, this Maltese politician became the youngest-ever, and first Maltese, president of a major European institution — who is she?
Roberta Metsola: President of the European Parliament since 2022.
Sparked by a Japanese army claim that a soldier had gone missing near Beijing in July 1937, this three-day clash is considered the start of the Second Sino-Japanese War — what was it?
Marco Polo Bridge incident: Initial battle of the Second Sino-Japanese War.
The youngest of Jacob's twelve sons, born in Canaan unlike his brother Joseph, this biblical figure gave his name to one of the twelve tribes of Israel — who is he?
Benjamin: Biblical figure and son of Jacob and Rachel.
Serving as his country's first president from independence in 1991 until his death in 2016, this Central Asian leader won a disputed election with 86 percent of the vote — who is he?
Islam Karimov: Leader of Uzbekistan from 1989 to 2016.
As one of the last twelve absolute monarchs in the world, this king renamed his country from its colonial-era name to its current one in 2018 — who is he?
Mswati III: King of Eswatini since 1986.
This twelve-year Central American conflict, fought between a U.S.-backed government and the FMLN guerrilla coalition, formally ended with the 1992 Chapultepec Peace Accords — which conflict?
Salvadoran Civil War: 1979–1992 conflict in El Salvador.
This Russian aristocrat is best remembered for his role in the 1916 assassination of Grigori Rasputin, and married a niece of Emperor Nicholas II — who is he?
This Romanian marshal ruled as a wartime dictator during World War II, facilitated the Holocaust in his country, and was executed for war crimes in 1946 — who was he?
Ion Antonescu: Dictator of Romania from 1940 to 1944.
Denied a military commission in France by Louis XIV himself, this commander went on to serve the Habsburgs for six decades, becoming one of the greatest generals of his era — who was he?
Prince Eugene of Savoy: Military commander in the service of Austria (1663–1736)
A leading figure in Taiwan's 2014 Sunflower Student Movement, this legal scholar later chaired the Taiwan People's Party starting in 2025 — who is he?
Huang Kuo-chang: Taiwanese legal scholar and politician (born 1973)
As a key figure in Boris Yeltsin's government, this economist oversaw Russia's post-Soviet privatization before fleeing to Israel in 2022 — who is he?
Anatoly Chubais: Russian politician and economist (born 1955)
Before becoming New Zealand's 42nd prime minister in 2023, this National Party leader spent years as CEO of the country's flag carrier airline — who is he?

Christopher Luxon: Prime Minister of New Zealand since 2023. Christopher Mark Luxon (born 19 July 1970) is a New Zealand politician and businessman who has served as the 42nd prime minister of New Zealand since 2023.
His controversial 'junk food' defense at trial became notorious after he killed San Francisco's mayor and a fellow city supervisor in 1978 — who was he?
Dan White: American politician and assassin (1946–1985)
Assassinated by the SS during the Night of the Long Knives in 1934, this German officer had served as the second-to-last chancellor of the Weimar Republic — who was he?
Kurt von Schleicher: Chancellor of Germany from 1932 to 1933.
A member of the Podemos party, this Spanish politician served as Minister of Equality from 2020 to 2023 before winning a seat in the European Parliament in 2024 — who is she?
Irene Montero: Spanish politician. Irene María Montero Gil (Spanish pronunciation: [iˈɾene monˈteɾo]; born 13 February 1988) is a Spanish politician, member of the Podemos party.
Serving as the UK's Deputy Prime Minister and Lord Chancellor in the early 2020s, this Conservative MP represented Esher and Walton and earlier held the role of Foreign Secretary — who is he?
Dominic Raab: Deputy Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (2021–2022, 2022–2023)

After leaving his party in 2021, this Dutch politician founded a new party called New Social Contract, which won 20 seats in the 2023 election, and helped expose the childcare benefits scandal — who is he?

A fighter pilot with over 3,000 flight hours, this retired Air Force general became the first African American to lead a branch of the US Armed Forces and served as chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff from 2023 to 2025 — who is he?
Charles Q. Brown Jr.: US Air Force general (born 1962)
According to Virgil's Aeneid, which mythical queen fled her tyrannical brother as joint ruler of Tyre to found the city of Carthage in what's now Tunisia?
Dido: Legendary founder and first queen of Carthage.
This law professor and TV pundit-turned-politician served as president of Portugal from 2016 to 2026, suspending his party membership for the job — who is he?

Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa: President of Portugal from 2016 to 2026. Marcelo Nuno Duarte Rebelo de Sousa (born 12 December 1948) is a Portuguese politician and academic who served as the president of Portugal from 2016 to 2026.
This Kansas senator was the GOP's vice-presidential nominee in 1976 and its presidential nominee two decades later in 1996 — who is he?
Bob Dole: American politician and attorney (1923–2021)
Co-founder of the 'Yippies' and a leading voice of the Flower Power movement, this activist was one of the Chicago Seven tried over the chaos at the 1968 Democratic National Convention — who is he?
Dubbed the 'Father of Japanese capitalism,' this Meiji-era business magnate founded the country's first joint-stock bank and the Tokyo Stock Exchange — who is he?
Known widely by his initials, this Telangana MLA is the son of a former chief minister and serves as working president of a regional party once called the Telangana Rashtra Samiti — who is he?
K. T. Rama Rao: Indian politician.
Sworn in as the 57th governor of New York in 2021, she became the state's first woman to hold the office — who is she?

Kathy Hochul: Governor of New York since 2021. Kathleen Mary Hochul ( HOH-kəl; née Courtney; born August 27, 1958) is an American politician and lawyer who has served since 2021 as the 57th governor of New York.
This Kentucky senator, a practicing ophthalmologist before entering politics, is the son of a three-time presidential candidate and 12-term Texas congressman — who is he?
Best known for playing 'Trapper' John McIntyre on the CBS series M*A*S*H, this actor later became a regular panelist on a Fox News investing show — who is he?
Documented in some form across Buddhism, Christianity, Vodou, Hinduism, Islam, and more, this altered state is attributed to control of the body by ghosts, demons, or deities — what is it called?
Spirit possession is an altered state of consciousness and associated behaviors purportedly caused by the control of a human body and its functions by spirits, ghosts, demons, angels, or deities.
This crusader lord ruled Antioch and Transjordan by right of marriage, and once tortured the Latin Patriarch of Antioch over unpaid funds before raiding Byzantine Cyprus — who was he?
Raynald of Châtillon: Crusader and military leader (1125–1187)
Succeeding his father Nurhaci, this second khan of the Later Jin conquered Inner Mongolia, invaded Korea, and renamed his people 'Manchu' before founding the Qing dynasty — who was he?
Hong Taiji: Founding emperor of the Qing dynasty.
This Indian politician became Minister of Defence in 2019 and was the first person born after independence to serve as Union Minister of Home Affairs — who is he?
Rajnath Singh: Defense Minister of India since 2019.

When France's government tried raising the retirement age from 62 to 64, over a million people marched nationwide, and the bill was forced through parliament via a special constitutional clause — what were these protests called?
2023 French pension reform strikes: 2023 civil unrest in France.
Born Nakhat Khan, this Indian actress-turned-politician appeared in over 200 films — mostly in Tamil cinema — and won three Tamil Nadu State Film Awards along the way — who is she?
Khushbu Sundar: Indian politician, actress and film producer (born 1970)
Once mayor and party secretary of Shanghai, this Chinese official became the country's vice premier in 2018 and its vice president in 2023 — who is he?
Han Zheng: Vice President of China since 2023.
Founded by Nayib Bukele in 2017, this party now holds near-unanimous control of El Salvador's Legislative Assembly — which party?
Nuevas Ideas: Political party in El Salvador. Nuevas Ideas (English: New Ideas; abbreviated N or NI) is the current ruling political party of El Salvador.
After rising through China's banking sector to become mayor of Beijing, this retired official later led the Communist Party's anti-corruption watchdog from 2012 to 2017 — who is he?
Wang Qishan: Vice President of China from 2018 to 2023.
The longest-serving governor in Massachusetts history, this Democrat lost the 1988 presidential election to George H. W. Bush — who is he?
Michael Dukakis: American politician and lawyer (born 1933)
This Ottoman sultan succeeded his brother in 1703 and presided over the flower-obsessed cultural flowering later called the Tulip Era — who is he?
Ahmed III: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1703 to 1730.
Married to Saudi Arabia's king in 1984, this royal spouse is the mother of the crown prince and five other princes — who is she?
Fahda bint Falah Al Hithlain: Third wife of King Salman of Saudi Arabia.
Three times across Bohemian history, angry factions hurled royal officials out of castle windows — the 1618 episode helped coin the English word for exactly that act — what's the term for this?
Defenestrations of Prague: Incidents of political violence (1419, 1483, 1618)
Spanish-born, she served as the first woman ever elected mayor of the French capital, holding the office from 2014 to 2026 — who is she?
Elected in 2020, this North Carolina congressman became the first member of Congress born in the 1990s, before controversies helped end his reelection bid in 2022 — who is he?
Founded in July 1999 by former Indian prime minister H. D. Deve Gowda as a breakaway faction, this party is recognized as a state party in Karnataka — which one?
Janata Dal (Secular): State political party in India.
Bordered by the Black Sea and wedged between the Soviet Union, Hungary, Yugoslavia, and Bulgaria, this Warsaw Pact communist state existed from 1947 until a 1989 revolution — what was it called?
Socialist Republic of Romania was a communist state that existed from 1947 to the Romanian revolution in 1989.
One of eleven military police convicted in 2005 for their roles in the Abu Ghraib prisoner abuse scandal, this former Army reservist served over a year in prison before parole — who is she?
Succeeding his father Oscar II in 1907 and reigning until his death at 92, the longest-lived Swedish monarch ever, this king was also the first since the Middle Ages never to be crowned — who was he?
Gustaf V: King of Sweden from 1907 to 1950.
Led by a man who declared himself the younger brother of Jesus Christ, this 1850s Chinese theocratic state waged a 14-year war against the Qing dynasty — what was it?
Taiping Heavenly Kingdom: Theocratic monarchy in China (1851–1864)

Once Adolf Hitler's personal chauffeur and bodyguard, this German officer rose to become the highest-ranking commissioned commander in the Waffen-SS despite having no formal staff training — who is he?
Sepp Dietrich: German Nazi politician and SS commander (1892–1966)

Banished to a remote province after his wife's affair with Nero, this Roman noble later murdered his ally Galba to seize the throne, becoming the second ruler of the Year of the Four Emperors — who was he?
Launching an expedition on his own initiative in 639, which companion of Muhammad conquered Egypt for the Muslim caliphate, capping it off with the surrender of Alexandria?
Amr ibn al-As: Arab military commander and governor (c. 573–664)
Often seen as a personification of storm winds, which half-human, half-bird creature from Greek and Roman mythology appears in Homer's poems?
Harpy: Half-bird half-woman monsters associated with storm winds.
Raised in Liverpool and once a trainee nurse, which British politician served as Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport before switching parties to Reform UK in 2025?
This daughter of Rome's first emperor became her stepbrother Tiberius's second wife, then grandmother to Caligula and great-grandmother to Nero — who was she?
Julia the Elder: Daughter of Augustus (39 BC – AD 14)

A high-profile 1990s feud between two American rap scenes and their star artists ended in a 1997 peace summit, but not before both leading rappers were killed in drive-by shootings — what was this conflict called?
East Coast–West Coast hip-hop rivalry: 1990s dispute between hip-hop artists and fans in the US.
Known as 'Mother of Modern China,' this wife of Sun Yat-sen became the only female, non-Communist head of state the People's Republic ever had — who was she?
Soong Ching-ling: Wife of Sun Yat-sen (1893–1981)
Nicknamed the 'Butcher' of a besieged Ukrainian port city for ordering deadly strikes on its theatre and hospital, this Russian general later served in the Wagner Group — who is he?
On March 5, 1770, nine British soldiers opened fire on an unruly crowd on King Street, killing five colonists in an event that helped spark the American Revolution — which incident?
Boston Massacre: 1770 shooting deaths of five colonists by British soldiers.
A former police officer who rose to deputy commissioner, this politician was the sole candidate approved by Beijing in the 2022 election that made him Hong Kong's chief executive — who is he?
John Lee Ka-chiu: Chief Executive of Hong Kong since 2022. After Carrie Lam became chief executive in 2017, Lee was promoted to secretary for security.
As the second husband of Mary, Queen of Scots, this Scottish king fathered the future James VI and I before being murdered at Kirk o' Field in 1567 — who was he?
Henry Stuart, Lord Darnley: King consort of Scotland from 1565 to 1567.
Nicknamed for his Thracian origins, this Roman emperor was proclaimed by his troops in 235 after Severus Alexander's assassination, kicking off decades of turmoil — who was he?
Maximinus Thrax: Roman emperor from 235 to 238.
This retired Marine lieutenant colonel and Vietnam veteran devised the plan to divert Iran arms-sale profits to Contra rebels, testifying before Congress under limited immunity — who is he?
Nominated by President Trump in 2018, this Supreme Court justice once helped draft the Starr Report recommending President Clinton's impeachment — who is he?
Brett Kavanaugh: US Supreme Court justice since 2018.
Known to local tribespeople as the 'hero of the jungle,' this Indian revolutionary led a 1922 guerrilla rebellion against British rule in the Andhra-Odisha borderlands — who is he?
Alluri Sitarama Raju: Indian freedom fighter and revolutionary.
Titled Rama VIII, this king of Siam was found shot dead in his bed in 1946, a death that was ruled murder despite years of controversy over the circumstances — who was he?
Ananda Mahidol: King of Thailand from 1935 to 1946.
This U.S. Navy officer's expedition ended Japan's isolation and led to the 1854 Convention of Kanagawa — who was he?
Matthew C. Perry: United States Navy officer (1794–1858)
Liberia's 22nd president, he resigned in 2003 during a civil war and was later sentenced to 50 years for war crimes committed in Sierra Leone — who is he?
Charles Taylor (Liberian politician): President of Liberia from 1997 to 2003.
Born in 1944, this Japanese politician is the daughter of a former prime minister and his official wife — who is she?
This Japanese prime minister presided over the 1937 invasion of China and pushed through laws that turned his country into a totalitarian state before World War II — who is he?
Fumimaro Konoe: Prime Minister of Japan (1937–1939; 1940–1941)
Fought in 1879 between the British Empire and an African kingdom, this conflict included the defeat at Isandlwana and the defence of Rorke's Drift — which conflict?
Anglo-Zulu War: British colonial war in 1879. Two famous battles of the war were the Zulu victory at Isandlwana and the British defence at Rorke's Drift.

Defended by weapons designed by the polymath Archimedes, this Roman conquest of a Sicilian city in 213–212 BC ended with the inventor's death at a soldier's hands despite orders to spare him — which historic clash?
Siege of Syracuse (213–212 BC): Roman victory during the Second Punic War.
Elected president of a breakaway Caucasus republic in 1997, he later led guerrilla resistance against Russian forces before being killed in 2005 — who is he?
Aslan Maskhadov: Chechen politician and military commander (1951-2005)
According to Galatians chapter 5, nine virtues — including love, joy, peace, and self-control — mark a life lived in step with God's presence; what biblical term describes this list?
Fruit of the Holy Spirit: Biblical term.
Founded by Dayananda Saraswati in the 1870s, this monotheistic Hindu reform movement was the first to introduce proselytizing into Hinduism — what movement is it?

Fought from 1921 to 1926, this conflict pitted Spain and later France against Berber guerrillas led by Abd el-Krim in northern Morocco, and saw history's first amphibious landing to use tanks and aircraft — which conflict?
Rif War: 1921–1926 war between Spain and Riffian tribes of Morocco.
Created in 1946 and headquartered in Paris, this government-owned utility operates 56 nuclear reactors across 18 sites and was the world's largest electricity producer in 2009 — which company?
Électricité de France: French multinational electric utility company.
In February 1488, this Portuguese mariner became the first European navigator to round the southern tip of Africa, paving the way for Vasco da Gama's route to Asia — who is he?
Praised by Lenin as a 'most valuable and major theorist' of the Communist Party, this Bolshevik wrote Imperialism and World Economy in 1915 before being purged in 1937 — who is he?
Nikolai Bukharin: Soviet revolutionary and politician (1888–1938)
This princess of Mycenae helped her brother Orestes kill their mother to avenge their father Agamemnon's murder, later lending her name to a psychological complex — who is she?
This BJP politician has served as Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh while representing the Ujjain South constituency since 2013 — who is he?
Mohan Yadav: Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh (born 1965)

Educated in Moscow and a veteran of several wars, this military officer was the eldest son of the Chinese Communist Party's founding chairman, before he was killed by a U.S. napalm strike in the Korean War. Who was he?
Mao Anying: Chinese military officer and son of Mao Zedong. Mao Anying (Chinese: 毛岸英; pinyin: Máo Ànyīng; 24 October 1922 – 25 November 1950) was a Chinese military officer.
Serving as Lyndon Johnson's vice president, this Minnesota senator lost the 1968 presidential election to Richard Nixon after helping found his state's Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party — who is he?
Hubert Humphrey: Vice President of the United States from 1965 to 1969.
After his mother's second marriage to Nazi propaganda minister Joseph Goebbels, this German industrialist later co-ran his father's empire, holding a stake in BMW and battery maker VARTA — who is he?
Described in the Hebrew Bible as the older sister of Moses and Aaron, this prophetess led the Israelite women out of Egypt and taught them Torah — who is she?
Miriam: Sister of Moses and Aaron. The Torah refers to her as "Miriam the Prophetess" and the Talmud names her as one of the seven major female prophets of Israel.

Co-founder of the Identitarian Movement of Austria in 2012, this far-right activist was barred from entering both the UK and the US, and later fought a German entry ban tied to a controversial 'remigration' speech — who is he?
Elected to Taipei's city council in 2018, this activist for LGBT rights and Taiwanese independence became one of Taiwan's first openly lesbian councillors — who is she?
Considered by many Egyptologists to be the same ruler as Menes, this Egyptian king is credited with unifying the country and founding its First Dynasty around 3100 BC — who is he?
Narmer: Ancient Egyptian pharaoh of the Early Dynastic Period.
Born and raised in Miami, this Republican rose from Florida House speaker to U.S. senator before becoming America's 72nd secretary of state in 2025 — who is he?
Marco Rubio: American politician and diplomat (born 1971)
Hired by a Moabite king to curse the Israelites, this biblical prophet blessed them instead, as recounted in the Book of Numbers — who was he?
Balaam: Prophet in the Book of Numbers. Balaam is also mentioned in the Book of Micah, the Second Epistle of Peter, the Book of Jude, and the Book of Revelation.
Born in St. Louis and once a public defender in Texas, this Democratic congresswoman ran for a Texas Senate seat in 2026 but lost the primary — who is she?
Active in local politics in Corrèze, this Frenchwoman spent 25 years heading a children's charity while her husband occupied the presidential palace — who was she?
This warrior united the Hawaiian Islands under a single crown and was later honored with a statue in Washington's National Statuary Hall — who was he?
Kamehameha I: King of Hawaii from 1795 to 1819.

The CIA's longest-serving director, he was forced to resign by President Kennedy after the failed Bay of Pigs invasion, then oddly ended up on the commission probing Kennedy's own assassination — who is he?
Allen Dulles: Director of Central Intelligence from 1953 to 1961.
The daughter of a top Nazi SS official, she testified at the Nuremberg trials but spent the rest of her life defending her father's reputation and aiding former SS members — who was she?
Gudrun Burwitz: Daughter of Heinrich Himmler (1929–2018)
As chairman of Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority, this Royal Court adviser also owned Spanish club Almería from 2019 to 2025 — who is he?
Serving as Iraq's president from 2022 to 2026, he previously ran the country's Ministry of Water Resources and became just the fourth non-Arab to hold the top office — who is he?
Abdul Latif Rashid: President of Iraq from 2022 to 2026. Rashid was formerly a spokesperson for the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) in the United Kingdom.

Founded in 1891 by Leandro N. Alem, this Argentine political party is the country's second-oldest active party and a longtime human-rights advocate that has been banned under military rule — which party?
Radical Civic Union: Political party in Argentina. The Radical Civic Union (Spanish: Unión Cívica Radical, UCR) is a major political party in Argentina.

This Indian politician serves as an MLA from Rajasthan while also holding the position of eighth spiritual head of the Nath sect, a role he received from his predecessor in a 2016 ceremony attended by Yogi Adityanath — who is he?
Mahant Balaknath: Indian politician and spiritual leader (born 1984)
As Ukraine's prime minister, he guided the country through the COVID-19 pandemic and the opening years of the 2022 Russian invasion before later becoming defence minister — who is he?
Denys Shmyhal: Prime Minister of Ukraine from 2020 to 2025.

The fifth Safavid shah of Iran, this ruler took the throne amid factional chaos that had already cost his mother and elder brother their lives, yet led the empire to its military and economic peak — who is he?
Abbas the Great: Shah of Safavid Iran from 1587 to 1629.
Representing Maryland's 8th congressional district since 2017, this progressive Democrat also founded Democracy Summer, a nationwide youth civic-organizing program — who is he?

A physics teacher turned politician, this former mayor of Sibiu represented Romania's ethnic German minority party before serving as the country's president from 2014 until his 2025 resignation — who is he?

Klaus Iohannis: President of Romania from 2014 to 2025. Iohannis was first elected the mayor of the Romanian town of Sibiu in 2000, on behalf of the Democratic Forum of Germans in Romania (FDGR/DFDR).
Known by his initials, this Indian politician served as chief minister of Andhra Pradesh for two terms before dying in a 2009 helicopter crash over a forest — who was he?
Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy: Chief minister of Andhra Pradesh, India. Yeduguri Sandinti Rajasekhara Reddy (8 July 1949 – 2 September 2009), popularly known as YSR, was an Indian politician.
Married for more than 40 years to a celebrated general, this English courtier's close bond with Queen Anne made her one of the most powerful women in early 18th-century Britain — who was she?
Sarah Churchill, Duchess of Marlborough: English noblewoman, courtier and politician (1660–1744)
This Chinese Communist Party official rose from mayor of Hangzhou to become General Secretary Xi Jinping's effective chief of staff — who is he?

Cai Qi: Chief of Staff for CCP general secretary Xi Jinping. A graduate of Fujian Normal University, Cai began his career in his native Fujian province, where he worked at the Fujian Provincial Committee of the CCP.

Formed in 1988 as a liberal youth movement opposing Hungary's Marxist-Leninist government, this party transformed into a right-wing force that dominated Hungarian politics under Viktor Orbán — which party?
Fidesz: Political party in Hungary. It was the country's main ruling party from 1998 to 2002 and dominated Hungarian politics from 2010 to 2026 during the Orbán era.
According to Exodus, the Israelites made this idol of a young bovine while Moses was away on Mount Sinai — what was it?
Golden calf: Idol in the Torah, the Bible, and the Quran.
Owned by the government of the United Arab Emirates, this budget carrier flies to 131 destinations across the Middle East, Africa, Asia, and Europe and its slogan is 'Get Going' — which airline?
Flydubai: Airline of the United Arab Emirates. The airline mainly operates out of Terminal 2 at Dubai International Airport, though some flights fly out from Terminal 3.

Hours after Vladimir Putin announced Russia's 'special military operation' on February 24, 2022, Russian airborne troops assaulted a strategic airfield near Kyiv, aiming to fly in reinforcements before being encircled and repelled by Ukrainian forces — which clash?
Battle of Antonov Airport: Part of the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

Emerging in Western Europe and the US during the Industrial Revolution, this socio-cultural phenomenon turns the acquisition of goods into something that shapes identity, not just meets basic needs — which term?
Consumerism: Acquisition of goods beyond essential needs.
A former Navy SEAL who lost his right eye to an IED in Afghanistan, this Texas congressman was first elected in 2018 but lost his 2026 primary to a state representative — who is he?

Marching his 13th Legion over a forbidden river into Italy in January 49 BC, Julius Caesar defied the Senate and triggered a civil war that made him dictator for life — this act gave its name to what idiom for a point of no return?
Crossing the Rubicon: Idiom meaning a point of no return. Caesar was not allowed to command an army within Italy proper, and by crossing the river with his forces was defying law and risking death.
Daughter of Thaumas and Electra, this winged personification of the rainbow served as messenger to the Olympians, especially Hera, and carried a caduceus and a pitcher of water — who is she?
Iris (mythology): Ancient Greek personification of the rainbow.
Captured and executed in 1533 during the Spanish conquest, he was the last effective ruler of the Inca Empire — who was he?

Serving as U.S. Special Envoy for Northern Ireland from 2022 to 2024, this Massachusetts congressman is also the grandson of a senator and attorney general and grandnephew of a president assassinated in 1963 — who is he?

Elected leader of the Social Democratic Party in 1913, this politician's support for war loans split his party before he became the first president of the newly declared German republic in 1919 — who was he?
Friedrich Ebert: President of Germany from 1919 to 1925.
As Colombia's Minister of Justice, he cracked down on cocaine traffickers until he was assassinated on the orders of a notorious drug baron in 1984 — who was he?
Rodrigo Lara Bonilla: Colombian lawyer and politician (1946-1984)
After narrowly losing a disputed 2014 mayoral race that went to the European Court of Human Rights, this lawyer-turned-politician finally became mayor of Turkey's capital in 2019 — who is he?
Mansur Yavaş: Turkish politician and mayor of Ankara.
In 1917, Mahatma Gandhi led his first mass civil-disobedience campaign in British India, organizing Bihar farmers who were forced to grow indigo for almost no pay — what was this movement called?
Champaran Satyagraha: First civil resistance movement led by Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi in India in 1917.
Appointed Professor of Greek at just 25, this British politician later served as Minister of Health before becoming notorious for a controversial 1968 speech on immigration — who is he?
In October 2025, she became the first woman ever to serve as Prime Minister of Japan — who is she?
Sanae Takaichi: Prime Minister of Japan since 2025. Takaichi's administration has consistently polled high in approval ratings.
A war correspondent in Afghanistan and Angola in the 1980s, this Oxford-educated Polish statesman later became his country's Foreign Minister and, since 2025, also Deputy Prime Minister — who is he?
Radosław Sikorski: Polish politician and journalist (born 1963)
Elected in 1987 as the first South Korean president chosen by direct popular vote, this former army general had earlier helped his military academy friend seize power in a 1979 coup. Who is he?
Roh Tae-woo: President of South Korea from 1988 to 1993.
The son of one former New Hampshire governor and younger brother of a U.S. senator, this Republican engineer became just the second person in state history elected governor four times. Who is he?
A former actor turned anti-establishment politician, this Japanese lawmaker founded a party called Reiwa Shinsengumi and once ran for Tokyo governor — who is he?
Taro Yamamoto: Japanese politician and former actor.
Leader of Russia's Communist Party since 1993, this politician ran for president four times, most famously losing to Boris Yeltsin in the 1996 runoff — who is he?
Known affectionately by his patients as 'Papa Doc,' this physician-turned-politician ruled as president from 1957 until his death in 1971 — who is he?

François Duvalier: President of Haiti from 1957 to 1971. Duvalier completed a degree in medicine from the University of Haiti in 1934 and spent a year at the University of Michigan studying public health.
Named after the TV show in which its founder played a fictional president, this Ukrainian political party has ruled since Volodymyr Zelenskyy won the presidency in 2019 — which party?
Servant of the People: Political party in Ukraine. It was formed in late 2017 and was officially registered on 31 March 2018 on the basis of the previously registered Party of Decisive Changes.
Born in Jaffna, this guerrilla leader founded and led a militant organization in a decades-long campaign for an independent Tamil state in Sri Lanka — who is he?
Velupillai Prabhakaran: Leader of militant Tamil organisation in Sri Lanka (1954–2009)
Nicknamed 'Kick,' this Kennedy sister — sibling to JFK, Robert, and Ted — was widowed within months of her 1944 wedding and died in a 1948 plane crash — who is she?
Kathleen Cavendish, Marchioness of Hartington: American socialite, sister of John F. Kennedy (1920–1948)
The second son of Libya's longtime leader, this political figure acted as de facto prime minister and was later acknowledged as his father's heir apparent despite once rejecting the role — who is he?
Saif al-Islam Gaddafi: Libyan political figure (1972–2026)
Founded in 1864 and headquartered near Paris's La Défense district, this bank is France's third-largest by assets, trailing only BNP Paribas and Crédit Agricole — which bank?
Société Générale: French multinational banking and financial services company.
He served as governor of New Mexico, U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, and Clinton's energy secretary, then chaired the 2004 Democratic National Convention — who is this diplomat?
Founded in 1969 by Nayef Hawatmeh in a split from a rival group, this secular Marxist-Leninist and Maoist organization joined the PLO and champions a state without discrimination — which group?
Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine
Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine

Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine: Palestinian Marxist–Leninist organization. It is also frequently referred to as the Democratic Front, or al-Jabha al-Dīmūqrāṭiyya (الجبهة الديمقراطية).
Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine
A close friend of Stalin who rose to lead the Communist Party in Leningrad, his 1934 assassination at the Smolny Institute became Stalin's pretext for the Great Purge — who was he?
Sergei Kirov: Soviet politician and revolutionary (1886–1934)
A doctor of chemistry who became Deputy Prime Minister of Communist Romania, she was executed alongside her husband on Christmas Day 1989 — who was she?
Elena Ceaușescu was Deputy Prime Minister of Communist Romania.
This French investment company once owned Universal Studios and Universal Music before spinning off 60% of its music arm starting in 2021 — which firm?
Vivendi: French investment company. Vivendi SE (stylized in all lowercase) is a French investment company headquartered in Paris.

Said by ancient tradition to have discovered the True Cross during a religious tour of Jerusalem, this Greek-born Augusta was canonized a saint by both the Catholic and Orthodox churches — who was she?
Helena, mother of Constantine I: Roman empress and saint (c. 246–c. 330)
Led by a Cossack hetman between 1648 and 1657, this rebellion against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth carved out the new Cossack Hetmanate — which revolt was it?

Khmelnytsky Uprising: Cossack rebellion within the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth in 1648–1657. Originating in Dnieper Ukraine, the uprising resulted in a Cossack victory and led to the creation of the Cossack Hetmanate.
Fill in the blank: “____ (15 February 1949 - 22 October 1988) was a Turkish military officer who was appointed governor of the Diyarbakr Prison after the 1980 Turkish coup d'tat.”

Esat Oktay Yıldıran (15 February 1949 - 22 October 1988) was a Turkish military officer who was appointed governor of the Diyarbakr Prison after the 1980 Turkish coup d'tat. During the PKK insurgency, Yıldıran became known for his extensive torture of PKK aligned Kurds in the Diyarbakır Prison.
Born in Caracas, this military leader fought in three revolutions — American, French, and Spanish American — and is remembered as a forerunner of South America's independence movement — who is he?
Francisco de Miranda: Venezuelan military leader (1750–1816)

After her husband was arrested ahead of Belarus's 2020 election, this activist entered the presidential race in his place — a decision the regime allowed, wrongly assuming a woman couldn't mount a real challenge — who is she?
This German Social Democratic politician led the party's youth wing, the Jusos, before serving as SPD General Secretary from 2021 to 2024 — who is he?

In the United States, this term describes people and cultures connected to Spain and the Spanish language, applying broadly across Spanish-speaking Latin America and even parts of Africa and Asia once ruled by the Spanish Empire — what term?
Hispanic: Spanish-speaking cultures and persons. The term Hispanic (Spanish: hispano) refers to people, cultures, or countries related to Spain, the Spanish language, or Hispanidad broadly.

After 25 years at the private equity firm Carlyle Group, where he rose to co-CEO, this Republican defeated former governor Terry McAuliffe in 2021 to become Virginia's first GOP governor since 2009 — who is he?
Glenn Youngkin: Governor of Virginia from 2022 to 2026.

Born in Dresden to a Russian aristocratic family, this reform-minded statesman served as prime minister and interior minister of the Russian Empire from 1906 until his assassination in 1911 — who is he?

Pyotr Stolypin: Prime Minister of the Russian Empire from 1906 to 1911. Born in Dresden, in the Kingdom of Saxony, to a prominent Russian aristocratic family, Stolypin became involved in government from his early 20s.

According to the Hebrew Bible, this son of King David killed his half-brother to avenge a grave wrong done to his sister, then fled into exile before later leading a rebellion against his father's house — who is he?
Absalom: Third son of the Israelite king David.

The eldest child of the last Tsar Nicholas II, this princess nursed wounded soldiers during the First World War before being murdered in 1918 amid revolutionary upheaval, and was later canonized as a passion bearer — who is she?
Grand Duchess Olga Nikolaevna of Russia
Grand Duchess Olga Nikolaevna of Russia

Grand Duchess Olga Nikolaevna of Russia was the eldest daughter of Tsar Nicholas II of Russia. Before the birth of her brother Alexei Nikolaevich, rumors spread that Nicholas II would declare Olga his heir.
Grand Duchess Olga Nikolaevna of Russia
Mentally ill for most of his reign, this 18th-century Danish-Norwegian king let his court physician rule as a de facto dictator from 1770 to 1772 before a coup deposed the doctor — who was the king?
Christian VII: King of Denmark and Norway from 1766 to 1808.
Founded by Muhammad I Ibn al-Ahmar after 1228, this Nasrid dynasty realm was the last independent Muslim state to survive in Western Europe — what was it called?
Emirate of Granada: State in the Iberian Peninsula, 1232–1492.
The daughter of a former Pakistani prime minister, this politician made history in February 2024 as the first woman to become chief minister of Punjab — who is she?
Maryam Nawaz: Chief Minister of Punjab (born 1973)
Marked by far-left and far-right terrorism from the late 1960s through the late 1980s, this period began amid 1969's Hot Autumn strikes and the deadly Piazza Fontana bombing — what was it called?
Years of Lead (Italy) were a period of social and political turmoil in Italy that lasted from the late 1960s to the late 1980s, marked by a wave of both far-left and far-right political terrorism.
Nicknamed Iran's 'hanging judge,' this cleric headed the country's revolutionary court from 1979 to 1981 and ordered the destruction of a former shah's mausoleum — who was he?
Sadegh Khalkhali: Iranian cleric and politician (1926–2003)
Serving as Saudi Arabia's defense minister for nearly five decades, which royal became Crown Prince in 2005 and held the title until his death in 2011?
Sultan bin Abdulaziz: Saudi royal and politician (1925–2011)
Founded in Leipzig in 1984 and now based in Zürich, which organization chronicles the history and statistics of association football despite having no official affiliation with FIFA?
IFFHS: Organisation chronicling the history and records of association football.
Serving as president of an organization that advocates overthrowing Iran's government, which Iranian dissident politician was born in December 1953?
Born in 1950, this Indian activist has served since 2009 as the sixth Sarsanghchalak, or chief, of a major Hindu nationalist organization — who is he?
In 1976, this Soviet pilot defected to the West by flying his MiG-25 'Foxbat' jet interceptor to Japan, handing the CIA what George H. W. Bush called an 'intelligence bonanza' — who is he?
Viktor Belenko: Soviet pilot who defected to the West (1947–2023)
A former judge who once led Turkey's Constitutional Court, this staunch secularist served as Turkish president from 2000 to 2007, succeeding Suleyman Demirel — who is he?
Ahmet Necdet Sezer: President of Turkey from 2000 to 2007. Ahmet Necdet Sezer (born 13 September 1941) is a Turkish statesman and judge who served as the president of Turkey from 2000 to 2007.
According to the New Testament, this figure is held to be the Son of God whose crucifixion and resurrection are believed to offer humanity salvation and eternal life — who is he?
Jesus in Christianity is the Son of God as chronicled in the Bible's New Testament, and is held to be God the Son, a prosopon (person) of the Trinity of God.
Having joined the Italian resistance as a teenager in World War II, this journalist grew famous for fierce interviews with the likes of Henry Kissinger, Golda Meir, and the Shah of Iran — who is she?
Oriana Fallaci: Italian journalist and author (1929–2006)
The third wife of Emperor Claudius, this Roman noblewoman was allegedly executed after conspiring against her husband, her scandalous reputation later immortalized in art and literature — who is she?
Messalina: Roman empress from AD 41 to 48.
This ancient Indian king fought valiantly against Alexander the Great at the Battle of the Hydaspes in 326 BC, and was rewarded with an expanded realm despite his defeat — who is he?

This Scottish businesswoman founded the lingerie brand Ultimo before becoming a Conservative life peer, later facing scrutiny after her husband's firm won a £200 million pandemic-era PPE contract — who is she?
Founded in 1926 by Éamon de Valera after a split from Sinn Féin, which party has been one of Ireland's two dominant political forces ever since?
Fianna Fáil: Irish political party. The party dominated Irish political life for most of the 20th century, and, since its foundation, either it or Fine Gael has led every government.
Serving as Foreign Minister in the 1820s, this royalist French writer and diplomat later had his memoirs published posthumously as 'Memoirs from Beyond the Grave' — who was he?
François-René de Chateaubriand: French writer, politician and historian (1768–1848)
Leader of the People's Mojahedin Organization of Iran from 1979, which Iranian revolutionary vanished shortly before the 2003 invasion of Iraq, leaving his wife as the group's public face?
Called 'Başbuğ,' or 'Leader,' by his devotees, this Turkish politician founded both the far-right Nationalist Movement Party and the Grey Wolves — who is he?
This leading man of 1950s Westerns and film noir later played General Jack D. Ripper in Dr. Strangelove and Captain McCluskey in The Godfather — who is he?
Appointed by Stalin to lead the Soviet secret police from 1934 to 1936, this official oversaw the show trials of the Great Purge before becoming a victim of the very system he built — who is he?
Genrikh Yagoda: Soviet secret police official (1891–1938)
Fought in November 636, this decisive clash between the Rashidun Caliphate and the Sasanian Empire opened the road to the siege of Ctesiphon and the eventual fall of Persia — which engagement?
Battle of al-Qadisiyyah: Part of the Muslim conquest of Persia (636 CE)
This 1944 amphibious assault on a Pacific island put Japan's home cities within range of B-29 bombers and triggered the resignation of Prime Minister Hideki Tōjō — which engagement?
Battle of Saipan was an amphibious assault launched by the United States against the Empire of Japan during the Pacific campaign of World War II between 15 June and 9 July 1944.
This pro-Russian separatist led the self-declared Donetsk People's Republic before being killed in a café bombing in August 2018. Who was he?
A former dentist turned politician, this founding member of the PTI served as Pakistan's 13th president from 2018 to 2024. Who is he?

Arif Alvi: President of Pakistan from 2018 to 2024. Arif-ur-Rehman Alvi (born 29 July 1949) is a Pakistani politician and former dentist who served as the 13th president of Pakistan from September 2018 to March 2024.

This medical condition, usually diagnosed shortly after birth, is defined as a length at least 2.5 standard deviations below the average and affects about 1.5 in 10,000 male newborns in North America. What is this condition?
Developed under the codename 'WhiteStar' and unveiled in Hawthorne, California in 2009, this full-size electric sedan won Motor Trend's Car of the Year in 2013 — which car?
Tesla Model S: Battery-electric full-size car. The Tesla Model S is a battery-electric, four-door full-size car that was produced by the American automaker Tesla from 2012 to 2026.

Diagnosed via Whipple's triad and most often triggered by diabetes medications like insulin, this condition causes shakiness, confusion, and sweating when blood sugar drops below 70 mg/dL — what is it?

Hypoglycemia: Decrease in blood sugar. It is defined as blood glucose below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), symptoms associated with hypoglycemia, and resolution of symptoms when blood sugar returns to normal.

Also known as gotu kola or Indian pennywort, this herbaceous perennial from the Apiaceae family is eaten as a vegetable and used in traditional medicine across Africa, Asia, and the Pacific — what is it?
Centella asiatica: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae.
Nominated by Donald Trump in 2020, this Notre Dame law professor became the fifth woman to serve as a US Supreme Court associate justice after previously sitting on the Seventh Circuit — who is she?

Amy Coney Barrett: US Supreme Court justice since 2020. Barrett graduated from Rhodes College before attending Notre Dame Law School, earning a Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree in 1997 and ranked first in her class.
Marketed under the brand name Imovane, this 'Z-drug' sedative treats insomnia by boosting GABA activity in the brain much like a benzodiazepine, though it's chemically distinct — what is it?
Caused by a genetic variant in the UGT1A1 gene, this harmless liver condition slows the breakdown of bilirubin and can trigger jaundice during stress, exercise, or fasting — what is it called?
Gilbert's syndrome: Medical condition. It is typically inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern and occasionally in an autosomal dominant pattern depending on the type of variant.
People with this anxiety disorder are fully capable of speech but fall silent in specific situations or around specific people, even when staying quiet brings shame or punishment — what is it called?
Selective mutism: Anxiety disorder blocking speech. Selective mutism usually co-exists with social anxiety disorder.
This branch of biology studies the microscopic structure of tissues, historically distinguished from cytology (the study of cells) and organology (the study of organs) — what is it called?
Histology: Study of the microscopic anatomy of cells and tissues of plants and animals.
Despite its name, only the soles of this tawny, spotted feline's paws are actually dark — and at just 35 to 52 centimetres long, it ranks as Africa's smallest wild feline species — what animal is it?
Black-footed cat: Small wild cat native to Southern Africa.
Derived from Greek words meaning 'healer of children,' this branch of medicine covers care from infancy through adolescence — what is it?
Pediatrics: Branch of medicine caring for children. Within the Commonwealth, pediatrics covers patients until the age of 18, except in India where the pediatric age is 12.
Home to more than 4,200 described species, this family of large crane flies can be identified by the length of their maxillary palps — what is it?
Tipulidae: Family of flies. There are more than 30 genera and 4,200 described species in Tipulidae, common and widespread throughout the world.
The only Old World member of its family to breed in the Northern Hemisphere's temperate zones, this migratory songbird winters in central and southern Africa — what is it?
Eurasian golden oriole: Species of bird.
Encompassing roadrunners, koels, and anis among its roughly 150 species, this widespread bird family favors trees but includes some ground-dwellers — what is it?
Cuckoo: Family of birds. The cuckoo family includes the common or European cuckoo, roadrunners, koels, malkohas, couas, coucals, and anis.
Co-founding a photo-sharing app with Mike Krieger, this entrepreneur sold the company to Facebook for $1 billion in 2012 when it had just 13 employees — who is he?
Kevin Systrom: American computer programmer and entrepreneur (born 1983)
Attracted to rotting fruit and fermenting drinks, this insect became the first animal launched into space in 1946 and has earned six Nobel Prizes for scientists who studied it — what is it?
Drosophila melanogaster: Species of fruit fly.
Sometimes called 'bipolar III,' this mood disorder involves cycling periods of mild depression and elevated mood that never reach the severity of full manic or depressive episodes — what is it?
Cyclothymia: Mental disorder. Cyclothymia differs from bipolar disorder in the fact that major depression and mania are not found.

Synthesized by Aristotle and taken as fact for two millennia, this superseded theory held that maggots could arise straight from dead flesh, until Louis Pasteur helped discredit it — what was it called?
Spontaneous generation: Theory of life arising from non-living matter.

Prized by the Inca, who reserved its ultra-fine wool for royalty alone, this wild Andean camelid is now believed to be the ancestor of the domesticated alpaca and is Peru's national animal — what is it?
This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats acute pain and osteoarthritis by blocking prostaglandins, though it carries a notable risk of liver problems — what is it?
Nimesulide: Anti-inflammatory drug. Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with pain medication and fever reducing properties.
Originally designated the DC-9 Series 80, this five-abreast single-aisle airliner first flew in October 1979 and entered service with launch customer Swissair the following year — what jet is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-80: Jet airliner model, series based on the DC-9.

Found above 3,500 metres on the Tibetan Plateau, this parasitic fungus grows out of moth larvae and is prized — despite containing arsenic — as an aphrodisiac in traditional Chinese medicine. What is it commonly called?
Ophiocordyceps sinensis: Species of fungus. It parasitizes larvae of ghost moths and produces a fruiting body which is valued in traditional Chinese medicine and Nepalese medicine as an aphrodisiac.
The larval stage of a darkling beetle, this insect is used in biomedical research, eaten as a food source for animals and humans, and is also a common food-storage pest — what is it called?
Mealworm: Species of darkling beetle, larval form.
Rolled out in March 2023 and designed to replace Turkey's F-16 fleet, this fifth-generation stealth fighter made its maiden flight in February 2024 — what is it?
TAI TF Kaan: Turkish fighter aircraft.
In mathematics, this is a selection of items from a set where the order of choosing them does not matter, unlike a permutation — what is it called?

Combination: Selection of items from a set. In mathematics, a combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).
This condition of involuntary eye movement can be triggered by stimulating the ear's semicircular canals — for example with the caloric test — while the head stays still. What is it?
Nystagmus: Dysfunction of eye movement. Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.

According to psychologist Alfred Adler, this persistent feeling of being deficient or lesser than others — often stemming from childhood comparisons to a sibling — can lead people to overcompensate. What is it called?
Inferiority complex: Intense feeling of inadequacy and inferior.
This inflammation of the voice box causes symptoms ranging from a hoarse voice to complete voice loss, typically clearing up within two weeks — what is the condition?
Laryngitis: Inflammation of the larynx (voice box). The primary symptom is loss of some vocal function, ranging from hoarse voice to no voice at all.
This infection and inflammation of hair follicles produces pimples with white tips anywhere on hair-covered skin — what is the condition called?
Folliculitis: Human and animal disease of follicles.
Named from the Greek word for cheese after being first isolated from casein in 1846, this amino acid carries the one-letter code Y — what is it?
Tyrosine: Amino acid. L-Tyrosine or tyrosine (symbol Tyr or Y) or 4-hydroxyphenylalanine is one of the 20 standard amino acids that are used by cells to synthesize proteins.
Sold under brand names like Sudafed PE, this nasal decongestant works as a selective alpha-1 adrenergic receptor agonist — what is the drug?
Phenylephrine: Decongestant medication. It is unclear whether its use during pregnancy and breastfeeding is safe.
Nicknamed 'brittle bone disease,' this genetic disorder causes fragile bones and blue-tinted eye whites, usually stemming from faulty type I collagen — what is it?
Osteogenesis imperfecta: Group of genetic disorders resulting in fragile bones.
Using only a triangle's three side lengths and their semiperimeter, this ancient geometric method computes the triangle's area — what is it known as?
Heron's formula: Triangle area in terms of side lengths.
This plant family — nicknamed the mustards or crucifers, and including cabbage — hosts the caterpillars of a notorious garden-pest butterfly as one of its worst enemies — name the family?
This abnormal enlargement of veins in the scrotum is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, affecting around 15% of all men — what is it called?
Varicocele: Abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform plexus veins in the scrotum.
Native to Southern Europe and Anatolia, this deciduous tree produces an edible nut that's been used in cooking since ancient times — what is it commonly called?
Sweet chestnut: Species of tree. A substantial, long-lived deciduous tree, it produces an edible seed, the chestnut, which has been used in cooking since ancient times.
This group of large hoofed mammals splits into odd-toed members like horses and rhinos, and even-toed members like cattle, giraffes, and camels — what are they called?
Ungulate: Group of mammals that walk on the tips of their toes or hooves.
Also nicknamed the cross spider or diadem spider for the white markings on its back, this orb-weaver is native to Europe but was introduced to North America — what species is it?

Araneus diadematus: Species of spider. The spider species Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.
This small Old World flycatcher breeds in rocky habitats from the British Isles to Morocco and central China, staying put in milder areas but migrating from colder ones — what bird is it?
Black redstart: Species of bird. The black redstart (Phoenicurus ochruros) is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family.

In physics, this phenomenon occurs when two coherent waves combine according to their phase difference, producing either a boosted 'constructive' amplitude or a canceling 'destructive' one — what's the effect called?
Wave interference is a phenomenon in which two coherent waves are combined by adding their intensities or displacements with due consideration for their phase difference.
Named after a 17th-century English physician, this ring-shaped network of arteries supplies blood to the brain in humans and other vertebrates — what is it called?
Circle of Willis: Circulatory anastomosis that supplies blood to the brain and surrounding structures.
First patented in Germany in 1920 and later synthesized by an American chemist in 1932, this semi-synthetic opioid is roughly ten times more potent than morphine — what is it called?
Desomorphine: Semi-synthetic opioid, morphine analogue. It was first discovered and patented in Germany by a German team working for Knoll in 1920 but was not generally recognized.
Known as the black shag in New Zealand, this widespread seabird breeds across much of the Old World, Australasia, and the Atlantic coast of North America — which bird?
Comprising the talocrural, subtalar, and inferior tibiofibular joints, this region where the foot meets the leg enables dorsiflexion and plantarflexion — which body part?
Ankle: Region where the foot and the leg meet. The ankle includes three joints: the ankle joint proper or talocrural joint, the subtalar joint, and the inferior tibiofibular joint.
This mathematical principle links differentiation and integration, showing the two operations to be essentially inverses of each other — what is it called?
Fundamental theorem of calculus: Relationship between derivatives and integrals.
Consisting of a phenyl group attached to an amino group, this organic compound smells like rotten fish and serves as a key precursor to polyurethane and dyes — what is it called?
Aniline: Organic compound (C6H5NH2); simplest aromatic amine.

Native to the Americas but now grown worldwide, one species of this flowering plant genus has become such a popular ornamental that it's classified as an invasive weed on four continents — which genus?
Jacaranda: Genus of trees. The generic name is also used as the common name.

Denied European certification after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, this single-aisle airliner made its maiden flight from Irkutsk in 2017 and is built by a UAC subsidiary of Rostec — which aircraft?
Yakovlev MC-21: Twin-engine Russian jet airliner.
Striking at the same hour every day for weeks at a time, usually around one eye, this excruciating neurological condition is considered one of the most painful known to medicine — what is it?
Cluster headache: Neurological disorder. The disease is considered among the most painful conditions known to medical science.
Nicknamed the corpse flower for its rotting-flesh stench, this Sumatran plant first bloomed in cultivation at Kew Gardens in 1889 — which species?
Amorphophallus titanum: Species of flowering plant in the arum family Araceae.
This academic discipline studies the methods, sources, and interpretive approaches historians use when writing about the past — what's it called?
Historiography: Study of the methods used by historians.

Credited with the oldest known systematic classification of chemical substances, this alchemist's corpus also contains the earliest instructions for deriving ammonium chloride from organic matter — who is he?
Jabir ibn Hayyan: Islamic alchemist and polymath (died c. 806–816)
Also known as the buckeye or conker tree, this deciduous flowering tree is often confused with the unrelated sweet chestnut — which species?
Aesculus hippocastanum: Species of tree in the soapberry family.
Meaning 'different lizard' and first described in 1877 by Othniel Marsh, most fossils of this Late Jurassic predator come from North America's Morrison Formation — which dinosaur?

Named after a mythological Greek youth transformed into a tree after killing his pet stag, this genus of evergreen conifers is found across warm temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere — which genus?
Cupressus: Several genera of evergreen conifers.
A U.S. Navy rear admiral who helped develop COBOL, this computer science pioneer wrote what's considered the first computer manual and worked on the Harvard Mark I — who is she?
Grace Hopper: U.S. naval officer and computer scientist (1906–1992)
This genus of over 650 succulent species includes a 'true' member long used in pharmaceutical products, native to Africa, Madagascar, and the Arabian Peninsula — which genus?
Aloe: Genus of succulent flowering plants.
Though they look like dolphins, these small toothed whales are actually closer kin to narwhals and belugas, with flat spade-shaped teeth instead of dolphins' cone-shaped ones — what are they called?
Porpoise: Small cetacean of the family Phocoenidae.
Common in coastal tropical waters worldwide, this group of cartilaginous fish includes about 220 species across 29 genera, from butterfly rays to manta and devil rays — what are they?
Standardized worldwide in 1907 as exactly 200 milligrams, this unit of mass is used to weigh gemstones and pearls, and is divisible into 100 smaller 'points' — what unit is it?
Carat (mass) (ct) is a unit of mass equal to 200 mg (0.00705 oz; 0.00643 ozt), which is used for measuring gemstones and pearls.
Traditionally pounded from cassava, plantains, and cocoyam, this West African staple gets a shoutout in Chinua Achebe's novel Things Fall Apart — what dish is it?
Fufu: Dough-like food in African cuisine.
Nicknamed the boto for its rosy pink hue (especially in males), this South American toothed whale is the largest species of its kind found in a freshwater habitat — what is it?
Amazon river dolphin: Species of toothed whale. The position of the Araguaian river dolphin (I. araguaiaensis) within the clade is still unclear.
This Gram-negative rod bacterium can turn deadly if aspirated into the lungs, producing a telltale bloody, brownish-yellow jelly-like sputum — which pathogen?
Klebsiella pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Klebsiella pneumoniae is a Gram-negative, non-motile, encapsulated, lactose-fermenting, facultative anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium.
This German-American physicist won a 1967 Nobel Prize for explaining how a nuclear cycle powers heavy stars, after heading the Theoretical Division at Los Alamos during World War II — who is he?
Sitting near the center of the Milky Way between Libra and Sagittarius, this zodiac constellation's recognition predates ancient Greek culture — which constellation?
Scorpius: Zodiac constellation in the southern celestial hemisphere.

Though its 83 species can grow as tall as trees, this genus is technically herbaceous, its 'trunk' just tightly wrapped leaf stalks, and it gives us edible bananas, plantains, and fiber for cloth — what genus is it?
Musa (plant) is one of three genera in the family Musaceae.
Discovered in 1969 and sold under the brand name Lotrimin, this azole-class medication treats athlete's foot, ringworm, and oral thrush — what is it?

This genus of 70 to 100 frost-tolerant annual, biennial, and perennial species native to temperate Eurasia, Africa, and North America is the type genus of its flowering plant family — what's the genus?
Papaver is a genus of 70-100 species of frost-tolerant annuals, biennials, and perennials native to temperate and cold regions of Eurasia, Africa and North America.
Resembling a mustelid despite being a wild cat, this Americas-native feline comes in gray or red color morphs and once roamed as far north as Texas — which species?
Jaguarundi: Species of felid. Its range extends from central Argentina in the south and much of South America east of the Andes, through Central America, and into northern Mexico.
Backed by President Nicolas Sarkozy, this French economist served as the IMF's tenth managing director from 2007 until resigning in 2011 amid scandal — who is he?
Dominique Strauss-Kahn: French economist and politician (born 1949)

Adapted from the Army's Black Hawk with folding rotor blades and a hinged tail to fit aboard ships, this twin-engine Navy helicopter handles everything from anti-submarine warfare to medical evacuation — which aircraft?
Sikorsky SH-60 Seahawk: Naval helicopter series of the H-60/S-70 family.
Naming his most famous pistol after his 17th patent — not for holding seventeen rounds, as many assume — this Austrian engineer got his design into Austrian service in 1982 — who was he?
Striking suddenly and resolving — one way or another — within 8 to 10 hours, this mysterious epidemic first hit England in 1485 and vanished after a final outbreak in 1551 — what was it called?
Sweating sickness: Contagious disease in Europe, 1485–1551.
Sometimes nicknamed 'math dyslexia' even though it's a distinct condition, this learning disorder involves persistent difficulty understanding numbers and performing calculations — what is it called?
Cultivated across the tropics for its fragrant essential oil, over 90% of this mint-family herb's global oil supply now comes from Indonesia — which plant?
Marked by physical traits such as a long face, large ears, and unusually flexible fingers, this inherited neurodevelopmental disorder stems from a repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene — which condition?
Fragile X syndrome: X-linked dominant genetic disorder.

This neurological emergency is sudden bleeding directly into brain tissue or its fluid-filled cavities — not from a blocked vessel, but a burst one — causing anything from headache to sudden paralysis. What is it?
Intracerebral hemorrhage: Type of intracranial bleeding that occurs within the brain tissue itself.

With a rich chestnut crown and a bold black patch on each white cheek, this small Old World songbird nests in cavities, walls, or abandoned magpie nests, and lays five or six eggs that hatch in under two weeks — which bird?
Eurasian tree sparrow: Species of bird. The sexes have similar plumage, and young birds are duller versions of the adult.

An advanced modification of its Korean War-era predecessor, this Soviet transonic fighter — NATO reporting name 'Fresco' — was license-built in China and Poland, and remains in North Korean service today — which jet?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Soviet jet fighter aircraft family.
Also called threadworm in the UK and seatworm elsewhere, this common intestinal roundworm spreads via the faecal-oral route and is especially prevalent among children — what parasite is it?

First published in 1797 by an Italian physicist, this phenomenon describes how a fluid's pressure drops as it speeds up through a narrowing pipe — an example of Bernoulli's principle at work in everything from atomizers to wine aerators. What's it called?
Venturi effect: Reduced pressure caused by a flow restriction in a tube or pipe.
First identified in Europe and interbreeding with Neanderthals as early as roughly 45,000 years ago, this term describes the earliest known modern humans on the continent — what are they called?
Cro-Magnon: Earliest anatomically modern humans in Europe and West Asia.

Derived from renewable resources such as corn starch and capable of biodegrading, this thermoplastic polyester made up about a quarter of the world's bioplastic market in 2022 — what compound is this?
This Chinese herbalist, martial artist, and tactical advisor died in 1933 having allegedly been born in 1677 — a longevity claim gerontologists dismiss as myth. Who was he?
Li Ching-Yuen: Chinese herbalist (died 1933). Li's year of birth was alleged to be 1677, though his true age has never been determined.

Endemic to New Zealand and often mistaken for a lizard, this reptile is the sole surviving member of an order that thrived back in the Mesozoic era — its Māori name means 'peaks on the back.' What is it?
Tuatara: Species of reptile. The tuatara (Māori: [ˈtʉ.a.ta.ɾa]; Sphenodon punctatus) is a species of reptile endemic to New Zealand.
This large, rainbow-plumed parrot native to the forests of Central and South America is the national bird of Honduras — what is it?
Scarlet macaw: Species of bird. Like its relative the blue-and-yellow macaw, the scarlet macaw is a popular bird in aviculture as a result of its striking plumage.
Found in pufferfish, blue-ringed octopuses, and rough-skinned newts, this potent sodium-channel-blocking neurotoxin is also being trialed as a treatment for cancer-related pain — what is it?
Tetrodotoxin: Neurotoxin. Its name derives from Tetraodontiformes, an order that includes pufferfish, porcupinefish, ocean sunfish, and triggerfish; several of these species carry the toxin.
With a long hooked bill and webbing between all four toes, this fish-eating aquatic bird family includes the 'great' species commonly seen around Britain and Ireland — what are they called?
Cormorant: Family of aquatic birds. The common names "cormorant" and "shag" have been assigned to different species in the family somewhat haphazardly.
In this condition, part of the stomach slips upward through the diaphragm into the chest, often triggering acid reflux, heartburn, or trouble swallowing — what is it?
Hiatal hernia: Entrance of abdominal organs into the middle chest through the diaphragm.
This field of geoscience studies the shape of land surfaces — not just elevation, but roads, boundaries, and buildings too, as shown on USGS terrain maps — what is it called?
Topography: Study of the forms of land surfaces in earth.
Unlike its niacin cousin, this form of vitamin B3 treats pellagra without causing skin flushing, and as a cream is used to fade acne scars and reduce hyperpigmentation — what is it?

This primate group includes every animal traditionally called a monkey or ape — including humans — and split from the tarsiers roughly 60 million years ago. What's the term for this broader classification?
Its leaves and flowers are covered in dense white hairs that shield it from Alpine cold and UV rays, making this daisy-family flower a symbol of mountaineering purity — what is it?
This age-related eye disease gradually damages the retina's central region, with a 'wet' form involving leaking blood vessels and a 'dry' form marked by deposits called drusen — what is it?
Macular degeneration: Vision loss due to damage to the macula of the eye.

Cataloged by the astronomer Ptolemy in the second century AD and still one of the 88 modern constellations, this zodiac constellation takes its Latin name from the mythological twins Castor and Pollux — what's the constellation?
Gemini (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.

Coated in cornmeal and pan-cooked while still unripe, this dish was originally a Northeastern and Midwestern staple before a hit movie rebranded it as quintessentially Southern comfort food — what is it?
Fried green tomatoes: American dish. Fried green tomatoes is a culinary dish usually found in the United States, made from unripe (green) tomatoes coated with cornmeal and fried.
Coined in 1814 by chemist William Hyde Wollaston, this polyatomic anion forms when carbonic acid loses a proton and plays a crucial role buffering the body's pH — what is it?
Bicarbonate: Polyatomic anion. It is a polyatomic anion with the chemical formula HCO−3.
Also known as cranesbills for their pointed seed pods, this 422-species genus bears five-petaled, often veined flowers and includes at least one protocarnivorous species — what's the genus?

A parasomnia in which wakefulness and deep non-REM sleep occur in different brain regions at once, this condition can produce anything from bathroom trips to attempts at cooking or even driving — what is it?
Sleepwalking: Sleeping phenomenon combined with wakefulness.

Until a 2020 taxonomic overhaul split many of its 261 species into 25 new genera, this rod-shaped, gram-positive bacterial genus formed a major part of the human gut and vaginal microbiota — what genus?
Lactobacillus: Genus of bacteria. Lactobacillus forms biofilms in the vaginal and gut microbiota, allowing them to persist in harsh environmental conditions and maintain ample populations.
This large mass of gray matter sits between the cerebral cortex and the midbrain, relaying sensory and motor signals to the cortex while regulating sleep and alertness — what is this brain structure?
Thalamus: Structure within the brain. It has several functions, such as the relaying of sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex and the regulation of consciousness, sleep, and alertness.
Native to the Mediterranean and nicknamed 'clove pink' for a spicy fragrance reminiscent of cinnamon and nutmeg, what flower is this?
Dianthus caryophyllus: Species of flowering plant.
This synthetic prostaglandin medication treats stomach ulcers, induces labor, and — often paired with mifepristone — is used to end a pregnancy. What drug is it?
Misoprostol: Medication to induce abortion and treat ulcers.
This Russian-American engineer built the first successful four-engine aircraft in 1913 and went on to pioneer the modern helicopter — who was he?
This large, muscular mastiff-type dog breed descends from ancestors brought to the British North American colonies, where they worked on small farms and ranches — what's the breed?
American Bulldog is a large, muscular breed of mastiff-type dog.
Marketed under brand names like Allegra, this second-generation antihistamine treats allergy symptoms without crossing the blood-brain barrier the way older drugs do — what medication is it?
Fexofenadine: Antihistamine medication. Fexofenadine is an antihistamine medication used in the treatment of allergy symptoms such as allergic rhinitis and urticaria.

Caused by excess growth hormone before a child's growth plates fuse — usually from a pituitary tumor — this rare disorder produces height at least three standard deviations above average. What condition is it?
Gigantism: Human growth disorder. It is a rare disorder resulting from increased levels of growth hormone before the fusion of the growth plate which usually occurs at some point soon after puberty.
