Having studied mathematics under Karl Weierstrass, which philosopher founded the school of phenomenology and argued that transcendental consciousness sets the limits of all possible knowledge?
Known across South Asia as Indian gooseberry or amla, this deciduous tree is native to tropical regions of the continent — which plant?
Phyllanthus emblica: Berry and plant. Phyllanthus emblica, commonly known as emblic, Indian gooseberry, amalaki, amloki, or amla, is a deciduous tree of the family Phyllanthaceae.
This physics law states that a black body's radiated energy per unit area is proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature — which law?
Stefan–Boltzmann law: Physical law on the emissive power of black body.
Once called 'hyposulphite of soda,' this reducing agent treats cyanide poisoning and served as photography's key fixer in the 19th century — what compound?
Sodium thiosulfate: Chemical compound. Sodium thiosulfate (sodium thiosulphate) is an inorganic compound with the formula Na2S2O3·xH2O.
Also called baked-apple berry or Arctic berry, this amber-hued fruit resembling a blackberry grows wild across boreal forests and Arctic tundra — what's its scientific name?
Rubus chamaemorus: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
Nicknamed the 'honey bear' though unrelated to actual bears, this nocturnal rainforest mammal is the only member of its genus and a cousin of raccoons and coatis — which arboreal creature?
Sold under the brand names Trintellix and Brintellix, this antidepressant belongs to a drug class called serotonin modulators and stimulators — which medication?
Vortioxetine: Serotonin modulator antidepressant. Its effectiveness is viewed as similar to that of other antidepressants.
Prized for its oil since Spanish and Portuguese traders carried it from South America to Europe in the 1600s, this citrus-scented herb also goes by 'beebrush' — what's its species name?
Aloysia citrodora: Species of plant. Aloysia citrodora, lemon verbena, is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family Verbenaceae, native to South America.
This Bletchley Park code-breaker helped crack the Enigma cipher during World War II and was later honored with an MBE for her work — who was she?
This Intel co-founder proposed the famous observation that the number of transistors on a chip roughly doubles every two years — who is he?
Once nicknamed 'the poor man's racehorse,' this British sighthound is believed to have the fastest idle-to-running acceleration of any dog breed — which breed?
Whippet: British breed of dog. It closely resembles the Greyhound and the smaller Italian Greyhound, and is intermediate between them in size.
Also badged as the Citroën Jumper and the Peugeot Boxer in Europe, this light commercial van entered North America in 2014 as the Ram ProMaster — which van?
Fiat Ducato is a light commercial vehicle jointly developed by FCA Italy and PSA Group (now Stellantis), and mainly manufactured by Sevel, a joint venture between the two companies since 1981.
Born in Taiwan but naturalized in Japan, this businessman invented the world's first prepackaged instant noodle brand and later created Cup Noodles — who is he?
Momofuku Ando: Taiwanese-Japanese inventor and businessman (1910–2007)
Marketed as Lanoxin, this centuries-old heart medication boosts contraction strength while slowing the heart rate, but can cause blurred vision and breast enlargement in excess — what is it?
Defined by at least one carbon-carbon triple bond and traditionally nicknamed for its simplest member, ethyne (better known as acetylene) — which class of hydrocarbon is this?
Alkyne: Hydrocarbon compound containing one or more C≡C bonds.
Made up of 12 paired bones plus the sternum and spine, this bony enclosure of the chest shields the heart and lungs while housing the muscles used for breathing — what is it?
Rib cage: Bone structure of the thorax.

This branch of zoology studying animal behavior traces its scientific roots to Darwin and came into its own in the 1930s through Nobel laureates Tinbergen, Lorenz, and von Frisch — what's the field called?
This medical and surgical specialty treats everything from inflammatory conditions and cancers to hair loss, requiring about four years of training beyond medical school — what field is it?
Dermatology: Field of medicine dealing with the hair, nails, skin, and its diseases.

Named after the Latin word for 'earth' despite being one of the rarest elements in Earth's crust, this brittle silver-white metalloid with atomic number 52 was first found in a Transylvanian gold mine — what is it?
Tellurium: Chemical element with atomic number 52 (Te)
Native to eastern North America's wet woods and swamps, this shrub genus produces bitter 'chokeberries' that reached Scandinavia and Russia by the eighteenth century — what genus is this?

Aronia: Genus of plants (chokeberries). Aronia is a genus of deciduous shrubs, the chokeberries, in the family Rosaceae native to eastern North America and most commonly found in wet woods and swamps.
Despite the name, these fifty species of rodent can't truly fly — they glide between trees using a furred membrane called a patagium. What are they?
Made by combining phenol and acetone, this compound forms 65 to 70 percent of the world's polycarbonate plastics production — which chemical?
Bisphenol A: Chemical used in plastics, xenoestrogen.
Living in damp spots like rotting wood, these polyphyletic organisms combine into fruiting bodies that release spores to help decompose dead plants — what are they?
Marketed as Nizoral, this antifungal medication also treats Cushing's syndrome and excess hair growth in women, though oral use risks liver damage — which drug?
Also known as flying foxes, these 197-plus species of fruit-eating bat likely evolved in Australasia some 31 million years ago — what are they called?
Representing the Nemean Lion slain by Heracles as one of his twelve labors, this zodiac constellation sits between Cancer and Virgo — which constellation?
Leo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac, between Cancer, the Crab, to the west and Virgo, the Maiden, to the east.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, these lizards are unusual for making vocal chirps and clicks, and most lack eyelids, relying on a transparent membrane instead — what are they?
Gecko: Lizards belonging to the suborder Gekkota.
Sharing the 2015 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Tomas Lindahl and Paul Modrich, this Turkish-American scientist was honored for mechanistic studies of DNA repair — who is he?
Aziz Sancar: Turkish biochemist and molecular biologist (born 1946)
Based on a civilian widebody jet, this European aerial-refueling tanker holds over 90% of the air-to-air refueling market outside the United States, with 17 countries as customers — which aircraft?

Airbus A330 MRTT: Aerial refuelling tanker aircraft. The Airbus A330 Multi Role Tanker Transport (MRTT) is a European aerial refueling and military transport aircraft based on the civilian Airbus A330.

Distinct from addiction, this biopsychological condition occurs when a person's body has adapted so much to a psychoactive drug that stopping triggers withdrawal, requiring continued use just to function — what is this condition called?
Substance dependence: Need for a drug, whose discontinuation results in withdrawal symptoms.
Named by Linnaeus after the mythical strongman Heracles, this genus of towering herbs in the carrot family includes hogweed and cow parsnip — what is it?
Heracleum (plant) is a genus of biennial and perennial herbs in the carrot family Apiaceae.
Closely related to the llama, this wild South American camelid shares its range with a higher-altitude cousin, the vicuña — what is it?
Shining as the brightest star in Taurus some 67 light-years from Earth, this red giant has swollen to roughly 45 times the Sun's size despite a cooler surface — which star?
Aldebaran: Taurus Brightest Star. Aldebaran (Arabic: الدَّبَرَان, lit. 'The Follower') is a star in the zodiac constellation of Taurus.

Originally bred for the hunt and later famous for trotting alongside horse-drawn firehouse carriages, this white breed with dark spots traces its roots to a region on the Adriatic coast — which breed?
Dalmatian dog: Croatian hunting/carriage/coach dog breed.

Named for a mythological daughter of Tantalus, this silvery transition metal with atomic number 41 was once called columbium and is now prized as a nickel-free option in hypoallergenic jewelry — which element?
Niobium: Chemical element with atomic number 41 (Nb)
Though overshadowed by the more famous Spitfire, this RAF fighter actually inflicted 60 percent of the Luftwaffe's losses during the Battle of Britain — which 1930s aircraft?
Hawker Hurricane: British fighter aircraft of the 1930s and 40s.

An essential nutrient your liver can only partly produce on its own, this compound builds phospholipids in cell membranes and helps make a neurotransmitter for muscle control, and occurs naturally in eggs, meat, and fish — which nutrient?
Choline: Chemical compound and essential nutrient. Choline is a cation with the chemical formula [(CH3)3NCH2CH2OH]+.
Known for a synchronized aerial swarming display called murmuration, this glossy-plumed bird family includes talkative mynas as members — which birds?
Starling: Family of birds. The Sturnidae are named for the genus Sturnus, which in turn comes from the Latin word for starling, sturnus.
Also known as an ischemic stroke, this necrotic brain condition is the second-leading cause of death worldwide and a leading cause of physical disability — what is it?
Cerebral infarction: Stroke resulting from lack of blood flow.
Native to southwestern Europe, this venomous viper is also called the asp or aspic viper, with about 4% of untreated bites proving fatal — which snake?
Vipera aspis: Species of snake. Its common names include asp, asp viper, European asp, and aspic viper, among others.
When fibroblasts overproduce collagen after repeated injury or chronic inflammation, this permanent connective-tissue scarring can impair an organ's normal function — what is it called?
Fibrosis: Excess connective tissue in healing.

Caused by a sudden burst of synchronized electrical activity in the brain, this neurological event affects roughly 50 million people worldwide and can range from a brief blank stare to a full convulsion — what is it?
Seizure: Period of symptoms due to excessive or synchronous neuronal brain activity.
This retired American physician turned ufologist founded both a center for extraterrestrial-intelligence study and a project pushing for the release of classified UFO information — who is he?
Introduced to Britain in the 19th century as an ornamental plant, this Caucasus-native's sap causes painful blistering burns when exposed skin meets sunlight — which species?
Heracleum mantegazzianum: Species of flowering plant. Heracleum mantegazzianum, commonly known as giant hogweed, is a monocarpic perennial herbaceous plant in the carrot family Apiaceae.
This passive, energy-free process moves water through a plant and releases it as vapor from its leaves, also cooling the plant and driving nutrient flow — what is it called?
Transpiration: Process of water movement through a plant. Transpiration is the process of water movement through a plant and its evaporation from aerial parts, such as leaves, stems and flowers.
Most often extracted from chicory, this plant-stored fructan earned FDA approval as a dietary fiber in 2018 and remains the gold-standard compound for measuring kidney filtration rates — what is it?
This genus of small-to-medium wildcats — ranging from the diminutive black-footed cat to the larger jungle cat — also includes humanity's domestic pet, the housecat — which genus?
Combined with formaldehyde to create hardwearing resins found in Formica countertops, plastic dinnerware, and the foam in a Magic Eraser, this nitrogen-rich compound also resists fire — what is it?
Melamine: Fire-resistant chemical used in dinnerware, insulation, and cleaning products.
This Turkish businesswoman served as one of her father's chief advisers back in 2013, when he held the office of prime minister and later became Turkey's president — who is she?
Sümeyye Erdoğan (ne Erdoan; born 22 August 1985) is a Turkish businesswoman and the daughter of President Recep Tayyip Erdoan.
Defined by a single skull opening behind each eye socket that anchors larger jaw muscles, this major branch of the amniote family tree includes all mammals and their extinct kin — which clade?
Synapsida: Clade of tetrapods. Synapsida is a diverse group of tetrapod vertebrates that includes all mammals and their extinct relatives.
This former Google CEO co-authored the Unix tool Lex as a Bell Labs intern in 1975, later ran Novell, and in 2025 became chief executive of a rocket manufacturer — who is he?

Eric Schmidt (born April 27, 1955) is an American businessman and former computer engineer who was the chief executive officer of Google from 2001 to 2011 and the company's executive chairman from 2011 to 2015.
A French soldier turned naturalist, this early proponent of biological evolution published the three-volume 'Flore françoise' and joined the French Academy of Sciences in 1779 — who is he?
Named after a Louisiana parish and named the state's official canine in 1979, this herding breed was traditionally used to hunt feral boars — what breed is it?
Catahoula Leopard Dog: American breed of dog.
Its Latin name means 'water-carrier,' and this zodiac constellation sits between Capricornus and Pisces, in a region of the sky nicknamed 'the Sea' for its watery neighbors — which constellation?

Aquarius (constellation) is an equatorial constellation of the zodiac, between Capricornus and Pisces. Its name is Latin for "water-carrier" or "cup-carrier", and its traditional astrological symbol is (♒︎), a representation of water.
Formulated in 1834, this principle of electromagnetism states that an induced current always flows in a direction that opposes the very change in magnetic field that created it — which principle?
Lenz's law: Electromagnetic opposition to change.
Derived from Greek words for 'brain' and 'suffering,' this umbrella medical term covers any disease or disorder that causes overall brain dysfunction — what is it?
Encephalopathy: Disorders or diseases of the brain.
Also known as tic douloureux, this chronic pain disorder causes sudden, shock-like facial pain and has been linked to depression — what condition is it?
Trigeminal neuralgia: Neurological pain disorder. There are two main types: typical and atypical trigeminal neuralgia.
A legendary Heian-era court diviner and astrologer, this figure lived 84 years free of illness, fueling belief in mystical powers — a Kyoto shrine bears his name today. Who is he?
Formed from the C5-T1 spinal nerve roots, this network of nerves runs through the neck and over the first rib to supply the shoulder, arm, and hand — what is it?
Brachial plexus: Network of nerves. This plexus extends from the spinal cord, through the cervicoaxillary canal in the neck, over the first rib, and into the armpit.

Steel-blue with wavy black markings on its back and silvery underneath, this shoaling fish thrives in the cooler waters of the Mediterranean, Black Sea, and northern ocean near Europe — which species?
Atlantic mackerel: Species of fish. The Atlantic mackerel's body is elongate, steel-blue marked with wavy black lines dorsally and silvery-white ventrally, its snout long and pointed.
Credited with popularizing the index fund, this investor founded The Vanguard Group and preached long-term patience over speculation — who is he?
John C. Bogle: American investor and business magnate (1929–2019)
This imperial unit of pressure equals about 6.895 kilopascals and is the number you check when filling a bicycle tire to around 65 — which unit?
Pound per square inch: Unit of pressure or stress. It is the pressure resulting from a force with magnitude of one pound-force applied to an area of one square inch.
Once tapped as a source of natural rubber, though no longer used commercially for that purpose, this houseplant native to South and Southeast Asia is nicknamed the 'rubber tree.' Which species?
Ficus elastica: Species of banyan tree.

Nicknamed the 'Flying Tank' by Soviet ground troops, this WWII ground-attack aircraft became, together with its successor, the most-produced military plane design in aviation history — which aircraft?

Ilyushin Il-2: Soviet ground attack aircraft of WWII. The Ilyushin Il-2 (Russian: Илью́шин Ил-2) is a ground-attack plane that was produced by the Soviet Union in large numbers during the Second World War.
This common, noncancerous enlargement of a male gland can cause frequent urination and a weak stream; it isn't linked to poor hygiene, and there's no known cure. What's the condition?
Benign prostatic hyperplasia: Noncancerous increase in size of the prostate gland.
Named after a barberry-related plant genus and glowing bright yellow under ultraviolet light, this alkaloid was recorded in an ancient Chinese herbal medicine text around 200 BC. What compound is it?

Made of one oxygen and one hydrogen atom bonded together with a negative charge, this ion is the active base in the sodium compound used to produce millions of tons of industrial chemicals yearly. What ion is it?

Affecting about half of all adults and often treated with antifungal cream, this common scalp condition causes flaking and mild itchiness but isn't actually caused by poor hygiene. What condition is it?
Dandruff: Skin condition of the scalp. It can result in social or self-esteem problems.
This genus of orb-weaving spiders, encompassing the European garden spider and the barn spider among its 500-plus species, was named by an 18th-century Swedish naturalist in 1757 — which genus?
Araneus: Genus of spiders. The genus was erected by Carl Alexander Clerck in 1757.
As Grand Pensionary of Holland during the Dutch Golden Age, this statesman dominated politics from 1650 until the 'Disaster Year' of 1672 — who was he?
Home to Polaris, the North Star, this far-northern constellation is also nicknamed the Little Dipper — which one?
Ursa Minor: Constellation in the northern celestial hemisphere.
Also called the Java plum, this fast-growing evergreen tree from the Indian subcontinent can top 30 meters and live for over a century — which tree?
Syzygium cumini: Species of tree. It can reach heights of up to 30 m (100 ft) and can live more than 100 years.
A Cambridge-educated lecturer in English literature, this Hashemite princess briefly reigned as Queen of Jordan as King Hussein's first wife — who is she?
Dina bint Abdul-Hamid: Queen of Jordan from 1955 to 1957.
Once a deputy district attorney in Weld County, Colorado, this now-suspended lawyer served on Donald Trump's 2020 campaign legal team — who is she?
With a glossy black head and a distinctive white bill shield, this rail-family waterbird is found from Europe to Australia — which bird?
Eurasian coot: Species of bird. The Eurasian coot (Fulica atra), also known as the common coot or Australian coot, is a member of the rail and crake bird family, the Rallidae.
Traditionally kept as an indoor watchdog, this small non-sporting dog breed hails from Tibet — which breed?
Lhasa Apso: Tibetan breed of dog. The Lhasa Apso ( LAH-sə AP-soh) is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet.
Squash, pumpkin, cucumber, watermelon, and the plant behind loofah sponges all belong to which family, nicknamed the gourds?
Cucurbitaceae: Family of plants. The Cucurbitaceae ( kew-KUR-bih-TAY-see-ee), also called cucurbits or the gourd family, are a plant family consisting of about 965 species in 101 genera.
Carnations and sweet williams both belong to which flowering plant genus of about 340 species, native mainly to Europe and Asia?
In 1900, this mathematician presented a list of unsolved problems that shaped 20th-century mathematical research — who is he?
This term for cancer that begins in gland cells applies to the most common form of breast cancer and one of the two major types of esophageal cancer — which term?
Adenocarcinoma: Cancer of epithelial cells with glandular origin or characteristics.

Now built by Leonardo but originally developed jointly by an Italian and an American helicopter maker, this 15-seat medium twin-engine helicopter serves VIP transport, firefighting, and search-and-rescue roles — which aircraft?
AgustaWestland AW139: Twin-engined, medium-lift helicopter manufactured by Leonardo.
Mentioned by Theophrastus as 'ágnos,' this Mediterranean shrub was long believed to act as an anaphrodisiac, giving it a purity-themed common name — which species?
Vitex agnus-castus: Species of flowering plant in the mint family Lamiaceae.
Grown to feed silkworms for commercial silk production, this fast-growing tree releases its pollen at more than half the speed of sound — which species?
Morus alba: Plant species in the fig family.
Formed by cross-linking phenolic precursors, this class of complex organic polymers gives rigidity to plant cell walls, especially in wood and bark — what is it?
Lignin: Structural phenolic polymer in plant cell walls.
Named for hindwings that resemble human ears when unfolded, this reddish-brown insect is a common household pest known for the pincers at the tip of its abdomen — which species?
Forficula auricularia: Species of earwig. It is an omnivorous insect belonging to the family Forficulidae.
Nicknamed the 'stinking corpse lily,' this Southeast Asian plant genus produces the world's largest flower and was first seen by a Briton in 1818 after a local servant pointed it out — which genus?
Grouped by their small size and use of echolocation, this suborder of flying mammals turns out to be genetically distinct from its bigger, fruit-eating relatives — which creatures?
Named from a Norwegian word for 'small fry of fish,' these shrimp-like crustaceans form a biomass of some 379 million tonnes in the Southern Ocean alone — which creatures?

Krill: Small, shrimp-like crustaceans; order of crustaceans. Krill (Euphausiids) (sing.: krill) are small and exclusively marine crustaceans of the order Euphausiacea, found in all of the world's oceans.
One of Europe's largest bee species, this dark, iridescent carpenter bee nests in dead wood and is generally not aggressive unless provoked — which insect?
Xylocopa violacea: Species of bee. Xylocopa violacea, the violet carpenter bee, is the common European species of carpenter bee, and one of the largest bees in Europe.
Often a complication of cancer treatment, this incurable, progressive swelling condition is managed with compression therapy and manual drainage rather than diuretics — what is it?
Lymphedema: Swelling due to a compromised lymphatic system.
Whether natural silk or synthetic nylon, this class of polymer is defined by repeating units joined through amide bonds — what is it?
Polyamide: Macromolecule with repeating units linked by amide bonds.

Historically defined by having two embryonic seed leaves, this once-standard division of flowering plants covers around 200,000 species but turned out not to share one common ancestor — which plant group?
Dicotyledon: Historical grouping of flowering plants.
Declared one of the world's most invasive species in 2000 and named Australia's top pest problem in 2008, which highly adaptable Asian bird thrives in cities?
Common myna: Bird of the family Sturnidae.
One of the largest snake species on Earth, this Southeast Asian native became invasive in Florida after escaping the pet trade — which snake is this?
Burmese python: Species of large, nonvenomous snake.
Ranging from roughly seawater-strength up to a fully saturated 26%, which salty solution is used for pickling food, de-icing roads, and turns up as a wastewater byproduct of desalination?
Brine: Concentrated solution of salt in water.
With atomic number 87 and a most stable isotope whose half-life is just 22 minutes, this alkali metal is the second-rarest naturally occurring element on Earth — which one?
Francium: Chemical element with atomic number 87 (Fr)
This ability to detect light and turn it into an image of one's surroundings can occur via daytime or night vision — what is it called?
Visual perception: Ability to interpret the surrounding environment using light in the visible spectrum.
This outdated 19th-century term for what's now called acute or chronic nephritis was marked by swelling and albumin showing up in the urine — what was it called?
Bright's disease is a historical classification of kidney diseases that are described in modern medicine as acute or chronic nephritis.

With six engines slung in nacelles beneath its swept wings — a design borrowed from captured German research — this Cold War-era American bomber was built to outrun Soviet interceptors at high altitude — which aircraft?
Boeing B-47 Stratojet: Cold War-era American jet bomber. The primary mission of the B-47 was as a nuclear bomber capable of striking targets within the Soviet Union.
Growing out of calculus and the study of derivatives and integrals, this branch of mathematics examines functions, spaces, and limits using methods of approximation and convergence — which field?

Mathematical analysis: Branch of mathematics. Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics that studies functions, spaces, and operators through quantitative methods of approximation and convergence.

Native to South Africa's Western Cape, this flowering bulb genus lends its common name to popular winter houseplants that actually belong to a different genus, Hippeastrum — which bulb, also called the naked lady or Jersey lily?
Amaryllis: Genus of plants. Amaryllis is the only genus in the subtribe Amaryllidinae (tribe Amaryllideae).
Found from Bangladesh to the Philippines, these nocturnal primates make up the genus Nycticebus and include at least eight recognized species — what are they called?
Slow loris: Genus of primates from Southeast Asia.

This American biologist founded a university institute for sex research in 1947 and gave his name to a scale measuring sexual orientation, after publishing landmark but controversial reports on human sexuality. Who was he?
Native to Africa and Yemen, this drought-resistant tree species has individuals radiocarbon-dated to over 1,275 years old — what is it?
Adansonia digitata: Species of plant native to Africa.
This category of mental health conditions involves an unconscious defense mechanism that fragments consciousness, memory, and identity to protect against traumatic stress — what is it called?
Dissociative disorder: Set of mental health conditions.

This digestive disorder involves weak stomach muscle contractions that delay how quickly food empties into the intestine, often linked to nerve damage from uncontrolled diabetes — what's the condition called?
Gastroparesis: Medical condition. The opposite of this, where stomach contents exit quickly into the duodenum, is called dumping syndrome.
Approved for medical use in the US back in 1950, this medication treats intestinal spasms such as those seen in irritable bowel syndrome — what is it called?

This deep-sea fish off Australia and New Zealand has almost no muscle and a gelatinous body just under water's density, letting it float effortlessly at depths beyond 600 meters — what is its scientific name?
Psychrolutes marcidus: Species of fish. Psychrolutes marcidus, the smooth-head blobfish, or simply the blobfish, is a deep-sea fish of the family Psychrolutidae.
This vertebrate group includes every amphibian and amniote — even limbless descendants like snakes, which still count as members through their four-limbed ancestry — what's the clade called?
Tetrapod: Clade of the first four-limbed vertebrates and their descendants.
Commonly called spurge, this giant plant genus includes the popular Christmas poinsettia and a thorny succulent nicknamed 'crown of thorns' — which genus is it?

Known for feigning death when cornered, which genus of cat-sized marsupials includes the only marsupial species found north of Mexico?
Didelphis: Genus of marsupials. The six species in the genus Didelphis, commonly known as Large American opossums, are members of the opossum order, Didelphimorphia.

First identified in 1846 and nicknamed 'Peter Elam's disease' in parts of South Asia, this skin condition causing patchy discoloration is caused by an overgrowth of Malassezia yeast — what is it called?
Tinea versicolor: Skin disease. Tinea versicolor (also pityriasis versicolor) is a condition characterized by a skin eruption on the trunk and proximal extremities.
Known by the common name 'greater celandine,' this perennial flowering plant belongs to the poppy family and is native to Europe and western Asia — what's its scientific name?
Chelidonium majus: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family. One of two species in the genus Chelidonium, it is native to Europe and western Asia and introduced widely in North America.
Made of collagen like its bone-to-bone cousin the ligament, this tough band of connective tissue instead links muscle to bone, and there are about 4,000 of them in your body — what is it called?
Tendon: Type of tissue that connects muscle to bone.

Believed to be the first coffee species ever cultivated, this plant, native to the forests of Ethiopia, South Sudan, and Yemen, still accounts for roughly 60% of global coffee production — what's its scientific name?
Coffea arabica: Species of coffee plant. Coffea arabica, also known as the Arabica coffee, is a species of flowering plant in the coffee and madder family Rubiaceae.
Commonly known as chaga, this parasitic fungus grows on birch trees and forms a charcoal-like black mass often marketed, questionably, as a health supplement — what's its scientific name?
Inonotus obliquus: Species of fungus. Inonotus obliquus, commonly called chaga (a Latinization of the Russian word ча́га), is a fungus in the family Hymenochaetaceae.

Also known as physiography, this branch of natural science studies the atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, and geosphere — as opposed to the branch focused on the built human environment. Which field of study?
