Brno: Statutory city in the Czech Republic. Brno ( BUR-noh, Czech pronunciation: [ˈbr̩no]; German: Brünn [bʁʏn]) is a city in the South Moravian Region of the Czech Republic.
Since 1923, this French city on the Sarthe River has hosted the world's oldest active endurance sports car race, run over 24 hours — which city?
Le Mans: Prefecture and commune in Pays de la Loire, France.
Sitting on the Loire River about 120 kilometres southwest of Paris, this French city was once a capital of the Kingdom of France and today serves as prefecture of the Loiret department — which city?
Orléans: Prefecture and commune in France. Orléans (US:; French: [ɔʁleɑ̃]) is a city in north-central France, about 120 kilometres (74 miles) southwest of Paris.
Nicknamed the 'Garden City,' this South Island metropolis sits where the Avon River winds through its center and the ancient volcanic Banks Peninsula rises to its south — which city?
Christchurch: City in Canterbury, New Zealand.
Named for the medieval Germanic tribes the Alemanni and Suebi, this southwestern German region today spans parts of Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg — what is it called?
Swabia: Cultural, historic, and linguistic region of Germany.
Rising 632 meters in Pudong's Lujiazui district, this 128-story building held the world's fastest elevators until 2017 and remains China's tallest skyscraper — what is it?
Shanghai Tower: Megatall skyscraper in China. The Shanghai Tower is a 128-story, 632-meter-tall (2,073-foot) megatall skyscraper located in Lujiazui, Pudong, Shanghai.
Home to the capital Culiacán Rosales, this northwestern Mexican state faces Baja California Sur across the Gulf of California and is crossed by the Sierra Madre Occidental — which state?
Sinaloa: State of Mexico. It is divided into 20 municipalities, and its capital and largest city is Culiacán Rosales.
With around 226,000 residents, this German city is the second-largest in Saxony-Anhalt and forms a shared conurbation with Leipzig, the two linked by an airport based in Schkeuditz — which city?
Halle (Saale): City in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Halle (Saale), or simply Halle (German pronunciation: [ˈhalə]), is the second largest city of the German state of Saxony-Anhalt.

Believed by Hindus to be the birthplace of the seventh avatar of Vishnu, this contested site in Ayodhya once sat beneath a mosque before archaeologists were court-ordered to excavate it — what is this site called?
Ram Janmabhoomi: Birthplace of Rama in Hindu mythology.
Sitting on the banks of the Biała River about 200 km northeast of Warsaw, this city is the capital of the Podlaskie Voivodeship and Poland's tenth-largest — which city?
Białystok: City county in Podlaskie Voivodeship, Poland. It is the tenth-largest city in Poland, second in terms of population density, and thirteenth in area.
Home to one of the largest ports on the Black Sea, this Russian city in Krasnodar Krai holds the Soviet-era honorific title of Hero City — which city?
Novorossiysk: City in Krasnodar Krai, Russia. Novorossiysk (Russian: Новоросси́йск, IPA: [nəvərɐˈsʲijsk]; Adyghe: ЦӀэмэз, romanized: C̣ămăz) is a city in Krasnodar Krai, Russia.
Founded in 1858 after an earthquake destroyed its ancient predecessor, this Peloponnese city serves as capital of its surrounding regional unit in Greece. Name the city?

Corinth (modern city) is a city in the Peloponnese in Greece. Corinth ( KORR-inth; Greek: Κόρινθος, romanized: Kórinthos, Modern Greek pronunciation: [ˈkorinθos]) is a city in the Peloponnese in Greece.
This Austrian town on the Bavarian border is best known as the birthplace of a 20th-century dictator, who lived there until he was three — name the town?
Braunau am Inn: Town in Upper Austria.
Formed in 1929 by merging five towns along a river valley in western Germany, this city is renowned as the country's greenest, with two-thirds green space — name the city?
Wuppertal: City in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.
Despite having the world's second-tallest church steeple, at over 161 meters, this German Gothic building has never been a bishop's seat, so it isn't technically a cathedral — what is it called?
Ulm Minster: Lutheran church in Germany; second tallest church in the world.
Home to Volkswagen's headquarters and, until 2022, the world's largest car plant, this planned German city sits on the river Aller near Hanover — which city?
Wolfsburg: City in Lower Saxony, German.
This major Algerian coastal city, second in size and importance only to Algiers, sits 432 kilometers to its west-southwest and anchors a metro area of roughly 1.5 million — what city is it?
Oran is a major coastal city located in the northwest of Algeria.
Wedged between the Caspian Sea and the Caucasus Mountains, this is Russia's southernmost city and, with records dating to the 8th century BC, also its oldest — which city?
Derbent: City in the Republic of Dagestan, Russia.
Formed by the confluence of the Uruguay and Paraná Rivers, this South American estuary is considered the widest river in the world at up to 220 kilometers across — which waterway?
Río de la Plata: River or estuary in South America. It empties into the Atlantic Ocean and forms a funnel-shaped indentation on the southeastern coastline of South America.
Home to over four million people as of 2020, this is the capital of China's Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region and the second-largest city in the country's northwestern interior — which city?
Ürümqi: Capital and largest city of Xinjiang, China.
Also historically known as Celebes, this Indonesian island shaped by four distinct peninsulas is the world's 11th-largest — which island?
Sulawesi: Region and island in Indonesia.
Renamed in 1964 after an Italian communist leader, this Russian city in Samara Oblast is home to carmaker AvtoVAZ and is nicknamed Russia's Motown — which city?
Tolyatti: City in Samara Oblast, Russia. Tolyatti or Togliatti, known before 1964 as Stavropol, is a city in Samara Oblast, Russia.
Nicknamed South Africa's 'judicial capital' alongside legislative Cape Town and administrative Pretoria, this Free State city also hosted matches in the 2010 FIFA World Cup — which city?

Bloemfontein: Judicial capital of South Africa. Bloemfontein ( BLOOM-fon-tayn; Afrikaans: [ˈblumfɔntəin]), also known as Bloem, is the capital and the largest city of the Free State province in South Africa.
Absent from the earliest legends, this fictional castle and court first appeared in 12th-century French romances as King Arthur's capital — what's it called?
Camelot: Castle and court associated with King Arthur.
This Turkish beach resort's Middle Ages heyday came under Seljuk sultan Alaeddin Kayqubad I, whose building campaign left many of its landmarks — which city, 83 miles east of Antalya?
Alanya: District and municipality in Antalya, Turkey.
Founded by Russian general Alexander Suvorov in 1792 on the Dniester River's eastern bank, this city serves as the capital of an unrecognized breakaway state within Moldova — which city?
Tiraspol: Capital and largest city of Transnistria.

Erected in 1923 as a temporary ad for a Los Angeles real-estate development, these giant white letters atop Mount Lee lost their last four ('LAND') in 1949 and were rebuilt in steel in 1978 — what famous landmark is it?
Hollywood Sign: Landmark in Los Angeles, California. The Hollywood Sign is an American landmark and cultural icon overlooking Hollywood, Los Angeles.
Built in the 1890s to serve a nearby mine, this Swedish city is now home to a space research center and a university's space science department — which city, the northernmost in its country?
Kiruna: Mining city in northern Sweden.
Nicknamed the 'Orange City,' this central Indian metropolis hosts the winter session of its state's legislature and serves as headquarters for a major Hindu nationalist organization — which city?
Home to over four million people, this Taiwanese special municipality completely surrounds the island's capital and traces its early history to the Ketagalan indigenous people — which municipality?
New Taipei City: Special municipality in Taiwan. During the Japanese rule of Taiwan, the entire area of New Taipei City was organized as part of the Taihoku Prefecture.

As the closest French town to England, this Channel port has been linked to Folkestone by tunnel since 1994, and the White Cliffs of Dover, across the water, are visible from it on a clear day — which city?
Calais: Subprefecture and commune in Hauts-de-France, France.

Located about eight kilometres southwest of central Athens along the Saronic Gulf, this ancient port city was founded in the early 5th century BC and is today Greece's fourth-largest municipality — which city?
Piraeus: Harbour of Athens and a port city in Attica, Greece.
Nicknamed the 'Armory Capital of Russia,' this city west of the Ural Mountains briefly bore the name Ustinov in the 1980s, honoring a Soviet defense minister — what is it, the capital of Udmurtia?
Izhevsk: City in Udmurtia, Russia. It is situated along the Izh River, west of the Ural Mountains in Eastern Europe.
Founded as a Roman fort around 8 BC at the meeting point of the Rhine and Moselle rivers, this German city's name comes from the Latin word for 'confluence' — what city is it?
Rising in the Carpathian foothills and flowing through Kraków and Warsaw before reaching the Baltic Sea, this waterway is Poland's longest river — what's it called?
Vistula: Major river in Central Europe.

Democracy took root here in 508 BC and lasted nearly two centuries, while this city-state's alliance with Sparta helped defeat the Persian Empire before it led the Delian League to its peak — which city-state?
Classical Athens: City-state in ancient Greece.
This windowless, 550-foot Brutalist skyscraper in Tribeca once served as a major AT&T telephone exchange and has been reported to double as an NSA surveillance site — which building?
33 Thomas Street: Skyscraper in Manhattan, New York, US.
Sitting on the River Gera in the middle of Thuringia's chain of six cities, this German state capital boasts one of the best-preserved medieval old towns in the country — what city is it?
Erfurt: Capital of Thuringia, Germany. Erfurt (German pronunciation: [ˈɛʁfʊʁt]) is the capital and largest city of the Central German state of Thuringia, with a population of around 216,000.
Located in the Gulf of Thailand and home to about 179,000 people, this is Vietnam's largest island and became a special administrative zone in 2025 — what is it called?
Phú Quốc: Largest island in Vietnam. Phú Quốc (Vietnamese: [fǔ wuə̌k]) is a special zone in An Giang province, Vietnam.
Founded by Russian imperial decree in 1784 on the site of a Crimean Tatar town called Aqmescit, this city has been the de facto capital of Russian-controlled Crimea since 2014 — what city is it?
Simferopol: Second-largest city on the Crimean Peninsula.
Founded around 600 BC and now Romania's principal Black Sea port, this city is the oldest continuously inhabited settlement in the country — what is it?
Constanța is a city in the Northern Dobruja historical region of Romania.

Standing 58 stories tall at 721-725 Fifth Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, this skyscraper houses the headquarters of a business empire founded by the current U.S. president, who also keeps a penthouse there — what is it?
Trump Tower: Skyscraper in Manhattan, New York.
Located in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley northeast of Beirut, this city's history stretches back at least 11,000 years, and it became a center of note after Alexander the Great's conquest — what is it?
Baalbek is a city located east of the Litani River in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley, about 67 km (42 mi) northeast of Beirut.
Home to the Venkateswara Temple — one of Hinduism's eight self-manifested shrines to Vishnu — this Andhra Pradesh city sits 150 km from Chennai. Which city?
Tirupati: City in Andhra Pradesh, India. Tirupati ( Tiru-pa-ti) is a city in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh and serves as the administrative headquarters of Tirupati district.
Founded as a 16th-century trading hub between the Deccan Plateau and Delhi, this Madhya Pradesh city was later ruled by the Holkars under the Maratha Empire — which city?
Indore: Metropolis in Madhya Pradesh, India.
Situated between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim about 49 km north of Jerusalem, this West Bank city was renamed Flavia Neapolis by the Roman emperor Vespasian in 72 CE — which city?
Nablus: Palestinian city in the northern West Bank.
A UNESCO World Heritage Site on the Vistula River, this Polish city was expanded by the Teutonic Knights in 1233 and later joined the Hanseatic League — which city?
Founded in 1561 by a Spanish explorer and later relocated to the banks of the Pirai River, this is Bolivia's largest city — which one?
Santa Cruz de la Sierra: Most populous city in Bolivia.
Straddling the confluence of the Vistula River and its tributary, this northern Polish city is the largest in the historical region of Kuyavia and home to over 339,000 people — which city?
Formerly known as Stanisławów, this city in western Ukraine was built in the mid-17th century as a fortress for a Polish noble family and later came under Habsburg rule in 1772 — what is it?
Ivano-Frankivsk is a city in western Ukraine. Ivano-Frankivsk (Ukrainian: Івано-Франківськ, IPA: [iˈwɑno frɐnˈkiu̯sʲk]), formerly Stanyslaviv, Stanislav and Stanisławów, is a city in western Ukraine.
Sitting on the Terek River at the foothills of the Caucasus, and once known as Ordzhonikidze, which Russian city is the capital of North Ossetia–Alania?
Vladikavkaz: City in North Ossetia–Alania, Russia. It is located in the southeast of the republic at the foothills of the Caucasus, situated on the Terek River.
Nicknamed 'The Florence of the South' for its Baroque architecture, which city at the heel of Italy's boot gives its name to a soft, sculptable local limestone?
This river, revered as a goddess and said to be the sun god's daughter, joins the Ganges at Prayagraj's Triveni Sangam, site of the Kumbh Mela festival — which river?
Yamuna: River in India. The Yamuna (pronounced [jəmʊnɑː]; IAST: Yamunā) is the second-largest tributary river of the Ganges by discharge and the longest tributary in India.
Italo Calvino spent his formative years in this Ligurian resort town, home to a famous annual song contest and a spring cycling classic — which town?
Characterized by its own dialect, this German cultural region spans three Bavarian districts plus neighboring parts of Thuringia and Baden-Württemberg — what region is it?
Franconia: Cultural region in Southern Germany.

Stretching from the Caspian Sea to the Gobi Desert and home mainly to Turkic peoples, this historical Asian region is split into western and eastern halves, the latter now part of China's Xinjiang — what is it called?
Turkestan: Historical region in Central Asia.
Sitting on the river Hase between the Wiehen Hills and the Teutoburg Forest, this Lower Saxony city was once home to the largest British army garrison outside the UK — which city?
Osnabrück: City in Lower Saxony, Germany. Osnabrück (German: [ɔsnaˈbʁʏk]; Westphalian: Ossenbrügge; archaic English: Osnaburg) is a city in Lower Saxony in western Germany.
The most populous city in its New England state, this coastal community serves as county seat of Cumberland County and hosts the region's second-largest tonnage seaport as of 2019 — what is it?
Portland, Maine is the most populous city in the U.S. Its population was 68,408 at the 2020 census.
Sitting on the banks of the Mekong near the Thai border, this Laotian capital is home to the golden stupa Pha That Luang and once housed the Emerald Buddha — which city?
Vientiane: Capital of Laos. Comprising the 5 urban districts of Vientiane Prefecture, the city is located on the banks of the Mekong, close to the border with Thailand.
Home to the world's third-tallest Shiva statue on India's Arabian Sea coast, this Karnataka town also has a stop on the Konkan railway line. What's the town?
Murdeshwar: Town in Karnataka, India. Murdeshwar is a town in Uttara Kannada district in the state of Karnataka, India, and lies on the coast of the Arabian Sea.
Sitting at over 4,000 feet above sea level in the center of Madagascar, this capital city is the highest national capital by elevation among the world's island nations — which city?

Antananarivo: Capital and largest city of Madagascar. The administrative area of the city, known as Antananarivo-Renivohitra ("Antananarivo-Mother Hill" or "Antananarivo-Capital"), is the capital of Analamanga region.
Granted city rights by King Casimir III the Great in 1354, this southeastern Polish city straddles the Wisłok River and once linked Ottoman trade routes to the Baltic via Gdańsk — which city?
Rzeszów: City in Podkarpackie Voivodeship, Poland.
Serving as the first capital of British East Africa before Nairobi took over in 1907, this coastal Kenyan city's downtown buildings are painted blue and white to evoke the ocean — which city?
Mombasa (mom-BASS-) is a coastal city in southeastern Kenya along the Indian Ocean.
Nestled in the heart of the Dolomites and known for its jet-set après-ski scene, this alpine resort town was conquered by the Republic of Venice in 1420 — which town?
Cortina d'Ampezzo: Town and comune in Veneto, Italy.
Originally founded as Caesarodunum by Emperor Augustus, this French city on the Loire hosted a pivotal 732 AD battle and later became the country's first hub of the silk industry — name it?
Tours: City in Centre-Val de Loire, France.
Stretching 1,006 kilometers from the Massif Central to the Atlantic at Saint-Nazaire, this waterway is the longest river in France — name it?
Loire: Longest river in France. The Loire gives its name to six departments: Loire, Haute-Loire, Loire-Atlantique, Indre-et-Loire, Maine-et-Loire, and Saône-et-Loire.
Sitting on the Uzh River near Ukraine's borders with Slovakia and Hungary, this city claims to be the most inland in its part of Europe — name it?
Uzhhorod: City and administrative center of Zakarpattia Oblast, Ukraine.
This Persian Gulf port city serves as the seat of Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province and ranks as the kingdom's fifth-largest city after Riyadh, Jeddah, Mecca and Medina — what is it?
Dammam: Capital of Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia. Dammam (Arabic: الدمام, romanized: ad-Dammām) is an industrial port city and the seat of the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia.
Covering 900,000 square kilometers, this semiarid sandy savanna stretches across Botswana and into Namibia and South Africa — what is it?
Kalahari Desert: Semi-arid sandy savanna in Southern Africa.
Construction on this vast Egyptian temple complex near Luxor began around 1971 BC and continued for nearly two millennia, centered on worship of the god Amun — what is it?
Karnak: Ancient Egyptian temple complex. The Karnak Temple Complex, commonly known as Karnak, comprises a vast mix of temples, pylons, chapels, and other buildings near Luxor, Egypt.
Home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga temple and host of the Kumbh Mela every twelve years, this ancient city on the Shipra River was once known as Avantika — which Indian city?
Ujjain: Metropolitan city in Madhya Pradesh, India.
Nicknamed the 'Pineapple Island' for its plantation past, this sixth-largest Hawaiian island is 98% owned by Oracle's cofounder — which island?
Lānaʻi: Sixth largest island in Hawaii. Lānaʻi, sometimes written Lanai, is the sixth-largest of the Hawaiian Islands and the smallest publicly accessible inhabited island in the chain.
Sitting at the confluence of two rivers in western Germany's Ruhr region, this city is home to Europe's largest inland port — which city?
Duisburg: City in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.
Sitting on the shore of Nahuel Huapi Lake in the Patagonian Andes, this Argentine city's name comes from a Mapuche phrase meaning 'people from the other side of the mountain' — which city?
Bariloche: City and municipality in Río Negro, Argentina.
Stretching roughly 1,200 kilometers down the length of peninsular Italy and joining the Ligurian Alps in the northwest, this range shelters some of Europe's best-preserved forests — which range?
Apennine Mountains: Mountain ranges stretching the length of Italy.
Known as the Czech national river, this waterway flows through Český Krumlov and Prague before joining the Elbe — what is it?
Vltava: Longest river in the Czech Republic.
Home to Dr. Oetker and sitting on the 156-km Hermannsweg hiking trail through the Teutoburg Forest, which German city of over 340,000 is the 18th largest in the country?
Bielefeld: City in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.

Construction on this 330-meter pyramid-shaped skyscraper in Pyongyang started in 1987, stalled for over a decade, and even after its exterior was finished in 2011 it has never opened — which unfinished landmark is this?
Ryugyong Hotel: Unfinished skyscraper in Pyongyang, North Korea.
Once known by its Manchu name Mukden, this Liaoning provincial capital is the largest city in Manchuria and was the site of a pivotal 1621 battle — which Chinese city is this?
Shenyang: Capital of Liaoning, China. The Shenyang metropolitan area is one of the major megalopolises in China, with a population of over 23 million.
Built over 38 years and still unexcavated, this Xi'an tomb complex sits beneath a 76-meter pyramid-shaped mound and honors China's first emperor — what is this burial complex called?
Mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang: 3rd-century BC site in Shaanxi, China.
Home to Europe's tallest peak and bordered by the Black, Azov, and Caspian seas, this Russian region came under imperial control after a 19th-century war — which region?
North Caucasus: Subregion in Eastern Europe.
Sitting between the Adriatic Sea and the Carnic Alps, this Italian city serves as capital of its own regional decentralization entity in Friuli-Venezia Giulia — which city?
Udine: Comune in Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Italy.
Ringed by Venetian-era fortifications and nestled in one of the Adriatic's most indented bays, this Montenegrin port town has become a magnet for cruise-ship tourists — which town?
Sitting at the southern tip of the Liaodong Peninsula, this Chinese port city is Liaoning's second-largest after the provincial capital, with over 7 million residents — which city?
Dalian: City in Liaoning, China. Today, Dalian is a financial, shipping, and logistics center for East Asia.
This Brazilian state capital, built across an island with 60 beaches, boasts the country's third-highest Human Development Index score — which city?
Florianópolis: Capital city of Santa Catarina, Brazil.
Sitting about 6 kilometers south of the Arctic Circle, this Finnish city is the regional capital of Lapland — which city?
Rovaniemi: City in Lapland, Finland. It is located near the Arctic Circle in the northern interior of the country.
Nicknamed the 'Roof of the World' since Victorian times, this Central Asian range sits at the junction of the Tian Shan, Karakoram, and Hindu Kush — which range?
Pamir Mountains: Mountain range in Central Asia.
This Brazilian state capital surpassed Salvador in population in the 2024 census, making it the country's fourth largest city and the wealthiest in the Northeast by GDP. What city is it?
Fortaleza: Capital city of Ceará, Brazil.

Called 'beautiful, crowned with flags' by the Avesta, this ancient Iranian civilization sat south of the Oxus River and north of the Hindu Kush, sheltered by mountain ranges on three sides. What was it?
Bactria: Historical region in Central Asia.
Forming the natural border between the Russian Far East and Northeast China, this 2,824-kilometer waterway is home to the kaluga, one of the largest freshwater fish on Earth. What river is it?
Amur: Major river in the Russian Far East and Northeast Asia.

Serving as the capital of its governorate in the southern Gaza Strip, this city was once known as 'Salqah' before a vast caravanserai — now called Barquq Castle — was built there in 1387–88. What city is it?
Khan Yunis: City in Gaza, Palestine. It has been largely destroyed during the Gaza war.
Historically known as the Oxus, this Central Asian river forms from the Vakhsh and Panj rivers and once flowed into the Aral Sea, though it no longer reaches it today — which river?
Amu Darya: River in Central Asia. The Amu Darya, historically known as the Oxus, is a major river in Central Asia which flows through Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan.
Known historically by its German name Memel, this Baltic Sea city is Lithuania's only major seaport and the busiest port in the Baltic states. What's the city?
Klaipėda: Coastal city in Lithuania. Klaipėda ( CLAY-ped-ə; Lithuanian: [ˈklˠɐɪ̯ˑpʲeːdˠɐ]; German: Memel) is a city in Lithuania on the Baltic Sea coast.

Home to roughly 2,400 timber houses in its UNESCO-listed old town, this Bavarian town on the river Regnitz was briefly the center of the Holy Roman Empire and holds the tomb of Emperor Henry II. What's the town?
Part of a royal endowment project in Mecca, this seven-building hotel complex boasts the world's largest timepiece faces atop its tallest structure, according to Guinness — which complex is this?
The Clock Towers: Building complex in Mecca, Saudi Arabia.

Renamed in 2023 but still historically known by its Mughal-era name, this Maharashtra city near the UNESCO-listed Ajanta and Ellora caves is a major center for cotton and silk textiles — what city is this?
One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, this Georgian city on the Rioni River briefly hosted the national parliament from 2012 to 2018 as part of a decentralization push. Which city?
Home to Manila and containing 55 percent of its country's population, this Philippine island is the fourth most populous island on Earth. Which island?
Luzon: Island in the Philippines. Luzon ( loo-ZON, Tagalog: [luˈson]) is the largest and most populous island in the Philippines.
Ruled by the Al Qasimi dynasty since the 18th century, which UAE port city and emirate capital is the country's third-most populous, behind only Dubai and Abu Dhabi?
Sharjah is a major port city and the third-most populous city in the United Arab Emirates, after Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
Founded in 1890 by the Pioneer Column and originally named Fort Salisbury, this city is now the capital of Zimbabwe — which city?
Harare: Capital and largest city of Zimbabwe. The city is situated in north-eastern Zimbabwe in the country's Mashonaland region.
Formerly known as Barrow, this borough seat sits north of the Arctic Circle and is the northernmost city in the United States — which city?
Utqiagvik, Alaska: Utqiaġvik, formerly known and still sometimes referred to as Barrow, is the borough seat and largest city of the North Slope Borough in the U.S.
Once the capital of the historic province of Anjou, this French city's residents are called Angevins and it ranks as the third-largest commune in northwestern France — which city?
Angers: Prefecture and commune in Pays de la Loire, France.

In classical antiquity, what name was given to the western Balkan region — spanning parts of modern Albania, Montenegro, and Bosnia — that neighbored Macedonia and Epirus and was home to numerous tribal peoples?
Illyria: Historical region in Western Balkan, Southeast Europe.
Sitting on the River Itchen 60 miles southwest of London, this Hampshire cathedral city grew from the Roman settlement of Venta Belgarum — which English city?

Winchester: City in Hampshire, England. The city lies at the heart of the wider City of Winchester, a local government district, at the western end of the South Downs National Park, on the River Itchen.
This Belgian city near Brussels has been a university town since 1425 — the oldest in the Low Countries — and hosts the headquarters of the world's largest brewing company — which city?
Leuven: Capital of Flemish Brabant province, Belgium.
Awarded city status in 2022, this North Wales settlement near the England border traces its roots to before the 11th century — which city?
Wrexham: City in north-east Wales. Wrexham ( REK-səm; Welsh: Wrecsam [ˈrɛksam]) is a city in the north-east of Wales.
Serving as the provisional capital of its Ukrainian region since 2014, this industrial city on the Kazennyi Torets river has repeatedly been struck by shelling during the ongoing war — which city?
Kramatorsk: City in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.
Called 'the first nucleus of the Roman Empire,' this centermost of Rome's seven hills once held the mansions of the wealthy before emperors starting with Augustus built palaces there — which site?
Palatine Hill (Classical; New), which is the centremost of the seven hills of Rome, is one of the most ancient parts of the city; it has been called "the first nucleus of the Roman Empire".
Split today between Romania and Ukraine on the northern slopes of the Eastern Carpathians, this historical region was once part of the medieval Principality of Moldavia — which region?

Bukovina: Historical region split between Romania and Ukraine. It is located on the northern slopes of the central Eastern Carpathians and the adjoining plains, today divided between Romania and Ukraine.
This Mexican resort city sits on the Bahía de Banderas along Jalisco's Pacific coast and is the state's second-largest urban area after Guadalajara — which city?
Puerto Vallarta: City in Jalisco, Mexico. The city is located at 20°40′N 105°16′W.

Home to the country's second-largest military port after Toulon, this Brittany city on the western tip is the region's biggest metro area even though much smaller Quimper is its administrative seat — which city?
Brest, France is a port city in the Finistre department, Brittany.
Home to Mount Whitney, the highest point in the contiguous United States, and the granite cliffs of Yosemite Valley, which mountain range is this?

Sierra Nevada: Mountain range in the United States. The Sierra Nevada ( see-ERR-ə nih-VA(H)D-ə) is a mountain range in the Western United States, between the Central Valley of California and the Great Basin.

Seized in 1090 AD by Hassan-i Sabbah, this mountain fortress in Iran served as headquarters of the Nizari Ismaili state until 1256 and was fabled for its heavenly gardens and library — which stronghold?
Alamut Castle: 9th-century fortress in Qazvin province, Iran.
France's 12th-largest city and the country's third-most-populous Mediterranean city after Marseille and Nice, this Var department capital is a major center for naval shipbuilding — which city?
Toulon: Prefecture and city in France. It is the centre of an urban unit with 580,281 inhabitants (2018), the ninth largest in France by population.
Nicknamed the 'City of Lakes,' this capital of Madhya Pradesh was the seat of a princely state ruled by Nawabs until India's 1947 independence — which city?
Bhopal: Metropolis and state capital in Madhya Pradesh, India. It is known as the City of Lakes, due to presence of various natural and artificial lakes near the city boundary.
Also known by another name, Khankendi, this city was the capital of the breakaway Republic of Artsakh until Azerbaijan's 2023 offensive retook the region — which city?
First mentioned in the year 806, this Bavarian city on the Danube became home to Bavaria's first university in 1472 and is today the second-largest city on the river after Regensburg — which city?
Ingolstadt: City in Bavaria, Germany. Ingolstadt is the second largest city in Upper Bavaria after Munich and the fifth largest city in Bavaria after Munich, Nuremberg, Augsburg and Regensburg.

Stretching from Westhampton to Montauk on Long Island's South Fork, this seaside resort region grew from old fishing and farming settlements into a famous summer colony by the late 1800s — which region?
The Hamptons: Seaside group of towns, villages and hamlets.
Covering the classical land once called Khwarazm, this autonomous republic in northwestern Uzbekistan has its capital at Nukus — which region?
Karakalpakstan: Suveren republic of Uzbekistan. Karakalpakstan has an area of 166,590 km2 (64,320 sq mi), and has a population of about 2 million people.
Rising 867 feet from base to summit in Wyoming's Black Hills, this laccolithic butte became the first-ever U.S. national monument in 1906 — what is it?
Devils Tower: Flat-topped volcanic plug in Wyoming, US.
Named after the Sanskrit word for date palm, this Indian city is home to the country's largest group of medieval Hindu and Jain temples renowned for erotic sculpture — which UNESCO site?
Khajuraho: City in Madhya Pradesh, India.
This Russian Far East port on Avacha Bay is nicknamed the 'city of Peter and Paul' and had about 165,000 residents at the 2021 census — which city?
Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky: City in Kamchatka Krai, Russia.
Founded in 1698 near the mouth of the Don River on the Sea of Azov, this Russian port city briefly served as the temporary capital of Soviet Ukraine in 1918 — which city?
Taganrog: City in Rostov Oblast, Russia.
Sitting at the confluence of four rivers near the Polish border, this city straddles Moravia and Silesia and anchors the Czech Republic's largest urban area outside Prague — which city?
Ostrava: City in the Czech Republic. It lies near the border with Poland, at the confluences of four rivers: Oder, Opava, Ostravice and Lučina.
Adopted in 1917 when its king declared war on Germany, this five-striped red-white-blue banner is said to symbolize nation, religion, and monarch — which Southeast Asian country flies it?
Flag of Thailand consists of five horizontal stripes of red, white, blue, white and red, with the central blue stripe being twice as wide as each of the other four.
Designed by architect Roger Anger and founded in 1968 by a spiritual figure known as 'the Mother,' this experimental township straddles Tamil Nadu and Puducherry — which town?
Auroville: Experimental township in Villupuram district and Puducherry, South India.
Sitting near Lake Baikal at the meeting of the Uda and Selenga rivers, this Russian city is the capital of Buryatia — which city?
Ulan-Ude: City in the Republic of Buryatia, Russia.
The fourth-largest metropolitan city in South Korea, this Yeongnam-region hub sits near the Geumho and Nakdong rivers and was once part of the ancient Silla kingdom — which city?
Daegu: City in South Korea. Daegu (Korean: 대구 [tɛ̝.ɡu]), formerly spelled Taegu and officially Daegu Metropolitan City (대구광역시), is a city in southeastern South Korea.

Bordered by Lancashire, West Yorkshire, Derbyshire, Cheshire, and Merseyside, this highly urbanised English county contains Salford, Rochdale, Stockport, Wigan, and Bolton, with over three million residents — which county?
Greater Manchester: Ceremonial county in North West England.
Once the core of a county within the Holy Roman and Austrian Empires, this Alpine region was split between Austria and Italy by the 1919 Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye — which region?
The southernmost state capital in Brazil, this city sits where five rivers converge into a giant freshwater lagoon, and was founded in 1769 under a settler's assumed name — which city?
Porto Alegre: Capital and largest city of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
The largest of the Ionian Islands, this Greek island's biggest towns are Argostoli and Lixouri — which island?
Cephalonia: Largest of the Ionian Islands, Greece. It is also a separate regional unit of the Ionian Islands region.
Nicknamed the 'Gateway to the Garhwal Himalayas,' this vegetarian-only, alcohol-free Indian town on the Ganges has hosted an International Yoga Festival since 1999 — which town?
Rishikesh: Municipal corporation and tehsil in Uttarakhand, India.
Founded in 636 as a military camp on the Shatt al-Arab, this scorching-hot Iraqi port city is traditionally said to be where Sinbad the Sailor set sail — which city?
Basra: Port city in southern Iraq.
This ancient fishing village on the northern shore of the Sea of Galilee is, by Christian tradition, the site of Saint Peter's home — which village?
Capernaum: Village at Lake Tiberias in historical Judea.
Adopted in 1989 after a revolution toppled the country's communist government, this vertical tricolour of blue, yellow, and red has flown in some form since the 19th century — which national banner?
Originally founded by the Sicels under a name meaning 'sickle,' this Sicilian harbour city sits at the strait connecting the island to mainland Calabria — which city?
Sitting on the river Tapti near the Arabian Sea, this Gujarati city polishes roughly 90 percent of the world's diamonds — which city?
Founded by Spartan colonists in the 8th century BC, this Southern Italian port city serves today as the country's main naval base — which city?

Though it ranks far behind Everest in height above sea level, this Ecuadorian volcano's summit is actually the point on Earth farthest from the planet's center, thanks to the equatorial bulge — which peak?
Chimborazo: Volcano and highest mountain in Ecuador.
With a death rate as high as 75 percent in its worst years, this French Guiana penal colony held political prisoners including the wrongly convicted Captain Alfred Dreyfus — what was it called?
Devil's Island: Prison of Cayenne in French Guiana.
Just northeast of Bologna on a branch of the Po River, this Renaissance city once hosted the court of the House of Este and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site — which city?

Sitting at the confluence of four rivers that form the Berounka, this Czech city resisted three sieges during the Hussite Wars and had grown into Bohemia's third-largest by the 14th century — which city is it?
Plzeň: City in the Czech Republic. Plzeň (Czech pronunciation: [ˈpl̩zɛɲ]), also known in English and German as Pilsen (German: [ˈpɪlzn̩]), is a city in the Czech Republic.
East of Cairo, this planned Egyptian city has hosted 14 relocated government ministries and became the country's official seat of government in 2024 — what's it called?
The New Capital: New urban community in Cairo Governorate, Egypt.

Sitting on the banks of the Southern Bug River, this west-central Ukrainian city is the largest in the historic Podillia region and was the site of massacres during both Stalin's purges and the Holocaust — which city?
Vinnytsia ((y), VEEN-) is a city in west-central Ukraine, located on the banks of the Southern Bug.
Sitting near the Pyrenees just before the Spanish border, this former capital of the Kingdom of Majorca is sometimes called the 'entrance' to the Iberian Peninsula — which French city?
Perpignan: Prefecture and commune in Occitania, France.
This Black Sea resort city on Crimea's south coast sits on the site of an ancient Greek colony and has been under de facto Russian control since the 2014 annexation — which city?
Yalta: City on the southern Crimean Peninsula.

Coined by Europeans after 1493, once they learned of the Americas, Oceania, and Antarctica, this term for Africa, Europe, and Asia together stands in contrast to the newly discovered lands across the Atlantic — what phrase?
Old World: Landmass corresponding to Afro–Eurasia.
This loosely defined Oceanic region always includes the two countries on either side of the Tasman Sea, and in its broadest sense stretches to the entire Malay Archipelago — what's it called?
Home to Carl Zeiss and a university founded in 1558, this German city has been a world centre of the optical industry for most of the 20th century — which city?
Jena: City in Germany. Jena (German: [ˈjeːna]) is a city in Germany and the second largest city in Thuringia.
Historically romanized as Amoy, this Chinese coastal city in Fujian lies less than 6 kilometers from the Kinmen Islands across a strait — which city?
Xiamen: City in Fujian, China. Xiamen, historically romanized as Amoy, is a sub-provincial city in southeastern Fujian, People's Republic of China, beside the Taiwan Strait.

Serving Bangladesh's capital, this mass rapid transit system's first operational line began commercial service in late 2022, with several more lines still under construction or in planning — which transit system?
Dhaka Metro Rail: Mass rapid transit system in Bangladesh. It is operated by the Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMTCL).
Nicknamed the 'French Rome' for its stunning ancient arena and temple, this southern French city sits between the Mediterranean Sea and the Cévennes mountains — which city?
Nîmes: Prefecture of Gard, Occitanie, France.
Founded by Viking settlers in 812 AD, this Irish city straddles the River Shannon and is the third-most populous urban area in the Republic of Ireland — which city?
Limerick: City in Ireland. Limerick (LIM-ər-ik; Irish: Luimneach [ˈl̪ˠɪmʲ(ə)nʲəx]) is a city in western Ireland, in County Limerick.
Located just 28 kilometers from the India-Pakistan border and headquarters of its own district, this is Punjab's second-largest city after Ludhiana — which city?
Amritsar: Metropolis in Punjab, India. Amritsar, also known as Ambarsar, is the second-largest city in the Indian state of Punjab, after Ludhiana.

Forming a natural border between Slovakia and Poland, this range within the Western Carpathians boasts the highest peaks in the whole Carpathian system, including 2,655-meter Gerlachovský štít — which range?
Tatra Mountains: Mountain range on the Polish–Slovak border.

This easternmost Ukrainian province, once named Voroshilovgrad until 1958, saw large portions fall to Russian-backed separatists in 2014 who declared their own breakaway republic there — which province?
Luhansk Oblast: Administrative region of Ukraine.
Sitting mostly on the east bank of the Niger River, this ethnically diverse capital replaced Zinder as the territorial seat in the early 20th century and is now Niger's largest city — which city?
Niamey: Capital and the largest city of Niger. It is in the western part of the country, surrounded by the Tillabéri Region.
The largest island in North Africa at 514 square kilometers, this Tunisian isle in the Gulf of Gabès earned UNESCO World Heritage status in 2023 — which island?
Djerba: Island off of the coast of Tunisia.
Rising in France and flowing through Belgium and the Netherlands, this 925-kilometer river empties into the North Sea via a delta it shares with the Rhine and the Scheldt — which river?
The southernmost capital city in Australia, this Tasmanian capital sits on the Derwent estuary beneath Mount Wellington and boasts the world's second-deepest natural harbour — which city?
Hobart: Capital city of Tasmania, Australia. Hobart (HOH-bart; Southeast Tasmanian: nipaluna) is the capital and most populous city of the island state of Tasmania, Australia.
Renowned for classical gardens that blend architecture, water, and rock, this Jiangsu city has long been paired with Hangzhou as 'paradise on earth' — which city?
Suzhou: Prefecture-level city in Jiangsu, China.
Home to the legendary king whose touch turned everything to gold, this ancient Anatolian kingdom also gave us the myth of the Gordian Knot — which kingdom?
Phrygia: Ancient Anatolian kingdom. This later Midas was, however, also the last independent king of Phrygia before Cimmerians sacked the Phrygian capital, Gordium, around 695 BC.
This Taliban-led state controlled roughly 90% of its country before international opposition surged after the September 11 attacks and the ensuing War on Terror — which state (1996–2001)?

Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (1996–2001): Afghan state. The Taliban continued to refer to itself as the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan in official communications when it was out of power from 2001 to 2021.
Home to nearly 1.8 million people, this East African capital generates more than half its country's entire GDP — which city?
Kampala: Capital and largest city of Uganda.

Spanning the northeastern Black Sea coast in the North Caucasus, this historical region was conquered by the Russian Empire in a 19th-century war that led to mass exile of its people — what was it called?
Circassia: Former country and region in Eastern Europe.
The seventh largest and westernmost of Hawaii's main islands, this land is home to the Hawaiian coot and stilt, with a 2020 census population of just 84 — which island?
Niʻihau: Seventh largest island in Hawaii. It is 17.5 miles (28.2 km) southwest of Kauaʻi across the Kaulakahi Channel.
Known as Dokdo in Korea and Takeshima in Japan, this disputed group of islets in the Sea of Japan is administered by South Korea — which islets?
Liancourt Rocks: Group of disputed islets in the Sea of Japan. The Liancourt Rocks lie in rich fishing grounds that may contain large deposits of natural gas.
Founded by Peter the Great on an island near Saint Petersburg, this port city anchored the Russian Baltic Fleet and gave its name to a 1921 sailors' rebellion — which city?
Kronstadt: Municipal town in Saint Petersburg, Russia.
Sitting between the Ruhr and Emscher rivers, this German city is the sixth-largest in North Rhine-Westphalia and home to nine institutions of higher education — which city?
Bochum: City in Germany. Bochum (BOHKH-uum; US: -⁠əm; German: [ˈboːxʊm]; Westphalian: Baukem) is a city in North Rhine-Westphalia.
Established in 1976 to decentralize growth from Delhi, this systematically planned Indian city boasts over 50 percent green cover between the Yamuna and Hindon rivers — which city?
Noida: City in Uttar Pradesh, India.
Perched on 12-meter cliffs above the Caribbean and serving as a major port for the city of Coba, which walled Maya city is one of the best-preserved coastal ruins in Mexico?
Tulum: Maya site in Quintana Roo, Mexico.
Birthplace of Constantine the Great and several other Roman emperors, this Serbian city earned the nickname 'Imperial City' — which one is it?

Lying just east of Puerto Rico and split into British and American jurisdictions, this Caribbean archipelago sits on a shared carbonate platform, except for one member, Saint Croix — which archipelago is it?
Virgin Islands is an archipelago between the North Atlantic Ocean and northeastern Caribbean Sea, located to the immediate east of the main island of Puerto Rico.
Birthplace of the mathematician behind a famous theorem about right triangles, this Greek Aegean island near the coast of Turkey is also home to a UNESCO-listed ancient aqueduct — which island?
Samos: Greek island in the eastern Aegean Sea.
Lying near the Khyber Pass, this ancient South Asian city served as capital of the Kushan Empire under Kanishka the Great and later as winter capital of the Durrani Empire — which city?
Peshawar: Capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

Situated on Pamban Island near Sri Lanka, this Tamil Nadu town is one of the four sites in Hinduism's Char Dham pilgrimage, and legend holds that Rama built a bridge to Lanka from nearby — which town?
Rameswaram: Pilgrimage centre and a town in Tamil Nadu, India.
Nicknamed 'The Town with Eyes' for its distinctive eyebrow-shaped dormer windows, this Transylvanian city twice served as capital of the Principality — which Romanian city?
Sibiu: City in Romania. Now the seat of Sibiu County, between 1692 and 1791 and 1849–65, Sibiu was the capital of the Principality of Transylvania.
Sitting across the Congo River from Kinshasa, this city served as the de facto capital of Free France during World War II — which capital city?
Brazzaville: Capital city of the Republic of the Congo. Brazzaville (French pronunciation: [bʁazavil]) is the capital and largest city of the Republic of the Congo.
Thanks to its unique elbow-shaped coastline, this Adriatic seaport is the only city in Italy where you can watch both sunrise and sunset over the water — which city?
Ancona: City and seaport in Marche, Italy. Ancona (also US:; Italian: [aŋˈkoːna]) is a city and a seaport in the Marche region of central Italy.
Known as the 'Gateway to North East India,' this Assam river port sits on the Brahmaputra's south bank and is home to the ancient Kamakhya Temple — which city?

Guwahati: Metropolis in Assam, India. Guwahati (Assamese: [ɡua.ɦa.ti]), formerly known as Gauhati, is the largest city of the Indian state of Assam, and also the largest metropolis in northeastern India.

Home to one of the world's oldest universities and famous for its ham, cheese, and an Etruscan-derived name the Romans later reused for a round shield, this is the second-largest city in Emilia-Romagna after Bologna — which city?
Parma: City in Emilia-Romagna, Italy. With a population of 202,111 inhabitants as of 2025, Parma is the second most populous city in Emilia-Romagna after Bologna, the region's capital.
Slovenia's second-largest city, first recorded as a castle in 1164, later shared the title of European Capital of Culture in 2012 with Portugal's Guimarães — which city?
Maribor: City in Styria, Slovenia. It is the seat of the Urban Municipality of Maribor and the Drava Statistical Region.
This French city, prefecture of the Calvados department, is connected to England by a cross-Channel ferry route and sits near the WWII landing beaches — which city?
Caen: Prefecture and commune in Normandy, France.
This Lombardy city on the Lambro River, once home to Queen Theodelinda's royal residence, has a cathedral housing the Iron Crown of Lombardy — which city?
Monza: City in Lombardy, Italy. Monza is internationally known for the Monza Circuit, one of the world's oldest permanent motor racing circuits and the long-standing host of the Italian Grand Prix.
Rising at Mount Fumaiolo and flowing through the city founded on its eastern banks, which Italian river meets the Tyrrhenian Sea near Ostia?
Tiber: Major river in central Italy.
Home to one of West Africa's largest markets and linked by rail to Abidjan, which city serves as the capital and largest city of Burkina Faso?
Ouagadougou: Capital of Burkina Faso. It has a population of 2,415,266 in 2019.
Sitting on the Pearl River halfway between Memphis and New Orleans, this state capital saw the largest population decline of any major U.S. city during the 2010s — which city?
Jackson, Mississippi is the capital and most populous city of the U.S.
Named after a people identified with the Etruscans of Italy, this body of water forms part of the Mediterranean off Italy's western coast — which body of water?

Tyrrhenian Sea: Part of the Mediterranean Sea off the western coast of Italy. The Tyrrhenian Sea (tih-REE-nee-ən,-RAY-; Italian: Mar Tirreno [mar tirˈrɛːno] or [-ˈreː-]) is part of the Mediterranean Sea off the western coast of Italy.
Sitting on the Karnaphuli River between hill tracts and the Bay of Bengal, this city is home to Bangladesh's busiest port and serves as the country's business capital. Which city?
Undrafted out of UC Santa Barbara, this Nigerian-American guard signed a two-way deal with the Miami Heat and reached the NBA Finals with them in both 2020 and 2023 — who is he?

Any footrace longer than the traditional 42.195-kilometre distance falls into this category, exemplified by events like the Comrades Marathon and races inspired by the Greek messenger Pheidippides' 246-km run from Athens to Sparta — what's this class of race called?
Ultramarathon: Footrace longer than the marathon. An ultramarathon is a footrace longer than the traditional marathon distance of 42.195 kilometres (26 mi 385 yd).
This German professional footballer, born in November 1992, plays in goal — who is he?
Stefan Ortega: German footballer (born 1992). Stefan Ortega Moreno is a German professional footballer who plays as a goalkeeper for Super League Greece club Olympiacos.
Once the world's No. 10 junior player, this British tennis pro reached a career-high WTA singles ranking of 23 and has held the title of Britain's top-ranked woman — who is she?

This NFL head coach guided the Green Bay Packers to victory over his hometown Pittsburgh Steelers in Super Bowl XLV in 2011, and now leads the Steelers himself after also coaching the Dallas Cowboys — who is he?
Nicknamed 'El Patron,' this Dominican shortstop debuted in MLB in 2021 with the Tampa Bay Rays and made the All-Star team in 2023 — who is he?
Wander Franco: Dominican baseball player and convicted sex offender (born 2001)
Founded in 2004 as a rebrand of the top flight, this professional football competition in China has crowned Guangzhou champion eight times, more than any other club — what is it called?
Chinese Super League: Highest tier of professional football in China.
Signed by Everton for £30 million in 2017, this England goalkeeper started between the posts for the Three Lions' run to the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the Euro 2020 final — who is he?
Born in December 1968, this German footballer spent his career playing centre-back before his death in 2015 — who is he?
Stephan Beckenbauer: German footballer (1968–2015). Stephan Beckenbauer (1 December 1968 – 31 July 2015) was a German footballer who played as a centre-back.
Also known in the ring as King Kong and the Masked Marauder, this American wrestler died in 1988 and became known for his blood-soaked hardcore brawling style in the U.S. and Japan — who was he?
Bruiser Brody: American professional wrestler and homicide victim (1946–1988)
Combining seven separate track and field events, this multi-discipline contest for women debuted at the 1984 Olympics — what is it?
Heptathlon: Track and field competition with 7 events.
A unanimous All-American at Nebraska in 2009, this defensive tackle went on to play in three separate Super Bowls with three different NFL teams — who is he?

A Heisman Trophy finalist at Ohio State after breaking the school's single-season sack record, this defensive end was picked second overall in the 2020 NFL Draft and recorded a sack in Super Bowl LVIII — who is he?
This Brentford striker began his career at hometown club Coventry City, won the Championship in his first season with Bournemouth, and was part of England's squad at the 2022 World Cup — who is he?
Born in 1996, this Argentine attacking midfielder plays his club football for La Liga side Real Betis while also turning out for his national team — who is he?
The first-ever winner of the Golden Boy Award, this Dutch playmaker drew comparisons to Johan Cruyff and earned 109 caps before spells at Real Madrid and Tottenham — who is he?
Rafael van der Vaart: Dutch footballer (born 1983)

Led by 1993 Ballon d'Or winner Roberto Baggio, this Italian club holds the record for most seasons played in Serie B and once fielded a young Andrea Pirlo, a product of its own youth academy — which club?
Brescia Calcio: Defunct Italian association football club.

Regarded as technically gifted but temperamental, this Italian forward scored over 100 goals across a career at Lazio, Juventus, Napoli, and Milan before seven years in the Premier League — who is he?
Paolo Di Canio: Italian footballer and manager.

Drafted fourth overall by the Jets in 2022, this cornerback was named Defensive Rookie of the Year and became the first rookie at his position since Ronnie Lott in 1981 to earn first-team All-Pro honors — who is he?
After two games with the Bulls in his rookie year, this guard signed with the Heat and reached the 2023 NBA Finals before later joining the Cavaliers — who is he?
Drafted seventh overall by Tampa Bay in 2014, this wide receiver tied Jerry Rice's NFL record with 11 straight 1,000-yard receiving seasons to start a career — who is he?
Mike Evans (wide receiver): American football player (born 1993)
Backup to Joe Flacco during Baltimore's Super Bowl XLVII win, this quarterback later took over as Buffalo's starter and earned a Pro Bowl nod in 2015 — who is he?
Nicknamed 'Megatron' after the Transformers villain, this Detroit wide receiver set the NFL's single-season receiving yardage record in 2012 — who is he?
This French striker surpassed André-Pierre Gignac as Toulouse's all-time league scorer before a €40 million move to Monaco in 2019 — who is he?
Nicknamed 'The Addicks,' this south-east London club has played at The Valley since 1919 and shares rivalries with Crystal Palace and Millwall — which club is it?
Charlton Athletic F.C.: Association football club in London, England.
Selected by the Raiders in the fourth round of the 2023 NFL draft, this quarterback played his college ball for Purdue — who is he?
A member of Michigan's 'Fab Five' in the early '90s, this NBA analyst later helped lead the Indiana Pacers to the 2000 NBA Finals alongside Reggie Miller — who is he?
Founded in 1920 in Tuscany, this Italian club is among a small group of Serie A participants not based in a provincial capital — which club is it?
Empoli FC: Association football club in Italy.
This Chilean goalkeeper won the treble and the Zamora Trophy in his first Barcelona season after a €12 million transfer in 2014 — who is he?
Widely considered the greatest female pole vaulter ever, this Russian two-time Olympic gold medalist was barred from the 2016 Rio Games over her country's doping scandal — who is she?
Yelena Isinbayeva: Russian Olympic pole-vaulter. Isinbayeva has been a major champion on nine occasions (Olympic, World outdoor and indoor champion and European outdoor and indoor champion).
Chairman and CEO of both an NFL franchise in Kansas City and an MLS club in Dallas, this billionaire is the son of the Chiefs' founder — who is he?
Now president of Porto, this Portuguese manager led the club to an unbeaten league season in 2010–11 and later guided Tottenham to a club-record points tally — who is he?
André Villas-Boas: Portuguese football executive and manager (born 1977)
Born in Tokorozawa, Saitama in 1992, this Japanese pitcher plays for the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters in Nippon Professional Baseball — who is he?
This Welsh centre-back captained his club to their first-ever Premier League promotion, then suffered an on-pitch cardiac arrest during a match in December 2023 — who is he?
Born on Réunion Island, this self-taught pilot achieved international fame in 1913 for the first non-stop flight across the Mediterranean Sea, from France to Tunisia — who is he?
Wrestling under ring names like X-Pac and the 1-2-3 Kid, this performer was part of a backstage group known as The Kliq and later joined Kevin Nash and Scott Hall in 1996 — who is he?

After working the docks and relying on relief checks during the Great Depression, this boxer staged a stunning comeback to beat Max Baer for the heavyweight title in 1935, earning the nickname 'Cinderella Man' — who is he?
Nicknamed a 'tackling machine' by FIFA, this Dutch midfielder won league titles in four different countries and became Bayern Munich's first foreign team captain — who is he?
Mark van Bommel: Dutch football player and manager (born 1977)
Currently a WWE Tag Team Champion alongside Damian Priest, this wrestler previously became the first African-American to hold the NWA World Heavyweight Championship, doing so twice — who is he?
Drafted out of Mississippi State in the second round of 2016, this NFL defensive tackle has won three Super Bowls with the Kansas City Chiefs and earned six All-Pro selections — who is he?
Chris Jones (defensive tackle, born 1994) (born July 3, 1994) is an American professional football defensive tackle for the Kansas City Chiefs of the National Football League (NFL).

This left-back won the Champions League in his first season at Chelsea after signing in 2020, then lifted the FA Cup on loan at Crystal Palace before making a permanent move to Strasbourg in 2025 — who is he?
Manchester United reportedly offered £10 million for this teenage prodigy before he broke into West Ham's first team in 1999 — he later won three Premier League titles at Chelsea. Who is he?
India lost only a single match under this middle-order batsman's captaincy, a reign that included masterminding the 2020-21 Border-Gavaskar Trophy win in Australia — who is he?
Nicknamed 'Spicy P,' this Cameroonian forward became the first player ever to win the NBA's Most Improved Player award and an NBA championship in the same season, with Toronto in 2019 — who is he?
This Brazilian forward partnered Romário in a lethal strike pairing to help Brazil win a record fourth World Cup title in 1994, then later won a seat in Rio's legislature — who is he?
In 1998, this Dominican right fielder chased Roger Maris's single-season home run record alongside Mark McGwire, becoming a seven-time All-Star mostly with the Chicago Cubs — who is he?
The son of a four-time Le Mans class winner and former F1 driver, this Dane raced in Formula One across two separate spells and now competes part-time in NASCAR for Trackhouse Racing — who is he?

Until Carlos Alcaraz came along in 2022, this Australian was the youngest man ever to reach world No. 1, doing so in 2001 en route to winning that year's US Open and the following year's Wimbledon — who is he?
Lleyton Hewitt: Australian professional tennis player (born 1981)
This Slovak cyclist won an unprecedented three consecutive road race World Championships from 2015 to 2017 and holds the record for seven points classifications at the Tour de France — who is he?
Peter Sagan: Slovak cyclist. Sagan is considered a generational talent, having earned many prestigious victories out of a total of 121 professional wins.
This French tennis player reached a career-high singles ranking of world No. 17 in January 2024 and has won five ATP Tour titles, three on hardcourts and two on grass — who is he?
Selected first overall in the 2012 NFL draft, this quarterback set rookie passing records while turning a 2-14 Colts team into an 11-5 playoff squad in year one — who is he?
Andrew Luck: American football player and executive (born 1989)
This Polish winger spent the bulk of his career at Borussia Dortmund, winning two Bundesliga titles, and captained his country when it co-hosted Euro 2012 — who is he?
This quarterback is the Chicago Bears' all-time leader in passing yards and touchdowns, having been traded there from Denver after winning SEC Offensive Player of the Year at Vanderbilt — who is he?
This Olympic multisport combining fencing, swimming, obstacle course racing, shooting, and running dropped equestrian jumping from its lineup in 2025 — which sport?
Nicknamed Dede in Ghana, this winger joined his father's former club's academy in 2006 and has earned 120 caps for the Ghana national team — who is he?
This Italian centre-back overcame testicular cancer treatment before returning to Serie A, later winning trophies with Lazio and joining Inter Milan in 2022 — who is he?
Reaching a career-high ranking of world No. 4, this player upset the top seed to reach the 2014 US Open final and later won Olympic bronze by beating Rafael Nadal — who is he?
Just two days after being drafted second overall by the Boston Celtics in 1986, this Maryland All-American's sudden death shocked the sports world — who was he?
A member of India's title-winning squads at the 2007 T20 World Cup and 2013 Champions Trophy, this batting coach now mentors Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the IPL — who is he?
