Amina bint Wahb: Mother of Muhammad. Amina bint Wahb ibn Abd Manaf al-Zuhriyya (Arabic: آمنة بنت وهب, romanized: Āmina bint Wahb, c. 549–577) was the mother of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.
A former member of the Russian State Duma who is also a television journalist and film director, who has spoken out continuously against the invasion of Ukraine?
Alexander Nevzorov: Russian-Ukrainian journalist and writer (born 1958)
Born in West Virginia, which cookbook author and Food Network personality co-hosts 'The Kitchen' and served as a judge on 'Iron Chef America'?
Katie Lee (chef) (born September 14, 1981) is an American cookbook author, television food critic, actor, chef, and novelist born in West Virginia.
Set eight years before its hero's earliest outing, this 2013 prequel finds Gotham's masked vigilante hunted by eight assassins hired by a crime lord on Christmas Eve — which game is it?
Batman: Arkham Origins: 2013 video game. Batman: Arkham Origins is a 2013 action-adventure game developed by WB Games Montréal and published by Warner Bros.
Introduced as the youngest child and only daughter of a large wizarding family, this character eventually marries Harry Potter and was played by Bonnie Wright in all eight films — who is she?
Ginny Weasley: Character in J. K. Rowling's Harry Potter series.
The first poker player to win $1 million in tournament earnings, this two-time WSOP Main Event champion, in 1976 and 1977, also won ten WSOP bracelets — who is he?
Created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko in 1963, which Spider-Man archenemy has four mechanical tentacle-like arms fused to his body and leads the Sinister Six?
Doctor Octopus: Marvel Comics fictional character.
Chief engineer of the Great Western Railway, which Victorian engineer also built the SS Great Western, SS Great Britain, and SS Great Eastern — then the largest steamships in the world?
Isambard Kingdom Brunel: English civil and marine engineer (1806–1859)

Developed by Gust for PlayStation 4, Nintendo Switch, and Windows in 2019, which role-playing game became the twenty-first main entry in its long-running Japanese series and later got two numbered sequels?
Atelier Ryza: Ever Darkness & the Secret Hideout
Atelier Ryza: Ever Darkness & the Secret Hideout
Atelier Ryza: Ever Darkness & the Secret Hideout: 2019 video game by Gust Co. Ltd.
Atelier Ryza: Ever Darkness & the Secret Hideout
Building on the 'nemesis system' from its 2014 predecessor, which action-adventure sequel has a Gondorian Ranger bonded with an Elf Lord's wraith forge a new Ring of Power against Sauron?
Middle-earth: Shadow of War: 2017 action-adventure video game.
In library cataloging and even in FDA guidelines, which term describes a long-form work focused on a single scholarly subject, usually by one author?
Monograph: Specialist work of writing on a single subject or an aspect of a subject.

This Mexican-American dog trainer's TV series about rehabilitating aggressive dogs aired in more than 80 countries, and his New York Times bestselling books share his approach to canine psychology — who is he?
Cesar Millan: Mexican dog trainer and TV personality. César Felipe Millán Favela ( SEE-zər mil-AHN, Spanish: [ˈsesaɾ miˈʝan]; born August 27, 1969) is a Mexican-American dog trainer.
Installed inside the Golden Temple in Amritsar in 1604 and regarded as the eternal successor to ten human spiritual leaders, this is Sikhism's central holy scripture — what is its name?
Guru Granth Sahib: Primary scripture of Sikhism. The Adi Granth (Punjabi: ਆਦਿ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ), its first rendition, was compiled by the fifth guru, Guru Arjan (1564–1606).
In this 2014 dystopian novel set on Mars, a lowborn miner named Darrow infiltrates the ranks of the elite ruling caste known as the Golds — which book?
Red Rising: 2014 dystopian novel by Pierce Brown.

Published in 1762, this Rousseau treatise argued that only the general will of the people — not divinely appointed monarchs — has the right to legislate, helping inspire the French Revolution. What is it?
The Social Contract: 1762 book by Jean-Jacques Rousseau.
This 1926 collection gathered centuries-old English translations of apocryphal Old and New Testament writings, with an introduction by Dr. Frank Crane. What is it?
The Lost Books of the Bible and the Forgotten Books of Eden
The Lost Books of the Bible and the Forgotten Books of Eden
The Lost Books of the Bible and the Forgotten Books of Eden: English translations of pseudepigrapha and apocryphon.
The Lost Books of the Bible and the Forgotten Books of Eden
Painted by Gustave Courbet in 1866, this provocative close-up nude sparked controversy for its intimate, unflinching realism. Which artwork?
L'Origine du monde: Oil-on-canvas painted by Gustave Courbet.
A former agricultural engineer who once served as mayor of Amarah, this politician rose to become Iraq's prime minister from 2022 to 2026. Who is he?
Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani: Prime Minister of Iraq from 2022 to 2026.
Co-founder of a Palestinian political and militant movement in 1987, this leader briefly headed its governing council before being assassinated himself in 2004. Who is he?
Abdel Aziz al-Rantisi: Palestinian political leader (1947–2004). Rantisi was born in Yibna, Mandatory Palestine in 1947.
Known for championing charter schools, this former superintendent led school districts in Philadelphia and Chicago before running — and narrowly losing — a bid for Chicago mayor in 2023. Who is he?
Paul Vallas: American politician and school administrator (born 1953)
As head of the presidential guard, this officer overthrew Niger's president in a 2023 coup and was formally inaugurated as president two years later. Who is he?
Abdourahamane Tchiani: President of Niger since 2025.
Meaning 'conclusion of the Vedas,' this orthodox school of Hindu philosophy interprets three core texts known as the Prasthanatrayi — what's it called?
Vedanta: One of the six orthodox traditions of Hindu philosophy.
A former army lieutenant colonel and radio operator in a war against Eritrea, this politician has served as Ethiopia's prime minister since 2018 — who is he?
Abiy Ahmed: Prime Minister of Ethiopia since 2018. In the 2010 national election, Abiy became an elected member of the Ethiopian parliament, representing the district of Agaro.
This early-1700s ruler of Saxony and Poland reportedly fathered up to 380 children and loved snapping horseshoes bare-handed to show off his grip — who was he?
Augustus II the Strong: King of Poland, Elector of Saxony and Grand Duke of Lithuania (1670–1733)
Leader of Spain's People's Party for fourteen years, this politician served as prime minister from 2011 to 2018 — who is he?
Mariano Rajoy: Prime Minister of Spain from 2011 to 2018. Born in Santiago de Compostela, Rajoy studied law and graduated from the University of Santiago de Compostela in 1977.

After nine years as a CIA clandestine officer, this politician represented a sprawling 550-mile Texas border district in Congress before mounting a brief 2024 presidential bid and endorsing Nikki Haley — who is he?
India's longest-serving Minister of Commerce and Industry, this politician also won the 2018 Carnot Prize for his work in energy policy — who is he?
The daughter of Oedipus and sister of Polynices, Eteocles, and Ismene, this Theban princess is the title character of one of Sophocles' three Theban tragedies — who is she?
Antigone: Daughter of Oedipus in Greek mythology.
Raised in France and later active in the Belgian Resistance during WWII, this coal miner's son became the de facto leader of communist Poland from 1970 to 1980 — who is he?
Edward Gierek: Polish politician; leader of Poland (1970–1980)
In Hinduism, what name is given to the feminine 'Universal Power' that complements Shiva and is worshipped at shrines called pithas?
Shakti: Divine feminine energy in Hinduism.
At 35, he became Russia's youngest-ever prime minister in 1998 and later ran the Rosatom nuclear agency for over a decade — who is this Kremlin technocrat?
Sergey Kiriyenko: Prime Minister of Russia In 1998.
Sparked by a succession crisis after King Frederick VII died heirless, Prussian and Austrian troops crossed into a Danish-controlled duchy in February 1864 — which 19th-century conflict?
Second Schleswig War: War between Denmark, Prussia, and Austria in 1864.
In existence from 1949 to 1989 and bordering Romania, Czechoslovakia, and Yugoslavia, this Soviet-aligned state saw a major uprising in 1956 — what was this Cold War government called?
Hungarian People's Republic: Country in Central Europe (1949–1989)
This Navy SEAL officer became the first U.S. Navy member since Vietnam to earn the Medal of Honor, after his team was surrounded by Taliban forces near Asadabad in 2005 — who is he?
Michael P. Murphy: United States Navy Medal of Honor recipient (1976–2005)
Ruled from Aigai and later Pella by the Argead dynasty, this Greek-speaking tribe expanded along the Haliacmon valley, absorbing neighboring Thracian and Illyrian peoples — who were they?
Ancient Macedonians (Ancient) were an ancient tribe that lived on the alluvial plain around the rivers Haliacmon and lower Axios in the northeastern part of mainland Greece.
This French company makes anise-flavored pastis apéritifs and ranks as the world's second-largest wine and spirits seller — which company?
Pernod Ricard: French company that produces distilled beverages.
This Indonesian businessman-turned-politician once owned Italian football giant Inter Milan and now chairs his country's football federation — who is he?
Erick Thohir: Indonesian politician and businessman (born 1970)
Appointed Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi in March 2023, this eldest son and heir apparent of the UAE's president also chairs the emirate's Executive Council — who is he?
Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan: Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi since 2023.

Ruled by a dynasty once known as the House of Austria, this 1516–1700 European empire commanded territory stretching from the Americas to the Philippines and briefly folded in Portugal — what's this historical era called?
Habsburg Spain: Period of Spanish history (1516–1700)

A one-time WCW International World Heavyweight Champion, this Japanese wrestler-turned-politician later served as governor of Ishikawa Prefecture after a stint as education minister under Shinzo Abe — who is he?

Hiroshi Hase: Japanese politician and professional wrestler. As a professional wrestler, Hase primarily worked for New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW), and also for All Japan Pro Wrestling (AJPW) and Stampede Wrestling.
Born a Danish prince and educated at the naval academy, this royal accepted Norway's throne after the 1905 split from Sweden was confirmed by referendum — who was he?
Haakon VII: King of Norway from 1905 to 1957.
This three-time French Prime Minister led the left-wing Popular Front government in the 1930s and later became a staunch opponent of the Vichy regime — who was he?
Ruling for less than a year in 684–685, this fourth Umayyad caliph founded a new ruling house that held power until 750 — who was he?
Marwan I: Umayyad caliph from 684 to 685. Marwan later served as governor of Medina under his distant kinsman Mu'awiya I (r. 661–680), founder of the Umayyad Caliphate.
The first Muslim president of Guyana, this politician was sworn in during August 2020 after a lengthy recount dispute and later won a second term — who is he?
Irfaan Ali: President of Guyana since 2020. Mohamed Irfaan Ali (born 25 April 1980) is a Guyanese politician serving as the tenth and current president of Guyana since 2020.
In 2007 this French politician became the first woman to reach the second round of a presidential election, ultimately losing to Nicolas Sarkozy — who is she?
In 1980, six gunmen demanding independence for a province of Iran stormed a London diplomatic compound, holding 26 hostages during a six-day standoff — which historic event?
Iranian Embassy siege: 1980 hostage situation in London.
Elected archon in 493 BC, this populist Athenian politician championed naval expansion, fought at Marathon, and became Athens's leading statesman ahead of the second Persian invasion — who is he?
Themistocles: Athenian politician and general (c. 524–459 BC)
As crown prince, this future king twice gave up his rights to the throne over scandalous romances, before a 1930 coup unseated his own son and put him on the throne instead — who is he?
Carol II of Romania was King of Romania (1930–1940). Carol's life and reign were beset with controversies, such as his desertion from the army during World War I.
Measured on 10 July 1913 at Furnace Creek Ranch in Death Valley, California, this scorching 134.1°F reading still stands as the world's hottest officially verified air mark — what is it?
Highest temperature recorded on Earth: Weather record.
Eldest daughter of King Amalric, this 12th-century ruler stood by her unpopular husband Guy of Lusignan even as her leprosy-stricken brother struggled to secure her succession — who is she?
Sibylla, Queen of Jerusalem: Crusader ruler from 1186 to 1190.

The heaviest aircraft ever built by its Brazilian manufacturer, this twin-engine jet transport was developed as a derivative of a regional jetliner, similar in role to the C-130 Hercules. Which aircraft?
Embraer C-390 Millennium: Brazilian military transport aircraft/tanker.
This condition involves involuntarily repeating words or sounds spoken by someone else, and is commonly seen in autism, ADHD, and Tourette syndrome. What is it called?
Made in the skin after sun exposure and also known as vitamin D3, this compound is converted by the liver and kidneys into forms that help the body absorb calcium. What is it?

Cholecalciferol: Vitamin D3, a chemical compound. Cholecalciferol, also known as vitamin D3, colecalciferol or calciol, is a skin-made vitamin D that is found in certain foods and used as a dietary supplement.
Discovered by naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace in 1859, this fungus hijacks carpenter ants' brains and marches them down to the forest floor before killing them — which organism?

Ophiocordyceps unilateralis: Species of fungus. Ophiocordyceps unilateralis, commonly known as zombie-ant fungus, is an insect-pathogenic fungus, discovered by the British naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace in 1859.
Carried out by the lungs, kidneys, and skin in vertebrates, this bodily process rids the body of metabolic byproducts like urea, carbon dioxide, and uric acid — what is it called?
Excretion: Elimination of metabolic waste products by an organism.
Known as rue or 'herb-of-grace,' this Mediterranean plant is prized for its bluish leaves and doubles as an insect repellent — which species?
Ruta graveolens: Species of plant. Ruta graveolens, commonly known as rue, common rue, ruda, arruda or herb-of-grace, is a species of the genus Ruta grown as an ornamental plant and herb.
Nicknamed 'Dr. Death,' this pathologist assisted at least 130 patients in dying and was convicted of murder after broadcasting one such case on television — who is he?
Jack Kevorkian: American pathologist and euthanasia activist (1928–2011)
Made by nearly every living organism, this protein locks iron away in a safe, soluble form inside cells, and its blood level is the standard test doctors use for anemia or iron overload — what is it?
Ferritin: Iron-carrying protein. Ferritin is a universal intracellular and extracellular protein that stores iron and releases it in a controlled fashion.
Named from the Latin word for hedgehog, this mammal family unites spiny Eurasian and African hedgehogs with their Southeast Asian cousins, the moonrats — which family?
Erinaceidae: Family of mammals. Erinaceidae (from Latin erinaceus, "hedgehog") is a family in the order Eulipotyphla, consisting of the hedgehogs and moonrats.
Also known as milo, jowar, or Guinea corn, this grass — domesticated in Sudan and now grown worldwide — ranks as the fifth most important cereal crop on Earth — which grain?
Sorghum: Species of grain. It is typically an annual, but some cultivars are perennial.
Introduced in 1948 by a French naturalist, this taxonomic tribe groups humans together with chimpanzees and bonobos, but excludes gorillas — which tribe?
Hominini: Tribe of mammals. The Hominini (hominins) form a taxonomic tribe of the subfamily Homininae (hominines).

This antibiotic is used as an eye ointment for conjunctivitis and, when safer options fail, to treat meningitis, plague, cholera, and typhoid — but in newborns it can trigger a dangerous swelling condition called gray baby syndrome — what drug is it?
Chloramphenicol: Antibiotic. Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic useful for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
Also known as pirarucu or paiche, this native of the Amazon River basin is among the largest freshwater fish on Earth — what species is it?
Powered by two rear-mounted engines under a T-tail and fitted with built-in airstairs, this twin-engine jetliner entered service with Delta Air Lines in December 1965 — which aircraft is it?
McDonnell Douglas DC-9: Jet airliner, produced 1965-1982.
This suborder of 'dog-like' carnivores includes bears, raccoons, weasels, and seals, and is thought to have diversified mainly across North America and northern Eurasia — what's it called?
Caniformia: Suborder of mammals. Caniformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "dog-like" carnivorans.

This physician was convicted of involuntary manslaughter in 2011 after inadvertently overdosing his famous patient with the anesthetic propofol, which he had been improperly using as a sleep aid — who is he?
Conrad Murray: American physician and convicted felon (born 1953)
This burrowing mammal builds ever-expanding tunnel systems, and its saliva contains toxins that paralyze its favorite prey, earthworms — what animal is it?
European mole: Species of mammal. The European mole (Talpa europaea) is a mammal of the order Eulipotyphla.

First described by 19th-century French psychiatrists Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, this rare condition — also called shared psychotic disorder — lets one person's delusion spread to another. What is it called?

Folie à deux: Shared psychosis, a psychotic disorder. The disorder, first conceptualized in 19th century French psychiatry by Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, is also known as Lasègue–Falret syndrome.
Which urban model uses digital technology and data from citizens, buildings, and cameras to improve sustainability, efficiency, and social inclusion?
Smart city is an urban model that leverages technology, human capital, and governance to improve sustainability, efficiency, and social inclusion, which are considered goals for cities of the future.
This deliquescent white salt helps make Dutch-process cocoa, soap, and glass, and can also turn up leaking from old alkaline batteries — what compound?
Potassium carbonate: Chemical compound. It is a white salt, which is soluble in water and forms a strongly alkaline solution.
Inside a ribosome, this cellular process reads messenger RNA three nucleotides at a time to build a chain of amino acids into protein — what is it called?
Translation (biology): Cellular process of protein synthesis. Translation is the process in biological cells in which proteins are produced using RNA molecules as templates.
Originally focused on water, this branch of physics studies liquids, gases, and plasmas, with applications from geophysics to aerospace engineering — which field?
Fluid mechanics: Branch of physics. Fluid mechanics is the branch of physics concerned with the mechanics of fluids (liquids, gases, and plasmas) and the forces on them.
First described in 1963, this rare disorder from a partial deletion on chromosome 5 gets its French name from the distinctive feline-sounding cry of affected infants — what is it called?
Cri du chat syndrome: Human medical condition.
Considered paradoxical by the ancient Greeks in Zeno's puzzle about motion, what term describes an infinite sum of terms added one after another, later made rigorous through the concept of a limit?
Series (mathematics): Infinite sum. In mathematics, a series is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
Working alongside Lise Meitner and Fritz Strassmann in 1938, this German chemist co-discovered nuclear fission and later won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alone — who is he?
Otto Hahn: German nuclear chemist and Nobel laureate (1879–1968)
Also known as trisomy 13, this chromosomal condition arises when cells carry extra genetic material from chromosome 13, causing widespread organ defects — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome: Chromosomal disorder in which there are three copies of chromosome 13.
With atomic number 54, this dense, colorless noble gas was the first to form a stable chemical compound, and now doubles as a general anesthetic and ion-thruster propellant — which element?
Xenon: Chemical element with atomic number 54 (Xe). It is a dense, colorless, odorless noble gas found in Earth's atmosphere in trace amounts.

Distinct from an unrelated American family with a similar name, these small seed-eating birds include house- and tree-dwelling species that nest on buildings in huge city numbers — which bird family is this?
Old World sparrow: Family of songbirds. Old World sparrows are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
This German-Finnish internet entrepreneur founded the file-hosting service Megaupload before U.S. authorities seized it in 2012 — who is he?

Distinguished by a fatty hump on its shoulders and a large dewlap, this heat-tolerant type of domestic cattle originated in South Asia and holds religious significance in parts of the world — what is it?
Zebu: South Asian domestic cattle. The zebu (Bos indicus), also known as indicine cattle and humped cattle, is a species or subspecies of domestic cattle originating in South Asia.
Commonly called the dog rose, this variable climbing wild plant is native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia — which species?

Despite its name, this African animal's hide actually ranges from brown to grey, and it's distinguished from its 'white' cousin by a pointed, hooked upper lip rather than a wide, square one — which species?
Black rhinoceros: Species of mammal. Although the species is referred to as black, its colours vary from brown to grey.
In 2023, she became the first woman ever to win the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences on her own, honored for her research on women in the labor market — who is this Harvard economist?
Claudia Goldin (born May 14, 1946) is an American economic historian and labor economist.
Certified in Canada in 1998, this large-cabin business jet shares its fuselage cross-section with the Challenger 600 and first flew in 1996 — which jet is it?
Bombardier Global Express: Large cabin business jet. The Bombardier Global Express is a large cabin, long-range business jet designed and manufactured by Bombardier Aviation.
Originating near the Beijing region and used throughout East Asian cooking, this Brassica rapa vegetable spread to Europe, the Americas, and Australia during the 20th century — which vegetable is it?
Napa cabbage: Subspecies of flowering plant.
This fungal genus growing on rye and other cereals produces alkaloids that cause a poisoning condition in humans and livestock who eat contaminated grain — which group of fungi?
Ergot: Fungi of the genus Claviceps. The most prominent member of this group is Claviceps purpurea (rye ergot fungus).

Built by a Swedish manufacturer, this single-engine fighter was the first mass-produced canard-design aircraft and the first with a digital avionics computer, unsurpassed until the Tornado arrived in 1981 — which jet?
Saab 37 Viggen: 1967 Swedish fighter aircraft family.
The first bomber capable of Mach 2 flight, this 1950s delta-winged bomber carried its nuclear payload in a combination bomb-and-fuel pod slung beneath the fuselage — which bomber?
Convair B-58 Hustler: Cold War-era American supersonic bomber.
Marked by dizziness, blurred vision, and fatigue, this cardiovascular condition is generally diagnosed when systolic readings fall under 90 mmHg — what is it?
Patented in 1967 and approved for medical use in 1980, this propionic-acid-class NSAID works by blocking prostaglandin production — what is it?

This movement disorder causes involuntary muscle contractions that twist the body into abnormal postures, and can sometimes be treated with botulinum toxin injections or deep brain stimulation — what is it?
Dystonia: Neurological movement disorder. Dystonia is often intensified or exacerbated by physical activity, and symptoms may progress into adjacent muscles.
Native to Eurasia and known by the common names 'cherry plum' and 'myrobalan plum,' this species is thought to be a parent of the cultivated plum — what is it, scientifically?
Prunus cerasifera: Species of plum. Native to Eurasia and naturalized elsewhere, P. cerasifera is believed to be one of the parents of the cultivated plum.

Approved for medical use in the US back in 1959 and sold under the brand name Adipex-P, this appetite-suppressing stimulant is a substituted amphetamine used alongside diet and exercise to treat obesity — what is it?
Revered by Ancient Egyptians as the god Khepri for rolling the sun across the sky, which insect feeds exclusively on feces?
Dung beetle: Informal group of insects.
Created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Müller, this esoteric programming language uses just eight simple commands and is often cited as a 'Turing tarpit' — what is it called?
Brainfuck: Esoteric, minimalist programming language. While Brainfuck is fully Turing-complete, it is not intended for practical use but to challenge and amuse programmers.
Synthesized in 1938 by German chemist Otto Eisleb and later marketed as Demerol, this synthetic opioid was the go-to pain medication for much of the 20th century — what is it?
Pethidine: Opioid analgesic. Pethidine, also known as meperidine and sold under the brand name Demerol among others, is a fully synthetic opioid pain medication of the phenylpiperidine class.
Launched in 1981 as a joint venture between French and Italian aerospace firms, this high-wing turboprop airliner later formed the basis for a stretched successor introduced in 1989 — which aircraft?

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
This medical term describes red blood cells rupturing and spilling their contents into the plasma — a process triggered by bacterial toxins or even intense exercise. What is it?
Hemolysis: Rupturing of red blood cells and release of their contents. Hemolysis may occur in vivo or in vitro.
Produced by the pancreas's alpha cells, this hormone raises blood sugar by triggering the liver to break down stored glycogen — the functional opposite of insulin. What is it?
Glucagon: Peptide hormone. It raises the concentration of glucose and fatty acids in the bloodstream and is considered to be the main catabolic hormone of the body.

This Russian political scientist studies authoritarian governance and legislative process, taught at Moscow institutions for nearly a decade, and by 2022 had a YouTube channel with a million subscribers — who is she?
Named from a Latin word for sword, this genus of cormous flowering plants in the iris family is sometimes called the 'sword lily' and is most diverse in South Africa's Cape region — which genus?
Gladiolus: Genus of perennial flowering plants. It is sometimes called the 'sword lily', but is usually called by its generic name (plural gladioli).
Coiled to just 6 to 7 centimetres but stretching nearly 20 feet if unraveled, this tube connects each testicle to the vas deferens and stores maturing sperm — what is it?

Epididymis: Tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens. The epididymis serves as an interconnection between the multiple efferent ducts at the rear of a testicle (proximally), and the vas deferens (distally).
Smaller than 3 millimetres and caused by leaking capillaries, these tiny red or purple skin spots can be forensically significant when found around the eyes or neck — what are they called?
Petechia: Small red or purple blemish on the skin, eyes, etc. due to rupture of capillaries.
This Swedish actor played Beorn in The Hobbit and starred in the Oscar-winning drama 'In a Better World,' directed by Susanne Bier. Who is he?
Mikael Persbrandt: Swedish actor. Mikael Åke Persbrandt (Swedish pronunciation: [ˈmîːkaɛl ˈpæ̂ːʂbrant]; born 25 September 1963) is a Swedish actor.

Known for rapid-fire dialogue, this writer-director created Gilmore Girls and later The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel, becoming the first woman to win Emmys for comedy writing and directing in the same year. Who is she?
Amy Sherman-Palladino: American television writer, director, and producer (born 1966)
Adapted from a Chinese movie of the same name, this South Korean romantic drama follows two friends across 14 years of friendship, love, and jealousy that began when they met at age 13. Which movie?
Soulmate (2023 film) is a 2023 South Korean romantic drama film directed by Min Yong-geun starring Kim Da-mi, Jeon So-nee and Byeon Woo-seok.
Often compared to Fellini and Antonioni, this Italian director won an Academy Award for Best International Film and made his debut with 'One Man Up' in 2001. Who is he?
Paolo Sorrentino: Italian film director and screenwriter. Paolo Sorrentino ( SORR-ən-TEE-noh, Italian: [ˈpaːolo sorrenˈtiːno]; born 31 May 1970) is an Italian film director, screenwriter, and writer.
Robin Williams and Nathan Lane play a gay couple whose son's engagement to a conservative senator's daughter causes chaos in this 1996 remake of a French farce — which film?
The Birdcage: 1996 film by Mike Nichols.
This Japanese voice actress lent her voice to Rebecca in 'Cyberpunk: Edgerunners' and Amiya in 'Arknights' — who is she?
Tomoyo Kurosawa: Japanese voice actress. Tomoyo Kurosawa (黒沢 ともよ, Kurosawa Tomoyo; born April 10, 1996) is a Japanese actress and singer.
This Russian actress won a TEFI award for Best Actress for her role in the tank drama 'T-34' — who is she?
In this French series, real celebrities play fictionalized versions of themselves as clients of a talent management firm — its English Netflix title is which show?
Call My Agent!: French comedy-drama television series.
Nicolas Cage recruits a physics student played by Jay Baruchel in this 2010 Disney fantasy adventure based on a segment from 1940's 'Fantasia' — which movie?
The Sorcerer's Apprentice (2010 film) is a 2010 American fantasy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures and starring Nicolas Cage and Jay Baruchel.
The daughter of a celebrated Bengali filmmaker and actress, this actress won a National Film Award for a movie her mother directed — who is she?
Konkona Sen Sharma: Indian actress and filmmaker (born 1979)
This Tamil filmmaker made his acting debut playing a mentally disabled man in his own 2010 drama, 'Nandalala' — who is he?
Mysskin: Indian film director and screenwriter.
This director-choreographer won a DGA Award for adapting a hit musical to film, then later helmed 'Mary Poppins Returns' and 'Into the Woods' — who is he?
Rob Marshall: American film and theatre director and producer (born 1960)
Ellen Burstyn won an Oscar playing a widow driving cross-country with her son in this 1974 Scorsese drama that later inspired a TV sitcom — which film?
Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore: 1974 film directed by Martin Scorsese.
This English actor is best known for playing scheming love interest Daniel Grayson on the drama series 'Revenge' — who is he?
Josh Bowman: English actor. Joshua Tobias Bowman (born 4 March 1988) is an English actor.
This Australian actor earned two SAG Award nominations for 'Picket Fences' before playing Detective Mark Hoffman in the 'Saw' franchise — who is he?
Susan Sarandon won an Oscar playing a nun who becomes spiritual adviser to a death-row inmate played by Sean Penn in this 1995 Tim Robbins drama — which movie?

Dead Man Walking (film) is a 1995 American crime drama film starring Susan Sarandon and Sean Penn, and co-produced and directed by Tim Robbins, who adapted the screenplay from the 1993 non-fiction book of the same name.
Ashley Judd and Tommy Lee Jones starred in this 1999 crime thriller that grossed nearly $178 million despite mixed reviews — which movie?
Double Jeopardy (1999 film) is a 1999 American crime thriller film directed by Bruce Beresford, and starring Ashley Judd, Tommy Lee Jones, and Bruce Greenwood.
This Israeli actress-activist co-executive produced HBO's 'In Treatment' and later served as a government envoy combating antisemitism — who is she?

As India's defence minister, this politician's tenure saw the exposure of the Bofors arms-deal scandal before he went on to serve as prime minister from 1989 to 1990 — who is he?
V. P. Singh: Prime Minister of India from 1989 to 1990. In the Rajiv Gandhi ministry, Singh was given various cabinet posts, including Minister of Finance and Minister of Defence.
Fought around 1274 BCE between Ramesses II's Egyptians and the Hittites under Muwatalli II, this Orontes River clash is believed to be the largest chariot engagement in ancient history — what was it?
Battle of Kadesh was a major military conflict in the early 13th century BC, between the attacking Ramesses II of the Egyptian Empire and defending Muwatalli II of the Hittite Empire.

The second son of Adam and Eve, this shepherd's offering was favored by God over his older brother's, leading that jealous brother to kill him in what the Bible calls the first murder — who was the victim?
Born in December 2014, this heir apparent to the Monegasque throne — twin brother of Princess Gabriella and son of Albert II and Charlene — has held the title Marquis of Baux since birth. Who is he?

Jacques, Hereditary Prince of Monaco: Heir apparent to the Monégasque throne (born 2014). Jacques, Hereditary Prince of Monaco, Marquis of Baux (Jacques Honoré Rainier Grimaldi; born 10 December 2014), is the heir apparent to the Monegasque throne.

This Telugu actor-politician served in India's upper house of parliament from 2008 to 2013, was a son of a former Andhra Pradesh chief minister and screen legend, and is the brother of actor-politician Balakrishna — who is he?
Nandamuri Harikrishna: Indian actor, film producer and politician.
Serving as Grand Vizier under Süleyman the Magnificent, this Ottoman statesman married the sultan's daughter Mihrimah in 1539, earning an epithet meaning 'son-in-law' — who is he?
Rüstem Pasha: Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire (1544–1553, 1555–1561)
Serving as both his country's first prime minister and later its third president, this Namibian leader also chaired the Southern African Development Community starting in 2018 — who is he?
Hage Geingob: President of Namibia from 2015 to 2024.

Ruled for most of its existence by Regent Miklos Horthy despite having no actual monarch on the throne, this interwar Central European state emerged after the suppression of a short-lived Soviet republic during the White Terror — which nation?
Kingdom of Hungary (1920–1946): Monarchy under regency.
In the Book of Genesis, harming this first murderer would supposedly bring sevenfold vengeance, and God gave him a sign of protection afterward — what is this combined biblical concept called?
Curse and mark of Cain: Phrase originating in the Hebrew Bible.

Founded in 2012 by former TV journalist Yair Lapid, this centrist Israeli party placed second with 19 Knesset seats in its debut election and later co-founded the short-lived Blue and White alliance in 2019 — which party?
Yesh Atid: Israeli political party. Yesh Atid (Hebrew: יֵשׁ עָתִיד, lit. 'There is a Future') is a centrist political party in Israel.
Serving over 12 years, this Iranian politician holds the record as his country's longest-serving prime minister, in office from 1965 to 1977 — who is he?
Amir-Abbas Hoveyda: Prime Minister of Iran from 1965 to 1977.
Born in Rostock and later a Prussian field marshal, this military leader helped defeat Napoleon at the Battle of Leipzig in 1813 and again at Waterloo in 1815 — who is he?
Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher: Prussian field marshal (1742–1819)

Ruled by a monarch called the Manikongo, this Central African state at its peak stretched from the Atlantic coast to the Kwango River and lasted as an independent power from around 1390 to 1862 — which realm?
Kingdom of Kongo: 1390–1914 state in Central Africa; Portuguese vassal from 1857.
Founded in 2020 by a cosmetics-company magnate, this liberal-leaning party takes a moderately supportive stance toward Vladimir Putin while opposing much of the ruling party's agenda — which party?
New People (Russia) is a political party in Russia formed in 2020.
Ruling a dynasty based in what is now central Afghanistan from 1173 to 1206, this figure extended his realm eastward into South Asia, ushering in centuries of Islamic rule there — who was he?
Muhammad of Ghor: Ghurid sultan from 1173 to 1206.
Spanning the reign of King Edward VII and often extended to the outbreak of the First World War in 1914, this period followed the death of Queen Victoria in 1901 — which age in British history?
Edwardian era: Historical period in Britain from 1901 to 1910.

Rising to prominence during Greece's government-debt crisis, this far-right, neo-Nazi organization became the third-largest party in the Greek parliament following the January 2015 election, before its support collapsed — which group?
Golden Dawn (Greece): Greek neo-Nazi criminal organisation.
Once a shoemaker before joining the Bolsheviks in 1911, this close associate of Stalin rose to the Politburo in 1930 after helping consolidate Soviet power across Ukraine and Turkestan — who is he?
Having led the 'Iron Brigade' with distinction in World War I, this Russian general co-founded the anti-Bolshevik Volunteer Army and led it on a failed offensive toward Moscow in 1919 — who is he?
Anton Denikin: Russian military and political leader (1872–1947)

Serving as Latvia's Minister of Welfare before becoming its second-ever female head of government in 2023, this politician stayed on as caretaker prime minister after her coalition collapsed in 2026 — who is she?
Evika Siliņa: Prime Minister of Latvia from 2023 to 2026. Evika Siliņa ([ˈævika ˈsiliɲa]; born 3 August 1975) is a Latvian politician who served as prime minister of Latvia from 2023 to 2026.
This Japanese politician has served in the House of Councillors for the Liberal Democratic Party after stints as Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Defense and of the Cabinet Office — who is she?
A Keio University graduate who entered Japan's National Diet in 1963, this politician served as prime minister from 1996 to 1998 before resigning after a coalition election defeat — who is he?

Ryutaro Hashimoto: Prime Minister of Japan from 1996 to 1998. Ryutaro Hashimoto (橋本 龍太郎, Hashimoto Ryūtarō; 29 July 1937 – 1 July 2006) was a Japanese politician who served as prime minister of Japan from 1996 to 1998.
Serving as regent of Hungary from 1446 to 1453, this military leader earned the nickname 'Turk-buster' for his campaigns against the Ottoman Empire — who is he?
John Hunyadi: Hungarian military and political figure (c. 1406–1456)
This Germanic people, first described by the historian Tacitus around 100 AD near the River Elbe, gave their name to a country and its language after settling in post-Roman Britain — which people?
Angles (tribe) (Old) were one of the main Germanic peoples who settled in Great Britain in the post-Roman period.
This Iranian Azeri military commander, a mechanical engineering graduate who joined the Revolutionary Guard, was killed in 1985 during Operation Badr in the Iran–Iraq War — who was he?
Mehdi Bakeri: Iranian military commander. Mehdi Bakeri (Persian: مهدی باکری‎; 1954 – 16 March 1985) was an Iranian Azeri military officer and prominent Iranian military figure in the Iran–Iraq War.
This Roman goddess of agriculture and grain, honored every April at a weeklong harvest festival, was considered the counterpart to the Greek goddess Demeter — who is she?
Ceres (mythology): Roman goddess of agriculture. In ancient Roman religion, Ceres ( SEER-eez, Latin: [ˈkɛreːs]) was a goddess of agriculture, grain crops, fertility, and motherly relationships.

Invented by a pseudonymous figure who combined ideas from the cryptography community, this decentralized digital currency evolved from a medium of exchange into primarily a store of value — which article recounts this asset's origins?
History of bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, a digital asset that uses cryptography to control its creation and management rather than relying on central authorities.
This third-century queen of the Palmyrene Empire conquered Egypt and expanded her realm across the Roman East before facing Emperor Aurelian's counterattack — who is she?
Whose members were nicknamed 'Nazbols,' this Russian opposition organization was banned as extremist in 2007 and published a newspaper named after a hand grenade — which group?
National Bolshevik Party was a Russian political party that operated from 1993 until it was banned in 2007.
Symbolizing both a diamond's indestructibility and a thunderbolt's force, this ritual scepter-like tool is used alongside a bell in Tibetan Buddhist ceremonies — what is it called?
Vajra: Spiritual weapon or symbol in Dharmic religions.
Nicknamed 'the Mad Baron,' this Baltic German warlord tried to revive the Mongol Empire under the Bogd Khan and expelled Chinese troops from Mongolia in 1921 — who was he?
Roman von Ungern-Sternberg: Russian general and warlord (1886–1921)

Founded in 1978 by Jacques Saadé and headquartered in a namesake tower in Marseille, this French firm is the world's third-largest container shipping company, running nearly 600 vessels — which company?
CMA CGM: French shipping company. CMA CGM operations include shipping, port operation, supply chain management, and warehousing.

This ancient Athenian orator first took the stand at age 20 to win back his inheritance from his own guardians, before becoming a professional speechwriter and, by 354 BC, a political voice — who is he?
Demosthenes: Classical Athenian statesman and orator (384–322 BC)
As a concubine of Selim I and mother of Suleiman the Magnificent, this woman became the very first to hold the empire's highest maternal title in the Ottoman court — who was she?
Hafsa Sultan (Ottoman; 1478/1479 - 19 March 1534), was a concubine of Selim I and the mother of Suleiman the Magnificent.
Serving as Lebanon's prime minister across three separate terms since 2005, this politician lost his final bid for a fourth term in January 2025 to the ICJ president, 9 votes to 84 — who is he?
Najib Mikati: Prime Minister of Lebanon (born 1955)

This Polish politician served two stints as justice minister — one ending under PM Mateusz Morawiecki in 2023 — while also holding the prosecutor general post and championing an anti-corruption crusade — who is he?
Representing the Goshamahal constituency in Hyderabad, this Indian politician served as a state assembly whip for the BJP in Telangana until 2025 — who is he?
T. Raja Singh: Indian politician. Thakur Raja Singh (born 15 April 1977) is an Indian politician from the state of Telangana.

Held every June in many cities to commemorate the 1969 Stonewall riots, this annual LGBTQ celebration of rights and self-acceptance began as marches in Chicago, New York, LA, and San Francisco in 1970 — what's it called?
Pride parade: LGBTQ celebration event. The events sometimes also serve as demonstrations for legal rights such as same-sex marriage.

In Hindu cosmology, this term denotes the archetypal first human and also the title given to fourteen rulers, one per cosmic age, the current holder having been warned of a great flood — what's the term?
Manu (Hinduism): Hindu concept. Manu (Sanskrit: मनु) is a term found with various meanings in Hinduism.
A sepoy in the Bengal Native Infantry who died in April 1857, this soldier's actions helped spark the rebellion that ended East India Company rule and ushered in the British Raj — who is he?
Mangal Pandey: Indian soldier and freedom fighter (1827–1857)

A night of anti-aircraft fire over a Californian city in February 1942, sparked by a rumored Japanese air raid that the Secretary of the Navy later dismissed as a "false alarm" — what is this incident called?
Battle of Los Angeles: Anti-aircraft shelling during WWII against an imagined invader.
Germany's first federal minister of Circassian ancestry, this politician co-led the Greens for a decade before becoming Baden-Württemberg's minister-president in 2026 — who is he?
Cem Özdemir: German politician, Minister-President of Baden-Württemberg since 2026 (born 1965)
Once one of the largest states in African history, this Sahelian power made Gao its capital under Sonni Ali and later controlled the trade hubs of Timbuktu and Djenné — which state?
Songhai Empire was a state located in the western part of the Sahel during the 15th and 16th centuries.
Forced to resign from the hospital company he co-founded after it pleaded guilty to defrauding Medicare, this businessman later became the 45th governor of Florida — who is he?
Fought in southern Anatolia on 5 November 333 BC, this clash saw Alexander the Great rout Darius III, who fled leaving behind his family and treasury — which engagement was it?
Battle of Issus (also Issos) occurred in southern Anatolia, on 5 November 333 BC between the Hellenic League led by Alexander the Great and the Achaemenid (or Persian) Empire, led by Darius III.
Serving as Japan's prime minister through most of the postwar occupation, this diplomat forged close ties with the United States and once served as ambassador to Italy — who is he?
Shigeru Yoshida: Prime Minister of Japan (1946–1947; 1948–1954)
First elected to the Iowa House in 1958, this senator has represented Iowa since 1981 and became Senate president pro tempore in 2025 — who is he?

Founded by Minamoto no Yoritomo after his victory in the Genpei War, this feudal military government ruled Japan from 1185 to 1333, surviving two Mongol invasions before its overthrow — what was it called?

Kamakura shogunate: Government of Japan (1192–1333). The Kamakura shogunate (Japanese: 鎌倉幕府, Hepburn: Kamakura bakufu) was the feudal military government of Japan during the Kamakura period from 1185 to 1333.
Meaning 'seal' or 'gesture' in Sanskrit, this hand or body pose is used in Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist ritual as well as yoga and Indian dance — what is it called?
Mudra: Symbolic gestures in Hinduism, Jainism and Buddhism.
Becoming chief minister at just 44 — the second-youngest in his state's history — this Indian politician is now serving his third term leading Maharashtra — who is he?
Devendra Fadnavis: 18th Chief Minister of Maharashtra (2014-2019; since 2024)
Founded in 1955 by a Dieppe garage owner, this French sports-car marque was bought by a bigger French carmaker in 1973 and now builds electric vehicles like the A290 — which company?

Automobiles Alpine: French car manufacturer. Société des Automobiles Alpine SAS, commonly known as Alpine (French: [alpin]), is a French manufacturer of sports cars and racing cars established in 1955.

Married to the sister of North Korea's former supreme leader, this politician was believed to hold de facto power as Kim Jong Il's health failed and rose to vice-chairman of the National Defence Commission — who is he?
The eldest of a hundred brothers born to King Dhritarashtra, this Mahabharata antagonist humiliated Draupadi in a rigged dice game, provoking Bhima's vow of revenge — who is he?
Duryodhana: Eldest Kaurava in the epic Mahabharata.

Created by Napoleon in 1807 from Polish lands ceded by Prussia, this French client state was ruled by Frederick Augustus I of Saxony and marked the first attempt to revive an independent Poland — what was it called?
Duchy of Warsaw: Polish state (1807–1815). The city of Kraków, Poland's cultural centre, was granted "free city" status until its incorporation into Austria in 1846.
Crowned after his father Alp Arslan died from battle wounds in 1072, this Seljuk ruler saw the empire reach its peak, though real power lay with vizier Nizam al-Mulk — who is he?
Malik-Shah I: Sultan of the Seljuk Empire from 1072 to 1092.
Married to King George V's third son and living to age 102, she became the British royal family's longest-lived member — who was she?
Princess Alice, Duchess of Gloucester: Member of the British royal family (1901–2004)
Nicknamed 'Netaji' by his party, this Indian politician founded the Samajwadi Party and served three terms as Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh — who is he?
The first African ever to lead the World Health Organization, this former Ethiopian health and foreign affairs minister steered the agency through Ebola, COVID-19, and the mpox outbreak — who is he?
Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus: Ethiopian public health official (born 1965)

Founded in Turkey in 2001 after its predecessor was banned by the Constitutional Court, this Islamist political movement split from the group that also produced the AKP, and regularly accuses Erdoğan of undermining democracy — which movement?
Felicity Party is an Islamist political party in Turkey. It was founded in 2001, and is mainly supported by conservative Muslims in Turkey.
The half-sister of Helen of Troy and wife of Mycenae's king, this figure from Greek mythology murdered her husband upon his return from Troy to avenge the sacrifice of their daughter — who is she?
Clytemnestra: Figure from Greek mythology. Clytemnestra appears as a character in several ancient Greek works, including the Homeric epics and plays by Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides.

Between 1978 and 1990, the overthrow of the Somoza dictatorship and the Contra War that followed turned this Central American country into a major Cold War proxy battleground — what was this conflict known as?
Nicaraguan Revolution was an armed conflict that took place in the Central American nation of Nicaragua between 1961 and 1990.
The only female judge named in the Hebrew Bible, this prophetess ordered the general Barak to attack the forces of a Canaanite king — who is she?
Deborah: Prophetess in the Bible. Alternatively, "lappid" translates as "torch" or "lightning", therefore the phrase, "woman of Lappidoth" could be referencing Deborah as a "fiery woman".

This ancient state, whose territory mostly overlapped modern Azerbaijan, gets its Western name from a Greek mistranslation of an Armenian term — which historical realm is this, whose descendants include the Udi people?

Caucasian Albania: Ancient state in the Caucasus. Caucasian Albania is a modern exonym for a former state located in ancient times in the Caucasus, mostly overlapping the region of present-day Azerbaijan.
This April 1940 assault saw Nazi Germany occupy Denmark within hours and invade Norway on the same morning, launching the Norwegian Campaign — what was this codenamed?
Operation Weserübung: 1940 German invasion of Denmark and Norway in WWII.
Serving as the UK's last Defence Secretary before the 2024 election, this politician also briefly held the Home Office and previously ran Transport under Boris Johnson — who is he?
Named the first viceroy of Italian East Africa, this general commanded Italian forces in both world wars and became Prime Minister after Fascism fell — who was he?
Ruling Sweden and Norway from 1872, this monarch saw his joint crown split apart in 1905 when Norway's throne passed to a Danish prince — who was he?
Oscar II: King of Sweden (1872–1907) and Norway (1872–1905)
In 751, an Abbasid-Tibetan force defeated Tang China's army for control of territory near the Syr Darya, ending Tang expansion into Central Asia — which clash?
Battle of Talas (pinyin: Dlus Zhny) was an armed confrontation between the Abbasid Caliphate along with the Tibetan Empire against the Tang dynasty and its allies in 751.
Born in 1664, which Ottoman sultan ruled the empire from 1695 until his death in 1703?

Mustafa II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1695 to 1703. Mustafa II (Ottoman Turkish: مصطفى ثانى Muṣṭafā-yi sānī; 6 February 1664 – 29 December 1703) was the sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1695 to 1703.

Daughter of Darius III of Persia, she was captured after her father's defeat at Issus and became the second bride of the Macedonian conqueror at the Susa weddings in 324 BC, before being killed by his other spouse, Roxana — who was she?
Stateira (wife of Alexander the Great): Daughter of Darius III, died 323 BC.
Born in London to a Ugandan-Indian family, this Conservative MP for Witham served as Home Secretary from 2019 to 2022 before becoming Shadow Foreign Secretary — who is she?
After cancelling a 1952 election he was losing, this military officer ruled Venezuela as dictator until 1958, funding lavish public works with oil money — who was he?
Marcos Pérez Jiménez: Dictator of Venezuela from 1952 to 1958. The economy of Venezuela developed rapidly while Pérez was in power.
Mother of Alexander the Great and de facto ruler of Macedon during his conquests, which ancient Greek princess was eventually defeated and executed by Cassander?
Olympias: Mother of Alexander the Great (c. 375–316 BC)

This cadet branch of the Capetian line ruled France from 1328 to 1589, spinning off junior branches in Orléans, Anjou, Burgundy, and Alençon before its male line died out and the Bourbons took over — which royal dynasty?
House of Valois: Cadet branch of the Capetian dynasty. The Capetian House of Valois (VAL-wah, also US: va(h)l-WAH, French: [valwa]) was a cadet branch of the Capetian dynasty.

Born in Canada to a Punjabi Sikh family, this lawyer led Canada's New Democratic Party from 2017 to 2025 and became the first non-white leader of a major federal party in the country's history — who is he?
This retired four-star Marine general commanded U.S. forces in the Gulf War, Afghanistan, and Iraq before serving as America's 26th secretary of defense from 2017 to 2019 — who is he?
Assassinated just six months before Burma's independence from Britain was achieved, this revolutionary is remembered as the founder of modern Myanmar and its armed forces — who is he?

The son of a former prime minister of India, this politician and film producer has twice served as chief minister of Karnataka and now leads India's Ministry of Heavy Industries and Steel — who is he?
H. D. Kumaraswamy: Indian politician and film producer (born 1959)
First featured in a late-12th-century tale by Chrétien de Troyes, this Knight of the Round Table was the original hero of the Grail quest before later authors replaced him with Galahad — who is he?
Perceval: One of King Arthur's legendary Knights.
This Greek personification of sleep, whose Roman counterpart is Somnus, lent his name to a word for a trance-like state and was said by Pausanias to be the Muses' dearest friend — who is he?
Hypnos: Personification of sleep in Greek mythology. In Greek mythology, Hypnos (Ancient Greek: Ὕπνος, 'sleep'), also spelled Hypnus, is the personification of sleep.

After graduating from SUNY Plattsburgh and joining Congressman Chuck Schumer's staff, this politician became New York City's youngest council member at 27, then resigned from Congress after a sex scandal — who is he?
Anthony Weiner: American politician and sex offender (born 1964)
This Polish farmer-turned-politician founded an agrarian populist party in 1992 known for blockading roads, then briefly served as Deputy Prime Minister in a 2006 coalition government — who is he?
Depicted in the Buddhist wheel of existence, these realms — from gods and humans to hungry ghosts and hell — are where beings are reborn according to their karma. What is it called?
Six Paths: Concept in Buddhist cosmology.
Serving as Saudi Arabia's intelligence chief from 2005 to 2012, this prince was briefly crown prince for just three months in 2015 during his half-brother's early reign — who is he?
Muqrin bin Abdulaziz: Saudi royal, military official and former Crown Prince (born 1945)
According to the Book of Genesis, this aristocratic Egyptian woman married the patriarch Joseph and became mother to Manasseh and Ephraim — who is she?
According to Catholic teaching, this change during the eucharistic prayer turns bread and wine into the Body and Blood of Christ while their outward appearance stays the same — what is it called?

Generally defined as profoundly immoral behavior that causes unnecessary suffering, this concept is usually framed as the opposite of good and can take personal, natural, or supernatural forms — what is it?
Evil: Opposite or absence of good. Evil, as a concept, is usually defined as profoundly immoral behavior, and it is related to acts that cause unnecessary pain and suffering to others.
Director of Russia's Federal Security Service since 2008, this powerful Putin ally is believed to have influenced the decision to invade Ukraine in 2022 — who is he?

Houthi forces in Yemen have launched missiles and drones at shipping tied to Israel amid the Gaza war, drawing military responses from Israel, the US and the UK — what is this ongoing maritime conflict called?
Red Sea crisis: Houthi involvement in the Gaza war. The Red Sea crisis is an ongoing armed conflict and maritime crisis instigated by the Houthis, an armed group in Yemen.
In 53 BC, seven Roman legions under Crassus were lured into the desert and crushed by Parthian cataphracts and horse archers near a town in modern-day Turkey — what was this military clash called?
Battle of Carrhae: Part of the Roman–Parthian Wars.

Serving as both the last prime minister of Great Britain and the first of the United Kingdom, this statesman held office through the French Revolution and Napoleonic Wars, and was distinguished from his father, who shared his surname — who was he?
William Pitt the Younger: British statesman (1759–1806)
A British peeress and former model who once worked as a political staffer, she is married to the 7th Marquess of Cholmondeley — who is she?
Rose Hanbury: English peeress and model (born 1984)
Founder of the German Workers' Party that became the Nazi Party, this early mentor to Adolf Hitler was ousted from party leadership by his protégé in 1921 — who is he?
This politician resigned as Kyrgyzstan's acting president in November 2020 just so he could run in — and win — the 2021 election that made him the country's sixth president. Who is he?
Sadyr Japarov: President of Kyrgyzstan since 2021. Japarov returned to Kyrgyzstan in 2017, where he was arrested and sentenced to an 11 year prison term due to his prior illegal political activities.
Often called the 'Bismarck of Japan' for his realpolitik nation-building, this Satsuma-born statesman was one of three nobles who led the 1868 Meiji Restoration — who is he?
Representing Uttar Pradesh's Mau constituency, this politician-turned-gangster won a state assembly seat five times, twice under the Bahujan Samaj Party banner — who is he?
This Russian admiral led naval operations off the Syrian coast in 2016 before taking command of the Black Sea Fleet during the Russo-Ukrainian war in 2022 — who is he?
Viktor Sokolov (naval officer) (born 4 April 1962) is an officer of the Russian Navy and former commander of the Black Sea Fleet.
This Aztec god of the night sky, hurricanes, and conflict had the jaguar as his animal double, and his main festival involved ritual human sacrifice — who is he?
Tezcatlipoca: Aztec deity of darkness and violence.
Central to Sufism, this Islamic devotional practice involves repeatedly reciting the names of God, often counted on prayer beads — what's it called?
Dhikr: Remembrance of God in Islam.
On 16 March 1988, thousands of Kurdish civilians were killed in a large-scale chemical weapons attack carried out during Iraq's Anfal campaign — what is this atrocity called?
Halabja massacre: 1988 chemical attack in Iraqi Kurdistan.
This 21st-century movement uses evidence and reason to calculate which charities and careers do the most good, treating everyone's interests as equally weighty — what's it called?
Effective altruism: Philosophical and social movement.

Controlling most of Eastern Galicia from late 1918 to mid-1919, this short-lived state also claimed parts of northern Bukovina and Carpathian Ruthenia, with power held by a nationalist democratic party — what was it called?
West Ukrainian People's Republic: 1918–1919 state in Central Europe.
Founded by crusading knights along the Baltic during the 13th-century Northern Crusades, this theocratic realm at its peak stretched from Prussia to Estonia and included Gotland — what was it called?
State of the Teutonic Order was a theocratic state located along the southeastern shore of the Baltic Sea in northern Europe.
Married into the Kennedy family and the driving force behind the creation of the Peace Corps, this 1972 Democratic vice-presidential nominee also founded Head Start and Job Corps — who is he?
Sargent Shriver: American diplomat, politician and activist (1915–2011)
This Imperial Japanese general captured Port Arthur twice — first from China in 1894, then from Russia a decade later — and became a national symbol of self-sacrificing loyalty — who is he?
Fill in the blank: “____ is the fifth and current caliph of the Islamic State.”
Abu Hafs al-Hashimi al-Qurashi is the fifth and current caliph of the Islamic State.

A former primary school teacher and union leader who rose to prominence during a 2017 teachers' strike, this politician served as Peru's president until his failed self-coup in December 2022 — who is he?
Pedro Castillo: President of Peru from 2021 to 2022.

Captured as a child and given as a gift to Peter the Great, this military engineer of African origin rose through the Russian imperial court and became an ancestor of poet Alexander Pushkin — who is he?
Abram Petrovich Gannibal: African-born Russian general and military engineer.
This Argentine politician served as the first Chief of Government of Buenos Aires from 1996 to 1999 before becoming president, a role he resigned from in 2001 — who is he?
Fernando de la Rúa: President of Argentina from 1999 to 2001. De la Rúa was born in Córdoba, and entered politics after graduating with a degree in law.
Once a commander of Alexander the Great's elite infantry, this Macedonian general later ruled Asia Minor, Syria, Mesopotamia, and Iran, founding an empire that bore his name — who was he?
Seleucus I Nicator: Macedonian general, Diadochus, and founder of the Seleucid Empire.
Regarded as one of history's most brutal dictators, this man led Equatorial Guinea to independence in 1968 before his erratic, cult-of-personality rule ended in a 1979 overthrow — who was he?
Francisco Macías Nguema: President of Equatorial Guinea from 1968 to 1979.
Established as a client state of Nazi Germany in March 1939, this Central European nation's army also joined the invasion of Poland that year — which state, whose capital was Bratislava?
Slovak Republic (1939–1945): Client state of Nazi Germany. The Slovak part of Czechoslovakia declared independence with German support one day before the German occupation of Bohemia and Moravia.

Serving as Prime Minister of Sardinia from 1852 through the Second Italian War of Independence, this statesman became the first Prime Minister of a newly united Italy but died just three months into the role — who is he?
Camillo Benso, Count of Cavour: First Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Italy from March to June in 1861.
Born in Iran and raised in Germany, this politician co-led the Greens alongside Ricarda Lang and has served as Vice President of the Bundestag since 2025 — who is he?
This Italian-born prelate succeeded Richelieu as chief minister to the French crown in 1642, guiding young King Louis XIV's early education — who is he?
Cardinal Mazarin: Italian clergyman and politician (1602–1661)
Kenya's current president since 2022, he previously became the country's first elected deputy president after representing Eldoret North in parliament — who is he?

William Ruto: President of Kenya since 2022. William Kipchirchir Samoei Arap Ruto (born 21 December 1966) is a Kenyan politician who is the fifth and current president of Kenya since 13 September 2022.
Ruling Rome alongside his adoptive brother Marcus Aurelius from 161, he was the empire's first co-emperor in its history — who is he?
Lucius Verus: Roman emperor from 161 to 169.
Sparked by a 1967 uprising in a West Bengal village, this decades-long rural rebellion against the Indian government has been waged by communist guerrilla groups since — what is it called?
Naxalite–Maoist insurgency: Indian anti-government conflict since 1967.
In the Book of Revelation, these divine horn blasts — sounded one at a time by angels after the breaking of the final seal — unleash a series of apocalyptic disasters. What are they called?
Seven trumpets: Described in the Book of Revelation. The seven trumpets are sounded by seven angels and the events that follow are described in detail in Revelation 8–11.

This European noble dynasty's founder led the Dutch Revolt against Spanish rule, and a later prince orchestrated England's Glorious Revolution — which royal family currently reigns over the Netherlands?
House of Orange-Nassau: European dynasty. Several members of the house served during the Eighty Years' War and after as stadtholder ("governor"; Dutch: stadhouder) during the Dutch Republic.
Elected to Taiwan's Legislative Yuan in 2020 as a Democratic Progressive Party lawyer, which politician is also an avid cosplayer?
Lai Pin-yu: Taiwanese politician and cosplayer.
Armed with the fire serpent Xiuhcoatl, which Aztec deity of sun and war was patron god of the Aztec capital and had human sacrifices offered in his honor?

National Action Party (Mexico) is a conservative political party in Mexico founded in 1939. The National Action Party (Spanish: Partido Acción Nacional, PAN) is a conservative political party in Mexico founded in 1939.
The illegitimate son of Mircea I of Wallachia, this nobleman was inducted into the Order of the Dragon in 1431 and twice ruled Wallachia as Voivode in the 1430s and 1440s — who is he?
Vlad II Dracul: Ruler of Wallachia (r. 1436–1442, 1443–1447)
Serving since 2023, this politician is Turkey's second-ever vice president and previously ran the country's Ministry of Development — who is he?
Cevdet Yılmaz: Vice President of Turkey since 2023. Cevdet Yılmaz (born 1 April 1967) is a Turkish politician who has been the 2nd and current vice president of Turkey since 2023.
Renowned as the fabulously wealthy last king of Lydia, he was ultimately defeated by Cyrus the Great after the siege of Sardis — who was he?
Croesus: King of Lydia from 585 or 561 to 547 BC.
This Italian entrepreneur-turned-politician founded a university in 2006, has presided over a football club since 2017, and became mayor of an Umbrian city in 2023 — who is he?
Stefano Bandecchi: Italian politician and entrepreneur. Stefano Bandecchi (born 4 April 1961) is an Italian politician and entrepreneur.
This Georgian super-heavyweight holds the all-time world records in the snatch, clean and jerk, and total, and became a parliamentarian for the Georgian Dream party in 2024 — who is he?

The first woman to serve as chief of naval operations and the first ROTC graduate to hold the post, she also became the first woman on the Joint Chiefs of Staff before being relieved in 2025 — who is she?
Crowned king of Judah at just eight years old after his father's assassination, he later launched sweeping religious reforms after a lost scroll was found during temple repairs — who is he?
Josiah: Biblical King of Judah. Following this discovery, Josiah destroyed idols, high places, and sacred poles and purged Judah of false priests, mediums, and magicians.
Founded in 1997 by Lalu Prasad Yadav, this Bihar-based political party built its support among Other Backward Classes, Dalits, and Muslims — which party?
Rashtriya Janata Dal: Political party in India. The Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD, lit. 'National People's Party') is an Indian political party, mainly based in the Indian state of Bihar.
This English media personality first gained fame as an Apprentice contestant in 2007, later became an LBC radio presenter, and underwent brain surgery to treat her epilepsy — who is she?

This fast-food chicken chain traces back to Colonel Harland Sanders selling Southern fried chicken from a roadside restaurant in Corbin, Kentucky, during the Great Depression — which chain, later sold in 1964 to a group led by John Y. Brown Jr.?

History of KFC: KFC (also commonly referred to by its historical name Kentucky Fried Chicken) was founded by Colonel Harland Sanders, an entrepreneur who began selling Southern fried chicken from his roadside restaurant in Corbin, Kentucky, during the Great Depression.
Nicknamed the 'White Whale' for its size, this Catholic-inspired centrist party dominated postwar politics for nearly fifty years until the Tangentopoli scandals ended its run in 1994 — which party?

Founded by P. A. Sangma after his 2012 break from another political group, this Meghalaya-based conservative outfit became, in 2019, the first group from the northeastern region to gain official country-wide recognized status — which organization?

National People's Party (India) (NPP) is a conservative national political party in India. Sangma after his expulsion from the Nationalist Congress Party in July 2012, it was accorded national party status on 7 June 2019.
A two-time Chief Minister of Maharashtra who also served as India's Minister of Earth Sciences, this Indian National Congress politician hailed from the Latur district — who is he?
Founded by Mamata Banerjee in 1998 as a breakaway faction, this West Bengal party ruled from 2011 until finally losing to the BJP in the 2026 election — which party?
Trinamool Congress: Political party in India.
Ruler of the Kingdom of Pontus in northern Anatolia, this king waged repeated but unsuccessful wars against Rome for dominance over Asia Minor and the Black Sea — who was he?
Mithridates VI Eupator: King of Pontus from 120 to 63 BC.
One of the founding members of an elite U.S. Army special-missions unit, this retired sergeant major served from 1968 to 1999 — who is he?
Better known by his nickname 'Calico Jack,' this English pirate was hanged in 1720 and is remembered for his two female crew members, Anne Bonny and Mary Read — who was he?
John Rackham: English pirate (died 1720). John Rackham (hanged 18 November 1720) was an English pirate operating in the Bahamas and Jamaica during the early 18th century.

Formed in 1989 as a federation of six regional parties advocating northern Italian independence, this right-wing party was later led by Matteo Salvini and rebranded before the 2018 election — which party?
Lega Nord: Political party in Italy.
This Austrian chancellor banned the Nazi Party, suppressed the Socialists in the Austrian Civil War, and was assassinated in 1934 during a failed coup by Nazi agents — who was he?
Engelbert Dollfuss: Chancellor of Austria from 1932 to 1934.
Made by young Indonesians on 28 October 1928, this nationalist declaration proclaimed one motherland, one nation, and one unifying language — what is it called?
Youth Pledge: 1928 declaration by Indonesian nationalists.
After her weaving skills provoked the wrath of Minerva in Ovid's telling, this mortal hanged herself in shame and was transformed into a spider -- who is she?
Arachne: Mythological weaver who was transformed into a spider.
A former tanner and shipowner from Le Havre, this politician became France's seventh president in 1895 and died suddenly in office four years later — who was he?
Félix Faure: President of France from 1895 to 1899. Félix François Faure (French: [feliks fʁɑ̃swa fɔʁ]; 30 January 1841 – 16 February 1899) was President of France from 1895 until his death in 1899.
Sparked by a deadly 1947 police crackdown on independence-day protesters, this guerrilla insurgency raged on a South Korean island from 1948 to 1949 — what is this event called?

Jeju uprising: 1948–1949 insurgency in South Korea. The Jeju uprising (in South Korea, the Jeju April 3 incident, Korean: 제주 4·3 사건) was an uprising on Jeju Island, South Korea, from April 1948 to May 1949.
This Bronze Age Semitic-speaking people founded Babylon, ruled much of the Levant and Mesopotamia, and later helped establish Egypt's 14th Dynasty — who were they?
Amorites: Ancient Semitic-speaking people from the Levant.
A Rhodes Scholar and former U.S. Army officer, this author-turned-politician became Maryland's 63rd governor in 2023 — who is he?
In 1902, this Indian princely ruler issued one of India's earliest affirmative-action orders, reserving half of government jobs and education for backward classes — who was he?
Shahu of Kolhapur: Indian ruler and social reformer (1894 to 1922)
Formerly known as Nene, this Buddhist nun was the principal wife of warlord Toyotomi Hideyoshi and matriarch who oversaw diplomacy with Japan's imperial court — who was she?
This Spanish traditionalist political movement backed an alternative Bourbon line descended from Don Carlos, sparking a series of 19th-century civil wars — what's the movement called?
Serving as Dachau's second commandant and later the first inspector of Nazi concentration camps, this SS commander was killed in 1943 when his plane was shot down over Kharkov — who was he?
This Russian-Israeli billionaire once owned the Brooklyn Nets and built his fortune atop Norilsk Nickel, the world's largest nickel and palladium producer — who is he?
Mikhail Prokhorov: Russian entrepreneur and politician (born 1965)
Founded in Turkey in 2018 by the son of a former prime minister, this Islamist movement sees itself as heir to his father's 1990s movement and the Millî Görüş ideology — which one?
New Welfare Party is an Islamist and ultraconservative political party in Turkey, founded on 23 November 2018.
This antimilitarist French socialist leader was assassinated in 1914 right as World War I broke out — who was he?
Jean Jaurès: French Socialist leader (1859–1914). The two parties merged in 1905 into the French Section of the Workers' International (SFIO).
Named for its founding year, this Dutch social-liberal party — led since August 2023 by Rob Jetten — draws its strongest support from university-educated, city-dwelling voters — which party?
Democrats 66: Political party in the Netherlands.
Dubbed 'the greatest living explorer' in 1984, this baronet was the first person to reach both poles by surface travel and later summited Everest at age 65 — who is he?
Rising from aide-de-camp to Tsar Nicholas II to lieutenant general in World War I, this nobleman seized power in a 1918 coup to become hetman of a short-lived Ukrainian state — who is he?
Pavlo Skoropadsky: Ukrainian and Russian Cossack military and political official; Hetman of Ukraine (1918)
Established on 14 November 1985 by politician Rahşan Ecevit, which of these political groups is this?
Democratic Left Party (Turkey) is a Turkish political party, founded on 14 November 1985 by Rahan Ecevit.

Known as Adolf Eichmann's right-hand man, this Austrian SS officer organized the deportation of tens of thousands of Jews from Austria, Greece and France to concentration camps during World War II — who is he?
Born in Austria to Russian and Estonian refugee parents, this former Vienna economics professor and Green Party leader has served as Austria's president since 2017 — who is he?
Alexander Van der Bellen: President of Austria since 2017. Van der Bellen has described himself as a centrist liberal, and supports green and social liberal policies.

In 1806, fearing Napoleon's growing power after the Confederation of the Rhine formed, Prussia joined Russia, Saxony, Sweden and Britain in a fresh multinational stand against the French Empire — which conflict?
War of the Fourth Coalition: 1806–1807 conflict of the Napoleonic Wars.

Fought alongside a wider Georgian civil conflict, this early-1990s fight pitted government forces against separatists backed by North Caucasian militants, Cossacks, and the Russian military — which conflict?
War in Abkhazia (1992–1993): Conflict between Georgia and Abkhaz separatists.
This Bolshevik revolutionary served as premier of both Russia and the Soviet Union in the 1920s before becoming one of the accused in Stalin's Great Purge show trials — who is he?
Alexei Rykov: Premier of the Soviet Union from 1924 to 1930.
This British MP represented Reigate for 27 years, chaired the Foreign Affairs Select Committee, and was reselected by a 5-to-1 vote after coming out publicly as gay in 2013 — who is he?

Medically retired from the Marines, this Medal of Honor recipient earned the nation's highest military honor for actions in Afghanistan's Helmand Province in 2010, making him the youngest living recipient — who is he?
A leading figure in Italy's national-conservative Brothers of Italy party, this politician has served as Minister of Agriculture since October 2022 and is a close ally of Giorgia Meloni — who is he?
Founder and chairman of the world's largest express transportation company, this American business magnate stepped down as CEO in 2022 after building a $5.3 billion fortune — who is he?
Frederick W. Smith: American business magnate (1944–2025)
Serving first as Albania's youngest-ever prime minister at 27, then president, then finally crowning himself monarch in 1928, this statesman ruled the country until 1939 — who was he?
Zog I: Leader of Albania from 1922 to 1939.
After two terms as governor of Maranhão, this Brazilian jurist served as President Lula's Minister of Justice before joining the Supreme Court — who is he?
Flávio Dino (born 30 April 1968) is a Brazilian attorney, Supreme Court Justice, politician and professor.
Dubbed a 'warrior Pharaoh,' this Twentieth Dynasty ruler is credited with defeating the invading 'Sea Peoples' and slowing Egypt's decline — who is he?
Ramesses III: Pharaoh of Egypt from 1186 to 1155 BC.
Canada's tenth deputy prime minister, she negotiated the USMCA trade deal with the United States and Mexico while serving as foreign affairs minister — who is she?
Chrystia Freeland: Canadian politician and journalist (born 1968)
This unofficial coalition of countries officially allied with the United States during the Cold War stood in opposition to the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact — what was this group called?
Western Bloc: Group of states aligned with the United States during the Cold War. The name "Western Bloc" emerged in response to and as the antithesis of its communist counterpart, the Eastern Bloc.
Founder of the agrarian movement AGROunia, this politician served as Poland's deputy minister of agriculture from 2023 to 2025 — who is he?
Michał Kołodziejczak: Polish politician. Michał Kołodziejczak (born 14 September 1988) is a Polish politician and founder of AGROunia.

During the Congo Crisis in 1961, a company of Irish UN peacekeepers was surrounded for five days by Katangese forces near a mining town before surrendering for lack of ammunition and water — which battle is this?
Siege of Jadotville: 1961 battle between Irish UN troops and Katanga during Congo Crisis.
This Indian politician, who leads the Andhra Pradesh unit of the Congress party, is the daughter of a former chief minister and younger sister of another prominent state politician — who is she?
A KGB colonel who secretly fed intelligence to MI6 for over a decade, this double agent was smuggled out of the Soviet Union in 1985 under the code name Operation Pimlico — who is he?
