Oleg Gordievsky: KGB colonel and double agent (1938–2025)
Active from 1973 to 1975, this American far-left militant group kidnapped newspaper heiress Patty Hearst and had six members die in a 1974 Los Angeles shootout with police — which group?
Symbionese Liberation Army: American militant organization (1973–1975). The three surviving fugitives recruited new members, but nearly all of them were apprehended in 1975 and prosecuted.
Serving as Prime Minister of Palestine from 2019 to 2024, this Fatah Central Committee member once headed a $1.6 billion investment fund called PECDAR — who is he?
Mohammad Shtayyeh: Palestinian politician, academic and economist (born 1958)
An American civil servant, diplomat and artist, he's remembered chiefly as the husband of a celebrated TV chef and cookbook author — who is he?
Fill in the blank: “____ (September 12, 1995 - July 12, 2014) was an American marine salvage captain who died by suicide at age 18.”

Death of Conrad Roy (September 12, 1995 - July 12, 2014) was an American marine salvage captain who died by suicide at age 18. Roy had seen numerous mental health professionals and had been prescribed psychiatric medication.
Trained as a philosopher before entering politics in 1874, this British PM later served as foreign secretary under Lloyd George after opposing Irish Home Rule — who is he?
Serving as Spain's prime minister from 1996 to 2004, this conservative leader survived a 1995 assassination attempt by the Basque separatist group ETA — who is he?
José María Aznar: Prime Minister of Spain from 1996 to 2004. Aznar attempted to negotiate with ETA between 1998 and 1999, but the parties did not reach an agreement and violence continued.
Founded in 1933 by the son of a former Spanish dictator, this fascist and national syndicalist movement merged with a rival group the following year to form FE de las JONS — which organization?
Falange Española: Spanish political organization. The Falange Española held its first rally in the Teatro de la Comedia in Madrid on October 29, 1933.

This Mexican politician served as mayor of Mexico City from 2006 to 2012, where he launched the Ecobici bike-share system, before later becoming the country's secretary of foreign affairs — who is he?
Backed by the Colorado Party after a 1954 coup, this general ruled Paraguay as its dictator for 35 years until his 1989 overthrow — who is he?
Alfredo Stroessner: Dictator of Paraguay from 1954 to 1989. Stroessner rose to power after leading the 1954 coup d'état on 4 May, with backing from the Colorado Party, and the Paraguayan Army.
The eldest son of a US president, this brigadier general received the Medal of Honor for directing troops at Utah Beach during the Normandy landings — who is he?
Theodore Roosevelt Jr.: American general and politician (1887–1944)
Known for the slogan 'Socialism with a human face,' this Slovak statesman led Czechoslovakia's brief liberalization known as the Prague Spring before Warsaw Pact tanks rolled in — who is he?
Alexander Dubček: Leader of Czechoslovakia from 1968 to 1969.
This Argentine general seized the presidency by ousting his predecessor in 1981, backed the Contras in Nicaragua, and continued the military junta's 'Dirty War' — who is he?
Leopoldo Galtieri: Argentine general and military ruler (1926–2003)

Formed in 1946 by former supporters of Benito Mussolini's Republican Fascist Party, which political party became postwar Italy's fourth-largest by the early 1960s while presenting itself as the defender of fascism's legacy?
Italian Social Movement: Neo-fascist political party, 1946–1955.
In 2015 this Spanish activist became the first woman elected mayor of Barcelona, having earlier co-founded a platform helping families fight foreclosure after the 2008 financial crisis — who is she?
Ada Colau (born 3 March 1974) is a Spanish activist and politician who was Mayor of Barcelona between 2015 and 2023.

Fought on June 17, 1775, during the Siege of Boston, this was the first major armed engagement of the American Revolutionary War, sparked when 1,200 colonial troops under William Prescott fortified high ground overnight — what was it?

Battle of Bunker Hill was fought on June 17, 1775, during the Siege of Boston in the first stage of the American Revolutionary War. The battle is named after Bunker Hill in Charlestown, Massachusetts, which was peripherally involved.
Leading a 'joyous religion' freedom movement from a base in Azerbaijan, this Iranian rebel fought the Abbasid Caliphate for over two decades before being betrayed and killed in 838 — who was he?
After voting against Russia's 2014 annexation of Crimea, this State Duma member was later charged with embezzlement, impeached, and went into exile in Ukraine — who is he?

Sparked by the assassination of India's prime minister at the hands of her own bodyguards, this wave of organized violence killed thousands nationwide after a military raid on a Punjab temple complex — what was it?
1984 anti-Sikh riots: Series of organised pogroms in India.
The son of Ivan III and Sophia Paleologue, this Grand Prince of Moscow annexed Pskov and Ryazan and captured Smolensk from Lithuania during his reign from 1505 to 1533 — who was he?
Vasili III of Russia: Grand Prince of Moscow from 1505 to 1533.
The first Mizrahi Jew elected to Israel's presidency, this former head of state resigned in 2007 amid scandal and later became the only former Israeli president convicted of a crime — who is he?
Moshe Katsav: President of Israel from 2000 to 2007.
Appointed by Emmanuel Macron in September 2025 after the previous government fell to a no-confidence vote, this politician had previously served as France's minister of the armed forces — who is he?
Sébastien Lecornu: Prime Minister of France since 2025.

Nicknamed 'Nene,' this 19th-century noblewoman married the Hereditary Prince of Thurn and Taxis in 1858 and ran the principality herself after his death from kidney disease, until their son came of age — who was she?
Duchess Helene in Bavaria: Hereditary Princess of Thurn and Taxis (1834–1890)
One of the four major tribes of ancient Greece, this group encompassed both the art-loving traders of Corinth and the isolationist warrior-state of Sparta — who were they?

Born from the coup of 18 Brumaire in 1799 and ending with the start of an empire in 1804, this government put Napoleon Bonaparte in charge as an authoritarian head of a still-nominal republic — what was it called?
French Consulate: Government of France from 1799 to 1804.

A trained physician, this politician became Norway's first female prime minister in 1981, later led the World Health Organization, and chaired the UN commission that popularized the term 'sustainable development.' Who is she?

This American fantasy author sold more than 90 million copies of his 14-book epic saga, having earlier in his career written tie-in novels featuring a sword-and-sorcery barbarian created by another writer. Who is he?

This short-lived 1990s state in the Balkans seceded from a disintegrating Yugoslavia in 1992, triggering a three-year war as rival Serb and Croat factions carved out their own unrecognized quasi-states — what state?
Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina: Balkan country (1992–1995)
Fill in the blank: “____ (born March 7, 1963) is a Canadian serial rapist, murderer and disgraced former colonel in the Royal Canadian Air Force.”

Russell Williams (criminal) (born March 7, 1963) is a Canadian serial rapist, murderer and disgraced former colonel in the Royal Canadian Air Force. Williams was born in Bromsgrove, Worcestershire, England and his family later emigrated to Canada.
Born Warren Wilhelm Jr., this Democratic politician served as New York City's public advocate before becoming its 110th mayor and describing economic inequality as a 'tale of two cities' — who is he?
Bill de Blasio: Mayor of New York City from 2014 to 2021.
This Weimar-era German chancellor and foreign minister shared the 1926 Nobel Peace Prize with Aristide Briand for reconciling Germany and France — who was he?
Gustav Stresemann: Chancellor of Germany in 1923. After obtaining his doctorate, Stresemann worked in trade associations before entering politics.
Having previously served as Japan's Foreign Minister and Chief Cabinet Secretary, which LDP politician became Minister for Internal Affairs and Communications in October 2025?
Led chiefly by Vladimir Lenin and aimed at seizing power to establish a dictatorship of the proletariat, which early-20th-century Russian revolutionary movement gave rise to the Soviet state?
Also known by the English name Ivan, this Taiwanese civil and transportation engineer joined the Legislative Yuan in December 2024 — who is he?
Wang Yi-chuan: Taiwanese politician and engineer (born 1972)
Before serving as the 51st speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives, this Illinois congressman spent 16 years teaching high school and coaching wrestling — who is he?
Also known as Hipponous, this Greek hero tamed the winged horse Pegasus and slew the fire-breathing Chimera — who is he?
Also known as 45,X, which chromosomal condition affects only females who are born with a single X chromosome instead of two, often causing short stature and a webbed neck?
Turner syndrome: X chromosome monosomy. Small chin (micrognathia), loose folds of skin on the neck, slanted eyelids and prominent ears are found in Turner syndrome, though not all will show it.

Synthesized by the liver in response to inflammation, this ring-shaped blood molecule binds to the surface of dead or dying cells to activate the immune system's complement cascade. What is it commonly called?
C-reactive protein (CRP) is an annular (ring-shaped) pentameric protein found in blood plasma, whose circulating concentration rises in response to inflammation.
Nicknamed 'Superman syndrome,' this genetic condition gives males an extra Y chromosome, often extra height but usually normal fertility — which one?
XYY syndrome: Genetic condition in which a male has an extra Y chromosome.
This common name describes small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs, especially popular in the UK and Commonwealth nations for larger swimming decapods — what is it?
Prawn: Common name applied to some types of crustaceans.
First described by J. D. Hooker in 1889 and nicknamed the Transvaal or Barberton daisy for its South African origins, what genus of flowering plant is this?
Gerbera: Genus of plants. Gerbera ( JUR-bər-ə or GUR-bər-ə) L. is a genus of plants in the Asteraceae (Compositae) family.
Defined as exactly 101,325 pascals and roughly equal to Earth's average sea-level air pressure, what is this reference unit of pressure called?
Standard atmosphere (unit) (symbol: atm) is a unit of pressure defined as 101325 Pa.
Predicted by Mendeleev decades before its discovery and sitting in the periodic table between manganese and rhenium, what is the lightest element whose isotopes are all radioactive?
Technetium: Chemical element with atomic number 43 (Tc)
Found in the rainforests and savannas of sub-Saharan Africa, this snake has the longest fangs of any venomous species — up to two inches — and the highest venom yield of any snake — which snake?
Gaboon viper: Species of snake. It is the largest member of the genus Bitis.

This branch of metabolism breaks down large molecules such as proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids into smaller units, releasing energy as cells convert the leftovers into waste like carbon dioxide and urea — what's it called?
Catabolism: Set of metabolic pathways that breaks down molecules into smaller units.
Popular as companion birds despite conservation concerns for several species, these large, long-tailed, brightly colored New World parrots belong to the tribe Arini — what are they?
Macaw: Group of birds in the parrot family.

This mammal family includes true digging specialists as well as aquatic desmans and the water-and-tunnel-adept star-nosed species, absent from Ireland but found from Eurasia to as far south as tropical Southeast Asian mountains — which family?
Talpidae: Family of small insectivorous mammals.
Nocturnal and tree-dwelling, this lizard species is native to Asia and various Pacific Islands — which reptile is it?
Tokay gecko: Species of reptile. The tokay gecko (Gekko gecko) is a nocturnal arboreal gecko in the genus Gekko, the true geckos.

In probability theory, this mathematical concept models a family of random variables indexed often by time, used to describe things like bacterial growth or a gas molecule's erratic path — what is it called?
Stochastic process: Collection of random variables. Stochastic processes are widely used as mathematical models of systems and phenomena that appear to vary in a random manner.
Pig-shaped with a short, flexible snout, this odd-toed ungulate mammal lives in the jungles of South and Central America and Southeast Asia, alongside equine and rhino relatives — which animal?
Working alongside longtime colleague Ken Thompson, this American computer scientist co-created the Unix operating system and the C programming language — who is he?
Dennis Ritchie: American computer scientist known for Unix (1941–2011)
Nicknamed a 'truth serum' in popular culture despite dubious real-world reliability, this fast-acting barbiturate anesthetic is marketed under the brand name Pentothal — which drug?
Sodium thiopental: Barbiturate general anesthetic. It is the thiobarbiturate analog of pentobarbital, and an analog of thiobarbital.
Though often mistaken for a true antelope, this hoofed North American mammal is actually the last living member of its own family, and its closest relatives are the giraffe and okapi — which animal?

Pronghorn: Species of North American hoofed mammal. The pronghorn (UK:, US:) (Antilocapra americana) is a species of artiodactyl (even-toed, hoofed) mammal indigenous to interior western and central North America.
Passed only from fathers to sons, this genetic structure carries the SRY gene that typically triggers development of male gonads in mammals — what is it?
Y chromosome is one of two sex chromosomes in therian mammals and other organisms.
Prized wood from this fruit tree's genus, Pyrus, is a favorite material for making high-quality woodwind instruments, and China grows about three-quarters of the world's crop — which fruit?
Pear: Edible fruits from the genus Pyrus.
This bird group's rock-dove species gave rise to most domesticated pigeon breeds, including racing and fantail pigeons, and was later introduced to the Americas — which classification is it?
Columba (genus) comprises a genus of medium to large pigeons.
Nicknamed the 'maker of modern Mysore,' this Indian civil engineer and statesman's birthday is now celebrated as Engineer's Day across India, Sri Lanka, and Tanzania — who is he?
M. Visvesvaraya: Indian civil engineer, administrator, and former prime minister of Mysore Kingdom.
Also known as all-trans retinoic acid, this medication treats acne as a topical cream but must be taken orally for leukemia patients with a specific gene fusion — what is it?
Tretinoin: Medication. Tretinoin, also known as all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), is a medication used for the treatment of acne and acute promyelocytic leukemia.
This genus of venomous elapid snakes across Africa and Asia is home to the 'true cobras' — after a 2009 taxonomic revision folded in two other genera, it now contains 38 species — which genus?
Naja: Genus of snakes. Until recently, the genus Naja had 20 to 22 species, but it has undergone several taxonomic revisions in recent years, so sources vary greatly.

The only birds whose first two neck vertebrae are fused together, these Old World birds have a long down-curved bill sometimes topped with a bony casque, and share an ecological niche with toucans in the Americas — which birds?
Hornbill: Family of birds. The family is omnivorous, feeding on fruit and small animals.
Named for antennae often longer than its own body, this insect family boasts over 35,000 species and gets its name from a Greek myth about a shepherd transformed after angering nymphs — which group?
Longhorn beetle (Cerambycidae), also known as long-horned or longicorns (whose larvae are often referred to as roundheaded borers), are a large family of beetles, with over 35,000 species described.
Nicknamed 'murderer's thumb' or 'stubbed thumb,' this genetic trait gives about 2% of people a short, rounded thumb linked to the HOXD13 gene — what is it?
Brachydactyly type D: Abnormal shortening of the distal part of the thumb.
Also called the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon or Red Car Theory, this cognitive bias makes you notice something everywhere right after you first learn about it — what is it?
Frequency illusion: Kind of cognitive bias. The name "Baader–Meinhof phenomenon" was coined in 1994 by Terry Mullen in a letter to the St.
Comprising cicadas, aphids, bed bugs, and more than 80,000 other species with piercing-sucking mouthparts, which insect order is nicknamed the 'true bugs'?
Hemiptera: Order of insects often called true bugs.
With an eagle-like body perched on crane-like legs and a bare red-orange face, which African bird of prey spends most of its time hunting on foot across the savanna?
Secretarybird: Bird of prey. The secretarybird or secretary bird (Sagittarius serpentarius) is a large bird of prey that is endemic to Africa.
Developed from the civilian DC-3 airliner and nicknamed 'Dakota' by the RAF, which WWII transport plane hauled troops, cargo, and paratroopers for roughly 100 countries' militaries?
Douglas C-47 Skytrain: Military transport aircraft derived from DC-3.
Despite centuries of use in Korean and Chinese traditional medicine, no clinical evidence supports health claims for this Panax-genus root, often sold as a dietary supplement — what is it?
Ginseng: Root of a plant used in herbal preparations.
Named the type genus of the walnut family, this group of deciduous trees produces the walnuts eaten worldwide, with China responsible for half the global supply — which genus?
Juglans: Genus of trees. Walnut trees are any species of tree in the plant genus Juglans, the type genus of the family Juglandaceae, the seeds of which are referred to as walnuts.

This genus of roughly 60 herbaceous perennials in the buckwheat family includes the familiar pie vegetable prized for its tart stalks despite mildly toxic leaves — which genus, native to Europe and Asia?
Rheum (plant) is a genus of about 60 herbaceous perennial plants in the family Polygonaceae.

Flown by the Royal Air Force's Red Arrows display team, this British jet-powered advanced trainer has been license-built in India by Hindustan Aeronautics, with over 1,000 sold to 18 countries — which aircraft?
BAE Systems Hawk: Military training aircraft family.
This Israeli-American physician turned billionaire donor owns the Las Vegas Review-Journal and Dallas Mavericks, and was one of Donald Trump's largest financial backers — who is she?

Miriam Adelson: Israeli-American physician, billionaire, and conservative donor. Miriam Adelson (née Farbstein; born October 10, 1945) is an Israeli-American physician, businesswoman, philanthropist, and conservative political donor.
Born in 1929 and died in 2001, this man was a respected Saudi Islamic scholar — who is he?
This functional group, formed by replacing a carboxylic acid's hydroxyl with an amino group, creates the peptide bonds that link amino acids into proteins — what is it?
Amide: Organic compounds of the form RC(=O)NR′R″.
This subfamily of cats, distinguished by a bony hyoid that lets its members purr instead of roar, is informally known as the small cats — which subfamily?
Felinae: Subfamily of Felidae. The Felinae or small cats are a subfamily of the Felidae distinguished by a bony hyoid, because of which they can purr but not roar.
Native to Mexico and Guatemala, this mint-family plant is prized for its hydrophilic seeds known as chia — what's its scientific name?
Salvia hispanica: Species of flowering plant in the mint family.

The first of the Century Series jet fighters, this supersonic aircraft was the U.S. Air Force's first fighter capable of level supersonic flight, first taking to the air in May 1953, seven months ahead of schedule — which jet?

North American F-100 Super Sabre: 1953 fighter aircraft family. The North American F-100 Super Sabre is an American supersonic jet fighter aircraft designed and produced by the aircraft manufacturer North American Aviation.
This hairy biennial plant can top two meters, packing small yellow flowers onto a tall spike that sprouts from a low leaf rosette in disturbed, sunlit soil — which weedy species?
Verbascum thapsus: Species of plant. It is a hairy biennial plant that can grow to 2 m tall or more.
Found naturally in grapes and other fruits, this crystalline compound's potassium salt is better known as cream of tartar, a key ingredient in homemade baking powder — which compound?
Tartaric acid is a white, crystalline organic acid that occurs naturally in many fruits, most notably in grapes but also in tamarinds, bananas, avocados, and citrus.

First described by Linnaeus in 1767, this citrus-family plant native to the Indian subcontinent has aromatic leaves essential to South Asian cooking, especially in India and Sri Lanka — which species?

Curry tree: Species of flowering plant. It is native to the Indian subcontinent, southern China and mainland Southeast Asia, and it has been introduced to other parts of southeast Asia and to Australia.
Around 2,500 species of this insect family defend themselves by secreting a skin-irritating toxin called cantharidin, often flaunting bold warning colors — which family?
Blister beetle are beetles of the family Meloidae, so called for their defensive secretion of a blistering agent, cantharidin.

This German banker headed the Reichsbank in both the Weimar Republic and the early Nazi era, and helped persuade Hindenburg to appoint Hitler's first government despite later opposing some rearmament policies — who is he?
Hjalmar Schacht: German politician, banker, and economist (1877–1970)

Ranging from the hefty black species of the Amazon basin to the diminutive dwarf species just over a metre long, these Central and South American relatives of alligators make up their own reptile subfamily — what are they called?
Caiman: Subfamily of reptiles. The black caiman is the largest caiman species in the world and is found in the slow-moving rivers and lakes that surround the Amazon basin.

Also known as the spectacled or binocellate snake, this reptile from South Asia is one of the 'Big Four' species responsible for most snakebites in the region and is revered in Hindu mythology — which snake?
Indian cobra: Species of snake. The species is native to the Indian subcontinent, and is a member of the "Big Four" species that are responsible for the most snakebite cases in Sri Lanka and India.
Discovered in 1861 via flame spectroscopy by Bunsen and Kirchhoff, this alkali metal is named from the Latin word for 'deep red' — which element?
Rubidium: Chemical element with atomic number 37 (Rb)
This inflammatory condition causes recurring, painful mouth sores along with eye inflammation and arthritis, and is diagnosed after at least three sore outbreaks in a year — which condition?
Behçet's disease: Inflammatory disorder. Behçet's disease or Behçet's syndrome (BD; sometimes written Behcet) is a type of inflammatory disorder which affects multiple parts of the body.
Historically used in the 18th century to track down escaped slaves, this large Brazilian dog breed of mastiff type now also serves as a guard dog and companion — which breed?
Fila Brasileiro: Brazilian breed of dog. The Fila Brasileiro (Portuguese pronunciation: [ˈfilɐ bɾaziˈlejɾu]) is a Brazilian breed of large working dog of mastiff type.
Derived from the design of the Vought F-8 Crusader, this subsonic carrier-based light attack aircraft replaced the Douglas Skyhawk and saw extensive action in the Vietnam War — which aircraft?
LTV A-7 Corsair II: American attack aircraft family.
A perennial herb from the mountains of East Asia, its root is the original source of a famous herbal supplement — though studies find little evidence it actually works. Which plant?
Panax ginseng: Species of flowering plant.
This Timurid sultan who ruled Samarkand spoke five languages and built a great 15th-century observatory there between 1424 and 1429 — who is he?
Ulugh Beg: Timurid sultan, astronomer and mathematician (1394–1449)
Also called gobō, this Eurasian plant is cultivated in Japan for its edible root but has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils elsewhere — which species?
Arctium lappa: Species of flowering plant. It has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils in North America, Australia, and other regions, but is cultivated for its vegetable root.

Developed in 1962 by an American pharmaceutical company and derived from a natural male hormone, this anabolic steroid treats hereditary angioedema and is unusual for surviving liver metabolism without being esterified — what is it?
Stanozolol: Discontinued steroid for heart treatment.
Powered by a Rolls-Royce Avon turbojet and featuring swept wings, this 1950s RAF fighter set a world air speed record of over 727 mph in September 1953 — which aircraft?
Hawker Hunter: 1950s family of British fighter aircraft.
Born to a Sephardic Jewish stockbroker's family, this classical economist eloped with a Quaker at 21, made a fortune financing government debt, and later bought a seat in Parliament — who is he?
David Ricardo: British economist and politician (1772–1823)
Nicknamed the pudding-pipe tree, this Fabaceae-family plant is the national tree of Thailand and doubles as the state flower of Kerala and Delhi — which species?

Cassia fistula: Species of flowering plant. Cassia fistula, also known as golden shower, purging cassia, Indian laburnum, kani konna, or pudding-pipe tree, is a flowering plant in the family Fabaceae.
Native to North America but now invasive across Europe after being introduced, this semiaquatic mustelid preys on rodents, fish, and frogs — which animal?
American mink: Semiaquatic species of mustelid. Because of range expansion, the American mink is classed as a least-concern species by the IUCN.
Marketed as Zinacef and used against everything from meningitis to Lyme disease, this second-generation cephalosporin antibiotic was patented in 1971 — which drug?
Cefuroxime: Antibiotic medication. It is used by mouth or by injection into a vein or muscle.
Known as sampaguita in the Philippines, where it's the national flower, this fragrant vine or shrub also lends its blossoms to a beloved variety of tea — which species?
Jasminum sambac: Species of jasmine. Jasminum sambac (Arabian jasmine or Sambac jasmine or Mogra) is a species of jasmine native to Bhutan and India.
This German engineer invented a fuel-efficient combustion engine so influential that both it and the fuel it burns bear his name — who was he?
Rudolf Diesel: German inventor and engineer (1858–1913)
Originating in French cuisine and beloved in Spain, this breaded, deep-fried roll often reuses leftover roasted chicken or broth meat as its filling — what is it called?
Dubbed 'the Gauss of modern mathematics,' this French polymath's work on the three-body problem uncovered the first chaotic deterministic system, laying the groundwork for chaos theory — who is he?
Henri Poincaré: French mathematician, physicist and engineer (1854–1912)
Native to the Americas, this plant is better known by its common names common ragweed, annual ragweed, or low ragweed — what is its scientific name?
Ambrosia artemisiifolia: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family.

Best known for the Cities of Salt quintet chronicling how oil discovery upended traditional Bedouin life, this novelist's criticism of Middle Eastern elites led Saudi Arabia to revoke his citizenship — who is he?
Structurally related to a calming brain chemical and acting like baclofen or GHB on the same receptor, this anxiety medication can also give a mild dopamine-driven lift at low doses — what is it?

Serving as royal executioner under Louis XVI and later chief executioner of the First Republic, this Frenchman carried out nearly 3,000 executions during his 40-year career, including those of the king, queen, and Robespierre — who is he?

Dropped from a B-52 and boosted by a modified Pegasus rocket stage before its own scramjet took over, this experimental hypersonic craft still holds the record for fastest jet-powered flight at about Mach 9.6 — what is it?
NASA X-43: Unmanned US experimental hypersonic aircraft, 1991-2000.
Native to South America but planted worldwide for its long-lasting violet blooms, this tree — also called the black poui — is listed as Vulnerable in its wild range by the IUCN. What is it?
Jacaranda mimosifolia: Species of sub-tropical tree.
This British Egyptologist discovered the untouched tomb of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings in November 1922 — who is he?
Howard Carter: British archaeologist and Egyptologist (1874–1939)
Appointed FBI director by Barack Obama in 2013, this former federal prosecutor was fired from the post in 2017 — who is he?
Named after the Greek word for 'hedgehog' because of its spiky central disk, this North American daisy relative is nicknamed the coneflower — what is it?
Echinacea: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family.
Usually diagnosed in infancy, this rare genetic disorder caused by a mutation in the SMN1 gene is the leading inherited cause of death in babies if left untreated — what condition is it?
Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a rare neuromuscular disorder that results in the loss of motor neurons and progressive muscle wasting.
Native to tropical Southeast Asia, this small tree bears bell-shaped rose-to-purple flowers and a ridged fruit that forms star-shaped slices when cut crosswise — which species?
Averrhoa carambola: Species of tree. It is a small tree or shrub that grows 5 to 12 m (16 to 39 ft) tall, with rose to red-purple flowers.
Caused by a mutation in the ATP7B gene, this inherited condition lets copper build up in the liver and brain, leading to tremors, personality changes, and yellowing skin — which condition?
Wilson's disease (also called hepatolenticular degeneration) is a genetic disorder characterized by the excess build-up of copper in the body.
Nicknamed 'mother-in-law's tongue' and 'snake plant,' this genus of stiff, sword-leaved succulents from Africa and southern Asia is now classified within Dracaena — which genus?
Traceable to fairy tales that weren't classified this way until the seventeenth century, this genre spans picture books for toddlers to young-adult fiction for teens — what category of writing?
Children's literature: Stories, books, magazines, and poems primarily written for children.
Named after a German physical chemist, this electrochemistry formula calculates a reaction's reduction potential from temperature, electron count, and reactant concentrations — which relationship?
Nernst equation: Physical law in electrochemistry.

Caused by a lack of intrinsic factor — often from an autoimmune attack on the stomach — this vitamin B12 deficiency disorder brings gradual fatigue, a smooth red tongue, and numbness in the hands and feet — which condition?
Pernicious anemia: Lack of red blood cells due to vitamin B12 deficiency.

Also known by names meaning 'water spinach' and 'kangkung,' this semi-aquatic tropical vegetable was likely first domesticated in Southeast Asia and thrives with barely any care near waterways — which plant is it?
Ipomoea aquatica: Species of plant. Ipomoea aquatica, commonly known as water spinach or kangkung, is a semi-aquatic, tropical plant grown as a vegetable for its tender shoots.

Numbering more than 9,000 species, these tiny hexapods are no longer classified as true insects and get their scientific class name from Greek words meaning 'glue' and 'peg,' after a structure called the collophore — what are they called?
Once down to just 94 individuals in Andalusia by 2002, largely due to a crash in its rabbit prey from myxomatosis, this medium-sized wild cat is endemic to a European peninsula — which species?
Iberian lynx: Species of mammal. The Iberian lynx (Lynx pardinus) is one of four extant species of Lynx, a genus of medium-sized wild cats.
Known online by the alias 'brokep,' this Swedish-born entrepreneur co-founded a famous BitTorrent search engine before launching the privacy-focused registrar Njalla in 2017 — who is he?
Peter Sunde: Swedish entrepreneur and politician. Peter Sunde Kolmisoppi (born 13 September 1978), alias brokep, is a Swedish-born Finnish-Norwegian entrepreneur and politician.
With the formula CaC2, this industrial compound reacts with trace moisture to give off a garlicky smell and is used to generate acetylene gas in old-fashioned lamps — what is it?
Calcium carbide: Chemical compound. Its main use industrially is in the production of acetylene and calcium cyanamide.

Named after the bones that house them — frontal, maxillary, ethmoid, and sphenoid — these four paired air-filled spaces surround the nasal cavity and have a still-debated evolutionary purpose — what are they called?
Paranasal sinuses: Air-filled spaces surrounding the nasal cavity.
Native to tropical Southeast Asia, this bumpy-skinned citrus fruit is prized in regional cooking for its intensely fragrant leaves and rind, and its oil is used in perfumery — which fruit?
Kaffir lime: Citrus fruit native to tropical Southeast Asia. Citrus hystrix, called the kaffir lime, Thai lime or makrut lime, (US:, UK:) is a citrus fruit native to tropical Southeast Asia.
Named from the Greek word for tallow, this soft waxy 18-carbon saturated fatty compound is common in animal fats like beef tallow and lard — what is it called?
Stearic acid (stee-) is a saturated fatty acid with an 18-carbon chain.
Also nicknamed the reed or swamp feline, this solitary wild predator ranges from the Caucasus to Southeast Asia and marks territory by urine spraying — which species?

This general term covers any organ that secretes substances either straight into the bloodstream, like endocrine ones, or through a duct to a body surface, like exocrine ones — what type of structure is it?
Gland: Type of animal organ. A gland may also function to remove unwanted substances such as urine from the body.

While still a teenager, this French mathematician solved a 350-year-old problem about which polynomials can be solved by radicals, laying the groundwork for group theory, before dying from wounds suffered in a duel — who was he?
Marketed under the brand name Plaquenil, this oral medication treats malaria as well as rheumatoid arthritis and lupus, though it can cause retinopathy with long-term use — what drug is it?
Hydroxychloroquine: Antimalarial medication. It is taken by mouth, often in the form of hydroxychloroquine sulfate.
Also called pseudocoma, this condition leaves a fully conscious patient paralyzed except for blinking and vertical eye movement, coined by two neurologists in 1966 — what is it called?
Locked-in syndrome: Condition in which a patient is aware but completely paralysed.

Founder of the quant hedge fund Renaissance Technologies, this mathematician-turned-investor co-developed a differential-geometry concept still used in string theory, and ran the legendary Medallion Fund — who is he?
Jim Simons: American mathematician and billionaire (1938–2024)

Found in Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, and northeastern Australia, this large flightless black bird is a close ratite relative of the emu and ostrich, and its Australian population is listed as endangered — which bird?
Southern cassowary: Species of flightless bird. It is one of the three living species of cassowary, alongside the dwarf cassowary and the northern cassowary.
This inherited birth defect from a RUNX2 gene mutation leaves the collarbones underdeveloped or missing, letting the shoulders touch in front of the chest — which condition?
Cleidocranial dysostosis: Birth defect of the collarbones, skull, and teeth.
Fill in the blank: “____ (April 21, 1971 - September 30, 2011) was an American-Yemeni Islamic cleric and lecturer.”

Anwar al-Awlaki (April 21, 1971 - September 30, 2011) was an American-Yemeni Islamic cleric and lecturer. Al-Awlaki was the first U.S. citizen to be targeted and assassinated by a U.S. government drone strike.
Secreted by small neck glands when blood calcium runs low, this peptide messenger raises calcium levels and boosts active vitamin D production — which one?
Parathyroid hormone: Mammalian protein found in humans.
Around 20 millimetres long with a shimmering structural-green shell and a coppery underside, this beetle is identified by its isosceles-triangle scutellum — which species?
Cetonia aurata: Species of beetle. The scutellum is the small V-shaped area between the wing cases; it may show several small, irregular, white lines and marks.

Built for the Marine Corps by adding a third engine and a seventh main rotor blade to an earlier heavy-lift helicopter, this aircraft entered service in 1981 and flies from Navy ships — which helicopter?
Sikorsky CH-53E Super Stallion is a heavy lift helicopter operated by the United States military.
Patented in 1967, this sympathomimetic drug helps people with asthma and other breathing disorders by acting as a bronchodilator — which substance?
Clenbuterol: Chemical compound which aids breathing.
From a startled jump to a cat automatically reorienting itself mid-fall, this involuntary, split-second reaction runs through the nervous system without needing conscious thought — what's it called?
Reflex: Automatic, involuntary response to a stimulus.
The only species in its genus, this cosmopolitan pelagic fish from the mackerel family can grow past a metre long and matters hugely to global fisheries — which species?
Skipjack tuna: Species of fish. The skipjack tuna (Katsuwonus pelamis) is a perciform fish in the tuna family, Scombridae, and is the only member of the genus Katsuwonus.

Originally built at a Boston hospital to manage patient records, this programming language pairs directly with an integrated key-value database and now underpins Epic's electronic health records — which language?
MUMPS: Programming language. It was originally developed at Massachusetts General Hospital for managing patient medical records and hospital laboratory information systems.
Nicknamed creeping charlie and alehoof, this aromatic mint-family creeper is eaten as a salad green in some countries but reviled as an invasive lawn weed in North America — what plant is it?
Glechoma hederacea: Species of plant in the mint family. It is commonly known as ground-ivy, gill-over-the-ground, creeping charlie, alehoof, tunhoof, catsfoot, field balm, and run-away-robin.
This inflammation of the sac surrounding the heart causes sharp chest pain that eases when sitting up and worsens when lying down or breathing deeply — what condition is it?
Pericarditis: Inflammation of the pericardium. Pericarditis (PER-i-kar-DYE-tis) is inflammation of the pericardium, the fibrous sac surrounding the heart.
In music theory, this concept for combining different pitches into chords and progressions has both a 'vertical' frequency dimension and a 'horizontal' time dimension — what is it called?
Harmony: Aspect of music. In music, harmony is the concept of combining different sounds in order to create new, distinct musical ideas.
This American astronomer proved that many so-called nebulae were actually separate galaxies, and in 1929 showed that galaxies recede faster the farther away they are — who is he?
On 18 March 1965, this Soviet cosmonaut became the first person to walk in space, spending over twelve minutes outside his capsule during a Voskhod mission — who is he?
Known historically as green vitriol or copperas, this blue-green heptahydrate salt is used to treat anemia and forms a paramagnetic octahedral complex in water — which compound?
Iron(II) sulfate: Chemical compound. Iron(II) sulfate or ferrous sulfate (British English: sulphate instead of sulfate) denotes a range of salts with the formula FeSO4·xH2O.
Biosynthesized in the body from the amino acid tyrosine, this compound is the direct precursor to dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine — what is it?
L-DOPA: Chemical compound. As is true for many molecules, the human body produces only one of these isomers (the l-DOPA form).

Named for the indigo-blue line seen in its spectrum when discovered in 1863, this soft, silvery-white metal with atomic number 49 is used to make the transparent conductive coating on flat-panel displays — what is it?
Indium: Chemical element with atomic number 49 (In)
Common in adolescents during growth spurts, this condition causes a painful bump just below the knee from inflammation where the patellar ligament attaches to the shinbone — what is it?

Osgood–Schlatter disease: Inflammation of the patellar ligament. Osgood–Schlatter disease (OSD) is inflammation of the patellar ligament at the tibial tuberosity (apophysitis) usually affecting adolescents during growth spurts.
Also known as the Burgundy snail and served as escargot, this large air-breathing land snail native to Europe has a globular brown shell — what species is it?

The only Allied jet aircraft to see combat in World War II, this British fighter entered service with No. 616 Squadron RAF in July 1944, powered by engines pioneered by Frank Whittle — which aircraft?
Gloster Meteor: Britain's first jet fighter, 1943–1980s.
Nicknamed 'no-see-ums' for their tiny 1-3mm size, these biting midges are also among the best-studied pollinators of cocoa plants — what is this fly family called?
Ceratopogonidae: Family of flies commonly known as no see ums, or biting midges.
Formed when two simple sugar molecules join via a glycosidic bond, sucrose, lactose, and maltose all belong to this class of 'double sugars' — what is it called?
Disaccharide: Complex sugar. A disaccharide (also called a double sugar or biose) is the sugar formed when two monosaccharides are joined by glycosidic linkage.
Developed in 1955 and later sold under the brand name Dianabol, this anabolic steroid was once widely used for physique and performance enhancement — what is it?
Metandienone: Androgen and anabolic steroid. It is also used non-medically for physique- and performance-enhancing purposes.
Designed in 1957 by a Soviet bureau and known to NATO as 'Coke,' this 50-seat twin-turboprop airliner is still license-built in China under a different name — which aircraft?
Antonov An-24: Soviet turboprop airplane. The aircraft was manufactured by the Kyiv, Irkutsk and Ulan-Ude Aviation Factories.
With more than 8,000 species known for their loud mating calls and leaf-like camouflage, this insect family also goes by the common name katydids or bush crickets — which family?
Tettigoniidae: Family of insects. Insects in the family Tettigoniidae are commonly called katydids (especially in North America) or bush crickets.
On January 26, 1926, this Scottish inventor gave the world's first demonstration of a working mechanical television system — who is he?
This inorganic salt, most commonly used as a soil fertilizer, is 21% nitrogen and 24% sulfur by content — what is it?

With arms and tentacles up to 26 feet long held at right angles to its body, this deep-sea cephalopod has been spotted as deep as 6,212 meters — the only one of its kind known to survive the hadal zone. What is it?
This spider's ghoulish nickname, the 'Nosferatu spider,' references a classic vampire — which species is it?
Zoropsis spinimana: Species of spider. Zoropsis spinimana, also known as Nosferatu spider, is a spider species belonging to the family Zoropsidae.

Commonly known as plantains or fleaworts — though unrelated to the banana-like cooking fruit of the same name — this genus of roughly 200 mostly herbaceous flowering plants tops out around 24 inches tall. Which genus?
Plantago: Genus of flowering plants. Plantago is a genus of about 200 species of flowering plants in the family Plantaginaceae, commonly called plantains or fleaworts.

Dubbed a 'living fossil' and commonly known as horsetail, this spore-reproducing plant genus once included 30-meter-tall trees in Carboniferous forests, its node-spacing pattern said to have inspired the invention of logarithms — which genus?
Also known in everyday speech as 'brain surgery,' this medical specialty treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and the entire nervous system — what is it called?
Neurosurgery: Medical specialty of disorders which affect any portion of the nervous system.
Too small to fuse hydrogen but massive enough to briefly burn deuterium, these objects between 13 and 80 Jupiter masses cool over time through spectral classes M, L, T, and Y — what are they called?

This polyatomic ion, CO3 with a 2- charge, is dissolved into water under pressure to make it fizzy, and also makes up much of the sedimentary rock in the Earth's crust — what's the ion (and salt) called?
Carbonate: Salt or ester of carbonic acid.

Cultivated for its edible nuts since prehistoric times and native to the Mediterranean and the Levant, this pine species has earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit — which species?
Pinus pinea: Species of pine tree. Pinus pinea, the Italian stone pine or Mediterranean stone pine, is a tree from the pine family, Pinaceae.
Discovered in 1885 by Carl Auer von Welsbach, this rare-earth element tarnishes quickly in air and produces pink, purple, and yellow compounds when oxidized — which element, atomic number 60?
Neodymium: Chemical element with atomic number 60 (Nd)
Dubbed 'the father of modern Kazakh history and ethnography,' this 19th-century scholar took part in the Great Game and has Kazakhstan's national science academy named in his honor — who is he?
Before becoming Ferrari's Formula One team principal in 2023, this Frenchman co-founded a junior-racing outfit that won back-to-back titles with Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg — who is he?
Named for its snake-like neck (its species epithet means 'snake'), this feisty freshwater reptile has powerful beak-like jaws and ranges from Nova Scotia down to Florida — which species is it?
Common snapping turtle (Chelydra serpentina) is a species of large, freshwater turtles in the family Chelydridae.
Nicknamed noni, this pungent-smelling fruit tree in the coffee family was spread across the Pacific by Polynesian sailors and is now used mainly in traditional medicine and juices — which plant?
Morinda citrifolia: Species of plant. It is commonly known as noni or Indian mulberry, among many other names.

Native to Europe, West Asia, and parts of North Africa, this widely introduced game fish is one of the world's worst invasive species outside its home range, with regional names like sewin in Wales and finnock in Scotland — which species is it?
Brown trout: Species of fish. Brown trout are highly adaptable and have evolved numerous ecotypes/subspecies.
This subfamily of horned, cloven-hooved ungulates includes cattle, bison, and both African and water buffalo, with the gaur as its largest living member — which group?
First identified in November 2002 and traced through civets to horseshoe bats in Yunnan, this viral respiratory disease had an 11% fatality rate before its outbreak ended in 2003 — which disease?

An anatomist and archaeologist turned TV presenter, she has served as professor of Public Engagement in Science at the University of Birmingham since 2012 and once led the charity Humanists UK — who is she?
Alice Roberts: English academic, TV presenter and author.
This Nigerian banking executive led one of the country's top five banks before dying in a 2024 helicopter crash while traveling to the Super Bowl — who was he?
Herbert Wigwe: Nigerian accountant and banker (1966–2024)
Ranging from Baja California to Japan's coast, this cephalopod is the largest of its kind on Earth and a common aquarium favorite — which creature?
Giant Pacific octopus: Species of cephalopod. It can be found from the intertidal zone down to 2,000 m (6,600 ft), and is best-adapted to colder, oxygen- and nutrient-rich waters.
Named for the genus of the Atlantic salmon, this family of cold-water fish also includes trout, char, and grayling — what family is it?

Born out of military planning before World War II, this branch of applied mathematics uses optimization and statistics to find the best possible outcome for real-world decisions — what field, sometimes called management science?
Operations research: Discipline concerning the application of advanced analytical methods.
Used to treat dangerous heart rhythms like ventricular fibrillation, which drug can take weeks to work when swallowed but carries risks of lung, liver, thyroid, and eye toxicity?
Starting as a metals trader after the Soviet Union's collapse, which Russian billionaire built the Sayanogorsk smelter into the world's largest aluminium company, Rusal?
This severe form of childhood protein malnutrition causes swelling and an enlarged, fatty liver, and is distinct from the calorie-deficient condition known as marasmus — what is it?
Kwashiorkor: Severe protein malnutrition. Kwashiorkor ( KWOSH-ee-OR-kor, -⁠kər) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.
Known on the street as flakka or gravel, this synthetic stimulant of the cathinone class was developed in the 1960s and later sold as a designer drug — what is it?
This medical term for a birthmark or mole covers marks present at birth as well as ones that appear later in life — what is it called?
Nevus: Mole or birthmark; visible, circumscribed, chronic skin lesion.
This colorless gas, made by swapping one hydrogen atom in ammonia for a methyl group, has a strong rotten-fish smell and serves as a building block for many compounds — what is it?
Struggling with a morphine addiction from a Civil War saber wound, this pharmacist and chemist developed a coca-and-caffeine beverage in 1886 that became Coca-Cola — who is he?
John Stith Pemberton: American pharmacist, inventor of Coca-Cola (1831–1888)
Part of the same species as cabbage and broccoli, this loose-leafed member of the 'kale group' has been grown for its big, dark-green leaves since classical antiquity — what is it?
Collard (plant) is a group of loose-leafed cultivars of Brassica oleracea (the same species as many common vegetables, including cabbage and broccoli).

Fill in the blank: “____ (PD) is a benign, acquired penile connective tissue disease characterized by the occurrence of fibrotic plaques within the tunica albuginea - the dense elastic covering of the corpora cavernosa.”

Peyronie's disease (PD) is a benign, acquired penile connective tissue disease characterized by the occurrence of fibrotic plaques within the tunica albuginea - the dense elastic covering of the corpora cavernosa. The plaques cause abnormal curvature, pain, penile deformities (e.g., narrowing or indentation), and usually erectile dysfunction, particularly during erection.

Nicknamed for their nighttime cries, these small nocturnal African primates are, according to the African Wildlife Foundation, the continent's most successful strepsirrhine group — what are they commonly called?
Galago: Family of primates. The Ghanaian name aposor is given to them because of their firm grip on branches.
This plant family — home to basil, rosemary, thyme, lavender, and sage — also counts teak among its rare tree species and chia among its edible seed crops — which family?

This term for 'parts in each thousand' is symbolized by ‰ — a percent sign with an extra zero — and sits right next to the percent sign in Unicode's General Punctuation block — what is this unit called?
Per mille: Unit for parts per thousand. The associated symbol is ‰, similar to a per cent sign % but with an extra zero in the divisor.

Nicknamed the 'Halloween beetle' in North America for invading homes each October to overwinter, this extremely color-variable insect was introduced there from eastern Asia to control aphids — what species is it?
Harmonia axyridis: Species of beetle. Harmonia axyridis is a lady beetle or ladybird species that is most commonly known as the harlequin, Asian, or multicoloured Asian lady beetle.
Native from Morocco and Portugal east to Iran, this flowering plant species includes thousands of varieties whose fruit is eaten fresh or dried into raisins and currants — what species is it?
Vitis vinifera: Species of flowering plant in the grape vine family.
This highly venomous snake in the Colubridae family, scientifically known as Dispholidus typus, is native to Sub-Saharan Africa — what is its common name?

Named after two French physicists who discovered it in 1820, this equation in magnetostatics relates a magnetic field to the strength, direction, and distance of an electric current — which physics rule?
Biot–Savart law: Law of classical electromagnetism.

Also called blepharoptosis and sometimes mistakenly called 'lazy eye,' this condition is marked by the drooping of the upper lid over the eye and can affect vision development in children if untreated — what is it?
Ptosis (eyelid) is a drooping or falling of the upper eyelid.
This soft, movable pair of appendages on the jaw helps with eating and speech, and is often used in kissing — what are they?
Lip: Visible body parts at the mouth.
Developed from a wide-body airliner and selected in 2011 to replace an aging fleet of aerial tankers, this refueling aircraft entered US Air Force service in 2019 — which aircraft?
Boeing KC-46 Pegasus: American military aerial refueling and transport aircraft.
Also known as Umbelliferae and including carrots, celery, parsley, and dill, this plant family also contains dangerously toxic members like poison hemlock and giant hogweed — which family?
Commonly known as barberry, this genus of deciduous and evergreen shrubs grows worldwide except Australia, and one of its species is Oregon's official state flower — what genus is it?
Berberis: Genus of flowering plants representing the barberry family.
Born in 1963, this woman is the daughter of the last Shah of Iran by his third wife — who is she?
Hardy enough to survive winters as cold as -43°C, this shrub genus's aggressive roots fight soil erosion, and its berries and leaves are turned into food and skincare products — which genus?
Hippophae: Genus of flowering plants including sea buckthorn.
Often mislabeled 'yellowtail tuna' on sushi menus, this northwest Pacific jack fish is unrelated to true tuna and is called hamachi when served as sashimi — which species?
Japanese amberjack: Species of fish. The Japanese amberjack or yellowtail, Seriola quinqueradiata, is a species of jack fish in the family Carangidae, native to the northwest Pacific Ocean.
This immune response causes tissue damage upon repeated exposure to an antigen and underlies conditions like hay fever, which affects roughly one in ten people worldwide — what is it called?
Hypersensitivity: Overreaction of the immune system to an antigen.

Nicknamed 'flying lemurs' despite not being lemurs at all, these Southeast Asian gliding mammals are primates' closest living relatives and belong to an order whose name means 'skin wing' — what are they called?
Nicknamed the mosquito hawk, which long-legged insect of the superfamily Tipuloidea is often mistaken for an oversized mosquito?
Crane fly: Superfamily of flies. The larvae of crane flies are known commonly as leatherjackets.
Smelling of vanilla but tasting bitter, which plant compound isn't itself an anticoagulant, though its derivatives inspired the blood-thinning drug warfarin?
Also called quaking aspen for the way its leaves flutter in the slightest breeze, which poplar species is native to the Old World's cool temperate regions?
Named from Greek words for 'thorn' and 'earthworm,' which genus of large tropical centipedes gives its name to an entire family of segmented, many-legged predators?
Cultivated since China's Song Dynasty and boasting thousands of ornamental cultivars, which flowering shrub from the tea family is native to forests of China and Japan?
Camellia japonica: Species of flowering plant.
Produced when beta-amylase breaks starch down two glucose units at a time, which reducing disaccharide gets its name from the germinating-seed process of malting?

Native to the tropical Americas, this flowering shrub was carried to Europe by Dutch explorers and later brought to Goa by the Portuguese, becoming a notorious invasive weed across some 50 countries — which plant?
Lantana camara: Species of plant. Lantana camara (common lantana) is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family (Verbenaceae), native to the tropics of the Americas.
Estimated to date back to the end of the Jurassic period roughly 156 million years ago, this fungal genus includes several species of truffles prized as culinary delicacies — which genus?
Tuber (fungus): Genus of fungi. Tuber is a genus in the fungal family Tuberaceae, with estimated molecular dating to the end of the Jurassic period (156 Mya).

Found at the ends of linear chromosomes, this repetitive DNA region works with specialized proteins to prevent the chromosome tip from being mistaken for a damaging double-strand break — what is it called?
Telomere: Region of repetitive nucleotide sequences on chromosomes.
Made up of the dura, arachnoid, and pia mater, these three protective membranes shield the brain and spinal cord while containing cerebrospinal fluid — what are they called?
Meninges: Three membranes protecting the brain. In anatomy, the meninges (sing. meninx; from Ancient Greek μῆνινξ (mêninx) 'membrane') are protective membranes that cover the brain and spinal cord.

Traditionally eaten whole in French cuisine, with diners often covering their heads with a napkin while doing so, this small Eurasian songbird's population crashed from overhunting despite EU protection — which bird?
Ortolan bunting: Species of bird in Eurasia.

Nicknamed 'lazy eye,' this childhood vision disorder occurs when the brain favors one eye over the other, and correcting the underlying cause doesn't restore sight right away — what is this condition?
Amblyopia: Failure of the brain to process input from one eye.
With more than 1,100 species including onions, garlic, leeks, and chives, this is the largest genus in the flowering plant family Amaryllidaceae — which genus?
Allium: Genus of flowering plants. The flowers form an umbel at the top of a leafless stalk.
Nicknamed 'angel's trumpets' for its pendulous, fragrant blooms, this toxic nightshade-family genus is officially Extinct in the Wild yet thrives worldwide as a garden plant — which genus?
Brugmansia: Genus of flowering plants in the nightshade family.
This American physician-turned-clown founded the Gesundheit Institute in 1989 and travels the world dressing up to bring humor to hospital patients — who is he?
Named by the medieval scholar Gerard of Cremona, this black-looking opening in the eye's iris is round in humans but a vertical slit in cats and a horizontal bar in goats — what is it?
Pupil: Part of an eye. The pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.
This genus contains most of the world's familiar bushy-tailed tree squirrels, found across North America, Europe, temperate Asia, and Central and South America — which genus?
Born in Kabul to a diplomat, this Afghan-American physician-turned-novelist wrote the bestselling 'The Kite Runner' before serving as a UNHCR goodwill ambassador — who is he?
Khaled Hosseini: Afghan-American novelist (born 1965). Hosseini's novels have spread awareness about Afghanistan's people and culture.
On April 3, 1973, this Motorola engineer made history's first public call from a handheld cell phone on a Manhattan sidewalk — who is he?
Exceeding 30 centimeters in length, this centipede from South America is the largest of its kind, preying on animals as large as small mammals and reptiles — which species?

Scolopendra gigantea: Species of Chilopoda (centipede). Scolopendra gigantea, also known as the Peruvian giant yellow-leg centipede or Amazonian giant centipede, is a centipede in the genus Scolopendra.
Also called broccoli rabe, this bitter, vitamin K-rich cruciferous vegetable is a Mediterranean cuisine staple with edible leaves, buds, and stems — what is it?
Developed under Kelly Johnson's Skunk Works team after the discovery of Germany's Me 262, this aircraft became the first jet fighter flown operationally by U.S. forces in World War II — which jet?
Lockheed P-80 Shooting Star: First jet aircraft in U.S. operational service.
Named after a Quechua word meaning the same thing, this New World vulture — with Andean and Californian species — is the largest flying land bird in the Western Hemisphere. What is it?
Condor: Name for two species of vultures.
Stretching about a meter from crown to tail-tip, this deep-blue South American parrot is the largest of its kind and can be mistaken for a smaller relative — which vulnerable parrot?
Despite common nicknames like 'Christmas rose' and 'Lenten rose,' this poisonous Eurasian flowering genus isn't actually related to roses at all — what is it?
Once classified among the thrushes, this small Old World flycatcher was later reassigned to the family Muscicapidae — which bird?
Common redstart: Species of bird. The common redstart (Phoenicurus phoenicurus), or often simply redstart, is a small passerine bird in the genus Phoenicurus.

Spread by the bite of certain infected arachnids, this viral illness of the central nervous system can cause meningitis and lasting cognitive problems, with cases up nearly 400% across Europe in three decades — what is it?

Tick-borne encephalitis: Viral infection of the nervous system. Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is a viral infectious disease involving the central nervous system, transmitted by the bite of several species of infected ticks.
Common in cancer, heart failure, and other serious illnesses, this syndrome causes muscle wasting that better nutrition alone can't reverse — what is it?
Often called the last physicist to master every branch of the field, this Soviet scientist co-discovered the density matrix method and developed the theory of superfluidity — who is he?
Also called cherry laurel, this evergreen shrub native to the Black Sea region was once woven into wreaths for its resemblance to true bay laurel, though the two aren't closely related — which plant?
Prunus laurocerasus: Species of plant. It is not to be confused with its American relative Prunus caroliniana, which is also called cherry laurel.
Named from Greek words meaning "over" and "formation," this condition enlarges tissue by increasing the number of cells rather than their size — which term, distinct from hypertrophy?
Hyperplasia: Enlargement of tissue due to cell proliferation.
Nearly always affecting women, this incurable condition causes fat buildup in both legs that's resistant to typical weight loss and often mistaken for other circulatory disorders — what is it?
Lipedema: Condition involving excessive deposition of fat in the legs.
Nicknamed 'the lawyer' and 'freshwater cod,' this coldwater fish is the only member of its genus and the sole freshwater species in its entire order — what fish is it?
Burbot: Species of fish. The species is closely related to marine fish such as the common ling and cusk, all of which belong to the family Lotidae (rocklings).
Critically endangered with barely two dozen wild individuals estimated in 2007, this big cat subspecies survives along the Russian-Chinese border in the Primorye region — which spotted predator?
Amur leopard: Subspecies of large cat. The Amur leopard (Panthera pardus orientalis) is a leopard subspecies native to the Primorye region of southeastern Russia and northern China.
Native to South and Southeast Asia and often sold as fresh stems, this tropical plant known as West Indian lemon grass can't survive a frost — what is it?
Bred for their dazzling colors since the early 19th century in Niigata, Japan, these ornamental carp come in patterns like Kōhaku and Shōwa Sanshoku — what are they?
Koi: Colored varieties of Amur carp.
These marine algae include the kelps that shelter fisheries and are estimated to produce at least half of Earth's oxygen — what are they collectively called?
Seaweed: Macroscopic marine algae. Seaweed, or macroalgae, refers to thousands of species of macroscopic, multicellular, marine algae.
Discovered entirely by accident and marketed as Librium, this 1960-approved medication was the first benzodiazepine ever synthesized — what is it?
Chlordiazepoxide: Benzodiazepine medication. Chlordiazepoxide hydrochloride, sold under the brand name Librium, is a sedative and hypnotic medication of the benzodiazepine class.
Its name comes from the Ancient Greek for 'female dragon,' and this genus of roughly 200 tree and shrub species now also includes what was once classified as Sansevieria — which genus is it?
Dracaena (plant) is a genus of about 200-220 species of trees and woody shrubs.
Domesticated roughly 8,000 years ago, this Southeast Asian bird species is the primary wild ancestor of today's chickens — which bird?
Red junglefowl: Species of bird; ancestor of the chicken. The red junglefowl was the primary species to give rise to today's many breeds of chicken (G. g. domesticus).
Found across North America (and one Siberian species in Asia), these small striped squirrels stash food in their cheek pouches to store for winter — what are they?
Part of the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family, some species in this plant genus share the common name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Sold over the counter as Unisom and combined with vitamin B6 to ease morning sickness, this first-generation antihistamine is one of the world's most widely used sleep aids — which drug?
Doxylamine: First-generation antihistamine used as a short-term sedative and hypnotic (sleep aid)
Once Mexico's top law-enforcement official as secretary of public security, this man was convicted in a Brooklyn courtroom in 2023 for taking millions in bribes from the Sinaloa Cartel — who is he?
Genaro García Luna: Mexican politician and convicted felon (born 1968)

Born from the French Revolution's push to standardize units into the metric system, this scientific field oversees everything from the SI unit system to the labs that keep rulers honest — what is it called?
Metrology: Science of measurement and its application.
Twice President of the Swiss Confederation, this Social Democratic politician left the Federal Council in 2023 to become Secretary General of the Council of Europe — who is he?
Alain Berset: Swiss Federal Councillor from 2012 to 2023.
Nicknamed the shaggy mane or lawyer's wig, this scaly white mushroom dissolves itself into black ink just hours after being picked — which fungus?
Coprinus comatus: Species of fungus. The young fruit bodies first appear as white cylinders emerging from the ground, then the bell-shaped caps open out.
This Old World tree species has two main cultivar groups, the dark-red Morello and the lighter Amarelle, prized for their tart, edible pulp — which fruit-bearing plant?
Prunus cerasus: Species of cherry tree. Prunus cerasus (sour cherry, tart cherry, or dwarf cherry) is an Old World species of Prunus in the subgenus Cerasus (cherries).
Studied by Confucius and central to rhetoric in ancient Greece and Rome, this skill involves delivering an address to a live audience — what is it called?
Public speaking: Performing a speech to a live audience.
Creator of a satirical comic strip about corporate cubicle life, this cartoonist also wrote the pandeistic novella 'God's Debris' — who is he?
Scott Adams: American cartoonist and author (1957–2026)
Found in mice, cats, birds, humans, and dogs but absent in whales and most reptiles, this triangular bone is the body's largest sesamoid — what is it?
Patella: Kneecap, bone covering knee joint.
Derived from a Greek word meaning 'concurrence,' this medical term describes a set of signs and symptoms that tend to occur together — what is it called?
Syndrome: Association of several clinically recognizable features.
Grown above the upper lip and below the nose, this facial hair style has taken many forms across history — what is it called?
Moustache: Strip of facial hair across the upper lip. A moustache (UK:) or mustache (US:) is a growth of facial hair grown above the upper lip and under the nose of men.

Known to NATO by the reporting name 'Mop' and to Canadian forces as the Canso, this WWII flying boat served every branch of the U.S. military and remained in some air forces into the 1980s — which aircraft?
Consolidated PBY Catalina: American 1930s flying boat.
Erected by entomologist Francis Walker back in 1855, this genus of moths belongs to the family Lasiocampidae — which genus?

Nicknamed 'Il Professore' for his academic background, this Italian politician served as European Commission President from 1999 to 2004 and was twice his country's prime minister, first after leading The Olive Tree coalition to victory — who is he?

Romano Prodi (born 9 August 1939) is an Italian politician who served as President of the European Commission from 1999 to 2004 and twice as Prime Minister of Italy, from 1996 to 1998, and again from 2006 to 2008.

This temporary condition throws your internal body clock out of sync with local time after rapid travel across multiple time zones — and most people find it harder to shake off flying east than west — what is it?

Jet lag: Condition due to travel across time zones. The phase shift when travelling from east to west is referred to as phase-delay of the circadian cycle, whereas going west to east is phase-advance of the cycle.

Discovered in 1879 via spectral analysis of Scandinavian minerals, this silvery-white rare-earth element with atomic number 21 wasn't isolated in metallic form until 1937, and today it's prized for strengthening aluminum alloys — which element?
Scandium: Chemical element with atomic number 21 (Sc)

NATO called it 'Farmer,' and this Soviet twin-engine fighter was the first Soviet production aircraft capable of supersonic speed in level flight, later battling American jets over North Vietnam — which aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19: Air superiority fighter aircraft family.
Native to tropical Central and South America, this genus of 59 flowering plant species belongs to the arum family — which genus?
Also nicknamed the French Mastiff, this large, powerfully muscled brachycephalic breed ranks among France's heaviest dogs — which breed?
Dogue de Bordeaux: Dog breed originating in France.
This class of central nervous system depressant increases GABA activity to calm irritability and anxiety, distinct from drugs used mainly to induce sleep — what is it?
Sedative: Drug that reduces excitement without inducing sleep.
This bird-of-prey family boasts 256 species including eagles, hawks, kites, and harriers, though the osprey and secretary bird are classified separately — which family is it?
Accipitridae: Family of birds of prey. The Accipitridae have a cosmopolitan distribution, being found on all the world's continents (except Antarctica) and a number of oceanic island groups.
Recognized by their unusually long snouts, these small herbivorous beetles number around 97,000 species and include notorious crop pests that damage stored grain — what are they called?
Weevil: Superfamily of beetles. It also includes bark beetles, which while morphologically dissimilar to other weevils in lacking the distinctive snout, is a subfamily of Curculionidae.
Named from Greek words for 'hare' and 'form,' this mammalian order splits into rabbits-and-hares on one branch and pikas on the other, totaling around 110 living species — which order?
Native to the high Himalayas, this large, shaggy bovine, scientific name Bos mutus, is the ancestor of the domesticated Bos grunniens — which animal?
Marketed under the brand name Mucinex, this expectorant medication has been used to loosen chest congestion since at least 1933 — what is it?
Guaifenesin: Expectorant medication. It may be used in combination with other medications.
Known for its fragrant leaves used to flavor dishes across Southeast Asia, Sri Lanka and Hainanese cuisine, this member of the screwpine genus is prized in many Asian kitchens — which plant?
Pandanus amaryllifolius: Species of tropical plant.
Native to Southern Europe, the Middle East, and the Caspian region, this mint-family shrub has long been used in traditional herbal medicine as an antiseptic and cough reliever — which plant?

Hyssopus officinalis: Species of plant. Hyssopus officinalis or hyssop is a shrub in the Lamiaceae or mint family native to Southern Europe, the Middle East, and the region surrounding the Caspian Sea.
The only operational rocket-powered fighter ever fielded, this WWII German interceptor became the first piloted aircraft to exceed 1,000 km/h in level flight — which aircraft?

Messerschmitt Me 163 Komet: German rocket-powered interceptor. The Messerschmitt Me 163 Komet is a rocket-powered interceptor aircraft primarily designed and produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Messerschmitt.
Named by Reginald Innes Pocock in 1917 to cover big cats of genus Panthera, this cat subfamily later grew to include the clouded leopards too — which subfamily?
Pantherinae: Subfamily of felids. The Pantherinae genetically diverged from a common ancestor between 9.32 to 4.47 million years ago and 10.67 to 3.76 million years ago.
Combining Greek words for 'earth,' 'form,' and 'study,' what field examines how landscapes and seafloor features form and evolve over time?
This French aerospace engineer flew to the International Space Station twice, first as a 2016 European Space Agency flight engineer and again in 2021 aboard a SpaceX Crew Dragon — who is he?
Thomas Pesquet: French aerospace engineer, pilot, and astronaut.
Discovered in 1972 and used to treat scabies and lice, this pyrethroid insecticide is safe for most mammals but especially dangerous to cats, who metabolize it slowly — what is it?
Permethrin: Medication and insecticide. It is applied to the skin as a cream or lotion.
Named from an Ancient Greek word for 'intestinal obstruction,' this medical condition disrupts the gut's normal propulsive movement, whether from lost peristalsis or a physical blockage — what is it?
Ileus: Disruption to the propulsive ability of the intestine.
This condition involves a long-term urge to pull out one's own hair, most often from the scalp or around the eyes, and is more common among those with OCD — what is it?
This spiral-shaped bacterium, spread mainly through sexual contact and known only to infect humans and baboons, causes syphilis along with yaws and bejel — what is it?
Treponema pallidum: Species of bacterium. T. pallidum can enter the host through mucosal membranes or open lesions in the skin and is primarily spread through sexual contact.
Also known by the nickname 'catawba,' this genus of flowering trees is native to warm regions of North America, the Caribbean, and East Asia — what genus is it?

Nicknamed the 'vampire fish' for feeding on the blood of larger fish through their gills, this tiny Amazonian catfish is infamous for an alleged, rare habit of entering human body openings — what is it?
Vandellia cirrhosa: Species of ray-finned fish.
While bacteria and some plants may be biologically immortal, this universal process in humans slows reaction time even as knowledge tends to grow — what is it called?
Ageing: Biological process of getting older.
Built from microfilaments, intermediate filaments, and microtubules, this network gives a cell its shape and lets it contract and migrate — what is it?
Cytoskeleton: Network of filamentous proteins that forms the internal framework of cells.

Not approved for general use in the US but sold across Europe for conditions such as vertigo and cortical myoclonus, this drug is a cyclic derivative of the neurotransmitter GABA and belongs to the 'racetam' group — what is it?
Encompassing peaches, cherries, plums, and almonds, this genus of flowering trees and shrubs in the rose family produces stone fruits called drupes — which genus?
Prunus: Genus of trees and shrubs.
Derived from Greek words for 'heart' and 'study,' this branch of internal medicine covers coronary artery disease, heart failure, and electrophysiology — which medical field?
Cardiology: Branch of medicine dealing with the heart.
Fluent in Quechua after being raised in two Indigenous households as a child, this Peruvian novelist and anthropologist became known for his intimate portrayals of Andean culture — who is he?
Scientifically named Gadus chalcogrammus, this schooling member of the cod family gathers in massive numbers in the eastern Bering Sea — which fish?
Alaska pollock: Species of fish. The Alaska pollock also known as Pacific pollock or walleye pollock (Gadus chalcogrammus) is a marine fish species of the cod genus Gadus and family Gadidae.
Grown worldwide as ornamentals in ponds and known to gardeners simply as water lilies, this widespread genus of aquatic plants also includes species considered weeds — which genus?
Nymphaea: Genus of aquatic plants. Nymphaea is a genus of hardy and tender aquatic plants in the family Nymphaeaceae.

A Belgian Catholic priest and physicist, he was first to argue that the recession of galaxies proves an expanding universe, and proposed a 'primeval atom' — the first version of the Big Bang theory. Who was he?
Georges Lemaître: Belgian scientist and Catholic priest (1894–1966)
Also known as thymol seeds, bishop's weed, or carom, this Apiaceae herb's fruit is often mistaken for lovage seed — what is it?
Named for a Tanzanian teenager who studied it scientifically in the 1960s, this puzzling phenomenon claims hot liquids can sometimes freeze faster than cold ones — what is it called?
Mpemba effect: Natural phenomenon that hot water freezes faster than cold.
Emerging from 16th-century moral philosophy and pursued by Adam Smith, Malthus, and Ricardo, this interdisciplinary field studies how governance and markets shape one another — what's it called?
Political economy: Study of the development of social production.
Nicknamed the hay bacterium for its soil habitat, this rod-shaped, spore-forming microbe is the best-studied Gram-positive species and a top industrial source of secreted enzymes — what is it?
Bacillus subtilis: Catalase-positive bacterium. It forms biofilms through the formation of extracellular polymeric matrix containing sugars and proteins.

This airway symptom — blood or blood-streaked mucus coughed up from the lungs or throat — turns dangerous mainly because of choking rather than blood loss once it passes 300 milliliters. What is it called?
This Mitsubishi engineer had the extraordinarily unlucky distinction of being caught in both the Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings in August 1945 — and lived to tell about it. Who is he?
Tsutomu Yamaguchi: Japanese atomic bombing survivor.
Sometimes triggered just by stepping into bright sunlight, a quirk called the photic reflex, this involuntary, explosive expulsion of air clears irritants from the nose and mouth. What is it?
Sneeze: Semi-autonomous, convulsive expulsion of air from the lungs through the nose and mouth.
First described to Europeans in 1812, this reddish-brown African antelope's males sport lyre-shaped horns up to three feet long — which animal?
Impala: Species of antelope found in Africa.
