Nicknamed 'dumb cane' because its poisonous sap can temporarily rob you of speech, this shade-tolerant tropical houseplant is native to the New World — which genus?
Dieffenbachia: Genus of plants. Dieffenbachia, commonly known as dumb cane or leopard lily, is a genus of tropical flowering plants in the family Araceae.
This order of hoofed mammals — horses, rhinos, and tapirs — bears its weight on an odd number of toes and digests plant fiber in its intestines rather than a multi-chambered stomach. Which order?
Perissodactyla: Order of hoofed mammals. Perissodactyla (from Ancient Greek περισσός, perissós 'odd' and δάκτυλος, dáktylos 'finger, toe'), or odd-toed ungulates, is an order of ungulates.
Native to Europe, northwestern Africa, and southwestern Asia, this flowering shrub's edible fruit stars in desserts and preserves — what's its species name, better known as the gooseberry?
Ribes uva-crispa: Species of flowering plant in the family Grossulariaceae.

Native across Europe, Asia, and Africa, this medium-sized game bird's family ties are murkier than expected — genetically, some species lean toward pheasants, others toward junglefowl. What bird is it?
Partridge: Common name for a type of bird.
Co-author of Mosaic, the first web browser to display images inline, this entrepreneur went on to co-found Netscape and a major Silicon Valley venture capital firm — who is he?
This healthcare discipline treats disorders of voice, fluency, and swallowing, practiced by clinicians licensed under boards overseen by groups like ASHA — which field of study?
Home to the supermassive black hole known as Sagittarius A*, this point roughly 26,000 light-years from Earth marks the barycenter around which the Milky Way rotates — what is it?
Galactic Center is the barycenter of the Milky Way and a corresponding point on the rotational axis of the galaxy.
This Romanian-American engineer served as Team Principal of the Alpine Formula One team from February 2022 to July 2023 — who is he?
Otmar Szafnauer: American-Romanian engineer, F1 team lead.
This scientific field measures Earth's precise shape, gravity, and orientation in space, underpinning satellite positioning systems and global mapping — which discipline?
Geodesy: Science of measuring the shape, orientation, and gravity of Earth.
Sold under the brand name Xyzal, this less-sedating second-generation antihistamine for hay fever and hives was patented in 1965 but not approved in the US until 2007 — what is it?
Levocetirizine: Antihistamine medication. It is classified as a second-generation antihistamine and works by blocking histamine H1-receptors.

Co-inventor of a heart-valve repair device called the MitraClip, this Turkish-American cardiac surgeon became a famous TV health personality before being named the 17th administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services in 2025 — who is he?
Mehmet Oz: American TV host and government official (born 1960)
Famous for mimicking the songs of other birds — and even singing well past midnight — this bird can recognize individual humans and is the state bird of five U.S. states. What kind of bird is it?
Mockingbird: Family of birds. The only mockingbird commonly found in North America is the northern mockingbird.

Serving under both Presidents Sukarno and Suharto, this Indonesian economist held posts across trade, finance, and research ministries, and once lobbied Washington against Dutch colonial rule — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo: Indonesian statesman and economist (1917–2001)
This New World family within the order Carnivora encompasses raccoons, ringtails, coatis, and kinkajous, most of them omnivorous — what family is it?
Procyonidae: Family of mammals. Procyonidae ( PROH-see-ON-i-dee) is a New World family of the order Carnivora.
Approved for medical use in the US in 1966, this xanthine oxidase inhibitor lowers uric acid to prevent gout and certain kidney stones — what medication is it?
Allopurinol: Medication. Allopurinol is a medication used to decrease high blood uric acid levels.
Born in Haifa, this Israeli historian and leading 'New Historian' wrote The Ethnic Cleansing of Palestine and now directs Palestine studies at the University of Exeter — who is he?
This Austrian-born economist briefly served as his country's Finance Minister before becoming a Harvard professor, and popularized the term 'creative destruction' — who is he?
Joseph Schumpeter: Austrian (later American) political economist (1883–1950)
Also known as the cane spider or giant crab spider, this huntsman species native to the tropics has spread to subtropical regions worldwide — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria: Species of spider. It is native to the tropical regions of the world, and it is present in some subtropical areas as an introduced species.
Native to Indomalaya and Australasia, this deciduous member of the mahogany family goes by names like chinaberry tree and Persian lilac — what is it?

Lasting anywhere from milliseconds to hours, these are the most luminous explosions in the universe after the Big Bang, sometimes triggered when massive stars collapse into black holes — what are they?
Gamma-ray burst (GRBs) are extremely energetic events occurring in distant galaxies that represent the brightest and most powerful class of explosion in the Universe.
This genus of over 570 flowering plants — the only living genus in its family — includes the evergreen shrub famous for Christmas decorations and cards. What genus is it?
Holly: Genus of flowering plants. Ilex or holly is a genus of over 570 species of flowering plants in the family Aquifoliaceae, and the only living genus in that family.

This medical term covers abnormal cell or organ growth — from hip conditions to bone marrow disorders — and is generally distinguished from cancerous neoplasia, though some forms are precancerous. What is it called?
Dysplasia: Abnormal development, at macroscopic or microscopical level.
As the single largest muscle in the human body, this hip extensor gives the buttocks their shape and is a key reason humans can stand upright, unlike other primates — what is it?
Gluteus maximus: Largest and most superficial of the three gluteal muscles.

A hemiparasitic plant that taps into its host tree via a structure called the haustorium to steal water and nutrients, its European species was introduced to Northern California in 1900 — what plant is it?
Mistletoe: Common name for various parasitic plants.

With 348 known species spanning an opportunistic human pathogen, a plant disease-causer, and a soil-dwelling growth-promoter, which gram-negative bacterial genus in Gammaproteobacteria is renowned for its metabolic diversity?
Pseudomonas: Genus of Gram-negative bacteria. Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Pseudomonadaceae in the class Gammaproteobacteria.
Usually triggered when a gallstone blocks the cystic duct, this inflammatory condition causes right-upper abdominal pain that radiates to the shoulder — what is it?
Known for darkly comic songs like 'Poisoning Pigeons in the Park' and satirical numbers for That Was the Week That Was, which musician later retired to teach mathematics at UC Santa Cruz?
Its name literally means 'blue cow,' though only the males actually sport a bluish-grey coat — which is the largest antelope species in Asia?
Named from a Tamil word for rice gruel, this savory porridge dish has been a famine and wartime staple across Asia and is often given to the sick as easy-to-digest comfort food — what is it?
Congee: Asian savoury rice porridge dish.
Also known as jícama or Mexican turnip, this pea-family vine's edible tuberous root comes in a milky-juice form and a watery-juice form — which species is it?
Pachyrhizus erosus: Species of legume. Pachyrhizus tuberosus and Pachyrhizus ahipa are the other two cultivated species in the genus.
Marked by up to 20 liters of dilute urine a day and intense thirst that drinking barely satisfies, this condition comes in four types tied to problems with the hormone vasopressin — what is it?
Diabetes insipidus: Condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst.
What is the medical term for a clump of platelets, fibrin, and blood cells that forms within the circulatory system — sometimes lifesaving, sometimes an obstruction?
Thrombus: Blood clot. There are two components to a thrombus: aggregated platelets and red blood cells that form a plug, and a mesh of cross-linked fibrin protein.
Native to the Mekong and Chao Phraya river basins, this freshwater catfish is marketed in the US as "swai" and in the UK as "river cobbler" — which fish?

Basa (fish) (Pangasius bocourti), as it is commonly referred to, is a species of primarily freshwater-dwelling catfish in the shark-catfish family, Pangasiidae, native to the Mekong and Chao Phraya river basins of Mainland Southeast Asia.
In 1948, this Japanese engineer turned a wooden shack producing bicycle motors into a multinational car and motorcycle manufacturer — who is he?
Soichiro Honda: Japanese businessman. Soichiro Honda (本田 宗一郎, Honda Sōichirō; 17 November 1906 – 5 August 1991) was a Japanese engineer and industrialist.
This plant genus in the mallow family produces the world's most famously pungent fruit, alongside eight other edible-fruit-bearing species — which genus?
Durio: Genus of plants. Several species produce an edible fruit known as durian, the most common species being Durio zibethinus, with eight others producing edible fruit.
Literally meaning "hardening of the arteries," this umbrella term covers vascular disorders marked by abnormal thickening and loss of elasticity in artery walls — what is it called?
Arteriosclerosis: Thickening, hardening and loss of elasticity of the walls of arteries.
Formed by the merger of two hip flexor muscles that join at the femur's lesser trochanter, this is the body's strongest flexor of the hip — what is it called?
Iliopsoas: Joined psoas and iliacus muscles of the hip and thigh.

A former Communist Party official who was later sidelined by Nicolae Ceaușescu, this engineer-turned-politician emerged from Romania's 1989 revolution to become the country's first freely elected president — who is he?

Extracted from a Central African plant sacred to Gabon's Bwiti tradition, this hallucinogenic alkaloid was once marketed in Europe as a stimulant before being studied for other therapeutic uses — what is it?
Ibogaine: Psychoactive substance found in plants in the family Apocynaceae.

Comprising some 150 to 175 species of shrubs and the occasional small tree, this flowering-plant genus is native across the temperate Northern Hemisphere but in Africa survives only in the Atlas Mountains — which genus?
Viburnum: Genus of flowering plants in the moschatel family.
This chromosomal condition gives a female an extra sex chromosome beyond the usual pair, often producing no noticeable symptoms — fewer than 1 in 10 who have it even know. What is the condition?
Trisomy X: Chromosome disorder in women.
Named for its males' mating call, which sounds like a farm animal bellowing, this large amphibian native to eastern North America has been introduced worldwide as a food source — which species?
American bullfrog: Species of amphibian. It typically inhabits large permanent water bodies such as swamps, ponds, and lakes.
Known as the 'true foxes,' animals in this genus are smaller and bushier-tailed than any wolf or jackal, with a signature dark triangular mask between the eyes — which genus?
Vulpes: Genus of true foxes. The members of this genus are colloquially referred to as true foxes, meaning they form a proper clade.
One of the very first vertebrate apex predators on Earth, this armor-plated, jointed-neck fish patrolled open Devonian seas some 380 million years ago — which genus?
This purplish-black Brazilian fruit doesn't dangle from branches — it sprouts straight out of the tree trunk itself. What is it?
Jabuticaba: Tree in the family Myrtaceae.
This blue supergiant in Orion, also known as Beta Orionis, outshines the Sun by up to 363,000 times and anchors a system of at least four stars — which star?
Rigel: Brightest star in the constellation Orion.
This whip-like appendage propels sperm cells and lets bacteria like Helicobacter pylori swim through stomach mucus, sometimes triggering ulcers — what is it called?
Flagellum: Cellular appendage functioning as locomotive or sensory organelle.

Nicknamed the 'solar' web for its sunburst of radiating nerve fibers, this abdominal structure sits behind the stomach and in front of the diaphragm's crura, near where several major arteries branch off the aorta — what is it?
Celiac plexus: Complex network of nerves located in the upper abdomen.
In this rare congenital condition affecting about 1 in 10,000 people, the heart and other major organs sit as a mirror image of their normal position — what's it called?
Situs inversus: Condition in which organs are reversed.
One of the smallest self-replicating organisms known, this cell-wall-lacking bacterium was originally called the 'Eaton agent' after being cultivated in chicken eggs in 1944 — what organism is it?
Mycoplasma pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a species of very small-cell bacteria that lack a cell wall, in the class Mollicutes.
Known by folk names like 'bird cherry' and 'Mayday tree,' this flowering plant in the rose family is native to Europe and northern Asia — what species is it?
Prunus padus: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
Working alongside biochemist Katalin Karikó on nucleoside base modifications, this University of Pennsylvania immunologist shared the 2023 Nobel Prize for enabling COVID-19 mRNA vaccines — who is he?
Drew Weissman: American physician and immunologist (born 1959)

First isolated from linseed oil and named from the Latin words for 'flax' and 'oil,' this omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid is one of the two essential fats humans must get from their diet — which acid?
Linoleic acid (LA) is an organic compound with the formula CH3(CH2)4CH=CHCH2CH=CH(CH2)7COOH.
This genus of fungi is responsible for both a groundbreaking antibiotic and the mold that ripens certain blue cheeses — which genus?
Marketed under brand names like Arcoxia, this selective COX-2 inhibitor developed by Merck was approved in 63 countries by 2007 — everywhere, notably, except the United States — what is the drug?

Nicknamed the 'last Soviet citizen' for being aboard Mir when the USSR dissolved, this cosmonaut flew six missions and helped connect the first Russian and American modules of a space station — who is he?
Sergei Krikalev: Soviet and Russian cosmonaut (born 1958)
Nicknamed 'knitbone' and 'boneset' for its traditional use in healing wounds, this perennial herb carries a liver-toxicity warning against internal use — which plant?
Symphytum officinale: Species of flowering plant in the borage family Boraginaceae.
A former finance minister and central bank board member, this economist became the 52nd president of Paraguay in 2023 after switching from a liberal party to the Colorado Party — who is he?
Santiago Peña: President of Paraguay since 2023. Peña served on leadership boards for the Central Bank of Paraguay and Banco Amambay.

This geometry rule holds that a triangle inscribed in a circle, with one side running through the center as a diameter, always has a right angle at its third point — proved by Euclid, though occasionally miscredited to Pythagoras. What's it called?
Thales's theorem: On triangles inscribed in a circle with a diameter as an edge.
With atomic number 39, this silvery metal is chemically similar to the lanthanides, never occurs freely in nature, and once gave old CRT televisions their red phosphor glow — which element?
Yttrium: Chemical element with atomic number 39 (Y)

These long-legged wading birds communicate by clattering their bills rather than calling, favor drier habitats than their heron cousins, and are collectively known as a 'muster' or a 'phalanx' — which birds?

This single-engine turboprop trainer, a license-built version of the Swiss Pilatus PC-9, replaced America's Cessna 'Tweet' and Turbo Mentor trainers in the 2010s and flies under the nickname 'Efroni' in Israel — which aircraft?
Beechcraft T-6 Texan II: Single-engine, low-wing tandem-seat turboprop military training aircraft.
Commonly known as the pork tapeworm, this parasite completes its life cycle by cycling between human waste, pig feed, and undercooked pork — which species?
Taenia solium: Species of tapeworm. Taenia solium, the pork tapeworm, belongs to the cyclophyllid cestode family Taeniidae.

This large flatfish native to the Northeast Atlantic, Baltic, and Mediterranean gave its name to a 1990s fishing dispute between Canada and Spain, even though a different species was the real catch at stake — which fish?
Turbot: Species of flatfish in the family Scophthalmidae.
The first person to ever call himself an anarchist, this French philosopher and self-taught Latin scholar coined the phrase 'property is theft!' — who is he?
Pierre-Joseph Proudhon: French philosopher and economist (1809–1865)
Its Latin name means 'horned goat,' and it's often pictured as a half-goat, half-fish sea creature — which is the smallest constellation of the zodiac?
Capricornus: Zodiac constellation in the southern hemisphere.
This Dutch scientist discovered Saturn's largest moon and invented the pendulum clock, the most accurate timekeeper for nearly three centuries — who is he?
Christiaan Huygens: Dutch mathematician and physicist (1629–1695)
One of China's 'Four Great Domestic Fish,' this herbivorous freshwater species was later introduced to Europe and the US to control aquatic weeds — which fish?
Grass carp: Species of fish. This Asian carp is the only species of the genus Ctenopharyngodon.
Distinct from a process that adds more cells, this one is an increase in the size of individual cells, like the uterus enlarging during pregnancy — what's it called?
Hypertrophy: Increase in the size of biological cells. Hypertrophy can lead to a relative increase in the volume of a tissue or organ, and contributes to the overall growth of an organism.
This colorless, sweet-smelling liquid made from benzene is the precursor to polystyrene, with global production reaching some 35 million tonnes by 2018 — what compound is it?
Styrene: Chemical compound. Styrene is an organic compound with the chemical formula C6H5CH=CH2.
In a landmark 1913 Columbia University address, this American psychologist championed behaviorism and later became known for the unsettling 'Little Albert' experiment — who is he?
Dubbed the 'king of the birds' in European folklore for its golden head crest, this tiny kinglet's scientific name literally means 'petty king' — which bird?
Goldcrest: Small passerine bird in the kinglet family.

This anatomic form of lung infection causes inflammatory fluid to consolidate across an entire continuous section of one lung, and in children shows up instead as a rounded pattern due to immature air-pore connections — what is it?
Lobar pneumonia: Lung infection. It is one of three anatomic classifications of pneumonia (the other being bronchopneumonia and atypical pneumonia).

A physician by training, this Polish politician has served as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence since 2023, after leading his country's labour ministry a decade earlier — who is he?
Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz: Polish physician and politician (born 1981)
Often paired with spirits like ouzo, raki, and arak at a traditional Eastern Mediterranean tavern, this appetizer spread is often compared to Spanish tapas — what's it called?
Meze: Small dish in Middle Eastern and Balkan cuisines.
This form of cancer that begins in the tubes carrying digestive fluid from the liver can cause yellowing skin, dark urine, and pale stools — what is it?
Cholangiocarcinoma: Cancer of the bile ducts.
Named from a Wiradjuri word imitating its own call, this Australian tree kingfisher's cackling laugh is a go-to sound effect for movie jungle scenes — what is it?
Kookaburra: Genus of birds (terrestrial tree kingfishers)
Cataloged as a nebula by a French astronomer in 1781, this supergiant elliptical galaxy boasts roughly 15,000 globular clusters, a hundred times more than our own — which galaxy is it?
Messier 87: Galaxy in the constellation Virgo.
This mushroom genus of more than 400 species includes both the common button mushroom and the field mushroom, the two most-cultivated fungi in the West — which genus is it?
Known online by the alias TiAMO, this Swede co-founded a notorious file-sharing site and stood trial for it in 2009, a saga captured in the documentary TPB AFK — who is he?
First described in 1880 by a French neurologist, this rare delusion convinces sufferers that they are dead, don't exist, or have lost their internal organs — what is it called?
Cotard's syndrome: Delusion that one is dead or non-existent.
This fluid-filled sac that forms within the ovary is usually harmless and often tied to ovulation, appearing as a follicular or corpus luteum type — what is it?
Ovarian cyst: Fluid-filled sac in the ovary. If the cyst either breaks open or causes twisting of the ovary, it may cause severe pain.
Known as lamb's quarters, goosefoot, or fat-hen, this fast-growing annual weed in the amaranth family is sometimes cultivated as food elsewhere — which plant?
Chenopodium album: Species of flowering plant in the goosefoot family.
This genus of anaerobic, Gram-positive bacteria found in soil and animal intestines includes the microbes responsible for both botulism and tetanus — which genus?
Clostridium: Genus of bacteria. Species of Clostridium inhabit soils and the intestinal tracts of animals, including humans.
This fibrous connective tissue links bone to bone in every one of the 30,000 known amniote species, and in birds it even anchors flight feathers to bone — what is it?
Known in North America as fireweed and in Britain as rosebay willowherb, this perennial flowering plant thrives across the boreal forests of the Northern Hemisphere — which plant?
Chamaenerion angustifolium: Species of flowering plant in the willowherb family.
Its name combines the Greek words for 'love' and 'tree,' and with over 600 accepted species it's the second-largest genus in the arum family after Anthurium — which popular houseplant genus?

This red-orange, sublimable heterocyclic solid is a stable aminoxyl radical used as a spin probe in electron spin resonance spectroscopy and as a mediator in controlled radical polymerization — what's this compound commonly called?
Born Giulia Maddalena Angela in Italy, this physician became a leading freethinker and activist for women's rights and social reform in early-20th-century Argentina — who is she?
Julieta Lanteri: Argentine doctor and activist (1873–1932)
This autoimmune disease attacks both the skin and skeletal muscles, causing a rash alongside worsening weakness, and is often linked to distinct myositis-specific autoantibodies — which condition?
Dermatomyositis: Autoimmune disease of skin and muscle. Dermatomyositis (DM) is a group of sytemic autoimmune inflammatory diseases primarily affecting the skin and skeletal muscles.
Known by folk names like bitter buttons and golden buttons, this Eurasian flowering plant in the daisy family has become invasive after being introduced to Australia and the Americas — which plant?
Tansy: Species of plant. Tansy (Tanacetum vulgare) is a perennial, herbaceous flowering plant in the genus Tanacetum in the family Asteraceae, native to temperate Europe and Asia.

This symptom can stem from something as mild as gastroenteritis or as serious as a ruptured aortic aneurysm or ectopic pregnancy, yet its exact cause goes unexplained in about a third of cases — what symptom is this?
This French economist's best-selling 2013 book argued that capital returns persistently outpace economic growth, driving ever-rising wealth inequality — who is he?
Known informally as bedwetting, this involuntary condition rarely stems from a specific medical cause and is often treated with alarms or hormone therapy — what is it called medically?
Nocturnal enuresis: Involuntary urination while asleep.

Native to the dry grasslands and deserts of Afghanistan, Iran, Pakistan, India, and Nepal, this ground-dwelling reptile is so widely captive-bred it's considered the first domesticated species of its kind — what is it?
Leopard gecko: Species of reptile. The leopard gecko is a popular pet, and due to extensive captive breeding it is sometimes referred to as the first domesticated species of lizard.
Often called the 'forgotten founder' of Apple, this retired electronics executive partnered with Steve Wozniak and Steve Jobs to launch the company in 1976 — who is he?
Ronald Wayne: American businessperson and co-founder of Apple (born 1934)
The smallest of its type, this Canadian gun dog has webbed feet and lures waterfowl to shore with playful antics before fetching them from the water — which breed is it?
Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever is a medium-sized gun dog bred primarily for hunting.
This frozen dessert blends ice with fruit juice or purée — and sometimes wine, liqueur, or honey — for a refreshing icy treat. What is it called?
Sorbet: Frozen dessert. Sorbet is a frozen dessert made using ice combined with fruit juice, fruit purée, or other ingredients, such as wine, liqueur, or honey.
This semiaquatic salamander's juvenile phase is nicknamed an 'eft,' and adults return to the water every year to breed after living mostly on land — what is it?
Newt: Salamander in the subfamily Pleurodelinae.
Made from red algae and dried into flat sheets through a process resembling papermaking, this ingredient has wrapped sushi and rice balls in Japan since the 700s — what is it?
Nori: Edible seaweed species of the red algae genus Pyropia.
Nicknamed the 'Radioactive Boy Scout,' this Michigan teenager built a crude neutron source in a backyard shed while chasing his dream of a homemade nuclear reactor — who is he?
David Hahn: American nuclear radiation enthusiast (1976–2016)
This British mathematician has studied the math of dating and pandemics, delivered the Royal Institution's 2019 Christmas Lectures, and hosted BBC's 'Secret Genius of Modern Life' — who is she?
Hannah Fry: British mathematician and broadcaster (born 1984)
Alongside James Watson, this English scientist co-authored the 1953 Nature paper unveiling DNA's double helix and later coined the phrase 'central dogma' — who is he?
Francis Crick: English physicist and biologist (1916–2004)
Named from Greek words for 'old man' and 'healer,' this medical specialty focuses on preventing and treating disease in older adults with no fixed age cutoff — what is it called?
Geriatrics: Medical specialty that focuses on health care of elderly people.
This legal document spells out how a business collects, stores, and shares personal details like your address, financial records, or medical history — what is it called?
Privacy policy: Management of personal data across media.
This cold-weather injury turns skin white or waxy-blue after tissue actually freezes, often preceded by a tingling, numb warning stage called frostnip — what is it?
Frostbite: Effect of low temperature on skin and other tissues.
This type of organ produces an organism's sex hormones and gametes — testicles in males, ovaries in females — what is it called?
Gonad: Gland that produces sex cells.
Serving under Bill Clinton from 1993 to 1997, this professor and author held the labor secretary's cabinet post and later advised Barack Obama's economic transition team — who is he?
Robert Reich: American former labor secretary and political commentator (born 1946)
Smaller, seedier, and more aromatic than its Persian cousin, this citrus hybrid lends its tart flavor to a beloved Florida pie named after the island chain it's associated with — what is it?
Key lime: Citrus fruit and plant.
Native to alpine lakes and polar coastal waters, this cold-water relative of salmon holds the title of the world's most northerly freshwater fish — what is it?

Essentially plasma with the clotting factors and cells removed, this pale yellow fluid still carries antibodies, hormones, and electrolytes and is central to typing tests done before a transfusion — what is it?
Serum (blood) is the fluid and solvent component of blood which does not play a role in clotting.

Nicknamed for its spider-like look and also called airplane plant or hen and chicks, this houseplant is native to tropical Africa but can suffer 'burnt tips' from fluoride in tap water — which species?
Chlorophytum comosum: Species of flowering plant. It is native to tropical and Southern Africa but has become naturalized in other parts of the world, including Western Australia and Bangladesh.
Secreted by eccrine and apocrine glands, this bodily fluid can flow at up to 4 litres per hour in adults and cools the body via evaporation — what is it?
Perspiration: Fluid secreted from sudoriferous glands.
Found naturally in chocolate — especially after fermentation — this trace amine stimulates the central nervous system by binding to a receptor called TAAR1. What compound is it?
Phenethylamine: Organic compound, a stimulant in humans.
Commonly called the guelder-rose, this Old World flowering shrub belongs to the Viburnaceae family — what's its scientific name?
Viburnum opulus: Species of flowering plant.
Named for the skull-shaped marking on its thorax and first classified by Carl Linnaeus in 1758, this large moth was immortalized on the poster for 'The Silence of the Lambs' — which insect?
Acherontia atropos: Species of moth. It is most commonly identified by the vaguely skull-shaped pattern adorning the thorax, the characteristic from which its common and scientific names are derived.
Often called the Judas tree, this small deciduous redbud native to Southern Europe and Western Asia bursts into deep pink blossoms each spring — what species is it?

Named from a Tupi word imitating the sound these macaws make, this genus of large, vividly colored Neotropical parrots includes eight living species prized — and poached — for the pet trade — which genus?
Ara (bird): Neotropical genus of macaws. Ara is a Neotropical genus of macaws with eight extant species and at least two extinct species.
This genus of highly sociable ruminants includes domestic sheep, believed to descend from the wild mouflon of central and southwest Asia — which genus?
Ovis: Genus of mammals. Ovis is a genus of mammals, part of the Caprinae subfamily of the ruminant family Bovidae.

Sold under a non-proprietary name once the original patent expires, this type of medication shares the same active ingredient as its brand-name predecessor, though packaging and coloring may differ — what's it called?
Generic drug: Pharmaceutical equivalent to a brand-name product.
The lone living family within its primate infraorder, these small Southeast Asian mammals favor forests thick with liana vines, which give them vertical support as they climb — which animal?
Also known as sixth disease, this childhood viral infection typically strikes before age three with a sudden fever followed by a pink rash lasting under three days — what's the condition called?
Roseola: Human disease caused by human herpesviruses.
Marked by weariness and a desire to act without the energy to do so, which condition can be a normal response to poor sleep or stress, or a sign of underlying illness?
Lethargy: State of tiredness, weariness, fatigue, or lack of energy.
The clinging seed burrs of this plant genus, commonly known as burdock, directly inspired the invention of the hook-and-loop fastener — which genus?
Also called the jigger or chigoe flea, this burrowing parasite causes an infestation known as tungiasis and is often mistaken for an unrelated mite — which species?
Tunga penetrans: Species of flea. It is a parasitic insect found in most tropical and sub-tropical climates.
This thick, fan-shaped muscle underlies the breast and is responsible for flexing, adducting, and internally rotating the upper arm — which chest muscle?
Pectoralis major: Main human chest muscle.
Nicknamed for its heart-shaped seed pods, this mustard-family weed is considered protocarnivorous because its seeds ooze a mucilage that traps nematodes — which species?
Capsella bursa-pastoris: Species of flowering plant in the mustard family.

Marked by deep gasping breaths and breath that smells oddly fruity or like acetone, this life-threatening condition arises when a shortage of insulin forces the body to burn fat into acidic ketones — what is it?
Diabetic ketoacidosis: Medical condition. Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a potentially life-threatening acute complication of diabetes mellitus.
This medical term describes the partial or complete wasting away of a body part due to poor nourishment, nerve loss, or disuse — what is the condition called?
Atrophy: Partial or complete wasting away of a part of the body. A diminished muscular trophic condition is designated as atrophy.
This genus of roughly 300 evergreen flowering plants includes one edible species enjoyed as a vegetable and another grown purely as an ornamental — which genus?
Asparagus (genus) is a genus of flowering plants in the family Asparagaceae, subfamily Asparagoideae.
Named for the Latin word for weighing scales and lying between Virgo and Scorpius, this faint zodiac constellation has no first-magnitude stars — which one?
Libra (constellation) is a constellation of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere.
Produced continuously from 1964 to 2021, this line of twin-turboprop utility aircraft outsold all of its turboprop rivals combined — which aircraft family?
Beechcraft King Air: Twin engine turboprop aircraft family. The King Air line comprises a number of twin-turboprop models that have been divided into two families.
Known also as yoke elm, this species of hornbeam native to Western Asia and Europe grows only up to elevations of about 1,000 metres — which species?
Carpinus betulus: Species of tree. It requires a warm climate for good growth, and occurs only at elevations up to 1,000 metres (3,300 ft).
This condition describes an abnormally dilated pupil that remains enlarged even in bright light, often triggered by trauma, disease, or certain drugs — what is it called?
Mydriasis: Excessive dilation of the pupil.
Commonly called geraniums or storksbills, this genus of roughly 280 evergreen species was split from a related genus by a botanist in 1789 — which genus, native largely to southern Africa?
Pelargonium: Genus of plants. It includes about 280 species of perennials, succulents, and shrubs.
Also called Bermuda grass, this hardy warm-climate turf species is ironically not native to the island of the same name — which plant, by its scientific name?
Cynodon dactylon: Species of grass. Cynodon dactylon, commonly known as Bermuda grass or as couch grass in Australia and New Zealand, is a grass found worldwide in warm and tropical climates.
Sold under the brand name Deca-Durabolin, this anabolic steroid is prescribed for conditions like anemia and osteoporosis despite masculinizing side effects — which compound?
Nandrolone: Androgenic Anabolic steroid. Nandrolone, also known as 19-nortestosterone, is an endogenous androgen.
Often caused by poor circulation or prolonged pressure on the skin, this open sore — also known as a bedsore when linked to immobility — can destroy tissue down to the fat layer. What is it called?
Turkey's only female prime minister to date, this economist-turned-politician led the country from 1993 to 1996 as head of the True Path Party — who is she?
Tansu Çiller: Prime Minister of Turkey from 1993 to 1996. As a professor of economics, Çiller was appointed Minister of State for the economy by Prime Minister Süleyman Demirel in 1991.

A pioneer in optical character recognition and speech synthesis, this futurist inventor received the National Medal of Technology from President Clinton in 1999 for his outlook on AI and life extension — who is he?
Ray Kurzweil: American computer scientist, author and futurist (born 1948)
Also known by the scientific name Gyps fulvus, this large Old World bird of prey belongs to the family Accipitridae — which species is it?
Eurasian griffon vulture: Species of bird. It is also known as the Eurasian griffon or griffon vulture, although the latter term is sometimes used for the genus Gyps as a whole.
This Australian speech and language therapist and amateur stage actor helped King George VI manage his stammer — who is he?
Lionel Logue: Australian speech and language therapist (1880–1953)
Nicknamed 'Crusty' by NATO, this twin-engined Soviet airliner featured a glazed nose and could operate from unpaved airfields — which aircraft is it?
Signified by the minus sign, this arithmetic operation represents removing objects from a collection and is the inverse of addition — which operation is it?
Subtraction: One of the four basic arithmetic operations.

Also known as 'wet brain,' this neurological condition results from a severe thiamine deficiency and classically presents with confusion, poor coordination, and eye movement problems — which condition is it?
Wernicke encephalopathy: Medical condition. The condition is part of a larger group of thiamine deficiency disorders that includes beriberi, in all its forms, and alcoholic Korsakoff syndrome.
This Japanese immunologist shared the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with James P. Allison for identifying the PD-1 protein — who is he?
Tasuku Honjo: Japanese immunologist and Nobel laureate (born 1942)
Created by Larry Wall in 1987 as a Unix scripting tool for report processing, this language's planned sixth version was eventually spun off and renamed Raku — which programming language?
Perl: Interpreted programming language first released in 1987.
This recurring set of hormone-driven reproductive changes in female mammals is interrupted by 'rest' phases and pregnancy, and has a male equivalent called rut — what is it?

Estrous cycle (from Latin oestrus 'frenzy', originally from Ancient Greek (ostros) 'gadfly') is a set of recurring physiological changes induced by reproductive hormones in females of mammalian subclass Theria.
Dubbed the 'father of information theory,' this polymath was the first to apply Boolean algebra to digital circuits and helped found the field of artificial intelligence — who is he?

Commonly called sowbread, this genus of 25 tuberous flowering plants is prized for upswept petals and patterned leaves, native from the Mediterranean to Iran with one species even found in Somalia — which genus?
Cyclamen: Genus of flowering plants in the primrose family.
This common name covers edible fruit from the Ribes genus — the same genus as currants — coming in colors from green and red to purple, yellow, white, or black — which fruit?
Gooseberry: Species of Ribes cultivated for its edible fruit.
This nearly worldwide genus of flowering plants — commonly called St. John's wort — was the subject of a definitive taxonomic monograph identifying 36 sections within it. Which genus?
Hypericum: Genus of flowering plants known as St. John's worts.
First described in 1893 during a flu pandemic and mistakenly blamed as its cause, this Gram-negative bacterium causes pneumonia and meningitis mainly in infants — which bacterium?
Haemophilus influenzae: Species of bacterium. The bacteria are mesophilic and grow best at temperatures between 35 and 37 °C.

A French mining engineer and executive, this theorist developed a general theory of business administration bearing his own name — independently of, yet alongside, Frederick Taylor's scientific management. Who is he?

Henri Fayol (29 July 1841 - 19 November 1925) was a French mining engineer, mining executive, author and director of mines who developed a general theory of business administration that is often called Fayolism.
This holotropical bird family comprises a dozen Afrotropical species and some 167 Neotropical species, including the blue-and-yellow macaw and the grey parrot — which family is this?
Psittacidae: Family of birds. The family Psittacidae or holotropical parrots is one of three families of true parrots.
Nicknamed 'Red-Stockings,' this French herding dog breed hails from the plains of Central France — which breed is it?
Beauceron (French) is a herding dog breed originating from the plains of Central France.
Named from the Latin word for 'bridge' after Italian anatomist Costanzo Varolio, this brainstem structure sits above the medulla and below the midbrain — what is it?
Pons: Part of the brainstem in humans and other bipeds.
This number-theory rule holds that if p is prime, then for any integer a, the value a to the power p minus a is always a multiple of p — which rule is this?

Fermat's little theorem: A prime p divides a^p–a for any integer a. Fermat's little theorem is the basis for the Fermat primality test and is one of the fundamental results of elementary number theory.
Marked by a stopped heartbeat and halted breathing, this reversible-sounding medical state was given its name once CPR and defibrillation made post-arrest resuscitation possible — what's it called?
Clinical death is the medical term for cessation of blood circulation and breathing, the two criteria necessary to sustain the lives of human beings and of many other organisms.
Defined as one joule of absorbed radiation energy per kilogram of matter, this SI measure is used in radiotherapy dosing and predicting acute radiation sickness — which measure is this?
Gray (unit) (symbol: Gy) is the unit of ionizing radiation dose in the International System of Units (SI), defined as the absorption of one joule of radiation energy per kilogram of matter.
This deciduous member of the rose family includes many varieties known as plums in English, with greengages and damsons among its subspecies — which species is it?
Prunus domestica: Species of flowering plant.
As Square's chief technology officer, this software engineer helped build Cash App before he was fatally stabbed in San Francisco in 2023 — who was he?
Bob Lee (businessman) (December 20, 1979 - April 4, 2023) was an American businessman and software engineer who was best known for helping to create the financial service Cash App.
Marketed under the brand name Flomax, this alpha-blocker medication treats enlarged prostate symptoms and helps ease the passage of kidney stones — which drug?
Tamsulosin: Medication. Tamsulosin, sold under the brand name Flomax among others, is a medication used to treat symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia and chronic prostatitis.
Co-founding a messaging app that Facebook bought in 2014 for $19.3 billion, this billionaire programmer ranked 44th on Forbes' list of richest Americans — who is he?
Located behind the nasal cavity where the nose meets the throat, which mass of lymphoid tissue is also known as the pharyngeal tonsil?
Adenoid: Type of tonsil. The adenoid, also known as the pharyngeal tonsil, or nasopharyngeal tonsil is the superior-most of the tonsils.
Native to western Europe and known scientifically as Ribes rubrum, which widely cultivated berry has escaped into the wild across many regions?
Redcurrant: Flowering plant species in the family Grossulariaceae.

In a late stage of stellar evolution, this puffed-up, low-to-intermediate-mass star has a surface temperature around 5,000 K and burns helium or hydrogen in shells around its core — what type of star is it?
Red giant: Type of large cool star.
Making up roughly 75% of antibodies found in the human bloodstream, which antibody type is produced by plasma B cells and features two paratopes?
Nicknamed 'Father of the National Parks,' this Scottish-born naturalist co-founded the Sierra Club and helped preserve Yosemite Valley and Sequoia National Park — who is he?
Capable of delivering shocks up to 860 volts, this South American knifefish helped inspire the invention of the battery in 1800 — what is it?
Electric eel: Genus of fishes in South America.

This fibrous gourd, edible only when picked young, becomes a scrubbing sponge once fully ripened — and one grown in Graham, NC, broke the world heaviest record in October 2025 at 11 lb 3.3 oz. What is it?
Native to the Andean forests of South America, this genus of trees is nicknamed the 'fever tree' because its bark yields quinine, the only effective malaria treatment for centuries — what is it?
Cinchona: Genus of plants, source of quinine.

Named after a bird of prey, this British-developed attack aircraft was the only truly successful vertical-takeoff design of its era, able to fly from car parks and forest clearings instead of vulnerable airbases — which aircraft?
Harrier jump jet: Multirole combat aircraft family by Hawker Siddeley, later British Aerospace.
This butterfly was the first species to be given the common name now applied to its entire family, and is widespread across the Palearctic and North America — which species?
Papilio machaon: Species of insect. Papilio machaon, the Old World swallowtail, is a butterfly of the family Papilionidae.
Nicknamed 'top shelf' dizziness, this inner-ear disorder causes brief spinning sensations lasting under a minute whenever you tilt or turn your head — what is this condition called?
Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo: Medical condition. Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), sometimes called "top shelf vertigo", is a disorder arising from a problem in the inner ear.
This memory disorder comes in two main forms — one blocking recall of events before a specific date, the other preventing new experiences from becoming lasting memories — what is it?
Amnesia: Cognitive disorder where memory is disturbed or lost.

Often called a 'collapsed lung' in casual speech, this condition is really the partial deflation of the lung's alveoli rather than fluid filling them, and shows up frequently on chest X-rays — what is it?
Atelectasis: Partial collapse of a lung causing reduced gas exchange.

Covering the asymmetric relationship between citizens and the state — including constitutional, administrative, tax, and criminal matters — this branch of the legal system contrasts with the branch governing relationships between individuals — which branch?
Public law: Law governing government actions.
Native to Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa, this flowering plant lent its name — and originally its root — to a fluffy campfire treat, and is used in herbal medicine — which plant?
Co-founder of a sprawling Russian conglomerate and a major private bank in 1991, this Ukrainian-born tycoon was once ranked Russia's second-richest person — who is he?
Mikhail Fridman: Russian–Israeli billionaire businessman and oligarch (born 1964)
Despite being named after a European bird for its reddish-orange breast, this thrush is the most abundant landbird on its continent, numbering some 370 million individuals — what is it?
American robin: Species of bird. The American robin (Turdus migratorius) is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family.

Famous for the male's song delivered while hovering 50 to 100 metres above open farmland, this streaked greyish-brown bird has been introduced to Australia, New Zealand, Canada and Hawaii — what is it?
Eurasian skylark: Species of bird. The Eurasian skylark (Alauda arvensis), commonly referred to in Europe as the lark, is a passerine bird in the lark family, Alaudidae.
First known as a portrait painter, this American inventor helped develop a single-wire telegraph system and lent his name to the dot-and-dash code introduced in 1837 — who is he?
Samuel Morse: American inventor and painter (1791–1872)
Nicknamed 'rabbit fever' and spread by ticks, deer flies or contact with infected animals, this bacterial infection causes fever, skin ulcers and swollen lymph nodes — what is it?
Tularemia: Infectious disease caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis.
This family of long-legged wading birds that live in wetlands and forests lent its name — mistakenly — to the scientific name of the western cattle egret in 1757 — what's the bird group called?
Ibis: Long-legged wading birds with down-curved beaks.
Nominated by Einstein, this Austrian physicist won the 1945 Nobel Prize for describing the exclusion principle and, in 1930, proposed the tiny neutral particle later named the neutrino — who is he?
This 12th-century polymath from Mesopotamia wrote a treatise describing 50 ingenious mechanical devices, including his famous elephant clock, earning him the title 'father of robotics' — who is he?
Ismail al-Jazari: Muslim engineer and artist (1136–1206)
Marketed as Hydrodiuril, this medication treats high blood pressure and fluid retention by blocking sodium and chloride reabsorption in the kidneys' distal tubules — what drug is it?

Hydrochlorothiazide: Diuretic medication. Hydrochlorothiazide, sold under the brand name Hydrodiuril among others, is a diuretic medication used to treat hypertension and swelling due to fluid build-up.
Originally developed as an antidepressant, this fast-acting SSRI was later approved to treat premature ejaculation and was sold to Johnson & Johnson in 2003 — what drug is it?
Dapoxetine: Medication used to treat premature ejaculation.

Affecting roughly one in 250 baby boys, this is the second most common birth defect of the male reproductive system, in which a key opening doesn't form in its usual place — what is this condition called?
Hypospadias: Malformation in which the urethral opening is misplaced.
Caused by bacteria in the Salmonella genus, this common form of food poisoning brings diarrhea, fever, and cramps within 12 to 36 hours of eating contaminated food — what is it called?
Salmonellosis: Infection caused by Salmonella bacteria. It is one of the most common diseases to be known as food poisoning (though the name refers to food-borne illness in general).
First made in 1969 and approved for medical use in 1978, this selective beta blocker treats high blood pressure, angina, and helps prevent migraines — what is it called?
Metoprolol: Beta blocker medication. It is also used to prevent further heart problems after myocardial infarction and to prevent headaches in those with migraines.

Despite having no formal medical education, this laboratory supervisor helped develop a life-saving shunt for blue baby syndrome alongside a surgeon and a cardiologist, later earning an honorary doctorate from Johns Hopkins — who was he?
Blooming for weeks each spring and thriving in the shade under trees, these flowering shrubs belong to the genus Rhododendron — what are they called?
Azalea: Subgroup of rhododendron flowering shrubs.
Spread mainly through the fecal-oral route, these single-stranded RNA enteroviruses share traits with poliovirus and rank among the leading causes of aseptic meningitis — which pathogens?
Coxsackievirus: Virus that causes digestive upset and sometimes heart damage.
Nicknamed the 'Human Computer' for her lightning mental arithmetic, this Indian writer also authored one of the earliest studies of homosexuality in India, back in 1977 — who is she?
Shakuntala Devi: Indian writer and mental calculator (1929–2013)
Also called a dassie, this small African and Middle Eastern mammal lives in crevice colonies of up to 80 and posts lookouts to warn of approaching predators — which animal?
Rock hyrax: Species of mammal native to Africa and the Middle East.
Grown as deciduous shrubs across the temperate Northern Hemisphere and related to the birch family, this plant produces a popular round brown nut — which plant genus?
This Russian physicist miraculously survived a 1978 accident in which a high-energy proton beam from a particle accelerator passed directly through his skull — who is he?
Anatoli Bugorski: Soviet and Russian scientist (born 1942)
In this eye disorder, the cornea gradually thins and bulges into a cone shape, causing blurry or double vision often linked to excessive eye rubbing as a risk factor — which condition?
Keratoconus: Medical condition involving the eye.

Named after a 19th-century British naturalist employed by the East India Company, this small deer species native to south-eastern China and Taiwan has also become an established wild population in the UK and Ireland — what is it?
Reeves's muntjac: Species of deer. It has also been introduced in the United Kingdom, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Japan.
Born in 1320, this ruler acceded to the throne in 1333 and became the last emperor of one dynasty and the first of its northern successor state after fleeing — who was he?
Toghon Temür: Emperor of Yuan dynasty from 1333 to 1368.
Also called pennyroyal, this minty flowering plant native to Europe, North Africa and the Middle East has a folk-remedy history despite being toxic to the liver — what species is it?
Sold under the brand name Luvox, this SSRI antidepressant treats OCD and other anxiety disorders, with milder side effects than most in its class except gastrointestinal ones — what drug is it?
Fluvoxamine: SSRI antidepressant. Fluvoxamine, sold under the brand name Luvox among others, is an antidepressant of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class.
Also known as reishi or lingzhi, this red-colored fungus grows on decaying hardwood in parts of Europe and China — what is it?

These small to medium passerine birds have stout conical bills for cracking seeds and nuts, a worldwide native range excluding Australia and the poles, and include canaries, siskins, and Darwin's famous Galápagos group — what bird family is this?
Finch: Family of birds. The true finches are small to medium-sized passerine birds in the family Fringillidae.

Diagnosed when a person has at least three of five red flags -- including abdominal obesity and high blood pressure -- this cluster of conditions raises the risk of heart disease and diabetes in about a quarter of US adults. What is it?
Metabolic syndrome: Cluster of diseases occurring with obesity.
Sitting atop the brainstem and linking it to the diencephalon and cerebrum, this structure governs vision, hearing, motor control, and arousal -- what is it called?
Midbrain: Forward-most portion of the brainstem.
Beginning about six hours after someone dependent on drinking stops, this set of symptoms can include shaking, sweating, seizures, and life-threatening delirium -- what is it called?
Developed for the Soviet Navy and known to NATO by a code name, this helicopter remains in service with several countries including Russia, Ukraine, and India -- which aircraft?
Shed and regrown every year on most male deer, this bony head growth serves as both a weapon and a symbol of sexual attraction — what is it?
Antler: Skull projections found in deer.
First classified as its own fossil order in 1835, this group of Mesozoic marine reptiles thrived through the Jurassic before dying out at the end of the Cretaceous — what are they called?
Plesiosaur: Order of reptiles (fossil). The Plesiosauria or plesiosaurs are an order or clade of extinct Mesozoic marine reptiles, belonging to the Sauropterygia.
Building his first firearm at age 13 in his father's gun shop, this American designer earned 128 patents and pioneered the autoloading pistol — who is he?
Praised by Einstein as the most important woman in the history of mathematics, she proved a theorem linking physical symmetries to conservation laws — who is she?
Discovered by Robert Koch in 1876, this rod-shaped microbe was the first ever shown experimentally to cause disease, providing the earliest evidence for germ theory — which organism?
Despite a scientific name meaning 'sand burrower,' this snake actually prefers rocky terrain and is considered Europe's most dangerous viper thanks to fangs up to 13mm long — which species?
Vipera ammodytes: Species of snake. It is reputed to be the most dangerous of the European vipers due to its large size, long fangs (up to 13 mm) and high venom toxicity.
The most widespread New World scavenger of its kind, this bird sniffs out the gases of early decay to find carrion and rides thermals instead of flapping — which bird?
Turkey vulture (Cathartes aura) is the most widespread of the New World vultures.
In 1949, this NASA mathematician became the first African-American woman to supervise a team at Langley, later teaching herself and her staff the Fortran language — who is she?
Dorothy Vaughan: American human computer and computer programmer (1910–2008)
Commonly nicknamed phlegm, this mucus coughed up from the trachea and bronchi is examined for tell-tale yellow or green coloring that signals infection — what is it?
Sputum: Mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways.

Often called the greatest mathematician of the twentieth century, this German-born Frenchman revolutionized algebraic geometry before abruptly leaving his post at a Paris research institute in 1970 — who is he?
This Italian physician who died in 1909 is considered the founder of modern criminology, arguing that 'born criminals' could be spotted by physical defects — who is he?
As the 14th chairman of the Federal Reserve, this economist steered the central bank's response to the 2008 financial crisis and later won a Nobel for his work on the Great Depression — who is he?
This interdisciplinary field examines moral questions raised by advances in biology, medicine, and biotechnology, touching everything from patient care to environmental policy — what is it called?
Bioethics: Study of the ethical issues emerging from advances in biology and medicine.
Able to breathe air thanks to lobed fins and a well-developed internal skeleton, these freshwater vertebrates are considered the closest living relatives of land animals — what are they?
Cultivated by the Aztecs and named partly for a Mexican state capital, this flower opens each evening between four and eight o'clock and perfumes the night before closing by morning — which plant?

Mirabilis jalapa: Species of flower. Mirabilis jalapa, the marvel of Peru or four o'clock flower, is the most commonly grown ornamental species of Mirabilis plant, and is available in a range of colors.
This Harvard-trained legal scholar who wrote on criminal punishment and retribution joined Florida State's faculty in 2005, and was later murdered in a plot tied to his ex-wife's family — who is he?
Dan Markel: American law professor and murder victim (1972–2014)
Known by common names like true lavender and English lavender despite not being native to England, this Mediterranean-basin plant belongs to the mint family — which species?
Lavandula angustifolia: Species of plant. Lavandula angustifolia, formerly L. officinalis, is a flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae, native to the Mediterranean basin.

Diagnosed in about 8% of male urology visits in the US, this umbrella term covers several bacterial and non-bacterial pelvic conditions, despite its name not always involving actual inflammation — which condition?
Prostatitis: Medical condition. Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.
This German polar researcher proposed in 1912 that the continents were slowly drifting apart, a theory mainstream geology only accepted decades later thanks to palaeomagnetism — who was he?
Alfred Wegener: German climatologist and geophysicist (1880–1930)

Tucked beneath the lateral fissure of the brain and named for its position near the head's temples, this region handles language comprehension, memory, and emotion — which part of the cerebral cortex?
Temporal lobe is one of the four major lobes of the cerebral cortex in the brain of mammals.

Derived from a Greek word meaning 'to lead out,' this scholarly practice of critically interpreting a text — often the Bible — also examines its historical background and literary genre — what is it called?
Exegesis: Critical investigation of a text.
This is the largest lizard family, boasting over 950 species that cling to surfaces via Van der Waals forces in their toe hairs — including house, tokay, and day varieties — which family?
Gekkonidae: Family of lizards. Gekkonidae (the common geckos) is the largest family of geckos, containing over 950 described species in 62 genera.
Expressed with symbols like < and >, this relation shows that one quantity is less than or greater than another, rather than equal — what's it called?
Inequality (mathematics): Mathematical relation making a non-equal comparison.
Also known as the holly oak, this large evergreen tree native to the Mediterranean produces acorns that mature within a single summer — which species is it?
Quercus ilex: Oak tree species native to the Mediterranean.
With the widest geographic range of any non-human primate, this brown-to-grey Old World monkey lives in matrilineal troops of up to 200 individuals — which species?
Rhesus macaque: Species of Old World monkey. The rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta), colloquially rhesus monkey, is a species of Old World monkey in the Macaca genus.

Nicknamed 'terror birds,' this family of large, mostly flightless carnivores roamed the Americas from the Cenozoic era, with one genus, Titanis, reaching as far as the southern United States — which family?
Phorusrhacidae: Extinct family of flightless birds. The exact number of genera is uncertain, as some taxa such as Brontornis may be different forms of bird instead.
Linked to the use of highly absorbent tampons, this bacterial-toxin condition causes fever, rash, skin peeling, and a dangerous drop in blood pressure — which condition?
Toxic shock syndrome: Medical condition caused by bacterial toxins.
Overharvested in the 19th century for old-fashioned bloodletting, this European leech remains endangered in many countries today — which species?
Hirudo medicinalis: Species of annelid worm.

Marked by platelet counts that fall too low — sometimes below 50,000 per microliter and requiring emergency care — this blood disorder is the most common coagulation problem in ICU patients — what is it called?
Thrombocytopenia: Abnormally low levels of platelets in the blood.
Patented in 1956, this glucocorticoid treats skin conditions, allergies, and rheumatic disorders, and was the 108th most prescribed U.S. medication in 2023 — which drug?
Triamcinolone: Steroid medication. Triamcinolone is a glucocorticoid used to treat certain skin diseases, allergies, and rheumatic disorders among others.
Striking children recovering from a viral illness like the flu, this brain disease has been linked in about 90% of cases to aspirin use — what is it called?
Reye syndrome: Rapidly worsening brain disease.

Typically affecting women between 35 and 50, this uterine condition occurs when endometrial-like tissue grows within the muscular wall of the uterus, causing painful, heavy periods — what is it called?
Adenomyosis: Extension of endometrial tissue into the myometrium.
Once classified under two different bacterial genera, this nonmotile coccobacillus forms small gray colonies on chocolate agar and has its own colistin-oxolinic acid selective medium — which species?
Gardnerella vaginalis: Species of bacterium. Gardnerella vaginalis is a species of Gram-variable-staining facultative anaerobic bacteria.
Also known as ash pumpkin or winter melon, this South and Southeast Asian plant is grown for its very large fruit, eaten as a vegetable once mature — which plant?
Wax gourd: Species of vine and edible fruit.
Known since 1983 by a fad-themed nickname, this inventor and TV host ran a show celebrating children's inventions from 1988 to 1994 — who is he?
Sold under the brand name Rituxan, this monoclonal antibody treats non-Hodgkin lymphoma, rheumatoid arthritis and several other autoimmune conditions via slow IV infusion — what is it?
Found on birds and even some non-avian dinosaurs, this complex evolutionary structure aids flight, insulation and waterproofing, and gives its name to the study of plumology — what is it?
Caused by the parasite Entamoeba histolytica, this intestinal infection can spread to the liver and trigger abscesses there even without any prior diarrhea — what condition is it?
Amoebiasis: Human disease caused by amoeba protists.

Dubbed 'probably the most successful British artist you've never heard of,' this progressive rock musician founded Porcupine Tree and has earned six Grammy nominations across various projects — who is he?

Derived from a Greek word meaning 'hump,' this abnormal, excessive curving of the upper spine can result from osteoporosis, disc disease, or a condition common in teens called Scheuermann's disease — what is it called?
Kyphosis: Excessive convex curvature of the lower and middle spine.
Genus name meaning 'horned' in Latin, this raptor nests in dense woodland edges but hunts over open ground, feeding mostly on voles — which bird?
Long-eared owl: Species of owl. The genus name, Asio, is Latin for "horned owl", and the specific epithet, otus, is derived from Greek and refers to a small eared owl.
This miniature Belgian-French dog breed comes in two varieties named for a butterfly and a moth, based on whether their ears stand erect or hang down — which breed?
Continental Toy Spaniel: Belgian and French breed of dog. The Épagneul Nain Continental or Continental Toy Spaniel is a Belgian and French breed of dog of spaniel type and of miniature or toy size.
This scientific practice of systematically measuring the human body has been used in paleoanthropology, historical living-standards research, and modern clothing design — what is it called?
Anthropometry: Measurement of the human individual.

First classified by Linnaeus in 1753, this genus in the family Myrtaceae includes only two accepted species today: one native to the Mediterranean, the other to the Saharan mountains of North Africa — which genus?
Myrtus: Genus of flowering plants in the family Myrtaceae.
Patented by Roche in 1961 and approved for medical use in 1974, which benzodiazepine, similar in effect to diazepam, is sometimes given as a presurgical sedative in 1.5, 3, or 6 mg tablets?
Bromazepam: Benzodiazepine drug. Bromazepam, sold under many brand names, is a benzodiazepine.
This Canadian-American author and former researcher wrote the bestselling book Outlive: The Science and Art of Longevity — who is he?
Peter Attia (born March 19, 1973) is a Canadian-American author and former researcher known for his work in longevity medicine.
This Brazilian software engineer co-founded Instagram in 2010 and served as its CTO until 2018, later co-launching Rt.live and Artifact before joining Anthropic in 2024 — who is he?
Mike Krieger: Brazilian entrepreneur and software engineer (born 1986)
With about 37 species ranging from central Canada down to Costa Rica, this slender, keeled-scaled reptile typically sports longitudinal stripes in blue, yellow, or red — which reptile is it?
Garter snake is the common name for small to medium-sized snakes belonging to the genus Thamnophis in the family Colubridae.
Emerging in the 1960s as scholars from once-colonized nations began writing back, this academic field examines the lingering cultural and political effects of empire — what's it called?
Postcolonialism: Study of the cultural legacy of colonialism and imperialism.
Formed when chlorine dissolves in water, this compound is the main disinfecting agent in chlorine solutions — and your own white blood cells make it to fight off invading germs. What is it?
Hypochlorous acid: Chemical compound. Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.
This Austrian-American economist developed the theory of praxeology and became a leading 20th-century defender of classical liberalism against rising authoritarianism — who is he?
Ludwig von Mises: Austrian–American political economist (1881–1973)
This small, fluid-filled pocket that forms in the skin's upper layers — usually from friction, burns, or infection — gets the name 'bleb' when it's especially tiny. What is it?
Blister: Small pocket of fluid within the upper layers of the skin. The word "blister" entered English in the 14th century.

Galaxies recede from Earth at speeds proportional to their distance, a relationship credited to a 1929 paper — though the maths behind an expanding universe had already been derived in 1922 by Alexander Friedmann. What's this relationship called?
Hubble's law: Observation in physical cosmology.
Known in veterinary medicine as inappetence when it strikes cats, dogs, or cattle, which general medical term describes any loss of appetite — a symptom rather than a diagnosis in itself?
Anorexia (symptom): Loss of appetite. The symptom also occurs in non-human animals, such as cats, dogs, cattle, goats, and sheep.
Named from a Tupi-Guarani word for tobacco filtered through French, this South American flowering plant genus is a garden hybrid favorite — which plant?
Petunia: Genus of flowering plants. The popular flower of the same name derived its epithet from the French, which took the word pétun, 'tobacco', from a Tupi–Guarani language.
Better known in the kitchen as cream of tartar, this winemaking byproduct helps stabilize egg whites for fluffier meringues — what compound is it?
Potassium bitartrate: Chemical salt used in cooking as cream of tartar.

Having composed nearly 1,000 songs and sold over 104 million records, this Austrian singer won the Eurovision Song Contest in 1966 and modernized German-language pop with a French chanson influence — who is he?
Udo Jürgens: Austrian singer and composer (1934–2014)
Born in 1983, this Mexican actress has built a multi-hyphenate career as a producer and screenwriter as well — who is she?
Martha Higareda: Mexican actress, writer, producer (b. 1983)
Two metalhead slacker teens time-travel to round up historical figures for a school presentation in this 1989 sci-fi comedy starring Keanu Reeves and Alex Winter — which film?
Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure: 1989 film by Stephen Herek.
This American actor appeared in the 2014 horror film Unfriended and the drama Men, Women & Children before joining the cast of the supernatural series Manifest in 2021 — who is he?
This Canadian actress played Kara Zor-El on Smallville before starring as a werewolf named Elena Michaels in a Space channel series — who is she?
Directed by Bryan Singer and based on two classic fairy tales, this 2013 film follows a farmhand who opens a gateway to a race of towering beings while trying to save a princess — which film?
Jack the Giant Slayer: 2013 fantasy adventure film by Bryan Singer.
This South Korean actor won Best Actor at the 61st Baeksang Arts Awards for a 2025 medical drama, after breaking out in 2006's 'Princess Hours' and starring in a zombie period series — who is he?
Ju Ji-hoon: South Korean actor and model (born 1982)
Born December 9, 1980, this performer works as both an actor and a singer in Japan — who is he?
Issey Takahashi: Japanese actor and singer (born 1980)
Best known for playing Allison Argent in a teen supernatural drama, this actress later took the lead role of Abby Arcane in a 2019 series — who is she?

Originating the role of Juan Perón on Broadway and playing the title role in a 1989 revival of a musical about a demon barber, this character actor also portrayed a corrupt warden in a 1994 prison drama — who is he?
Bob Gunton: American film, television, and theatre actor (born 1945)
With roles in over 100 Hindi films including '3 Idiots' and 'PK,' this actor made his directorial debut in 2025 with a self-starring drama — who is he?
Boman Irani: Indian actor, producer, filmmaker, voice artist and photographer (born 1959)
Filmed on location in Paris and pairing Cary Grant with Audrey Hepburn, this 1963 mystery-comedy has a Henry Mancini score and animated titles by Maurice Binder — which film?
Charade (1963 film) is a 1963 American romantic screwball comedy mystery film produced and directed by Stanley Donen, written by Peter Stone and Marc Behm, and starring Cary Grant and Audrey Hepburn.
The third film in a prehistoric-mammal franchise, this 2009 sequel sends its herd into a tropical lost world beneath the frozen surface to rescue a sloth kidnapped by a giant reptile — which film?
Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs
Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs
Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs: 2009 American animated film.
Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs
Starring Ji Sung across 16 episodes on tvN in 2021, this South Korean drama also got a 48-chapter webtoon adaptation on Comico — which series?
The Devil Judge: 2021 South Korean television series. The Devil Judge (Korean: 악마판사) is a South Korean television series starring Ji Sung, Kim Min-jung, Park Jin-young and Park Gyu-young.
In this 1936 part-talkie, Charlie Chaplin's Little Tramp struggles to survive amid factories and assembly lines in his final outing as the iconic character — which film?
Modern Times (film) is a 1936 American part-talkie satirical slapstick comedy film produced, scored, co-edited, written and directed by Charlie Chaplin.
Adapted from Stephen King's fictional Maine town, this Hulu supernatural horror series gave its second season an entirely standalone story starring Lizzy Caplan and Tim Robbins — which series?
Castle Rock (TV series) is an American supernatural horror television series, adapted from Stephen King's fictional town of Castle Rock, Maine.
This Australian actress played FBI agent Samantha Spade on 'Without a Trace' before starring as Detective Carrie Wells on 'Unforgettable' — who is she?
Directed by Ron Howard, this 1991 thriller follows Chicago firefighters hunting a serial arsonist, and later inspired a special-effects attraction at Universal Studios Hollywood — which film?
Backdraft (film) is a 1991 American action thriller drama film directed by Ron Howard and written by Gregory Widen.

A former stunt performer and martial artist, this American actress wrote and directed the 2008 film 'The Sensei' and later authored a children's book called 'The Curious Mind of Sebastian' — who is she?
Diana Lee Inosanto: American actress, director, and martial artist.
This 2019 Disney+ film follows a musher and his sled dog racing to deliver diphtheria antitoxin to Nome, Alaska during the famous 1925 serum run — which film?
Togo (film) is a 2019 American historical adventure film directed by Ericson Core and produced by Walt Disney Pictures.

Drawing on writer-director James Gray's own childhood in Queens, this 2022 coming-of-age drama follows a young Jewish-American boy's friendship with an African-American classmate amid family pressure and prejudice — which film?
Armageddon Time: 2022 film by James Gray. The film stars Anne Hathaway, Jeremy Strong, Banks Repeta, Jaylin Webb, and Anthony Hopkins.
This 2023 Chinese action comedy stars Jackie Chan as an old-school stunt performer whose closest companion is his trusty stunt horse — which film?
Ride On (film) is a 2023 Chinese action comedy film written and directed by Larry Yang.
This Irish-Canadian actress starred as the title orphan in a CBC/Netflix series based on Lucy Maud Montgomery's 1908 novel, and later joined the cast of a Netflix sci-fi hit as Vickie — who is she?
Amybeth McNulty: Irish and Canadian actress (born 2001)
This comic writer created a wildly popular zombie apocalypse series and a superhero saga for Image Comics, later co-founding a media company to develop them into TV, film, and games — who is he?
Robert Kirkman: American comic book writer.

One of the first French comedians to use profanities as onstage humor, this irreverent stand-up won a César Award for a dramatic role and later founded a charity restaurant network still feeding people today — who is he?
Coluche: French stage comedian and film actor (1944–1986)
Adapted from Rhonda Byrne's 2006 self-help bestseller, this 2020 romantic drama starring Katie Holmes and Josh Lucas debuted via video on demand that July — which film?
The Secret: Dare to Dream: 2020 film directed by Andy Tennant.

Created by J. J. Abrams, this WB college drama starred Keri Russell as a California student who followed her crush across the country to a fictionalized NYU, with each of its four seasons matching a class year — which series?
Felicity (TV series) is an American drama television series created by J. J. Abrams and Matt Reeves.
After starting out in Wong Fu web productions, this American actor played Ben Hargreeves in Netflix's 'The Umbrella Academy' (2019–2024) and took the title role in 2021's 'After Yang' — who is he?
